### Class Traverser (com.landawn.abacus.guava.Traverser)
Provides methods for traversing a graph or tree structure in various orders.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### forTree(...) -> Traverser<T>
- **Signature:** `public static <T> Traverser<T> forTree(final Function<? super T, ? extends Iterable<T>> tree) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new traverser for a directed acyclic graph that has at most one path from the start node to any node reachable from the start node, such as a tree.
- **Contract:**
  - This method is optimized for tree-like structures and will perform better than #forGraph(Function) when the graph is known to be a tree.
  - Providing graphs that don't conform to the tree structure may lead to: Traversal not terminating (if the graph has cycles) Nodes being visited multiple times (if multiple paths exist from the start node to any node reachable from it) In these cases, use #forGraph(Function) instead.
  - Null children must be filtered out because successor iterables may not contain nulls: Usage Examples: Note: the successor function must not return `null`; return an empty Iterable for leaf nodes.
  - The function itself is first invoked when a traversal method is called (once per start node, see the class note), so an exception it throws for a start node propagates from that call.
- **Parameters:**
  - `tree` (`Function<? super T, ? extends Iterable<T>>`) — Function representing a directed acyclic graph that has at most one path between any two nodes. The function takes a node and returns its children (an empty Iterable for leaf nodes; must not return `null`).
- **Returns:** a new Traverser for the specified tree structure
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `tree` is `null`.
- **Performance:** While traversing, the traverser will use O(H) space (where H is the number of nodes that have been seen but not yet visited, that is, the "horizon").
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  a     b      c
      / \   / \     |
     /   \ /   \    |
    d     e     f   g
          |
          |
          h
  ```
  ```java
  a     b
      / \   / \
     /   \ /   \
    c     d     e
           \   /
            \ /
             f
  ```
  ```java
  record BinaryNode(BinaryNode left, BinaryNode right) {}
    Traverser<BinaryNode> binaryTree = Traverser.forTree(node ->
        java.util.stream.Stream.of(node.left(), node.right())
            .filter(java.util.Objects::nonNull)
            .toList());
  ```
  ```java
  // Traverse an organizational hierarchy
    class Employee {
        String name;
        List<Employee> directReports = new ArrayList<>();
        List<Employee> getDirectReports() { return directReports; }
        String getName() { return name; }
    }
  
    Employee ceo = new Employee();
    Traverser<Employee> orgTraverser = Traverser.forTree(Employee::getDirectReports);
    orgTraverser.breadthFirst(ceo)
        .forEach(employee -> System.out.println(employee.getName()));
  ```
- **See also:** #forGraph(Function)
##### forGraph(...) -> Traverser<T>
- **Signature:** `public static <T> Traverser<T> forGraph(final Function<? super T, ? extends Iterable<T>> graph) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new traverser for the given general graph that may contain cycles.
- **Contract:**
  - This method should be used when the graph may have cycles or multiple paths between nodes.
  - If `graph` is known to be tree-shaped, consider using #forTree(Function) instead for better performance.
  - Usage Examples: Note: the successor function must not return `null`; return an empty Iterable for nodes with no successors.
  - The function itself is first invoked when a traversal method is called (once per start node, see the class note), so an exception it throws for a start node propagates from that call.
- **Parameters:**
  - `graph` (`Function<? super T, ? extends Iterable<T>>`) — Function representing a general graph that may have cycles. The function takes a node and returns its adjacent nodes (successors); return an empty Iterable for nodes with no successors (must not return `null`).
- **Returns:** a new Traverser for the specified graph structure
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `graph` is `null`.
- **Performance:** While traversing, the traverser will use O(n) space (where n is the number of nodes that have thus far been visited), plus O(H) space (where H is the number of nodes that have been seen but not yet visited, that is, the "horizon").
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Traverse a social network graph (which may have cycles)
    class Person {
        List<Person> friends = new ArrayList<>();
        List<Person> getFriends() { return friends; }
    }
  
    Person person = new Person();
    Traverser<Person> socialTraverser = Traverser.forGraph(Person::getFriends);
  
    // Visit at most 1000 people in breadth-first order (this does not impose a depth limit).
    Set<Person> network = socialTraverser.breadthFirst(person)
        .limit(1000)  // stops after 1000 nodes
        .toSet();
  ```
- **See also:** #forTree(Function)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### breadthFirst(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `public Stream<T> breadthFirst(final T startNode) throws NullPointerException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a Stream over the nodes reachable from `startNode`, in the order of a breadth-first traversal.
- **Contract:**
  - Breadth-first traversal is useful when you want to explore nodes level by level, such as finding the shortest path or exploring nodes in increasing distance from the start.
  - Example: For the following directed tree (edges point downward) with `startNode` `a`, and assuming each node's successors are returned in alphabetical order, breadth-first traversal returns the nodes in the order `a, b, c, d, e, f` (`a` at depth 0; then `b, c` at depth 1; then `d, e, f` at depth 2): The behavior of this method is undefined if the nodes, or the topology of the graph, change while iteration is in progress.
- **Parameters:**
  - `startNode` (`T`) — the node to start traversal from
- **Returns:** a Stream of nodes in breadth-first order
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `startNode` is `null`
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the successor function rejects a starting node as not belonging to the graph.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  a
         / \
        b   c
       / \   \
      d   e   f
  ```
  ```java
  // Only traverse the first 100 nodes
    // Assuming: TreeNode startNode; void processNode(TreeNode node);
    Traverser<TreeNode> traverser = Traverser.forTree(TreeNode::getChildren);
    traverser.breadthFirst(startNode)
        .limit(100)
        .forEach(node -> processNode(node));
  ```
- **See also:** #breadthFirst(Iterable), #depthFirstPreOrder(Object), #depthFirstPostOrder(Object)
- **Signature:** `public Stream<T> breadthFirst(final Iterable<? extends T> startNodes) throws NullPointerException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a Stream over the nodes reachable from any of the given `startNodes`, in the order of a breadth-first traversal.
- **Contract:**
  - This is the multi-root counterpart of #breadthFirst(Object): it behaves as if a virtual root with edges to each of the `startNodes` were traversed, except that the virtual root itself is not returned.
  - The behavior of this method is undefined if the nodes, or the topology of the graph, change while iteration is in progress.
- **Parameters:**
  - `startNodes` (`Iterable<? extends T>`) — the nodes to start traversal from
- **Returns:** a Stream of nodes in breadth-first order
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `startNodes` is `null` or contains a `null` element
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the successor function rejects a starting node as not belonging to the graph.
- **See also:** #breadthFirst(Object), #depthFirstPreOrder(Iterable), #depthFirstPostOrder(Iterable)
##### depthFirstPreOrder(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `public Stream<T> depthFirstPreOrder(final T startNode) throws NullPointerException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a Stream over the nodes reachable from `startNode`, in the order of a depth-first pre-order traversal.
- **Contract:**
  - Example: For the following directed tree (edges point downward) with `startNode` `a`, and assuming each node's successors are returned in alphabetical order, depth-first pre-order traversal returns the nodes in the order `a, b, d, e, c, f` (each node is emitted before its descendants; the `b` subtree is fully visited before `c`): The behavior of this method is undefined if the nodes, or the topology of the graph, change while iteration is in progress.
- **Parameters:**
  - `startNode` (`T`) — the node to start traversal from
- **Returns:** a Stream of nodes in depth-first pre-order
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `startNode` is `null`
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the successor function rejects a starting node as not belonging to the graph.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  a
         / \
        b   c
       / \   \
      d   e   f
  ```
  ```java
  // Find the first node matching a condition
    // Assuming: TreeNode root; boolean meetsCondition(TreeNode node);
    Traverser<TreeNode> traverser = Traverser.forTree(TreeNode::getChildren);
    Optional<TreeNode> found = traverser.depthFirstPreOrder(root)
        .filter(node -> meetsCondition(node))
        .findFirst();
  ```
- **See also:** #depthFirstPreOrder(Iterable), #breadthFirst(Object), #depthFirstPostOrder(Object)
- **Signature:** `public Stream<T> depthFirstPreOrder(final Iterable<? extends T> startNodes) throws NullPointerException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a Stream over the nodes reachable from any of the given `startNodes`, in the order of a depth-first pre-order traversal.
- **Contract:**
  - This is the multi-root counterpart of #depthFirstPreOrder(Object): it behaves as if a virtual root with edges to each of the `startNodes` were traversed, except that the virtual root itself is not returned.
  - The behavior of this method is undefined if the nodes, or the topology of the graph, change while iteration is in progress.
- **Parameters:**
  - `startNodes` (`Iterable<? extends T>`) — the nodes to start traversal from
- **Returns:** a Stream of nodes in depth-first pre-order
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `startNodes` is `null` or contains a `null` element
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the successor function rejects a starting node as not belonging to the graph.
- **See also:** #depthFirstPreOrder(Object), #breadthFirst(Iterable), #depthFirstPostOrder(Iterable)
##### depthFirstPostOrder(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `public Stream<T> depthFirstPostOrder(final T startNode) throws NullPointerException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a Stream over the nodes reachable from `startNode`, in the order of a depth-first post-order traversal.
- **Contract:**
  - Example: For the following directed tree (edges point downward) with `startNode` `a`, and assuming each node's successors are returned in alphabetical order, depth-first post-order traversal returns the nodes in the order `d, e, b, f, c, a` (each node is emitted only after all of its descendants): The behavior of this method is undefined if the nodes, or the topology of the graph, change while iteration is in progress.
- **Parameters:**
  - `startNode` (`T`) — the node to start traversal from
- **Returns:** a Stream of nodes in depth-first post-order
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `startNode` is `null`
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the successor function rejects a starting node as not belonging to the graph.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  a
         / \
        b   c
       / \   \
      d   e   f
  ```
  ```java
  // Calculate sizes of all subtrees
    // Assuming: TreeNode root; List<TreeNode> getChildren(TreeNode node);
    Traverser<TreeNode> traverser = Traverser.forTree(TreeNode::getChildren);
    Map<TreeNode, Integer> sizes = new HashMap<>();
    traverser.depthFirstPostOrder(root)
        .forEach(node -> {
            int size = 1 + getChildren(node).stream()
                .mapToInt(sizes::get)
                .sum();
            sizes.put(node, size);
        });
  ```
- **See also:** #depthFirstPostOrder(Iterable), #breadthFirst(Object), #depthFirstPreOrder(Object)
- **Signature:** `public Stream<T> depthFirstPostOrder(final Iterable<? extends T> startNodes) throws NullPointerException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a Stream over the nodes reachable from any of the given `startNodes`, in the order of a depth-first post-order traversal.
- **Contract:**
  - This is the multi-root counterpart of #depthFirstPostOrder(Object): it behaves as if a virtual root with edges to each of the `startNodes` were traversed, except that the virtual root itself is not returned.
  - The behavior of this method is undefined if the nodes, or the topology of the graph, change while iteration is in progress.
- **Parameters:**
  - `startNodes` (`Iterable<? extends T>`) — the nodes to start traversal from
- **Returns:** a Stream of nodes in depth-first post-order
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `startNodes` is `null` or contains a `null` element
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the successor function rejects a starting node as not belonging to the graph.
- **See also:** #depthFirstPostOrder(Object), #breadthFirst(Iterable), #depthFirstPreOrder(Iterable)

## com.landawn.abacus.guava.hash
### Interface HashFunction (com.landawn.abacus.guava.hash.HashFunction)
A hash function is a collision-averse pure function that maps an arbitrary block of data to a fixed-size number called a hash code.

**Thread-safety:** thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### newHasher(...) -> Hasher
- **Signature:** `Hasher newHasher()`
- **Summary:** Creates a new Hasher instance for incremental hashing.
- **Contract:**
  - Each hasher instance should be used for exactly one hash computation.
  - After calling Hasher#hash(), the hasher should not be used again.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a new, empty hasher instance ready to receive data
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HashFunction hf = Hashing.sha256();
    long id = 12345L;
    boolean isActive = true;
    String name = "example";
    HashCode hc = hf.newHasher()
        .put(id)
        .put(isActive)
        .put(name, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
        .hash();
  ```
- **Signature:** `Hasher newHasher(int expectedInputSize) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new Hasher instance with a hint about the expected input size.
- **Contract:**
  - If unsure, use #newHasher() instead.
- **Parameters:**
  - `expectedInputSize` (`int`) — a hint about the expected total size of input in bytes (must be non-negative)
- **Returns:** a new hasher instance optimized for the expected input size
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `expectedInputSize` is negative.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  byte[] largeData = new byte[1024 * 1024];  // 1MB
    HashCode hash = hashFunction.newHasher(largeData.length)
        .put(largeData)
        .hash();
  ```
##### hash(...) -> HashCode
- **Signature:** `HashCode hash(int input)`
- **Summary:** Computes the hash code for a single integer value.
- **Parameters:**
  - `input` (`int`) — the integer value to hash
- **Returns:** the hash code for the input value
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HashCode hash = Hashing.murmur3_32().hash(42);
  ```
- **Signature:** `HashCode hash(long input)`
- **Summary:** Computes the hash code for a single long value.
- **Parameters:**
  - `input` (`long`) — the long value to hash
- **Returns:** the hash code for the input value
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HashCode hash = Hashing.sha256().hash(System.currentTimeMillis());
  ```
- **Signature:** `HashCode hash(byte[] input) throws NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Computes the hash code for a byte array.
- **Parameters:**
  - `input` (`byte[]`) — the byte array to hash
- **Returns:** the hash code for the input bytes
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `input` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  byte[] data = "Hello, World!".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    HashCode hash = Hashing.sha256().hash(data);
  ```
- **Signature:** `HashCode hash(byte[] input, int off, int len) throws NullPointerException, IndexOutOfBoundsException`
- **Summary:** Computes the hash code for a portion of a byte array.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful when working with buffers or when only part of an array contains valid data.
- **Parameters:**
  - `input` (`byte[]`) — the byte array containing data to hash
  - `off` (`int`) — the starting offset in the array (zero-based, inclusive)
  - `len` (`int`) — the number of bytes to hash from the array
- **Returns:** the hash code for the specified bytes
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `input` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `off < 0` or `len < 0` or `off + len > input.length`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  byte[] buffer = new byte[1024];
    int bytesRead = inputStream.readNBytes(buffer, 0, buffer.length); // zero at end of input
    HashCode hash = Hashing.md5().hash(buffer, 0, bytesRead);
  ```
- **Signature:** `HashCode hash(CharSequence input) throws NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Computes the hash code for a character sequence without encoding.
- **Contract:**
  - Warning: This method produces different output than most other languages when hashing strings.
- **Parameters:**
  - `input` (`CharSequence`) — the character sequence to hash
- **Returns:** the hash code for the input characters
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `input` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HashCode hash = Hashing.murmur3_128().hash("fast hash");
  ```
- **Signature:** `HashCode hash(CharSequence input, Charset charset) throws NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Computes the hash code for a character sequence using the specified character encoding.
- **Contract:**
  - This method is useful for cross-language compatibility as it produces consistent results when the same encoding is used.
- **Parameters:**
  - `input` (`CharSequence`) — the character sequence to hash
  - `charset` (`Charset`) — the character encoding to use
- **Returns:** the hash code for the encoded input
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `input` or `charset` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String text = "Hello 世界";
    HashCode hash = Hashing.sha256().hash(text, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
  ```
- **Signature:** `<T> HashCode hash(T instance, Funnel<? super T> funnel) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Computes the hash code for an arbitrary object using a Guava Funnel to decompose the object into primitive values.
- **Contract:**
  - The funnel receives a Guava `PrimitiveSink` and should call Guava sink methods such as `putString`, `putInt`, and `putLong` (not the abacus Hasher#put overloads).
- **Parameters:**
  - `instance` (`T`) — the object instance to hash; may be `null` if the funnel accepts `null` (it is passed to the funnel unchecked)
  - `funnel` (`Funnel<? super T>`) — the funnel used to decompose the object into primitive values
- **Returns:** the hash code for the object
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `funnel` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  class Person {
        String name;
        int age;
  
        Person(String name, int age) {
            this.name = name;
            this.age = age;
        }
    }
  
    Funnel<Person> personFunnel = (person, into) -> {
        into.putString(person.name, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
            .putInt(person.age);
    };
  
    Person person = new Person("Alice", 30);
    HashCode hash = Hashing.sha256().hash(person, personFunnel);
  ```
##### bits(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `int bits()`
- **Summary:** Returns the number of bits in each hash code produced by this hash function.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the number of bits in hash codes produced by this function (always positive and typically a multiple of 32)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HashFunction sha256 = Hashing.sha256();
    System.out.println(sha256.bits());   // prints: 256
  ```

### Interface Hasher (com.landawn.abacus.guava.hash.Hasher)
A stateful object for computing hash codes incrementally.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### put(...) -> Hasher
- **Signature:** `Hasher put(byte b)`
- **Summary:** Adds a single byte to this hasher's internal state.
- **Parameters:**
  - `b` (`byte`) — the byte value to add to the hash computation
- **Returns:** this hasher instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  hasher.put((byte) 0xFF).put((byte) 0x00);
  ```
- **Signature:** `Hasher put(byte[] bytes) throws NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Adds all bytes in the given array to this hasher's internal state.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bytes` (`byte[]`) — the byte array containing data to add to the hash computation; must not be `null`
- **Returns:** this hasher instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `bytes` is `null`. Note the deliberate asymmetry with #put(char\[\]) just below, which documents a `null` array as empty.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  byte[] data = "Hello".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    hasher.put(data);
  ```
- **Signature:** `Hasher put(byte[] bytes, int off, int len) throws NullPointerException, IndexOutOfBoundsException`
- **Summary:** Adds a portion of the given byte array to this hasher's internal state.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bytes` (`byte[]`) — the byte array containing data to add to the hash computation
  - `off` (`int`) — the starting offset in the array (zero-based, inclusive)
  - `len` (`int`) — the number of bytes to process from the array
- **Returns:** this hasher instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `bytes` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `off` or `len` is negative, or if `off + len > bytes.length`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  byte[] buffer = new byte[1024];
    int bytesRead = inputStream.read(buffer);
    if (bytesRead > 0) {
        hasher.put(buffer, 0, bytesRead);
    }
  ```
- **Signature:** `Hasher put(ByteBuffer bytes) throws NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Adds all remaining bytes from the given ByteBuffer to this hasher's internal state.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bytes` (`ByteBuffer`) — the ByteBuffer containing data to add to the hash computation
- **Returns:** this hasher instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `bytes` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ByteBuffer buffer = ByteBuffer.wrap("data".getBytes());
    hasher.put(buffer);   // position is now at the buffer's limit
  ```
- **Signature:** `Hasher put(short s)`
- **Summary:** Adds a short value to this hasher's internal state.
- **Parameters:**
  - `s` (`short`) — the short value to add to the hash computation (interpreted in little-endian byte order)
- **Returns:** this hasher instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**

- **Signature:** `Hasher put(int i)`
- **Summary:** Adds an integer value to this hasher's internal state.
- **Parameters:**
  - `i` (`int`) — the integer value to add to the hash computation (interpreted in little-endian byte order)
- **Returns:** this hasher instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  hasher.put(42).put(Integer.MAX_VALUE);
  ```
- **Signature:** `Hasher put(long l)`
- **Summary:** Adds a long value to this hasher's internal state.
- **Parameters:**
  - `l` (`long`) — the long value to add to the hash computation (interpreted in little-endian byte order)
- **Returns:** this hasher instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**

- **Summary:** Adds a float value to this hasher's internal state.
- **Parameters:**

- **Returns:** this hasher instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**

- **Signature:** `Hasher put(double d)`
- **Summary:** Adds a double value to this hasher's internal state.
- **Parameters:**
  - `d` (`double`) — the double value to add to the hash computation (using its raw binary representation)
- **Returns:** this hasher instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**

- **Signature:** `Hasher put(boolean b)`
- **Summary:** Adds a boolean value to this hasher's internal state.
- **Parameters:**
  - `b` (`boolean`) — the boolean value to add to the hash computation (true=1, false=0)
- **Returns:** this hasher instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**

- **Signature:** `Hasher put(char c)`
- **Summary:** Adds a character value to this hasher's internal state.
- **Parameters:**
  - `c` (`char`) — the character value to add to the hash computation (interpreted in little-endian byte order)
- **Returns:** this hasher instance for method chaining

- **Signature:** `Hasher put(char[] chars)`
- **Summary:** Adds all characters from the given array to this hasher's internal state.

- **Returns:** this hasher instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**

  ```java
    hasher.put(password);
  ```
- **Signature:** `Hasher put(char[] chars, int off, int len) throws IllegalArgumentException, IndexOutOfBoundsException`
- **Summary:** Adds a portion of the given character array to this hasher's internal state.

  - `off` (`int`) — the starting offset in the array (zero-based, inclusive)
  - `len` (`int`) — the number of characters to process from the array
- **Returns:** this hasher instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `len` is negative.
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `off` is negative or the requested range exceeds the array length, treating a `null` array as empty.
- **Examples:**

  ```java
  char[] buffer = new char[100];
    int charsRead = reader.read(buffer);
    if (charsRead > 0) {

    }
  ```

- **Signature:** `Hasher put(CharSequence charSequence) throws NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Adds all characters from the given CharSequence to this hasher's internal state without performing any character encoding.
- **Contract:**
  - This method is faster than #put(CharSequence, Charset) and produces consistent results across Java versions, but the output will differ from most other programming languages when hashing the same string.
- **Parameters:**
  - `charSequence` (`CharSequence`) — the character sequence to add to the hash computation (String, StringBuilder, etc.)
- **Returns:** this hasher instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `charSequence` is `null`
- **Examples:**

  ```java
  hasher.put("fast hash").put(new StringBuilder("builder"));
  ```
- **Signature:** `Hasher put(CharSequence charSequence, Charset charset) throws NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Adds the given CharSequence to this hasher's internal state after encoding it using the specified charset.
- **Contract:**
  - This method is useful for cross-language compatibility as it produces the same hash values as other languages when using the same character encoding.
  - Use the unencoded version for better performance when cross-language compatibility is not required.
  - Chunked calls equal one call over the concatenation only when the encoding has no per-call state and chunk boundaries do not split surrogate pairs.
- **Parameters:**
  - `charSequence` (`CharSequence`) — the character sequence to encode and add to the hash computation
  - `charset` (`Charset`) — the character encoding to use for converting the sequence to bytes
- **Returns:** this hasher instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `charSequence` or `charset` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  hasher.put("Hello 世界", StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
          .put("Здравствуй", StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
  ```
- **Signature:** `<T> Hasher put(T instance, Funnel<? super T> funnel) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Adds an arbitrary object to this hasher's internal state using a Guava Funnel to decompose the object into primitive values.
- **Contract:**
  - The funnel receives a Guava `PrimitiveSink` (not this abacus `Hasher`) and should therefore call Guava sink methods such as `putString`, `putInt`, and `putLong`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `instance` (`T`) — the object instance to add to the hash computation; may be `null` if the funnel accepts `null` (it is passed to the funnel unchecked)
  - `funnel` (`Funnel<? super T>`) — the funnel used to decompose the object into primitive values
- **Returns:** this hasher instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `funnel` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  class Person {
        String name;
        int age;
        long id;
        Person(String name, int age, long id) {
            this.name = name;
            this.age = age;
            this.id = id;
        }
    }
  
    Funnel<Person> personFunnel = (person, into) -> {
        into.putString(person.name, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
            .putInt(person.age)
            .putLong(person.id);
    };
  
    Person person = new Person("Alice", 30, 12345L);
    hasher.put(person, personFunnel);
  ```
##### hash(...) -> HashCode
- **Signature:** `HashCode hash()`
- **Summary:** Computes and returns the final hash code based on all data that has been added to this hasher.
- **Contract:**
  - After calling this method, the hasher instance should not be used again.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the computed hash code
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  long timestamp = System.currentTimeMillis();
    HashCode result = hasher
        .put("data", StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
        .put(timestamp)
        .hash();
  
    byte[] hashBytes = result.asBytes();
    String hashHex = result.toString();
  ```

### Class Hashing (com.landawn.abacus.guava.hash.Hashing)
Utility class providing static factory methods to obtain various HashFunction instances and other hashing-related utilities.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### goodFastHash(...) -> HashFunction
- **Signature:** `public static HashFunction goodFastHash(final int minimumBits) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a general-purpose, temporary-use, non-cryptographic hash function that produces hash codes of at least the specified number of bits.
- **Contract:**
  - The returned function is suitable for in-memory data structures but should not be used for persistent storage or cross-process communication.
  - Warning: Do not use this method if hash codes may escape the current process in any way (e.g., being sent over RPC or saved to disk).
  - When to Use goodFastHash() vs.
- **Parameters:**
  - `minimumBits` (`int`) — a positive integer specifying the minimum number of bits the hash code should have (the actual number of bits may be higher; currently 32 bits, or the next multiple of 128 bits). Must not exceed `Integer.MAX_VALUE - 127`, the largest value whose rounding to a multiple of 128 still fits in an `int`.
- **Returns:** a hash function that produces hash codes of length `minimumBits` or greater
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `minimumBits` is not positive or is greater than `Integer.MAX_VALUE - 127`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // For temporary in-memory use
    HashFunction hashFunc = Hashing.goodFastHash(128);
    HashCode hash = hashFunc.hash("data".getBytes());
  
    // For persistent use, choose a specific algorithm instead:
    HashFunction persistentHash = Hashing.murmur3_128();
    HashCode stableHash = persistentHash.hash("data".getBytes());
  ```
- **See also:** #murmur3_128(), #murmur3_32(), #sha256(), #sipHash24(long, long)
##### murmur3_32(...) -> HashFunction
- **Signature:** `public static HashFunction murmur3_32(final int seed)`
- **Summary:** Returns a hash function implementing the 32-bit Murmur3 algorithm (x86 variant) with the specified seed value.
- **Contract:**
  - This method returns the fixed version that corrects a bug in Guava's earlier `murmur3_32` implementation (which produced incorrect results for strings containing supplementary Unicode characters when hashing text as UTF-8), hence the internal name `murmur3_32_fixed`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `seed` (`int`) — the seed value to initialize the hash function (different seeds produce different hash values for the same input)
- **Returns:** a Murmur3 32-bit hash function initialized with the given seed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HashFunction murmur = Hashing.murmur3_32(42);   // seed is 42
    HashCode hash = murmur.hash("example".getBytes());
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static HashFunction murmur3_32()`
- **Summary:** Returns a hash function implementing the 32-bit Murmur3 algorithm (x86 variant) with a seed value of zero.
- **Contract:**
  - This is a convenient method for when you don't need a specific seed value.
  - Like #murmur3_32(int), this method returns the fixed version that corrects a bug in Guava's earlier `murmur3_32` implementation (incorrect results for strings containing supplementary Unicode characters when hashing text as UTF-8); if you relied on the affected old hash values, migration is required.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a Murmur3 32-bit hash function with seed value 0
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HashCode hash = Hashing.murmur3_32().hash("data".getBytes());
  ```
- **See also:** #murmur3_32(int)

##### hmacMd5(...) -> HashFunction
- **Signature:** `public static HashFunction hmacMd5(final Key key) throws IllegalArgumentException, NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Returns a hash function implementing the HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code) algorithm using MD5 as the underlying hash function (128 hash bits).
- **Parameters:**
  - `key` (`Key`) — the secret key for HMAC computation
- **Returns:** a hash function implementing HMAC-MD5 with the given key
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the given key is inappropriate for initializing this MAC (e.g., a key that is not a raw secret key, such as an RSA public key). Note that the key's algorithm name is not checked against the MAC algorithm, so a `SecretKeySpec` labelled `"HmacSHA256"` is accepted by this method and yields the same MAC as #hmacMd5(byte\[\]) over its raw bytes.
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `key` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Key secretKey = new SecretKeySpec("secret".getBytes(), "HmacMD5");
    HashFunction hmac = Hashing.hmacMd5(secretKey);
    HashCode mac = hmac.hash("message".getBytes());
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static HashFunction hmacMd5(final byte[] key) throws IllegalArgumentException, NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Returns a hash function implementing HMAC-MD5 using a javax.crypto.spec.SecretKeySpec created from the given byte array.
- **Parameters:**
  - `key` (`byte[]`) — the key material for the secret key as a byte array
- **Returns:** a hash function implementing HMAC-MD5 with a key created from the given bytes
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `key` is empty.
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `key` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  byte[] keyBytes = "secret key".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    HashFunction hmac = Hashing.hmacMd5(keyBytes);
    HashCode mac = hmac.hash("message".getBytes());
  ```

##### concatenating(...) -> HashFunction
- **Signature:** `public static HashFunction concatenating(final HashFunction first, final HashFunction second) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a hash function that computes its hash code by concatenating the hash codes of two underlying hash functions.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful when you need a hash code of a specific length that is not directly available.
  - Concatenate different functions (or the same algorithm with different seeds) if the added width is meant to carry added information.
- **Parameters:**
  - `first` (`HashFunction`) — the first hash function
  - `second` (`HashFunction`) — the second hash function
- **Returns:** a hash function that concatenates the results of the two input functions
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if either function is `null` or is not a `HashFunction` obtained from the factory methods of this class.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // 768 bits from two different algorithms
    HashFunction hash768 = Hashing.concatenating(
        Hashing.sha256(),
        Hashing.sha512()
    );
  ```
- **See also:** #concatenating(Iterable)
- **Signature:** `public static HashFunction concatenating(final HashFunction first, final HashFunction second, final HashFunction third) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a hash function that computes its hash code by concatenating the hash codes of three underlying hash functions.
- **Parameters:**
  - `first` (`HashFunction`) — the first hash function
  - `second` (`HashFunction`) — the second hash function
  - `third` (`HashFunction`) — the third hash function
- **Returns:** a hash function that concatenates the results of the three input functions
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any function is `null` or is not a `HashFunction` obtained from the factory methods of this class.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Create a 384-bit hash by combining three 128-bit functions
    HashFunction hash384 = Hashing.concatenating(
        Hashing.murmur3_128(),
        Hashing.murmur3_128(42),
        Hashing.murmur3_128(123)
    );
  ```
- **See also:** #concatenating(Iterable)
- **Signature:** `public static HashFunction concatenating(final Iterable<HashFunction> hashFunctions) throws NullPointerException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a hash function that computes its hash code by concatenating the hash codes of the underlying hash functions in the provided iterable.
- **Parameters:**
  - `hashFunctions` (`Iterable<HashFunction>`) — an iterable of hash functions to concatenate (must not be empty)
- **Returns:** a hash function that concatenates the results of all input functions
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `hashFunctions` itself is `null` (a `null` element is an `IllegalArgumentException`, see below)
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `hashFunctions` is empty, or if any element is `null` or is not a `HashFunction` obtained from the factory methods of this class.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // 384 bits from three independently seeded Murmur3 functions
    List<HashFunction> functions = Arrays.asList(
        Hashing.murmur3_128(),      // 128 bits
        Hashing.murmur3_128(42),    // 128 bits
        Hashing.murmur3_128(123)    // 128 bits
    );
    HashFunction hash384 = Hashing.concatenating(functions);
  ```
##### combineOrdered(...) -> HashCode
- **Signature:** `public static HashCode combineOrdered(final HashCode first, final HashCode second) throws NullPointerException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Combines two hash codes in an ordered fashion to produce a new hash code with the same bit length as the input hash codes.
- **Parameters:**
  - `first` (`HashCode`) — the first hash code to combine
  - `second` (`HashCode`) — the second hash code to combine
- **Returns:** a hash code combining the input hash codes in order
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if either hash code is `null`
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the hash codes have different bit lengths.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HashCode hash1 = Hashing.sha256().hash("first".getBytes());
    HashCode hash2 = Hashing.sha256().hash("second".getBytes());
    HashCode combined = Hashing.combineOrdered(hash1, hash2);
  ```
- **See also:** #combineOrdered(Iterable)
- **Signature:** `public static HashCode combineOrdered(final HashCode first, final HashCode second, final HashCode third) throws NullPointerException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Combines three hash codes in an ordered fashion to produce a new hash code with the same bit length as the input hash codes.
- **Parameters:**
  - `first` (`HashCode`) — the first hash code to combine
  - `second` (`HashCode`) — the second hash code to combine
  - `third` (`HashCode`) — the third hash code to combine
- **Returns:** a hash code combining the input hash codes in order
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if any hash code is `null`
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the hash codes have different bit lengths.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HashCode hash1 = Hashing.md5().hash("part1".getBytes());
    HashCode hash2 = Hashing.md5().hash("part2".getBytes());
    HashCode hash3 = Hashing.md5().hash("part3".getBytes());
    HashCode combined = Hashing.combineOrdered(hash1, hash2, hash3);
  ```
- **See also:** #combineOrdered(Iterable)
- **Signature:** `public static HashCode combineOrdered(final Iterable<HashCode> hashCodes) throws NullPointerException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a hash code that combines the information from multiple hash codes in an ordered fashion.
- **Contract:**
  - This method is designed such that if two equal hash codes are produced by two calls to this method, it is as likely as possible that each was computed from the same input hash codes in the same order.
- **Parameters:**
  - `hashCodes` (`Iterable<HashCode>`) — an iterable of hash codes to combine
- **Returns:** a hash code combining all input hash codes in order
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `hashCodes` or any of its elements is `null`
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `hashCodes` is empty or if the hash codes do not all have the same bit length.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<HashCode> hashes = new ArrayList<>();
    for (String part : dataParts) {
        hashes.add(Hashing.sha256().hash(part.getBytes()));
    }
    HashCode combined = Hashing.combineOrdered(hashes);
  ```

- **Parameters:**
  - `first` (`HashCode`) — the first hash code to combine
  - `second` (`HashCode`) — the second hash code to combine
  - `third` (`HashCode`) — the third hash code to combine
- **Returns:** a hash code combining the input hash codes without regard to order

  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if any hash code is `null`

- **Signature:** `public static HashCode combineUnordered(final Iterable<HashCode> hashCodes) throws NullPointerException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a hash code that combines the information from multiple hash codes in an unordered fashion.
- **Contract:**
  - This method is designed such that if two equal hash codes are produced by two calls to this method, it is as likely as possible that each was computed from the same set of input hash codes, regardless of order.
- **Parameters:**
  - `hashCodes` (`Iterable<HashCode>`) — an iterable of hash codes to combine
- **Returns:** a hash code combining all input hash codes without regard to order
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `hashCodes` or any of its elements is `null`
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `hashCodes` is empty or if the hash codes do not all have the same bit length.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Set<String> items = new HashSet<>(Arrays.asList("x", "y", "z"));
    List<HashCode> hashes = new ArrayList<>();
    for (String item : items) {
        hashes.add(Hashing.sha256().hash(item.getBytes()));
    }
    HashCode setHash = Hashing.combineUnordered(hashes);
  ```
##### consistentHash(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `public static int consistentHash(final HashCode hashCode, final int buckets) throws NullPointerException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Assigns a "bucket" index in the range `\[0, buckets)` to the given hash code using consistent hashing.
- **Contract:**
  - Specifically, `consistentHash(h, n)` equals: `n - 1`, with approximate probability `1/n` `consistentHash(h, n - 1)`, otherwise (probability `1 - 1/n`) This property makes consistent hashing ideal for distributed systems where you want to minimize redistribution when adding or removing nodes.
  - When the number of buckets increases from n-1 to n, only approximately 1/n of the items need to be remapped.
- **Parameters:**
  - `hashCode` (`HashCode`) — the hash code to assign to a bucket
  - `buckets` (`int`) — the number of buckets available (must be positive)
- **Returns:** a bucket index in the range `\[0, buckets)`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `hashCode` is `null`
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `buckets` is not positive.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HashCode itemHash = Hashing.sha256().hash("user123".getBytes());
    int serverCount = 10;
    int assignedServer = Hashing.consistentHash(itemHash, serverCount);
    // assignedServer will be in range [0, 10)
  ```
- **See also:** Consistent hashing on Wikipedia (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consistent_hashing)
- **Signature:** `public static int consistentHash(final long input, final int buckets) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Assigns a "bucket" index in the range `\[0, buckets)` to the given long value using consistent hashing.
- **Contract:**
  - This method provides the same consistent hashing properties as #consistentHash(HashCode, int), minimizing redistribution when the number of buckets changes.
- **Parameters:**
  - `input` (`long`) — the input value to assign to a bucket
  - `buckets` (`int`) — the number of buckets available (must be positive)
- **Returns:** a bucket index in the range `\[0, buckets)`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `buckets` is not positive.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  long userId = 12345L;
    int shardCount = 100;
    int assignedShard = Hashing.consistentHash(userId, shardCount);
    // assignedShard will consistently map userId to a shard in [0, 100)
  ```
- **See also:** #consistentHash(HashCode, int)

### Class HARUtil (com.landawn.abacus.http.HARUtil)
Utility class for working with HTTP Archive (HAR) files.

##### setThreadLocalHeaderFilter(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static void setThreadLocalHeaderFilter(final BiPredicate<? super String, String> httpHeaderFilterForHARRequest) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets a custom HTTP header filter for HAR request processing.
- **Contract:**
  - The filter is used to determine which headers from the HAR file should be included when replaying requests.
  - The filter receives the header name and value as parameters and should return `true` to include the header or `false` to exclude it.
- **Parameters:**
  - `httpHeaderFilterForHARRequest` (`BiPredicate<? super String, String>`) — the filter to apply to headers; must not be `null`. Use #resetThreadLocalHeaderFilter() to restore the default filter.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `httpHeaderFilterForHARRequest` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Exclude authorization headers when replaying requests
    HARUtil.setThreadLocalHeaderFilter((name, value) ->
        !name.equalsIgnoreCase("Authorization"));
  ```

- **Signature:** `public static void resetThreadLocalHeaderFilter()`
- **Summary:** Resets the HTTP header filter to the default implementation.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)

- **See also:** #setThreadLocalHeaderFilter(BiPredicate)
##### configureCurlLoggingForCurrentThread(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static void configureCurlLoggingForCurrentThread(final boolean logRequest)`
- **Summary:** Enables or disables logging of curl commands for HAR requests.
- **Contract:**
  - When enabled, a curl command equivalent to each HAR request will be logged using the default logger at `INFO` level.
  - HAR files captured from browsers routinely contain credentials and session tokens; avoid enabling this in production or when the log destination is untrusted.
- **Parameters:**
  - `logRequest` (`boolean`) — `true` to enable curl logging, `false` to disable.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HARUtil.configureCurlLoggingForCurrentThread(true);
  ```
- **See also:** #configureCurlLoggingForCurrentThread(boolean, char), #configureCurlLoggingForCurrentThread(boolean, char, Consumer)
- **Signature:** `public static void configureCurlLoggingForCurrentThread(final boolean logRequest, final char quoteChar)`
- **Summary:** Enables or disables logging of curl commands for HAR requests with a custom quote character.
- **Contract:**
  - When enabled, a curl command equivalent to each HAR request will be logged using the default logger at `INFO` level.
  - HAR files captured from browsers routinely contain credentials and session tokens; avoid enabling this in production or when the log destination is untrusted.
- **Parameters:**
  - `logRequest` (`boolean`) — `true` to enable curl logging, `false` to disable.
  - `quoteChar` (`char`) — the character to use for quoting in curl commands (typically `'` or `"`).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HARUtil.configureCurlLoggingForCurrentThread(true, '"');
  ```
- **See also:** #configureCurlLoggingForCurrentThread(boolean), #configureCurlLoggingForCurrentThread(boolean, char, Consumer)
- **Signature:** `public static void configureCurlLoggingForCurrentThread(final boolean logRequest, final char quoteChar, final Consumer<? super String> logHandler) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Enables or disables logging of curl commands for HAR requests with custom settings.
- **Contract:**
  - If your `logHandler` persists or forwards these strings, ensure the destination is trusted.
- **Parameters:**
  - `logRequest` (`boolean`) — `true` to enable curl logging, `false` to disable.
  - `quoteChar` (`char`) — the character to use for quoting in curl commands.
  - `logHandler` (`Consumer<? super String>`) — the consumer that will handle the generated curl command strings; must not be `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `logHandler` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Log curl commands to a file instead of standard logger
    HARUtil.configureCurlLoggingForCurrentThread(true, '"', curl -> {
        try {
            Files.write(Paths.get("curl-commands.txt"),
                    (curl + System.lineSeparator()).getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8),
                    StandardOpenOption.CREATE, StandardOpenOption.APPEND);
        } catch (IOException e) {
            throw new java.io.UncheckedIOException(e);
        }
    });
  ```
- **See also:** #configureCurlLoggingForCurrentThread(boolean), #configureCurlLoggingForCurrentThread(boolean, char)
##### resetCurlLoggingForCurrentThread(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static void resetCurlLoggingForCurrentThread()`
- **Summary:** Resets curl logging for the current thread back to the default (logging disabled, single-quote style, default log handler).
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HARUtil.configureCurlLoggingForCurrentThread(true);
    try {
        String response = HARUtil.sendRequest(
            new File("capture.har"),
            "http://localhost:18080/data"
        );
    } finally {
        HARUtil.resetCurlLoggingForCurrentThread();
    }
  ```
- **See also:** #configureCurlLoggingForCurrentThread(boolean), #configureCurlLoggingForCurrentThread(boolean, char), #configureCurlLoggingForCurrentThread(boolean, char, Consumer)
##### sendRequest(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `public static String sendRequest(final File har, final String targetUrl) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException, ParsingException, UnsupportedOperationException, NoSuchElementException`
- **Summary:** Sends an HTTP request extracted from a HAR file for the specified target URL.
- **Parameters:**
  - `har` (`File`) — the HAR file containing captured HTTP requests.
  - `targetUrl` (`String`) — the exact URL to match in the HAR file.
- **Returns:** the response body as a string.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `har` is `null`, the HAR content contains no entries under `log.entries`, or the matching entry cannot be replayed (see #sendRequestByRequestEntry(Map, Class))
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if the HAR file cannot be read or an I/O error occurs while replaying a matching request
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if the HAR content cannot be parsed as a JSON object
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if a matching entry's method is `PATCH` or `CONNECT` (see HttpMethod#PATCH and HttpMethod#CONNECT)
  - `java.util.NoSuchElementException` — if no request entry matches `targetUrl`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String response = HARUtil.sendRequest(
        new File("capture.har"),
        "http://localhost:18080/users/123"
    );
  ```
- **See also:** HAR Viewer (http://www.softwareishard.com/har/viewer/), Generating HAR files (https://confluence.atlassian.com/kb/generating-har-files-and-analyzing-web-requests-720420612.html)
- **Signature:** `public static String sendRequest(final File har, final Predicate<? super String> filterForTargetUrl) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException, ParsingException, UnsupportedOperationException, NoSuchElementException`
- **Summary:** Sends an HTTP request extracted from a HAR file for URLs matching the given filter.
- **Parameters:**
  - `har` (`File`) — the HAR file containing captured HTTP requests.
  - `filterForTargetUrl` (`Predicate<? super String>`) — predicate to test URLs; the first matching URL's request will be sent.
- **Returns:** the response body as a string.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `har` is `null`, `filterForTargetUrl` is `null`, the HAR content contains no entries under `log.entries`, or the matching entry cannot be replayed (see #sendRequestByRequestEntry(Map, Class))
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if the HAR file cannot be read or an I/O error occurs while replaying a matching request
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if the HAR content cannot be parsed as a JSON object
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if a matching entry's method is `PATCH` or `CONNECT` (see HttpMethod#PATCH and HttpMethod#CONNECT)
  - `java.util.NoSuchElementException` — if no request entry matches `filterForTargetUrl`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Send request for first URL containing "/api/users"
    String response = HARUtil.sendRequest(
        new File("capture.har"),
        url -> url.contains("/api/users")
    );
  ```
- **See also:** HAR Viewer (http://www.softwareishard.com/har/viewer/), Generating HAR files (https://confluence.atlassian.com/kb/generating-har-files-and-analyzing-web-requests-720420612.html)

##### streamRequests(...) -> Stream<Tuple2<Map<String, Object>, HttpResponse>>
- **Signature:** `public static Stream<Tuple2<Map<String, Object>, HttpResponse>> streamRequests(final File har, final Predicate<? super String> filterForTargetUrl) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException, ParsingException`
- **Summary:** Creates a stream of HTTP requests and their responses from a HAR file.
- **Parameters:**
  - `har` (`File`) — the HAR file containing captured HTTP requests.
  - `filterForTargetUrl` (`Predicate<? super String>`) — predicate to test URLs; only matching URLs will be included in the stream.
- **Returns:** a stream of tuples where the first element is the request entry map and the second is the `HttpResponse`; an empty stream if the HAR has no entries or none of them match
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `har` or `filterForTargetUrl` is `null`
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if the HAR file cannot be read
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if the HAR content cannot be parsed as a JSON object
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HARUtil.streamRequests(harFile, url -> url.contains("/api/"))
        .forEach(tuple -> {
            Map<String, Object> request = tuple._1;
            com.landawn.abacus.http.HttpResponse response = tuple._2;
            System.out.println("URL: " + request.get("url"));
            System.out.println("Status: " + response.statusCode());
        });
  ```
- **See also:** HAR Viewer (http://www.softwareishard.com/har/viewer/), Generating HAR files (https://confluence.atlassian.com/kb/generating-har-files-and-analyzing-web-requests-720420612.html)
- **Signature:** `public static Stream<Tuple2<Map<String, Object>, HttpResponse>> streamRequests(final String har, final Predicate<? super String> filterForTargetUrl) throws IllegalArgumentException, ParsingException`
- **Summary:** Creates a stream of HTTP requests and their responses from a HAR string.
- **Contract:**
  - Request replay remains lazy: matching requests are only sent when the returned stream is consumed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `har` (`String`) — the HAR content as a JSON string.
  - `filterForTargetUrl` (`Predicate<? super String>`) — predicate to test URLs; only matching URLs will be included in the stream.
- **Returns:** a stream of tuples where the first element is the request entry map and the second is the `HttpResponse`; an empty stream if the HAR has no entries under `log.entries` or none of them match
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `har` or `filterForTargetUrl` is `null`
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if the HAR content cannot be parsed as a JSON object
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HARUtil.streamRequests(harContent, url -> url.contains("/api/"))
        .map(tp -> tp._2.statusCode())
        .forEach(System.out::println);
  ```
- **See also:** HAR Viewer (http://www.softwareishard.com/har/viewer/), Generating HAR files (https://confluence.atlassian.com/kb/generating-har-files-and-analyzing-web-requests-720420612.html)
##### sendRequestByRequestEntry(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T sendRequestByRequestEntry(final Map<String, Object> requestEntry, final Class<T> responseClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, ClassCastException, UnsupportedOperationException, UncheckedIOException`
- **Summary:** Sends an HTTP request based on a HAR request entry.
- **Contract:**
  - The method will: Extract URL, HTTP method, headers from the request entry Apply the configured header filter to include/exclude headers Extract request body and MIME type if present Log curl command if logging is enabled Send the HTTP request and return the response Usage Examples: Among supported methods, the body is attached for `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, and `OPTIONS`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `requestEntry` (`Map<String, Object>`) — the HAR request entry map containing request details.
  - `responseClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class to deserialize the response into.
- **Returns:** the response deserialized into the specified type.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `requestEntry` is `null`, has no `method` field, or its value is not a recognized HttpMethod, or the entry carries a non-empty body (`postData.text` or `postData.params`) but its method is none of `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS`, `PATCH`.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if the entry's `url` field is present but is not a `String`
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if the entry's method is `PATCH` or `CONNECT`, which the underlying `java.net.HttpURLConnection` cannot issue (see HttpMethod#PATCH and HttpMethod#CONNECT).
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if the HTTP request execution fails with an I/O error.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Object> requestEntry = new HashMap<>();
    requestEntry.put("url", "http://localhost:18080/users");
    requestEntry.put("method", "GET");
    HttpResponse response = HARUtil.sendRequestByRequestEntry(requestEntry, HttpResponse.class);
    // returns the HttpResponse from replaying the HAR entry (when executed against a live server)
  ```
##### findRequestEntry(...) -> Optional<Map<String, Object>>
- **Signature:** `public static Optional<Map<String, Object>> findRequestEntry(final File har, final Predicate<? super String> filterForTargetUrl) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException, ParsingException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves a request entry from a HAR file based on URL filtering.
- **Parameters:**
  - `har` (`File`) — the HAR file containing captured HTTP requests.
  - `filterForTargetUrl` (`Predicate<? super String>`) — predicate to test URLs.
- **Returns:** an `Optional` containing the first matching request entry map, or empty if no match is found.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `har` or `filterForTargetUrl` is `null`.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if the HAR file cannot be read.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if the HAR content cannot be parsed as a JSON object
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  com.landawn.abacus.util.u.Optional<Map<String, Object>> requestOpt = HARUtil.findRequestEntry(
        new File("capture.har"),
        url -> url.contains("/api/users")
    );
  
    requestOpt.ifPresent(request -> {
        String url = HARUtil.getRequestUrl(request);
        HttpMethod method = HARUtil.getHttpMethodByRequestEntry(request);
        com.landawn.abacus.http.HttpHeaders headers = HARUtil.getHeadersByRequestEntry(request);
        System.out.println("Found request: " + method + " " + url);
    });
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static Optional<Map<String, Object>> findRequestEntry(final String har, final Predicate<? super String> filterForTargetUrl) throws IllegalArgumentException, ParsingException`

- **Parameters:**
  - `har` (`String`) — the HAR content as a JSON string.
  - `filterForTargetUrl` (`Predicate<? super String>`) — predicate to test URLs.
- **Returns:** an `Optional` containing the first matching request entry map, or empty if no match is found.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `har` or `filterForTargetUrl` is `null`.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if the HAR content cannot be parsed as a JSON object
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  com.landawn.abacus.util.u.Optional<Map<String, Object>> requestOpt = HARUtil.findRequestEntry(
        harContent,
        url -> url.endsWith("/login")
    );
  
    requestOpt.ifPresent(request -> {
        String method = HARUtil.getHttpMethodByRequestEntry(request).name();
        com.landawn.abacus.http.HttpHeaders headers = HARUtil.getHeadersByRequestEntry(request);
        System.out.println("Method: " + method);
        headers.forEach((name, value) -> System.out.println(name + ": " + value));
    });
  ```

- **Parameters:**
  - `requestEntry` (`Map<String, Object>`) — the HAR request entry map containing a "headers" array.
- **Returns:** a new `HttpHeaders` object containing the filtered headers; empty (never `null`) if the `headers` field is absent or null, or nothing passes the filter
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `requestEntry` is `null`, the headers container or entries are malformed, or included repeated headers cannot be combined without changing their semantics
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpHeaders headers = HARUtil.getHeadersByRequestEntry(requestEntry);
    String contentType = (String) headers.get(HttpHeaders.Names.CONTENT_TYPE);
  ```
- **See also:** #setThreadLocalHeaderFilter(BiPredicate)
##### getBodyAndMimeTypeByRequestEntry(...) -> Tuple2<String, String>
- **Signature:** `public static Tuple2<String, String> getBodyAndMimeTypeByRequestEntry(final Map<String, Object> requestEntry)`
- **Summary:** Extracts the request body and MIME type from a HAR request entry.
- **Contract:**
  - If `postData.text` is absent or empty and HAR `postData.params` are present, the params are encoded as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` form data.
  - Because the synthesized bytes are URL-encoded, the returned MIME type is also `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, even if a different (for example multipart) MIME type was recorded without its original body text.
- **Parameters:**
  - `requestEntry` (`Map<String, Object>`) — the HAR request entry map. A `null` entry is treated as having no `postData` and yields a tuple of `null` body and `null` MIME type.
- **Returns:** a tuple where the first element is the request body text (may be `null` if the request has no body) and the second element is the MIME type (may be `null` if no MIME type is present).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Tuple2<String, String> bodyAndType = HARUtil.getBodyAndMimeTypeByRequestEntry(requestEntry);
    String requestBody = bodyAndType._1;  // {"user":"john","pass":"secret"}, for example
    String mimeType = bodyAndType._2;     // "application/json", for example
  ```

### Class HttpClient (com.landawn.abacus.http.HttpClient)
A thread-safe HTTP client built on HttpURLConnection, with automatic serialization of request bodies, automatic deserialization of responses, optional compression, SSL/TLS and proxy configuration, and asynchronous execution through ContinuableFuture.

**Thread-safety:** thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified

- **Signature:** `public static HttpClient create(final String url, final int maxConnection, final long connectTimeoutInMillis, final long readTimeoutInMillis, final HttpSettings settings, final AtomicInteger sharedActiveConnectionCounter) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException`
- **Summary:** Creates an HttpClient instance with a shared active connection counter.
- **Contract:**
  - Useful when you need to enforce a global connection limit across multiple HTTP endpoints.
- **Parameters:**
  - `url` (`String`) — The base URL for the HTTP client
  - `maxConnection` (`int`) — Maximum number of concurrent in-flight requests for this client; `0` selects #DEFAULT_MAX_CONNECTION. This is not a connection-pool size: a request that would exceed it fails immediately with a RejectedExecutionException
  - `connectTimeoutInMillis` (`long`) — Connection timeout in milliseconds; `0` selects #DEFAULT_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT (it does not mean "no timeout")
  - `readTimeoutInMillis` (`long`) — Read timeout in milliseconds; `0` selects #DEFAULT_READ_TIMEOUT (it does not mean "no timeout")
  - `settings` (`HttpSettings`) — Additional HTTP settings
  - `sharedActiveConnectionCounter` (`AtomicInteger`) — Shared counter for active connections across multiple HttpClient instances; must not be `null`
- **Returns:** A new HttpClient instance
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `url` is `null`, empty, relative, or has malformed URI syntax, or its recognized protocol is neither HTTP nor HTTPS, or a supplied connection limit or timeout is negative, or `sharedActiveConnectionCounter` is `null`.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if converting the URL text to a URL fails, including when its protocol has no installed handler
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AtomicInteger sharedCounter = new AtomicInteger(0);
    HttpClient client1 = HttpClient.create("http://localhost:18080/api1", 10, 5000, 10000, null, sharedCounter);
    HttpClient client2 = HttpClient.create("http://localhost:18080/api2", 10, 5000, 10000, null, sharedCounter);
    // Both clients share a maximum of 10 concurrent connections total
  ```

#### Public Instance Methods
##### url(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `public String url()`
- **Summary:** Gets the base URL configured for this HTTP client.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** The base URL as a string
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpClient client = HttpClient.create("http://localhost:18080");
    String baseUrl = client.url();
  ```
##### get(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public String get() throws RejectedExecutionException, UncheckedIOException, HttpResponseException`
- **Summary:** Performs a GET request and returns the response as a String.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** The response body as a String
- **Throws:**
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if this client already has `maxConnection` requests in flight
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if opening the connection, transmitting the request, or reading or writing the response fails
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.HttpResponseException` — if the response status code is not 2xx

##### execute(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public String execute(final HttpMethod httpMethod, final Object request) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException, RejectedExecutionException, UncheckedIOException, HttpResponseException`
- **Summary:** Executes an HTTP request with the specified method and request body.
- **Parameters:**
  - `httpMethod` (`HttpMethod`) — The HTTP method to use
  - `request` (`Object`) — The payload: the request body for POST/PUT/OPTIONS, or query parameters appended to the URL (pre-encoded `String`, `Map` or bean) for every other method. May be `null` for no payload
- **Returns:** The response body as a String
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `httpMethod` is `null`, the payload is routed to the URL and cannot be encoded as a query (a pre-encoded `String` that is not valid URI syntax, or a `Map` with a `null` key), or the effective settings declare a `Content-Encoding` that conflicts with the compression the active content format applies; the in-flight slot is not consumed
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `httpMethod` is HttpMethod#PATCH or HttpMethod#CONNECT, which HttpURLConnection cannot issue
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if this client already has `maxConnection` requests in flight
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if opening the connection, transmitting the request, or reading or writing the response fails
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.HttpResponseException` — if the response status code is not 2xx
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String response = client.execute(HttpMethod.POST, requestBody);
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <T> T execute(final HttpMethod httpMethod, final Object request, final Class<T> resultClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException, RejectedExecutionException, UncheckedIOException, HttpResponseException`
- **Summary:** Executes an HTTP request and deserializes the response to the specified type.
- **Parameters:**
  - `httpMethod` (`HttpMethod`) — The HTTP method to use (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD, etc.)
  - `request` (`Object`) — The payload: the request body for POST/PUT/OPTIONS, or query parameters appended to the URL (pre-encoded `String`, `Map` or bean) for every other method. May be `null` for no payload
  - `resultClass` (`Class<T>`) — The class of the expected response object (for deserialization)
- **Returns:** The deserialized response object
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `httpMethod` is `null`, the payload is routed to the URL and cannot be encoded as a query (a pre-encoded `String` that is not valid URI syntax, or a `Map` with a `null` key), or the effective settings declare a `Content-Encoding` that conflicts with the compression the active content format applies; the in-flight slot is not consumed
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `httpMethod` is HttpMethod#PATCH or HttpMethod#CONNECT, which HttpURLConnection cannot issue
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if this client already has `maxConnection` requests in flight
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if opening the connection, transmitting the request, or reading or writing the response fails
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.HttpResponseException` — if the response status code is not 2xx and `resultClass` is not HttpResponse
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpClient client = HttpClient.create("https://example.com/api/users");
    User user = client.execute(HttpMethod.GET, null, User.class);
    // returns the response deserialized into a User instance (when executed)
  ```

  - `settings` (`HttpSettings`) — Additional HTTP settings for this request (headers, timeouts, etc.)
- **Returns:** The response body as a String
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `httpMethod` is `null`, the payload is routed to the URL and cannot be encoded as a query (a pre-encoded `String` that is not valid URI syntax, or a `Map` with a `null` key), or the effective settings declare a `Content-Encoding` that conflicts with the compression the active content format applies; the in-flight slot is not consumed
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `httpMethod` is HttpMethod#PATCH or HttpMethod#CONNECT, which HttpURLConnection cannot issue
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if this client already has `maxConnection` requests in flight
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if opening the connection, transmitting the request, or reading or writing the response fails
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.HttpResponseException` — if the response status code is not 2xx
- **Examples:**

- **Signature:** `public <T> T execute(final HttpMethod httpMethod, final Object request, final HttpSettings settings, final Class<T> resultClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException, RejectedExecutionException, UncheckedIOException, HttpResponseException`
- **Summary:** Executes an HTTP request with all options and deserializes the response to the specified type.
- **Parameters:**
  - `httpMethod` (`HttpMethod`) — The HTTP method to use (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD, etc.)
  - `request` (`Object`) — The payload: the request body for POST/PUT/OPTIONS, or query parameters appended to the URL (pre-encoded `String`, `Map` or bean) for every other method. May be `null` for no payload
  - `settings` (`HttpSettings`) — Additional HTTP settings for this request (headers, timeouts, etc.)
  - `resultClass` (`Class<T>`) — The class of the expected response object (for deserialization)
- **Returns:** The deserialized response object, or `null` if `resultClass` is `Void` or the effective settings mark the request as one-way (HttpSettings#setOneWayRequest(boolean)) - this applies even when `resultClass` is HttpResponse
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `httpMethod` is `null`, the payload is routed to the URL and cannot be encoded as a query (a pre-encoded `String` that is not valid URI syntax, or a `Map` with a `null` key), or the effective settings declare a `Content-Encoding` that conflicts with the compression the active content format applies; the in-flight slot is not consumed
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `httpMethod` is HttpMethod#PATCH or HttpMethod#CONNECT, which HttpURLConnection cannot issue
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if this client already has `maxConnection` requests in flight
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if opening the connection, transmitting the request, or reading or writing the response fails
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.HttpResponseException` — if the response status code is not 2xx and `resultClass` is not HttpResponse
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpClient client = HttpClient.create("https://example.com/api/users");
    HttpSettings settings = HttpSettings.create().header("Authorization", "Bearer token123");
    User created = client.execute(HttpMethod.POST, new User("John"), settings, User.class);
    // returns the created resource deserialized into a User (when executed)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public void execute(final HttpMethod httpMethod, final Object request, final HttpSettings settings, final File output) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException, RejectedExecutionException, UncheckedIOException, HttpResponseException`
- **Summary:** Executes an HTTP request and writes the response to a file.
- **Parameters:**
  - `httpMethod` (`HttpMethod`) — The HTTP method to use
  - `request` (`Object`) — The payload: the request body for POST/PUT/OPTIONS, or query parameters appended to the URL (pre-encoded `String`, `Map` or bean) for every other method. May be `null` for no payload
  - `settings` (`HttpSettings`) — Additional HTTP settings for this request
  - `output` (`File`) — The file to write the response to. It is created (and an existing file truncated) only once a successful status has been received. Connection or HTTP-status failures leave an existing file untouched; a failure while copying the body can leave a partial file
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `httpMethod` or `output` is `null`, the payload is routed to the URL and cannot be encoded as a query (a pre-encoded `String` that is not valid URI syntax, or a `Map` with a `null` key), or the effective settings declare a `Content-Encoding` that conflicts with the compression the active content format applies
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `httpMethod` is HttpMethod#PATCH or HttpMethod#CONNECT, which HttpURLConnection cannot issue
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if this client already has `maxConnection` requests in flight
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if opening the connection, transmitting the request, or reading or writing the response fails
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.HttpResponseException` — if the response status code is not 2xx
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File outputFile = new File("response.json");
    client.execute(HttpMethod.GET, null, settings, outputFile);
  ```
- **Signature:** `public void execute(final HttpMethod httpMethod, final Object request, final HttpSettings settings, final OutputStream output) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException, RejectedExecutionException, UncheckedIOException, HttpResponseException`
- **Summary:** Executes an HTTP request and writes the response to an output stream.
- **Parameters:**
  - `httpMethod` (`HttpMethod`) — The HTTP method to use (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD, etc.)
  - `request` (`Object`) — The payload: the request body for POST/PUT/OPTIONS, or query parameters appended to the URL (pre-encoded `String`, `Map` or bean) for every other method. May be `null` for no payload
  - `settings` (`HttpSettings`) — Additional HTTP settings for this request (headers, timeouts, etc.)
  - `output` (`OutputStream`) — The output stream to write the response to
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `httpMethod` or `output` is `null`, the payload is routed to the URL and cannot be encoded as a query (a pre-encoded `String` that is not valid URI syntax, or a `Map` with a `null` key), or the effective settings declare a `Content-Encoding` that conflicts with the compression the active content format applies
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `httpMethod` is HttpMethod#PATCH or HttpMethod#CONNECT, which HttpURLConnection cannot issue
  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if this client already has `maxConnection` requests in flight
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if opening the connection, transmitting the request, or reading or writing the response fails
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.HttpResponseException` — if the response status code is not 2xx
- **Examples:**
  ```java

    try (OutputStream out = new FileOutputStream("download.zip")) {
  ```
