  - `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException` — if this client already has `maxConnection` requests in flight
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if opening the connection, transmitting the request, or reading or writing the response fails

##### openConnection(...) -> HttpURLConnection
- **Signature:** `public HttpURLConnection openConnection(final HttpMethod httpMethod, final HttpSettings settings, final boolean doOutput) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException, UncheckedIOException`
- **Summary:** Opens a new HTTP connection with the specified method and settings.
- **Parameters:**
  - `httpMethod` (`HttpMethod`) — The HTTP method to use
  - `settings` (`HttpSettings`) — Additional HTTP settings for the connection
  - `doOutput` (`boolean`) — Whether the connection will send a request body
- **Returns:** A configured HttpURLConnection ready for use
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `httpMethod` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `httpMethod` is HttpMethod#PATCH or HttpMethod#CONNECT, which HttpURLConnection cannot issue
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if creating the connection or configuring its request method fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpURLConnection conn = client.openConnection(HttpMethod.GET, settings, false);
    // Manually configure and use the connection
    conn.connect();
  ```
- **Signature:** `public HttpURLConnection openConnection(final HttpMethod httpMethod, final Object queryParameters, final HttpSettings settings, final boolean doOutput) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException, UncheckedIOException`
- **Summary:** Opens a new HTTP connection with query parameters and the specified settings.
- **Parameters:**
  - `httpMethod` (`HttpMethod`) — The HTTP method to use
  - `queryParameters` (`Object`) — Query parameters appended to this client's URL (a pre-encoded query `String`, a `Map` or a bean), or `null` for none. They are applied for every HTTP method
  - `settings` (`HttpSettings`) — Additional HTTP settings for the connection
  - `doOutput` (`boolean`) — Whether the connection will send a request body
- **Returns:** A configured HttpURLConnection ready for use
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `httpMethod` is `null`, or `queryParameters` cannot be encoded as a query (a pre-encoded `String` that is not valid URI syntax, or a `Map` with a `null` key). The same applies to every `get`/`delete`/`execute` overload that takes query parameters.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `httpMethod` is HttpMethod#PATCH or HttpMethod#CONNECT, which HttpURLConnection cannot issue
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if creating the connection or configuring its request method fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Object> params = Map.of("id", 123);
    HttpURLConnection conn = client.openConnection(HttpMethod.GET, params, settings, false);
  ```

### Class HttpHeaders (com.landawn.abacus.http.HttpHeaders)
A mutable container for HTTP headers with a fluent API for setting and retrieving header values.

**Thread-safety:** not thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified

##### valueOf(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `public static String valueOf(final Object headerValue) throws ArithmeticException`
- **Summary:** Converts a header value to its string representation.
- **Contract:**
  - An array is not a `Collection` and is rendered by `N.stringOf` as a JSON array literal - `new String\[\] {"a", "b"}` becomes `\["a", "b"\]`, which is what would go on the wire - so pass a `Collection` (for example `Arrays.asList(array)`) when a comma-joined value is intended.
  - Not every multiply-valued header field is comma-separated: use #valueOf(String, Object) when the header name is known, so that a field with its own list grammar (such as `Cookie`) is rendered with the separator its grammar requires.
- **Parameters:**
  - `headerValue` (`Object`) — the header value to convert
- **Returns:** the string representation of the header value, or an empty string if `headerValue` is `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if `headerValue` is an Instant whose epoch-millisecond value overflows a `long`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String value = HttpHeaders.valueOf(Arrays.asList("gzip", "br"));   // "gzip, br"
    String date = HttpHeaders.valueOf(new Date());                     // date is formatted as an HTTP date
  ```
- **See also:** #valueOf(String, Object)
- **Signature:** `public static String valueOf(final String headerName, final Object headerValue) throws ArithmeticException`
- **Summary:** Converts a header value to the text of a single header line for the named field.
- **Contract:**
  - This method does not validate whether an arbitrary field permits a list; callers must supply values appropriate for that field.
- **Parameters:**
  - `headerName` (`String`) — the header field name; a `null` name is treated as an ordinary field
  - `headerValue` (`Object`) — the header value to convert
- **Returns:** the text to put on the header line, or an empty string if `headerValue` is `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if `headerValue` is an Instant whose epoch-millisecond value overflows a `long`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpHeaders.valueOf("Accept-Encoding", Arrays.asList("gzip", "br"));   // "gzip, br"
    HttpHeaders.valueOf("Cookie", Arrays.asList("a=1", "b=2"));            // "a=1; b=2"
  ```
- **See also:** #valueOf(Object)

##### setIfAbsent(...) -> HttpHeaders
- **Signature:** `public HttpHeaders setIfAbsent(final String name, final Object value) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException, NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Sets a header only if it is not already present, following Map#putIfAbsent semantics.
- **Contract:**
  - The header is set when there is currently no mapping for the given name or when the name is explicitly mapped to `null`; in both cases such a name is treated as absent and the new value is stored.
  - If the name is already mapped to a non-`null` value, this method does nothing and that existing value is preserved.
- **Parameters:**
  - `name` (`String`) — The header name
  - `value` (`Object`) — The header value (can be a `String`, `Collection`, `Date`, `Instant`, or any object)
- **Returns:** This HttpHeaders instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `name` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if the backing map does not support the requested modification.
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `value` is `null` and the backing map does not permit null values.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  headers.setIfAbsent("User-Agent", "MyApp/1.0");   // set: no existing mapping
    headers.set("X-Trace", (Object) null);
    headers.setIfAbsent("X-Trace", "abc");            // set: previous value was null (treated as absent)
    headers.setIfAbsent("User-Agent", "Other/2.0");   // no-op: already mapped to a non-null value
  ```

##### get(...) -> Object
- **Signature:** `public Object get(final String headerName)`
- **Summary:** Gets the raw stored value of a header.
- **Parameters:**
  - `headerName` (`String`) — The name of the header to retrieve; a `null` name never matches
- **Returns:** The header value, or `null` if not present (or if the header is stored with a `null` value)
- **Examples:**

- **See also:** #getAsString(String)
##### getAsString(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `public String getAsString(final String headerName) throws ArithmeticException`
- **Summary:** Returns the value of a header coerced to its String form via #valueOf(String, Object).
- **Contract:**
  - Unlike #get(String) (which returns the raw stored value), this applies the same coercion used when writing the header to the wire: Collection values are joined with the separator the named field's grammar requires (`"; "` for `Cookie`, `", "` otherwise), Date/Instant values are HTTP-date formatted, and a `null` (absent) header yields `null`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `headerName` (`String`) — The name of the header to retrieve
- **Returns:** The coerced header value, or `null` if the header is not present or is stored with a `null` value
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if the header value is an Instant whose epoch-millisecond value overflows a `long`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  headers.set("Accept-Encoding", Arrays.asList("gzip", "br"));
    String value = headers.getAsString("Accept-Encoding");   // "gzip, br"
  
    headers.set("Cookie", Arrays.asList("a=1", "b=2"));
    String cookie = headers.getAsString("Cookie");           // "a=1; b=2"
  ```
- **See also:** #valueOf(String, Object)

### Class HttpRequest (com.landawn.abacus.http.HttpRequest)
A fluent, builder-style API for building and executing a single HTTP request using HttpClient.

**Thread-safety:** not thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### create(...) -> HttpRequest
- **Signature:** `public static HttpRequest create(final HttpClient httpClient) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates an HttpRequest instance with the specified HttpClient.
- **Contract:**
  - This method is useful when you want to use an existing HttpClient with specific configuration.
- **Parameters:**
  - `httpClient` (`HttpClient`) — The HttpClient to use for the request. Must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a new HttpRequest instance
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `httpClient` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpClient client = HttpClient.create("http://localhost:18080/data");
    HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.create(client);
    // String response = request.get(String.class);  // network call happens here (when executed)
  ```
##### url(...) -> HttpRequest
- **Signature:** `public static HttpRequest url(final String url) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException`
- **Summary:** Creates an HttpRequest for the specified URL with default connection and read timeouts.
- **Parameters:**
  - `url` (`String`) — The target URL for the request
- **Returns:** a new HttpRequest instance
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `url` is `null`, empty, relative, or has malformed URI syntax, or its recognized protocol is neither HTTP nor HTTPS.

- **Examples:**

  - `readTimeoutInMillis` (`long`) — Read timeout in milliseconds

- **Examples:**

##### connectTimeout(...) -> HttpRequest
- **Signature:** `public HttpRequest connectTimeout(final long connectTimeout) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets the connection timeout in milliseconds for this HTTP request.
- **Contract:**
  - The connection timeout defines how long to wait when establishing a connection to the remote server before timing out.
- **Parameters:**
  - `connectTimeout` (`long`) — The connection timeout in milliseconds. Must be non-negative; `0` means "not set", so the client-level default applies.
- **Returns:** This HttpRequest instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `connectTimeout` is negative.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpRequest.url("http://localhost:18080")
        .connectTimeout(5000) // 5 seconds
        .get();
  ```
- **Signature:** `public HttpRequest connectTimeout(final Duration connectTimeout) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets the connection timeout using a Duration.
- **Parameters:**
  - `connectTimeout` (`Duration`) — The connection timeout as a Duration; must not be `null` and must not be negative. Sub-millisecond precision is truncated.
- **Returns:** This HttpRequest instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `connectTimeout` is `null` or negative.
- **Examples:**
  ```java

        .connectTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(5))
        .get();
  ```

### Class HttpResponse (com.landawn.abacus.http.HttpResponse)
Represents an immutable HTTP response containing status code, headers, and body.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### isSuccessful(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public boolean isSuccessful()`
- **Summary:** Checks if the response status code indicates success.
- **Contract:**
  - Returns `true` if the status code is in the range `\[200, 300)`, which means the request was successfully received, understood, and accepted.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** `true` if the response indicates success, `false` otherwise
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpResponse response = client.get(HttpResponse.class);
    if (response.isSuccessful()) {
        // Process successful response
    } else {
        // Handle error
    }
  ```

- **Signature:** `public String requestUrl()`
- **Summary:** Gets the URL of the original request that generated this response.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** The request URL as a string
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpResponse response = client.get(HttpResponse.class);
    String url = response.requestUrl();  // e.g. "http://localhost:18080/users"
  ```
##### requestSentAtMillis(...) -> long
- **Signature:** `public long requestSentAtMillis()`
- **Summary:** Gets the timestamp when the request was sent, in milliseconds since epoch.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** The request sent timestamp in milliseconds
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpResponse response = client.get(HttpResponse.class);
    long sentAt = response.requestSentAtMillis();
    long elapsed = response.responseReceivedAtMillis() - sentAt;  // round-trip time in ms
  ```

- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Deserialize to a list of users
    Type<List<User>> listType = Type.of(new TypeReference<List<User>>() {});
    List<User> users = response.body(listType);
  
    // Deserialize to a map
    Type<Map<String, Object>> mapType = Type.of(new TypeReference<Map<String, Object>>() {});
    Map<String, Object> data = response.body(mapType);
  
    // Alternative: pass the Type inline instead of via a local variable
    List<User> users2 = response.body(Type.of(new TypeReference<List<User>>() {}));
  ```

### Class HttpSettings (com.landawn.abacus.http.HttpSettings)
Configuration settings for HTTP requests.

**Thread-safety:** not thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- `public HttpSettings()` — Creates a new HttpSettings instance with default values.
  ```java
  HttpSettings settings = new HttpSettings();   // all values at their defaults
    settings.setConnectTimeout(5000);             // connect timeout = 5000 ms
    settings.useCaches(false);                    // caching disabled (the default)
  ```

#### Public Static Methods
##### create(...) -> HttpSettings
- **Signature:** `public static HttpSettings create()`
- **Summary:** Creates a new HttpSettings instance with default values.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a new HttpSettings instance
- **Examples:**
  ```java

        .setConnectTimeout(5000)
        .header("Accept", "application/json");
  ```

#### Public Instance Methods
##### getConnectTimeout(...) -> long
- **Signature:** `public long getConnectTimeout()`
- **Summary:** Gets the connection timeout in milliseconds.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the connection timeout in milliseconds, or 0 if not set
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpSettings settings = HttpSettings.create();
    settings.getConnectTimeout();                  // returns 0 (not set yet)
  
    settings.setConnectTimeout(5000);
    settings.getConnectTimeout();                  // returns 5000
  ```
- **See also:** #setConnectTimeout(long)
##### setConnectTimeout(...) -> HttpSettings
- **Signature:** `public HttpSettings setConnectTimeout(final long connectTimeout) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets the connection timeout in milliseconds.
- **Contract:**
  - This timeout begins when the connection attempt starts and expires if the connection cannot be established within the specified time.
  - If the timeout expires before a connection is established, a java.net.SocketTimeoutException will be thrown.
  - Because java.net.HttpURLConnection exposes an `int`-valued timeout, larger positive values are saturated at Integer#MAX_VALUE when the connection is configured.
- **Parameters:**
  - `connectTimeout` (`long`) — the connection timeout in milliseconds (0 = not set; the client-level default applies)
- **Returns:** this HttpSettings instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `connectTimeout` is negative.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Set 5 second connection timeout
    settings.setConnectTimeout(5000);
  
    // Set different timeouts for connection and read operations
    settings.setConnectTimeout(5000)   // 5s to establish connection
            .setReadTimeout(10000);    // 10s to read response
  ```

  - (none)

##### getContentFormat(...) -> ContentFormat
- **Signature:** `public ContentFormat getContentFormat()`

- **See also:** HttpHeaders
- **Signature:** `public HttpSettings headers(final Map<String, ?> headers) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Merges the given header entries into the headers already on this settings object.
- **Contract:**
  - This is a merge, not a replace-all: use #setHeaders(HttpHeaders) if you want to discard all prior headers and install a fresh set.
- **Parameters:**
  - `headers` (`Map<String, ?>`) — a map containing header names and values to merge in; must not be `null`
- **Returns:** this HttpSettings instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `headers` or any key in `headers` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  settings.header("Old", "value");                // pre-existing header
  
    Map<String, String> headers = Map.of(
        "Authorization", "Bearer token123",
        "Accept", "application/json",
        "User-Agent", "MyApp/1.0"
    );
    settings.headers(headers);          // merges the three entries in
    settings.headers().get("Old");      // still "value" (kept, not in the map)
    settings.headers().get("Accept");   // "application/json" (added/overwritten)
  ```
- **See also:** HttpHeaders, #setHeaders(HttpHeaders)
- **Signature:** `@Deprecated public HttpSettings headers(final HttpHeaders headers) throws IllegalArgumentException`

##### setHeaders(...) -> HttpSettings
- **Signature:** `public HttpSettings setHeaders(final HttpHeaders headers) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Resets the headers by removing all existing headers first and then adds the specified headers (replace-all).
- **Parameters:**

- **Returns:** this HttpSettings instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**

### Class HttpUtil (com.landawn.abacus.http.HttpUtil)
Internal utility class for HTTP operations.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified
**Annotations:** @Internal

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### isSuccessfulResponseCode(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean isSuccessfulResponseCode(final int code)`
- **Summary:** Checks if the HTTP response code indicates success.
- **Contract:**
  - A response code is considered successful if it's in the range \[200, 300).
- **Parameters:**
  - `code` (`int`) — The HTTP response code to check
- **Returns:** `true` if the code indicates success, `false` otherwise
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpURLConnection connection = (HttpURLConnection) new URL("http://localhost:18080/users").openConnection();
    if (HttpUtil.isSuccessfulResponseCode(connection.getResponseCode())) {
        // Process successful response
    }
  ```
- **See also:** HttpResponse#isSuccessful()
##### hasResponseBody(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean hasResponseBody(final String requestMethod, final int statusCode)`
- **Summary:** Returns whether a response can contain a message body, independently of its representation headers.
- **Parameters:**
  - `requestMethod` (`String`) — the request method, or `null` if unknown
  - `statusCode` (`int`) — the response status code
- **Returns:** `false` for HEAD, informational, 204, 205, and 304 responses, and successful CONNECT responses
##### isValidHttpHeader(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean isValidHttpHeader(final String key, final String value)`
- **Summary:** Validates an HTTP header key-value pair.
- **Contract:**
  - Obsolete line folding (`CRLF SP/HTAB`) is rejected: RFC 7230 allows recipients to interpret legacy folded fields, but senders must not generate them.
- **Parameters:**
  - `key` (`String`) — The header key to validate
  - `value` (`String`) — The header value to validate
- **Returns:** `true` if the header is valid, `false` otherwise
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Valid headers
    boolean valid1 = HttpUtil.isValidHttpHeader("Content-Type", "application/json");       // true
    boolean valid2 = HttpUtil.isValidHttpHeader("Authorization", "Bearer token123");       // true
  
    // Invalid headers
    boolean invalid1 = HttpUtil.isValidHttpHeader("", "value");                            // false (empty key)
    boolean invalid2 = HttpUtil.isValidHttpHeader("Key:Name", "value");                    // false (contains colon)
    boolean invalid3 = HttpUtil.isValidHttpHeader("Key\nName", "value");                   // false (contains line separator)
    boolean invalid4 = HttpUtil.isValidHttpHeader("Key", "value\nwithout continuation");   // false (unescaped newline)
  ```
##### readHttpHeaderValue(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull public static String readHttpHeaderValue(final Object value)`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Reads an HTTP header value from various object types.
- **Contract:**
  - Arrays are not joined: they fall through to `N.stringOf` and render as a JSON array literal such as `\["a", "b"\]` - pass a `Collection` when a comma-joined header value is wanted.
  - Use HttpHeaders#valueOf(String, Object) instead when the header name is known and the field may have a list grammar of its own, such as `Cookie`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `value` (`Object`) — The header value (can be `null`, String, Collection, or any object)
- **Returns:** The header value as a string, or `null` if value is null (may return null)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Single value
    String header1 = HttpUtil.readHttpHeaderValue("text/plain");
  
    // Multiple values
    List<String> values = Arrays.asList("gzip", "deflate");

  ```

##### getContentFormat(...) -> ContentFormat
- **Signature:** `public static ContentFormat getContentFormat(String contentType, String contentEncoding)`
- **Summary:** Determines the ContentFormat from content type and encoding strings.
- **Contract:**
  - Do not advertise such codings in `Accept-Encoding` when the response is to be deserialized by this library; see HttpSettings#setContentEncoding(String) for the request-side counterpart.
- **Parameters:**
  - `contentType` (`String`) — The content type (e.g., "application/json")
  - `contentEncoding` (`String`) — The content encoding (e.g., "gzip")
- **Returns:** The matching ContentFormat, or ContentFormat.NONE if no match is found
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ContentFormat format = HttpUtil.getContentFormat("application/json", "gzip");
    // Returns ContentFormat.JSON_GZIP
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static ContentFormat getContentFormat(final HttpURLConnection connection) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Gets the ContentFormat from an HttpURLConnection.
- **Parameters:**
  - `connection` (`HttpURLConnection`) — The HTTP connection
- **Returns:** The ContentFormat, or ContentFormat.NONE if not determined
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `connection` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpURLConnection conn = (HttpURLConnection) new URL("http://example.com/api").openConnection();
    conn.connect();
    ContentFormat format = HttpUtil.getContentFormat(conn);
    // For a "Content-Type: application/json" + "Content-Encoding: gzip" response,
    // returns ContentFormat.JSON_GZIP (when executed against a live server)
  ```
##### getResponseContentFormat(...) -> ContentFormat
- **Signature:** `public static ContentFormat getResponseContentFormat(final Map<String, ?> respHeaders, final ContentFormat requestContentFormat)`
- **Summary:** Gets the response ContentFormat based on response headers and request format.
- **Contract:**
  - If the response doesn't specify a Content-Type, falls back to the request format's content type.
- **Parameters:**
  - `respHeaders` (`Map<String, ?>`) — The response headers
  - `requestContentFormat` (`ContentFormat`) — The request content format (used only as a content-type fallback, may be `null`)
- **Returns:** The response ContentFormat, or ContentFormat#NONE if neither could be determined
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, String> respHeaders = new HashMap<>();
    respHeaders.put("Content-Type", "application/json");
    respHeaders.put("Content-Encoding", "gzip");
    ContentFormat format = HttpUtil.getResponseContentFormat(respHeaders, null);
    // returns ContentFormat.JSON_GZIP
  
    // When the response omits Content-Type, the request format supplies it as a fallback:
    ContentFormat fallback = HttpUtil.getResponseContentFormat(new HashMap<>(), ContentFormat.XML);
    // returns ContentFormat.XML
  ```

##### wrapInputStream(...) -> InputStream
- **Signature:** `public static InputStream wrapInputStream(final InputStream is, final ContentFormat contentFormat) throws UncheckedIOException`
- **Summary:** Wraps an input stream with decompression based on the content format.
- **Parameters:**
  - `is` (`InputStream`) — The input stream to wrap
  - `contentFormat` (`ContentFormat`) — The content format indicating compression
- **Returns:** The wrapped input stream, or the original stream if no decompression is needed. Returns an empty stream if `is` is `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if a decoder must read a stream header on construction (GZIP) and `is` is empty or does not start with a valid header
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  InputStream wrapped = HttpUtil.wrapInputStream(inputStream, ContentFormat.JSON_GZIP);
    // wrapped stream will automatically decompress GZIP data
  ```
##### wrapOutputStream(...) -> OutputStream
- **Signature:** `public static OutputStream wrapOutputStream(final OutputStream os, final ContentFormat contentFormat) throws UnsupportedOperationException, UncheckedIOException`
- **Summary:** Wraps an output stream with compression based on the content format.
- **Parameters:**
  - `os` (`OutputStream`) — The output stream to wrap; may be `null`
  - `contentFormat` (`ContentFormat`) — The content format indicating compression
- **Returns:** The wrapped output stream, or the original stream if no compression is needed. Returns `null` if `os` is `null` (unlike #wrapInputStream(InputStream, ContentFormat), which substitutes an empty stream).
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `os` is non-null and `contentFormat` requests Brotli compression, which has no bundled encoder
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if constructing the compression stream fails while writing its header
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  OutputStream wrapped = HttpUtil.wrapOutputStream(outputStream, ContentFormat.JSON_GZIP);
    // Data written to wrapped stream will be automatically compressed
  ```
- **See also:** #wrapInputStream(InputStream, ContentFormat)
##### getOutputStream(...) -> OutputStream
- **Signature:** `public static OutputStream getOutputStream(final HttpURLConnection connection, final ContentFormat contentFormat, String contentType, // NOSONAR String contentEncoding) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, IOException, UnsupportedOperationException, UncheckedIOException`
- **Summary:** Gets an output stream from an HttpURLConnection with appropriate headers and wrapping.
- **Contract:**
  - Sets Content-Type and Content-Encoding headers based on the content format, and wraps the stream with compression if needed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `connection` (`HttpURLConnection`) — The HTTP connection
  - `contentFormat` (`ContentFormat`) — The content format for the request body
  - `contentType` (`String`) — The Content-Type header value (can be null)
  - `contentEncoding` (`String`) — The Content-Encoding header value (can be null)
- **Returns:** The output stream, possibly wrapped with compression
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `connection` is `null`
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if a request header must be set after the connection has already been established
  - `java.io.IOException` — if opening the connection output stream fails
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `contentFormat` requests Brotli compression, which has no bundled encoder
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if constructing the compression stream fails while writing its header
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpURLConnection conn = (HttpURLConnection) new URL("http://example.com/api").openConnection();
    conn.setRequestMethod("POST");
    conn.setDoOutput(true);
    OutputStream os = HttpUtil.getOutputStream(conn, ContentFormat.JSON_GZIP, null, null);
    // sets "Content-Type: application/json" and "Content-Encoding: gzip" on the connection,
    // then returns a GZIP-wrapping output stream (when executed against a live server)
  ```
##### getInputStream(...) -> InputStream
- **Signature:** `public static InputStream getInputStream(final HttpURLConnection connection, final ContentFormat contentFormat) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException`
- **Summary:** Gets an input stream from an HttpURLConnection with appropriate unwrapping.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: If the body (or the error body) opens but the decoder for `contentFormat` cannot be constructed over it - typically an empty or malformed compressed body under a stale `Content-Encoding` header - the stream that was opened is closed before the exception propagates, so a failed call never leaves a response stream dangling.
- **Parameters:**
  - `connection` (`HttpURLConnection`) — The HTTP connection
  - `contentFormat` (`ContentFormat`) — The content format for decompression
- **Returns:** The input stream, possibly wrapped with decompression; never `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `connection` is `null`.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if the response body cannot be opened and the connection exposes no error stream to fall back to, or if a compressed body is empty or malformed so that its decoder cannot be constructed (on the error-stream branch the original IOException is attached as a suppressed exception)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpURLConnection conn = (HttpURLConnection) new URL("http://example.com/api").openConnection();
    conn.connect();
    InputStream is = HttpUtil.getInputStream(conn, ContentFormat.JSON_GZIP);
    // returns a GZIP-decompressing input stream over the response body
    // (falls back to the error stream on a non-2xx response; when executed against a live server)
  ```
##### flush(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static void flush(final OutputStream os) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Flushes an output stream, handling special cases for compression streams.
- **Parameters:**
  - `os` (`OutputStream`) — The output stream to flush
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `os` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if `os` is an LZ4 stream that has already been finished by an earlier `flush` (or `close`)
  - `java.io.IOException` — if finishing the compression stream or flushing its underlying output fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  OutputStream os = HttpUtil.wrapOutputStream(connection.getOutputStream(), ContentFormat.JSON_GZIP);
    os.write(payloadBytes);
    HttpUtil.flush(os);  // finishes the GZIP stream, then flushes all buffered data
  ```
##### getRequestCharset(...) -> Charset
- **Signature:** `public static Charset getRequestCharset(final HttpHeaders headers)`
- **Summary:** Gets the charset to use for HTTP requests based on headers.
- **Contract:**
  - Extracts the charset from the Content-Type header if present, otherwise returns the default charset (UTF-8).
- **Parameters:**
  - `headers` (`HttpHeaders`) — The HTTP headers
- **Returns:** The charset to use for the request
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpHeaders headers = HttpHeaders.create().setContentType("application/json; charset=ISO-8859-1");
    Charset charset = HttpUtil.getRequestCharset(headers);   // returns ISO-8859-1
  
    // No charset parameter -> the default (UTF-8) is used
    Charset dft = HttpUtil.getRequestCharset(HttpHeaders.create().setContentType("application/json"));
    // returns UTF-8
  ```
##### getResponseCharset(...) -> Charset
- **Signature:** `public static Charset getResponseCharset(final Map<String, ?> headers, final Charset requestCharset)`
- **Summary:** Gets the charset to use for HTTP responses based on headers.
- **Contract:**
  - Extracts the charset from the Content-Type header if present, otherwise returns the request charset as a fallback.
- **Parameters:**
  - `headers` (`Map<String, ?>`) — The response headers
  - `requestCharset` (`Charset`) — The charset used in the request (as fallback)
- **Returns:** The charset to use for the response
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, String> respHeaders = new HashMap<>();
    respHeaders.put("Content-Type", "text/html; charset=UTF-16");
    Charset charset = HttpUtil.getResponseCharset(respHeaders, Charsets.UTF_8);  // returns UTF-16
  
    // No charset in the response -> the request charset is used as a fallback
    Charset fallback = HttpUtil.getResponseCharset(new HashMap<>(), Charsets.UTF_8);  // returns UTF-8
  ```
##### getCharset(...) -> Charset
- **Signature:** `public static Charset getCharset(final String contentType)`
- **Summary:** Extracts the charset from a Content-Type header value.
- **Parameters:**
  - `contentType` (`String`) — The Content-Type header value; may be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** The charset, or the default charset (UTF-8) if no `charset` parameter is present or the named charset is not supported by this JVM
- **Examples:**
  ```java

    Charset dft = HttpUtil.getCharset("application/json");                    // returns UTF-8 (no charset)

  ```

- **Signature:** `public static Charset getCharset(final String contentType, final Charset defaultIfNull)`
- **Summary:** Extracts the charset from a Content-Type header value with a specified default.

  - `defaultIfNull` (`Charset`) — The default charset to return if none is found; may be `null`, in which case `null` is returned
- **Returns:** The charset from the content type, or `defaultIfNull` if no `charset` parameter is present or the named charset is not supported by this JVM
- **Examples:**

- **Signature:** `public static OkHttpRequest create(final String url, final OkHttpClient httpClient) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new OkHttpRequest instance with the specified URL and HTTP client.
- **Parameters:**
  - `url` (`String`) — the URL string for the request
  - `httpClient` (`OkHttpClient`) — the OkHttpClient to use for executing the request

  ```java
            .header("Accept", "application/json");

  ```

##### connectTimeout(...) -> OkHttpRequest
- **Signature:** `public OkHttpRequest connectTimeout(final long connectTimeout) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets the connection timeout in milliseconds for this HTTP request.
- **Contract:**
  - The connection timeout defines how long to wait when establishing a connection to the remote server before timing out.
- **Parameters:**
  - `connectTimeout` (`long`) — The connection timeout in milliseconds. Must be non-negative and must fit in an `int`; `0` disables the timeout.
- **Returns:** This OkHttpRequest instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `connectTimeout` is negative or too large for an `int`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  OkHttpRequest.url("http://localhost:18080")
        .connectTimeout(5000) // 5 seconds
        .get(String.class);
  ```
- **Signature:** `public OkHttpRequest connectTimeout(final Duration connectTimeout) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets the connection timeout using a Duration.
- **Parameters:**
  - `connectTimeout` (`Duration`) — The connection timeout as a Duration; must not be `null` and must not be negative. Duration#ZERO disables the timeout; any other value must be at least 1 ms and fit in an `int` number of milliseconds.
- **Returns:** This OkHttpRequest instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `connectTimeout` is `null`, negative, positive but shorter than 1 ms, or too large for an `int` number of milliseconds.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  OkHttpRequest.url("http://localhost:18080")
        .connectTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(5))
        .get(String.class);
  ```

##### tag(...) -> OkHttpRequest
- **Signature:** `public OkHttpRequest tag(final Object tag)`
- **Summary:** Attaches `tag` to the request under the `Object.class` key.
- **Parameters:**
  - `tag` (`Object`) — the tag to attach to the request, or `null` to remove it
- **Returns:** this OkHttpRequest instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Object requestTag = "my-request-id";
    OkHttpClient client = new OkHttpClient();
    try {
        ContinuableFuture<Response> future = OkHttpRequest.create("http://localhost:18080/data", client)
            .tag(requestTag)
            .asyncGet();
  
        // Later, cancel matching calls that have started executing in OkHttp.
        // Work still waiting in the request executor is not yet visible to the dispatcher.
        for (okhttp3.Call call : client.dispatcher().runningCalls()) {
            if (requestTag.equals(call.request().tag())) {
                call.cancel();
            }
        }
        // Observe completion and close any response delivered before cancellation.
        try (Response response = future.get()) {
            // Consume the response if the call succeeded.
        }
    } finally {
        // Release this example's dedicated client even if the request fails or is cancelled.
        client.dispatcher().executorService().shutdown();
        client.connectionPool().evictAll();
    }
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <T> OkHttpRequest tag(final Class<? super T> type, final T tag)`
- **Summary:** Attaches `tag` to the request using `type` as a key.
- **Parameters:**
  - `type` (`Class<? super T>`) — the class type used as a key for the tag
  - `tag` (`T`) — the tag to attach, or `null` to remove existing tag
- **Returns:** this OkHttpRequest instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  class RequestMetadata {
        long startTime;
        String requestId;
    }
  
    RequestMetadata metadata = new RequestMetadata();
    metadata.startTime = System.currentTimeMillis();
    metadata.requestId = "req-123";
  
    OkHttpRequest.url("http://localhost:18080/data")
        .tag(RequestMetadata.class, metadata)
        .get(String.class);
  ```

- **Signature:** `public Response get() throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException`
- **Summary:** Executes a GET request and returns the response.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)

  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a request body has been configured on this request (OkHttp forbids a body on GET)

- **Examples:**

  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.HttpResponseException` — if the status code is not 2xx and resultClass is not okhttp3.Response.class

### Class WebUtil (com.landawn.abacus.http.WebUtil)
Utility class providing methods for handling HTTP requests, responses, and cURL command conversions.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### curlToHttpRequestCode(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `public static String curlToHttpRequestCode(final String curl) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts a cURL command string into Java code for creating an HttpRequest.
- **Contract:**
  - HTTP Method Detection: If `-X` is specified, uses that method If `-d` is present without `-X`, defaults to POST If `-I` (or `--head`) is present without `-X`, defaults to HEAD Otherwise defaults to GET `PATCH` and `CONNECT` are emitted as `.execute(HttpMethod.PATCH)` / `.execute(HttpMethod.CONNECT)`, which HttpRequest rejects at run time with an UnsupportedOperationException because `java.net.HttpURLConnection` cannot issue them.
  - If a request body is present and the resolved method accepts one, it is declared as a separate `requestBody` variable for readability; otherwise the body is omitted and the generated code carries a comment saying so.
  - Attached data defaults to `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` when no Content-Type header was supplied, matching cURL's data options.
  - Empty contributions are ignored when combining.
- **Parameters:**
  - `curl` (`String`) — the cURL command string to convert, must not be `null` or empty and must start with "curl" (case-insensitive)
- **Returns:** Java code string for creating an equivalent HttpRequest, formatted with proper indentation and line separators
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the curl parameter is `null`, empty, doesn't start with "curl", contains an unclosed quote, contains no URL or more than one URL, uses an unsupported option, a request/data/header option has a missing or unsupported argument, a header references a file (`-H @file`) or has an empty name, or repeated headers cannot be combined.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String curl = "curl -X POST http://localhost:18080/users "
        + "-H \"Content-Type: application/json\" "
        + "-H \"Authorization: Bearer token123\" "
        + "-d '{\"name\":\"John\",\"age\":30}'";
    String javaCode = WebUtil.curlToHttpRequestCode(curl);
    System.out.println(javaCode);
  ```
- **See also:** #curlToOkHttpRequestCode(String)

- **Parameters:**

- **Returns:** Java code string for creating an equivalent OkHttpRequest, formatted with proper indentation and line separators
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the curl parameter is `null`, empty, doesn't start with "curl", contains an unclosed quote, contains no URL or more than one URL, uses an unsupported option, a request/data/header option has a missing or unsupported argument, a header references a file (`-H @file`) or has an empty name, or repeated headers cannot be combined.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String curl = "curl -X POST http://localhost:18080/users "
        + "-H \"Content-Type: application/json\" "
  ```

##### createCurlLoggingOkHttpRequest(...) -> OkHttpRequest
- **Signature:** `public static OkHttpRequest createCurlLoggingOkHttpRequest(final String url, final Consumer<? super String> logHandler) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates an OkHttpRequest configured to log cURL commands for each HTTP request.
- **Parameters:**
  - `url` (`String`) — the base URL for the HTTP request, must not be `null`
  - `logHandler` (`Consumer<? super String>`) — consumer that receives the generated cURL command string for each request.
- **Returns:** an OkHttpRequest configured with cURL logging interceptor

- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Create request with cURL logging
    OkHttpRequest request = WebUtil.createCurlLoggingOkHttpRequest(
        "http://localhost:18080",
        curl -> logger.debug("cURL command: {}", curl)
    );
  
    // When you make a request, it will log the cURL equivalent
    request.header("Authorization", "Bearer token123")
           .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
           .jsonBody(requestData)
           .post(String.class);
  
    // The logHandler will receive something like:
    // curl -X POST 'http://localhost:18080' \
    //   -H 'Authorization: Bearer token123' \
    //   -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    //   -d '{"key":"value"}'
  ```
- **See also:** #createCurlLoggingOkHttpRequest(String, char, Consumer), CurlInterceptor, Ok2Curl - OkHttp to cURL converter (https://github.com/mrmike/Ok2Curl)
- **Signature:** `public static OkHttpRequest createCurlLoggingOkHttpRequest(final String url, final char quoteChar, final Consumer<? super String> logHandler) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates an OkHttpRequest configured to log cURL commands with a custom quote character.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful when you need to generate cURL commands compatible with specific POSIX shell quoting styles or documentation standards.
- **Parameters:**
  - `url` (`String`) — the base URL for the HTTP request, must not be `null`
  - `quoteChar` (`char`) — the character to use for quoting in cURL commands; must be a single quote (') or a double quote (")
  - `logHandler` (`Consumer<? super String>`) — consumer that receives the generated cURL command string for each request.
- **Returns:** an OkHttpRequest configured with cURL logging interceptor using the specified quote character
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `url` is `null` or empty, or if `logHandler` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Use double quotes in generated cURL commands for a POSIX shell
    OkHttpRequest request = WebUtil.createCurlLoggingOkHttpRequest(
        "http://localhost:18080",
        '"',
        curl -> System.out.println("cURL: " + curl)
    );
  
    request.header("Content-Type", "application/json")
           .post(String.class);
  
    // Generates:
    // curl -X POST "http://localhost:18080" \
    //   -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  ```
- **See also:** #createCurlLoggingOkHttpRequest(String, Consumer), CurlInterceptor
##### buildCurl(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `public static String buildCurl(final HttpMethod httpMethod, final String url, final Map<String, ?> headers, final String body, final String bodyContentType, final char quoteChar) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Builds a cURL command string from HTTP request parameters.
- **Contract:**
  - It handles proper quoting and escaping of all components to ensure the command works correctly when executed.
  - The generated cURL command includes: HTTP method using the `-X` flag (`-I` for HEAD, which is what curl requires - unless a body is given, since curl refuses `-I` together with a data option; then `-X HEAD` is used) URL enclosed in the specified quote character, with `--globoff` to preserve literal brackets and braces All headers using `-H` flags with proper quoting and escaping; a header whose value resolves to an empty or all-whitespace string is written as `-H 'Name;'`, curl's spelling for "send this header empty" (`-H 'Name: '` would instead tell curl to remove the header, because curl skips the whitespace after the colon) Request body using `--data-raw` if body is not empty; a leading `@` is sent literally Content-Type header if body is present, `headers` carries no `Content-Type` entry at all - one present with a `null`, empty or blank value counts as present, so a command never carries two `Content-Type` lines - and `bodyContentType` is not blank (a blank one could only be written as `-H 'Content-Type: '`, which removes the header) Special handling: If `body` is not empty but Content-Type header is not present in `headers`, and `bodyContentType` is not blank, the Content-Type header is automatically added Header values are converted using the field-aware HttpHeaders#valueOf(String, Object), including its handling of java.util.Collection (joined with `", "`, or with `"; "` on the `Cookie` field) and java.util.Date/java.time.Instant (HTTP-date formatted) values URLs, header names and values, and bodies are escaped for the chosen `quoteChar`: inside single quotes each `'` becomes `'\\''`; inside double quotes `\\ " $ `` are backslash-escaped The command is formatted with line separators at the beginning and end Quoting targets POSIX-compatible shells.
- **Parameters:**
  - `httpMethod` (`HttpMethod`) — the HTTP method (e.g., HttpMethod#GET, HttpMethod#POST), must not be `null`
  - `url` (`String`) — the target URL, must not be `null` or empty
  - `headers` (`Map<String, ?>`) — map of HTTP headers whose values are converted by HttpHeaders#valueOf(String, Object) (can be `null` or empty)
  - `body` (`String`) — the request body string (can be `null` or empty for requests without a body)
  - `bodyContentType` (`String`) — the MIME type of the body (e.g., "application/json"), used to add Content-Type header if not already present in headers (can be null)
  - `quoteChar` (`char`) — the character to use for quoting values in the cURL command; must be a single quote (') or a double quote (")
- **Returns:** a formatted cURL command string with line separators, ready for execution
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `httpMethod` is `null`, `url` is `null` or empty, `quoteChar` is neither a single nor a double quote, or a header name is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, String> headers = new HashMap<>();
    headers.put("Content-Type", "application/json");
    headers.put("Authorization", "Bearer token123");
  
    String curl = WebUtil.buildCurl(
        HttpMethod.POST,
        "http://localhost:18080/users",
        headers,
        "{\"name\":\"John\",\"email\":\"john@example.com\"}",
        "application/json",
        '\''
    );
    System.out.println(curl);
  ```
- **See also:** HttpHeaders#valueOf(String, Object), Strings#escapeQuotes(String, char)
##### setContentTypeByRequestBodyType(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static void setContentTypeByRequestBodyType(final String requestBodyType, final HttpHeaders httpHeaders) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets the Content-Type header based on the request body type if not already present.
- **Contract:**
  - The header is only set if: The `requestBodyType` parameter is not `null` or empty The `httpHeaders` does not already have a Content-Type header This method is particularly useful when: Processing HAR (HTTP Archive) files where body type is specified separately Building HTTP requests programmatically where content type needs to be inferred Importing requests from external sources that specify MIME type separately Ensuring a default Content-Type without overriding existing values If the Content-Type header is already present in `httpHeaders`, this method does nothing, preserving the existing header value.
- **Parameters:**
  - `requestBodyType` (`String`) — the MIME type of the request body (e.g., "application/json", "text/xml", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"), can be `null` or empty
  - `httpHeaders` (`HttpHeaders`) — the HttpHeaders object to conditionally update, must not be `null` when `requestBodyType` is not `null` or empty
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `httpHeaders` is `null` and `requestBodyType` is not `null` or empty
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Case 1: Setting Content-Type when not present
    HttpHeaders headers = HttpHeaders.create();
    WebUtil.setContentTypeByRequestBodyType("application/json", headers);
    // headers now contains: Content-Type: application/json
  
    // Case 2: Preserving existing Content-Type
    HttpHeaders headers2 = HttpHeaders.create();
    headers2.setContentType("text/xml");
    WebUtil.setContentTypeByRequestBodyType("application/json", headers2);
    // headers2 still contains: Content-Type: text/xml (not changed)
  
    // Case 3: No-op when requestBodyType is empty
    HttpHeaders headers3 = HttpHeaders.create();
    WebUtil.setContentTypeByRequestBodyType("", headers3);
    // headers3 has no Content-Type header (nothing was set)
  ```
- **See also:** HttpHeaders#setContentType(String), HttpHeaders#get(String)

#### Public Instance Methods
- (none)

  ```java
    // String body = request.get(String.class);
  ```

  ```java
  HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.url("http://localhost:18080/data", 5000, 30000);
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static HttpRequest url(final URL url) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new HttpRequest instance with the specified URL using the default HTTP client.
- **Contract:**
  - An IllegalArgumentException may be thrown later, when the request is executed, if it is not a valid `http` or `https` URI.
- **Parameters:**
  - `url` (`URL`) — the URL object for the request
- **Returns:** a new HttpRequest instance
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `url` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  URL url = new URL("http://localhost:18080/users");
    HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.url(url);  // uses the default HttpClient
    // String body = request.get(String.class);  // network call happens here (when executed)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static HttpRequest url(final URL url, final long connectTimeoutInMillis, final long readTimeoutInMillis) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new HttpRequest instance with the specified URL and timeout settings.
- **Parameters:**
  - `url` (`URL`) — the URL object for the request
  - `connectTimeoutInMillis` (`long`) — the connection timeout in milliseconds; `0` means no connect timeout (the JDK default, unbounded)
  - `readTimeoutInMillis` (`long`) — the maximum duration allowed for the response, in milliseconds; `0` means no response timeout (the JDK default, unbounded)
- **Returns:** a new HttpRequest instance
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `url` is `null` or either timeout is negative.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  URL url = new URL("http://localhost:18080/data");
    HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.url(url, 5000, 30000);  // 5s connect, 30s response timeout
    // String body = request.get(String.class);  // network call happens here (when executed)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static HttpRequest url(final URI uri) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new HttpRequest instance with the specified URI using the default HTTP client.
- **Contract:**
  - Scheme/host validity is not verified at construction; an IllegalArgumentException may be thrown later, when the request is executed, if its scheme is not `http` or `https`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `uri` (`URI`) — the URI object for the request
- **Returns:** a new HttpRequest instance
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `uri` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  URI uri = URI.create("http://localhost:18080/users");
    HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.url(uri);  // uses the default HttpClient
    // String body = request.get(String.class);  // network call happens here (when executed)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static HttpRequest url(final URI uri, final long connectTimeoutInMillis, final long readTimeoutInMillis) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new HttpRequest instance with the specified URI and timeout settings.
- **Parameters:**
  - `uri` (`URI`) — the URI object for the request
  - `connectTimeoutInMillis` (`long`) — the connection timeout in milliseconds; `0` means no connect timeout (the JDK default, unbounded)
  - `readTimeoutInMillis` (`long`) — the maximum duration allowed for the response, in milliseconds; `0` means no response timeout (the JDK default, unbounded)
- **Returns:** a new HttpRequest instance
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `uri` is `null`, or either timeout is negative.

#### Public Instance Methods
##### connectTimeout(...) -> HttpRequest
- **Signature:** `public HttpRequest connectTimeout(final Duration connectTimeout) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets the connection timeout for this request.
- **Contract:**
  - This creates a new HttpClient builder if one doesn't exist, or copies settings from the existing client.
  - The connection timeout is the maximum time to wait when establishing a connection to the server.
  - If the connection cannot be established within this timeout, the request will fail.
- **Parameters:**
  - `connectTimeout` (`Duration`) — the connection timeout; `null` or zero leaves the current setting unchanged
- **Returns:** this HttpRequest instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `connectTimeout` is negative.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpRequest.url("http://localhost:18080/data")
        .connectTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(10))
        .get();
  ```
- **Signature:** `public HttpRequest connectTimeout(final long connectTimeoutInMillis) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets the connection timeout for this request, in milliseconds.
- **Parameters:**
  - `connectTimeoutInMillis` (`long`) — the connection timeout in milliseconds (`0` leaves the current setting unchanged, so a previously configured timeout survives)
- **Returns:** this HttpRequest instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `connectTimeoutInMillis` is negative.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpRequest.url("http://localhost:18080/data")
        .connectTimeout(10_000L)
        .get();
  ```
##### readTimeout(...) -> HttpRequest
- **Signature:** `public HttpRequest readTimeout(final Duration readTimeout) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets the timeout for the request to complete.
- **Parameters:**
  - `readTimeout` (`Duration`) — the request timeout (maximum duration allowed for the response); `null` or zero leaves the current setting unchanged
- **Returns:** this HttpRequest instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `readTimeout` is negative.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpRequest.url("http://localhost:18080/slow-endpoint")
        .readTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(60))
        .get();
  ```
- **Signature:** `public HttpRequest readTimeout(final long readTimeoutInMillis) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets the request-completion timeout, in milliseconds.
- **Parameters:**
  - `readTimeoutInMillis` (`long`) — the maximum duration allowed for the response, in milliseconds (`0` leaves the current setting unchanged, so a previously configured timeout survives)
- **Returns:** this HttpRequest instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `readTimeoutInMillis` is negative.
- **Examples:**

##### authenticator(...) -> HttpRequest
- **Signature:** `public HttpRequest authenticator(final Authenticator authenticator) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets the authenticator for this request.
- **Contract:**
  - The authenticator will be used to provide credentials when the server requests authentication (for example, HTTP Basic authentication).
- **Parameters:**
  - `authenticator` (`Authenticator`) — the authenticator to use for providing credentials
- **Returns:** this HttpRequest instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `authenticator` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Authenticator auth = new Authenticator() {
        @Override
        protected PasswordAuthentication getPasswordAuthentication() {
            return new PasswordAuthentication("username", "password".toCharArray());
        }
    };
  
    HttpRequest.url("http://localhost:18080/secure")
        .authenticator(auth)
        .get();
  ```
- **See also:** #basicAuth(String, Object)
##### basicAuth(...) -> HttpRequest
- **Signature:** `public HttpRequest basicAuth(final String username, final Object password) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets the Basic Authentication header for this request.
- **Parameters:**
  - `username` (`String`) — the username for authentication
  - `password` (`Object`) — the password for authentication; a `char\[\]` is converted with `new String(char\[\])`, any other value with String#valueOf(Object)
- **Returns:** this HttpRequest instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the resulting header value contains characters the JDK client rejects; see #header(String, Object) for the header restrictions
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpRequest.url("http://localhost:18080/secure")
        .basicAuth("username", "password")
        .get();
  ```
- **See also:** #basicAuth(String, String), HttpHeaders, HttpHeaders.Names, HttpHeaders.Values
- **Signature:** `public HttpRequest basicAuth(final String username, final String password)`
- **Summary:** Sets the `Authorization` header using HTTP Basic authentication.
- **Parameters:**
  - `username` (`String`) — the username for authentication
  - `password` (`String`) — the password for authentication
- **Returns:** this HttpRequest instance for method chaining

- **See also:** HttpHeaders
##### header(...) -> HttpRequest
- **Signature:** `public HttpRequest header(final String name, final Object value) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets the HTTP header specified by `name/value`.
- **Contract:**
  - If this HttpRequest already has any headers with that name, they are all replaced.
- **Parameters:**
  - `name` (`String`) — the header name
  - `value` (`Object`) — the header value, converted with HttpHeaders#valueOf(String, Object) (`null` becomes `""`; a `Collection` is joined with `", "`, or with `"; "` on the `Cookie` field)
- **Returns:** this HttpRequest instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `name` is `null`, is a restricted header name or `name`/`value` contains characters that are illegal in an HTTP header.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpRequest.url("http://localhost:18080/data")
        .header("Accept", "application/json")
        .header("User-Agent", "MyApp/1.0")
        .get();
  ```
- **See also:** HttpHeaders, HttpHeaders.Names, HttpHeaders.Values
##### headers(...) -> HttpRequest
- **Signature:** `public HttpRequest headers(final String name1, final Object value1, final String name2, final Object value2) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets HTTP headers specified by `name1/value1`, `name2/value2`.
- **Contract:**
  - If this HttpRequest already has any headers with those names, they are all replaced.
- **Parameters:**
  - `name1` (`String`) — the first header name
  - `value1` (`Object`) — the first header value (will be converted to string)
  - `name2` (`String`) — the second header name
  - `value2` (`Object`) — the second header value (will be converted to string)
- **Returns:** this HttpRequest instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a name is restricted or a name/value contains illegal characters; see #header(String, Object)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpRequest.url("http://localhost:18080/data")
        .headers("Accept", "application/json", "User-Agent", "MyApp/1.0")
        .get();
  ```
- **See also:** HttpHeaders, HttpHeaders.Names, HttpHeaders.Values
- **Signature:** `public HttpRequest headers(final String name1, final Object value1, final String name2, final Object value2, final String name3, final Object value3) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets HTTP headers specified by `name1/value1`, `name2/value2`, `name3/value3`.
- **Contract:**
  - If this HttpRequest already has any headers with those names, they are all replaced.
- **Parameters:**
  - `name1` (`String`) — the first header name
  - `value1` (`Object`) — the first header value (will be converted to string)
  - `name2` (`String`) — the second header name
  - `value2` (`Object`) — the second header value (will be converted to string)
  - `name3` (`String`) — the third header name
  - `value3` (`Object`) — the third header value (will be converted to string)
- **Returns:** this HttpRequest instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a name is restricted or a name/value contains illegal characters; see #header(String, Object)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  HttpRequest.url("http://localhost:18080/data")
        .headers("Accept", "application/json",
                 "User-Agent", "MyApp/1.0",
                 "X-Custom-Header", "custom-value")
        .get();
  ```
- **See also:** HttpHeaders, HttpHeaders.Names, HttpHeaders.Values
- **Signature:** `public HttpRequest headers(final Map<String, ?> headers) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Merges the given header entries into the headers already on this request.
- **Contract:**
  - Create a new request when you need to discard all prior headers and install a fresh set.
- **Parameters:**
  - `headers` (`Map<String, ?>`) — a map containing header names and values
- **Returns:** this HttpRequest instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a name is restricted or a name/value contains illegal characters; see #header(String, Object). Entries before the offending one have already been applied.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, String> headers = new HashMap<>();
    headers.put("Accept", "application/json");
    headers.put("Authorization", "Bearer token123");
  
    HttpRequest.url("http://localhost:18080/data")
        .headers(headers)
        .get();
  ```
- **See also:** HttpHeaders, HttpHeaders.Names, HttpHeaders.Values

  - An exception is thrown if the response status code indicates an error (not 2xx).
- **Parameters:**
  - `httpMethod` (`HttpMethod`) — the HTTP method to use (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD)
  - `resultClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class of the result type to deserialize the response body into
- **Returns:** a CompletableFuture that completes with the deserialized response body, or exceptionally with HttpResponseException (surfacing as `CompletionException`/`ExecutionException`) for a non-2xx status
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `httpMethod` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  CompletableFuture<User> future =
        HttpRequest.url("http://localhost:18080/users/123")
            .asyncExecute(HttpMethod.GET, User.class);
  
    future.thenAccept(user -> {
        System.out.println("User: " + user.getName());
    });
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Beta public <T> CompletableFuture<HttpResponse<T>> asyncExecute(final HttpMethod httpMethod, final HttpResponse.BodyHandler<T> responseBodyHandler, final PushPromiseHandler<T> pushPromiseHandler) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Executes an HTTP request asynchronously with the specified method, custom response body handler, and push promise handler.
- **Parameters:**
  - `httpMethod` (`HttpMethod`) — the HTTP method to use (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD)
  - `responseBodyHandler` (`HttpResponse.BodyHandler<T>`) — the handler for processing the response body
  - `pushPromiseHandler` (`PushPromiseHandler<T>`) — the handler for processing HTTP/2 server push promises
- **Returns:** a CompletableFuture that will complete with the HTTP response
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `httpMethod`, `responseBodyHandler`, or `pushPromiseHandler` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  PushPromiseHandler<String> pushHandler = (initiatingRequest, pushPromiseRequest, acceptor) -> {
        System.out.println("Server push for: " + pushPromiseRequest.uri());
        acceptor.apply(BodyHandlers.ofString());
    };
  
    CompletableFuture<HttpResponse<String>> future =
        HttpRequest.url("http://localhost:18080/page")
            .asyncExecute(HttpMethod.GET, BodyHandlers.ofString(), pushHandler);
  ```
- **See also:** java.net.http.HttpResponse.PushPromiseHandler

### Interface Logger (com.landawn.abacus.logging.Logger)
The main Logger interface providing a unified API for logging across different implementations.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### getName(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `String getName()`
- **Summary:** Gets the name of this logger instance.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the name of this logger
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Logger logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger(MyClass.class);
    String loggerName = logger.getName(); // returns "com.example.MyClass"
  ```
##### isTraceEnabled(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `boolean isTraceEnabled()`
- **Summary:** Checks if the logger instance is enabled for the `TRACE` level.
- **Contract:**
  - This method should be used to guard expensive trace message construction.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** `true` if this Logger is enabled for the `TRACE` level, `false` otherwise
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  if (logger.isTraceEnabled()) {
        logger.trace("Entry count: " + expensiveCalculation());
    }
  ```

### Class LoggerFactory (com.landawn.abacus.logging.LoggerFactory)
A factory for creating Logger objects with automatic detection of the logging framework.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### getLogger(...) -> Logger
- **Signature:** `public static Logger getLogger(final Class<?> clazz) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Gets a logger instance for the specified class.
- **Contract:**
  - If a logger with the same name already exists, the cached instance is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `clazz` (`Class<?>`) — the class for which to get the logger; must not be `null`
- **Returns:** a Logger instance for the specified class
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `clazz` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  public class MyService {
        private static final Logger logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger(MyService.class);
  
        public void doSomething() {
            logger.debug("Starting operation");
        }
    }
  ```
- **Signature:** `@SuppressFBWarnings("SF_SWITCH_FALLTHROUGH") @SuppressWarnings("fallthrough") public static Logger getLogger(final String name) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Gets a logger instance for the specified name.
- **Contract:**
  - This method returns a cached logger if one exists for the given name, otherwise it creates a new logger starting with the last successfully selected logging framework.
  - If that backend fails to initialize the new logger, selection continues to the next fallback.
- **Parameters:**
  - `name` (`String`) — the name of the logger; must not be `null`
- **Returns:** a Logger instance for the specified name
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `name` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Logger logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger("com.mycompany.MyComponent");
    logger.warn("Configuration not found, using defaults");
  ```

#### Public Instance Methods
- (none)
