### Class AvroParser (com.landawn.abacus.parser.AvroParser)
Parser implementation for Apache Avro format serialization and deserialization.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- `public AvroParser()` — Constructs a new AvroParser instance.
  ```java
  AvroParser parser = new AvroParser();  // creates a ready-to-use parser
  
    Schema schema = new Schema.Parser().parse(schemaJson);
    AvroSerConfig config = new AvroSerConfig().setSchema(schema);
    Map<String, Object> data = Map.of("name", "John", "age", 30);
    String encoded = parser.serialize(data, config);  // returns a Base64 encoded string
  ```

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### serialize(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `@Override public String serialize(final Object obj, final AvroSerConfig config) throws IllegalArgumentException, ArithmeticException, NumberFormatException`
- **Summary:** Serializes an object to a Base64 encoded string representation.
- **Parameters:**
  - `obj` (`Object`) — the object to serialize (may be `null`; serializes nothing in that case)
  - `config` (`AvroSerConfig`) — the serialization configuration to use (must contain a schema unless `obj` is a `SpecificRecord` or a collection of `SpecificRecord`s)
- **Returns:** the Base64 encoded string representation of the serialized object, or an empty string if `obj` is `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a required schema is missing, the source type is unsupported, an inferred `SpecificRecord` collection contains nulls or more than one record class, or an enum value is not one of the schema's symbols.
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if a `Number` does not fit an `int`/`long` field
  - `java.lang.NumberFormatException` — if a floating-point or decimal `Number` is written to an `int`/`long` field
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User user = new User("John", 30);
    AvroSerConfig config = new AvroSerConfig()
        .setSchema(User.getClassSchema());
    String base64Encoded = parser.serialize(user, config);
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Override public void serialize(final Object obj, final AvroSerConfig config, final File output) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException, ArithmeticException, NumberFormatException`
- **Summary:** Serializes an object to a file with raw binary content (NOT Base64 encoded).
- **Contract:**
  - The file will be created if it doesn't exist, or overwritten if it does.
- **Parameters:**
  - `obj` (`Object`) — the object to serialize (may be `null`; serializes nothing in that case)
  - `config` (`AvroSerConfig`) — the serialization configuration to use (may be `null` for default behavior)
  - `output` (`File`) — the output file to write to (must not be `null`)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a required schema is missing, the source type is unsupported, an inferred `SpecificRecord` collection contains nulls or more than one record class, or an enum value is not one of the schema's symbols; or `output` is `null`.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if creating or opening the output file, writing the Avro container, or flushing the output fails.
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if a `Number` does not fit an `int`/`long` field
  - `java.lang.NumberFormatException` — if a floating-point or decimal `Number` is written to an `int`/`long` field
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<User> users = List.of(
        new User("John", 30),
        new User("Jane", 25)
    );
    // SpecificRecord collections carry their own schema, so no config is required.
    parser.serialize(users, null, new File("users.avro"));
  ```
- **Signature:** `@SuppressFBWarnings @Override public void serialize(final Object obj, final AvroSerConfig config, final OutputStream output) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException, ArithmeticException, NumberFormatException`
- **Summary:** Serializes an object to an output stream with raw binary content (NOT Base64 encoded).
- **Parameters:**
  - `obj` (`Object`) — the object to serialize (may be `null`; serializes nothing in that case)
  - `config` (`AvroSerConfig`) — the serialization configuration to use (may be `null` for default behavior)
  - `output` (`OutputStream`) — the output stream to write to; may be `null` only when `obj` is `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a required schema is missing, the source type is unsupported, an inferred `SpecificRecord` collection contains nulls or more than one record class, or an enum value is not one of the schema's symbols; or `obj` is non-null and `output` is `null`.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if writing the Avro container header or records, or flushing the output fails.
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if a `Number` does not fit an `int`/`long` field
  - `java.lang.NumberFormatException` — if a floating-point or decimal `Number` is written to an `int`/`long` field
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // With SpecificRecord
    User user = new User("John", 30);
    try (OutputStream os = new FileOutputStream("user.avro")) {
        parser.serialize(user, null, os);
    }
  
    // With regular bean and schema
    Person person = new Person("John", 30);
    AvroSerConfig config = new AvroSerConfig()
        .setSchema(personSchema);
    parser.serialize(person, config, outputStream);
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Deprecated @Override public void serialize(final Object obj, final AvroSerConfig config, final Writer output) throws UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Serialization to Writer is not supported for Avro format.
- **Parameters:**
  - `obj` (`Object`) — the object to serialize
  - `config` (`AvroSerConfig`) — the serialization configuration
  - `output` (`Writer`) — the writer (not supported)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — always thrown as this operation is not supported
##### deserialize(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `@Override public <T> T deserialize(String source, AvroDeserConfig config, Type<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException, ParsingException`
- **Summary:** Deserializes an object from a Base64 encoded string representation.
- **Contract:**
  - The input string must be Base64 encoded Avro binary data.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`String`) — the Base64 encoded string to deserialize from (must not be `null`); an empty string, which is what #serialize(Object, AvroSerConfig) returns for a `null` object, yields the default value of the target type
  - `config` (`AvroDeserConfig`) — the deserialization configuration to use (may be `null` for default behavior)
  - `targetType` (`Type<? extends T>`) — the type of the object to create (must not be `null`)
- **Returns:** the deserialized object instance, or the default value of `targetType` (`null` for beans, maps and collections) if `source` is empty
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `source` or `targetType` is `null`; if `source` is not valid Base64; or, for nonempty input, a required schema is absent or the target is neither a supported record, bean, map nor collection
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if the nonempty Base64-decoded bytes have an invalid or truncated Avro container header or record
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if a schema field has no matching bean property and `ignoreUnmatchedProperty` is disabled
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AvroParser parser = new AvroParser();
    User original = new User("John", 30);
    AvroSerConfig serConfig = new AvroSerConfig()
        .setSchema(User.getClassSchema());
    String base64Data = parser.serialize(original, serConfig);
    AvroDeserConfig config = AvroDeserConfig.create()
        .setSchema(User.getClassSchema());
    User user = parser.deserialize(base64Data, config, User.class);
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Override public <T> T deserialize(final String source, final AvroDeserConfig config, final Class<? extends T> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException, ParsingException`
- **Summary:** Deserializes an object from a Base64 encoded string representation.
- **Contract:**
  - The input string must be Base64 encoded Avro binary data.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`String`) — the Base64 encoded string to deserialize from (must not be `null`); an empty string, which is what #serialize(Object, AvroSerConfig) returns for a `null` object, yields the default value of the target class
  - `config` (`AvroDeserConfig`) — the deserialization configuration to use (may be `null` for default behavior)
  - `targetClass` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the class of the object to create (must not be `null`)
- **Returns:** the deserialized object instance, or the default value of `targetClass` (`null` for beans, maps and collections) if `source` is empty
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `source` or `targetClass` is `null`; if `source` is not valid Base64; or, for nonempty input, a required schema is absent or the target is neither a supported record, bean, map nor collection
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if the nonempty Base64-decoded bytes have an invalid or truncated Avro container header or record
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if a schema field has no matching bean property and `ignoreUnmatchedProperty` is disabled
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AvroParser parser = new AvroParser();
    User original = new User("John", 30);
    AvroSerConfig serConfig = new AvroSerConfig()
        .setSchema(User.getClassSchema());
    String base64Data = parser.serialize(original, serConfig);
    AvroDeserConfig config = AvroDeserConfig.create()
        .setSchema(User.getClassSchema());
    User user = parser.deserialize(base64Data, config, User.class);
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Override public <T> T deserialize(File source, AvroDeserConfig config, Type<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException, ParsingException`
- **Summary:** Deserializes an object from a file containing raw binary data (NOT Base64 encoded).
- **Contract:**
  - The file should contain raw binary Avro data (not Base64 encoded).
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`File`) — the source file to read from (must not be `null` and must exist)
  - `config` (`AvroDeserConfig`) — the deserialization configuration to use (may be `null` for default behavior)
  - `targetType` (`Type<? extends T>`) — the type of the object to create (must not be `null`)
- **Returns:** the deserialized object instance
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `source` or `targetType` is `null`, or `source` is a directory; or a required schema is absent or the target is neither a supported record, bean, map nor collection
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if opening, reading or closing `source` fails, including a missing file or invalid or truncated Avro container data
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if a schema field has no matching bean property and `ignoreUnmatchedProperty` is disabled
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File avroFile = new File("users.avro");
    AvroDeserConfig config = AvroDeserConfig.create().setElementType(User.class);
    List<User> users = parser.deserialize(avroFile, config, List.class);
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Override public <T> T deserialize(final File source, final AvroDeserConfig config, final Class<? extends T> targetClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException, ParsingException`
- **Summary:** Deserializes an object from a file containing raw binary data (NOT Base64 encoded).
- **Contract:**
  - The file should contain raw binary Avro data (not Base64 encoded).
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`File`) — the source file to read from (must not be `null` and must exist)
  - `config` (`AvroDeserConfig`) — the deserialization configuration to use (may be `null` for default behavior)
  - `targetClass` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the class of the object to create (must not be `null`)
- **Returns:** the deserialized object instance
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `source` or `targetClass` is `null`, or `source` is a directory; or a required schema is absent or the target is neither a supported record, bean, map nor collection
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if opening, reading or closing `source` fails, including a missing file or invalid or truncated Avro container data
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if a schema field has no matching bean property and `ignoreUnmatchedProperty` is disabled
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File avroFile = new File("users.avro");
    AvroDeserConfig config = AvroDeserConfig.create().setElementType(User.class);
    List<User> users = parser.deserialize(avroFile, config, List.class);
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Override public <T> T deserialize(InputStream source, AvroDeserConfig config, Type<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException, ParsingException`
- **Summary:** Deserializes an object from an input stream containing raw binary data (NOT Base64 encoded).
- **Contract:**
  - The stream should contain raw binary Avro data (not Base64 encoded).
  - This method supports: SpecificRecord classes (Avro generated classes) Collections of SpecificRecord GenericRecord Regular Java beans and Maps (requires schema in config) Usage Examples: When the target is a bean, a schema field without a matching bean property is skipped while the inherited `ignoreUnmatchedProperty` option is enabled (the default) and rejected with a ParsingException otherwise.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`InputStream`) — the input stream to read from (must not be `null`); an empty stream is not a valid Avro container
  - `config` (`AvroDeserConfig`) — the deserialization configuration to use (may be `null` for default behavior)
  - `targetType` (`Type<? extends T>`) — the type of the object to create (must not be `null`)
- **Returns:** the deserialized object instance
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `source` or `targetType` is `null`; or a required schema is absent or the target is neither a supported record, bean, map nor collection
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if reading the Avro container header or records from `source` fails, including an empty, invalid or truncated container
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if a schema field has no matching bean property and `ignoreUnmatchedProperty` is disabled
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Deserialize to SpecificRecord
    try (InputStream is = new FileInputStream("user.avro")) {
        User user = parser.deserialize(is, null, User.class);
    }
  
    // Deserialize to regular bean with schema
    AvroDeserConfig config = AvroDeserConfig.create()
        .setSchema(schema)
        .setElementType(Person.class);
    List<Person> people = parser.deserialize(inputStream, config, List.class);
  ```

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- `public AvroSerConfig()` — Constructs a new instance of `AvroSerConfig` with default settings.
  ```java
  AvroSerConfig config = new AvroSerConfig()
        .setSchema(schema);
  ```

#### Public Static Methods
##### create(...) -> AvroSerConfig

- **Summary:** Creates a new instance of `AvroSerConfig` with default settings.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)

- **Examples:**

  ```java
  AvroSerConfig config = AvroSerConfig.create()
        .setSchema(schema);
  ```

#### Public Instance Methods
##### isIgnoreUnknownFields(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public boolean isIgnoreUnknownFields()`
- **Summary:** Returns whether source bean/map fields absent from the Avro record schema may be discarded.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** true for explicit projection mode; false (the default) for strict field validation
##### setIgnoreUnknownFields(...) -> AvroSerConfig
- **Signature:** `public AvroSerConfig setIgnoreUnknownFields(final boolean ignoreUnknownFields)`
- **Summary:** Enables explicit projection of source beans/maps onto the record schema, including nested records.
- **Contract:**
  - By default, unknown fields fail serialization with the field and schema names, even when their values are null.
- **Parameters:**
  - `ignoreUnknownFields` (`boolean`) — whether to discard source fields absent from the schema
- **Returns:** this configuration
##### getSchema(...) -> Schema
- **Signature:** `public Schema getSchema()`
- **Summary:** Gets the Avro Schema used for serialization.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the Avro schema, or `null` if not set
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AvroSerConfig config = new AvroSerConfig();
    Schema none = config.getSchema();  // returns null (not set)
  
    Schema schema = new Schema.Parser().parse(schemaJson);
    config.setSchema(schema);
    Schema current = config.getSchema();  // returns the configured schema
  ```
##### setSchema(...) -> AvroSerConfig
- **Signature:** `public AvroSerConfig setSchema(final Schema schema)`
- **Summary:** Sets the Avro Schema for serialization.
- **Parameters:**
  - `schema` (`Schema`) — the Avro schema to use for serialization
- **Returns:** this instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String schemaJson = "{\"type\":\"record\",\"name\":\"User\"," +
        "\"fields\":[{\"name\":\"name\",\"type\":\"string\"}," +
        "{\"name\":\"age\",\"type\":\"int\"}]}";
    Schema schema = new Schema.Parser().parse(schemaJson);
    config.setSchema(schema);
  ```

- **Summary:** Compares this configuration with another object for equality.

### Class DeserializationConfig (com.landawn.abacus.parser.DeserializationConfig)
Abstract base configuration class for deserialization operations.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### isIgnoreUnmatchedProperty(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public boolean isIgnoreUnmatchedProperty()`
- **Summary:** Checks if unmatched properties should be ignored during deserialization.
- **Contract:**
  - When set to `true` (default), properties in the source data that don't match any property in the target class will be silently ignored.
  - When `false`, unmatched properties will cause an exception to be thrown.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** `true` if unmatched properties are ignored, `false` otherwise
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  JsonDeserConfig config = new JsonDeserConfig();
    boolean ignored = config.isIgnoreUnmatchedProperty();  // returns true (default)
  
    config.setIgnoreUnmatchedProperty(false);
    boolean strict = config.isIgnoreUnmatchedProperty();   // returns false
  ```
##### setIgnoreUnmatchedProperty(...) -> C
- **Signature:** `public C setIgnoreUnmatchedProperty(final boolean ignoreUnmatchedProperty)`
- **Summary:** Sets whether unmatched properties should be ignored during deserialization.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful when deserializing data that may contain extra fields not present in the target class.
  - When set to `false`, the parser will throw a com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException (e.g.
  - `"Unknown property: zzz"`) when encountering properties in the source data that don't have corresponding fields in the target class.
- **Parameters:**
  - `ignoreUnmatchedProperty` (`boolean`) — `true` to ignore unmatched properties, `false` to throw a `ParsingException`
- **Returns:** this configuration instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // JSON: {"name": "John", "age": 30, "unknownField": "value"}
    // Target class only has name and age properties
    config.setIgnoreUnmatchedProperty(true);    // unknownField is ignored
    config.setIgnoreUnmatchedProperty(false);   // unknownField is rejected, causing an exception
  ```

- **Summary:** Gets the element type for collection and array deserialization.
- **Contract:**

- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the configured element type, or `null` if not set
- **Examples:**

  ```java
    Type<Object> none = config.getElementType();  // returns null (not set)
  
    config.setElementType(String.class);
    Type<String> type = config.getElementType();   // returns the String type
    String typeName = type.name();                 // returns "String"
  ```

##### copy(...) -> C
- **Signature:** `@Override public C copy()`
- **Summary:** Creates a copy of this configuration.
- **Contract:**
  - In addition to the shallow copy made by ParserConfig#copy(), the value-type map is copied, so #setValueType(String, Type) on the copy never affects the original (and vice versa), regardless of whether the original already had value types when it was copied.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a copy of this configuration with its own value-type map
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  JsonDeserConfig original = new JsonDeserConfig().setValueType("x", String.class);
    JsonDeserConfig copy = original.copy().setValueType("y", Integer.class);
    original.getValueType("y");   // returns null - the original is untouched
  ```

##### isIgnoreNullOrEmpty(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public boolean isIgnoreNullOrEmpty()`
- **Summary:** Checks whether `null` or empty values in the JSON source should be silently ignored (i.e., not assigned to the target bean property) during deserialization.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** `true` if `null` or empty source values are ignored and the target property is left unchanged, `false` (default) if they are assigned normally
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  JsonDeserConfig config = new JsonDeserConfig();
    boolean ignored = config.isIgnoreNullOrEmpty(); // returns false (default)
  
    config.setIgnoreNullOrEmpty(true);
    boolean enabled = config.isIgnoreNullOrEmpty(); // returns true
  ```
##### setIgnoreNullOrEmpty(...) -> JsonDeserConfig
- **Signature:** `public JsonDeserConfig setIgnoreNullOrEmpty(final boolean ignoreNullOrEmpty)`
- **Summary:** Sets whether `null` or empty values encountered in the JSON source should be ignored during deserialization.
- **Contract:**
  - When `true`, a JSON `null` or empty string will not overwrite the corresponding property on the target bean, leaving it at its existing value.
- **Parameters:**
  - `ignoreNullOrEmpty` (`boolean`) — `true` to skip assigning `null` or empty JSON values to target properties; `false` (default) to assign them normally
- **Returns:** `this` instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  JsonDeserConfig config = new JsonDeserConfig();
    config.setIgnoreNullOrEmpty(true);                 // returns this (config)
    boolean enabled = config.isIgnoreNullOrEmpty();    // returns true
  
    config.setIgnoreNullOrEmpty(false);                // returns this (config)
    boolean disabled = config.isIgnoreNullOrEmpty();   // returns false (default)
  ```
##### isReadNullToEmpty(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public boolean isReadNullToEmpty()`
- **Summary:** Checks whether `null` values should be deserialized to empty values (empty CharSequence/Array/Collection/Map) instead of `null`.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** `true` if `null` values are read as empty, `false` (default) otherwise
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  JsonDeserConfig config = new JsonDeserConfig();
    boolean asNull = config.isReadNullToEmpty(); // returns false (default)
  
    config.setReadNullToEmpty(true);
    boolean asEmpty = config.isReadNullToEmpty(); // returns true
  ```

##### getMapInstanceType(...) -> Class<? extends Map>
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("rawtypes") public Class<? extends Map> getMapInstanceType()`
- **Summary:** Gets the Map implementation class to use when deserializing to Map instances.
- **Contract:**
  - This returns the concrete Map class that will be instantiated when the deserializer needs to create a Map instance.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the Map implementation class
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  JsonDeserConfig config = new JsonDeserConfig();
    Class<?> type = config.getMapInstanceType(); // returns HashMap.class (default)
  
    config.setMapInstanceType(java.util.LinkedHashMap.class);
    Class<?> updated = config.getMapInstanceType(); // returns LinkedHashMap.class
  ```
- **See also:** #setMapInstanceType(Class)
##### setMapInstanceType(...) -> JsonDeserConfig
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("rawtypes") public JsonDeserConfig setMapInstanceType(final Class<? extends Map> mapInstanceType) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets the Map implementation class to use when deserializing to Map instances.
- **Contract:**
  - `Map`/`AbstractMap` -> `HashMap`, `SortedMap` -> `TreeMap`, `EnumMap` -> `HashMap`); an unsupported abstract class fails when the first map is created, not in this setter.
  - A concrete class must have a public no-argument constructor.
- **Parameters:**
  - `mapInstanceType` (`Class<? extends Map>`) — the Map implementation class to use (must not be `null`); interfaces/abstract classes are resolved by `Suppliers.ofMap` at deserialization time
- **Returns:** `this` instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapInstanceType` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  config.setMapInstanceType(LinkedHashMap.class);
    // Maps will be created as LinkedHashMap to preserve insertion order
  
    config.setMapInstanceType(TreeMap.class);
    // Maps will be created as TreeMap for sorted keys
    parser.deserialize(json, config, Map.class);       // -> TreeMap
    parser.deserialize(json, config, HashMap.class);   // -> HashMap (declared concrete type wins)
  ```
##### setPropHandler(...) -> JsonDeserConfig
- **Signature:** `public JsonDeserConfig setPropHandler(final String propName, final BiConsumer<? super Collection<Object>, ?> handler) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets a custom handler for processing collection property values during deserialization.
- **Parameters:**
  - `propName` (`String`) — the local property or map-key name under which the JSON array appears (dotted paths are not resolved)
  - `handler` (`BiConsumer<? super Collection<Object>, ?>`) — the handler invoked for each element of a JSON array property (first parameter is the Collection being populated, second is the current element)
- **Returns:** `this` instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `propName` is empty or `handler` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  config.setPropHandler("items", (collection, element) -> {
        // Custom processing for each element
        if (element != null && isValid(element)) {
            collection.add(processElement(element));
        }
    });
  
    // Matched by the local property name, at any nesting depth
    config.setPropHandler("model", (collection, model) -> {
        collection.add(model.toString().toUpperCase());
    });
  ```
##### getPropHandler(...) -> BiConsumer<? super Collection<Object>, ?>
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull public BiConsumer<? super Collection<Object>, ?> getPropHandler(final String propName) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Gets the property handler for the specified property name.
- **Contract:**
  - If no handler has been registered for the property, this method returns `null`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `propName` (`String`) — the property name (must not be empty)
- **Returns:** the handler for the property, or `null` if not set (may return null)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `propName` is empty.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  JsonDeserConfig config = new JsonDeserConfig();
    Object handler = config.getPropHandler("items"); // returns null (none registered)
  
    config.setPropHandler("items", (collection, element) -> collection.add(element));
    Object registered = config.getPropHandler("items"); // returns the registered handler (non-null)
  ```
- **See also:** #setPropHandler(String, BiConsumer)

### Interface JsonParser (com.landawn.abacus.parser.JsonParser)
Interface for JSON parsing and serialization operations.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

##### parse(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `<T> T parse(String source, Type<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException, ParsingException, UncheckedIOException`
- **Summary:** Parses a JSON string into an object of the specified type.
- **Contract:**
  - See the class-level documentation for when to prefer `parse()` over `deserialize()`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`String`) — the JSON string to parse (may be `null` or empty, in which case the target type's default value, or an empty value, is returned)
  - `targetType` (`Type<? extends T>`) — the type of the target object to deserialize into (must not be `null`)
- **Returns:** an instance of `T` parsed from the JSON string; if `source` is `null` or empty, the target type's default value (or an empty value) is returned
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetType` is `null`
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if the source contains invalid JSON
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if a delegated value reader or converter reports an I/O failure while materializing values from the JSON text
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String json = "{\"name\":\"John\",\"age\":30}";
    Person person = parser.parse(json, Type.of(Person.class));
  
    // For collections
    String jsonArray = "[{\"id\":1},{\"id\":2}]";
    List<Item> items = parser.parse(jsonArray, Type.of(new com.landawn.abacus.util.TypeReference<List<Item>>() {}));
  ```
- **See also:** #parseInto(String, Collection), #parseInto(String, Map)

##### parseInto(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `void parseInto(String source, Object[] output) throws IllegalArgumentException, IndexOutOfBoundsException, ParsingException, UncheckedIOException`
- **Summary:** Parses a JSON string into an existing array.
- **Contract:**
  - The array must have room for all retained elements; unused output slots are left unchanged.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`String`) — the JSON string to parse (may be `null` or empty, in which case the method returns without modifying `output`); accepts an array or the parser's supported unwrapped element sequence
  - `output` (`Object[]`) — the pre-allocated array to populate with parsed values (must not be `null`)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `output` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if more parsed elements are retained than the output array can hold
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if the source contains invalid JSON
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if a delegated value reader or converter reports an I/O failure while materializing values from the JSON text
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String json = "[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]";
    Integer[] numbers = new Integer[5];
    parser.parseInto(json, numbers);
    // numbers array is now filled with values [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
  ```

  - `output` (`Collection<?>`) — the Collection to populate with parsed values, must not be `null`; existing elements are preserved

##### deserialize(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `<T> T deserialize(String source, int fromIndex, int toIndex, Type<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException, IndexOutOfBoundsException, ParsingException, UncheckedIOException`
- **Summary:** Deserializes a range of a JSON string into an object of the specified type.
- **Contract:**
  - Useful when the JSON payload is embedded in a larger string.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`String`) — the JSON string containing the data to deserialize
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the starting index (inclusive) of the JSON content
  - `toIndex` (`int`) — the ending index (exclusive) of the JSON content
  - `targetType` (`Type<? extends T>`) — the type of the target object (must not be `null`)
- **Returns:** an instance of `T` deserialized from the JSON string; if the selected range is empty, the target type's default value (or an empty value) is returned
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetType` is `null`
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if the indices are out of bounds or `fromIndex > toIndex`
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if the selected range contains invalid JSON
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if a delegated value reader or converter reports an I/O failure while materializing values from the JSON text
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String json = "prefix{\"name\":\"John\"}suffix";
    // Deserialize only the JSON object part (indices 6 to 21)
    Person person = parser.deserialize(json, 6, 21, Type.of(Person.class));
  ```

##### stream(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `<T> Stream<T> stream(String source, Type<? extends T> elementType) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException, ParsingException`
- **Summary:** Creates a stream for parsing JSON array elements lazily from a JSON string.
- **Contract:**
  - The stream should be closed after use to free resources.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`String`) — the JSON string containing a JSON array (may be `null` or empty, in which case an empty stream is returned)
  - `elementType` (`Type<? extends T>`) — the type of array elements. Only Bean/Map/MapEntity/Collection/Array/Dataset/Sheet/EntityId element types are supported.
- **Returns:** a `Stream` of parsed elements that must be closed after use; never `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `elementType` is null or unsupported for streaming.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if the root of the source is a JSON object or a quoted string
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if the initial token is an unquoted scalar or malformed JSON; malformed later elements fail while consuming the returned stream.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String json = "[{\"id\":1},{\"id\":2},{\"id\":3}]";
    try (Stream<MyObject> stream = parser.stream(json, Type.of(MyObject.class))) {
        stream.filter(obj -> obj.getId() > 1)
              .forEach(obj -> processObject(obj));
    }
  ```

  - `elementType` (`Type<? extends T>`) — the type of array elements. Only Bean/Map/MapEntity/Collection/Array/Dataset/Sheet/EntityId element types are supported.

- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `source` is null, or `elementType` is null or unsupported for streaming.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if opening or initially reading the source fails; later read failures are raised while consuming the returned stream.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if the root of the source content is a JSON object or a quoted string
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if the initial token is an unquoted scalar or malformed JSON; malformed later elements fail while consuming the returned stream.
- **Examples:**
  ```java

    }
    // InputStream is automatically closed when stream is closed
  ```

### Class JsonSerConfig (com.landawn.abacus.parser.JsonSerConfig)
Configuration class for JSON serialization operations.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- `public JsonSerConfig()` — Creates a new instance of JsonSerConfig with default settings.
  ```java
  JsonSerConfig config = new JsonSerConfig();
    String json = parser.serialize(object, config);
  ```

#### Public Static Methods
##### create(...) -> JsonSerConfig
- **Signature:** `public static JsonSerConfig create()`
- **Summary:** Creates a new instance of JsonSerConfig with default settings.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a new JsonSerConfig instance
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  JsonSerConfig config = JsonSerConfig.create()
        .setPrettyFormat(true)
        .setDateTimeFormat(DateTimeFormat.ISO_8601_DATE_TIME);
  ```

#### Public Instance Methods
##### isWriteNullToEmpty(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public boolean isWriteNullToEmpty()`
- **Summary:** Checks if `null` bean properties should be written as empty values.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** `true` if `null` CharSequence/collection/array/Map bean properties should be written as `""`/`\[\]`/{}, `false` otherwise
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  JsonSerConfig config = new JsonSerConfig();
    config.isWriteNullToEmpty();                  // returns false (default)
    config.setWriteNullToEmpty(true);
    config.isWriteNullToEmpty();                  // returns true
  ```
##### setWriteNullToEmpty(...) -> JsonSerConfig
- **Signature:** `public JsonSerConfig setWriteNullToEmpty(final boolean writeNullToEmpty)`
- **Summary:** Sets whether `null` bean properties should be written as empty values during serialization.
- **Contract:**
  - Only bean properties are affected, and only when they survive the exclusion strategy: the default exclusion (Exclusion#NULL, applied when no exclusion is set on the config or on the bean's `@JsonXmlConfig`) drops `null` properties before this flag is consulted, so the flag has no visible effect unless the effective exclusion is Exclusion#NONE, selected through #setExclusion(Exclusion) or the bean annotation.
  - This flag only wins over #setWriteNullStringAsEmpty(boolean), for the slots that have an empty form: a surviving `null` `CharSequence`/collection/array/`Map` property is emptied even when that flag is off.
  - A `null` number or boolean has no empty form, so #setWriteNullNumberAsZero(boolean) / #setWriteNullBooleanAsFalse(boolean) still apply to such a property when they are on, writing `0` / `false`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `writeNullToEmpty` (`boolean`) — `true` to write surviving `null` CharSequence/collection/array/Map bean properties as `""`/`\[\]`/{}, `false` to write them as `null`
- **Returns:** `this` instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  JsonSerConfig config = new JsonSerConfig().setWriteNullToEmpty(true);
    config.isWriteNullToEmpty();                  // returns true
    config.setWriteNullToEmpty(false);
    config.isWriteNullToEmpty();                  // returns false
  
    // bean with String s = null, List<String> l = null, Map<String, Integer> m = null, Integer i = null, Address a = null:
    jsonParser.serialize(bean, new JsonSerConfig().setWriteNullToEmpty(true));
    // -> {}                                                          (default Exclusion.NULL drops them first)
    jsonParser.serialize(bean, new JsonSerConfig().setWriteNullToEmpty(true).setExclusion(Exclusion.NONE));
    // -> {"s": "", "l": [], "m": {}, "i": null, "a": null}          (number and nested bean stay null)
  ```
- **See also:** #setExclusion(Exclusion)

  ```java
    // map {"str" -> 1, 2 -> 2, true -> 3, null -> 4}
    jsonParser.serialize(map, new JsonSerConfig().setQuoteMapKey(false));   // {"str": 1, 2: 2, true: 3, null: 4}
    jsonParser.serialize(map, new JsonSerConfig().setQuoteMapKey(true));    // {"str": 1, "2": 2, "true": 3, "null": 4}
  ```

##### getPropNamingPolicy(...) -> NamingPolicy
- **Signature:** `public NamingPolicy getPropNamingPolicy()`
- **Summary:** Gets the property naming policy used during serialization.
- **Contract:**
  - `null` (the default) does not mean "original names": it means the bean's own `@JsonXmlConfig(namingPolicy)` annotation applies, falling back to NamingPolicy#CAMEL_CASE (which leaves conventional `camelCase` property names unchanged) when the bean is not annotated.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the property naming policy, or `null` (default) if the bean's own `@JsonXmlConfig(namingPolicy)` applies, falling back to NamingPolicy#CAMEL_CASE
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  JsonSerConfig config = new JsonSerConfig();
    config.getPropNamingPolicy();                                                // returns null (default: the bean's @JsonXmlConfig policy, else CAMEL_CASE)
    config.setPropNamingPolicy(NamingPolicy.SNAKE_CASE).getPropNamingPolicy();   // returns SNAKE_CASE
  ```
##### setPropNamingPolicy(...) -> C
- **Signature:** `public C setPropNamingPolicy(final NamingPolicy propNamingPolicy)`
- **Summary:** Sets the property naming policy for serialization.
- **Parameters:**
  - `propNamingPolicy` (`NamingPolicy`) — the naming policy to use for bean properties, or `null` to defer to each bean's `@JsonXmlConfig(namingPolicy)` (falling back to NamingPolicy#CAMEL_CASE)
- **Returns:** this instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  config.setPropNamingPolicy(NamingPolicy.CAMEL_CASE);
    // Property "firstName" remains "firstName"; a bean annotated with SNAKE_CASE is forced back to "firstName" too
  
    config.setPropNamingPolicy(NamingPolicy.SNAKE_CASE);
    // Property "firstName" becomes "first_name"; Map key "firstName" stays "firstName"
  
    config.setPropNamingPolicy(NamingPolicy.SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE);
    // Property "firstName" becomes "FIRST_NAME"
  
    config.setPropNamingPolicy(null);
    // Each bean's own @JsonXmlConfig(namingPolicy) applies, falling back to CAMEL_CASE
  ```

- **Signature:** `public boolean isWriteNullStringAsEmpty()`
- **Summary:** Checks if `null` string values should be written as empty strings.

- **Returns:** `true` if `null` string bean properties and typed string elements are written as `""` in JSON, `false` otherwise
- **Examples:**
  ```java

    config.isWriteNullStringAsEmpty();                                   // returns false (default)
    config.setWriteNullStringAsEmpty(true).isWriteNullStringAsEmpty();   // returns true
  ```
##### setWriteNullStringAsEmpty(...) -> C
- **Signature:** `public C setWriteNullStringAsEmpty(final boolean writeNullStringAsEmpty)`
- **Summary:** Sets whether to write `null` string values as empty strings.
- **Contract:**
  - Scope (JSON): the flag is consulted wherever a `null` is rendered through the com.landawn.abacus.type.Type of a `String`/`CharSequence` slot: `null` bean properties declared as `String`/`CharSequence` - but only when the property survives the exclusion strategy: the default Exclusion#NULL drops `null` properties before this flag is consulted, so use SerializationConfig#setExclusion(Exclusion) with Exclusion#NONE to see the effect.
  - JsonSerConfig#setWriteNullToEmpty(boolean) empties a `null` `CharSequence` property even when this flag is off, so the two agree on `""` for strings.
- **Parameters:**
  - `writeNullStringAsEmpty` (`boolean`) — `true` to write `null` string bean properties and typed string elements as `""` in JSON, `false` to write `null`
- **Returns:** this instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  JsonSerConfig config = new JsonSerConfig();
    config.setWriteNullStringAsEmpty(true).isWriteNullStringAsEmpty();    // returns true
    config.setWriteNullStringAsEmpty(false).isWriteNullStringAsEmpty();   // returns false
  
    // JSON output of a bean with String name = null, Integer age = null, List<String> tags = ["a", null]:
    jsonParser.serialize(bean, new JsonSerConfig().setWriteNullStringAsEmpty(true));
    // -> {"tags": ["a", ""]}                                  (default Exclusion.NULL dropped name and age)
    jsonParser.serialize(bean, new JsonSerConfig().setWriteNullStringAsEmpty(true).setExclusion(Exclusion.NONE));
    // -> {"name": "", "age": null, "tags": ["a", ""]}         (only the String slots are affected)
  ```

##### setCircularReferenceSupported(...) -> C
- **Signature:** `public C setCircularReferenceSupported(final boolean circularReferenceSupported)`
- **Summary:** Sets whether to support circular references during serialization.
- **Contract:**
  - When enabled, the JSON and XML parsers track objects on the current serialization path and write a null representation for a repeated reference.
  - This prevents recursion; it does not encode object identities or reconstruct the original cycle when deserialized.
  - When disabled, those parsers reject excessive nesting rather than tracking identities.
- **Parameters:**
  - `circularReferenceSupported` (`boolean`) — `true` to support circular references, `false` otherwise
- **Returns:** this instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  JsonSerConfig config = new JsonSerConfig();
    config.setCircularReferenceSupported(true).isCircularReferenceSupported();    // returns true
    config.setCircularReferenceSupported(false).isCircularReferenceSupported();   // returns false
  ```

### Class KryoParser (com.landawn.abacus.parser.KryoParser)
High-performance binary serialization parser using the Kryo framework.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### serialize(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `@Override public String serialize(final Object obj, final KryoSerConfig config) throws UncheckedIOException, KryoException`
- **Summary:** Serializes an object to a Base64 encoded string representation.
- **Parameters:**
  - `obj` (`Object`) — the object to serialize (may be `null`)
  - `config` (`KryoSerConfig`) — the serialization configuration to use (may be `null` for default behavior)
- **Returns:** the Base64 encoded string representation of the serialized object
- **Throws:**
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if a configured serializer reports an I/O cause while encoding the object graph

##### shallowCopy(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public <T> T shallowCopy(final T source) throws KryoException`
- **Summary:** Creates a shallow copy of the source object.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`T`) — the object to shallow copy
- **Returns:** a shallow copy of the source object
- **Throws:**
  - `com.esotericsoftware.kryo.KryoException` — if a copied object cannot be instantiated or copied by its registered serializer
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MyObject original = new MyObject();
    original.setName("Test");
    original.setList(new ArrayList<>(List.of("a", "b")));
  
    MyObject copy = parser.shallowCopy(original);
    // copy.getName() equals "Test"
    // copy.getList() == original.getList() (same reference)
  ```

  ```java
    original.setList(new ArrayList<>(List.of("a", "b")));

    // copy.getName() equals "Test"
  ```

##### register(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public void register(final Class<?> type) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Registers a class with this parser instance for improved performance.
- **Contract:**
  - If the class was registered previously through another overload, this call replaces that registration; the most recent call is authoritative.
- **Parameters:**
  - `type` (`Class<?>`) — the class to register
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if type is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  parser.register(MyDomainObject.class);
    parser.register(MyValueObject.class);
    // Now these classes will serialize more efficiently
  ```
- **Signature:** `public void register(final Class<?> type, final int id) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Registers a class with a specific ID for this parser instance.
- **Contract:**
  - If the ID is one of the primitive slots (0 for `int` and 2-8 for `float`, `boolean`, `byte`, `char`, `short`, `long` and `double`), the displaced primitive and its wrapper are re-registered with their original serializer at the next free implicit ID instead, so they stay serializable.
  - That implicit ID depends on the order in which registrations are replayed (built-ins, then global, then instance registrations), so two JVMs exchanging payloads that contain the displaced type must perform the same registrations.
- **Parameters:**
  - `type` (`Class<?>`) — the class to register
  - `id` (`int`) — the non-negative unique ID for this class
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if type is `null`, `id` is negative, or `id` is already assigned to another class.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  parser.register(User.class, 100);
    parser.register(Order.class, 101);
    parser.register(Product.class, 102);
  ```
- **Signature:** `public void register(final Class<?> type, final Serializer<?> serializer) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Registers a class with a custom serializer for this parser instance.
- **Parameters:**
  - `type` (`Class<?>`) — the class to register
  - `serializer` (`Serializer<?>`) — the custom serializer for this class
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if type or serializer is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  parser.register(DateTime.class, new DateTimeSerializer());
    parser.register(Money.class, new MoneySerializer());
  ```
- **Signature:** `public void register(final Class<?> type, final Serializer<?> serializer, final int id) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Registers a class with a custom serializer and specific ID for this parser instance.
- **Parameters:**
  - `type` (`Class<?>`) — the class to register
  - `serializer` (`Serializer<?>`) — the custom serializer for this class
  - `id` (`int`) — the non-negative unique ID for this class
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if type or serializer is `null`, `id` is negative, or `id` is already assigned to another class.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  parser.register(BigDecimal.class, new BigDecimalSerializer(), 200);
    parser.register(UUID.class, new UUIDSerializer(), 201);
  ```

### Class KryoSerConfig (com.landawn.abacus.parser.KryoSerConfig)
Configuration class for Kryo serialization settings.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- `public KryoSerConfig()` — Creates a new `KryoSerConfig` with default settings.
  ```java
  KryoSerConfig config = new KryoSerConfig()
        .setWriteClass(true);
  ```

#### Public Static Methods
##### create(...) -> KryoSerConfig
- **Signature:** `public static KryoSerConfig create()`
- **Summary:** Creates a new `KryoSerConfig` instance with default settings.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a new `KryoSerConfig` instance
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  KryoSerConfig config = KryoSerConfig.create()
        .setWriteClass(true);
  ```

#### Public Instance Methods
##### isWriteClass(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public boolean isWriteClass()`
- **Summary:** Checks if class information should be written during serialization.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** `true` if class information should be written, `false` otherwise
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  KryoSerConfig config = new KryoSerConfig();
    boolean writes = config.isWriteClass();  // returns false (default)
  
    config.setWriteClass(true);
    boolean enabled = config.isWriteClass();  // returns true
  ```
##### setWriteClass(...) -> KryoSerConfig
- **Signature:** `public KryoSerConfig setWriteClass(final boolean writeClass)`
- **Summary:** Sets whether class metadata should be written with the object during serialization.
- **Contract:**
  - When `true` (or when the object is `null`), KryoParser writes both class and object so deserialization must use a null `Class` target to read that format.
  - When `false` (default), only the object is written and deserialization must supply the target type.
- **Parameters:**
  - `writeClass` (`boolean`) — `true` to write class information, `false` to omit it
- **Returns:** this configuration instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  KryoSerConfig config = new KryoSerConfig();
    config.setWriteClass(true);                 // returns this (config) for chaining
    boolean enabled = config.isWriteClass();    // returns true
  
    config.setWriteClass(false);                // returns this (config) for chaining
    boolean disabled = config.isWriteClass();   // returns false (default)
  ```
##### hashCode(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `@Override public int hashCode()`
- **Summary:** Computes a hash code for this configuration based on its settings.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a hash code value for this configuration
##### equals(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@SuppressFBWarnings @Override public boolean equals(final Object obj)`
- **Summary:** Determines whether this configuration is equal to another object.
- **Contract:**
  - Two `KryoSerConfig` instances are considered equal if they are of exactly the same class, all inherited settings are equal (see SerializationConfig#equals(Object)), and they have the same `writeClass` setting.
- **Parameters:**
  - `obj` (`Object`) — the object to compare with
- **Returns:** `true` if the configurations are equal, `false` otherwise
##### toString(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `@Override public String toString()`
- **Summary:** Returns a string representation of this configuration.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a string representation of this configuration

### Class ParserConfig (com.landawn.abacus.parser.ParserConfig)
Abstract base class for parser configuration that provides common settings shared by both serialization and deserialization configurations.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### getIgnoredPropNames(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public Map<Class<?>, Set<String>> getIgnoredPropNames()`
- **Summary:** Gets the complete map of ignored property names organized by class.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the map of ignored properties by class, or `null` if none are configured
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  KryoSerConfig config = new KryoSerConfig();
    Map<Class<?>, Set<String>> none = config.getIgnoredPropNames();  // returns null (none configured)
  
    config.setIgnoredPropNames(Set.of("password", "version"));
    Map<Class<?>, Set<String>> map = config.getIgnoredPropNames();
    Set<String> global = map.get(Object.class);  // returns ["password", "version"] (global ignores)
  ```
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull public Collection<String> getIgnoredPropNames(final Class<?> cls)`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Gets the ignored property names for a specific class.
- **Contract:**
  - If none are found (no entry for the class, or an entry set to `null`), it returns the globally ignored properties (those registered for `Object.class`).
- **Parameters:**
  - `cls` (`Class<?>`) — the class to get ignored properties for
- **Returns:** collection of ignored property names, or `null` if none are configured (may return null)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Collection<String> ignoredProps = config.getIgnoredPropNames(User.class);
    if (ignoredProps != null) {
        // Process ignored properties
    }
  ```
##### setIgnoredPropNames(...) -> C
- **Signature:** `public C setIgnoredPropNames(final Set<String> ignoredPropNames) throws UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Sets globally ignored property names that apply to all classes.
- **Parameters:**
  - `ignoredPropNames` (`Set<String>`) — set of property names to ignore globally; `null` keeps an (empty) entry for `Object.class`
- **Returns:** this configuration instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if the previously supplied ignored-property map does not support adding or replacing the entry.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  config.setIgnoredPropNames(Set.of("internalId", "version", "deleted"));
  
    config.setIgnoredPropNames((Set<String>) null);            // no global ignores, but getIgnoredPropNames() is {Object.class=null}
    config.setIgnoredPropNames((Map<Class<?>, Set<String>>) null);   // getIgnoredPropNames() is null again
  ```
- **Signature:** `public C setIgnoredPropNames(final Class<?> cls, final Set<String> ignoredPropNames) throws UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Sets ignored property names for a specific class.
- **Contract:**
  - A non-null set overrides the global settings for this class - including an empty set, which makes the class ignore nothing even when a global set exists.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cls` (`Class<?>`) — the class to set ignored properties for
  - `ignoredPropNames` (`Set<String>`) — set of property names to ignore for this class; an empty set overrides the global set with "nothing", `null` removes the class-specific override so the global set applies again
- **Returns:** this configuration instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if the previously supplied ignored-property map does not support adding or replacing the entry.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  config.setIgnoredPropNames(User.class, Set.of("password", "salt"));
    config.setIgnoredPropNames(Order.class, Set.of("internalNotes"));
  
    config.setIgnoredPropNames(Set.of("version"));                 // global
    config.setIgnoredPropNames(Audit.class, Set.of());             // Audit ignores nothing (overrides the global set)
    config.setIgnoredPropNames(User.class, null);                  // User falls back to the global set: ["version"]
  ```
- **Signature:** `public C setIgnoredPropNames(final Map<Class<?>, Set<String>> ignoredPropNames)`
- **Summary:** Sets the complete map of ignored property names by class.
- **Parameters:**
  - `ignoredPropNames` (`Map<Class<?>, Set<String>>`) — complete map of ignored properties by class
- **Returns:** this configuration instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<Class<?>, Set<String>> ignoredMap = new HashMap<>();
    ignoredMap.put(Object.class, Set.of("version"));
    ignoredMap.put(User.class, Set.of("password"));
    config.setIgnoredPropNames(ignoredMap);
  ```
##### copy(...) -> C
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("unchecked") public C copy()`
- **Summary:** Creates a copy of this configuration.
- **Contract:**
  - The ignored-property map is copied, so #setIgnoredPropNames(Class, Set) / #setIgnoredPropNames(Set) / #setIgnoredPropNames(Map) on the copy never affects the original (and vice versa), regardless of whether the original already had ignored properties when it was copied.
  - The sets it holds are shared, but the setters replace an entry rather than mutate a set, so a shared set only changes if the caller mutates it directly.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a copy of this configuration with its own ignored-property map
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  JsonSerConfig original = new JsonSerConfig().setPrettyFormat(true);
    JsonSerConfig copy = original.copy();
    // copy has the same settings as original
  
    copy.setIgnoredPropNames(User.class, Set.of("password"));
    original.getIgnoredPropNames(User.class);   // returns null - the original is untouched
  ```

##### registerKryo(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static void registerKryo(final Class<?> type) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Registers a class with Kryo for serialization.
- **Contract:**
  - If this class was registered previously through another overload, this call replaces that registration; the most recent call is authoritative.
- **Parameters:**
  - `type` (`Class<?>`) — the class to register (must not be `null`)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `type` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Register commonly used classes
    ParserFactory.registerKryo(MyDomainObject.class);
    ParserFactory.registerKryo(MyValueObject.class);
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static void registerKryo(final Class<?> type, final int id) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Registers a class with Kryo using a specific ID.
- **Parameters:**
  - `type` (`Class<?>`) — the class to register (must not be `null`)
  - `id` (`int`) — the non-negative unique ID for this class
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `type` is `null`, `id` is negative, or `id` is assigned to another class.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Register with fixed IDs for compatibility
    ParserFactory.registerKryo(User.class, 100);
    ParserFactory.registerKryo(Order.class, 101);
    ParserFactory.registerKryo(Product.class, 102);
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static void registerKryo(final Class<?> type, final Serializer<?> serializer) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Registers a class with Kryo using a custom serializer.
- **Parameters:**
  - `type` (`Class<?>`) — the class to register (must not be `null`)
  - `serializer` (`Serializer<?>`) — the custom serializer for this class (must not be `null`)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `type` or `serializer` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Register with custom serializer
    ParserFactory.registerKryo(DateTime.class, new DateTimeSerializer());
    ParserFactory.registerKryo(Money.class, new MoneySerializer());
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static void registerKryo(final Class<?> type, final Serializer<?> serializer, final int id) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Registers a class with Kryo using a custom serializer and specific ID.
- **Parameters:**
  - `type` (`Class<?>`) — the class to register (must not be `null`)
  - `serializer` (`Serializer<?>`) — the custom serializer for this class (must not be `null`)
  - `id` (`int`) — the non-negative unique ID for this class
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `type` or `serializer` is `null`, `id` is negative, or `id` is assigned to another class.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Register with both custom serializer and ID
    ParserFactory.registerKryo(BigDecimal.class, new BigDecimalSerializer(), 200);
    ParserFactory.registerKryo(UUID.class, new UUIDSerializer(), 201);
  ```

  ```java
  BeanInfo first = ParserUtil.getBeanInfo(User.class);
  ```

##### getPropInfo(...) -> PropInfo
- **Signature:** `@Override public PropInfo getPropInfo(final String propName) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Gets property information by property name.

- **Returns:** the PropInfo for the property, or `null` if not found

- **See also:** PropInfo
- **Signature:** `public PropInfo getPropInfo(final PropInfo propInfoFromOtherBean)`
- **Summary:** Gets property information using property information from another bean.
- **Contract:**
  - This method attempts to find a matching property by first checking the property name, then checking any aliases if the direct name match fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `propInfoFromOtherBean` (`PropInfo`) — property information from another bean
- **Returns:** matching PropInfo in this bean, or `null` if no match found
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  BeanInfo sourceBeanInfo = ParserUtil.getBeanInfo(SourceBean.class);
    BeanInfo targetBeanInfo = ParserUtil.getBeanInfo(TargetBean.class);
    PropInfo sourceProp = sourceBeanInfo.getPropInfo("firstName");
    PropInfo targetProp = targetBeanInfo.getPropInfo(sourceProp);
  ```
##### getPropValue(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("unchecked") public <T> T getPropValue(final Object obj, final String propName) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Gets the value of a property from the specified object.
- **Contract:**
  - If any intermediate property in a nested path is `null`, returns the default value for the final property type.
- **Parameters:**
  - `obj` (`Object`) — the object to get the property value from
  - `propName` (`String`) — the property name (supports nested paths)
- **Returns:** the property value, or the type's default value if an intermediate object in a nested path is `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if no getter method is found for the property.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Person person = new Person("John", 30);
    Object value = beanInfo.getPropValue(person, "name");
    Object nestedValue = beanInfo.getPropValue(person, "address.city");
  ```
##### setPropValue(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public void setPropValue(final Object obj, final String propName, final Object propValue) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets the value of a property on the specified object.
- **Parameters:**
  - `obj` (`Object`) — the object to set the property value on
  - `propName` (`String`) — the property name
  - `propValue` (`Object`) — the value to set
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if no setter is found for `propName`, or the property is read-only (a getter with no backing field and no setter).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Person person = new Person();
    beanInfo.setPropValue(person, "name", "John");
    beanInfo.setPropValue(person, "age", 30);
  ```
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("rawtypes") public boolean setPropValue(final Object obj, final String propName, final Object propValue, final boolean ignoreUnmatchedProperty) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets the value of a property on the specified object with optional unmatched property handling.
- **Contract:**
  - For nested properties, intermediate objects are created as needed if they are `null`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `obj` (`Object`) — the object to set the property value on
  - `propName` (`String`) — the property name (supports nested paths)
  - `propValue` (`Object`) — the value to set
  - `ignoreUnmatchedProperty` (`boolean`) — if `true`, silently ignore properties that don't exist or that are read-only (a getter with no backing field and no setter)
- **Returns:** `true` if the property was set, `false` if it was ignored
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if no setter is found for `propName`, or the property is read-only, and `ignoreUnmatchedProperty` is `false`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Person person = new Person();
    beanInfo.setPropValue(person, "name", "John", false);
    beanInfo.setPropValue(person, "address.city", "New York", true);
  ```
- **Signature:** `public void setPropValue(final Object obj, final PropInfo propInfoFromOtherBean, final Object propValue) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets a property value using property information from another bean.
- **Parameters:**
  - `obj` (`Object`) — the object to set the property value on
  - `propInfoFromOtherBean` (`PropInfo`) — property information from another bean
  - `propValue` (`Object`) — the value to set
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if no writable property is found for the name or any of its aliases (a read-only property - a getter with no backing field and no setter - counts as no match).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Person source = new Person("John", 30);
    Person target = new Person();
    PropInfo sourceProp = sourceBeanInfo.getPropInfo("name");
    targetBeanInfo.setPropValue(target, sourceProp, source.getName());
  ```
- **Signature:** `public boolean setPropValue(final Object obj, final PropInfo propInfoFromOtherBean, final Object propValue, final boolean ignoreUnmatchedProperty) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets a property value using property information from another bean with optional unmatched property handling.
- **Parameters:**
  - `obj` (`Object`) — the object to set the property value on
  - `propInfoFromOtherBean` (`PropInfo`) — property information from another bean
  - `propValue` (`Object`) — the value to set
  - `ignoreUnmatchedProperty` (`boolean`) — if `true`, silently ignore properties that don't exist or that are read-only (a getter with no backing field and no setter)
- **Returns:** `true` if the property was set, `false` if it was ignored
- **Throws:**

- **Examples:**

##### readPropInfo(...) -> PropInfo
- **Signature:** `@Override public PropInfo readPropInfo(final char[] cbuf, final int fromIndex, final int toIndex)`
- **Summary:** Reads property information from a character buffer for efficient parsing.
- **Contract:**
  - The answer is the same one #getPropInfo(String) gives for the exact text: when two properties share a naming-policy spelling or column name (for example `userName` and `user_name` both spell `USER_NAME`), the explicit binding - `@Column`, alias, then declaration order - wins, whichever property the length/hash shortcut proposed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cbuf` (`char[]`) — the character buffer containing the property name
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the starting index in the buffer
  - `toIndex` (`int`) — the ending index in the buffer
- **Returns:** the PropInfo if found, `null` otherwise
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  char[] buffer = "name".toCharArray();
    PropInfo propInfo = beanInfo.readPropInfo(buffer, 0, buffer.length);
  ```

  - This method handles different access strategies: For immutable beans stored as arrays, directly accesses the array element For regular objects, uses field access if available, otherwise uses the getter method Usage Examples:
- **Parameters:**
  - `obj` (`Object`) — the object to get the property value from
- **Returns:** the property value, cast to type T
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the target is incompatible with this property, its array representation lacks the property slot, or reading its field or invoking its getter throws an exception
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  class Person {
        public String name;
    }
    Person person = new Person();
    person.name = "John";
    PropInfo nameProp = ParserUtil.getBeanInfo(Person.class).getPropInfo("name");
    String name = nameProp.getPropValue(person); // returns "John"
  ```
##### setPropValue(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@SuppressFBWarnings public void setPropValue(final Object obj, Object propValue) throws UnsupportedOperationException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Sets the value of this property on the specified object.
- **Contract:**
  - This method provides intelligent property setting with the following features: Automatic type conversion when necessary Support for immutable beans and builder patterns Handling of JSON raw values Performance optimization for repeated operations Fallback strategies for different access methods The method attempts to set the value in the following order: Direct field access (if accessible and settable) Setter method invocation Setting via getter for collections/maps (XML binding) Forced field access as last resort For a builder-based immutable bean `obj` is the builder instance, so the value is routed to the builder's setter.
- **Parameters:**
  - `obj` (`Object`) — the object to set the property value on
  - `propValue` (`Object`) — the value to set (will be converted if necessary)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if this property is read-only and cannot accept `propValue`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the target cannot accept the property value, conversion to the property type is unsupported, or accessing the field or invoking its getter or setter throws an exception
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  class Person {
        public int age;
    }
    Person person = new Person();
    PropInfo ageProp = ParserUtil.getBeanInfo(Person.class).getPropInfo("age");
    ageProp.setPropValue(person, 25);
    ageProp.setPropValue(person, "30");   // value is converted from String
  ```
##### readPropValue(...) -> Object
- **Signature:** `public Object readPropValue(final String strValue) throws UnsupportedOperationException, IllegalArgumentException, DateTimeException, ArithmeticException, ParsingException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Reads and converts a string value to the appropriate property type.
- **Parameters:**
  - `strValue` (`String`) — the string value to parse
- **Returns:** the parsed value in the property's own type. A number-format read converts the parsed number to the property type (`Integer` for an `int`/`Integer` property, an exact `BigDecimal`/`BigInteger` for those property types, and so on), so the value can be stored without a further conversion. A `null` input returns `null` in the number-format branch and most date-format readers; without formatting it follows the property type's `valueOf` policy (primitive types return their default value). Every nullable date-format reader also returns `null` for empty text and the literal `"null"` (case-insensitive), the same markers the no-format date types accept. A primitive `long` property with the `"long"` date format returns `0L` for those markers, and a `String` property - whose reader is the identity - returns the text it was handed unchanged
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if a date format is specified for an unsupported type, or non-null, nonempty text other than the null literal uses the long date format for a LocalDate or LocalTime property
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if non-null date text other than an empty string or the null literal cannot be parsed as epoch milliseconds or by the configured legacy or Joda-Time date format
  - `java.time.DateTimeException` — if non-null date text other than an empty string or the null literal cannot be parsed by the configured java.time formatter or converted to the property's temporal type and time zone
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if a parsed SQL date or time cannot be represented as epoch milliseconds
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if a number format is specified and `strValue` cannot be parsed against it in full
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the parsed number cannot be converted to the property type (for example `NaN` into a `BigDecimal` property, which raises an `ArithmeticException`)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  class Event {
        @JsonXmlField(dateFormat = "yyyy-MM-dd", timeZone = "UTC")
        public java.util.Date date;
  
        @JsonXmlField(dateFormat = "long")
        public java.util.Date createdAt;
    }
  
    BeanInfo beanInfo = ParserUtil.getBeanInfo(Event.class);
    PropInfo dateProp = beanInfo.getPropInfo("date");
    java.util.Date date = (java.util.Date) dateProp.readPropValue("2023-12-25");
  
    PropInfo longDateProp = beanInfo.getPropInfo("createdAt");
    java.util.Date date2 = (java.util.Date) longDateProp.readPropValue("1703462400000");
  ```
##### writePropValue(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public void writePropValue(final CharacterWriter writer, final Object x, final JsonXmlSerConfig<?> config) throws UnsupportedOperationException, IllegalArgumentException, DateTimeException, ArithmeticException, UncheckedIOException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Writes a property value to a character writer with appropriate formatting.
- **Parameters:**
  - `writer` (`CharacterWriter`) — the character writer to write to
  - `x` (`Object`) — the value to write
  - `config` (`JsonXmlSerConfig<?>`) — the serialization configuration
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if a date format is specified for an unsupported type, or the long date format is selected for a LocalDate or LocalTime property
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a legacy date pattern, time zone, year or UTC offset cannot be represented by the selected format, or a number format is applied to a nonnumeric value
  - `java.time.DateTimeException` — if a java.time formatter cannot represent the value's temporal fields, or appending its formatted text to the destination fails
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if a LocalDateTime or ZonedDateTime value with the long date format exceeds the epoch-millisecond range
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if appending a formatted legacy date or calendar value to the destination fails
  - `java.io.IOException` — if writing raw or type-serialized text, epoch milliseconds, String or Joda-Time formatted text, quotation marks or the null literal to `writer` fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  class Event {
        @JsonXmlField(dateFormat = "yyyy-MM-dd", timeZone = "UTC")
        public java.util.Date date;
    }
  
    PropInfo dateProp = ParserUtil.getBeanInfo(Event.class).getPropInfo("date");
    com.landawn.abacus.util.BufferedJsonWriter writer =
            com.landawn.abacus.util.Objectory.createBufferedJsonWriter();
    try {
        dateProp.writePropValue(writer, new java.util.Date(), new JsonSerConfig());
        String jsonValue = writer.toString();
    } finally {
        com.landawn.abacus.util.Objectory.recycle(writer);
    }
  ```

##### getAnnotation(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public <T extends Annotation> T getAnnotation(final Class<T> annotationClass)`
- **Summary:** Gets the specified annotation from this property.
- **Contract:**
  - If the same annotation is present in multiple places, the value collected last wins, so the precedence order is: setter annotations, then getter annotations, then field annotations.
- **Parameters:**
  - `annotationClass` (`Class<T>`) — the annotation class to retrieve
- **Returns:** the annotation instance, or `null` if not present
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  JsonXmlField jsonField = propInfo.getAnnotation(JsonXmlField.class);
    if (jsonField != null) {
        String customName = jsonField.name();
    }
  ```

##### getExclusion(...) -> Exclusion
- **Signature:** `public Exclusion getExclusion()`
- **Summary:** Gets the current exclusion strategy for field serialization.
- **Contract:**
  - The exclusion strategy determines which fields should be excluded from serialization based on their values or other criteria.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the current Exclusion strategy, or `null` if no exclusion is set
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  KryoSerConfig config = new KryoSerConfig();
    Exclusion current = config.getExclusion();  // returns null (default, no exclusion set)
  
    config.setExclusion(Exclusion.NULL);
    Exclusion updated = config.getExclusion();  // returns Exclusion.NULL
  ```
- **See also:** Exclusion
##### setExclusion(...) -> C
- **Signature:** `public C setExclusion(final Exclusion exclusion)`
- **Summary:** Sets the exclusion strategy for field serialization in beans.
- **Parameters:**
  - `exclusion` (`Exclusion`) — the exclusion strategy to use, or `null` to use the bean annotation or the parser default
- **Returns:** this configuration instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  config.setExclusion(Exclusion.NULL);      // removes null fields
    config.setExclusion(Exclusion.DEFAULT);   // removes fields with default values
    config.setExclusion(Exclusion.NONE);      // disables value-based exclusion; other filters still apply
  ```
- **See also:** Exclusion
##### isSkipTransientField(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public boolean isSkipTransientField()`
- **Summary:** Checks whether transient fields should be skipped during serialization.
- **Contract:**
  - When `true`, fields marked with the `transient` keyword or `@Transient` annotation will be excluded from serialization.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** `true` if transient fields should be skipped, `false` otherwise
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  KryoSerConfig config = new KryoSerConfig();
    boolean skips = config.isSkipTransientField();  // returns true (default)
  
    config.setSkipTransientField(false);
    boolean keeps = config.isSkipTransientField();  // returns false
  ```
##### setSkipTransientField(...) -> C
- **Signature:** `public C setSkipTransientField(final boolean skipTransientField)`
- **Summary:** Sets whether transient fields should be skipped during serialization.
- **Contract:**
  - When set to `true`, fields marked with the `transient` keyword or `@Transient` annotation will be excluded from serialization.

- **Parameters:**

- **Returns:** this configuration instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**

  ```java
    config.setSkipTransientField(false);   // keeps transient fields
  ```
