##### deserialize(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `<T> T deserialize(Node source, Type<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException, ParsingException`
- **Summary:** Deserializes an XML DOM node to an object of the specified type using a Type descriptor.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`Node`) — the DOM node containing the XML data to deserialize (must not be `null`)
  - `targetType` (`Type<? extends T>`) — the Type descriptor of the object to create (must not be `null`)
- **Returns:** the deserialized object of type `T`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `source` or `targetType` is null.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if the XML structure does not match the target type
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  try {
        Document doc = XmlUtil.createDOMParser().parse(xmlFile);
        Type<MyBean> type = Type.of(MyBean.class);
        MyBean bean = parser.deserialize(doc.getDocumentElement(), type);
    } catch (Exception e) {
        // Handle parsing exception
    }
  ```
- **Signature:** `<T> T deserialize(Node source, Class<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException, ParsingException`

- **Throws:**

- **Signature:** `<T> T deserialize(Node source, XmlDeserConfig config, Type<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException, ParsingException`
- **Summary:** Deserializes an XML DOM node to an object of the specified type with custom deserialization configuration.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`Node`) — the DOM node containing the XML data to deserialize (must not be `null`)
  - `config` (`XmlDeserConfig`) — the deserialization configuration to use (may be `null` for default behavior)
  - `targetType` (`Type<? extends T>`) — the Type descriptor of the object to create (must not be `null`)
- **Returns:** the deserialized object of type `T`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `source` or `targetType` is null.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if the XML structure does not match the target type
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  XmlDeserConfig config = new XmlDeserConfig()
        .setIgnoreUnmatchedProperty(true);
  
    try {
        Document doc = XmlUtil.createDOMParser().parse(xmlFile);

        MyBean bean = parser.deserialize(doc.getDocumentElement(), config, type);
  ```

- **Signature:** `<T> T deserialize(Node source, XmlDeserConfig config, Class<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException, ParsingException`
- **Summary:** Deserializes an XML DOM node to an object of the specified type with custom deserialization configuration.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`Node`) — the DOM node containing the XML data to deserialize (must not be `null`)
  - `config` (`XmlDeserConfig`) — the deserialization configuration to use (may be `null` for default behavior)
  - `targetType` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the class of the object to create (must not be `null`)
- **Returns:** the deserialized object of type `T`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `source` or `targetType` is null.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if the XML structure does not match the target type
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  XmlDeserConfig config = new XmlDeserConfig()
        .setIgnoreUnmatchedProperty(true);
  
    try {
        Document doc = XmlUtil.createDOMParser().parse(xmlFile);
        MyBean bean = parser.deserialize(doc.getDocumentElement(), config, MyBean.class);

        // Handle parsing exception
    }
  ```
- **Signature:** `<T> T deserialize(File source, XmlDeserConfig config, Map<String, Type<?>> nodeTypes) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException, ParsingException`
- **Summary:** Deserializes XML from a file using node class mappings for dynamic type resolution.
- **Contract:**
  - The root element's name attribute (or, when that attribute is absent or empty, its tag name) is looked up in the nodeTypes map to determine which class to instantiate (nested elements are not resolved through the map).
  - This is useful when the target type cannot be determined statically.
  - The `<T>` merely saves the caller an explicit cast; callers should treat the result as `Object` and only narrow it once the actual element type is known.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`File`) — the file containing XML data to deserialize (must not be `null`)
  - `config` (`XmlDeserConfig`) — the deserialization configuration to use (may be `null` for default behavior)
  - `nodeTypes` (`Map<String, Type<?>>`) — mapping of XML element names to their corresponding types (must not be `null`)
- **Returns:** the deserialized object of type `T`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `source` is null or is a directory that cannot be opened.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if opening `source` fails, or the selected XML backend reports an `IOException` while reading the XML file
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if no matching type is found in `nodeTypes` or the XML is malformed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Type<?>> nodeTypes = new HashMap<>();
    nodeTypes.put("customer", Type.of(Customer.class));
    nodeTypes.put("invoice", Type.of(Invoice.class));
  
    File xmlFile = new File("data.xml");
    Object result = parser.deserialize(xmlFile, config, nodeTypes);
  ```
- **Signature:** `<T> T deserialize(InputStream source, XmlDeserConfig config, Map<String, Type<?>> nodeTypes) throws ParsingException, UncheckedIOException`
- **Summary:** Deserializes XML from an input stream using node class mappings for dynamic type resolution.
- **Contract:**
  - The root element's name attribute (or, when that attribute is absent or empty, its tag name) is looked up in the nodeTypes map to determine which class to instantiate (nested elements are not resolved through the map).
  - This is useful when the target type cannot be determined statically.
  - The `<T>` merely saves the caller an explicit cast; callers should treat the result as `Object` and only narrow it once the actual element type is known.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`InputStream`) — the input stream containing XML data to deserialize (must not be `null`)
  - `config` (`XmlDeserConfig`) — the deserialization configuration to use (may be `null` for default behavior)
  - `nodeTypes` (`Map<String, Type<?>>`) — mapping of XML element names to their corresponding types (must not be `null`)
- **Returns:** the deserialized object of type `T`
- **Throws:**
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if no matching type is found in `nodeTypes` or the XML is malformed
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if the selected XML backend reports an `IOException` while reading XML from `source`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Type<?>> nodeTypes = new HashMap<>();
    nodeTypes.put("item", Type.of(Item.class));
    nodeTypes.put("order", Type.of(Order.class));
  
    try (InputStream inputStream = new FileInputStream("data.xml")) {
        Object result = parser.deserialize(inputStream, config, nodeTypes);
    }
  ```

- **Signature:** `<T> T deserialize(Node source, XmlDeserConfig config, Map<String, Type<?>> nodeTypes) throws IllegalArgumentException, ParsingException`
- **Summary:** Deserializes an XML DOM node using node class mappings for dynamic type resolution.
- **Contract:**

  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.ParsingException` — if no matching type is found in `nodeTypes` or the XML structure is invalid
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Type<?>> nodeTypes = new HashMap<>();
    nodeTypes.put("product", Type.of(Product.class));
    nodeTypes.put("category", Type.of(Category.class));
  ```

  - When `false`, every property is written as a generic `<property name="...">` element and the bean element carries a `name` attribute instead, e.g.

## com.landawn.abacus.poi
### Class ExcelUtil (com.landawn.abacus.poi.ExcelUtil)
Utility class for reading, writing, and converting Excel files using Apache POI.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### readDatasetFromSheet(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `public static Dataset readDatasetFromSheet(final File excelFile) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedException`
- **Summary:** Loads the first sheet from the specified Excel file into a Dataset.
- **Contract:**
  - Header handling: the `readDatasetFromSheet` family always consumes the first physically defined row returned by the sheet iterator as the header row and uses the #CELL_TO_STRING rendering of those cells as column names (a numeric header `2024` becomes `"2024.0"`, a formula its text); only a missing cell, a `CellType.BLANK` cell or an empty string is replaced by a synthesized unique `"Column_i"` (with a numeric suffix when needed), while a whitespace-only name is kept as-is and may not repeat.
- **Parameters:**
  - `excelFile` (`File`) — the Excel file to read, must exist and be a valid Excel file.
- **Returns:** a Dataset containing the sheet data with the first row as column names, or an empty Dataset if the sheet is empty.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `excelFile` is `null`, or the workbook has no sheet at index 0, or the header row contains duplicate non-empty column names (whitespace-only names count as non-empty).
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedException` — if opening or reading `excelFile`, creating its workbook, or closing the workbook or an owned input stream fails with an `IOException`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = ExcelUtil.readDatasetFromSheet(new File("sales_data.xlsx"));
    // Access data by column name
    List<String> productNames = dataset.getColumn("Product");
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static Dataset readDatasetFromSheet(final File excelFile, final int sheetIndex, final TriConsumer<? super String[], ? super Row, ? super Object[]> rowExtractor) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedException`
- **Summary:** Loads the specified sheet from the Excel file into a Dataset using a custom row extractor.
- **Parameters:**
  - `excelFile` (`File`) — the Excel file to read, must exist and be a valid Excel file.
  - `sheetIndex` (`int`) — the zero-based index of the sheet to read (0 for first sheet).
  - `rowExtractor` (`TriConsumer<? super String[], ? super Row, ? super Object[]>`) — custom function to extract row data. Receives three parameters: column headers array, current row, and output array to populate with extracted values.
- **Returns:** a Dataset containing the extracted sheet data with the first row as column names.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `excelFile` or `rowExtractor` is `null`, or the sheet index is out of bounds, or the header row contains duplicate non-empty column names (whitespace-only names count as non-empty).
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedException` — if opening or reading `excelFile`, creating its workbook, or closing the workbook or an owned input stream fails with an `IOException`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  TriConsumer<String[], Row, Object[]> customExtractor = (headers, row, output) -> {
        for (int i = 0; i < headers.length; i++) {
            Cell cell = row.getCell(i);
            output[i] = cell == null ? null : cell.getStringCellValue();
        }
    };
    Dataset dataset = ExcelUtil.readDatasetFromSheet(new File("data.xlsx"), 0, customExtractor);
  ```

- **Signature:** `public static Dataset readDatasetFromSheet(final File excelFile, final String sheetName, final TriConsumer<? super String[], ? super Row, ? super Object[]> rowExtractor) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedException`
- **Summary:** Loads the sheet with the specified name from the Excel file into a Dataset.
- **Contract:**
  - This method allows loading a specific sheet by name rather than index, which is useful when working with workbooks that have meaningful sheet names.
- **Parameters:**
  - `excelFile` (`File`) — the Excel file to read, must exist and be a valid Excel file.
  - `sheetName` (`String`) — the name of the sheet to read, case-insensitive.
  - `rowExtractor` (`TriConsumer<? super String[], ? super Row, ? super Object[]>`) — custom function to extract row data. Receives three parameters: column headers array, current row, and output array to populate with extracted values.
- **Returns:** a Dataset containing the extracted sheet data with the first row as column names.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `excelFile` or `rowExtractor` is `null`, or the sheet name is not found in the workbook, or the header row contains duplicate non-empty column names (whitespace-only names count as non-empty).
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedException` — if opening or reading `excelFile`, creating its workbook, or closing the workbook or an owned input stream fails with an `IOException`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = ExcelUtil.readDatasetFromSheet(
        new File("workbook.xlsx"),
        "Sales2024",
        ExcelUtil.RowExtractors.DEFAULT
    );
  ```

##### readRowsFromSheet(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public static List<List<Object>> readRowsFromSheet(final File excelFile) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedException`
- **Summary:** Reads the first sheet of the Excel file and returns rows as a list of lists.
- **Parameters:**
  - `excelFile` (`File`) — the Excel file to read, must exist and be a valid Excel file.
- **Returns:** a list of rows, where each row is a list of cell values with preserved types.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `excelFile` is `null`, or the workbook has no sheet at index 0.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedException` — if opening or reading `excelFile`, creating its workbook, or closing the workbook or an owned input stream fails with an `IOException`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<List<Object>> rows = ExcelUtil.readRowsFromSheet(new File("data.xlsx"));
    for (List<Object> row : rows) {
        System.out.println("Row: " + row);
    }
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <T> List<T> readRowsFromSheet(final File excelFile, final int sheetIndex, final boolean skipFirstRow, final Function<? super Row, ? extends T> rowMapper) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedException`
- **Summary:** Reads the specified sheet and maps each row to a custom object type using the provided mapper.
- **Contract:**
  - Optionally skips the first row if it contains headers.
  - The `skipFirstRow` flag merely discards the first physically defined row when `true`; its cell values are not used as names.
- **Parameters:**
  - `excelFile` (`File`) — the Excel file to read, must exist and be a valid Excel file.
  - `sheetIndex` (`int`) — the zero-based index of the sheet to read (0 for first sheet).
  - `skipFirstRow` (`boolean`) — `true` to skip the first row (typically headers), `false` to process all rows.
  - `rowMapper` (`Function<? super Row, ? extends T>`) — function to convert each Row to an object of type T.
- **Returns:** a list of mapped objects, one per row (excluding skipped rows).
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `excelFile` or `rowMapper` is `null`, or the sheet index is out of bounds.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedException` — if opening or reading `excelFile`, creating its workbook, or closing the workbook or an owned input stream fails with an `IOException`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Function<Row, String> rowToString = row -> {
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
        row.forEach(cell -> sb.append(cell).append(","));
        return sb.toString();
    };
    List<String> rows = ExcelUtil.readRowsFromSheet(new File("data.xlsx"), 0, true, rowToString);
  ```

##### streamRowsFromSheet(...) -> Stream<Row>
- **Signature:** `public static Stream<Row> streamRowsFromSheet(final File excelFile, final int sheetIndex, final boolean skipFirstRow) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedException`
- **Summary:** Creates a stream of Row objects from the specified sheet in the Excel file.
- **Contract:**
  - Important: The Stream must be closed after use to release file handles and workbook resources.
  - Always use try-with-resources or explicitly call `close()` on the stream when done.
- **Parameters:**
  - `excelFile` (`File`) — the Excel file to read, must exist and be a valid Excel file
  - `sheetIndex` (`int`) — the zero-based index of the sheet to stream (0 for first sheet)
  - `skipFirstRow` (`boolean`) — `true` to skip the first row (typically headers), `false` to process all rows
- **Returns:** a Stream of Row objects from the specified sheet that must be closed after use
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `excelFile` is `null`, or the sheet index is out of bounds.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedException` — if opening or reading `excelFile` to create the workbook fails with an `IOException`, including unreadable or unsupported workbook content
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  try (Stream<Row> stream = ExcelUtil.streamRowsFromSheet(new File("large_data.xlsx"), 0, true)) {
        stream.filter(row -> row.getCell(0).getNumericCellValue() > 1000)
              .forEach(row -> processRow(row));
    }
  ```

- **Throws:**

- **Summary:** Creates a stream of Row objects from the sheet with the specified name in the Excel input stream.
- **Contract:**
  - Important: The returned Stream must be closed after use.
  - Closing the Stream closes the underlying workbook but does not close the supplied `excelInputStream`; the caller retains ownership of the stream and must close it (typically after the Stream).
  - Unlike the `readDatasetFromSheet` family, no row is interpreted as a header row; the `skipFirstRow` flag simply discards the first physically defined row when `true`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `excelInputStream` (`InputStream`) — the input stream of the Excel content, must be a valid Excel stream. It is not closed by the returned Stream.
  - `sheetName` (`String`) — the name of the sheet to stream, case-insensitive
  - `skipFirstRow` (`boolean`) — `true` to skip the first row (typically headers), `false` to process all rows
- **Returns:** a Stream of Row objects from the specified sheet that must be closed after use
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `excelInputStream` is `null`, or the sheet name is not found in the workbook.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedException` — if reading `excelInputStream` to create the workbook fails with an `IOException`, including unreadable or unsupported workbook content

- **Summary:** Writes data to a new Excel file with the specified sheet name and headers.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sheetName` (`String`) — the name of the sheet to create in the workbook; 1 to 31 characters, must not contain any of `: \\ /? * \[ \]` and must not start or end with an apostrophe (Excel sheet names are case-insensitive)
  - `headers` (`List<?>`) — the column headers as a list of objects (will be converted to strings)
  - `rows` (`List<? extends Collection<?>>`) — the data rows, where each row is a collection of cell values
  - `outputExcelFile` (`File`) — the file to write the Excel data to; an existing file is replaced only after the write succeeds (see the class-level note on file destinations), never truncated up front
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `headers`, `rows`, `outputExcelFile` or `sheetName` is `null`, or if `sheetName` is empty, longer than 31 characters or contains a character POI rejects (see the parameter). Validation occurs before any temporary file is created.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedException` — if creating or writing the temporary workbook file, closing the workbook or output stream, or replacing the destination file fails with an `IOException`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<Object> headers = List.of("Name", "Age", "City");
    List<List<Object>> rows = List.of(
        List.of("John", 30, "New York"),
        List.of("Jane", 25, "London")
    );
    ExcelUtil.writeRowsToSheet("Users", headers, rows, new File("users.xlsx"));
  ```

  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `headers`, `rows`, `outputExcelFile` or `sheetName` is `null`, or if `sheetName` is empty, longer than 31 characters or contains a character POI rejects (see the parameter). Validation occurs before any temporary file is created.

- **Summary:** Writes data to a new Excel file with a custom sheet configuration function.
- **Contract:**
  - Use this when you need formatting options beyond what SheetCreateOptions provides, such as custom column widths, conditional formatting, cell styles, or data validation rules.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sheetName` (`String`) — the name of the sheet to create in the workbook; 1 to 31 characters, must not contain any of `: \\ /? * \[ \]` and must not start or end with an apostrophe (Excel sheet names are case-insensitive).
  - `headers` (`List<?>`) — the column headers as a list of objects (will be converted to strings).
  - `rows` (`List<? extends Collection<?>>`) — the data rows, where each row is a collection of cell values.
  - `sheetSetter` (`Consumer<? super Sheet>`) — a consumer to apply custom formatting to the sheet after data is written; must not be `null`.
  - `outputExcelFile` (`File`) — the file to write the Excel data to; an existing file is replaced only after the write succeeds (see the class-level note on file destinations), never truncated up front.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `headers`, `rows`, `sheetSetter`, `outputExcelFile` or `sheetName` is `null`, or if `sheetName` is empty, longer than 31 characters or contains a character POI rejects (see the parameter). Validation occurs before any temporary file is created.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedException` — if creating or writing the temporary workbook file, closing the workbook or output stream, or replacing the destination file fails with an `IOException`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Consumer<Sheet> customFormatter = sheet -> {
        sheet.setDefaultColumnWidth(15);
        sheet.createFreezePane(0, 1);
        sheet.setAutoFilter(new CellRangeAddress(0, 0, 0, 3));
    };
  
    List<Object> headers = List.of("ID", "Name", "Amount", "Status");
    List<List<Object>> rows = List.of(
        List.of(1, "North", 1250.0, "Open"),
        List.of(2, "South", 980.0, "Closed")
    );
    ExcelUtil.writeRowsToSheet("CustomSheet", headers, rows, customFormatter, new File("custom.xlsx"));
  ```

- **Signature:** `public static void exportSheetToCsv(final File excelFile, final int sheetIndex, final File outputCsvFile) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException, UncheckedException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Converts the specified sheet from an Excel file to a CSV file.
- **Parameters:**
  - `excelFile` (`File`) — the Excel file to read, must exist and be a valid Excel file
  - `sheetIndex` (`int`) — the zero-based index of the sheet to convert (0 for first sheet)
  - `outputCsvFile` (`File`) — the CSV file to write to; an existing file is replaced only after the write succeeds (see the class-level note on file destinations), never truncated up front
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `excelFile` or `outputCsvFile` is `null`, or the sheet index is out of bounds.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if creating or closing the temporary CSV output, closing its writer, or replacing `outputCsvFile` fails; failures while writing CSV rows are wrapped as `UncheckedException`
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedException` — if opening or reading `excelFile`, creating or closing its workbook, or writing CSV headers or rows fails with an `IOException`
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if a cell has a type that cannot be represented by this CSV exporter
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ExcelUtil.exportSheetToCsv(
        new File("data.xlsx"),
        0,
        new File("output.csv")
    );
  ```

- **Summary:** Converts the sheet with the specified name from an Excel file to a CSV file.
- **Contract:**
  - This method allows exporting a specific worksheet by name rather than index, which is more robust when working with workbooks where sheet positions might change.
- **Parameters:**
  - `excelFile` (`File`) — the Excel file to read, must exist and be a valid Excel file
  - `sheetName` (`String`) — the name of the sheet to convert, case-insensitive
  - `outputCsvFile` (`File`) — the CSV file to write to; an existing file is replaced only after the write succeeds (see the class-level note on file destinations), never truncated up front
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `excelFile` or `outputCsvFile` is `null`, or the sheet name is not found in the workbook.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if creating or closing the temporary CSV output, closing its writer, or replacing `outputCsvFile` fails; failures while writing CSV rows are wrapped as `UncheckedException`
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedException` — if opening or reading `excelFile`, creating or closing its workbook, or writing CSV headers or rows fails with an `IOException`
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if a cell has a type that cannot be represented by this CSV exporter
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ExcelUtil.exportSheetToCsv(
        new File("workbook.xlsx"),
        "SalesData",
        new File("sales.csv")
    );
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static void exportSheetToCsv(final File excelFile, final int sheetIndex, final List<String> csvHeaders, final Writer outputWriter) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Converts the specified sheet from an Excel file to a CSV file with custom options.
- **Contract:**
  - When custom headers are provided, the first row of the Excel sheet is skipped and replaced with the custom headers.
- **Parameters:**
  - `excelFile` (`File`) — the Excel file to read, must exist and be a valid Excel file
  - `sheetIndex` (`int`) — the zero-based index of the sheet to convert (0 for first sheet)
  - `csvHeaders` (`List<String>`) — custom headers for the CSV file. `null` or empty preserves the original Excel rows (the sheet's own first row becomes the first CSV record); a non-empty list is written as the header record and the sheet's first row is skipped, i.e. it replaces rather than prepends. All records, including replacement headers, are padded with empty fields to the widest emitted record. A `null` label is written as the unquoted token `null`, an empty label as `""`.
  - `outputWriter` (`Writer`) — the Writer to write the CSV content to; it is flushed but not closed.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `excelFile` or `outputWriter` is `null`, or the sheet index is out of bounds.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedException` — if opening or reading `excelFile`, creating or closing its workbook, or writing CSV headers or rows fails with an `IOException`
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if a cell has a type that cannot be represented by this CSV exporter
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> customHeaders = List.of("Product ID", "Product Name", "Price");
    try (Writer writer = IOUtil.newFileWriter(new File("products.csv"))) {
        ExcelUtil.exportSheetToCsv(
            new File("products.xlsx"),
            0,
            customHeaders,
            writer
        );
    }
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static void exportSheetToCsv(final File excelFile, final String sheetName, final List<String> csvHeaders, final Writer outputWriter) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Converts the sheet with the specified name to CSV output, writing to the given Writer.
- **Contract:**
  - When custom headers are provided, the first row of the Excel sheet is skipped and replaced with the custom headers in the CSV output.
  - When custom headers are provided, they replace the first row of the Excel sheet in the CSV output.
- **Parameters:**
  - `excelFile` (`File`) — the Excel file to read, must exist and be a valid Excel file
  - `sheetName` (`String`) — the name of the sheet to convert, case-insensitive
  - `csvHeaders` (`List<String>`) — custom headers for the CSV file. `null` or empty preserves the original Excel rows (the sheet's own first row becomes the first CSV record); a non-empty list is written as the header record and the sheet's first row is skipped, i.e. it replaces rather than prepends. All records, including replacement headers, are padded with empty fields to the widest emitted record. A `null` label is written as the unquoted token `null`, an empty label as `""`.
  - `outputWriter` (`Writer`) — the Writer to write the CSV content to; it is flushed but not closed.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `excelFile` or `outputWriter` is `null`, or the sheet name is not found in the workbook.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedException` — if opening or reading `excelFile`, creating or closing its workbook, or writing CSV headers or rows fails with an `IOException`
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if a cell has a type that cannot be represented by this CSV exporter
- **Examples:**

- **Returns:** a Function that converts Row to delimited String
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Function<Row, String> pipeMapper = RowMappers.toDelimitedString("|");
    List<String> rows = ExcelUtil.readRowsFromSheet(file, 0, true, pipeMapper);
    // Results in rows like: "John|30.0|New York" (numeric cells render as double values)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static Function<Row, String> toDelimitedString(final String cellSeparator, final Function<Cell, String> cellMapper) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a row mapper that converts rows to delimited strings with custom cell processing.
- **Contract:**
  - Use this when you need special formatting, value transformations, or custom handling of specific cell types.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cellSeparator` (`String`) — the string to use as separator between cell values
  - `cellMapper` (`Function<Cell, String>`) — custom function to convert each cell to a string
- **Returns:** a Function that converts Row to delimited String
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `cellMapper` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Function<Cell, String> customCellMapper = cell ->
        cell.getCellType() == CellType.NUMERIC
            ? String.format("%.2f", cell.getNumericCellValue())
            : ExcelUtil.CELL_TO_STRING.apply(cell);
  
    Function<Row, String> mapper = RowMappers.toDelimitedString(",", customCellMapper);
  ```
##### toList(...) -> Function<Row, List<T>>
- **Signature:** `public static <T> Function<Row, List<T>> toList(final Function<Cell, T> cellMapper) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a row mapper that converts rows to Lists with custom cell processing.
- **Contract:**
  - Particularly useful when you need to extract specific data types, perform validation, or apply transformations during the read process.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cellMapper` (`Function<Cell, T>`) — function to convert each cell to type T
- **Returns:** a Function that converts Row to List<T>
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `cellMapper` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Extract only numeric values as Double
    Function<Cell, Double> numericMapper = cell ->
        cell.getCellType() == CellType.NUMERIC
            ? cell.getNumericCellValue()
            : 0.0;
  
    Function<Row, List<Double>> mapper = RowMappers.toList(numericMapper);
    List<List<Double>> numericData = ExcelUtil.readRowsFromSheet(file, 0, true, mapper);
  ```

### Class AbstractPool (com.landawn.abacus.pool.AbstractPool)
Abstract base class for implementing object pools with eviction, balancing, and memory management capabilities.

**Thread-safety:** thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### capacity(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `@Override public int capacity()`
- **Summary:** Returns the maximum capacity of this pool.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the maximum number of objects this pool can hold (readable even after the pool is closed)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  if (pool.size() >= pool.capacity() * 0.9) {
        // Pool is 90% full, consider scaling
    }
  ```
##### stats(...) -> PoolStats
- **Signature:** `@Override public PoolStats stats() throws IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Returns a snapshot of the current pool statistics.
- **Contract:**
  - PoolStats#dataSize() is the current total of the retained admission charges whenever memory is tracked (#isMemoryTracked()), including a pool that has a memory measure but no limit; it is `-1` only when no memory measure is configured.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a PoolStats object containing current pool statistics
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  PoolStats stats = pool.stats();
    double hitRate = stats.getCount() > 0 ?
        (double) stats.hitCount() / stats.getCount() : 0.0;
    System.out.println("Hit rate: " + (hitRate * 100) + "%");
    System.out.println("Pool utilization: " + stats.size() + "/" + stats.capacity());
  ```

### Class GenericKeyedObjectPool (com.landawn.abacus.pool.GenericKeyedObjectPool)
A generic implementation of KeyedObjectPool that manages poolable objects by keys.

**Thread-safety:** thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### put(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@Override public boolean put(final K key, final E value) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Associates the specified element with the specified key in this pool.
- **Contract:**
  - If the pool previously contained a mapping for the key, the old element is detached and accounted with Caller#REMOVE_REPLACE_CLEAR before the new value is inserted.
  - Detachment still happens when the later insertion fails (capacity/memory rejection), so a failing `put` can remove the previous mapping for `key`.
  - The old element is not destroyed when it is the same instance as `value` (re-pooling the same instance simply re-inserts it, and the mapping is restored if that re-pooling fails).
  - The put operation returns `false` (does not insert) if: The element has already expired (on entry, or by the time it is checked under the lock) The pool is at capacity and either auto-balancing is disabled, or balancing did not free a slot The element would exceed memory constraints (when a memory measure is configured) and balancing did not free enough memory The memory measure returns a negative size or throws an exception Usage Examples:
- **Parameters:**
  - `key` (`K`) — the key with which the specified value is to be associated
  - `value` (`E`) — the value to be associated with the specified key
- **Returns:** `true` if the mapping was successfully added, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the key or value is null.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  DBConnection conn = new DBConnection("server1");
    if (pool.put("database1", conn)) {
        System.out.println("Connection added successfully");
    } else {
        System.out.println("Failed to add - pool full or connection expired");
        conn.destroy(Caller.PUT_ADD_FAILURE);
    }
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Override public boolean put(final K key, final E value, final boolean autoDestroyOnFailedToPut) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Associates the specified element with the specified key in this pool, with optional automatic destruction on failure.
- **Contract:**
  - This is a convenience method that wraps #put(Object, Poolable) and optionally destroys the element if the put operation fails.
  - The destruction occurs in a finally block to ensure cleanup even if an exception is thrown, unless the same instance remains pooled under any key at the cleanup check.
- **Parameters:**
  - `key` (`K`) — the key with which the specified value is to be associated
  - `value` (`E`) — the value to be associated with the specified key
  - `autoDestroyOnFailedToPut` (`boolean`) — if `true`, calls `value.destroy(PUT_ADD_FAILURE)` when put fails, unless the same instance remains pooled at the cleanup check
- **Returns:** `true` if the mapping was successfully added, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the key or value is null.
- **Signature:** `@Override public boolean put(final K key, final E value, final long timeout, final TimeUnit unit) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, InterruptedException`
- **Summary:** Attempts to associate the value with the key, waiting up to the given timeout for a capacity slot when the pool is full and auto-balancing is disabled.
- **Contract:**
  - When auto-balancing is enabled (the default for every PoolFactory overload without an explicit `autoBalance` flag), a full pool is first balanced under the lock - a balance-factor share of the existing mappings is detached and destroyed with Caller#VACATE - and the value is inserted without waiting.
  - Waiting for a slot occurs only when auto-balancing is disabled (or the capacity is `0`).
- **Parameters:**
  - `key` (`K`) — the key, must not be `null`
  - `value` (`E`) — the value, must not be `null`
  - `timeout` (`long`) — the maximum time to wait for a slot
  - `unit` (`TimeUnit`) — the time unit of the timeout, must not be `null`
- **Returns:** `true` if the value was added, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the key, value, or unit is null.
  - `java.lang.InterruptedException` — if interrupted while waiting
- **Signature:** `@Override public boolean put(final K key, final E value, final long timeout, final TimeUnit unit, final boolean autoDestroyOnFailedToPut) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, InterruptedException`
- **Summary:** Attempts to associate the value with the key within the timeout, with optional automatic destruction on failure.
- **Parameters:**
  - `key` (`K`) — the key, must not be `null`

- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull @Override public E get(final K key) throws IllegalStateException`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Returns the element associated with the specified key, or `null` if no mapping exists.
- **Contract:**
  - If the element has expired, it is removed and destroyed, and `null` is returned.
  - This method performs the following operations: Retrieves the element associated with the key Checks if the element has expired If expired: removes and destroys the element, returns `null` If valid: updates last access time and access count, returns the element An expired mapping is detached and accounted while locked.

- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed

- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull @Override public E remove(final K key) throws IllegalStateException`

- **Summary:** Removes and returns the element associated with the specified key.

  - The pool does not invoke Poolable#destroy(Caller) on the returned element; the caller takes ownership and is responsible for destroying it when no longer needed.

- **Examples:**
  ```java

    if (element != null) {

        } finally {

            element.destroy(Caller.OTHER_EXTERNAL);
        }
    }
  ```
##### peek(...) -> E
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull @Override public E peek(final K key) throws IllegalStateException`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Returns the element associated with the specified key without updating access statistics.
- **Contract:**
  - If the element has expired, it is removed and destroyed, and `null` is returned.
  - Important Side Effects: Does NOT update last access time - element's access time remains unchanged Does NOT update access count - element's access counter remains unchanged DOES remove and destroy expired elements - if the element has expired, it will be destroyed and removed from the pool, and `null` will be returned Does NOT remove the element from the pool (if valid) - the element remains available for future requests An expired mapping is detached and accounted while locked.

  - If you need to use the element for regular operations, use #get(Object) instead.

  - `key` (`K`) — the key whose associated element is to be returned; a `null` key matches no mapping (`null` is returned)
- **Returns:** the element associated with the key, or `null` if no mapping exists or element expired (may return null)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed
- **Examples:**
  ```java

    DBConnection conn = pool.peek("database1");
    if (conn != null) {
        System.out.println("Connection available: " + conn.isActive());
        // Connection remains in pool with unchanged access statistics
    }
  ```

### Interface KeyedObjectPool (com.landawn.abacus.pool.KeyedObjectPool)
A pool that manages objects associated with keys, similar to a Map but with pooling capabilities.

**Thread-safety:** thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### put(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `boolean put(K key, E value) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Associates the specified poolable element with the specified key in this pool.
- **Contract:**
  - If the pool previously contained an element for the key, the old element is removed and accounted (with Poolable.Caller#REMOVE_REPLACE_CLEAR) before the new value is inserted, and it is destroyed as part of the put; its destruction callback may run after the new mapping is already visible.
  - The removal happens even when the subsequent insertion of the new value fails.
  - The old element is not destroyed when it is the same instance as `value`.
  - The put operation returns `false` (does not insert) if: The value has already expired The pool is at capacity and either auto-balancing is disabled, or balancing did not free a slot The value would exceed memory constraints (when a memory measure is configured) and balancing did not free enough memory The memory measure returns a negative size or throws an exception
- **Parameters:**
  - `key` (`K`) — the key with which the specified value is to be associated, must not be `null`
  - `value` (`E`) — the value to be associated with the specified key, must not be `null`
- **Returns:** `true` if the value was successfully added, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the key or value is null.
- **Signature:** `boolean put(K key, E value, boolean autoDestroyOnFailedToPut) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Associates the specified element with the specified key in this pool, with optional automatic destruction on failure.
- **Contract:**
  - This is a convenience method that ensures proper cleanup if the object cannot be pooled.
  - Execution Order: Attempts to add the object to the pool using #put(Object, Poolable) If put fails and `autoDestroyOnFailedToPut` is `true`, destroys the non-null value unless still pooled by identity Returns the success status of the put operation Cleanup is attempted in a finally block even if an exception occurs.
  - Callers must coordinate concurrent ownership transfers of the same instance; the check does not prevent a later admission by another thread.
- **Parameters:**
  - `key` (`K`) — the key with which the specified value is to be associated, must not be `null`
  - `value` (`E`) — the value to be associated with the specified key, must not be `null`
  - `autoDestroyOnFailedToPut` (`boolean`) — if `true`, destroys a rejected non-null value unless that same instance remains pooled at the cleanup check
- **Returns:** `true` if the value was successfully added, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the key or value is null.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Assume DBConnection extends AbstractPoolable and implements close logic in destroy()
    DBConnection conn = new DBConnection("server1");
    // Connection will be destroyed if it can't be added to pool
    pool.put("db1", conn, true);
  ```
- **Signature:** `boolean put(K key, E value, long timeout, TimeUnit unit) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, InterruptedException`
- **Summary:** Attempts to associate the specified element with the specified key, waiting if necessary for a capacity slot to become available.
- **Contract:**
  - This is the keyed mirror of ObjectPool#add(Poolable, long, TimeUnit): when the pool is at capacity and auto-balancing is disabled, this method blocks until a slot frees up (because another thread removes/evicts an entry), the timeout expires, or the thread is interrupted.
  - Rejection of one waiting candidate allows other waiting candidates to proceed when space is available.
  - When auto-balancing is enabled (the PoolFactory default), a full pool is first balanced under the lock - a balance-factor share of the existing mappings is detached and destroyed with Poolable.Caller#VACATE - and the value is inserted without waiting.
  - Waiting for a slot occurs only when auto-balancing is disabled (or the capacity is `0`).
  - All other `put` semantics of #put(Object, Poolable) still apply: the previous mapping for `key` (if any, and a different instance) is removed and destroyed before insertion, an already-expired value is rejected (`false`), and a configured memory measure is consulted.
  - The method returns `false` if the timeout elapses before a slot becomes available.
  - If another thread inserts this key while the call waits, that mapping can be replaced even when the pool is full.
- **Parameters:**
  - `key` (`K`) — the key with which the specified value is to be associated, must not be `null`
  - `value` (`E`) — the value to be associated with the specified key, must not be `null`
  - `timeout` (`long`) — the maximum time to wait for a capacity slot to become available
  - `unit` (`TimeUnit`) — the time unit of the timeout argument, must not be `null`
- **Returns:** `true` if the value was successfully added, `false` if the timeout elapsed (or the value was already/became expired, or memory constraints rejected it)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the key, value, or unit is null.
  - `java.lang.InterruptedException` — if interrupted while waiting
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  DBConnection conn = new DBConnection("server1");
    if (pool.put("database1", conn, 5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)) {
        // Successfully pooled
    } else {
        // Timed out waiting for a slot - handle the connection
        conn.destroy(Poolable.Caller.PUT_ADD_FAILURE);
    }
  ```
- **Signature:** `boolean put(K key, E value, long timeout, TimeUnit unit, boolean autoDestroyOnFailedToPut) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, InterruptedException`
- **Summary:** Attempts to associate the specified element with the specified key within the given timeout, with optional automatic destruction on failure.
- **Contract:**
  - If the put fails (timeout elapsed, capacity could not be freed, the value expired, or memory constraints rejected it) and `autoDestroyOnFailedToPut` is `true`, the pool calls `value.destroy(PUT_ADD_FAILURE)` in a finally block even if an exception is thrown, unless the value is null or the same instance remains pooled at the cleanup check.
- **Parameters:**
  - `key` (`K`) — the key with which the specified value is to be associated, must not be `null`
  - `value` (`E`) — the value to be associated with the specified key, must not be `null`
  - `timeout` (`long`) — the maximum time to wait for a capacity slot to become available
  - `unit` (`TimeUnit`) — the time unit of the timeout argument, must not be `null`
  - `autoDestroyOnFailedToPut` (`boolean`) — if `true`, destroys a rejected non-null value unless that same instance remains pooled at the cleanup check
- **Returns:** `true` if the value was successfully added, `false` if the timeout elapsed or put failed
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the key, value, or unit is null.
  - `java.lang.InterruptedException` — if interrupted while waiting

  - `key` (`K`) — the key whose associated element is to be returned; a `null` key matches no mapping (the call waits out the timeout, returns `null` and records a miss)
  - `timeout` (`long`) — the maximum time to wait for a valid mapping for the key to become available
  - `unit` (`TimeUnit`) — the time unit of the timeout argument, must not be `null`
- **Returns:** the element associated with the key, or `null` if the timeout elapsed before a valid mapping was available (may return null)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the unit is null.
  - `java.lang.InterruptedException` — if interrupted while waiting
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  DBConnection conn = pool.get("database1", 10, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
    if (conn != null) {
        // use connection (still pooled under "database1")
    } else {
        // timed out - no connection became available for that key
    }
  ```
##### remove(...) -> E
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull E remove(K key) throws IllegalStateException`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Removes and returns the element associated with the specified key.
- **Contract:**
  - The pool does not invoke Poolable#destroy(Poolable.Caller) on the returned element — the caller takes ownership and is responsible for either returning the element to a pool or destroying it when no longer needed.
  - Borrowers that care should test `element.activityPrint().isExpired()` before using it.
- **Parameters:**
  - `key` (`K`) — the key whose mapping is to be removed from the pool; a `null` key matches no mapping (`null` is returned)
- **Returns:** the element previously associated with the key, or `null` if no mapping exists (may return null)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed
##### peek(...) -> E
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull E peek(K key) throws IllegalStateException`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Returns the element associated with the specified key without updating access statistics.
- **Contract:**
  - Important Side Effects: Does NOT update last access time - element's access time remains unchanged Does NOT update access count - element's access counter remains unchanged DOES remove and destroy expired elements - if the element has expired, it will be destroyed and removed from the pool, and `null` will be returned Does NOT remove the element from the pool (if valid) - the element remains available for future requests Use this method when you need to inspect pool contents for monitoring, debugging, or administrative purposes without affecting the element's eviction priority.
  - If you need to use the element for regular operations, use #get(Object) instead.
- **Parameters:**
  - `key` (`K`) — the key whose associated element is to be returned; a `null` key matches no mapping (`null` is returned)
- **Returns:** the element associated with the key, or `null` if no mapping exists or element expired (may return null)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Check if an element exists without affecting its access statistics
    DBConnection conn = pool.peek("database1");
    if (conn != null) {
        System.out.println("Connection available: " + conn.isActive());
        // Connection remains in pool with unchanged access statistics
    }
  ```
##### keySet(...) -> Set<K>
- **Signature:** `Set<K> keySet() throws IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Returns a Set containing a snapshot of the keys contained in this pool.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a set containing all keys currently in the pool
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Set<String> keys = pool.keySet();
    for (String key : keys) {
        System.out.println("Pool contains key: " + key);
    }
  ```
##### values(...) -> Collection<E>
- **Signature:** `Collection<E> values() throws IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Returns a Collection containing a snapshot of the values contained in this pool.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a collection containing all values currently in the pool
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed
##### containsKey(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `boolean containsKey(K key) throws IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Checks if this pool contains a mapping for the specified key.
- **Parameters:**
  - `key` (`K`) — the key whose presence in this pool is to be tested; a `null` key matches no mapping (`false` is returned)
- **Returns:** `true` if this pool contains a mapping for the specified key, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed

### Interface ObjectPool (com.landawn.abacus.pool.ObjectPool)
A pool of reusable objects that extends the base Pool interface with object-specific operations.

**Thread-safety:** thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### add(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `boolean add(E element) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Adds a new object to the pool.
- **Contract:**
  - The object will only be added if the pool has capacity and the object has not expired.
  - The add operation returns `false` (does not insert) if: The object has already expired The pool is at capacity and either auto-balancing is disabled, or balancing did not free a slot The object would exceed memory constraints (when a memory measure is configured) and balancing did not free enough memory The memory measure returns a negative size or throws an exception
- **Parameters:**
  - `element` (`E`) — the object to be added to the pool, must not be `null`
- **Returns:** `true` if the object was successfully added, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the element is null.
- **Signature:** `boolean add(E element, boolean autoDestroyOnFailedToAdd) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Adds a new object to the pool with optional automatic destruction on failure.
- **Contract:**
  - This is a convenience method that ensures proper cleanup if the object cannot be pooled.
  - Execution Order: Attempts to add the object to the pool using #add(Poolable) If add fails and `autoDestroyOnFailedToAdd` is `true`, destroys the non-null element unless still pooled by identity Returns the success status of the add operation Cleanup is attempted in a finally block even if an exception occurs.
  - Callers must coordinate concurrent ownership transfers of the same instance; the check does not prevent a later admission by another thread.
- **Parameters:**
  - `element` (`E`) — the object to be added to the pool, must not be `null`
  - `autoDestroyOnFailedToAdd` (`boolean`) — if `true`, destroys a rejected non-null element unless that same instance remains pooled at the cleanup check
- **Returns:** `true` if the object was successfully added, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the element is null.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MyPoolable obj = createExpensiveObject();
    // Object will be automatically destroyed if it can't be added
    pool.add(obj, true);
  ```
- **Signature:** `boolean add(E element, long timeout, TimeUnit unit) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, InterruptedException`
- **Summary:** Attempts to add an object to the pool, waiting if necessary for space to become available.
- **Contract:**
  - Rejection of one waiting candidate allows other waiting candidates to proceed when space is available.
  - Waiting only happens when auto-balancing is disabled (or the capacity is `0`).
  - When auto-balancing is enabled (the PoolFactory default), a full pool is first balanced - a balance-factor share of the existing elements is detached and destroyed with Poolable.Caller#VACATE - and the element is inserted without waiting, so a full pool costs the caller's other pooled elements rather than time.
- **Parameters:**
  - `element` (`E`) — the object to be added to the pool, must not be `null`
  - `timeout` (`long`) — the maximum time to wait for space to become available
  - `unit` (`TimeUnit`) — the time unit of the timeout argument, must not be `null`
- **Returns:** `true` if successful; `false` if the timeout elapsed before space was available, the element was already (or became) expired, or the memory measure rejected the element
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the element or unit is null.
  - `java.lang.InterruptedException` — if interrupted while waiting
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MyPoolable obj = new MyPoolable();
    if (pool.add(obj, 5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)) {
        // Successfully added
    } else {
        // Timeout - handle the object
        obj.destroy(Poolable.Caller.PUT_ADD_FAILURE);
    }
  ```
- **Signature:** `boolean add(E element, long timeout, TimeUnit unit, boolean autoDestroyOnFailedToAdd) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, InterruptedException`
- **Summary:** Attempts to add an object to the pool with timeout and automatic destruction on failure.
- **Contract:**
  - Execution Order: Attempts to add the object to the pool using #add(Poolable, long, TimeUnit), waiting up to the specified timeout If add fails (timeout or capacity) and `autoDestroyOnFailedToAdd` is `true`, destroys the non-null element unless still pooled by identity Returns the success status of the add operation Cleanup follows the identity-retention and concurrency rules of #add(Poolable, boolean), including when the admission throws.
- **Parameters:**
  - `element` (`E`) — the object to be added to the pool, must not be `null`
  - `timeout` (`long`) — the maximum time to wait for space to become available
  - `unit` (`TimeUnit`) — the time unit of the timeout argument, must not be `null`
  - `autoDestroyOnFailedToAdd` (`boolean`) — if `true`, destroys a rejected non-null element unless that same instance remains pooled at the cleanup check
- **Returns:** `true` if successful, `false` if timeout elapsed or add failed
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the element or unit is null.
  - `java.lang.InterruptedException` — if interrupted while waiting
##### poll(...) -> E
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull E poll() throws IllegalStateException`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Retrieves and removes an object from the pool immediately, or returns `null` if the pool is empty.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** an object from the pool, or `null` if the pool is empty (may return null)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  E obj = pool.poll();
    if (obj != null) {
        try {
            // use the object
        } finally {
            pool.add(obj, true);   // return it, or destroy it if rejected
        }
    }
  ```
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull E poll(long timeout, TimeUnit unit) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, InterruptedException`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Retrieves and removes an object from the pool, waiting if necessary for an object to become available.
- **Parameters:**
  - `timeout` (`long`) — the maximum time to wait for an object to become available
  - `unit` (`TimeUnit`) — the time unit of the timeout argument, must not be `null`
- **Returns:** an object from the pool, or `null` if the timeout elapsed before an object was available (may return null)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the unit is null.
  - `java.lang.InterruptedException` — if interrupted while waiting
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  E obj = pool.poll(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
    if (obj != null) {
        try {
            // use the object
        } finally {
            pool.add(obj, true);   // return it, or destroy it if rejected
        }
    } else {
        // timeout - pool was empty
    }
  ```
##### contains(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `boolean contains(E element) throws IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Checks if the specified object is currently in the pool.
- **Parameters:**
  - `element` (`E`) — the object to search for in the pool
- **Returns:** `true` if the pool contains the specified object, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the pool has been closed
