### Interface Type (com.landawn.abacus.type.Type)
The core type abstraction interface representing types in the abacus-common type system.

**Thread-safety:** thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### of(...) -> Type<T>
- **Signature:** `static <T> Type<T> of(final java.lang.reflect.Type javaType) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns the Type instance for the given Java reflection Type.
- **Parameters:**
  - `javaType` (`java.lang.reflect.Type`) — the Java reflection type
- **Returns:** the corresponding Type instance (never `null`; unrecognized types resolve to a generic Object-backed handler rather than failing)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `javaType` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Get type from a reflection Type
    java.lang.reflect.Type reflectType = String.class;
    Type<String> stringType = Type.of(reflectType);
  
    // Get type from a generic type
    ParameterizedType listType = (ParameterizedType) new TypeReference<List<String>>(){}.javaType();
    Type<List<String>> type = Type.of(listType);
  ```
- **Signature:** `static <T> Type<T> of(final TypeReference<T> typeRef) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns the Type instance for the given TypeReference.
- **Parameters:**
  - `typeRef` (`TypeReference<T>`) — the type reference
- **Returns:** the corresponding Type instance (never `null`)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `typeRef` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Capture generic type using TypeReference
    Type<List<String>> listType = Type.of(new TypeReference<List<String>>(){});
  
    // Capture complex generic types
    Type<Map<String, List<Integer>>> mapType = Type.of(new TypeReference<Map<String, List<Integer>>>(){});
  ```
- **Signature:** `static <T> Type<T> of(final Class<? extends T> cls) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns the Type instance for the given Class.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cls` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the class
- **Returns:** the corresponding Type instance (never `null`; unrecognized classes resolve to a generic Object-backed handler or a bean handler rather than failing)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `cls` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Get type for String
    Type<String> stringType = Type.of(String.class);
  
    // Get type for Integer
    Type<Integer> intType = Type.of(Integer.class);
  
    // Get type for a custom class
    Type<User> userType = Type.of(User.class);
  ```
- **Signature:** `static <T> Type<T> of(final String typeName) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns the Type instance by parsing the given type name string.
- **Parameters:**
  - `typeName` (`String`) — the type name string; must not be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** the corresponding Type instance (never `null`; unrecognized names resolve to a generic Object-backed handler rather than failing)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `typeName` is `null` or empty.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Simple type by name
    Type<String> stringType = Type.of("String");
  
    // Generic type by name
    Type<List<Integer>> listType = Type.of("List<Integer>");
  
    // Complex generic type by name
    Type<Map<String, List<Long>>> mapType = Type.of("Map<String, List<Long>>");
  ```
##### ofAll(...) -> List<Type<T>>
- **Signature:** `@SafeVarargs static <T> List<Type<T>> ofAll(final Class<? extends T>... classes)`
- **Summary:** Returns a list of Type instances for the given array of classes.
- **Parameters:**
  - `classes` (`Class<? extends T>[]`) — the array of classes; may be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** list of corresponding Type instances (never `null`; empty when `classes` is empty)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Get types for multiple classes
    List<Type<Object>> types = Type.ofAll(String.class, Integer.class, Date.class);
    // types: [Type<String>, Type<Integer>, Type<Date>]
  
    // Get types for custom classes
    List<Type<Object>> customTypes = Type.ofAll(User.class, Order.class);
  ```
- **Signature:** `static <T> List<Type<T>> ofAll(final Collection<Class<? extends T>> classes)`
- **Summary:** Returns a list of Type instances for the given collection of classes.
- **Parameters:**
  - `classes` (`Collection<Class<? extends T>>`) — the collection of classes; may be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** list of corresponding Type instances (never `null`; empty when `classes` is empty)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Get types from a collection
    Collection<Class<?>> classList = Arrays.asList(String.class, Integer.class);
    List<Type<Object>> types = Type.ofAll(classList);
  
    // Process types from a set
    Set<Class<? extends Number>> numberClasses = new HashSet<>(Arrays.asList(Integer.class, Long.class));
    List<Type<Number>> numberTypes = Type.ofAll(numberClasses);
  ```
##### ofList(...) -> Type<List<T>>
- **Signature:** `static <T> Type<List<T>> ofList(final Class<? extends T> eleClass) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a List type with the specified element type.
- **Parameters:**
  - `eleClass` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the element class
- **Returns:** Type instance for List of the specified element type
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `eleClass` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Create a List<String> type
    Type<List<String>> listType = Type.ofList(String.class);
  
    // Create a List<Integer> type
  ```

- **Signature:** `int compare(T x, T y) throws UnsupportedOperationException`

  - `y` (`T`) — the second value; may be `null`

- **See also:** #isComparable()

- **Returns:** the converted value, or the result of `valueOf((String) null)` when `obj` is `null`: `null` for reference types, the type's default (`0` / `false`) for primitive types
- **See also:** #valueOf(String), #stringOf(Object)
- **Signature:** `T valueOf(char[] cbuf, int offset, int len)`

- **Returns:** the parsed value, or the result of `valueOf((String) null)` when `cbuf` is `null` (`null` for reference types, the type's default for primitive types; typically the same when `len == 0`, depending on the concrete implementation)
- **See also:** #valueOf(String), #stringOf(Object)

##### appendTo(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `void appendTo(Appendable appendable, T x) throws NullPointerException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Appends a plain, human-readable string representation of a value to an `Appendable` (the literal `"null"` string for a `null` value).
- **Parameters:**
  - `appendable` (`Appendable`) — the target to append to
  - `x` (`T`) — the value to append
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `appendable` is `null`
  - `java.io.IOException` — if appending the value to `appendable` fails
- **See also:** #serializeTo(CharacterWriter, Object, JsonXmlSerConfig)
##### serializeTo(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `void serializeTo(CharacterWriter writer, T x, JsonXmlSerConfig<?> config) throws NullPointerException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Writes the serialized form of a value to a `CharacterWriter`, applying string quotation and character escaping according to the supplied configuration (a `null` config means no surrounding quotation).
- **Parameters:**
  - `writer` (`CharacterWriter`) — the CharacterWriter to write to
  - `x` (`T`) — the value to write
  - `config` (`JsonXmlSerConfig<?>`) — the serialization configuration, may be `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `writer` is `null`
  - `java.io.IOException` — if writing the serialized value to `writer` fails
- **See also:** #appendTo(Appendable, Object)

### Class TypeFactory (com.landawn.abacus.type.TypeFactory)
A factory class for creating, registering, and retrieving Type objects in the abacus-common type system.

**Thread-safety:** thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### getType(...) -> Type<T>
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings({ "rawtypes", "unchecked" }) public static <T> Type<T> getType(final Class<?> cls) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves the Type object corresponding to the specified Class object.
- **Contract:**
  - If the type is not found in the cache, it creates a new Type instance and atomically publishes it for future use.
  - If a custom registration or another lookup publishes a mapping concurrently, that existing mapping wins and is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cls` (`Class<?>`) — the Class object for which to retrieve the Type
- **Returns:** the Type object corresponding to the specified class (never `null`)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `cls` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Type<String> stringType = TypeFactory.getType(String.class);
    Type<Integer> intType = TypeFactory.getType(Integer.class);
    Type<List> listType = TypeFactory.getType(List.class);
  ```
- **See also:** #getType(String), #getType(java.lang.reflect.Type)
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("rawtypes") public static <T> Type<T> getType(final java.lang.reflect.Type javaType) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves the Type object corresponding to the specified java.lang.reflect.Type.
- **Contract:**
  - Cache publication is atomic: when another lookup has already published a result for the same reflection type, that result is retained and returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `javaType` (`java.lang.reflect.Type`) — the java.lang.reflect.Type to convert, including Class, ParameterizedType and GenericArrayType
- **Returns:** the corresponding Type object (never `null`)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `javaType` is `null`, or if the type name format is structurally invalid.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  java.lang.reflect.Type listType = new TypeReference<List<String>>() {}.javaType();
    Type<List<String>> strings = TypeFactory.getType(listType);
  
    java.lang.reflect.Type mapType = new TypeReference<Map<String, Integer>>() {}.javaType();
    Type<Map<String, Integer>> mapping = TypeFactory.getType(mapType);
  ```
- **See also:** #getType(Class), #getType(String)
- **Signature:** `public static <T> Type<T> getType(final String typeName) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves the Type object corresponding to the specified type name string.
- **Contract:**
  - If the type pool size reaches multiples of 100, a warning is logged about the pool size.
- **Parameters:**
  - `typeName` (`String`) — the name of the type to retrieve, with optional type parameters; must not be `null`, empty or blank; surrounding whitespace is ignored
- **Returns:** the Type object corresponding to the type name (never `null`; an ObjectType is returned for unresolvable names)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `typeName` is `null`, empty or blank, or if the type name format is structurally invalid (a mismatched type-parameter count, unused constructor arguments on a resolved class, misplaced brackets).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Type<String> t1 = TypeFactory.getType("String");
    t1.javaType();                  // returns String.class
  
    Type<List<String>> t2 = TypeFactory.getType("List<String>");
    t2.name();            // returns "List<String>"
    t2.declaringName();   // returns "List<String>"
    t2.javaType();        // returns List.class
  
    Type<?> t3 = TypeFactory.getType("CompletelyUnknownName");
    t3.isObject();                        // returns true (ObjectType fallback, not an exception)
  
    boolean sameInstance = TypeFactory.getType(" Integer ") == TypeFactory.getType("Integer");   // true
    TypeFactory.getType("List<? extends Person>").elementType().javaType();   // Person.class
  
    TypeFactory.getType((String) null);   // throws IllegalArgumentException
    TypeFactory.getType("");              // throws IllegalArgumentException
    TypeFactory.getType("String(MD5)");   // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
- **See also:** #getType(Class), #registerType(String, Type)
##### getTypeIfPresent(...) -> Type<?>
- **Signature:** `public static Type<?> getTypeIfPresent(final String typeName)`
- **Summary:** Returns an already registered type without attempting to load or derive a class from the supplied name.
- **Contract:**
  - This non-creating lookup is useful when a name comes from an untrusted source and class loading must not be triggered as a side effect.
- **Parameters:**
  - `typeName` (`String`) — the exact registered type name; may be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** the registered type, or `null` when `typeName` is `null` or empty, or when the exact name has not been registered
##### registerType(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static <T> void registerType(final Class<T> targetClass, final BiFunction<? super T, JsonParser, String> toStringFunc, final BiFunction<? super String, JsonParser, T> fromStringFunc) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Registers a custom Type for the specified target class with custom serialization/deserialization functions.
- **Contract:**
  - This method allows you to define how objects of a specific class should be converted to and from strings.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class for which to register the custom type
  - `toStringFunc` (`BiFunction<? super T, JsonParser, String>`) — the function to convert an object of type T to a String, receives the object and a JsonParser
  - `fromStringFunc` (`BiFunction<? super String, JsonParser, T>`) — the function to convert a String to an object of type T, receives the string and a JsonParser
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetClass`, `toStringFunc`, or `fromStringFunc` is `null`, if `targetClass` has a built-in type, or if a type has already been resolved and cached for it by a prior lookup by class (`getType(Class)`, bean introspection, serialization). A fabricated fallback cached only by canonical name may be superseded.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  TypeFactory.registerType(
        MyCustomClass.class,
        (obj, parser) -> obj.toCustomString(),
        (str, parser) -> MyCustomClass.fromString(str)
    );
  ```
- **See also:** #registerType(Class, Function, Function), #registerType(Class, Type)
- **Signature:** `public static <T> void registerType(final Class<T> cls, final Function<? super T, String> toStringFunc, final Function<? super String, T> fromStringFunc) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Registers a custom Type for the specified class with simple serialization/deserialization functions.
- **Contract:**
  - This method provides a simpler alternative to #registerType(Class, BiFunction, BiFunction) when you don't need access to a JsonParser instance for serialization/deserialization.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cls` (`Class<T>`) — the class for which to register the custom type
  - `toStringFunc` (`Function<? super T, String>`) — the function to convert an object of type T to a String
  - `fromStringFunc` (`Function<? super String, T>`) — the function to convert a String to an object of type T
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `cls`, `toStringFunc`, or `fromStringFunc` is `null`, if `cls` has a built-in type, or if a type has already been resolved and cached for it by a prior lookup by class (`getType(Class)`, bean introspection, serialization). A fabricated fallback cached only by canonical name may be superseded.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  TypeFactory.registerType(
        EmailAddress.class,
        email -> email.getValue(),
        str -> new EmailAddress(str)
    );
  ```
- **See also:** #registerType(Class, BiFunction, BiFunction), #registerType(Class, Type)
- **Signature:** `public static <T> void registerType(final Class<T> cls, final Type<T> type) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Registers a custom Type implementation for the specified class.
- **Contract:**
  - Attempting to do so will throw an IllegalArgumentException, so custom types should be registered before the class is first used.
  - A successfully registered mapping is retained if a concurrent lookup was already constructing a default type for the same class.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cls` (`Class<T>`) — the class for which to register the type
  - `type` (`Type<T>`) — the Type implementation to register for the class
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `cls` or `type` is `null`, if a type is already registered or built in for the class, if a type has already been resolved and cached for the class by a prior lookup, or if a type with the same name (as returned by Type#name()) already exists.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Type<MyClass> customType = new MyCustomType();
    TypeFactory.registerType(MyClass.class, customType);
    Type<MyClass> retrieved = TypeFactory.getType(MyClass.class);
  
    TypeFactory.registerType(Map.class, customMapType); // throws IllegalArgumentException: built-in
  ```
- **See also:** #registerType(String, Type), #getType(Class)
- **Signature:** `public static <T> void registerType(String typeName, final Class<T> targetClass, final BiFunction<? super T, JsonParser, String> toStringFunc, final BiFunction<? super String, JsonParser, T> fromStringFunc) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Registers a custom Type with a specific type name and target class, using custom serialization functions with JsonParser.
- **Contract:**
  - It also becomes the type of `targetClass` when nothing already answers for that class; a class that has a built-in handler (`Map`, `List`, `java.util.Date`, `LocalDateTime`,...) or whose type a prior lookup has already resolved keeps the type it has.
- **Parameters:**
  - `typeName` (`String`) — the custom name for this type registration; surrounding whitespace is ignored
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class that this type handles
  - `toStringFunc` (`BiFunction<? super T, JsonParser, String>`) — the function to convert an object of type T to a String, receives the object and a JsonParser
  - `fromStringFunc` (`BiFunction<? super String, JsonParser, T>`) — the function to convert a String to an object of type T, receives the string and a JsonParser
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `typeName` is `null`, empty or blank, if it is not a well-formed type declaration (e.g. `"X<Y"`), if a type is already registered under that name, or if `targetClass`, `toStringFunc`, or `fromStringFunc` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  TypeFactory.registerType(
        "CustomDate",
        LocalDate.class,
        (date, parser) -> date.format(DateTimeFormatter.ISO_DATE),
        (str, parser) -> LocalDate.parse(str, DateTimeFormatter.ISO_DATE)
    );
  ```
- **See also:** #registerType(String, Class, Function, Function), #registerType(String, Type)
- **Signature:** `public static <T> void registerType(String typeName, final Class<T> targetClass, final Function<? super T, String> toStringFunc, final Function<? super String, T> fromStringFunc) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Registers a custom Type with a specific type name and target class, using simple serialization functions.
- **Contract:**
  - This method provides a simpler alternative to #registerType(String, Class, BiFunction, BiFunction) when you don't need access to a JsonParser instance.
  - It also becomes the type of `targetClass` when nothing already answers for that class; a class that has a built-in handler or whose type a prior lookup has already resolved keeps the type it has, so a lookup by class and a lookup by name cannot disagree.
- **Parameters:**
  - `typeName` (`String`) — the custom name for this type registration; surrounding whitespace is ignored
  - `targetClass` (`Class<T>`) — the class that this type handles
  - `toStringFunc` (`Function<? super T, String>`) — the function to convert an object of type T to a String
  - `fromStringFunc` (`Function<? super String, T>`) — the function to convert a String to an object of type T
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `typeName` is `null`, empty or blank, if it is not a well-formed type declaration (e.g. `"X<Y"`), if a type is already registered under that name, or if `targetClass`, `toStringFunc`, or `fromStringFunc` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  TypeFactory.registerType(
        "ISODate",
        LocalDate.class,
        date -> date.toString(),
        LocalDate::parse
    );
  ```
- **See also:** #registerType(String, Class, BiFunction, BiFunction), #registerType(String, Type)
- **Signature:** `public static void registerType(String typeName, final Type<?> type) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Registers a Type implementation with a specific type name.
- **Contract:**
  - Note: A type name must be unique.
- **Parameters:**
  - `typeName` (`String`) — the name to register the type under; surrounding whitespace is ignored, and the name must be one that #getType(String) can parse (a well-formed type declaration)
  - `type` (`Type<?>`) — the Type implementation to register
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if typeName is `null`, empty or blank, if it is not a well-formed type declaration (e.g. `"X<Y"`), if type is `null`, if a type with the given name already exists, or if a type with the same name (as returned by Type#name()) already exists.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Type<MyClass> customType = new MyCustomType();
    TypeFactory.registerType("CustomTypeName", customType);
    Type<MyClass> retrieved = TypeFactory.getType("CustomTypeName");
  ```
- **See also:** #registerType(Type), #getType(String)
- **Signature:** `public static void registerType(final Type<?> type) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Registers a Type implementation using its built-in name.
- **Contract:**
  - This is typically used internally when registering built-in types or when the type already has an appropriate name defined.
  - Note: The type's name must be unique.
- **Parameters:**
  - `type` (`Type<?>`) — the Type implementation to register
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if type is `null` or if a type with the same name already exists.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Type<MyClass> customType = new MyCustomType();
    TypeFactory.registerType(customType);
    Type<MyClass> retrieved = TypeFactory.getType("MyClass");
  ```
- **See also:** #registerType(String, Type), Type#name()

#### Public Instance Methods

#### Public Constructors

##### javaType(...) -> Class<URI>
- **Signature:** `@Override public Class<URI> javaType()`

##### stringOf(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `@Override public String stringOf(final URI x)`
- **Summary:** Converts a URI instance to its string representation (the URI text).
- **Contract:**

- **Parameters:**
  - `x` (`URI`) — the URI instance to convert to string
- **Returns:** the string representation of the URI, or `null` if the input is null
- **Examples:**
  ```java

    URI uri = URI.create("https://example.com/path");

  ```
- **See also:** #valueOf(String), #valueOf(Object)
##### valueOf(...) -> URI
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull @Override public URI valueOf(final String str) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Parses a string representation to create a URI instance.
- **Contract:**
  - If the string is `null`, this method returns `null`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to convert to a URI
- **Returns:** a URI instance created from the string, or `null` if the string is `null` (may return null)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the string violates RFC 2396 URI syntax rules.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Type<URI> type = TypeFactory.getType(URI.class);
    URI uri = type.valueOf("https://example.com/path");   // Creates a URI
  ```
- **See also:** #valueOf(Object), #stringOf(URI)
##### isComparable(...) -> boolean

- **Summary:** Indicates whether URI values are comparable.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** `true`, always, because URI is Comparable
##### get(...) -> URI
- **Signature:** `@Override public URI get(final ResultSet rs, final int columnIndex) throws NullPointerException, SQLException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves a URI value from a ResultSet at the specified column index.
- **Parameters:**
  - `rs` (`ResultSet`) — the ResultSet to read from
  - `columnIndex` (`int`) — the column index (1-based) of the URI value
- **Returns:** the URI value, or `null` if the database value is NULL
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `rs` is `null`.
  - `java.sql.SQLException` — if the result set is closed, the requested column is invalid, or the JDBC read fails.
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the column text violates URI syntax.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Type<URI> type = TypeFactory.getType(URI.class);
    try (ResultSet rs = statement.executeQuery("SELECT homepage FROM websites")) {
        if (rs.next()) {
            URI homepage = type.get(rs, 1);   // Get URI from first column
        }
    }
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Override public URI get(final ResultSet rs, final String columnName) throws NullPointerException, SQLException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves a URI value from a ResultSet using the specified column label.
- **Parameters:**
  - `rs` (`ResultSet`) — the ResultSet to read from
  - `columnName` (`String`) — the label of the column containing the URI value
- **Returns:** the URI value, or `null` if the database value is NULL
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `rs` is `null`.
  - `java.sql.SQLException` — if the result set is closed, the requested column is invalid, or the JDBC read fails.
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the column text violates URI syntax.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Type<URI> type = TypeFactory.getType(URI.class);
    try (ResultSet rs = statement.executeQuery("SELECT homepage FROM websites")) {
        if (rs.next()) {
            URI homepage = type.get(rs, "homepage");   // Get URI by column name
        }
    }
  ```
##### set(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@Override public void set(final PreparedStatement stmt, final int columnIndex, final URI x) throws NullPointerException, SQLException`
- **Summary:** Sets a URI value in a PreparedStatement at the specified parameter index.
- **Contract:**
  - If the URI is `null`, a NULL value is set.
- **Parameters:**
  - `stmt` (`PreparedStatement`) — the PreparedStatement to set the value in
  - `columnIndex` (`int`) — the parameter index (1-based) where to set the URI value
  - `x` (`URI`) — the URI value to set, or `null` for SQL NULL
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `stmt` is `null`.
  - `java.sql.SQLException` — if the statement is closed, the parameter is invalid, or the JDBC bind fails.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Type<URI> type = TypeFactory.getType(URI.class);
    PreparedStatement stmt = conn.prepareStatement("INSERT INTO websites (homepage) VALUES (?)");
    type.set(stmt, 1, URI.create("https://example.com"));   // Set URI at parameter index 1
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Override public void set(final CallableStatement stmt, final String parameterName, final URI x) throws NullPointerException, SQLException`
- **Summary:** Sets a URI value in a CallableStatement using the specified parameter name.
- **Contract:**
  - If the URI is `null`, a NULL value is set.
- **Parameters:**
  - `stmt` (`CallableStatement`) — the CallableStatement to set the value in
  - `parameterName` (`String`) — the name of the parameter where to set the URI value
  - `x` (`URI`) — the URI value to set, or `null` for SQL NULL
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `stmt` is `null`.
  - `java.sql.SQLException` — if the statement is closed, the parameter is invalid, or the JDBC bind fails.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Type<URI> type = TypeFactory.getType(URI.class);
    CallableStatement stmt = conn.prepareCall("{call update_website(?)}");
    type.set(stmt, "homepage", URI.create("https://example.com"));   // Set URI by parameter name
  ```

##### valueOf(...) -> XMLGregorianCalendar
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull @Override public XMLGregorianCalendar valueOf(final String str) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Converts a string to an XMLGregorianCalendar instance.
- **Contract:**
  - Use javax.xml.datatype.DatatypeFactory#newXMLGregorianCalendar(String) when exact XML lexical reconstruction (including an undefined timezone), partial calendar values, leap seconds, or fractions finer than nanoseconds is required.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to convert to XMLGregorianCalendar
- **Returns:** an XMLGregorianCalendar instance, or `null` if the string is `null` or empty (may return null)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the string cannot be parsed as a valid date/time, or if numeric input resolves, in the default time zone, to an offset that is not a whole number of minutes within `-14:00..+14:00` (an `XMLGregorianCalendar` cannot carry such an offset; this affects pre-1900 instants in zones whose historical local mean time offset has a seconds part)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  XMLGregorianCalendar cal1 = type.valueOf("2023-10-15T10:30:00");
    XMLGregorianCalendar cal2 = type.valueOf("SYS_TIME");   // Current time
  ```
- **See also:** #valueOf(Object), #stringOf(XMLGregorianCalendar)
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull @Override public XMLGregorianCalendar valueOf(final char[] cbuf, final int offset, final int len) throws IndexOutOfBoundsException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Converts a character array to an XMLGregorianCalendar instance.
- **Contract:**
  - This method first checks if the character array represents a long value (epoch milliseconds: digits ending in a digit, so a trailing `L`/`d`/`f` type suffix is not accepted).
  - If so, it creates an XMLGregorianCalendar from that timestamp.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cbuf` (`char[]`) — the character array containing the date/time representation
  - `offset` (`int`) — the starting position in the character array
  - `len` (`int`) — the number of characters to process
- **Returns:** an XMLGregorianCalendar instance, or `null` if the input is `null` or empty (may return null)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if the requested nonempty region is read outside `cbuf`; a `null` buffer or zero length returns `null` without reading.
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the text is not a recognized date-time or numeric form (see #valueOf(String), including its default-zone offset restriction on numeric input), or if numeric text lies outside the `long` range
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  char[] chars = "1697364600000".toCharArray();
    XMLGregorianCalendar cal = type.valueOf(chars, 0, chars.length);   // From epoch millis
  ```

- **Returns:** the string representation of the XMLGregorianCalendar, or `null` if the input is null
- **Examples:**

- **Summary:** Appends the string representation of an XMLGregorianCalendar to an Appendable.
- **Implementation note:** For a non-null value this method appends exactly the same XML lexical text as #stringOf(XMLGregorianCalendar). For `null`, it appends the literal `"null"`, whereas `stringOf(null)` returns `null`. The inverse-parsing limitations for partial values, leap seconds, fine fractions, and undefined timezones are described by #stringOf(XMLGregorianCalendar).
- **Contract:**
  - If the XMLGregorianCalendar is `null`, it appends the string "null".
- **Parameters:**
  - `appendable` (`Appendable`) — the Appendable to write to
  - `x` (`XMLGregorianCalendar`) — the XMLGregorianCalendar value to append
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `x` and `appendable` are both null
  - `java.io.IOException` — if appending the null literal fails
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `x` is non-null and `appendable` is null
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the fields of `x` do not form a valid XML Schema date/time type
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if appending the XML lexical representation of a non-null value fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
    type.appendTo(sb, xmlGregorianCalendar);   // Appends formatted date/time
  ```
##### serializeTo(...) -> void

- **Summary:** Writes the character representation of an XMLGregorianCalendar to a CharacterWriter.
- **Parameters:**
  - `writer` (`CharacterWriter`) — the CharacterWriter to write to
  - `x` (`XMLGregorianCalendar`) — the XMLGregorianCalendar value to write
  - `config` (`JsonXmlSerConfig<?>`) — the serialization configuration controlling format and quoting
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `writer` is null when writing the null literal, a quotation mark or the LONG representation
  - `java.io.IOException` — if directly writing the null literal, a quotation mark or the LONG representation fails
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `writer` is null when formatting a non-null value without quotation, or an explicit ISO format cannot represent the value's year
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the default format is selected and the fields of `x` do not form a valid XML Schema date/time type
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if writing a non-null value through `Dates.formatTo` fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  BufferedJsonWriter writer = Objectory.createBufferedJsonWriter();
    JsonSerConfig config = JsonSerConfig.create();
    try {
        type.serializeTo(writer, xmlGregorianCalendar, config);   // Writes formatted date/time
    } finally {
        Objectory.recycle(writer);
    }
  ```

- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull @Override public ZonedDateTime valueOf(final Object obj) throws IllegalArgumentException, DateTimeParseException`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Converts an object to a ZonedDateTime instance.
- **Contract:**
  - This method handles conversion from: ZonedDateTime - returned unchanged Number or java.util.Date - interpreted as epoch milliseconds in the default zone java.util.Calendar - interpreted as epoch milliseconds in the calendar's own time zone (the default zone if it has none), so the zone the caller supplied survives the conversion Other non-null objects - converted to a string and parsed according to supported date/time formats `null` - returns `null` Usage Examples: SQL Timestamp inputs preserve nanoseconds in the default zone.
- **Parameters:**

- **Returns:** a ZonedDateTime instance, or `null` if the input is null (may return null)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the input is a non-lenient calendar containing invalid field values.
  - `java.time.format.DateTimeParseException` — if the text representation is neither a supported millisecond value nor a valid ISO-8601 `ZonedDateTime` (see #valueOf(String)).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ZonedDateTime zdt1 = type.valueOf(1697364600000L);           // From epoch milliseconds
    ZonedDateTime zdt2 = type.valueOf("2023-10-15T10:30:00Z");   // From string
  ```

- **Examples:**

- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ZonedDateTime zdt = type.get(resultSet, "created_date");
    // Retrieves timestamp from the "created_date" column
  ```
##### set(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@Override public void set(final PreparedStatement stmt, final int columnIndex, final ZonedDateTime x) throws IllegalArgumentException, NullPointerException, SQLException`
- **Summary:** Sets a ZonedDateTime value in a PreparedStatement at the specified parameter index.
- **Contract:**
  - If the ZonedDateTime is `null`, a NULL value is set.
- **Parameters:**
  - `stmt` (`PreparedStatement`) — the PreparedStatement to set the value in
  - `columnIndex` (`int`) — the parameter index (1-based) where to set the value
  - `x` (`ZonedDateTime`) — the ZonedDateTime value to set, or `null` for SQL NULL
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a non-null value cannot be converted to a `Timestamp` because its epoch-millisecond value overflows
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `stmt` is null when the JDBC operation is invoked
  - `java.sql.SQLException` — if a database access error occurs or the parameter index is invalid
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ZonedDateTime zdt = ZonedDateTime.now();
    type.set(preparedStatement, 1, zdt);   // Sets timestamp at first parameter
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Override public void set(final CallableStatement stmt, final String parameterName, final ZonedDateTime x) throws IllegalArgumentException, NullPointerException, SQLException`
- **Summary:** Sets a ZonedDateTime value in a CallableStatement using the specified parameter name.
- **Contract:**
  - If the ZonedDateTime is `null`, a NULL value is set.
- **Parameters:**
  - `stmt` (`CallableStatement`) — the CallableStatement to set the value in
  - `parameterName` (`String`) — the name of the parameter where to set the value
  - `x` (`ZonedDateTime`) — the ZonedDateTime value to set, or `null` for SQL NULL
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a non-null value cannot be converted to a `Timestamp` because its epoch-millisecond value overflows
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `stmt` is null when the JDBC operation is invoked
  - `java.sql.SQLException` — if a database access error occurs or the parameter name is invalid
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ZonedDateTime zdt = ZonedDateTime.now();
    type.set(callableStatement, "created_date", zdt);   // Sets timestamp parameter
  ```
##### appendTo(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@Override public void appendTo(final Appendable appendable, final ZonedDateTime x) throws NullPointerException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Appends the string representation of a ZonedDateTime to an Appendable.
- **Implementation note:** This method appends a string representation of `x` to `appendable` (the literal `"null"` for a `null` value). Conceptually this is the human-readable form produced by `toString()`, not the value returned by `stringOf`, which is a formatted, serializable representation (typically a JSON string) that #valueOf(String) can convert back into an equivalent value. For values whose nested structure makes the two forms differ (collections, maps, arrays), `appendTo` emits the unquoted, `toString()`-style form; it is therefore not, in the general contract, a plain `appendable.append(x == null? NULL_STRING: stringOf(x))`. (For value types whose human-readable and serialized forms coincide, the appended text is naturally identical to `stringOf(x)`.)
- **Contract:**
  - If the ZonedDateTime is `null`, it appends the string `"null"`.
  - serializeTo: `appendTo` produces a plain, `toString()`-style rendering with no JSON/XML quoting or escaping (for general text output), whereas `serializeTo` writes the configured JSON/XML serialized form, including string quotation for non-LONG date/time formats when requested by config.
- **Parameters:**
  - `appendable` (`Appendable`) — the Appendable to write to
  - `x` (`ZonedDateTime`) — the ZonedDateTime value to append
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `appendable` is `null`.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if appending the formatted date/time text or null literal to `appendable` fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
    type.appendTo(sb, ZonedDateTime.now());   // Appends formatted date/time
  ```
##### serializeTo(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("null") @Override public void serializeTo(final CharacterWriter writer, final ZonedDateTime x, final JsonXmlSerConfig<?> config) throws NullPointerException, IOException, ArithmeticException`
- **Summary:** Writes the character representation of a ZonedDateTime to a CharacterWriter.
- **Contract:**
  - DateTimeFormat#LONG writes epoch milliseconds without quotes; string date/time formats use the requested string quotation when configured.
- **Parameters:**
  - `writer` (`CharacterWriter`) — the CharacterWriter to write to
  - `x` (`ZonedDateTime`) — the ZonedDateTime value to write
  - `config` (`JsonXmlSerConfig<?>`) — the serialization configuration controlling format and quoting; may be `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `writer` is `null`.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if writing the selected date/time representation, quotation marks or null literal to `writer` fails
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if the LONG format is selected and the epoch-millisecond value overflows a long
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  BufferedJsonWriter writer = Objectory.createBufferedJsonWriter();
    JsonSerConfig config = JsonSerConfig.create();
    try {
        type.serializeTo(writer, ZonedDateTime.now(), config);   // Writes formatted date/time
    } finally {
        Objectory.recycle(writer);
    }
  ```

### Class AddrUtil (com.landawn.abacus.util.AddrUtil)
Utility class for handling and parsing network addresses.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### getServerList(...) -> List<String>
- **Signature:** `public static List<String> getServerList(final String servers) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Splits a string containing whitespace or comma separated host or IP addresses and port numbers into a List of server strings without parsing or validating them.
- **Parameters:**
  - `servers` (`String`) — the string containing server addresses separated by whitespace or commas
- **Returns:** a non-empty list of trimmed server address strings
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `servers` is `null`, empty, or results in an empty list after splitting and trimming.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> servers = AddrUtil.getServerList("server1:8080, server2:8080");
    // Returns: ["server1:8080", "server2:8080"]
  ```
##### getAddressList(...) -> List<InetSocketAddress>
- **Signature:** `public static List<InetSocketAddress> getAddressList(final String servers) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Parses a string containing whitespace or comma separated host or IP addresses and port numbers into a List of InetSocketAddress instances.
- **Contract:**
  - An unbracketed address holding more than one colon is split only when that reading is the only possible one: if the whole token is itself a valid IPv6 literal it is rejected as ambiguous (`"fe80::1:8080"`, `"::1:1121"`), and otherwise the part before the last colon must itself be a valid IPv6 literal (`"::1:11211"` is accepted, `"abc:def:1234"` is not).
  - This method supports various address formats including: Standard format: `"host:port host2:port"` or `"host:port, host2:port"` IPv4 addresses: `"192.168.1.1:8080"` IPv6, bracketed: `"\[::1\]:11211"`, `"\[fe80::1\]:8080"` IPv6, unbracketed and unambiguous: `"::1:11211"` (but `"::1:1121"` is rejected - it is itself a valid address) Hostnames: `"localhost:8080"` or `"example.com:443"` The port number must be a valid integer in the range 0-65535.
  - Each address must contain at least one colon separating the host and port.
  - Both the host part and port part must be non-empty.
  - That call may block on DNS, and a host that cannot be resolved yields an unresolved address rather than an exception - test InetSocketAddress#isUnresolved() if that matters to the caller.
- **Parameters:**
  - `servers` (`String`) — the string containing server addresses to parse; must not be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** a non-empty list of InetSocketAddress instances corresponding to the parsed addresses
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the servers string is `null`, empty, or contains invalid addresses (missing colon, an unbracketed multi-colon address that is itself a valid IPv6 literal or whose host part is not one, invalid port number, empty host or port, or port out of valid range 0-65535).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<InetSocketAddress> addrs = AddrUtil.getAddressList("localhost:11211, 192.168.1.100:11211");
    // Can be used with network clients:
    // MemcachedClient client = new MemcachedClient(addrs);
  ```
- **See also:** #getAddressList(Collection), #getServerList(String)
- **Signature:** `public static List<InetSocketAddress> getAddressList(final Collection<String> servers) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts a collection of server address strings into a list of InetSocketAddress instances.
- **Contract:**
  - Each string in the collection should be in the format `"host:port"`.
  - This method parses each address string individually by finding the last colon to separate the host from the port; an unbracketed address holding more than one colon is split only when that reading is the only possible one, exactly as in #getAddressList(String).
  - Supported address formats: Hostnames: `"localhost:8080"`, `"example.com:443"` IPv4 addresses: `"192.168.1.1:8080"` IPv6, bracketed: `"\[::1\]:11211"`, `"\[fe80::1\]:8080"` IPv6, unbracketed and unambiguous: `"::1:11211"` Each address must contain at least one colon separating the host and port.
  - The port must be a valid integer in the range 0-65535.
  - Both host and port parts must be non-empty.
  - That call may block on DNS, and a host that cannot be resolved yields an unresolved address rather than an exception - test InetSocketAddress#isUnresolved() if that matters to the caller.
- **Parameters:**
  - `servers` (`Collection<String>`) — a collection of server addresses where each string is in the format `"host:port"`; must not be `null`
- **Returns:** a non-empty list of InetSocketAddress instances corresponding to the server addresses
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `servers` is `null`, any server address is invalid (missing colon, an unbracketed multi-colon address that is itself a valid IPv6 literal or whose host part is not one, invalid port number, empty host or port, or port out of valid range 0-65535), or if the collection results in an empty address list.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> serverStrings = Arrays.asList("127.0.0.1:8080", "192.168.1.1:8080");
    List<InetSocketAddress> addresses = AddrUtil.getAddressList(serverStrings);
  ```
- **See also:** #getAddressList(String), #getServerList(String)
##### getAddressFromUrl(...) -> InetSocketAddress
- **Signature:** `public static InetSocketAddress getAddressFromUrl(final URL url) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates an InetSocketAddress from a URL object by extracting its host and port information.
- **Contract:**
  - The host is extracted from the URL's authority component, and the port is taken from the URL's explicit port (if specified) or the default port for the protocol.
  - If the URL does not specify a port explicitly and URL#getPort() returns -1, the method will attempt to use URL#getDefaultPort() to get the protocol's default port.
  - If neither an explicit nor a default port is available (i.e., the resolved port is outside the valid range 0-65535), an IllegalArgumentException is thrown.
- **Parameters:**
  - `url` (`URL`) — a URL from which the host and port are to be extracted; must not be `null`
- **Returns:** an InetSocketAddress instance corresponding to the host and port of the URL
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `url` is `null` or if the URL has no host or no usable port (resolved port is outside the range 0-65535).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  URL url = new URL("http://localhost:8080/path");
    InetSocketAddress addr = AddrUtil.getAddressFromUrl(url);
    // Returns InetSocketAddress with host="localhost" and port=8080
  ```
- **See also:** #getAddressList(Collection)
##### getAddressListFromUrls(...) -> List<InetSocketAddress>
- **Signature:** `public static List<InetSocketAddress> getAddressListFromUrls(final Collection<URL> urls) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts a collection of URL objects into a list of InetSocketAddress instances.
- **Contract:**
  - If a URL does not specify a port explicitly and URL#getPort() returns -1, the method will attempt to use URL#getDefaultPort() to get the protocol's default port.
  - If neither an explicit nor a default port is available (i.e., the resolved port is outside the valid range 0-65535), an IllegalArgumentException is thrown.
- **Parameters:**
  - `urls` (`Collection<URL>`) — a collection of URL objects to be converted; may be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** a list of InetSocketAddress instances corresponding to the URLs, or an empty list if the input collection is `null` or empty
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the collection contains a `null` URL, or any URL has no host or no usable port (resolved port is outside the range 0-65535).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<URL> urls = Arrays.asList(
        new URL("http://localhost:8080"),
        new URL("http://127.0.0.1:9090")
    );
    List<InetSocketAddress> addresses = AddrUtil.getAddressListFromUrls(urls);
    // Returns a list with two InetSocketAddress instances
  ```
- **See also:** #getAddressFromUrl(URL)

- **Summary:** Appends a subsequence of the specified character sequence to this writer.
- **Parameters:**

  - `start` (`int`) — the index of the first character in the subsequence
  - `end` (`int`) — the index of the character following the last character in the subsequence
- **Returns:** this writer
- **Throws:**

### Class Array (com.landawn.abacus.util.Array)
A comprehensive utility class providing an extensive collection of static methods for array manipulation, creation, transformation, and processing operations.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified
**Permitted subtypes:** Array.ArrayUtil

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### newInstance(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T newInstance(final Class<?> componentType, final int length) throws IllegalArgumentException, NegativeArraySizeException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new instance of an array with the specified component type and length.
- **Parameters:**
  - `componentType` (`Class<?>`) — the Class object representing the component type of the new array. Must not be `null` or Void#TYPE.
  - `length` (`int`) — the length of the new array.
- **Returns:** a new array of the specified component type and length. When `length` is 0 and `componentType` is one of the common built-in types, a shared immutable empty array is returned instead of a fresh one; for every other component type a new array is returned.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `componentType` is `null` or Void#TYPE, or the resulting array would exceed 255 dimensions.
  - `java.lang.NegativeArraySizeException` — if the specified length is negative.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Integer[] intArray = Array.newInstance(Integer.class, 5);   // returns an Integer array of length 5
    String[] strArray = Array.newInstance(String.class, 10);    // returns a String array of length 10
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T newInstance(final Class<?> componentType, final int... dimensions) throws IllegalArgumentException, NegativeArraySizeException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new instance of an array with the specified component type and dimensions.
- **Contract:**
  - The dimensions should be a valid int array representing the dimensions of the new array.
- **Parameters:**
  - `componentType` (`Class<?>`) — the Class object representing the component type of the new array. Must not be `null` or Void#TYPE.
  - `dimensions` (`int[]`) — the dimensions of the new array. Must not be `null` or empty, and there must be no more than 255 of them.
- **Returns:** a new multi-dimensional array of the specified component type and dimensions.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `componentType` is null or Void#TYPE, `dimensions` is null or empty, or the sum of its length and the existing array dimensions of `componentType` exceeds 255.
  - `java.lang.NegativeArraySizeException` — if any of the specified dimensions is negative.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Array.newInstance(Integer.class, 5, 5);     // returns a 5x5 Integer array
    Array.newInstance(String.class, 3, 3, 3);   // returns a 3x3x3 String array
  ```
- **See also:** java.lang.reflect.Array#newInstance(Class, int...)
##### getLength(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `public static int getLength(final Object array) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Retrieves the length of the provided array.
- **Contract:**
  - If the array is `null`, this method returns 0.
- **Parameters:**
  - `array` (`Object`) — the array whose length is to be determined.
- **Returns:** the length of the array, or 0 if the array is `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the provided object is not an array.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String[] array = {"a", "b", "c"};
    int length = Array.getLength(array);   // returns 3
    int[] nums = {1, 2, 3, 4};
    int numLength = Array.getLength(nums);    // returns 4
    int nullLength = Array.getLength(null);   // returns 0
  ```

##### asList(...) -> List<T>
- **Signature:** `@SafeVarargs @NullSafe public static <T> List<T> asList(@NullSafe final T... a)`
- **Annotations:** @NullSafe
- **Summary:** Returns a fixed-size list backed by the specified array if it's not `null` or empty, otherwise an immutable/unmodifiable empty list is returned.
- **Contract:**
  - The returned list is: Fixed-size - cannot be resized (no add/remove operations) Backed by the original array when non-empty - changes to the list affect the array and vice versa An unmodifiable empty list if the input array is `null` or empty Usage Examples:
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`@NullSafe T[]`) — the array to be converted to a list. Can be `null` or empty.
- **Returns:** a fixed-size list backed by the specified array, or an empty list if the array is `null` or empty.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String[] array = {"a", "b", "c"};
    List<String> list = Array.asList(array);
    list.set(0, "x");   // array is {"x", "b", "c"}
  
    String[] emptyArray = {};
    List<String> emptyList = Array.asList(emptyArray);   // returns empty list
  
    String[] nullArray = null;
    List<String> nullList = Array.asList(nullArray);   // returns empty list
  ```
- **See also:** Arrays#asList(Object...), N#asList(Object...), N#asArray(Object...), List#of(Object...), N#toList(Object...), N#emptyList()

- **Signature:** `public static char[] range(char startInclusive, final char endExclusive)`
- **Summary:** Generates a range of characters from the start (inclusive) to the end (exclusive).
- **Contract:**
  - If the start is greater than or equal to the end, an empty array is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `startInclusive` (`char`) — the first character (inclusive) in the char array.
  - `endExclusive` (`char`) — the upper bound (exclusive) of the char array.
- **Returns:** a char array containing characters from startInclusive to endExclusive, or an empty array if startInclusive >= endExclusive.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  char[] chars = Array.range('a', 'e');    // returns {'a', 'b', 'c', 'd'}
    char[] digits = Array.range('0', '5');   // returns {'0', '1', '2', '3', '4'}
    char[] empty = Array.range('z', 'a');    // returns empty array
  ```

- **Signature:** `public static char[] range(char startInclusive, final char endExclusive, final int by) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Generates a range of characters from the start (inclusive) to the end (exclusive) with a specific step.

- **Signature:** `public static int[] rangeClosed(int startInclusive, final int endInclusive, final int by) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Generates a range of integers from the start (inclusive) to the end (inclusive) with a specific step.
- **Contract:**
  - The integers are generated in ascending order if by is positive, and in descending order if by is negative.
  - If the step direction is inconsistent with the range (e.g., positive step but end < start), an empty array is returned.
  - If start equals end, a single-element array containing that value is returned for any non-zero step.
- **Parameters:**
  - `startInclusive` (`int`) — the first integer (inclusive) in the integer array.
  - `endInclusive` (`int`) — the upper bound (inclusive) of the integer array.
  - `by` (`int`) — the step to increment (if positive) or decrement (if negative) for each subsequent integer.
- **Returns:** an integer array containing integers from startInclusive to endInclusive incremented or decremented by by, or an empty array if the range is empty or direction is inconsistent.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if by is zero or if the resulting array size exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE (overflow detected).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  int[] nums = Array.rangeClosed(0, 100, 10);     // returns {0, 10, 20, 30, ..., 90, 100}
    int[] reverse = Array.rangeClosed(50, 0, -5);   // returns {50, 45, 40, ..., 5, 0}
    int[] evens = Array.rangeClosed(0, 20, 2);      // returns {0, 2, 4, ..., 18, 20}
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static long[] rangeClosed(long startInclusive, final long endInclusive, final long by) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Generates a range of long integers from the start (inclusive) to the end (inclusive) with a specific step.
- **Contract:**
  - The long integers are generated in ascending order if by is positive, and in descending order if by is negative.
  - If the step direction is inconsistent with the range (e.g., positive step but end < start), an empty array is returned.
  - If start equals end, a single-element array containing that value is returned for any non-zero step.
- **Parameters:**
  - `startInclusive` (`long`) — the first long integer (inclusive) in the long array.
  - `endInclusive` (`long`) — the upper bound (inclusive) of the long array.
  - `by` (`long`) — the step to increment (if positive) or decrement (if negative) for each subsequent long integer.
- **Returns:** a long array containing long integers from startInclusive to endInclusive incremented or decremented by by, or an empty array if the range is empty or direction is inconsistent.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if by is zero or if the resulting array size exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE (overflow detected).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  long[] longs = Array.rangeClosed(0L, 1000L, 100L);                // returns {0, 100, 200, ..., 900, 1000}
    long[] reverse = Array.rangeClosed(5000L, 1000L, -500L);          // returns {5000, 4500, 4000, ..., 1500, 1000}
    long[] timestamps = Array.rangeClosed(0L, 86400000L, 3600000L);   // 25 hourly values from 0 to 86400000
  ```

- **Signature:** `public static <T> T[] repeat(final T element, final int n, final Class<? extends T> elementClass) throws IllegalArgumentException, ClassCastException, ArrayStoreException`
- **Summary:** Generates a new array of a specified length, with all elements set to the element value.
- **Parameters:**
  - `element` (`T`) — the value to be repeated in the array; may be `null`.
  - `n` (`int`) — the length of the array to be generated.
  - `elementClass` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the class of the elements in the array; this becomes the array's component type. Must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** an array of type 'T' and length n with all elements set to element.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `n` is negative, `elementClass` is `null` or Void#TYPE, or the resulting array length or dimension count exceeds the supported limit.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if `elementClass` is a primitive type other than `void`, producing an array that cannot be returned as an object array.
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if at least one value is copied and it is not assignable to the result array component type.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String[] words = Array.repeat("hello", 3, String.class);
    // Returns ["hello", "hello", "hello"]
  
    Integer[] numbers = Array.repeat(42, 5, Integer.class);
    // Returns [42, 42, 42, 42, 42]
  ```
- **See also:** #repeatNonNull(Object, int), N#repeat(Object, int)

##### repeatNonNull(...) -> T\[\]
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T[] repeatNonNull(final T element, final int n) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Generates a new array of a specified length, with all elements set to the element value.
- **Contract:**
  - Use Array#repeat(Object, int, Class) if the element may be `null`.
  - The array's component type is `element.getClass()`, not `T` — the returned array is only as wide as the element's runtime class, so storing a sibling subtype into it throws ArrayStoreException even though the static type `T\[\]` permits it: Use Array#repeat(Object, int, Class) and pass the intended component type when the result must accept other subtypes of `T`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `element` (`T`) — the value to be repeated in the array; must not be `null`
  - `n` (`int`) — the length of the array to be generated. Must be non-negative.
- **Returns:** an array of type 'T' and length n with all elements set to element.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if element is `null` or if n is negative.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Number[] a = Array.repeatNonNull((Number) Integer.valueOf(1), 3);   // runtime type is Integer[]
    a[0] = Double.valueOf(1.5);                                         // throws ArrayStoreException
  
    // An enum constant with a body is its own anonymous subclass, so this bites without any cast:
    enum E { A { public String toString() { return "A!"; } }, B }
    E[] es = Array.repeatNonNull(E.A, 2);   // runtime type is E$1[], not E[]
    es[0] = E.B;                            // throws ArrayStoreException
  ```
  ```java
  Integer[] integers = Array.repeatNonNull(42, 5);               // returns {42, 42, 42, 42, 42}
    String[] strings = Array.repeatNonNull("hello", 3);            // returns {"hello", "hello", "hello"}
    LocalDate[] dates = Array.repeatNonNull(LocalDate.now(), 4);   // returns 4 references to the same LocalDate
    // Array.repeatNonNull(null, 5);  // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
- **See also:** #repeat(Object, int, Class), N#repeat(Object, int)

  - `endExclusive` (`int`) — the upper bound (exclusive) of the random integers.

##### concat(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public static boolean[][] concat(final boolean[][] a, final boolean[][] b) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Concatenates two two-dimensional boolean arrays element-wise by combining their corresponding row elements.
- **Contract:**
  - For each row index: If both arrays have a row at that index, the rows are concatenated together If only one array has a row at that index, a copy of that row is used in the result If neither array has a row at that index (both are null), the result row is an empty array A `null` row inside either input is therefore treated as an empty row: the returned array never contains a `null` row, whatever the other argument is.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`boolean[][]`) — the first two-dimensional boolean array to concatenate. Can be `null` or empty, in which case the result is a row-wise copy of `b` (or an empty array if both are null/empty).
  - `b` (`boolean[][]`) — the second two-dimensional boolean array to concatenate. Can be `null` or empty, in which case the result is a row-wise copy of `a` (or an empty array if both are null/empty).
- **Returns:** a new two-dimensional boolean array containing the element-wise concatenation of the input arrays. The length equals max(a.length, b.length). Each row in the result is the concatenation of the corresponding rows from `a` and `b`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the combined length of a corresponding row pair exceeds `Integer.MAX_VALUE`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Example 1: Basic concatenation of two two-dimensional arrays
    boolean[][] a = {{true, false}, {true}};
    boolean[][] b = {{false}, {true, true}};
    boolean[][] result = Array.concat(a, b);
    // result = {{true, false, false}, {true, true, true}}
  
    // Example 2: Arrays with different lengths
    boolean[][] a = {{true, false}, {true}};
    boolean[][] b = {{false}};
    boolean[][] result = Array.concat(a, b);
    // result = {{true, false, false}, {true}}
  
    // Example 3: Concatenation with empty array
    boolean[][] a = {{true, false}};
    boolean[][] b = new boolean[0][];
    boolean[][] result = Array.concat(a, b);
    // result = {{true, false}} (a row-wise copy of a)
  
    // Example 4: Both arrays are null/empty
    boolean[][] result = Array.concat((boolean[][]) null, null);
    // result = new boolean[0][]
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static boolean[][][] concat(final boolean[][][] a, final boolean[][][] b) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Concatenates two three-dimensional boolean arrays element-wise by combining their corresponding two-dimensional layer elements.
- **Contract:**

- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`boolean[][][]`) — the first three-dimensional boolean array to concatenate. Can be `null` or empty, in which case the result is a layer-wise copy of `b` (or an empty array if both are null/empty).
  - `b` (`boolean[][][]`) — the second three-dimensional boolean array to concatenate. Can be `null` or empty, in which case the result is a layer-wise copy of `a` (or an empty array if both are null/empty).
- **Returns:** a new three-dimensional boolean array containing the element-wise concatenation of the input arrays. The length equals max(a.length, b.length). Each two-dimensional layer in the result is the concatenation of the corresponding layers from `a` and `b`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the combined length of a corresponding row pair (inside corresponding layers) exceeds `Integer.MAX_VALUE`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Example 1: Basic concatenation of two three-dimensional arrays
    boolean[][][] a = {{{true, false}}, {{true}}};
    boolean[][][] b = {{{false}}, {{true, true}}};
    boolean[][][] result = Array.concat(a, b);
    // result = {{{true, false, false}}, {{true, true, true}}}
  
    // Example 2: Arrays with different lengths
    boolean[][][] a = {{{true, false}}, {{true}}};
    boolean[][][] b = {{{false}}};
    boolean[][][] result = Array.concat(a, b);
    // result = {{{true, false, false}}, {{true}}}

  ```

- **Summary:** Concatenates two two-dimensional long arrays element-wise by combining their corresponding row elements.
- **Contract:**

  - `b` (`long[][]`) — the second two-dimensional long array to concatenate. Can be `null` or empty, in which case the result is a row-wise copy of `a` (or an empty array if both are null/empty).

##### concat2D(...) -> T\[\]\[\]
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull public static <T> T[][] concat2D(final T[][] a, final T[][] b) throws ArrayStoreException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Concatenates two two-dimensional arrays of generic type T element-wise by combining their corresponding row elements.
- **Contract:**
  - For each row index: If both arrays have a row at that index, the rows are concatenated together If only one array has a row at that index, a copy of that row is used in the result If neither array has a row at that index (both are null), the result row is `null` Deliberate divergence from the primitive overloads.
  - This method propagates `null` instead, consistently on every path, so that a result row is `null` exactly when both input rows are `null` - matching N#concat(Object\[\], Object\[\]), which returns `null` for two `null` rows, and matching the top-level rule that `concat2D(null, null)` is `null` rather than an empty array.
  - Result component type: the returned array's runtime component type is always `a`'s, whatever `a`'s length - it falls back to `b`'s only when `a` itself is `null`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`T[][]`) — the first two-dimensional array to concatenate. Can be `null` or empty, in which case the result is a row-wise copy of `b` (or, when `b` is `null` too, an empty array if `a` is non-`null` and `null` if it is not). Note that a non-`null` `a` still dictates the result's runtime component type even when it is empty.
  - `b` (`T[][]`) — the second two-dimensional array to concatenate. Can be `null` or empty, in which case the result is a row-wise copy of `a`.
- **Returns:** a new two-dimensional array containing the element-wise concatenation of the input arrays. The length equals max(a.length, b.length). Each row in the result is the concatenation of the corresponding rows from `a` and `b`. Returns `null` only when both `a` and `b` are `null`. (may return null)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if a copied element, row, or layer is incompatible with the runtime component type selected from the corresponding non-null input arrays.
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the combined length of a corresponding row pair exceeds `Integer.MAX_VALUE`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Example 1: Basic concatenation of two two-dimensional String arrays
    String[][] a = {{"a", "b"}, {"c"}};
    String[][] b = {{"d"}, {"e", "f"}};
    String[][] result = Array.concat2D(a, b);
    // result = {{"a", "b", "d"}, {"c", "e", "f"}}
  
    // Example 2: Arrays with different lengths
    Integer[][] a = {{1, 2}, {3}};
    Integer[][] b = {{4}};
    Integer[][] result = Array.concat2D(a, b);
    // result = {{1, 2, 4}, {3}}
  
    // Example 3: Concatenation with empty array
    String[][] a = {{"hello", "world"}};
    String[][] b = new String[0][];
    String[][] result = Array.concat2D(a, b);
    // result = {{"hello", "world"}} (a row-wise copy of a)
  
    // Example 4: Both arrays are null
    String[][] result = Array.concat2D(null, null);
    // result = null
  
    // Example 5: Non-null empty first array with null second array
    String[][] result = Array.concat2D(new String[0][], null);
    // result = String[0][] (non-null empty array)
  
    // Example 6: an empty first array still fixes the result's component type
    Number[][] nums = {{2.5}, {3}};
    Array.concat2D(new Integer[0][], nums);   // throws ArrayStoreException - a Number[] row cannot go into an Integer[][]
  ```
- **See also:** N#concat(Object\[\], Object\[\]), #concat3D(Object\[\]\[\]\[\], Object\[\]\[\]\[\])

- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull public static Boolean[] box(final boolean... a)`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Converts an array of primitive booleans to an array of Boolean objects.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`boolean[]`) — the array of primitive booleans to be converted. May be `null`.
- **Returns:** an array of Boolean objects, or `null` if the input array is `null`. (may return null)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  boolean[] primitives = {true, false, true};
    Boolean[] objects = Array.box(primitives);            // returns {Boolean.TRUE, Boolean.FALSE, Boolean.TRUE}
  ```

- **See also:** #box(boolean\[\], int, int)
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull public static Boolean[] box(final boolean[] a, final int fromIndex, final int toIndex) throws IndexOutOfBoundsException`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Converts a portion of an array of primitive booleans to an array of Boolean objects.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`boolean[]`) — the array of primitive booleans to be converted. May be `null`.
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the start index of the portion to be converted (inclusive).
  - `toIndex` (`int`) — the end index of the portion to be converted (exclusive).
- **Returns:** an array of Boolean objects representing the specified portion of the input array, `null` if the input array is `null`. (may return null)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `a` is non-`null` and fromIndex < 0, toIndex > a.length or fromIndex > toIndex. A `null` `a` returns `null` without any range validation, so no index is rejected in that case.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  boolean[] primitives = {true, false, true, false, true};
    Boolean[] objects = Array.box(primitives, 1, 4);   // returns {Boolean.FALSE, Boolean.TRUE, Boolean.FALSE}
    Boolean[] empty = Array.box(primitives, 2, 2);     // returns empty Boolean array
  ```
- **See also:** #box(boolean\[\])

- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Converts a portion of an array of primitive bytes to an array of Byte objects.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`byte[]`) — the array of primitive bytes to be converted. May be `null`.
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the start index of the portion to be converted (inclusive).
  - `toIndex` (`int`) — the end index of the portion to be converted (exclusive).
- **Returns:** an array of Byte objects representing the specified portion of the input array, `null` if the input array is `null`. (may return null)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `a` is non-`null` and fromIndex < 0, toIndex > a.length or fromIndex > toIndex. A `null` `a` returns `null` without any range validation, so no index is rejected in that case.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  byte[] primitives = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    Byte[] objects = Array.box(primitives, 1, 4);   // returns {Byte.valueOf((byte) 2), Byte.valueOf((byte) 3), Byte.valueOf((byte) 4)}
    Byte[] empty = Array.box(primitives, 2, 2);     // returns empty Byte array
  ```

##### unbox(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull public static boolean[] unbox(final Boolean... a)`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Converts an array of Boolean objects into an array of primitive booleans.
- **Contract:**
  - If a `null` value is encountered in the input array, it is replaced with the default value `false`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`Boolean[]`) — the array of Boolean objects to be converted. May be `null`.
- **Returns:** an array of primitive booleans, or `null` if the input array is `null`. (may return null)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Boolean[] objects = {Boolean.TRUE, null, Boolean.FALSE};
    boolean[] primitives = Array.unbox(objects);            // returns {true, false, false}
    boolean[] nullResult = Array.unbox((Boolean[]) null);   // returns null
  ```
- **See also:** #unbox(Boolean\[\], boolean), #unbox(Boolean\[\], int, int, boolean)
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull public static boolean[] unbox(final Boolean[] a, final boolean valueForNull)`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Converts an array of Boolean objects into an array of primitive booleans.
- **Contract:**
  - If a `null` value is encountered in the input array, it is replaced with the specified default value.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`Boolean[]`) — the array of Boolean objects to be converted. May be `null`.
  - `valueForNull` (`boolean`) — the value to be used for `null` values in the input array.
- **Returns:** an array of primitive booleans, or `null` if the input array is `null`. (may return null)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Boolean[] objects = {true, null, false};
    boolean[] primitives = Array.unbox(objects, true);   // returns {true, true, false}
    boolean[] withFalse = Array.unbox(objects, false);   // returns {true, false, false}
  ```

- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull @Beta public static boolean[][] transpose(final boolean[][] a) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull, @Beta
- **Summary:** Transposes the input two-dimensional array.
- **Contract:**
  - If the input is a matrix of size m x n, then the output will be another matrix of size n x m.
  - This method will return `null` if the input array is `null`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`boolean[][]`) — the two-dimensional array to be transposed. May be `null`.
- **Returns:** the transposed two-dimensional array, or `null` if the input array is `null`. (may return null)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the input array is not a valid matrix (i.e. contains a `null` sub-array or sub-arrays of differing lengths).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  boolean[][] matrix = {
        {true, false, true},
        {false, true, false}
    };
    boolean[][] transposed = Array.transpose(matrix);
    // Result: {{true, false}, {false, true}, {true, false}}
    // Original matrix is 2x3, transposed is 3x2
  ```

### Class AsyncExecutor (com.landawn.abacus.util.AsyncExecutor)
Provides a convenient way to execute tasks asynchronously using a configurable thread pool.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- `public AsyncExecutor()` — Constructs an AsyncExecutor with default configuration.
  ```java
  AsyncExecutor executor = new AsyncExecutor();
    executor.execute(() -> System.out.println("Hello from async task"));
  ```
- `public AsyncExecutor(final int coreThreadPoolSize, final int maxThreadPoolSize, final long keepAliveTime, final TimeUnit unit) throws IllegalArgumentException` — Constructs an AsyncExecutor with specified thread pool configuration.
  - **Throws:**
    - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `coreThreadPoolSize` is negative, if `maxThreadPoolSize` is negative, if `coreThreadPoolSize` and `maxThreadPoolSize` are both zero, if `keepAliveTime` is negative, or if `unit` is `null`.
  ```java
  // Create executor with 10 core threads, 20 max threads, 60 second keep-alive
    AsyncExecutor executor = new AsyncExecutor(10, 20, 60L, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
  ```
- `public AsyncExecutor(final Executor executor) throws IllegalArgumentException` — Constructs an AsyncExecutor that wraps an existing Executor.
  - **Throws:**
    - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `executor` is `null`.
  ```java
  ExecutorService customExecutor = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(5);
    try {
        AsyncExecutor asyncExecutor = new AsyncExecutor(customExecutor);
        asyncExecutor.execute(() -> processData()).get();
    } finally {
        // AsyncExecutor does not own an externally supplied executor.
        customExecutor.shutdown();
    }
  ```
