  ```java
  User user = new User("John", 25);
    user.setActive(true);
  
    Beans.beanToMap(user);   // returns {name=John, age=25, active=true}
  
    user.setActive(null);
    Beans.beanToMap(user);            // returns {name=John, age=25} (null "active" omitted)
  
    Beans.beanToMap((Object) null);   // returns {} (empty map)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <M extends Map<String, Object>> M beanToMap(final Object bean, final IntFunction<? extends M> mapSupplier) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts a bean object into a map using the provided map supplier.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object to be converted into a map; if `null`, an empty map is returned.
  - `mapSupplier` (`IntFunction<? extends M>`) — a function that creates a new Map instance given an initial capacity.
- **Returns:** a map of the specified type containing the non-`null` property name-value pairs of the bean; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapSupplier` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User user = new User("John", 25);
    // Using TreeMap to get keys sorted
    // sortedMap: {age=25, name=John} (sorted by key; null "active" omitted)
    TreeMap<String, Object> sortedMap = Beans.beanToMap(user, IntFunctions.<String, Object> ofTreeMap());
  
    Beans.beanToMap((Object) null, IntFunctions.<String, Object> ofMap());   // returns {} (empty map)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static Map<String, Object> beanToMap(final Object bean, final Collection<String> selectPropNames) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts a bean object into a map, selecting only the properties specified in the provided collection.
- **Contract:**
  - If `selectPropNames` is `null`, all non-`null` properties are included.
  - If it is empty, no properties are included.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object to be converted into a map; if `null`, an empty map is returned.
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — a collection of property names to be included in the map. If `null`, all non-`null` properties are included. If empty, no properties are included. Selected properties are included even when their values are `null`.
- **Returns:** a java.util.LinkedHashMap with the selected (or all non-`null`) property name-value pairs; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a selected property does not exist in the bean class.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User user = new User("John", 25);
    user.setActive(true);
  
    // Only include "name" and "age"
    Beans.beanToMap(user, Arrays.asList("name", "age"));   // returns {name=John, age=25}
  
    Beans.beanToMap(user, (Collection<String>) null);      // returns all non-null props
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <M extends Map<String, Object>> M beanToMap(final Object bean, final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final IntFunction<? extends M> mapSupplier) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts a bean object into a map, selecting only the properties specified in the provided collection.
- **Contract:**
  - If `selectPropNames` is `null`, all non-`null` properties are included.
  - If it is empty, no properties are included.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object to be converted into a map; if `null`, an empty map is returned.
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — a collection of property names to be included in the map. If `null`, all non-`null` properties are included. If empty, no properties are included. Selected properties are included even when their values are `null`.
  - `mapSupplier` (`IntFunction<? extends M>`) — a function that creates a new Map instance given an initial capacity.
- **Returns:** a map of the specified type with the selected (or all non-`null`) property name-value pairs; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a selected property does not exist in the bean class, or if `mapSupplier` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User user = new User("John", 25);
    user.setActive(true);
  
    // Only include "name" and "age", using a TreeMap
    TreeMap<String, Object> sortedMap = Beans.beanToMap(user, Arrays.asList("name", "age"), IntFunctions.<String, Object> ofTreeMap());
    // sortedMap: {age=25, name=John} (sorted by key)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <M extends Map<String, Object>> M beanToMap(final Object bean, final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final NamingPolicy keyNamingPolicy, final IntFunction<? extends M> mapSupplier) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts a bean object into a map, selecting only the properties specified.
- **Contract:**
  - If `selectPropNames` is `null`, all non-`null` properties are included.
  - If it is empty, no properties are included.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object to be converted into a map; if `null`, an empty map is returned.
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the property names to include. If `null`, all non-`null` properties are included. If empty, no properties are included. Selected properties are included even when their values are `null`. A name may be any spelling the property resolver accepts (case-insensitive, underscore-stripped, or `get`/`is`/ `has`-prefixed); the emitted key is always the bean's own property name with `keyNamingPolicy` applied, so two spellings of one property yield one entry.
  - `keyNamingPolicy` (`NamingPolicy`) — the naming policy applied to map keys; if `null`, defaults to NamingPolicy#CAMEL_CASE. NamingPolicy#CAMEL_CASE and NamingPolicy#NO_CHANGE both emit the bean's property names unchanged — see the class documentation.
  - `mapSupplier` (`IntFunction<? extends M>`) — a function that creates a new Map instance given an initial capacity.
- **Returns:** a map of the specified type with property name-value pairs; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a selected property does not exist in the bean class, or if `mapSupplier` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  class User {
        private String firstName;
        private String lastName;
        public String getFirstName() { return firstName; }
        public void setFirstName(String firstName) { this.firstName = firstName; }
        public String getLastName() { return lastName; }
        public void setLastName(String lastName) { this.lastName = lastName; }
    }
    User user = new User();
    user.setFirstName("John");
    user.setLastName("Doe");
    Collection<String> props = Arrays.asList("firstName", "lastName");
  
    Beans.beanToMap(user, props, NamingPolicy.SNAKE_CASE, IntFunctions.<String, Object> ofLinkedHashMap());
    // returns {first_name=John, last_name=Doe}
  
    Beans.beanToMap(user, props, NamingPolicy.SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, IntFunctions.<String, Object> ofLinkedHashMap());
    // returns {FIRST_NAME=John, LAST_NAME=Doe}
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static void beanToMap(final Object bean, final Map<String, Object> output) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts a bean object into the provided output map.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object to be converted into a map; if `null`, the output map is not modified.
  - `output` (`Map<String, Object>`) — the map into which the bean's non-`null` properties will be put. Existing entries are preserved unless overwritten by a generated key. Must not be `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `output` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java

    user.setActive(true);
  
    Map<String, Object> existingMap = new HashMap<>();
    existingMap.put("id", 123);
  
    // existingMap now also contains name=John, age=25, active=true (id=123 preserved)
    Beans.beanToMap(user, existingMap);
  
    Beans.beanToMap(null, existingMap);   // existingMap is unchanged
  ```

- **Signature:** `public static Map<String, Object> deepBeanToMap(final Object bean) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts the provided bean into a Map where the keys are the property names of the bean and the values are the corresponding property values.
- **Contract:**
  - For example, a bidirectional `parent <-> child` pair throws IllegalArgumentException when both properties are traversed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean to be converted into a Map; if `null`, an empty map is returned.
- **Returns:** a java.util.LinkedHashMap representation of the provided bean; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the traversed bean graph contains a reference cycle.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Example with nested beans
    User user = new User();
    user.setName("John");
    Address address = new Address();
    address.setCity("New York");
    address.setZipCode("10001");
    user.setAddress(address);
  
    Map<String, Object> deepMap = Beans.deepBeanToMap(user);
    // deepMap: {
    //   name=John,
    //   address={city=New York, zipCode=10001}
    // }
    // Note: address is converted to a Map, not kept as Address object
  ```

- **Summary:** Converts the provided bean into a Map where the keys are the property names of the bean and the values are the corresponding property values.

- **Signature:** `public static Map<String, Object> deepBeanToMap(final Object bean, final Collection<String> selectPropNames) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts the provided bean into a Map where the keys are the property names of the bean and the values are the corresponding property values.
- **Contract:**
  - If `selectPropNames` is `null`, all non-`null` properties are included.
  - If it is empty, no properties are included.
  - For example, a bidirectional `parent <-> child` pair throws IllegalArgumentException when both properties are traversed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean to be converted into a Map; if `null`, an empty map is returned.
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — a collection of property names to be included during the conversion process. If `null`, all non-`null` properties are included. If empty, no properties are included. In selection mode, selected top-level properties are included even when `null`, while `null` properties inside nested beans are always omitted. A selected nested bean whose every property is `null` therefore comes back as an empty nested map rather than being dropped; the `beanToFlatMap` twin, which cannot represent an empty nested object in a flat key space, drops it instead. Use Beans#mapBuilder(Object), whose null policy applies at every level, when the nested `null`s must survive.
- **Returns:** a java.util.LinkedHashMap representation of the provided bean; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a selected property does not exist, or if the traversed bean graph contains a reference cycle.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Example with selected properties
    User user = new User();
    user.setName("John");
    user.setAge(25);
    Address address = new Address();
    address.setCity("New York");
    user.setAddress(address);
  
    Collection<String> props = Arrays.asList("name", "address");
    Map<String, Object> selectedDeepMap = Beans.deepBeanToMap(user, props);
    // selectedDeepMap: {
    //   name=John,
    //   address={city=New York}
    // }
    // age is not included
  ```
- **See also:** #deepBeanToMap(Object, Collection, NamingPolicy, IntFunction)

- **Signature:** `public static Map<String, Object> deepBeanToMap(final Object bean, final boolean ignoreNullProperty, final Set<String> ignoredPropNames) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts the provided bean into a Map where the keys are the property names of the bean and the values are the corresponding property values.
- **Contract:**
  - For example, a bidirectional `parent <-> child` pair throws IllegalArgumentException when both properties are traversed.
- **Parameters:**

  ```java

    Set<String> ignored = new HashSet<>(Arrays.asList("email", "age"));
  ```

- **Signature:** `public static <M extends Map<String, Object>> M deepBeanToMap(final Object bean, final boolean ignoreNullProperty, final Set<String> ignoredPropNames, final IntFunction<? extends M> mapSupplier) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts the provided bean into a Map where the keys are the property names of the bean and the values are the corresponding property values.
- **Contract:**
  - For example, a bidirectional `parent <-> child` pair throws IllegalArgumentException when both properties are traversed.
- **Parameters:**

- **Signature:** `public static Map<String, Object> deepBeanToMap(final Object bean, final boolean ignoreNullProperty, final Set<String> ignoredPropNames, final NamingPolicy keyNamingPolicy) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts the provided bean into a Map where the keys are the property names of the bean and the values are the corresponding property values.
- **Contract:**
  - For example, a bidirectional `parent <-> child` pair throws IllegalArgumentException when both properties are traversed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object to be converted into a Map; if `null`, an empty map is returned.
  - `ignoreNullProperty` (`boolean`) — if `true`, properties with `null` values will not be included in the resulting Map.
  - `ignoredPropNames` (`Set<String>`) — a set of property names to be ignored during the conversion process. Applies to TOP-LEVEL property names only; properties inside nested beans are not matched.
  - `keyNamingPolicy` (`NamingPolicy`) — the naming policy applied to map keys; if `null`, defaults to NamingPolicy#CAMEL_CASE. NamingPolicy#CAMEL_CASE and NamingPolicy#NO_CHANGE both emit the bean's property names unchanged — see the class documentation.
- **Returns:** a java.util.LinkedHashMap representation of the bean with keys transformed according to the naming policy; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the traversed bean graph contains a reference cycle.
- **Examples:**
  ```java

    user.setFirstName("John");
    user.setLastName("Doe");
  
    Map<String, Object> snakeCase = Beans.deepBeanToMap(user, false, null,
        NamingPolicy.SNAKE_CASE);
    // snakeCase: {first_name=John, last_name=Doe}
  
    Map<String, Object> upperCase = Beans.deepBeanToMap(user, false, null,
        NamingPolicy.SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE);
    // upperCase: {FIRST_NAME=John, LAST_NAME=Doe}
  ```

  - For example, a bidirectional `parent <-> child` pair throws IllegalArgumentException when both properties are traversed.

- **Summary:** Converts a bean object into a flat map representation where nested properties are represented with dot notation.
- **Contract:**
  - For example, a bidirectional `parent <-> child` pair throws IllegalArgumentException when both properties are traversed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object to be converted into a flat map; if `null`, an empty map is returned.

  ```java

    // Deep nesting
    Company company = new Company("TechCorp",
        new Address("NYC", new Location(40.7128, -74.0060)));
    Map<String, Object> result = Beans.beanToFlatMap(company);
    // result: {name=TechCorp, address.city=NYC,
    //          address.location.latitude=40.7128,
    //          address.location.longitude=-74.0060}
  ```

- **Signature:** `public static Map<String, Object> beanToFlatMap(final Object bean, final Collection<String> selectPropNames) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts a bean object into a flat map representation with only selected properties.
- **Contract:**
  - If `selectPropNames` is `null`, all non-`null` properties are included.
  - If it is empty, no properties are included.
  - For example, a bidirectional `parent <-> child` pair throws IllegalArgumentException when both properties are traversed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object to be converted into a flat map; if `null`, an empty map is returned.
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — a collection of property names to be included in the resulting map. Nested properties of selected beans are automatically included. If `null`, all non-`null` properties are included. If empty, no properties are included. In selection mode, selected top-level properties are included even when `null`, while `null` properties inside nested beans are always omitted. A selected nested bean can therefore contribute no key at all: a flat map has no way to represent an empty nested object, so a nested bean whose every property is `null` simply disappears. Given a `User` whose `address` is non-`null` but whose `address.city` is `null`, `beanToFlatMap(user, \["address"\])` returns `{}` - while the deep twin `deepBeanToMap(user, \["address"\])` returns `{address={}}`. Use Beans#mapBuilder(Object), whose null policy applies at every level, when a selected property must always appear: `mapBuilder(user).flat().select("address").toMap()` yields `{address.city=null}`.
- **Returns:** a map with only the selected properties flattened; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a selected property does not exist, or if the traversed bean graph contains a reference cycle.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Select specific properties including nested ones
    User user = new User("John", 25, new Address("NYC", "10001"));
    Collection<String> select = Arrays.asList("name", "address");
    // result: {name=John, address.city=NYC, address.zipCode=10001}
    Map<String, Object> result = Beans.beanToFlatMap(user, select);
  
    // Select only top-level properties
    Collection<String> topLevel = Arrays.asList("name", "age");
    Map<String, Object> flat = Beans.beanToFlatMap(user, topLevel);
    // flat: {name=John, age=25} (address excluded)
  ```
