If empty, no properties are included. In selection mode, selected top-level properties are included even when `null`, while `null` properties inside nested beans are always omitted. A selected nested bean can therefore contribute no key at all: a flat map has no way to represent an empty nested object, so a nested bean whose every property is `null` simply disappears. Given a `User` whose `address` is non-`null` but whose `address.city` is `null`, `beanToFlatMap(user, \["address"\])` returns `{}` - while the deep twin `deepBeanToMap(user, \["address"\])` returns `{address={}}`. Use Beans#mapBuilder(Object), whose null policy applies at every level, when a selected property must always appear: `mapBuilder(user).flat().select("address").toMap()` yields `{address.city=null}`.
  - `keyNamingPolicy` (`NamingPolicy`) — the naming policy applied to map keys; if `null`, defaults to NamingPolicy#CAMEL_CASE. NamingPolicy#CAMEL_CASE and NamingPolicy#NO_CHANGE both emit the bean's property names unchanged — see the class documentation.
  - `output` (`Map<String, Object>`) — the Map instance into which the flattened bean properties will be put. Must not be `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `output` is `null`, or if a selected property does not exist, or if the traversed bean graph contains a reference cycle.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Full customization of flattening process
    Map<String, Object> output = new TreeMap<>();
    Collection<String> select = Arrays.asList("productName", "category");
  
    Product product = new Product("WidgetPro",
        new Category("Electronics", "Gadgets"));
    Beans.beanToFlatMap(product, select, NamingPolicy.SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, output);
    // output: {CATEGORY.NAME=Electronics, CATEGORY.SUBCATEGORY=Gadgets,
    //          PRODUCT_NAME=WidgetPro} (sorted, uppercase)
  ```
- **See also:** #beanToFlatMap(Object, Collection, NamingPolicy, IntFunction)
- **Signature:** `public static Map<String, Object> beanToFlatMap(final Object bean, final boolean ignoreNullProperty) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts a bean object into a flat map representation with control over `null` property handling.
- **Contract:**
  - For example, a bidirectional `parent <-> child` pair throws IllegalArgumentException when both properties are traversed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object to be converted into a flat map; if `null`, an empty map is returned.
  - `ignoreNullProperty` (`boolean`) — if `true`, properties with `null` values will not be included in the resulting map.
- **Returns:** a flat map representation of the bean with `null` handling as specified; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the traversed bean graph contains a reference cycle.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Include null properties
    User user = new User("John", (Integer) null, new Address("NYC", (String) null));
    // withNulls: {name=John, age=null, address.city=NYC, address.zipCode=null}
    Map<String, Object> withNulls = Beans.beanToFlatMap(user, false);
  
    // Exclude null properties
    Map<String, Object> noNulls = Beans.beanToFlatMap(user, true);
    // noNulls: {name=John, address.city=NYC}
  ```
- **See also:** #beanToFlatMap(Object, Collection, NamingPolicy, IntFunction)
- **Signature:** `public static Map<String, Object> beanToFlatMap(final Object bean, final boolean ignoreNullProperty, final Set<String> ignoredPropNames) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts a bean object into a flat map representation with control over `null` property handling and property exclusion.
- **Contract:**
  - For example, a bidirectional `parent <-> child` pair throws IllegalArgumentException when both properties are traversed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object to be converted into a flat map; if `null`, an empty map is returned.
  - `ignoreNullProperty` (`boolean`) — if `true`, properties with `null` values will not be included in the resulting map.
  - `ignoredPropNames` (`Set<String>`) — a set of property names to be excluded from the resulting map. Applies to TOP-LEVEL property names only; properties inside nested beans are not matched (dotted names such as `"address.city"` are not supported).
- **Returns:** a flat map with the specified filtering applied; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the traversed bean graph contains a reference cycle.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Filter nulls and exclude specific properties
    User user = new User("John", (Integer) null, "secret123", new Address("NYC"));
    Set<String> ignored = new HashSet<>(Arrays.asList("password"));
  
    Map<String, Object> result = Beans.beanToFlatMap(user, true, ignored);
    // result: {name=John, address.city=NYC}
    // (age is null, password is in ignored set)
  ```
- **See also:** #beanToFlatMap(Object, Collection, NamingPolicy, IntFunction)
- **Signature:** `public static <M extends Map<String, Object>> M beanToFlatMap(final Object bean, final boolean ignoreNullProperty, final Set<String> ignoredPropNames, final IntFunction<? extends M> mapSupplier) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts a bean object into a flat map representation with control over `null` handling, property exclusion, and Map type.
- **Contract:**
  - For example, a bidirectional `parent <-> child` pair throws IllegalArgumentException when both properties are traversed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object to be converted into a flat map; if `null`, an empty map is returned.
  - `ignoreNullProperty` (`boolean`) — if `true`, properties with `null` values will not be included in the resulting map.
  - `ignoredPropNames` (`Set<String>`) — a set of property names to be excluded from the resulting map. Applies to TOP-LEVEL property names only; properties inside nested beans are not matched (dotted names such as `"address.city"` are not supported).
  - `mapSupplier` (`IntFunction<? extends M>`) — a function that creates a new Map instance. The function argument is the initial capacity.
- **Returns:** a map of the specified type with filtering applied; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapSupplier` is `null`, or if the traversed bean graph contains a reference cycle.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Custom map with filtering
    Employee emp = new Employee("John", null, "IT", new Office("Building A"));
    Set<String> ignored = new HashSet<>(Arrays.asList("department"));
  
    TreeMap<String, Object> result = Beans.beanToFlatMap(emp, true, ignored,
        size -> new TreeMap<>());
    // result: {name=John, office.building=Building A}
    // (sorted, salary null excluded, department ignored)
  ```
- **See also:** #beanToFlatMap(Object, Collection, NamingPolicy, IntFunction)
- **Signature:** `public static Map<String, Object> beanToFlatMap(final Object bean, final boolean ignoreNullProperty, final Set<String> ignoredPropNames, final NamingPolicy keyNamingPolicy) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts a bean object into a flat map representation with control over `null` handling, property exclusion, and key naming policy.
- **Contract:**
  - For example, a bidirectional `parent <-> child` pair throws IllegalArgumentException when both properties are traversed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object to be converted into a flat map; if `null`, an empty map is returned.
  - `ignoreNullProperty` (`boolean`) — if `true`, properties with `null` values will not be included in the resulting map.
  - `ignoredPropNames` (`Set<String>`) — a set of property names to be excluded from the resulting map. Applies to TOP-LEVEL property names only; properties inside nested beans are not matched (dotted names such as `"address.city"` are not supported).
  - `keyNamingPolicy` (`NamingPolicy`) — the naming policy applied to map keys; if `null`, defaults to NamingPolicy#CAMEL_CASE. NamingPolicy#CAMEL_CASE and NamingPolicy#NO_CHANGE both emit the bean's property names unchanged — see the class documentation.
- **Returns:** a flat map with comprehensive customization applied; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the traversed bean graph contains a reference cycle.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Transform to snake_case with filtering
    UserProfile profile = new UserProfile();
    profile.setFirstName("John");
    profile.setLastLogin(null);
    profile.setHomeAddress(new Address("NYC"));
  
    Set<String> ignored = new HashSet<>(Arrays.asList("internalId"));
    Map<String, Object> result = Beans.beanToFlatMap(profile, true, ignored,
        NamingPolicy.SNAKE_CASE);
    // result: {first_name=John, home_address.city=NYC}
    // (last_login null excluded, internal_id ignored, snake_case keys)
  ```
- **See also:** #beanToFlatMap(Object, Collection, NamingPolicy, IntFunction)
- **Signature:** `public static <M extends Map<String, Object>> M beanToFlatMap(final Object bean, final boolean ignoreNullProperty, final Set<String> ignoredPropNames, final NamingPolicy keyNamingPolicy, final IntFunction<? extends M> mapSupplier) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts a bean object into a flat map representation with full control over all conversion aspects.
- **Contract:**
  - For example, a bidirectional `parent <-> child` pair throws IllegalArgumentException when both properties are traversed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object to be converted into a flat map; if `null`, an empty map is returned.
  - `ignoreNullProperty` (`boolean`) — if `true`, properties with `null` values will not be included in the resulting map.
  - `ignoredPropNames` (`Set<String>`) — a set of property names to be excluded from the resulting map. Applies to TOP-LEVEL property names only; properties inside nested beans are not matched (dotted names such as `"address.city"` are not supported).
  - `keyNamingPolicy` (`NamingPolicy`) — the naming policy applied to map keys; if `null`, defaults to NamingPolicy#CAMEL_CASE. NamingPolicy#CAMEL_CASE and NamingPolicy#NO_CHANGE both emit the bean's property names unchanged — see the class documentation.
  - `mapSupplier` (`IntFunction<? extends M>`) — a function that creates a new Map instance. The function argument is the initial capacity.
- **Returns:** a fully customized flat map representation of the bean; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapSupplier` is `null`, or if the traversed bean graph contains a reference cycle.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Complete customization example
    Order order = new Order("ORD-123", null,
        new Customer("John", new Address("NYC", "10001")));
    Set<String> ignored = new HashSet<>(Arrays.asList("internalNotes"));
  
    LinkedHashMap<String, Object> result = Beans.beanToFlatMap(order, true, ignored,
        NamingPolicy.SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE,
        size -> new LinkedHashMap<>(size * 2));
    // result: {ORDER_ID=ORD-123, CUSTOMER.NAME=John,
    //          CUSTOMER.ADDRESS.CITY=NYC, CUSTOMER.ADDRESS.ZIP_CODE=10001}
    // (amount null excluded, internal_notes ignored, ordered map)
  ```
- **See also:** #beanToFlatMap(Object, Collection, NamingPolicy, IntFunction)
- **Signature:** `public static void beanToFlatMap(final Object bean, final boolean ignoreNullProperty, final Map<String, Object> output) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts a bean object into a flat map representation and stores the result in the provided Map instance with `null` handling.
- **Contract:**
  - For example, a bidirectional `parent <-> child` pair throws IllegalArgumentException when both properties are traversed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object to be converted into a flat map; if `null`, the output map is not modified.
  - `ignoreNullProperty` (`boolean`) — if `true`, properties with `null` values will not be included in the output map.
  - `output` (`Map<String, Object>`) — the map into which the flattened bean properties will be put. Must not be `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `output` is `null`, or if the traversed bean graph contains a reference cycle.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Populate existing map with null filtering
    Map<String, Object> output = new HashMap<>();
    output.put("timestamp", new Date());
  
    User user = new User("John", (Integer) null, new Address("NYC"));
    Beans.beanToFlatMap(user, true, output);
    // output: {timestamp=..., name=John, address.city=NYC}
    // (age null is excluded)
  ```
- **See also:** #beanToFlatMap(Object, Collection, NamingPolicy, IntFunction)
- **Signature:** `public static void beanToFlatMap(final Object bean, final boolean ignoreNullProperty, final Set<String> ignoredPropNames, final Map<String, Object> output) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts a bean object into a flat map representation and stores the result in the provided Map instance with filtering options.
- **Contract:**
  - For example, a bidirectional `parent <-> child` pair throws IllegalArgumentException when both properties are traversed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object to be converted into a flat map; if `null`, the output map is not modified.
  - `ignoreNullProperty` (`boolean`) — if `true`, properties with `null` values will not be included in the output map.
  - `ignoredPropNames` (`Set<String>`) — a set of property names to be excluded from the output map. Applies to TOP-LEVEL property names only; properties inside nested beans are not matched (dotted names such as `"address.city"` are not supported).
  - `output` (`Map<String, Object>`) — the map into which the flattened bean properties will be put. Must not be `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `output` is `null`, or if the traversed bean graph contains a reference cycle.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // In-place population with multiple filters
    Map<String, Object> output = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    Set<String> ignored = new HashSet<>(Arrays.asList("password", "ssn"));
  
    Account account = new Account("john123", "pass", null, "123-45-6789");
    Beans.beanToFlatMap(account, true, ignored, output);
    // output: {username=john123}
    // (password and ssn ignored, balance null excluded)
  ```
- **See also:** #beanToFlatMap(Object, Collection, NamingPolicy, IntFunction)
- **Signature:** `public static void beanToFlatMap(final Object bean, final boolean ignoreNullProperty, final Set<String> ignoredPropNames, final NamingPolicy keyNamingPolicy, final Map<String, Object> output) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts a bean object into a flat map representation and stores the result in the provided Map instance with full customization.
- **Contract:**
  - For example, a bidirectional `parent <-> child` pair throws IllegalArgumentException when both properties are traversed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object to be converted into a flat map; if `null`, the output map is not modified.
  - `ignoreNullProperty` (`boolean`) — if `true`, properties with `null` values will not be included in the output map.
  - `ignoredPropNames` (`Set<String>`) — a set of property names to be excluded from the output map. Applies to TOP-LEVEL property names only; properties inside nested beans are not matched (dotted names such as `"address.city"` are not supported).
  - `keyNamingPolicy` (`NamingPolicy`) — the naming policy applied to map keys; if `null`, defaults to NamingPolicy#CAMEL_CASE. NamingPolicy#CAMEL_CASE and NamingPolicy#NO_CHANGE both emit the bean's property names unchanged — see the class documentation.
  - `output` (`Map<String, Object>`) — the map into which the flattened bean properties will be put. Must not be `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `output` is `null`, or if the traversed bean graph contains a reference cycle.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Full control in-place flattening
    Map<String, Object> output = new TreeMap<>();
    Set<String> ignored = new HashSet<>(Arrays.asList("metadata"));
  
    Document doc = new Document("Report", null,
        new Author("John", new Department("Research")));
    Beans.beanToFlatMap(doc, true, ignored,
        NamingPolicy.SNAKE_CASE, output);
    // output: {author.department.name=Research, author.name=John, title=Report}
    // (sorted keys, snake_case, version null excluded, metadata ignored)
  ```
- **See also:** #beanToFlatMap(Object, Collection, NamingPolicy, IntFunction)
##### mapBuilder(...) -> BeanMapBuilder
- **Signature:** `public static BeanMapBuilder mapBuilder(final Object bean)`
- **Summary:** Creates a fluent builder for converting the given bean into a Map, capping the large family of `beanToMap` / `deepBeanToMap` / `beanToFlatMap` overloads with a single configurable entry point.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean to convert; if `null`, the terminal methods produce an empty map.
- **Returns:** a new BeanMapBuilder for `bean`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Object> m = Beans.mapBuilder(user)
            .exclude("password")
            .skipNulls()
            .naming(NamingPolicy.SNAKE_CASE)
            .deep()
            .toMap();
  
    // Filter by name/value (no overload ambiguity: filter is a builder method, not an overload)
    Map<String, Object> strings = Beans.mapBuilder(user)
            .filter((name, value) -> value instanceof String)
            .toMap();
  ```
- **See also:** BeanMapBuilder
##### newBean(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T newBean(final Class<T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new instance of the specified bean class.
- **Contract:**
  - The class must have an accessible no-argument constructor.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetType` (`Class<T>`) — the class to instantiate; must not be `null` and must have an accessible no-argument constructor.
- **Returns:** a new instance of the specified class; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetType` is `null`, or the class cannot be instantiated (e.g., abstract, no accessible no-arg constructor).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // user.getName() returns null; user.getAge() returns 0
    User user = Beans.newBean(User.class);   // returns a new User instance
  ```
##### deepCopy(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull @SuppressWarnings("unchecked") public static <T> T deepCopy(final T obj) throws RuntimeException`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Creates a deep clone of the given object using Kryo copying or an XML round trip.
- **Contract:**
  - This method first attempts Kryo's object-copy operation when available, then falls back to serializing and deserializing XML.
  - The object must support Kryo copying or XML serialization.
  - If the Kryo copy throws a RuntimeException, the method falls back to XML serialization.
  - Kryo is used only for a same-class copy when Kryo is on the classpath, and that path preserves cycles and shared identity.
- **Parameters:**
  - `obj` (`T`) — the object to clone; must support Kryo copying or Abacus XML serialization.
- **Returns:** a deep clone of the object, or `null` if `obj` is `null`. (may return null)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the object cannot be copied by either mechanism. Kryo failures are absorbed (the XML round trip is tried next), but a failure of the XML round trip itself propagates as whatever the parser raises - typically a `ParseException`, or an Error such as `NoClassDefFoundError` when the XML binding API is absent.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User original = new User("John", 25);
  
    User clone = Beans.deepCopy(original);
  
    // clone != original but clone.getName().equals("John")
    // original.getName() is still "John"
    clone.setName("Jane");
  
    Beans.deepCopy(null);   // returns null
  ```
- **See also:** #deepCopyAs(Object, Class)
##### deepCopyAs(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("unchecked") public static <T> T deepCopyAs(final Object obj, @NotNull final Class<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Creates a deep clone of the given object and converts it to the specified target type.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful for creating type-converted copies or for ensuring type safety when cloning objects.
  - If the source object is `null`, the method creates a new instance of the target type by calling #copyAs(Object, Class) for bean targets or N#newInstance(Class) for non-bean targets (which requires an accessible no-arg constructor).
- **Parameters:**
  - `obj` (`Object`) — the source object; if `null`, a new empty instance of `targetType` is returned.
  - `targetType` (`@NotNull Class<? extends T>`) — the class of the target type to create; must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a new instance of the target type populated from the source object; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetType` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the object cannot be copied by either mechanism - see #deepCopy(Object). A Kryo failure is absorbed and remembered per class so it is not retried; an Error raised by Kryo is not absorbed, because an `OutOfMemoryError` or `StackOverflowError` says nothing about the class and must reach the caller.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User user = new User("John", 25);
    User copy = Beans.deepCopyAs(user, User.class);   // returns a populated User copy
  
    // Null source produces a new empty (non-null) instance
    User empty = Beans.deepCopyAs(null, User.class);   // returns a new empty User
  
    Beans.deepCopyAs(user, null);                      // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
##### copy(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull @SuppressWarnings("unchecked") public static <T> T copy(final T sourceBean)`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Creates a shallow copy of the given source bean.
- **Contract:**
  - That shortcut also carries fields which are not properties (a private field with no accessor, for instance), and it is only available when the optional Kryo library initializes successfully.
  - Do not rely on non-property field state being either preserved or reset; pass an explicit selection when only the properties must be copied.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`T`) — the source bean to copy; may be `null`.
- **Returns:** a new instance of the same class as `sourceBean` with all properties copied, or `null` if `sourceBean` is `null`. (may return null)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User original = new User("John", 25);
  
    // copy != original; copy.getName() returns "John", copy.getAge() returns 25
    User copy = Beans.copy(original);
  
    Beans.copy((User) null);   // returns null
  ```
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull public static <T> T copy(final T sourceBean, final Collection<String> selectPropNames) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Creates a shallow copy of the source bean with only selected properties.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`T`) — the source bean to copy; may be `null`.
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the property names to copy; unselected properties retain their default values. If `null`, all properties are copied; an empty collection copies no properties.
- **Returns:** a new instance of the same class as `sourceBean` with the selected properties copied, or `null` if `sourceBean` is `null`. (may return null)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a selected property is not found in the bean class.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User original = new User("John", 25);
  
    // Copy only "name"
    // partial.getName() returns "John"; partial.getAge() returns 0 (default)
    User partial = Beans.copy(original, Arrays.asList("name"));
  
    Beans.copy(original, Collections.emptyList());   // returns an empty copy (no props set)
  ```
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull public static <T> T copy(final T sourceBean, final BiPredicate<? super String, Object> propFilter) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Creates a shallow copy of the source bean with properties filtered by a predicate.
- **Contract:**
  - The predicate receives the property name and value and should return `true` to include the property in the copy.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`T`) — the source bean to copy; may be `null`.
  - `propFilter` (`BiPredicate<? super String, Object>`) — a predicate receiving the property name and value; returns `true` to include the property in the copy.
- **Returns:** a new instance of the same class as `sourceBean` with the properties that pass `propFilter` copied, or `null` if `sourceBean` is `null`. (may return null)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `propFilter` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User original = new User("John", 25);
  
    // Copy only String-valued properties
    User copy = Beans.copy(original,
        (propName, propValue) -> propValue instanceof String);
    // copy.getName() returns "John"; copy.getAge() returns 0 (age is int, filtered out)
  ```
- **See also:** Fn#identity(), Fn#selectFirst()
##### copyAs(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T copyAs(final Object sourceBean, final Class<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new instance of the specified target type with properties copied from the source bean.
- **Contract:**
  - Properties are matched by name - if a property exists in both source and target types with the same name, its value will be copied.
  - Usage Examples: Non-property state: when `targetType` is the source's own class and no property selection or name conversion is requested, an optimized whole-object copy may be used instead of a property-by-property copy.
  - That copy also carries fields which are not properties, and it is only available when the optional Kryo library initializes successfully.
  - It is not reachable from #copyAs(Object, boolean, Set, Class), which must skip `null`/default source values and so always copies property by property.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`Object`) — the source bean to copy properties from; may be `null`.
  - `targetType` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the class of the target bean to create; must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a new instance of the target type with matching properties copied from `sourceBean`; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetType` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User user = new User("John", 25);
  
    // Convert/copy to another bean type that shares property names
    UserDTO dto = Beans.copyAs(user, UserDTO.class);   // returns UserDTO with matching properties
  
    Beans.copyAs(null, User.class);                    // returns a new empty (non-null) instance
    Beans.copyAs(user, (Class<User>) null);            // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T copyAs(final Object sourceBean, final Collection<String> selectPropNames, @NotNull final Class<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new instance of the target type with selected properties copied from the source bean.
- **Contract:**
  - This method allows selective property copying when converting between different bean types.
  - Only properties whose names are in the selection list will be copied, and they must exist in both source and target types.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`Object`) — the source bean to copy properties from; may be `null`.
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the property names to copy; unselected properties retain their default values. If `null`, all matching properties are copied; an empty collection copies no properties.
  - `targetType` (`@NotNull Class<? extends T>`) — the class of the target bean to create; must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a new instance of the target type with the selected properties copied; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetType` is `null`, or if a selected property is not found in the source bean or in the target bean.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  UserEntity entity = new UserEntity("John", 25, "john@example.com", "password123");
  
    // Convert to DTO excluding sensitive data
    UserDTO dto = Beans.copyAs(entity,
        Arrays.asList("name", "age", "email"),
        UserDTO.class); // dto has name, age, and email but not password
  ```
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("unchecked") public static <T> T copyAs(final Object sourceBean, final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Function<String, String> propNameConverter, @NotNull final Class<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new instance of the target type with selected properties copied from the source bean, applying property name conversion.
- **Contract:**
  - This method is useful when property names differ between source and target beans.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`Object`) — the source bean to copy properties from; may be `null`.
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the source property names to copy; if `null`, all matching properties are copied; an empty collection copies no properties.
  - `propNameConverter` (`Function<String, String>`) — a function that converts each source property name to the corresponding target property name; use Fn#identity() to keep names unchanged.
  - `targetType` (`@NotNull Class<? extends T>`) — the class of the target bean to create; must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a new instance of the target type with properties copied and names converted; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetType` is `null`, or if a selected property is not found in the source bean or its (converted) name is not found in the target bean, or if `propNameConverter` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Source has camelCase, target expects snake_case
    UserEntity entity = new UserEntity();
    entity.setFirstName("John");
    entity.setLastName("Doe");
  
    UserDTO dto = Beans.copyAs(entity,
        Arrays.asList("firstName", "lastName"),
        propName -> Strings.toSnakeCase(propName),
        UserDTO.class);
    // dto.first_name will be "John"
    // dto.last_name will be "Doe"
  ```
- **See also:** Fn#identity(), Fn#selectFirst()
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T copyAs(final Object sourceBean, final BiPredicate<? super String, Object> propFilter, final Class<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new instance of the target type with properties filtered by a predicate and copied from the source bean.
- **Contract:**
  - Unlike #copyAs(Object, Class) - which silently skips a source property the target does not have, and is what makes copying into a narrower DTO work - a property that passes the filter is treated as explicitly requested, so it must exist on the target too or an IllegalArgumentException is thrown.
  - Exclude such properties in the filter itself, or drop the filter, if that is not what you want.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`Object`) — the source bean to copy properties from; may be `null`.
  - `propFilter` (`BiPredicate<? super String, Object>`) — a predicate receiving the property name and value; returns `true` to include the property in the copy.
  - `targetType` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the class of the target bean to create; must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a new instance of the target type with filtered properties copied; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetType` is `null`, or if a source property that passes the filter has no matching property in the target bean, or if `propFilter` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  UserEntity entity = new UserEntity("John", 25, null, "password123");
  
    // Copy only non-null and non-sensitive properties
    UserDTO dto = Beans.copyAs(entity,
        (propName, propValue) -> propValue != null && !propName.equals("password"),
        UserDTO.class); // dto has name and age but not email (null) or password
  ```
- **See also:** Fn#identity(), Fn#selectFirst()
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T copyAs(final Object sourceBean, final BiPredicate<? super String, Object> propFilter, final Function<String, String> propNameConverter, final Class<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new instance of the target type with properties filtered by a predicate and copied from the source bean, applying property name conversion.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`Object`) — the source bean to copy properties from; may be `null`.
  - `propFilter` (`BiPredicate<? super String, Object>`) — a predicate receiving the property name and value; returns `true` to include the property in the copy.
  - `propNameConverter` (`Function<String, String>`) — a function that converts each source property name to the corresponding target property name; use Fn#identity() to keep names unchanged.
  - `targetType` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the class of the target bean to create; must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a new instance of the target type with filtered and name-converted properties copied; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetType` is `null`, or if a source property that passes the filter has no matching (converted) property name in the target bean, or if any of `propFilter`, `propNameConverter` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  UserEntity entity = new UserEntity();
    entity.setFirstName("John");
    entity.setLastName("Doe");
    entity.setPassword("secret");
  
    // Copy non-sensitive properties with name conversion
    UserDTO dto = Beans.copyAs(entity,
        (propName, propValue) -> !propName.equals("password"),
        propName -> Strings.toSnakeCase(propName),
        UserDTO.class);
    // dto.first_name will be "John"
    // dto.last_name will be "Doe"
    // password is excluded
  ```
- **See also:** Fn#identity(), Fn#selectFirst()
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("unchecked") public static <T> T copyAs(final Object sourceBean, final boolean ignoreUnmatchedProperty, final Set<String> ignoredPropNames, @NotNull final Class<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new instance of the target type with properties copied from the source bean, excluding specified properties and optionally ignoring unmatched properties.
- **Contract:**
  - This method is useful when you want to copy most properties except for a specific set.
  - The `ignoreUnmatchedProperty` parameter controls whether an exception is thrown when a property exists in the source but not in the target.
  - The unmatched-property check (and the resulting exception when `ignoreUnmatchedProperty` is `false`) is therefore only applied to source properties whose value is non-`null` (and non-default).
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`Object`) — the source bean to copy properties from; may be `null`.
  - `ignoreUnmatchedProperty` (`boolean`) — if `true`, source properties without a matching target property are silently skipped; if `false`, an IllegalArgumentException is thrown.
  - `ignoredPropNames` (`Set<String>`) — a set of source property names to exclude from copying; ignored if `null`.
  - `targetType` (`@NotNull Class<? extends T>`) — the class of the target bean to create; must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a new instance of the target type with properties copied (excluding ignored ones); never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetType` is `null`, or if `ignoreUnmatchedProperty` is `false` and an unmatched property with a non-`null` source value is found.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  UserEntity entity = new UserEntity("John", 25, "john@example.com", "password123");
  
    // Copy all properties except sensitive ones
    UserDTO dto = Beans.copyAs(entity,
        true,
        N.asSet("password", "internalId"),
        UserDTO.class); // dto has all properties except password and internalId
  ```
##### mergeInto(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T mergeInto(final Object sourceBean, final T targetBean) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Merges properties from the source bean into the target bean.
- **Contract:**
  - The default merge strategy uses the source value when it is non-`null`; when the source value is `null`, the existing target value is retained (note: primitive properties are never `null`, so their values — including defaults such as `0` — always overwrite the target).
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`Object`) — the source bean from which properties are copied; if `null`, the target bean is returned unchanged.
  - `targetBean` (`T`) — the target bean into which properties are merged; must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** `targetBean` with merged properties applied.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetBean` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `targetBean` is an instance of a class treated as an immutable bean (a record, a builder-based class, one with no writable property, or one with no accessible no-arg constructor); it cannot be merged into in place.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User source = new User("Jane", 30);
    User target = new User("John", 25);
  
    // target.getName() returns "Jane"; target.getAge() returns 30
    Beans.mergeInto(source, target);
  
    Beans.mergeInto(null, target);   // target is unchanged
    Beans.mergeInto(source, null);   // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T mergeInto(final Object sourceBean, final T targetBean, final BinaryOperator<?> mergeFunc) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Merges properties from the source bean into the target bean using a custom merge function.
- **Contract:**
  - The merge function determines how to combine values when a property exists in both beans.
  - Use an overload that accepts a `boolean ignoreUnmatchedProperty` (passing `false`) if you instead want an IllegalArgumentException thrown for an unmatched source property.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`Object`) — the source bean from which properties are copied; if `null`, the target bean is returned unchanged.
  - `targetBean` (`T`) — the target bean into which properties are merged; must not be `null`.
  - `mergeFunc` (`BinaryOperator<?>`) — a binary operator that receives `(sourceValue, targetValue)` and returns the value to set on the target.
- **Returns:** `targetBean` with merged properties applied.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetBean` is `null`, or if `mergeFunc` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `targetBean` is an instance of a class treated as an immutable bean (a record, a builder-based class, one with no writable property, or one with no accessible no-arg constructor); it cannot be merged into in place.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User source = new User("A", 5);
    User target = new User("B", 10);
  
    // Sum numeric properties; otherwise keep the source value.
    Beans.mergeInto(source, target, (sourceVal, targetVal) -> {
        if (sourceVal instanceof Integer && targetVal instanceof Integer) {
            return ((Integer) sourceVal) + ((Integer) targetVal);
        }
        return sourceVal;
    });
    // target.getName() returns "A"; target.getAge() returns 15 (5 + 10)
  ```
- **See also:** Fn#identity(), Fn#selectFirst()
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T mergeInto(final Object sourceBean, @NotNull final T targetBean, final boolean ignoreUnmatchedProperty, final Set<String> ignoredPropNames) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Merges properties from the source bean into the target bean, excluding specified properties.
- **Contract:**
  - The `ignoreUnmatchedProperty` parameter controls whether an exception is thrown when a property exists in the source but not in the target.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`Object`) — the source bean from which properties are copied; if `null`, the target bean is returned unchanged.
  - `targetBean` (`@NotNull T`) — the target bean into which properties are merged; must not be `null`.
  - `ignoreUnmatchedProperty` (`boolean`) — if `true`, source properties without a matching target property are silently skipped; if `false`, an IllegalArgumentException is thrown.
  - `ignoredPropNames` (`Set<String>`) — a set of source property names to exclude from merging; ignored if `null`.
- **Returns:** `targetBean` with properties merged (excluding ignored ones).
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetBean` is `null`, or if `ignoreUnmatchedProperty` is `false` and an unmatched property is found.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `targetBean` is an instance of a class treated as an immutable bean (a record, a builder-based class, one with no writable property, or one with no accessible no-arg constructor); it cannot be merged into in place.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User source = new User("John", 30, "john@example.com", "password123");
    User target = new User("Jane", 25, "jane@example.com", "oldpass");
  
    // Merge all except password
    Beans.mergeInto(source, target,
        true,
        N.asSet("password")); // keeps target password unchanged
    // target: name="John", age=30, email="john@example.com", password="oldpass"
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T mergeInto(final Object sourceBean, @NotNull final T targetBean, final boolean ignoreUnmatchedProperty, final Set<String> ignoredPropNames, final BinaryOperator<?> mergeFunc) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Merges properties from the source bean into the target bean with a custom merge function, excluding specified properties.
- **Contract:**
  - This method combines exclusion-based merging with custom merge logic, useful when you want to merge most properties with special handling for certain values.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`Object`) — the source bean from which properties are copied; if `null`, the target bean is returned unchanged.
  - `targetBean` (`@NotNull T`) — the target bean into which properties are merged; must not be `null`.
  - `ignoreUnmatchedProperty` (`boolean`) — if `true`, source properties without a matching target property are silently skipped; if `false`, an IllegalArgumentException is thrown.
  - `ignoredPropNames` (`Set<String>`) — a set of source property names to exclude from merging; ignored if `null`.
  - `mergeFunc` (`BinaryOperator<?>`) — a binary operator that receives `(sourceValue, targetValue)` and returns the value to set on the target.
- **Returns:** `targetBean` with properties merged using custom logic.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetBean` is `null`, or if `ignoreUnmatchedProperty` is `false` and an unmatched property is found, or if `mergeFunc` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `targetBean` is an instance of a class treated as an immutable bean (a record, a builder-based class, one with no writable property, or one with no accessible no-arg constructor); it cannot be merged into in place.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Product source = new Product("New Product", 200, 15, "2024-01-01");
    Product target = new Product("Old Product", 150, 10, "2023-01-01");
  
    // Merge all except createdDate, using custom logic to add integer values
    Beans.mergeInto(source, target,
        true,
        N.asSet("createdDate"),
        (srcVal, tgtVal) -> {
            // For integer values, add them together
            if (srcVal instanceof Integer && tgtVal instanceof Integer) {
                return ((Integer) srcVal) + ((Integer) tgtVal);
            }
            return srcVal;
        });
    // target: name="New Product", price=350, quantity=25, createdDate="2023-01-01"
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T mergeInto(final Object sourceBean, final T targetBean, final Function<String, String> propNameConverter, final BinaryOperator<?> mergeFunc) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Merges properties from the source bean into the target bean with property name conversion and a custom merge function.
- **Contract:**
  - This method allows property name mapping during the merge operation, useful when source and target beans have different naming conventions.
  - When source and target are the same bean, matching source values are read before any target property is written, including when the converter exchanges property names.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`Object`) — the source bean from which properties are copied; if `null`, the target bean is returned unchanged.
  - `targetBean` (`T`) — the target bean into which properties are merged; must not be `null`.
  - `propNameConverter` (`Function<String, String>`) — a function that converts each source property name to the corresponding target property name; use Fn#identity() to keep names unchanged.
  - `mergeFunc` (`BinaryOperator<?>`) — a binary operator that receives `(sourceValue, targetValue)` and returns the value to set on the target.
- **Returns:** `targetBean` with merged properties applied.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetBean` is `null`, or if any of `propNameConverter`, `mergeFunc` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `targetBean` is an instance of a class treated as an immutable bean (a record, a builder-based class, one with no writable property, or one with no accessible no-arg constructor); it cannot be merged into in place.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Source has camelCase, target has snake_case
    SourceBean source = new SourceBean();
    source.setFirstName("John");
    TargetBean target = new TargetBean();
  
    Beans.mergeInto(source, target,
        propName -> Strings.toSnakeCase(propName),
        (srcVal, tgtVal) -> srcVal != null ? srcVal : tgtVal);
    // target.first_name is now "John"
  ```
- **See also:** Fn#identity(), Fn#selectFirst()
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T mergeInto(final Object sourceBean, @NotNull final T targetBean, final Collection<String> selectPropNames) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Merges selected properties from the source bean into the target bean.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful for partial updates where only specific fields should be modified.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`Object`) — the source bean from which properties are copied; if `null`, the target bean is returned unchanged.
  - `targetBean` (`@NotNull T`) — the target bean into which properties are merged; must not be `null`.
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the source property names to merge. If `null`, all properties are merged. If empty, no properties are merged.
- **Returns:** `targetBean` with the selected properties merged.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetBean` is `null`, or if a selected property is not found in the source bean or in the target bean.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `targetBean` is an instance of a class treated as an immutable bean (a record, a builder-based class, one with no writable property, or one with no accessible no-arg constructor); it cannot be merged into in place.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User existingUser = new User("John", 25, "john@old.com");
    User updates = new User("Jane", 30, "jane@new.com");
  
    // Only update email
    Beans.mergeInto(updates, existingUser, Arrays.asList("email"));
    // existingUser still has name="John", age=25, but email="jane@new.com"
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T mergeInto(final Object sourceBean, @NotNull final T targetBean, final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final BinaryOperator<?> mergeFunc) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Merges selected properties from the source bean into the target bean using a custom merge function.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`Object`) — the source bean from which properties are copied; if `null`, the target bean is returned unchanged.
  - `targetBean` (`@NotNull T`) — the target bean into which properties are merged; must not be `null`.
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the source property names to merge. If `null`, all properties are merged. If empty, no properties are merged.
  - `mergeFunc` (`BinaryOperator<?>`) — a binary operator that receives `(sourceValue, targetValue)` and returns the value to set on the target.
- **Returns:** `targetBean` with the selected properties merged.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetBean` is `null`, or if a selected property is not found in the source bean or in the target bean, or if `mergeFunc` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `targetBean` is an instance of a class treated as an immutable bean (a record, a builder-based class, one with no writable property, or one with no accessible no-arg constructor); it cannot be merged into in place.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User existingUser = new User("John", 25);
    existingUser.setScore(100);
    User updates = new User("Jane", 30);
    updates.setScore(200);
  
    // Only merge age and score, keeping the higher value when both are integers
    Beans.mergeInto(updates, existingUser,
        Arrays.asList("age", "score"),
        (srcVal, tgtVal) -> {
            if (srcVal instanceof Integer && tgtVal instanceof Integer) {
                return Math.max((Integer) srcVal, (Integer) tgtVal);
            }
            return srcVal;
        });
    // existingUser: name="John", age=30, score=200
  ```
- **See also:** Fn#identity(), Fn#selectFirst()
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T mergeInto(final Object sourceBean, @NotNull final T targetBean, final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Function<String, String> propNameConverter) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Merges selected properties from the source bean into the target bean with property name conversion.
- **Contract:**
  - This method combines selective property merging with name conversion, useful when merging between beans with different naming conventions.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`Object`) — the source bean from which properties are copied; if `null`, the target bean is returned unchanged.
  - `targetBean` (`@NotNull T`) — the target bean into which properties are merged; must not be `null`.
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the source property names to merge. If `null`, all properties are merged. If empty, no properties are merged.
  - `propNameConverter` (`Function<String, String>`) — a function that converts each source property name to the corresponding target property name; use Fn#identity() to keep names unchanged.
- **Returns:** `targetBean` with the selected (and name-converted) properties merged.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetBean` is `null`, or if a selected property is not found in the source bean or in the target bean, or if `propNameConverter` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `targetBean` is an instance of a class treated as an immutable bean (a record, a builder-based class, one with no writable property, or one with no accessible no-arg constructor); it cannot be merged into in place.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  SourceBean source = new SourceBean();
    source.setFirstName("John");
    source.setLastName("Doe");
  
    TargetBean target = new TargetBean();
  
    // Merge only firstName, converting to snake_case
    Beans.mergeInto(source, target,
        Arrays.asList("firstName"),
        propName -> Strings.toSnakeCase(propName));
    // target.first_name is now "John"
  ```
- **See also:** Fn#identity(), Fn#selectFirst()
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T mergeInto(final Object sourceBean, @NotNull final T targetBean, final Collection<String> selectPropNames, final Function<String, String> propNameConverter, final BinaryOperator<?> mergeFunc) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Merges selected properties from the source bean into the target bean with property name conversion and a custom merge function.
- **Contract:**
  - Matching source values are read before any target property is written when properties are explicitly selected or source and target are the same bean.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`Object`) — the source bean from which properties are copied; if `null`, the target bean is returned unchanged.
  - `targetBean` (`@NotNull T`) — the target bean into which properties are merged; must not be `null`.
  - `selectPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the source property names to merge. If `null`, all properties are merged. If empty, no properties are merged.
  - `propNameConverter` (`Function<String, String>`) — a function that converts each source property name to the corresponding target property name; use Fn#identity() to keep names unchanged.
  - `mergeFunc` (`BinaryOperator<?>`) — a binary operator that receives `(sourceValue, targetValue)` and returns the value to set on the target.
- **Returns:** `targetBean` with the selected, name-converted, and merged properties applied.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetBean` is `null`, or if a selected property is not found in the source bean or in the target bean, or if any of `propNameConverter`, `mergeFunc` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `targetBean` is an instance of a class treated as an immutable bean (a record, a builder-based class, one with no writable property, or one with no accessible no-arg constructor); it cannot be merged into in place.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  SourceBean source = new SourceBean();
    source.setFirstName("John");
    source.setTotalAmount(150);
  
    TargetBean target = new TargetBean();
    target.setTotal_amount(100);
  
    Beans.mergeInto(source, target,
        Arrays.asList("firstName", "totalAmount"),
        propName -> Strings.toSnakeCase(propName),
        (srcVal, tgtVal) -> {
            // For amounts, add them together
            if (srcVal instanceof Number && tgtVal instanceof Number) {
                return ((Number) srcVal).intValue() + ((Number) tgtVal).intValue();
            }
            return srcVal;
        });
    // target.first_name = "John"
    // target.total_amount = 250 (150 + 100)
  ```
- **See also:** Fn#identity(), Fn#selectFirst()
##### mergeIntoIf(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T mergeIntoIf(final Object sourceBean, final T targetBean, final BiPredicate<? super String, Object> propFilter) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Merges properties from the source bean into the target bean based on a filter predicate.
- **Contract:**
  - The predicate receives each property name and value from the source bean and determines whether that property should be merged into the target.
  - #mergeInto(Object, Object) and the `mergeFunc`-only overload silently skip a source property the target does not have; a property that passes this filter is instead treated as explicitly requested, so it must exist on the target or an IllegalArgumentException is thrown - the same rule an explicit `selectPropNames` collection follows.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`Object`) — the source bean from which properties are copied; if `null`, the target bean is returned unchanged.
  - `targetBean` (`T`) — the target bean into which properties are merged; must not be `null`.
  - `propFilter` (`BiPredicate<? super String, Object>`) — a predicate receiving the property name and source value; returns `true` to merge the property into the target.
- **Returns:** `targetBean` with matching properties merged.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetBean` is `null`, or if a property that passes the filter has no matching property in the target bean, or if `propFilter` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `targetBean` is an instance of a class treated as an immutable bean (a record, a builder-based class, one with no writable property, or one with no accessible no-arg constructor); it cannot be merged into in place.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User source = new User("John", 0, null);
    User target = new User("Jane", 25, "jane@example.com");
  
    // Only merge non-null and non-zero values.
    Beans.mergeIntoIf(source, target,
        (propName, propValue) -> propValue != null &&
            !(propValue instanceof Number && ((Number) propValue).intValue() == 0));
    // target keeps age=25 and email="jane@example.com" but name becomes "John"
  ```
- **See also:** Fn#identity(), Fn#selectFirst()
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T mergeIntoIf(final Object sourceBean, @NotNull final T targetBean, final BiPredicate<? super String, Object> propFilter, final BinaryOperator<?> mergeFunc) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Merges properties from the source bean into the target bean based on a filter predicate and using a custom merge function.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`Object`) — the source bean from which properties are copied; if `null`, the target bean is returned unchanged.
  - `targetBean` (`@NotNull T`) — the target bean into which properties are merged; must not be `null`.
  - `propFilter` (`BiPredicate<? super String, Object>`) — a predicate receiving the property name and source value; returns `true` to merge the property into the target.
  - `mergeFunc` (`BinaryOperator<?>`) — a binary operator that receives `(sourceValue, targetValue)` and returns the value to set on the target.
- **Returns:** `targetBean` with filtered and merged properties applied.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetBean` is `null`, or if a property that passes the filter has no matching property in the target bean, or if any of `propFilter`, `mergeFunc` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `targetBean` is an instance of a class treated as an immutable bean (a record, a builder-based class, one with no writable property, or one with no accessible no-arg constructor); it cannot be merged into in place.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Product source = new Product("New Name", 150, 10);
    Product target = new Product("Old Name", 100, 5);
  
    // Merge numeric properties by adding them, others by replacing
    Beans.mergeIntoIf(source, target,
        (propName, propValue) -> propValue != null,
        (srcVal, tgtVal) -> {
            if (srcVal instanceof Number && tgtVal instanceof Number) {
                return ((Number) srcVal).intValue() + ((Number) tgtVal).intValue();
            }
            return srcVal;
        });
    // target: name="New Name", price=250, quantity=15
  ```
- **See also:** Fn#identity(), Fn#selectFirst()
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T mergeIntoIf(final Object sourceBean, @NotNull final T targetBean, final BiPredicate<? super String, Object> propFilter, final Function<String, String> propNameConverter) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Merges properties from the source bean into the target bean based on a filter predicate with property name conversion.
- **Contract:**
  - This method allows filtering properties and converting their names during the merge, useful when working with beans that have different naming conventions.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`Object`) — the source bean from which properties are copied; if `null`, the target bean is returned unchanged.
  - `targetBean` (`@NotNull T`) — the target bean into which properties are merged; must not be `null`.
  - `propFilter` (`BiPredicate<? super String, Object>`) — a predicate receiving the property name and source value; returns `true` to merge the property into the target.
  - `propNameConverter` (`Function<String, String>`) — a function that converts each source property name to the corresponding target property name; use Fn#identity() to keep names unchanged.
- **Returns:** `targetBean` with filtered and name-converted properties merged.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetBean` is `null`, or if a property that passes the filter has no matching property in the target bean, or if any of `propFilter`, `propNameConverter` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `targetBean` is an instance of a class treated as an immutable bean (a record, a builder-based class, one with no writable property, or one with no accessible no-arg constructor); it cannot be merged into in place.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  SourceBean source = new SourceBean();
    source.setFirstName("John");
    source.setLastName("");   // source is set with an empty lastName
  
    TargetBean target = new TargetBean();
  
    // Only merge non-empty strings, converting to snake_case
    Beans.mergeIntoIf(source, target,
        (propName, propValue) -> propValue instanceof String && !((String) propValue).isEmpty(),
        propName -> Strings.toSnakeCase(propName));
    // target.first_name = "John", last_name is not merged
  ```
- **See also:** Fn#identity(), Fn#selectFirst()
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T mergeIntoIf(final Object sourceBean, @NotNull final T targetBean, final BiPredicate<? super String, Object> propFilter, final Function<String, String> propNameConverter, final BinaryOperator<?> mergeFunc) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Merges properties from the source bean into the target bean with full control over filtering, name conversion, and merge logic.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sourceBean` (`Object`) — the source bean from which properties are copied; if `null`, the target bean is returned unchanged.
  - `targetBean` (`@NotNull T`) — the target bean into which properties are merged; must not be `null`.
  - `propFilter` (`BiPredicate<? super String, Object>`) — a predicate receiving the property name and source value; returns `true` to merge the property into the target.
  - `propNameConverter` (`Function<String, String>`) — a function that converts each source property name to the corresponding target property name; use Fn#identity() to keep names unchanged.
  - `mergeFunc` (`BinaryOperator<?>`) — a binary operator that receives `(sourceValue, targetValue)` and returns the value to set on the target.
- **Returns:** `targetBean` with filtered, name-converted, and merged properties applied.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetBean` is `null`, or if a property that passes the filter has no matching property in the target bean, or if any of `propFilter`, `propNameConverter`, `mergeFunc` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `targetBean` is an instance of a class treated as an immutable bean (a record, a builder-based class, one with no writable property, or one with no accessible no-arg constructor); it cannot be merged into in place.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  SourceBean source = new SourceBean();
    source.setFirstName("John");
    source.setTotalCount(10);
    source.setLastUpdated(new Date());
  
    TargetBean target = new TargetBean();
    target.setTotal_count(5);
  
    Beans.mergeIntoIf(source, target,
        // Only merge non-null values
        (propName, propValue) -> propValue != null,
        // Convert camelCase to snake_case
        propName -> Strings.toSnakeCase(propName),
        // Custom merge logic
        (srcVal, tgtVal) -> {
            if (srcVal instanceof Integer && tgtVal instanceof Integer) {
                return ((Integer) srcVal) + ((Integer) tgtVal);
            } else if (srcVal instanceof Date && tgtVal instanceof Date) {
                // Keep the more recent date
                return ((Date) srcVal).after((Date) tgtVal) ? srcVal : tgtVal;
            }
            return srcVal;
        });
    // Result: first_name="John", total_count=15, last_updated=most recent date
  ```
- **See also:** Fn#identity(), Fn#selectFirst()
##### clearProps(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static void clearProps(final Object bean, final String... propNames) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Erases (sets to default values) the specified properties of the given bean.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object whose properties are to be cleared; if `null`, the method does nothing.
  - `propNames` (`String[]`) — the names of the properties to clear; if empty, the method does nothing.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any name in `propNames` is not a property of the bean.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `bean` is an instance of a class treated as an immutable bean (a record, a builder-based class, one with no writable property, or one with no accessible no-arg constructor); its properties cannot be set in place - build a new instance instead.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User user = new User("John", 25);
    user.setActive(true);
  
    // user.getName() returns null; user.getAge() returns 0; user.getActive() still true
    Beans.clearProps(user, "name", "age");
  
    Beans.clearProps(user, new String[0]);   // no change
    Beans.clearProps(null, "name");          // no change
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static void clearProps(final Object bean, final Collection<String> propNames) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Erases (sets to default values) the specified properties of the given bean.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object whose properties are to be cleared; if `null`, the method does nothing.
  - `propNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the collection of property names to clear; if empty, the method does nothing.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any name in `propNames` is not a property of the bean.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `bean` is an instance of a class treated as an immutable bean (a record, a builder-based class, one with no writable property, or one with no accessible no-arg constructor); its properties cannot be set in place - build a new instance instead.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User user = new User("John", 25);
    user.setActive(true);
  
    Beans.clearProps(user, Arrays.asList("name", "age"));
    // user.getName() returns null; user.getAge() returns 0; user.getActive() still true
  
    Beans.clearProps(user, Collections.emptyList());   // no change
    Beans.clearProps(null, Arrays.asList("name"));     // no change
  ```

##### randomize(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static void randomize(final Object bean) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Fills all properties of the specified bean with random values.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object to populate; must not be `null` and must be a valid bean class.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `bean` is `null` or not a valid bean class.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `bean` is an instance of a class treated as an immutable bean (a record, a builder-based class, one with no writable property, or one with no accessible no-arg constructor); its properties cannot be set in place - build a new instance instead.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User user = new User();
    Beans.randomize(user);
    // every property is now filled with a random value
    // user.getName() is a non-null random String (e.g. a 16-char UUID fragment)
  
    Beans.randomize((Object) null);   // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static void randomize(final Object bean, final Collection<String> propNamesToFill) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Fills the specified properties of the bean with random values.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful when you want to test specific scenarios with only certain fields populated.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object to populate; must not be `null` and must be a valid bean class.
  - `propNamesToFill` (`Collection<String>`) — the names of the properties to fill with random values; must not be `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `bean` is `null` or not a valid bean class, if `propNamesToFill` is `null`, or if a property name is not found in the bean.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `bean` is an instance of a class treated as an immutable bean (a record, a builder-based class, one with no writable property, or one with no accessible no-arg constructor); its properties cannot be set in place - build a new instance instead.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User user = new User();
    Beans.randomize(user, Arrays.asList("name"));
    // user.getName() is now a non-null random value; user.getAge() stays 0; active stays null
  ```
##### newRandomBean(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T newRandomBean(final Class<? extends T> beanClass) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new instance of the specified bean class and fills all its properties with random values.
- **Parameters:**
  - `beanClass` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the class to instantiate and populate; must not be `null` and must be a valid bean class.
- **Returns:** a new instance with all properties filled with random values; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `beanClass` is `null` or not a valid bean class.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // user is non-null with every property filled (user.getName() is non-null)
    User user = Beans.newRandomBean(User.class);
  
    Beans.newRandomBean((Class<?>) null);   // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T newRandomBean(final Class<? extends T> beanClass, final Collection<String> propNamesToFill) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new instance of the specified bean class and fills only the specified properties.
- **Parameters:**
  - `beanClass` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the class to instantiate and populate; must not be `null` and must be a valid bean class.
  - `propNamesToFill` (`Collection<String>`) — the names of the properties to fill with random values; must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a new instance with the specified properties filled with random values; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `beanClass` is `null` or not a valid bean class, if `propNamesToFill` is `null`, or if a property name is not found in the class.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  class User {
        private String name;
        private int age;
        private Boolean active;
        public String getName() { return name; }
        public void setName(String name) { this.name = name; }
        public int getAge() { return age; }
        public void setAge(int age) { this.age = age; }
        public Boolean getActive() { return active; }
        public void setActive(Boolean active) { this.active = active; }
    }
    User user = Beans.newRandomBean(User.class, Arrays.asList("name"));
  
    // user.getName() is a non-null random value; user.getAge() stays 0; active stays null
  ```
##### newRandomBeanList(...) -> List<T>
- **Signature:** `public static <T> List<T> newRandomBeanList(final Class<? extends T> beanClass, final int count) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates multiple instances of the specified bean class, each filled with random values.
- **Contract:**
  - This method is useful for generating test data sets or when you need multiple test objects with varying random data.
- **Parameters:**
  - `beanClass` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the class to instantiate and populate; must not be `null` and must be a valid bean class.
  - `count` (`int`) — the number of instances to create; must not be negative.
- **Returns:** a list containing exactly `count` newly created and fully populated bean instances; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `beanClass` is `null`, not a valid bean class, or `count` is negative.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // users.size() == 3; each element has every property filled with a random value
    List<User> users = Beans.newRandomBeanList(User.class, 3);
  
    Beans.newRandomBeanList(User.class, 0);   // returns [] (empty list)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <T> List<T> newRandomBeanList(final Class<? extends T> beanClass, final Collection<String> propNamesToFill, final int count) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates multiple instances of the specified bean class with only the specified properties filled.
- **Parameters:**
  - `beanClass` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the class to instantiate and populate; must not be `null` and must be a valid bean class.
  - `propNamesToFill` (`Collection<String>`) — the names of the properties to fill with random values; must not be `null`.
  - `count` (`int`) — the number of instances to create; must not be negative.
- **Returns:** a list containing exactly `count` newly created bean instances with the specified properties filled; never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `beanClass` is `null` or not a valid bean class, `propNamesToFill` is `null` or contains an unknown property name, or `count` is negative.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  class User {
        private String name;
        private int age;
        private Boolean active;
        public String getName() { return name; }
        public void setName(String name) { this.name = name; }
        public int getAge() { return age; }
        public void setAge(int age) { this.age = age; }
        public Boolean getActive() { return active; }
        public void setActive(Boolean active) { this.active = active; }
    }
    // users.size() == 2; each user has a random name but age stays 0 and active stays null
    List<User> users = Beans.newRandomBeanList(User.class, Arrays.asList("name"), 2);
  
    Beans.newRandomBeanList(User.class, Arrays.asList("name"), 0);   // returns [] (empty list)
  ```
##### stream(...) -> Stream<Map.Entry<String, Object>>
- **Signature:** `public static Stream<Map.Entry<String, Object>> stream(final Object bean) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a stream of property name-value pairs from the specified bean.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object to extract properties from; must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a Stream of Map.Entry objects where each key is a property name and each value is the corresponding property value (which may be `null`).
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `bean` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User user = new User("John", 25);
    user.setActive(true);
  
    Beans.stream(user).count();   // returns 3 (one entry per property)
    // Outputs: name: John / age: 25 / active: true
    Beans.stream(user).forEach(e -> System.out.println(e.getKey() + ": " + e.getValue()));
  
    Beans.stream(null);   // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static Stream<Map.Entry<String, Object>> stream(final Object bean, final BiPredicate<? super String, Object> propFilter) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a filtered stream of property name-value pairs from the specified bean.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bean` (`Object`) — the bean object to extract properties from; must not be `null`.
  - `propFilter` (`BiPredicate<? super String, Object>`) — a BiPredicate that receives the property name and its value and returns `true` to include the property in the stream, or `false` to skip it.
- **Returns:** a lazy Stream of Map.Entry objects where each key is a property name and each value is the corresponding property value (which may be `null`), containing only those properties for which `propFilter` returned `true`. As with #stream(Object), the getters run at consumption time, not at call time.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `bean` is `null`, or if `propFilter` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  User user = new User("John", 25);
  
    // Only String-valued properties
    Beans.stream(user, (name, value) -> value instanceof String).count();   // returns 1 (name)
  
    // Only non-null properties (active is null, excluded)
    Beans.stream(user, (name, value) -> value != null).count();             // returns 2 (name, age)
  ```

- **Annotations:** @Beta, @SequentialOnly, @Stateful
- **Summary:** Returns a stateful BiFunction that applies a function based on element index position.
- **Contract:**
  - Important: This method is marked as `@Beta`, `@SequentialOnly`, and `@Stateful`, indicating it should not be saved, cached for reuse, or used in parallel streams.

  ```java
  // Create indexed pairs from two lists
    List<String> names = Arrays.asList("Alice", "Bob", "Charlie");
    List<Integer> ages = Arrays.asList(25, 30, 35);
  
    BiFunction<String, Integer, String> indexedFormatter =
        BiFunctions.indexed((idx, name, age) ->
            String.format("[%d] %s is %d years old", idx, name, age));
  
    // Apply to pairs - index increments with each call
    System.out.println(indexedFormatter.apply(names.get(0), ages.get(0)));
    // Output: "[0] Alice is 25 years old"
    System.out.println(indexedFormatter.apply(names.get(1), ages.get(1)));
    // Output: "[1] Bob is 30 years old"
  ```
