  ```java
    // | North  | USA     | Boston      | 800   | 40       |
    // | North  | Canada  | Toronto     | 600   | 30       |
    // | South  | Mexico  | Mexico City | 400   | 20       |
    // +--------+---------+-------------+-------+----------+
  
    Function<DisposableObjArray, String> keyExtractor = keyRow -> keyRow.join("-");
    Stream<Dataset> rollupResult = dataset.rollup(
        Arrays.asList("region", "country", "city"),
        keyExtractor,
        Arrays.asList("sales", "quantity"),
        "aggregated_data",
        row -> Tuple.of((Integer) row.get(0), (Integer) row.get(1)),
        Collectors.reducing(Tuple.of(0, 0), Function.identity(),
            (a, b) -> Tuple.of(a._1 + b._1, a._2 + b._2)));
  
    // Returns a stream of 4 datasets:
    // Level 1: Grouped by region, country, city (most detailed)
    // +--------+---------+-------------+-----------------+
    // | region | country | city        | aggregated_data |
    // +--------+---------+-------------+-----------------+
    // | North  | USA     | New York    | (1000, 50)      |
    // | North  | USA     | Boston      | (800, 40)       |
    // | North  | Canada  | Toronto     | (600, 30)       |
    // | South  | Mexico  | Mexico City | (400, 20)       |
    // +--------+---------+-------------+-----------------+
    // Level 2: Grouped by region, country
    // +--------+---------+-----------------+
    // | region | country | aggregated_data |
    // +--------+---------+-----------------+
    // | North  | USA     | (1800, 90)      |
    // | North  | Canada  | (600, 30)       |
    // | South  | Mexico  | (400, 20)       |
    // +--------+---------+-----------------+
    // Level 3: Grouped by region
    // +--------+-----------------+
    // | region | aggregated_data |
    // +--------+-----------------+
    // | North  | (2400, 120)     |
    // | South  | (400, 20)       |
    // +--------+-----------------+
    // Level 4: Grand total (no grouping)
    // +-----------------+
    // | aggregated_data |
    // +-----------------+
    // | (2800, 140)     |
    // +-----------------+
  ```
- **See also:** #rollup(Collection), #rollup(Collection, Function), #groupBy(Collection, Function), #cube(Collection), What is the difference between cube, rollup and groupBy operators? (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/37975227)
##### cube(...) -> Stream<Dataset>
- **Signature:** `@Beta Stream<Dataset> cube(Collection<String> keyColumnNames) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Performs a cube operation on the Dataset using the specified columns.
- **Contract:**
  - If one of the key columns is itself named `"count"`, the result column becomes `"count_2"` (then `"count_3"`,...) so the names stay distinct.
  - Column selections are snapshotted when this method is called, and aggregation reads Dataset values lazily as each level is requested.
  - The returned stream computes each grouping when consumed.
  - Traversal throws ConcurrentModificationException if this dataset changes after the stream is created; exceptions from grouping callbacks or collector operations propagate during traversal.
- **Parameters:**
  - `keyColumnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the names of the columns on which the cube operation is to be performed. Must not be `null` or empty.
- **Returns:** a Stream of Datasets, each representing a level of the cube operation, covering all possible combinations of the specified columns. Arguments are validated when this method is called, before the Stream is returned.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `keyColumnNames` is null or empty; a specified column name is null or unknown; a column selection contains duplicate names; more than 30 key columns are selected.
- **Performance:** The iterator retains O(keyCount) state; requesting every result still produces 2^keyCount grouping sets.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("region", "country", "sales"),
        new Object[][] {
             {"North", "USA", 1000},
             {"North", "Canada", 600},
             {"South", "Mexico", 400}
        });
  
    // +--------+---------+-------+
    // | region | country | sales |
    // +--------+---------+-------+
    // | North  | USA     | 1000  |
    // | North  | Canada  | 600   |
    // | South  | Mexico  | 400   |
    // +--------+---------+-------+
  
    Stream<Dataset> cubeResult = dataset.cube(Arrays.asList("region", "country"));
    // Returns a stream of 4 datasets:
    // Level 1: Grouped by region, country (most detailed)
    // +--------+---------+-------+
    // | region | country | count |
    // +--------+---------+-------+
    // | North  | USA     | 1     |
    // | North  | Canada  | 1     |
    // | South  | Mexico  | 1     |
    // +--------+---------+-------+
    // Level 2: Grouped by region only
    // +--------+-------+
    // | region | count |
    // +--------+-------+
    // | North  | 2     |
    // | South  | 1     |
    // +--------+-------+
    // Level 3: Grouped by country only
    // +---------+-------+
    // | country | count |
    // +---------+-------+
    // | USA     | 1     |
    // | Canada  | 1     |
    // | Mexico  | 1     |
    // +---------+-------+
    // Level 4: Grand total (no grouping)
    // +-------+
    // | count |
    // +-------+
    // | 3     |
    // +-------+
  ```
- **See also:** #rollup(Collection), #cube(Collection, Function, Collection, String, Function, Collector), What is the difference between cube, rollup and groupBy operators? (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/37975227)
- **Signature:** `@Beta Stream<Dataset> cube(Collection<String> keyColumnNames, String aggregateOnColumnName, String aggregateResultColumnName, Collector<?, ?, ?> collector) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Performs a cube operation on the Dataset using the specified columns and an aggregate operation.
- **Contract:**
  - Column selections are snapshotted when this method is called, and aggregation reads Dataset values lazily as each level is requested.
  - The returned stream computes each grouping when consumed.
  - Traversal throws ConcurrentModificationException if this dataset changes after the stream is created; exceptions from grouping callbacks or collector operations propagate during traversal.
- **Parameters:**
  - `keyColumnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the names of the columns on which the cube operation is to be performed.
  - `aggregateOnColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the column on which the aggregate operation is to be performed.
  - `aggregateResultColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the new column that will store the result of the aggregate operation. Must not be `null` or empty, and must not be one of `keyColumnNames` - like every other argument here, that is checked when this method is called, not when the Stream is consumed.
  - `collector` (`Collector<?, ?, ?>`) — the collector defining the aggregate operation.
- **Returns:** a Stream of Datasets, each representing a level of the cube operation. Arguments are validated when this method is called, before the Stream is returned.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `keyColumnNames` is null or empty; a specified column name is null or unknown; a column selection contains duplicate names; `aggregateResultColumnName` is null, empty, or duplicates a key column name; `collector` is null; more than 30 key columns are selected.
- **Performance:** The iterator retains O(keyCount) state; requesting every result still produces 2^keyCount grouping sets.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("region", "product", "amount"), new Object[][] {{"APAC", "A", 42}});
    Stream<Dataset> levels = dataset.cube(Arrays.asList("region", "product"), "amount", "total_amount", Collectors.summingInt(Integer.class::cast));
  ```

  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `keyColumnNames` is null or empty; a specified column name is null or unknown; a column selection contains duplicate names; `aggregateOnColumnNames` is null or empty; `aggregateResultColumnName` is null, empty, or duplicates a key column name; `keyExtractor`, `rowMapper`, `collector` is null; more than 30 key columns are selected.
- **Performance:** The iterator retains O(keyCount) state; requesting every result still produces 2^keyCount grouping sets.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("region", "country", "sales"),
        new Object[][] {
             {"North", "USA", 1000},
             {"North", "Canada", 600},
             {"South", "Mexico", 400}
        });
  
    // +--------+---------+-------+
    // | region | country | sales |
    // +--------+---------+-------+
    // | North  | USA     | 1000  |
    // | North  | Canada  | 600   |
    // | South  | Mexico  | 400   |
    // +--------+---------+-------+
  
    Function<DisposableObjArray, String> keyExtractor = keyRow -> keyRow.join("-");
    Function<DisposableObjArray, Double> rowMapper = row -> (Integer) row.get(0) * 1.1;
    Stream<Dataset> cubeResult = dataset.cube(
        Arrays.asList("region", "country"),
        keyExtractor,
        Arrays.asList("sales"),
        "total_sales_with_markup",
        rowMapper,
        Collectors.collectingAndThen(Collectors.summingDouble(Double::doubleValue), r -> Numbers.round(r, 2)));
    // Returns a stream of 4 datasets:
    // Level 1: Grouped by region, country (most detailed)
    // +--------+---------+-------------------------+
    // | region | country | total_sales_with_markup |
    // +--------+---------+-------------------------+
    // | North  | USA     | 1100.0                  |
    // | North  | Canada  | 660.0                   |
    // | South  | Mexico  | 440.0                   |
    // +--------+---------+-------------------------+
    // Level 2: Grouped by region only
    // +--------+-------------------------+
    // | region | total_sales_with_markup |
    // +--------+-------------------------+
    // | North  | 1760.0                  |
    // | South  | 440.0                   |
    // +--------+-------------------------+
    // Level 3: Grouped by country only
    // +---------+-------------------------+
    // | country | total_sales_with_markup |
    // +---------+-------------------------+
    // | USA     | 1100.0                  |
    // | Canada  | 660.0                   |
    // | Mexico  | 440.0                   |
    // +---------+-------------------------+
    // Level 4: Grand total (no grouping)
    // +-------------------------+
    // | total_sales_with_markup |
    // +-------------------------+
    // | 2200.0                  |
    // +-------------------------+
  ```
- **See also:** #rollup(Collection, Function, Collection, String, Function, Collector), What is the difference between cube, rollup and groupBy operators? (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/37975227)
##### pivot(...) -> Sheet<R, C, T>
- **Signature:** `@Beta <R, C, T> Sheet<R, C, T> pivot(String keyColumnName, String pivotColumnName, String aggregateOnColumnName, Collector<?, ?, ? extends T> collector) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Performs a pivot operation on the Dataset using the specified key column, aggregate column, pivot column, and a collector.
- **Contract:**
  - Obtain those retained keys from Sheet#rowKeySet() and Sheet#columnKeySet(), or supply Wrapper#of(Object) keys in this Dataset when content-based lookup is required on the result.
- **Parameters:**
  - `keyColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used as the row identifier in the resulting Sheet.
  - `pivotColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used as the column identifier in the resulting Sheet.
  - `aggregateOnColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the column on which the aggregate operation is to be performed.
  - `collector` (`Collector<?, ?, ? extends T>`) — the collector that defines the aggregate operation.
- **Returns:** a Sheet representing the result of the pivot operation.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; `collector` is null; the key and pivot column names are equal, or either selected key column contains a null value.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a collector supplier, accumulator, or finisher throws while grouping a row or producing an aggregate result.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("region", "product", "sales"),
        new Object[][] {
             {"North", "A", 100},
             {"North", "B", 200},
             {"South", "A", 150},
             {"South", "B", 250}
        });
  
    // +--------+---------+-------+
    // | region | product | sales |
    // +--------+---------+-------+
    // | North  | A       | 100   |
    // | North  | B       | 200   |
    // | South  | A       | 150   |
    // | South  | B       | 250   |
    // +--------+---------+-------+
  
    Sheet<String, String, Integer> pivotResult = dataset.pivot(
        "region",      // "region" is the row identifier
        "product",     // "product" is the column identifier
        "sales",       // "sales" is the aggregate column
        Collectors.summingInt(Integer::intValue));
  
    // Result Sheet:
    //         +-----+-----+
    //         | A   | B   |
    // +-------+-----+-----+
    // | North | 100 | 200 |
    // | South | 150 | 250 |
    // +-------+-----+-----+
  ```
- **See also:** #groupBy(Collection), #rollup(Collection), #cube(Collection), Difference between groupby and pivot_table for pandas dataframes (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/34702815)
- **Signature:** `@Beta <R, C, T> Sheet<R, C, T> pivot(String keyColumnName, String pivotColumnName, Collection<String> aggregateOnColumnNames, Collector<? super Object[], ?, ? extends T> collector) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Performs a pivot operation on the Dataset using the specified key column, aggregate columns, pivot column, and a collector.
- **Contract:**
  - Obtain those retained keys from Sheet#rowKeySet() and Sheet#columnKeySet(), or supply Wrapper#of(Object) keys in this Dataset when content-based lookup is required on the result.
- **Parameters:**
  - `keyColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used as the row identifier in the resulting Sheet.
  - `pivotColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used as the column identifier in the resulting Sheet.
  - `aggregateOnColumnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the names of the columns on which the aggregate operation is to be performed. Must not be `null` or empty.
  - `collector` (`Collector<? super Object[], ?, ? extends T>`) — the collector that defines the aggregate operation.
- **Returns:** a Sheet representing the result of the pivot operation.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; a column selection contains duplicate names; `aggregateOnColumnNames` is null or empty; `collector` is null; the key and pivot column names are equal, or either selected key column contains a null value.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a collector supplier, accumulator, or finisher throws while grouping a row or producing an aggregate result.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("region", "product", "sales", "quantity"),
        new Object[][] {
             {"North", "A", 100, 10},
             {"North", "B", 200, 20},
             {"South", "A", 150, 15},
             {"South", "B", 250, 25}
        });
  
    // +--------+---------+-------+----------+
    // | region | product | sales | quantity |
    // +--------+---------+-------+----------+
    // | North  | A       | 100   | 10       |
    // | North  | B       | 200   | 20       |
    // | South  | A       | 150   | 15       |
    // | South  | B       | 250   | 25       |
    // +--------+---------+-------+----------+
  
    Sheet<String, String, Integer> pivotResult = dataset.pivot(
        "region",                                                           // "region" is the row identifier
        "product",                                                          // "product" is the column identifier
        Arrays.asList("sales", "quantity"),                                 // "sales" and "quantity" are the aggregate columns
        Collectors.summingInt(arr -> (Integer) arr[0] + (Integer) arr[1])); // sums sales + quantity
  
    // Result Sheet:
    //         +-----+-----+
    //         | A   | B   |
    // +-------+-----+-----+
    // | North | 110 | 220 |
    // | South | 165 | 275 |
    // +-------+-----+-----+
  ```
- **See also:** #pivot(String, String, String, Collector), #groupBy(Collection), #rollup(Collection), #cube(Collection), Difference between groupby and pivot_table for pandas dataframes (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/34702815)
- **Signature:** `@Beta <R, C, U, T> Sheet<R, C, T> pivot(String keyColumnName, String pivotColumnName, Collection<String> aggregateOnColumnNames, Function<? super DisposableObjArray, ? extends U> rowMapper, Collector<? super U, ?, ? extends T> collector) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Performs a pivot operation on the Dataset using the specified key column, aggregate columns, pivot column, a row mapper, and a collector.
- **Contract:**
  - Obtain those retained keys from Sheet#rowKeySet() and Sheet#columnKeySet(), or supply Wrapper#of(Object) keys in this Dataset when content-based lookup is required on the result.
- **Parameters:**
  - `keyColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used as the row identifier in the resulting Sheet.
  - `pivotColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used as the column identifier in the resulting Sheet.
  - `aggregateOnColumnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the names of the columns on which the aggregate operation is to be performed. Must not be `null` or empty.
  - `rowMapper` (`Function<? super DisposableObjArray, ? extends U>`) — the function to transform the row data before aggregation.
  - `collector` (`Collector<? super U, ?, ? extends T>`) — the collector that defines the aggregate operation.
- **Returns:** a Sheet representing the result of the pivot operation.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; a column selection contains duplicate names; `aggregateOnColumnNames` is null or empty; `rowMapper`, `collector` is null; the key and pivot column names are equal, or either selected key column contains a null value.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the rowMapper, a collector supplier, accumulator, or finisher throws while grouping a row or producing an aggregate result.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("region", "product", "sales", "quantity"),
        new Object[][] {
             {"North", "A", 100, 10},
             {"North", "B", 200, 20},
             {"South", "A", 150, 15},
             {"South", "B", 250, 25}
        });
  
    // +--------+---------+-------+----------+
    // | region | product | sales | quantity |
    // +--------+---------+-------+----------+
    // | North  | A       | 100   | 10       |
    // | North  | B       | 200   | 20       |
    // | South  | A       | 150   | 15       |
    // | South  | B       | 250   | 25       |
    // +--------+---------+-------+----------+
  
    Function<DisposableObjArray, Double> rowMapper = row -> (Integer) row.get(0) * 1.1;  // transforms sales with a 10% markup
  
    Sheet<String, String, Double> pivotResult = dataset.pivot(
        "region",                                                                                               // "region" is the row identifier
        "product",                                                                                              // "product" is the column identifier
        Arrays.asList("sales", "quantity"),                                                                     // "sales" and "quantity" are the aggregate columns
        rowMapper,                                                                                              // transforms each row value
        Collectors.collectingAndThen(Collectors.summingDouble(Double::doubleValue), r -> Numbers.round(r, 2))); // collects aggregated values
    //         +-------+-------+
    //         | A     | B     |
    // +-------+-------+-------+
    // | North | 110.0 | 220.0 |
    // | South | 165.0 | 275.0 |
    // +-------+-------+-------+
  ```
- **See also:** #pivot(String, String, String, Collector), #pivot(String, String, Collection, Collector), #groupBy(Collection), #rollup(Collection), #cube(Collection), Difference between groupby and pivot_table for pandas dataframes (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/34702815)
##### sortBy(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `void sortBy(String columnName) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, ClassCastException`
- **Summary:** Sorts the Dataset based on the specified column name.
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used for sorting.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the dataset is frozen.
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; the sorting algorithm detects an ordering that violates the comparator contract.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if compared non-null cell values or extracted keys are not mutually comparable under the selected ordering.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset employees = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("name", "age", "salary"), new Object[][] { { "Alice", 25, 50000.0 }, { "Bob", 30, 60000.0 } });
    employees.sortBy("age");   // sorts by age in ascending order
  ```
- **Signature:** `void sortBy(String columnName, Comparator<?> cmp) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, ClassCastException, NullPointerException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Sorts the Dataset based on the specified column name using the provided Comparator.
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used for sorting.
  - `cmp` (`Comparator<?>`) — the Comparator to determine the order of the elements.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the dataset is frozen.
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; `cmp` is null; the sorting algorithm detects an ordering that violates the comparator contract.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if compared non-null cell values or extracted keys are not mutually comparable under the selected ordering.
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if a comparison is reached with a null value and the supplied comparator does not support it.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the supplied comparator throws when invoked to determine row order.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name"), new Object[][] {{2, "Bob"}, {1, "Alice"}});
    dataset.sortBy("id", Comparator.reverseOrder());  // sorts in place by id in descending order
  ```
- **Signature:** `void sortBy(Collection<String> columnNames) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, ClassCastException`
- **Summary:** Sorts the Dataset based on the specified collection of column names.
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the collection of column names to be used for sorting.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the dataset is frozen.
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; `columnNames` is null, contains duplicate names, or is empty while the dataset has columns; the sorting algorithm detects an ordering that violates the comparator contract.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if compared non-null cell values or extracted keys are not mutually comparable under the selected ordering.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("department", "name"), new Object[][] {{"Sales", "Bob"}, {"IT", "Alice"}});
    dataset.sortBy(Arrays.asList("department", "name"));  // sorts in place by department, then by name
  ```
- **Signature:** `void sortBy(Collection<String> columnNames, Comparator<? super Object[]> cmp) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, ClassCastException, NullPointerException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Sorts the Dataset based on the specified collection of column names using the provided Comparator.
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the collection of column names to be used for sorting.
  - `cmp` (`Comparator<? super Object[]>`) — the Comparator to determine the order of the elements. It compares Object arrays, each representing a row.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the dataset is frozen.
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; `columnNames` is null, contains duplicate names, or is empty while the dataset has columns; `cmp` is null; the sorting algorithm detects an ordering that violates the comparator contract.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if compared non-null cell values or extracted keys are not mutually comparable under the selected ordering.
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if a comparison is reached with a null value and the supplied comparator does not support it.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the supplied comparator throws when invoked to determine row order.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name"), new Object[][] {{2, "Bob"}, {1, "Alice"}});
    // Sort by id in descending order, comparing the first element of each row array
    dataset.sortBy(Arrays.asList("id", "name"),
        (a, b) -> Integer.compare((Integer)b[0], (Integer)a[0]));  // sorts in place with custom comparator
  ```
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("rawtypes") void sortBy(Collection<String> columnNames, Function<? super DisposableObjArray, ? extends Comparable> keyExtractor) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Sorts the Dataset based on the specified column names and a key mapper function.
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the names of the columns to be used for sorting. The order of the column names determines the order of the elements in the DisposableObjArray passed to the key mapper function.
  - `keyExtractor` (`Function<? super DisposableObjArray, ? extends Comparable>`) — a function that takes a DisposableObjArray representing a row of the Dataset and returns a Comparable object that is used for sorting.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the dataset is frozen.
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; `columnNames` is null, contains duplicate names, or is empty while the dataset has columns; `keyExtractor` is null; the sorting algorithm detects an ordering that violates the comparator contract.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if compared non-null cell values or extracted keys are not mutually comparable under the selected ordering.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the supplied key extractor throws when invoked to determine row order.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("firstName", "lastName"),
        new Object[][] {
            {"John", "Smith"},
            {"Jane", "Doe"},
            {"Bob", "Anderson"}
        });
    // Sort by concatenated full name (case-insensitive)
    dataset.sortBy(Arrays.asList("firstName", "lastName"),
        row -> ((String)row.get(0) + " " + (String)row.get(1)).toLowerCase());  // sorts in place by full name
  ```

##### topBy(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `Dataset topBy(String columnName, int n) throws IllegalArgumentException, ClassCastException`
- **Summary:** Returns the top n rows from the Dataset based on the values in the specified column.
- **Contract:**
  - If the Dataset contains fewer than n rows, all rows are returned.
  - When more rows tie at the cut-off than there is room for, the earliest of them are kept.
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used for determining the top rows.
  - `n` (`int`) — the number of top rows to return.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset containing the top n rows.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; `n < 1`.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if compared non-null cell values or extracted keys are not mutually comparable under the selected ordering and `n < size()`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset employees = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("name", "salary", "age"), data);
    Dataset topPaid = employees.topBy("salary", 5);   // keeps top 5 highest salaries
  ```
- **Signature:** `Dataset topBy(String columnName, int n, Comparator<?> cmp) throws IllegalArgumentException, ClassCastException, NullPointerException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Returns the top n rows from the Dataset based on the values in the specified column, as ranked by the provided Comparator.
- **Contract:**
  - If the Dataset contains fewer than n rows, all rows are returned.
  - When more rows tie at the cut-off than there is room for, the earliest of them are kept.
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used for determining the top rows.
  - `n` (`int`) — the number of top rows to return.
  - `cmp` (`Comparator<?>`) — the Comparator used to rank the column values; rows with the greatest values according to this Comparator are kept.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset containing the top n rows.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; `cmp` is null; `n < 1`.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if compared non-null cell values or extracted keys are not mutually comparable under the selected ordering and `n < size()`.
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if a comparison is reached with a null value and the supplied comparator does not support it.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the supplied comparator throws when invoked to select the top rows.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "score"), new Object[][] {{1, 85}, {2, 95}, {3, 90}});
    // With reverseOrder, the "greatest" values per the comparator are the smallest scores
    Dataset bottom = dataset.topBy("score", 2, Comparator.reverseOrder());  // keeps rows {1, 85} and {3, 90}
  ```
- **Signature:** `Dataset topBy(Collection<String> columnNames, int n) throws IllegalArgumentException, ClassCastException`
- **Summary:** Returns the top n rows from the Dataset based on the values in the specified columns.
- **Contract:**
  - If the Dataset contains fewer than n rows, all rows are returned.
  - When more rows tie at the cut-off than there is room for, the earliest of them are kept.
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the names of the columns to be used for determining the top rows.
  - `n` (`int`) — the number of top rows to return.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset containing the top n rows.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; `columnNames` is null, contains duplicate names, or is empty while the dataset has columns; `n < 1`.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if compared non-null cell values or extracted keys are not mutually comparable under the selected ordering and `n < size()`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset employees = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("name", "level", "salary"), data);
    Dataset top = employees.topBy(Arrays.asList("level", "salary"), 5);   // keeps the 5 highest (level, salary) pairs
  ```
- **Signature:** `Dataset topBy(Collection<String> columnNames, int n, Comparator<? super Object[]> cmp) throws IllegalArgumentException, ClassCastException, NullPointerException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Returns the top n rows from the Dataset based on the values in the specified columns, as ranked by the provided Comparator.
- **Contract:**
  - If the Dataset contains fewer than n rows, all rows are returned.
  - When more rows tie at the cut-off than there is room for, the earliest of them are kept.
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the names of the columns to be used for determining the top rows.
  - `n` (`int`) — the number of top rows to return.
  - `cmp` (`Comparator<? super Object[]>`) — the Comparator used to rank the rows; it compares Object arrays, each representing the specified columns of a row. Rows with the greatest values are kept.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset containing the top n rows.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; `columnNames` is null, contains duplicate names, or is empty while the dataset has columns; `cmp` is null; `n < 1`.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if compared non-null cell values or extracted keys are not mutually comparable under the selected ordering and `n < size()`.
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if a comparison is reached with a null value and the supplied comparator does not support it.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the supplied comparator throws when invoked to select the top rows.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset employees = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("name", "salary"), data);
    // Rank by salary only, so the 5 lowest-paid rows are the "greatest" per this Comparator
    Dataset bottom = employees.topBy(Arrays.asList("name", "salary"), 5,
        (a, b) -> Integer.compare((Integer) b[1], (Integer) a[1]));
  ```
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("rawtypes") Dataset topBy(Collection<String> columnNames, int n, Function<? super DisposableObjArray, ? extends Comparable> keyExtractor) throws IllegalArgumentException, ClassCastException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Returns the top n rows from the Dataset based on the Comparable keys derived from the specified columns by the provided keyExtractor function.
- **Contract:**
  - If the Dataset contains fewer than n rows, all rows are returned.
  - When more rows tie at the cut-off than there is room for, the earliest of them are kept.
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the names of the columns to be used for determining the top rows.
  - `n` (`int`) — the number of top rows to return.
  - `keyExtractor` (`Function<? super DisposableObjArray, ? extends Comparable>`) — the function that maps a row to a Comparable key used for ranking. It takes a DisposableObjArray representing the specified columns of a row and returns a Comparable.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset containing the top n rows.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; `columnNames` is null, contains duplicate names, or is empty while the dataset has columns; `keyExtractor` is null; `n < 1`.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if compared non-null cell values or extracted keys are not mutually comparable under the selected ordering and `n < size()`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the supplied key extractor throws when invoked to select the top rows.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset employees = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("name", "salary", "bonus"), data);
    // Keep the 5 rows with the highest salary + bonus
    Dataset top = employees.topBy(Arrays.asList("salary", "bonus"), 5,
        row -> (Integer) row.get(0) + (Integer) row.get(1));
  ```
##### distinct(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `@Beta Dataset distinct()`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Returns a new Dataset containing only the distinct rows from the original Dataset.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a new Dataset containing only distinct rows.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset orders = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("product", "customer"), new Object[][] { { "widget", "Acme" }, { "gadget", "Globex" } });
    Dataset uniqueOrders = orders.distinct();   // removes duplicate rows
  ```
- **See also:** #distinctBy(String), #distinctBy(Collection), #removeDuplicateRowsBy(String), #removeDuplicateRowsBy(Collection)
##### distinctBy(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `Dataset distinctBy(String columnName) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a new Dataset containing only the distinct rows based on the specified column from the original Dataset.
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used for determining distinctness.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset containing only distinct rows based on the specified column.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset employees = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("name", "department", "salary"),
            new Object[][] { { "Alice", "Sales", 50000.0 }, { "Bob", "Engineering", 60000.0 } });
    Dataset uniqueDepts = employees.distinctBy("department");   // keeps one row per department
  ```
- **See also:** #removeDuplicateRowsBy(String), #removeDuplicateRowsBy(Collection)
- **Signature:** `Dataset distinctBy(String columnName, Function<?, ?> keyExtractor) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Returns a new Dataset containing only the distinct rows based on the specified column from the original Dataset.
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used for determining distinctness.
  - `keyExtractor` (`Function<?, ?>`) — a function to process the column values before determining distinctness.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset containing only distinct rows based on the specified column and keyExtractor function.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; `keyExtractor` is null.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if `keyExtractor` throws while computing a row key.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset employees = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("name", "email"),
        new Object[][] {
            {"alice", "ALICE@example.com"},
            {"bob", "bob@example.com"},
            {"Alice", "alice@example.com"}
        });
    // Get distinct rows by email, case-insensitive
    Dataset uniqueEmails = employees.distinctBy("email", (String email) -> email.toLowerCase());
    // Result: two rows (alice@example.com appears twice but is treated as one when lowercased)
  ```
- **See also:** #removeDuplicateRowsBy(String, Function), #removeDuplicateRowsBy(Collection, Function)
- **Signature:** `Dataset distinctBy(Collection<String> columnNames) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a new Dataset containing only the distinct rows based on the specified columns from the original Dataset.
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the names of the columns to be used for determining distinctness.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset containing only distinct rows based on the specified columns.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; `columnNames` is null, contains duplicate names, or is empty while the dataset has columns.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name"), new Object[][] {{1, "Alice"}, {1, "Alice"}});
    Dataset distinct = dataset.distinctBy(Arrays.asList("id"));
  ```
- **See also:** #distinctBy(Collection, Function), #removeDuplicateRowsBy(Collection), #removeDuplicateRowsBy(Collection, Function)
- **Signature:** `Dataset distinctBy(Collection<String> columnNames, Function<? super DisposableObjArray, ?> keyExtractor) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Returns a new Dataset containing only the distinct rows based on the specified columns from the original Dataset.
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the names of the columns to be used for determining distinctness.
  - `keyExtractor` (`Function<? super DisposableObjArray, ?>`) — a function to process the column values before determining distinctness.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset containing only distinct rows based on the specified columns and keyExtractor function.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; `columnNames` is null, contains duplicate names, or is empty while the dataset has columns; `keyExtractor` is null.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if `keyExtractor` throws while computing a row key.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset employees = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("firstName", "lastName", "email"),
        new Object[][] {
            {"John", "Smith", "john.smith@example.com"},
            {"JOHN", "SMITH", "different@example.com"},
            {"Jane", "Doe", "jane.doe@example.com"}
        });
    // Get distinct rows by first and last name, case-insensitive
    Dataset uniqueNames = employees.distinctBy(Arrays.asList("firstName", "lastName"),
        row -> ((String)row.get(0) + " " + (String)row.get(1)).toLowerCase());
    // Result: two rows (John Smith appears twice with different cases, but is treated as one)
  ```
- **See also:** #removeDuplicateRowsBy(String, Function), #removeDuplicateRowsBy(Collection, Function)
##### filter(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `Dataset filter(Predicate<? super DisposableObjArray> filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Filters the rows of the Dataset based on the provided predicate.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Predicate<? super DisposableObjArray>`) — the predicate to apply to each row. It takes an instance of DisposableObjArray, which represents a row in the Dataset.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset containing only the rows that satisfy the provided predicate.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if `filter` throws an unchecked exception while evaluating a row.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset employees = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("name", "age", "salary"),
        new Object[][] {
            {"Alice", 25, 50000},
            {"Bob", 35, 80000},
            {"Charlie", 28, 60000}
        });
    // Filter employees with salary > 55000
    Dataset highEarners = employees.filter(row -> (Integer)row.get(2) > 55000);
    // Result contains: Bob and Charlie
  ```
- **Signature:** `Dataset filter(Predicate<? super DisposableObjArray> filter, int max) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Filters the rows of the Dataset based on the provided predicate and limits the number of results.
- **Parameters:**
  - `filter` (`Predicate<? super DisposableObjArray>`) — the predicate to apply to each row. It takes an instance of DisposableObjArray, which represents a row in the Dataset.
  - `max` (`int`) — the maximum number of rows to include in the returned Dataset.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset containing only the rows that satisfy the provided predicate, up to the specified maximum limit.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is `null`, or `max < 0`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if `filter` throws an unchecked exception while evaluating a row.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset employees = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("name", "age", "salary"), data);
    // Get first 5 employees with salary > 50000
    Dataset topEarners = employees.filter(row -> (Integer)row.get(2) > 50000, 5);
  ```

- **Summary:** Filters the rows of the Dataset based on the provided predicate and within the specified row index range.
- **Parameters:**

  - `toRowIndex` (`int`) — the ending index of the row range (exclusive).
  - `filter` (`Predicate<? super DisposableObjArray>`) — the predicate to apply to each row within the specified range. It takes an instance of DisposableObjArray, which represents a row in the Dataset.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset containing only the rows within the specified range that satisfy the provided predicate.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `fromRowIndex < 0`, `fromRowIndex > toRowIndex`, or `toRowIndex > size()`.
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if `filter` throws an unchecked exception while evaluating a row.
- **Examples:**

##### mapColumn(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `Dataset mapColumn(String fromColumnName, String newColumnName, String copyingColumnName, Function<?, ?> mapper) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Transforms the Dataset by applying a mapping function to the specified column and creating a new column with the results.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fromColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used as input for the mapping function.
  - `newColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the new column that will store the results of the mapping function. Must not be `null` or empty, and must not be one of the copied columns.
  - `copyingColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be copied to the new Dataset. Must not be `null`.
  - `mapper` (`Function<?, ?>`) — the mapping function to apply to each row of the specified column. It takes an instance of the column's value and returns a new value.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset with the new column added and the specified column copied.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapper` is `null`, `newColumnName` is null or empty, the new name duplicates a copied column, or a source or copied column does not exist.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if `mapper` throws an unchecked exception while mapping a row.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset employees = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("name", "salary"), new Object[][] {{"Alice", 50000.0}});
    Dataset result = employees.mapColumn("salary", "bonus", "name", salary -> (Double) salary * 0.1);
    // Result columns: name, bonus
  ```

  - `mapper` (`Function<?, ?>`) — the mapping function to apply to each row of the specified column. It takes an instance of the column's value and returns a new value.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset with the new column added and the specified columns copied.

  ```java
  Dataset ds = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "a", "b", "c"), new Object[][] {{1, "x", "y", "z"}});
    Dataset result = ds.flatMapColumns(Tuple.of("a", "b", "c"), "value", Arrays.asList("id"),
        (a, b, c) -> Arrays.asList(a, b, c));

  ```
- **Signature:** `Dataset flatMapColumns(Collection<String> fromColumnNames, String newColumnName, Collection<String> copyingColumnNames, Function<? super DisposableObjArray, ? extends Collection<?>> mapper) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Transforms the Dataset by applying a mapping function to the specified columns and creating new rows with the results.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fromColumnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — a collection of column names to be used as input for the mapping function.
  - `newColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the new column that will store the results of the mapping function. Must not be `null` or empty, and must not be one of the copied columns.
  - `copyingColumnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — a collection of column names to be copied to the new Dataset. May be `null` or empty, in which case the result holds only the new column.
  - `mapper` (`Function<? super DisposableObjArray, ? extends Collection<?>>`) — the mapping function to apply to each row of the specified columns. It takes an instance of DisposableObjArray, which represents the values in the Dataset's row for the specified columns, and returns a Collection of new rows. Rows for which the mapper returns `null` or an empty Collection contribute no rows to the result.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset with the new rows added and the specified columns copied.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapper` is `null`, `newColumnName` is null or empty, the new name duplicates a copied column, or a source or copied column does not exist, or `fromColumnNames` is `null`, is empty while this Dataset has columns, contains an unknown column name, or selects the same column more than once, or `copyingColumnNames` selects the same column more than once.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if `mapper` throws an unchecked exception while mapping a row.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset ds = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "a", "b"), new Object[][] {{1, "x", "y"}});
    Dataset result = ds.flatMapColumns(Arrays.asList("a", "b"), "value", Arrays.asList("id"),
        row -> Arrays.asList(row.get(0), row.get(1)));
    // Result columns: id, value; result rows: {1, "x"}, {1, "y"}
  ```
##### innerJoin(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `Dataset innerJoin(Dataset right, String columnName, String joinColumnNameOnRight) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Performs an inner join operation between this Dataset and another Dataset based on the specified column names.

- **Throws:**

- **Signature:** `Dataset innerJoin(Dataset right, Map<String, String> onColumnNames, String newColumnName, Class<?> newColumnType) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Performs an inner join operation between this Dataset and another Dataset based on the specified column names.

- **Parameters:**
  - `right` (`Dataset`) — the Dataset to join with.
  - `onColumnNames` (`Map<String, String>`) — a map where the key is the column name in this Dataset and the value is the column name in the right Dataset to join on. Must not be `null` or empty.
  - `newColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the new column to be added to the resulting Dataset.

  - `collSupplier` (`IntFunction<? extends Collection>`) — a function that generates a collection to hold the joined rows for the new column for one-many or many-many mapping.

  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `right` is `null` or a join column is absent from its corresponding Dataset, or `onColumnNames` is null or empty, or `newColumnName` is null, empty, or already present in this Dataset, or `newColumnType` is null or is not an object-array, collection, map, or bean type, or `collSupplier` is null or returns null for a group.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the collection supplier throws an unchecked exception, its result rejects a joined row, or a right-hand row cannot be constructed or populated as `newColumnType`.
- **Examples:**

  ```java
    Dataset right = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "score"), new Object[][] {{1, 95}, {3, 85}});
    Dataset joined = left.fullJoin(right, N.asMap("id", "id"), "joinData", Map.class);
    // Result includes all rows from both datasets with joined data in joinData column
  ```
- **See also:** What is the difference between "INNER JOIN" and "OUTER JOIN" (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/38549)
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("rawtypes") Dataset fullJoin(Dataset right, Map<String, String> onColumnNames, String newColumnName, Class<?> newColumnType, IntFunction<? extends Collection> collSupplier) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Performs a full join operation between this Dataset and another Dataset based on the specified column names.
- **Contract:**
  - If there is no match, the result is `null` on the side of the Dataset that does not have a match.
- **Parameters:**
  - `right` (`Dataset`) — the other Dataset to join with.
  - `onColumnNames` (`Map<String, String>`) — a map where the key is the column name in this Dataset to join on, and the value is the column name in the other Dataset to join on. Must not be `null` or empty.
  - `newColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the new column to be added to the resulting Dataset.
  - `newColumnType` (`Class<?>`) — the type of each right-hand row stored in the new column's collection. It must be Object\[\], Collection, Map, or Bean class.
  - `collSupplier` (`IntFunction<? extends Collection>`) — a function that generates a collection to hold the joined rows for the new column for one-many or many-many mapping.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset that is the result of the full join operation.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `right` is `null` or a join column is absent from its corresponding Dataset, or `onColumnNames` is null or empty, or `newColumnName` is null, empty, or already present in this Dataset, or `newColumnType` is null or is not an object-array, collection, map, or bean type, or `collSupplier` is null or returns null for a group.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the collection supplier throws an unchecked exception, its result rejects a joined row, or a right-hand row cannot be constructed or populated as `newColumnType`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset left = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name"), new Object[][] {{1, "Alice"}, {2, "Bob"}});
    Dataset right = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "score"), new Object[][] {{1, 95}, {1, 88}, {3, 70}});
    Dataset joined = left.fullJoin(right, N.asMap("id", "id"), "scores", Map.class, size -> new ArrayList<>(size));
    // The "scores" cell of the id = 1 row holds a List with both matching right rows; ids 2 and 3 are kept with nulls
  ```
- **See also:** What is the difference between "INNER JOIN" and "OUTER JOIN" (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/38549)

##### cartesianProduct(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `Dataset cartesianProduct(Dataset other) throws IllegalArgumentException, ArithmeticException`
- **Summary:** Performs a cartesian product operation with this Dataset and another Dataset.
- **Contract:**
  - The resulting Dataset will have the combined columns of both Datasets, so the two Datasets must not share any column names.
  - For example, if this Dataset has 3 rows and the other Dataset has 2 rows, the resulting Dataset will have 6 rows (3 × 2).
- **Parameters:**
  - `other` (`Dataset`) — the Dataset to perform the cartesian product with.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset that is the result of the cartesian product operation.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `other` is `null`, or the Datasets share a column name.
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if `size() * other.size()` exceeds Integer#MAX_VALUE.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset1 = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name"),
        new Object[][] {
             {1, "Alice"},
             {2, "Bob"}
        });
    Dataset dataset2 = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("category", "score"),
        new Object[][] {
             {"A", 95},
             {"B", 90}
        });
  
    Dataset result = dataset1.cartesianProduct(dataset2);
    // Result contains columns: id, name, category, score
    // Result contains: {1, "Alice", "A", 95}, {1, "Alice", "B", 90},
    //                  {2, "Bob", "A", 95}, {2, "Bob", "B", 90}
  ```
- **See also:** #merge(Dataset), #innerJoin(Dataset, String, String), #leftJoin(Dataset, String, String), #union(Dataset)

- **Returns:** a Stream of Datasets, each containing chunkSize rows from the original Dataset, or an empty Stream if this Dataset is empty.
- **Throws:**

- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id"), new Object[][] {{1}, {2}, {3}});
    Stream<Dataset> parts = dataset.split(2);
  ```

##### slice(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `Dataset slice(int fromRowIndex, int toRowIndex) throws IndexOutOfBoundsException`
- **Summary:** Returns an immutable slice of this Dataset from the specified fromRowIndex to toRowIndex.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fromRowIndex` (`int`) — the starting index of the slice, inclusive.
  - `toRowIndex` (`int`) — the ending index of the slice, exclusive.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset containing the rows from fromRowIndex to toRowIndex from the original Dataset.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `fromRowIndex < 0`, `fromRowIndex > toRowIndex`, or `toRowIndex > size()`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name"), new Object[][] {{1, "Alice"}, {2, "Bob"}});
    Dataset slice = dataset.slice(0, 1);
  ```
- **See also:** List#subList(int, int)
- **Signature:** `Dataset slice(Collection<String> columnNames) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns an immutable slice of this Dataset that includes only the columns specified in the columnNames collection from the original Dataset.
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the collection of column names to be included in the sliced Dataset. If null or empty, the row range must also be empty.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset containing the same rows as the original Dataset, but only the columns specified in the columnNames collection.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the selection contains an unknown or duplicate column name, or `columnNames` is null or empty and the selected row range is nonempty.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name", "age"), new Object[][] {{1, "Alice", 25}, {2, "Bob", 30}});
    Dataset slice = dataset.slice(Arrays.asList("id", "name"));
  ```
- **See also:** List#subList(int, int)
- **Signature:** `Dataset slice(int fromRowIndex, int toRowIndex, Collection<String> columnNames) throws IndexOutOfBoundsException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns an immutable slice of this Dataset from the specified fromRowIndex to toRowIndex and only includes the columns specified in the columnNames collection.
- **Parameters:**

  - `toRowIndex` (`int`) — the ending index of the slice, exclusive.

- **Returns:** a new Dataset containing the rows from fromRowIndex to toRowIndex from the original Dataset, but only the columns specified in the columnNames collection.
- **Throws:**

  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the selection contains an unknown or duplicate column name, or `columnNames` is null or empty and the selected row range is nonempty.

- **Signature:** `<T> Stream<T> stream(IntObjFunction<? super DisposableObjArray, ? extends T> rowMapper) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a Stream of objects of type `T` by applying the provided rowMapper function to each row in the Dataset.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: The row mapper is invoked when a row is materialized from the returned stream.
  - The returned stream checks for dataset modifications during traversal and throws java.util.ConcurrentModificationException if it detects an invalidating change.
- **Parameters:**
  - `rowMapper` (`IntObjFunction<? super DisposableObjArray, ? extends T>`) — a function that takes an integer and a DisposableObjArray as input and produces an object of type T. The integer represents the index of the row in the Dataset, and the DisposableObjArray represents the row itself.
- **Returns:** a Stream of objects of type T, created by applying the rowMapper function to each row in the Dataset.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `rowMapper` is null.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset employees = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("name", "age", "salary"), new Object[][] { { "Alice", 25, 50000.0 }, { "Bob", 30, 60000.0 } });
    Stream<String> summaries = employees.stream((rowIndex, row) ->
        row.get(0) + " is " + row.get(1) + " years old"
    );
  ```

- **Summary:** Creates a Stream of type T from the Dataset using the specified column names and a row mapper function.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: The row mapper is invoked when a row is materialized from the returned stream.
  - The returned stream checks for dataset modifications during traversal and throws java.util.ConcurrentModificationException if it detects an invalidating change.

  - `columnNames` (`Tuple2<String, String>`) — a Tuple2 containing the names of the two columns to be used

  ```java
        (first, last) -> first + " " + last
    );
  ```

##### apply(...) -> R
- **Signature:** `<R, E extends Exception> R apply(Throwables.Function<? super Dataset, ? extends R, E> func) throws IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Summary:** Applies the provided function to this Dataset and returns the result.
- **Parameters:**
  - `func` (`Throwables.Function<? super Dataset, ? extends R, E>`) — the function to apply to the Dataset. This function should take a Dataset as input and return a result of type R.
- **Returns:** the result of applying the provided function to the Dataset.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `func` is `null`.
  - `E` — if `func` throws an exception when invoked.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id"), new Object[][] {{1}});
    int count = dataset.apply(Dataset::columnCount);
  ```
##### applyIfNotEmpty(...) -> Optional<R>
- **Signature:** `<R, E extends Exception> Optional<R> applyIfNotEmpty(Throwables.Function<? super Dataset, ? extends R, E> func) throws IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Summary:** Applies the provided function to this Dataset if it is not empty and returns the result wrapped in an Optional.
- **Contract:**
  - If the Dataset is empty, it returns an empty Optional.
- **Parameters:**
  - `func` (`Throwables.Function<? super Dataset, ? extends R, E>`) — the function to apply to the Dataset. This function should take a Dataset as input and return a result of type R.
- **Returns:** an Optional containing the result of applying the provided function to the Dataset, or an empty Optional if the Dataset is empty.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `func` is `null`.
  - `E` — if `func` throws an exception when invoked for this nonempty Dataset.
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if the function returns `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id"), new Object[][] {{1}});
    Optional<Integer> maybeCount = dataset.applyIfNotEmpty(Dataset::size);
  ```
##### accept(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `<E extends Exception> void accept(Throwables.Consumer<? super Dataset, E> action) throws IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Summary:** Performs the provided action on this Dataset.
- **Parameters:**
  - `action` (`Throwables.Consumer<? super Dataset, E>`) — the action to be performed on the Dataset. This action should take a Dataset as input.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `action` is `null`.
  - `E` — if `action` throws an exception when invoked.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id"), new Object[][] {{1}});
    dataset.accept(ds -> System.out.println(ds.size()));
  ```
##### acceptIfNotEmpty(...) -> OrElse
- **Signature:** `<E extends Exception> OrElse acceptIfNotEmpty(Throwables.Consumer<? super Dataset, E> action) throws IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Summary:** Performs the provided action on this Dataset if it is not empty.
- **Contract:**
  - If the Dataset is empty, it does nothing and returns an instance of OrElse.
- **Parameters:**
  - `action` (`Throwables.Consumer<? super Dataset, E>`) — the action to be performed on the Dataset. This action should take a Dataset as input.
- **Returns:** an instance of OrElse, which can be used to perform an alternative action if the Dataset is empty.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `action` is `null`.
  - `E` — if `action` throws an exception when invoked for this nonempty Dataset.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id"), new Object[][] {{1}});
    dataset.acceptIfNotEmpty(Dataset::freeze).orElse(() -> System.out.println("empty"));
  ```
##### freeze(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `void freeze()`
- **Summary:** Freezes the Dataset to prevent further modification through its mutating API.
- **Contract:**
  - This method is useful when you want to ensure the Dataset remains constant after a certain point in your program.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset config = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("key", "value"), new Object[][] { { "k1", "v1" }, { "k2", "v2" } });
    config.freeze();   // stops further modifications
  ```
##### isFrozen(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `boolean isFrozen()`
- **Summary:** Checks if the Dataset is frozen.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** `true` if the Dataset is frozen and cannot be modified, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id"), new Object[][] {{1}});
    boolean locked = dataset.isFrozen();
  ```
##### clear(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `void clear() throws IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Clears the Dataset.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if this Dataset is frozen.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset tempData = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name"), new Object[][] { { 1, "Alice" }, { 2, "Bob" } });
    tempData.clear();   // removes all rows
  ```
##### isEmpty(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `boolean isEmpty()`
- **Summary:** Checks if the Dataset is empty.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** `true` if the Dataset is empty, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name"), new Object[][] { { 1, "Alice" }, { 2, "Bob" } });
    if (dataset.isEmpty()) {
       // handle empty Dataset
    }
  ```
##### trimToSize(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `void trimToSize()`
- **Summary:** Trims the size of the Dataset to its current size.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name", "age"), data);
    dataset.removeRows(100, 200);   // removes some rows
    dataset.trimToSize();           // memory is reclaimed
  
    // Can also be called on frozen datasets
    dataset.freeze();
    dataset.trimToSize();   // no change to content
  ```
- **See also:** #freeze(), #isFrozen()
##### size(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `int size()`
- **Summary:** Returns the number of rows in the Dataset.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the number of rows in the Dataset.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset employees = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("name", "age"), new Object[][] { { "Alice", 25 }, { "Bob", 30 } });
    int totalEmployees = employees.size();   // returns row count
  ```
- **See also:** #rowCount()
##### rowCount(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `default int rowCount()`
- **Summary:** Returns the number of rows in the Dataset.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the number of rows in the Dataset
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset employees = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("name", "age"), new Object[][] { { "Alice", 25 }, { "Bob", 30 } });
    int totalEmployees = employees.rowCount();   // same value as employees.size()
  ```
- **See also:** #size(), #columnCount()
##### getProperties(...) -> Map<String, Object>
- **Signature:** `@Beta Map<String, Object> getProperties()`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Retrieves the properties of the Dataset as a Map.
- **Contract:**
  - Because it is a view, the entries #append(Dataset), #prepend(Dataset) and the `merge` family add in place do show up in a view obtained earlier - but only when this Dataset already had at least one property.
  - An empty Map is returned when no property has been set.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a read-only Map containing the properties of the Dataset.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id"), new Object[][] {{1}});
    Map<String, Object> props = dataset.getProperties();
  ```
- **See also:** #setProperties(Map)
##### setProperties(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@Beta void setProperties(final Map<String, ?> properties) throws IllegalStateException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Sets the properties of the Dataset.
- **Parameters:**
  - `properties` (`Map<String, ?>`) — a Map containing the properties to set on the Dataset.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if this Dataset is frozen.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id"), new Object[][] {{1}});
    Map<String, Object> newProps = new HashMap<>();
    newProps.put("source", "generated");
    newProps.put("version", 1);
    dataset.setProperties(newProps);
  ```
##### withMissingPropertyPolicy(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `Dataset withMissingPropertyPolicy(MissingPropertyPolicy policy) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a frozen, backed view whose bean conversions use the specified missing-property policy.
- **Parameters:**
  - `policy` (`MissingPropertyPolicy`) — the policy for unmatched bean properties; must not be null
- **Returns:** a new read-only view configured for bean conversion
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `policy` is `null`.
##### println(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `void println() throws RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Prints the content of the Dataset to the standard output.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a selected cell to text fails.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name", "age", "salary"), data);
    dataset.println();
  
    // +----+---------+-----+---------+
    // | id | name    | age | salary  |
    // +----+---------+-----+---------+
    // | 1  | John    | 25  | 50000.0 |
    // | 2  | Jane    | 30  | 60000.0 |
    // | 3  | Bob     | 35  | 70000.0 |
    // | 4  | Alice   | 28  | 55000.0 |
    // | 5  | Charlie | 40  | 80000.0 |
    // +----+---------+-----+---------+
  ```
- **See also:** #println(String)
- **Signature:** `void println(String prefix) throws RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Prints the content of the Dataset to the standard output.
- **Parameters:**
  - `prefix` (`String`) — the prefix string to be printed before each line of the Dataset output
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a selected cell to text fails.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name", "age", "salary"), data);
    dataset.println("## ");   // prints entire Dataset to console with prefix "## "
  
    // ## +----+---------+-----+---------+
    // ## | id | name    | age | salary  |
    // ## +----+---------+-----+---------+
    // ## | 1  | John    | 25  | 50000.0 |
    // ## | 2  | Jane    | 30  | 60000.0 |
    // ## | 3  | Bob     | 35  | 70000.0 |
    // ## | 4  | Alice   | 28  | 55000.0 |
    // ## | 5  | Charlie | 40  | 80000.0 |
    // ## +----+---------+-----+---------+
  ```
- **See also:** #println()
- **Signature:** `void println(int fromRowIndex, int toRowIndex) throws IndexOutOfBoundsException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Prints a portion of the Dataset to the standard output.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fromRowIndex` (`int`) — the starting index of the row range (inclusive).
  - `toRowIndex` (`int`) — the ending index of the row range (exclusive).
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `fromRowIndex < 0`, `fromRowIndex > toRowIndex`, or `toRowIndex > size()`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a selected cell to text fails.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name"), data);
    dataset.println(0, 10);   // prints first 10 rows to console
  ```
- **See also:** #println(), #println(String)
- **Signature:** `void println(int fromRowIndex, int toRowIndex, Collection<String> columnNames) throws IndexOutOfBoundsException, IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Prints a portion of the Dataset to the standard output.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fromRowIndex` (`int`) — the starting index of the row range (inclusive).
  - `toRowIndex` (`int`) — the ending index of the row range (exclusive).
  - `columnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the collection of column names to be printed; if `null` or empty, no columns are printed
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `fromRowIndex < 0`, `fromRowIndex > toRowIndex`, or `toRowIndex > size()`.
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a nonempty `columnNames` selection contains an unknown or duplicate column name.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a selected cell to text fails.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name", "age"), data);
    dataset.println(0, 5, Arrays.asList("id", "name"));   // prints first 5 rows, only id and name columns
  ```
- **See also:** #println(), #println(String)
- **Signature:** `void println(Appendable output) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Prints the Dataset to the provided Appendable.
- **Parameters:**
  - `output` (`Appendable`) — the appendable where the Dataset will be printed
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `output` is `null`.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if appending the formatted table to `output`, or flushing a writer, throws an java.io.IOException.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a selected cell to text fails, or the supplied output throws an unchecked exception while appending.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name"), new Object[][] { { 1, "Alice" }, { 2, "Bob" } });
    StringWriter writer = new StringWriter();
    dataset.println(writer);   // prints Dataset to StringWriter
  ```
- **See also:** #println(), #println(String)
