##### append(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public static void append(final byte[] bytes, final File targetFile) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Appends the given byte array to the specified file.
- **Contract:**
  - If the file exists, data will be appended.
  - If the file's parent directory doesn't exist, it will be created.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bytes` (`byte[]`) — the byte array to append to the file.
  - `targetFile` (`File`) — the file to which the byte array will be appended. If the file exists, the content will be appended to it. If the file's parent directory doesn't exist, it will be created.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetFile` is `null`.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if opening `targetFile` for append or writing the appended data fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  byte[] data = "Additional data\n".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    File file = new File("log.txt");
    IOUtil.append(data, file);  // Appends to existing file
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static void append(final byte[] bytes, final int offset, final int count, final File targetFile) throws IllegalArgumentException, IndexOutOfBoundsException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Appends a portion of a byte array to the specified file.
- **Contract:**
  - If the file exists, data will be appended.
  - If the file's parent directory doesn't exist, it will be created.
- **Parameters:**
  - `bytes` (`byte[]`) — the byte array to append to the file.
  - `offset` (`int`) — the starting index from where to append the bytes.
  - `count` (`int`) — the number of bytes to append from the byte array.
  - `targetFile` (`File`) — the file to which the byte array will be appended. If the file exists, the content will be appended to it. If the file's parent directory doesn't exist, it will be created.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `offset` or `count` is negative, or if `targetFile` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `offset` exceeds the input length or `count` exceeds the number of elements remaining after `offset`; a `null` input has length zero.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if opening `targetFile` for append or writing the appended data fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  byte[] data = "Hello, World!".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    File file = new File("log.txt");
    IOUtil.append(data, 7, 5, file);  // Appends "World"
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static void append(final char[] chars, final File targetFile) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Appends the given character array to the specified file using the default charset.
- **Contract:**
  - If the file exists, data will be appended.
  - If the file's parent directory doesn't exist, it will be created.
- **Parameters:**
  - `chars` (`char[]`) — the character array to append to the file.
  - `targetFile` (`File`) — the file to which the character array will be appended. If the file exists, the content will be appended to it. If the file's parent directory doesn't exist, it will be created.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetFile` is `null`.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if opening `targetFile` for append or writing the appended data fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  char[] chars = "Additional text\n".toCharArray();
    File file = new File("log.txt");
    IOUtil.append(chars, file);
  ```

  ```java
  char[] chars = "Additional text\n".toCharArray();

    IOUtil.append(chars, StandardCharsets.UTF_8, file);
  ```
- **See also:** #charsToBytes(char\[\], Charset)
- **Signature:** `public static void append(final char[] chars, final int offset, final int count, final File targetFile) throws IllegalArgumentException, IndexOutOfBoundsException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Appends the content of the character array to the target file using the default charset.
- **Contract:**
  - If the file exists, data will be appended.
  - If the file's parent directory doesn't exist, it will be created.
- **Parameters:**
  - `chars` (`char[]`) — the character array to append to the file.
  - `offset` (`int`) — the initial offset in the character array.
  - `count` (`int`) — the number of characters to append.
  - `targetFile` (`File`) — the file to which the character array will be appended, must not be `null`. If the file exists, the content will be appended to it. If the file's parent directory doesn't exist, it will be created.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `offset` or `count` is negative, or if `targetFile` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `offset` exceeds the input length or `count` exceeds the number of elements remaining after `offset`; a `null` input has length zero. The range is validated before the target is created or opened, so a bad range never leaves a freshly created empty file behind.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if opening `targetFile` for append or writing the appended data fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  char[] chars = "Hello, World!".toCharArray();
    File file = new File("log.txt");
    IOUtil.append(chars, 7, 5, file);  // Appends "World"
  ```
- **See also:** #charsToBytes(char\[\], int, int, Charset)
- **Signature:** `public static void append(final char[] chars, final int offset, final int count, final Charset charset, final File targetFile) throws IllegalArgumentException, IndexOutOfBoundsException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Appends the content of the character array to the target file.
- **Parameters:**
  - `chars` (`char[]`) — the character array to append to the file.
  - `offset` (`int`) — the initial offset in the character array.
  - `count` (`int`) — the number of characters to append.
  - `charset` (`Charset`) — the Charset to be used to encode the character array into a sequence of bytes, if `null` the default charset (UTF-8) is used.
  - `targetFile` (`File`) — the file to which the character array will be appended, must not be `null`. If the file exists, the content will be appended to it. If the file's parent directory doesn't exist, it will be created.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `offset` or `count` is negative, or if `targetFile` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `offset` exceeds the input length or `count` exceeds the number of elements remaining after `offset`; a `null` input has length zero. The range is validated before the target is created or opened, so a bad range never leaves a freshly created empty file behind.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if opening `targetFile` for append or writing the appended data fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File file = File.createTempFile("data", ".txt");                            // may throw IOException
    IOUtil.append("hello".toCharArray(), 0, 3, StandardCharsets.UTF_8, file);   // appends "hel"
    IOUtil.append("hello".toCharArray(), 2, 0, StandardCharsets.UTF_8, file);   // count 0: no-op
    String content = IOUtil.readAllToString(file);                              // returns "hel"
  ```
- **See also:** #charsToBytes(char\[\], int, int, Charset)

- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `source` or `targetFile` is `null`, or if `offset` or `count` is negative.

##### transfer(...) -> long
- **Signature:** `public static long transfer(final ReadableByteChannel src, final WritableByteChannel output) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Transfers bytes from a source channel to a target channel.
- **Contract:**
  - For a FileChannel source that is `size() - position()`, captured once when the call starts; for any other source it is "until end of input".
  - The buffered path has no promised size to measure against: it stops at end of input, or when the source repeatedly answers a read with no bytes at all, and returns what actually moved - so check the count against the source yourself when the source is not a `FileChannel`.
  - When both channels are FileChannels and the source reports a size, the transfer is delegated to FileChannel#transferFrom(ReadableByteChannel, long, long), which lets the operating system move the bytes without copying them through a user-space buffer.
- **Parameters:**
  - `src` (`ReadableByteChannel`) — the source channel from which bytes are to be read.
  - `output` (`WritableByteChannel`) — the target channel to which bytes are to be written.
- **Returns:** the number of bytes transferred, which is everything the source held unless it shrank during the call - or, on the buffered path, stopped making progress.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `src` or `output` is `null`.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if reading `src`, writing `output`, or accessing a file-channel position or size fails, or if, on the `FileChannel` path, neither channel can make progress before the whole source has been moved. On the buffered path a source that stops making progress ends the transfer with a short return value instead, and a destination that stops accepting bytes fails with an unchecked exception from the wrapping stream.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  try (ReadableByteChannel src = Channels.newChannel(new FileInputStream("src.dat"));
         WritableByteChannel dest = Channels.newChannel(new FileOutputStream("dest.dat"))) {
        long bytesTransferred = IOUtil.transfer(src, dest);
    }
  ```
##### skip(...) -> long
- **Signature:** `public static long skip(final InputStream input, final long bytesToSkip) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Skips over and discards a specified number of bytes from the input stream.
- **Contract:**
  - That difference is worth knowing when the source is a file: `skip(new FileInputStream(f), n)` seeks, but wrapping the same file in a java.io.BufferedInputStream first does not, because a buffered stream's own `skip` may delegate to a source that cannot seek and there is no way to tell from the outside.
  - Pass the unwrapped `FileInputStream` when the offset is large; buffer afterwards if you need to.
- **Parameters:**
  - `input` (`InputStream`) — the `InputStream` from which bytes are to be skipped, must not be `null`.
  - `bytesToSkip` (`long`) — the number of bytes to be skipped, must be >= 0.
- **Returns:** the actual number of bytes skipped, which may be less than `bytesToSkip` if the end of the stream is reached.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `input` is `null`, or if `bytesToSkip` is negative.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if skipping or reading from `input` to advance its position fails
- **Performance:** Cost: the seek path is O(1) - skipping 64 MB of a warm file measures ~0.01 ms - while the reading path is O(n), ~23 ms for the same 64 MB.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  try (InputStream is = new ByteArrayInputStream("0123456789".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8))) {
        long skipped = IOUtil.skip(is, 3);   // returns 3
        int next = is.read();                // returns '3' (51)
    }
    try (InputStream is = new ByteArrayInputStream("ab".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8))) {
        long skipped = IOUtil.skip(is, 100); // returns 2 (capped at end of stream)
        long none = IOUtil.skip(is, 0);      // returns 0
        // IOUtil.skip(is, -1);              // throws IllegalArgumentException
    }
  ```
- **See also:** #skipFully(InputStream, long)
- **Signature:** `public static long skip(final Reader input, final long charsToSkip) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Skips over and discards a specified number of characters from the input reader.
- **Parameters:**
  - `input` (`Reader`) — the `Reader` from which characters are to be skipped, must not be `null`.
  - `charsToSkip` (`long`) — the number of characters to be skipped, must be >= 0.
- **Returns:** the actual number of characters skipped, which may be less than `charsToSkip` if the end of the reader is reached.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `input` is `null`, or if `charsToSkip` is negative.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if skipping or reading from `input` to advance its position fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  try (Reader reader = new StringReader("abcdefghij")) {
        long skipped = IOUtil.skip(reader, 3);         // skips "abc", returns 3
        char[] buf = new char[7];
        IOUtil.read(reader, buf);                      // reads "defghij"
    }
    try (Reader reader = new StringReader("abc")) {
        long skipped = IOUtil.skip(reader, 10);        // skips all 3 chars, returns 3 (not 10)
    }
  ```
- **See also:** #skipFully(Reader, long)
##### skipFully(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static void skipFully(final InputStream input, final long bytesToSkip) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Skips over and discards a specified number of bytes from the input stream.
- **Parameters:**
  - `input` (`InputStream`) — the input stream to be skipped, must not be `null`.
  - `bytesToSkip` (`long`) — the number of bytes to be skipped.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `input` is `null`, or if `bytesToSkip` is negative.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if skipping or reading from `input` to advance its position fails
  - `java.io.EOFException` — if the stream ends before `bytesToSkip` bytes have been skipped. Whatever was skipped before that stays skipped - the stream is not rewound. `EOFException` is an `IOException`, and is the same type `org.apache.commons.io.IOUtils.skipFully` raises for this case, so it can be caught on its own to tell a short input apart from a read failure.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  try (InputStream is = new FileInputStream("data.bin")) {
        IOUtil.skipFully(is, 1024);
        byte[] data = IOUtil.readAllBytes(is);
    }
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static void skipFully(final Reader input, final long charsToSkip) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Skips over and discards a specified number of characters from the input reader.
- **Parameters:**
  - `input` (`Reader`) — the `Reader` from which characters are to be skipped, must not be `null`.
  - `charsToSkip` (`long`) — the number of characters to be skipped.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `input` is `null`, or if `charsToSkip` is negative.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if skipping or reading from `input` to advance its position fails
  - `java.io.EOFException` — if the reader ends before `charsToSkip` characters have been skipped. Whatever was skipped before that stays skipped - the reader is not rewound. `EOFException` is an `IOException`, and is the same type `org.apache.commons.io.IOUtils.skipFully` raises for this case, so it can be caught on its own to tell a short input apart from a read failure.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  try (Reader reader = new FileReader("data.txt")) {
        IOUtil.skipFully(reader, 1024);
        char[] data = IOUtil.readAllChars(reader);
    }
  ```
##### map(...) -> MappedByteBuffer
- **Signature:** `public static MappedByteBuffer map(final File file) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException`
- **Summary:** Note: It's copied from Google Guava under Apache License 2.0 and may be modified.
- **Contract:**
  - Flags such as `--add-opens java.base/java.nio=ALL-UNNAMED` and `--add-opens java.base/sun.nio.ch=ALL-UNNAMED` are only needed if the caller wants to forcibly unmap the returned buffer via reflection into JDK internals (which this method does not do).
  - Usage Examples: The mapped region cannot exceed Integer#MAX_VALUE bytes, which here means the whole file must fit.
- **Parameters:**
  - `file` (`File`) — the file to be mapped into memory, must not be `null` and must exist.
- **Returns:** a MappedByteBuffer that represents the content of the file.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the provided file is `null`, or is a directory.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if the file does not exist (wrapping a FileNotFoundException), or if another I/O error occurs during the operation.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File file = new File("large_data.bin");
    MappedByteBuffer buffer = IOUtil.map(file);
    byte data = buffer.get();
  ```
- **See also:** #map(File, MapMode), FileChannel#map(MapMode, long, long)
- **Signature:** `public static MappedByteBuffer map(final File file, final MapMode mode) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException`
- **Summary:** Note: It's copied from Google Guava under Apache License 2.0 and may be modified.
- **Contract:**
  - The mapped region cannot exceed Integer#MAX_VALUE bytes, which here means the whole file must fit.
  - Flags such as `--add-opens java.base/java.nio=ALL-UNNAMED` and `--add-opens java.base/sun.nio.ch=ALL-UNNAMED` are only needed if the caller wants to forcibly unmap the returned buffer via reflection into JDK internals (which this method does not do).
- **Parameters:**
  - `file` (`File`) — the file to map, must not be `null` and must exist.
  - `mode` (`MapMode`) — the mode to use when mapping `file`.
- **Returns:** a buffer reflecting `file`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the file or mode is `null`, or if the file is a directory.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if the file does not exist (wrapping a FileNotFoundException), or if another I/O error occurs.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File file = new File("data.bin");
    MappedByteBuffer buffer = IOUtil.map(file, MapMode.READ_ONLY);
    // Read from memory-mapped file
  ```
- **See also:** #map(File, MapMode, long, long), FileChannel#map(MapMode, long, long)
- **Signature:** `public static MappedByteBuffer map(final File file, final MapMode mode, final long offset, final long count) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException`
- **Summary:** Note: It's copied from Google Guava under Apache License 2.0 and may be modified.
- **Contract:**
  - If the mode is MapMode#READ_WRITE or MapMode#PRIVATE and the file does not exist, it will be created - along with any missing parent directories, as every other file-creating method in this class does - and extended to `offset + count` bytes.
  - With MapMode#READ_ONLY the region must already exist: an `offset + count` that runs past the end of the file is an `UncheckedIOException`, because extending the file is the one thing a read-only mapping cannot do.
  - Map `Math.min(count, file.length() - offset)` bytes, or ask for `READ_WRITE`, when the region may run short.
  - Flags such as `--add-opens java.base/java.nio=ALL-UNNAMED` and `--add-opens java.base/sun.nio.ch=ALL-UNNAMED` are only needed if the caller wants to forcibly unmap the returned buffer via reflection into JDK internals (which this method does not do).
- **Parameters:**
  - `file` (`File`) — the file to map. With MapMode#READ_ONLY it must exist; with MapMode#READ_WRITE or MapMode#PRIVATE - both of which need write access - it is created, along with any missing parent directories, if it does not.
  - `mode` (`MapMode`) — the mode to use when mapping `file`.
  - `offset` (`long`) — the offset within the file at which the mapped region is to start; must be non-negative.
  - `count` (`long`) — the size of the region to be mapped; must be non-negative and no greater than Integer#MAX_VALUE.
- **Returns:** a buffer reflecting `file`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `file` or `mode` is `null`, if `offset` or `count` is negative, or if another precondition on the parameters does not hold - including a `count` greater than Integer#MAX_VALUE, which FileChannel#map rejects, or a `file` that exists but is a directory.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if the file does not exist and cannot be created for the requested mode (wrapping a FileNotFoundException), if a missing parent directory cannot be created, or if another I/O error occurs.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Map a file for reading
    File file = new File("data.bin");
    MappedByteBuffer buffer = IOUtil.map(file, MapMode.READ_ONLY, 0, file.length());
    byte value = buffer.get(0);
  
    // Map a portion of a large file for read-write
    MappedByteBuffer rwBuffer = IOUtil.map(file, MapMode.READ_WRITE, 1024, 4096);
    rwBuffer.putInt(0, 42);
  ```
- **See also:** #map(File, MapMode), FileChannel#map(MapMode, long, long)
##### simplifyPath(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `public static String simplifyPath(String pathname)`
- **Summary:** Note: It's copied from Google Guava under Apache License 2.0 and may be modified.
- **Contract:**
  - fold out./ fold out../ when possible collapse multiple slashes delete trailing slashes (unless the path is just "/") backslashes are treated as separators and normalized to `/` a Windows drive prefix such as `C:/` is kept as the root and cannot be ascended above a UNC prefix such as `//host/share` keeps both leading slashes and is kept as the root These heuristics do not always match the behavior of the filesystem.
  - If `a` is a symlink to `x`, `a/../b` may refer to a sibling of `x`, rather than the sibling of `a` referred to by `b`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `pathname` (`String`) — the file path to simplify; `null` or empty yields `"."`.
- **Returns:** the simplified path string with redundant elements removed; never `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String simplified = IOUtil.simplifyPath("/a/./b/./c/");   // returns "/a/b/c"
    String simplified2 = IOUtil.simplifyPath("a/b/./c");      // returns "a/b/c"
    String simplified3 = IOUtil.simplifyPath("a/b/../c");     // returns "a/c"
    String simplified4 = IOUtil.simplifyPath("a\\b\\c");      // returns "a/b/c"
    String simplified5 = IOUtil.simplifyPath("");             // returns "."
    String simplified6 = IOUtil.simplifyPath("//host/share/./x");   // returns "//host/share/x"
    String simplified7 = IOUtil.simplifyPath("C:/a/../../b");       // returns "C:/b"
  ```
- **See also:** java.nio.file.Path#normalize(), FilenameUtil#normalize(String), FilenameUtil#normalize(String, boolean)

  - The file, along with any missing parent directories, is created first if it does not exist.
- **Parameters:**
  - `file` (`File`) — the file to be opened for writing. It is created, along with any missing parent directories, if it does not exist.
  - `charset` (`Charset`) — the Charset to be used for creating the FileWriter; `null` uses the default charset (UTF-8).
  - `append` (`boolean`) — `true` to append to the existing content instead of truncating the file.
- **Returns:** a new FileWriter instance.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `file` is `null`, or is a directory rather than a file.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if opening `file` for writing fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File file = new File("log.txt");
    try (FileWriter writer = IOUtil.newFileWriter(file, StandardCharsets.UTF_8, true)) {
        writer.write("New log entry\n");
    }
  ```
- **See also:** FileWriter#FileWriter(File, Charset, boolean)

- **Signature:** `public static java.io.BufferedReader newBufferedReader(final Path path, final Charset charset) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new BufferedReader instance for the specified path with a specified charset.
- **Contract:**
  - It is deliberately not java.nio.file.Files#newBufferedReader(Path, Charset), whose reader raises java.nio.charset.MalformedInputException part-way through a read, opens a directory without complaint on Unix and fails only when read, and names an absent file with java.nio.file.NoSuchFileException - three answers no other method in this class gives.
- **Parameters:**
  - `path` (`Path`) — the path of the file to be read from.
  - `charset` (`Charset`) — the charset to be used; `null` uses the default charset (UTF-8).
- **Returns:** a new BufferedReader instance.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `path` is `null`, or exists but is a directory.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if the file does not exist (wrapping a FileNotFoundException) or cannot be opened.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Path path = Paths.get("file.txt");
    try (BufferedReader br = IOUtil.newBufferedReader(path, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) {
        String line = br.readLine();
    }
  ```
- **See also:** #newBufferedReader(File, Charset)

  ```java
         BufferedReader br = IOUtil.newBufferedReader(is)) {
        String line = br.readLine();
    }
  ```

- **Summary:** Creates a new GZIPInputStream instance with the specified InputStream and buffer size.
- **Parameters:**

  - `bufferSize` (`int`) — the size of the buffer to be used; must be positive.
- **Returns:** a new GZIPInputStream instance.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `is` is `null`, or if `bufferSize` is not positive.

##### close(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static void close(final URLConnection conn)`
- **Summary:** Closes the provided `URLConnection` by calling HttpURLConnection#disconnect() if it is an `HttpURLConnection`; otherwise does nothing.
- **Parameters:**
  - `conn` (`URLConnection`) — the connection to close.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  URLConnection conn = new URL("http://example.com").openConnection();   // may throw IOException
    try {
        try (InputStream input = conn.getInputStream()) {
            byte[] responseBody = IOUtil.readAllBytes(input);
        }
    } finally {
        IOUtil.close(conn);   // disconnects if it is an HttpURLConnection; otherwise no-op
    }
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static void close(final AutoCloseable closeable) throws RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Closes the provided `AutoCloseable` object.
- **Contract:**
  - If a checked exception occurs during the close operation, it is wrapped in a `RuntimeException`; runtime exceptions are propagated unchanged.
  - If the object is `null`, this method does nothing.
- **Parameters:**
  - `closeable` (`AutoCloseable`) — the AutoCloseable object to be closed. It can be `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if `closeable.close()` throws an exception; checked exceptions are wrapped and runtime exceptions are propagated
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  InputStream is = new FileInputStream("file.txt");
    try {
        // Use the stream
    } finally {
        IOUtil.close(is);  // Safely closes and throws RuntimeException if an error occurs
    }
  ```
- **See also:** #closeQuietly(AutoCloseable)
- **Signature:** `public static void close(final AutoCloseable closeable, final Consumer<Exception> exceptionHandler) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Closes the provided `AutoCloseable` object and handles any exceptions that occur during the closing operation using the specified `exceptionHandler`.
- **Contract:**
  - If the object is `null`, this method does nothing.
- **Parameters:**
  - `closeable` (`AutoCloseable`) — the AutoCloseable object to be closed. It can be `null`.
  - `exceptionHandler` (`Consumer<Exception>`) — the Consumer to handle any exceptions thrown during the close operation.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `exceptionHandler` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  InputStream is = new FileInputStream("file.txt");
    try {
        // Use the stream
    } finally {
        IOUtil.close(is, e -> logger.error("Failed to close stream", e));
    }
  ```
##### closeAll(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@SafeVarargs public static void closeAll(final AutoCloseable... closeables) throws RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Closes all provided `AutoCloseable` objects.
- **Contract:**
  - If an exception occurs while closing any of the objects, the first exception encountered is propagated unchanged if it is a runtime exception, or wrapped in a `RuntimeException` otherwise, with subsequent exceptions added as suppressed exceptions.
  - If an object is `null`, it is ignored.
- **Parameters:**
  - `closeables` (`AutoCloseable[]`) — the AutoCloseable objects to be closed. It may contain `null` elements.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if closing a non-null element of `closeables` throws an exception; the first exception is propagated or wrapped after all elements are attempted
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  InputStream a = new ByteArrayInputStream("x".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
    InputStream b = new ByteArrayInputStream("y".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
    IOUtil.closeAll(a, b, null);   // closes a and b in order; null is ignored
    IOUtil.closeAll();             // empty varargs: no-op
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static void closeAll(final Iterable<? extends AutoCloseable> closeables) throws RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Closes all provided `AutoCloseable` objects in the `Iterable`.
- **Contract:**
  - If an exception occurs while closing any of the objects, the first exception encountered is propagated unchanged if it is a runtime exception, or wrapped in a `RuntimeException` otherwise, with subsequent exceptions added as suppressed exceptions.
  - If an object is `null`, it is ignored.
- **Parameters:**
  - `closeables` (`Iterable<? extends AutoCloseable>`) — the Iterable of AutoCloseable objects to be closed. It may contain `null` elements.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if closing a non-null element of `closeables` throws an exception; the first exception is propagated or wrapped after all elements are attempted
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<AutoCloseable> closeables = Arrays.asList(
            new ByteArrayInputStream("a".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)),
            new ByteArrayInputStream("b".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)));
    IOUtil.closeAll(closeables);                               // closes all in order
    IOUtil.closeAll(Collections.<AutoCloseable>emptyList());   // empty collection, no-op
  ```
##### closeQuietly(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static void closeQuietly(final AutoCloseable closeable)`
- **Summary:** Closes the provided `AutoCloseable` object quietly, suppressing any exceptions.
- **Contract:**
  - If an exception occurs during the close operation, it is logged at error level but not rethrown.
  - If the object is `null`, this method does nothing.
- **Parameters:**
  - `closeable` (`AutoCloseable`) — the AutoCloseable object to be closed. It can be `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  InputStream is = null;
    try {
        is = new FileInputStream("file.txt");
        // Use the stream
    } finally {
        IOUtil.closeQuietly(is);  // Closes silently, ignoring exceptions but logging them
    }
  ```
- **See also:** #close(AutoCloseable)
##### closeAllQuietly(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@SafeVarargs public static void closeAllQuietly(final AutoCloseable... closeables)`
- **Summary:** Closes all provided AutoCloseable objects quietly.
- **Parameters:**
  - `closeables` (`AutoCloseable[]`) — the AutoCloseable objects to be closed. It may contain `null` elements.
- **Examples:**

  ```java
    AutoCloseable failing = () -> { throw new IOException("boom"); };

    IOUtil.closeAllQuietly();                   // empty varargs: no-op
  ```

- **Signature:** `public static void closeAllQuietly(final Iterable<? extends AutoCloseable> closeables)`
- **Summary:** Closes all provided AutoCloseable objects quietly.
- **Parameters:**
  - `closeables` (`Iterable<? extends AutoCloseable>`) — the Iterable of AutoCloseable objects to be closed. It may contain `null` elements.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<AutoCloseable> closeables = Arrays.asList(
            new ByteArrayInputStream("a".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)),

    IOUtil.closeAllQuietly(Collections.<AutoCloseable>emptyList());   // empty collection, no-op
  ```

##### copyToDirectory(...) -> File
- **Signature:** `public static File copyToDirectory(final File srcFile, final File destDir) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Copies the specified source file or directory to the specified destination directory.
- **Contract:**
  - Existing files in the destination are never overwritten: an `IOException` is thrown if a destination file already exists, or if a file or a link of any kind (a live directory link included: a copy never writes through one) sits where a copied subdirectory would be created.
  - If a file is copied into its own parent directory, the copy is created under the name `"Copy of " + fileName` - inspect the returned `File` rather than assuming `destDir/srcFile.getName()`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `srcFile` (`File`) — the source file or directory to be copied. It must not be `null`.
  - `destDir` (`File`) — the destination directory where the source file or directory will be copied to. It must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** the file or directory actually created inside `destDir`, whose own path is resolved to its canonical form (so a `destDir` containing `.` or a symlink comes back resolved). This is normally `new File(destDir, srcFile.getName())` - a symlink source keeps its own name - but it carries the `"Copy of "` prefix when a file, or a link to one, is copied into the directory that already holds it. It is never the source itself - a copy that would land there is rejected rather than reported as done.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `srcFile` is `null`, if `destDir` is `null` or exists but is not a directory, if the destination directory is inside or the same as the source directory, or if the directory the source would be recreated as is the source itself or one of its ancestors.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if opening or reading `srcFile`, creating entries in `destDir`, or writing their contents fails
  - `java.io.FileNotFoundException` — if `srcFile` does not exist, cannot be read, or is neither a file nor a directory.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File sourceFile = new File("document.pdf");
    File targetDir = new File("backups");
    File copy = IOUtil.copyToDirectory(sourceFile, targetDir);
    // copy is backups/document.pdf
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static File copyToDirectory(final File srcFile, final File destDir, final boolean preserveFileDate) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Copies the specified source file or directory to the specified destination directory.
- **Contract:**
  - If the source is a directory, it is recreated (by its own name) inside the destination directory, along with all of its contents.
  - Existing files in the destination are never overwritten: an `IOException` is thrown if a destination file already exists, or if a file or a link of any kind (a live directory link included: a copy never writes through one) sits where a copied subdirectory would be created.
  - If a file is copied into its own parent directory, the copy is created under the name `"Copy of " + fileName` - inspect the returned `File` rather than assuming `destDir/srcFile.getName()`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `srcFile` (`File`) — the source file or directory to be copied. It must not be `null`.
  - `destDir` (`File`) — the destination directory where the source file or directory will be copied to. It must not be `null`.
  - `preserveFileDate` (`boolean`) — if `true`, the last modified date of the file will be preserved in the copied file.
- **Returns:** the file or directory actually created inside `destDir`, whose own path is resolved to its canonical form (so a `destDir` containing `.` or a symlink comes back resolved). This is normally `new File(destDir, srcFile.getName())` - a symlink source keeps its own name - but it carries the `"Copy of "` prefix when a file, or a link to one, is copied into the directory that already holds it. It is never the source itself - a copy that would land there is rejected rather than reported as done.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `srcFile` is `null`, if `destDir` is `null` or exists but is not a directory, if the destination directory is inside or the same as the source directory, or if the directory the source would be recreated as is the source itself or one of its ancestors.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if opening or reading `srcFile`, creating entries in `destDir`, or writing their contents fails
  - `java.io.FileNotFoundException` — if `srcFile` does not exist, cannot be read, or is neither a file nor a directory.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File sourceFile = new File("document.pdf");
    File targetDir = new File("backups");
    File copy = IOUtil.copyToDirectory(sourceFile, targetDir, true);
    // copy is backups/document.pdf, with the modification date preserved
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <E extends Exception> File copyToDirectory(final File srcFile, final File destDir, final boolean preserveFileDate, final Throwables.BiPredicate<? super File, ? super File, E> filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException, E`
- **Summary:** Copies the specified source file or directory to the specified destination directory.
- **Contract:**
  - If the source is a directory, it is recreated (by its own name) inside the destination directory, along with all of its contents.
  - Existing files in the destination are never overwritten: an `IOException` is thrown if a destination file already exists, or if a file or a link of any kind (a live directory link included: a copy never writes through one) sits where a copied subdirectory would be created.
  - If a file is copied into its own parent directory, the copy is created under the name `"Copy of " + fileName` - inspect the returned `File` rather than assuming `destDir/srcFile.getName()`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `srcFile` (`File`) — the source file or directory to be copied. It must not be `null`.
  - `destDir` (`File`) — the destination directory where the source file or directory will be copied to. It must not be `null`. It is created only after every argument has been validated, so a rejected call never leaves a new directory behind.
  - `preserveFileDate` (`boolean`) — if `true`, the last modified date of the file will be preserved in the copied file.
  - `filter` (`Throwables.BiPredicate<? super File, ? super File, E>`) — a BiPredicate that takes the source directory and the file being evaluated as arguments and returns a boolean. If the predicate returns `true`, the file is copied; if it returns `false`, the file is not copied. It selects the source's contents and is never asked about `srcFile` itself, so a plain-file source is copied whatever the filter answers (the same convention as #deleteFilesFromDirectory(File, Throwables.BiPredicate)). A rejected subdirectory is still descended into, so that its own matching entries are copied - which means the destination mirrors the source's directory structure in full, including directories that ended up holding nothing.
- **Returns:** the file or directory actually created inside `destDir`. This is normally `new File(destDir, srcFile.getName())` (with `destDir` resolved to its canonical form; a symlink source keeps its own name), but it carries the `"Copy of "` prefix when a file, or a link to one, is copied into the directory that already holds it. It is never the source itself - a copy that would land there is rejected rather than reported as done.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `srcFile` or `filter` is `null`, if `destDir` is `null` or exists but is not a directory, if the destination directory is inside or the same as the source directory, or if the directory the source would be recreated as is the source itself or one of its ancestors.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if opening or reading `srcFile`, creating entries in `destDir`, or writing their contents fails
  - `E` — if the filter throws an exception.
  - `java.io.FileNotFoundException` — if `srcFile` does not exist, cannot be read, or is neither a file nor a directory.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Assume "input" is a directory containing "keep.txt" and "skip.log",
    // and "backup" is an existing destination directory.
    File srcDir = new File("input");
    File destDir = new File("backup");
    // copy only files whose name ends with ".txt"
    File copiedDir = IOUtil.copyToDirectory(srcDir, destDir, false, (parent, file) -> file.getName().endsWith(".txt"));
    // copiedDir is destDir/<srcDir-name>, which now holds keep.txt; skip.log is not copied
  ```
##### copyDirectory(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static void copyDirectory(final File srcDir, final File destDir) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Copies the contents of a directory to another directory.
- **Contract:**
  - If the destination directory does not exist, it is created.
  - `destDir` must not be `srcDir` itself, nor lie inside it: the copy would keep finding the entries it had just written.
  - Last-modified times are preserved, as in #copyToDirectory(File, File): the copy fails after writing a file's bytes if its last-modified time cannot be applied.
  - There is no switch on this method; copy the entries with #copyToDirectory(File, File, boolean) and `false` when the dates must not be carried over.
- **Parameters:**
  - `srcDir` (`File`) — the source directory to copy from, must not be `null`; it must exist and be readable.
  - `destDir` (`File`) — the destination directory to copy to, must not be `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `srcDir` is `null` or exists but is not a directory, if `destDir` is `null` or exists but is not a directory, if `destDir` is `srcDir` or is inside it, or if one of `srcDir`'s subdirectories would be copied onto one of its own ancestors.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if listing or reading `srcDir`, creating `destDir` or its descendants, or copying their contents fails, if the source directory does not exist or cannot be read (a FileNotFoundException), if its contents cannot be listed — which is reported rather than mistaken for an empty directory, so a normal return always means the whole source was copied — or if a copied file's timestamp cannot be applied.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File sourceDir = new File("source_directory");
    File destDir = new File("destination_directory");
    IOUtil.copyDirectory(sourceDir, destDir);
  ```
- **See also:** #copyToDirectory(File, File)
##### copyFile(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public static void copyFile(final File srcFile, final File destFile) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Copies a file to a new location preserving the file date.
- **Contract:**
  - The directory holding the destination file is created if it does not exist.
  - If the destination file exists, then this method overwrites it.
  - Whether an existing read-only destination is replaced is platform-defined: POSIX replaces the entry when its directory is writable, Windows refuses with an `AccessDeniedException`.
  - If the modification operation fails, it falls back to File#setLastModified(long), and if that fails, the method throws IOException.
  - This method preserves the source's last-modified time (failing if it cannot) and attempts to preserve the other file times too.
- **Parameters:**
  - `srcFile` (`File`) — an existing file to copy, must not be `null`.
  - `destFile` (`File`) — the new file, must not be `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `srcFile` is `null` or is a directory, or if `srcFile` and `destFile` denote the same file.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if source or destination is invalid, or if reading `srcFile` or writing `destFile` fails.
  - `java.io.FileNotFoundException` — if the source does not exist, is not readable, or is neither a file nor a directory (a FIFO, socket or device node, or a link to one).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File source = new File("original.txt");
    File dest = new File("copy.txt");
    IOUtil.copyFile(source, dest);
  ```
- **See also:** #copyToDirectory(File, File), #copyFile(File, File, boolean), #write(File, File)
- **Signature:** `public static void copyFile(final File srcFile, final File destFile, final boolean preserveFileDate) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Copies an existing file to a new file location.
- **Contract:**
  - The directory holding the destination file is created if it does not exist.
  - If the destination file exists, then this method overwrites it.
  - Whether an existing read-only destination is replaced is platform-defined: POSIX replaces the entry when its directory is writable, Windows refuses with an `AccessDeniedException`.
  - If the modification operation fails, it falls back to File#setLastModified(long), and if that fails, the method throws IOException.
- **Parameters:**
  - `srcFile` (`File`) — an existing file to copy, must not be `null`.
  - `destFile` (`File`) — the new file, must not be `null`.
  - `preserveFileDate` (`boolean`) — `true` if the file date of the copy should be the same as the original.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `srcFile` is `null` or is a directory, or if `srcFile` and `destFile` denote the same file.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if source or destination is invalid, if reading `srcFile` or writing `destFile` fails, if setting the last-modified time didn't succeed, or if the output file length differs from the input after copying.
  - `java.io.FileNotFoundException` — if the source does not exist, is not readable, or is neither a file nor a directory (a FIFO, socket or device node, or a link to one).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File source = new File("original.txt");
    File dest = new File("copy.txt");
    IOUtil.copyFile(source, dest, true);
  ```
- **See also:** #copyFile(File, File, boolean, CopyOption...)
- **Signature:** `@SafeVarargs public static void copyFile(final File srcFile, final File destFile, final CopyOption... copyOptions) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Copies a file to a new location.
- **Contract:**
  - The directory holding the destination file is created if it does not exist.
  - If the destination file exists, you can overwrite it if you use StandardCopyOption#REPLACE_EXISTING.
  - That also means it can fail after the bytes have been copied, if the timestamps cannot be applied.
- **Parameters:**
  - `srcFile` (`File`) — an existing file to copy, must not be `null`.
  - `destFile` (`File`) — the new file, must not be `null`.
  - `copyOptions` (`CopyOption[]`) — options specifying how the copy should be done, for example StandardCopyOption. Must not be `null`; pass no arguments, or an empty array, for "no options".
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `srcFile`, `destFile` or `copyOptions` is `null`, if `srcFile` is a directory, or if `srcFile` and `destFile` denote the same file.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if reading `srcFile` or writing `destFile` fails, or if setting the last-modified time didn't succeed.
  - `java.io.FileNotFoundException` — if the source does not exist, is not readable, or is neither a file nor a directory (a FIFO, socket or device node, or a link to one).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File source = new File("original.txt");
    File dest = new File("copy.txt");
    IOUtil.copyFile(source, dest, StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING);
  ```
- **See also:** #copyFile(File, File, boolean, CopyOption...), StandardCopyOption
- **Signature:** `@SafeVarargs public static void copyFile(final File srcFile, final File destFile, final boolean preserveFileDate, final CopyOption... copyOptions) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Copies the contents of a file to a new location.
- **Contract:**
  - The directory holding the destination file is created if it does not exist.
  - If the destination file exists, you can overwrite it with StandardCopyOption#REPLACE_EXISTING.
  - If the modification operation fails, it falls back to File#setLastModified(long), and if that fails, the method throws IOException.
- **Parameters:**
  - `srcFile` (`File`) — an existing file to copy, must not be `null`.
  - `destFile` (`File`) — the new file, must not be `null`.
  - `preserveFileDate` (`boolean`) — `true` if the file date of the copy should be the same as the original.
  - `copyOptions` (`CopyOption[]`) — options specifying how the copy should be done, for example StandardCopyOption. Must not be `null`; pass no arguments, or an empty array, for "no options".
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `srcFile`, `destFile` or `copyOptions` is `null`, if `srcFile` is not a file (unless it is a link copied as a link), if `destFile` is a directory, or if they denote the same file.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if reading `srcFile` or writing `destFile` fails, if setting the last-modified time didn't succeed, or if the destination is not writable.
  - `java.io.FileNotFoundException` — if the source does not exist or is not readable (for a link copied as a link, if the link itself does not exist).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File source = new File("original.txt");
    File dest = new File("copy.txt");
    IOUtil.copyFile(source, dest, true, StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING);
  ```
- **See also:** #copyToDirectory(File, File, boolean)
- **Signature:** `public static long copyFile(final File srcFile, final OutputStream output) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Copies bytes from a File to an OutputStream.
- **Contract:**
  - Use whichever reads better at the call site; prefer #write(File, long, long, OutputStream) when only a slice of the file is wanted.
- **Parameters:**
  - `srcFile` (`File`) — the File to read.
  - `output` (`OutputStream`) — the OutputStream to write.
- **Returns:** the number of bytes copied.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `srcFile` or `output` is `null`.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if reading `srcFile` or writing `output` fails
  - `java.io.FileNotFoundException` — if `srcFile` does not exist or is not readable.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File source = new File("data.txt");
    try (OutputStream out = new FileOutputStream("output.bin")) {
        long bytesCopied = IOUtil.copyFile(source, out);
    }
  ```
- **See also:** #write(File, OutputStream), #copyFile(File, File)
##### copyURLToFile(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static void copyURLToFile(final URL source, final File destination) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Copies bytes from the URL `source` to a file `destination`.
- **Contract:**
  - The directories up to `destination` will be created if they don't already exist.
  - `destination` will be overwritten if it already exists.
  - When a temporary sibling can be created, the previous content survives a failed download.
  - Preserving the destination's POSIX permissions when replacing the entry is best effort; a failure is logged.
  - Whether a read-only destination is replaced is platform-defined: the replacing move succeeds on POSIX when the directory is writable, and Windows refuses it.
  - If no temporary sibling can be created, the download is written directly to `destination`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`URL`) — the `URL` to copy bytes from, must not be `null`.
  - `destination` (`File`) — the non-directory `File` to write bytes to (possibly overwriting), must not be `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `source` or `destination` is `null`, if `destination` is a directory, or if `source` is a `file:` URL naming `destination` itself.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if opening or reading `source` or writing or installing the downloaded file at `destination` fails.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  URL url = new URL("https://example.com/data.txt");
    File dest = new File("downloaded.txt");
    IOUtil.copyURLToFile(url, dest);
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static void copyURLToFile(final URL source, final File destination, final int connectTimeout, final int readTimeout) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Copies bytes from the URL `source` to a file `destination`.
- **Contract:**
  - The directories up to `destination` will be created if they don't already exist.
  - `destination` will be overwritten if it already exists.
  - When a temporary sibling can be created, a failed download (including a read timeout) preserves the previous content.
  - If no sibling can be created, the direct-write fallback can truncate or partially overwrite the destination even when the download fails.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`URL`) — the `URL` to copy bytes from, must not be `null`.
  - `destination` (`File`) — the non-directory `File` to write bytes to (possibly overwriting), must not be `null`.
  - `connectTimeout` (`int`) — the number of milliseconds until this method will timeout if no connection could be established to the `source`.
  - `readTimeout` (`int`) — the number of milliseconds until this method will timeout if no data could be read from the `source`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `source` or `destination` is `null`, if `destination` is a directory, or if `source` is a `file:` URL naming `destination` itself.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if opening or reading `source` or writing or installing the downloaded file at `destination` fails.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  URL url = new URL("https://example.com/data.txt");
    File dest = new File("downloaded.txt");
    IOUtil.copyURLToFile(url, dest, 5000, 10000);
  ```
##### copy(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `@SafeVarargs public static Path copy(final Path source, final Path target, final CopyOption... options) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Copies a file, or creates an empty directory if the source is a directory.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`Path`) — the source path of the file or directory to be copied.
  - `target` (`Path`) — the target path where the file or directory will be copied to.
  - `options` (`CopyOption[]`) — optional arguments that specify how the copy should be done. Must not be `null`; pass no arguments, or an empty array, for "no options".
- **Returns:** the path to the target file or directory.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `source`, `target` or `options` is `null`.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if reading `source` or writing `target` fails
  - `java.io.FileNotFoundException` — if `source` does not exist, or a path required by the copy is missing.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Assume input.txt exists and input-copy.txt does not.
    Path source = Path.of("input.txt");
    Path target = Path.of("input-copy.txt");
    Path result = IOUtil.copy(source, target);                          // returns target; file contents copied
    // overwrite an existing target:
    IOUtil.copy(source, target, StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING);   // returns target
  ```
- **See also:** Files#copy(Path, Path, CopyOption...)
- **Signature:** `@SafeVarargs public static long copy(final InputStream in, final Path target, final CopyOption... options) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Copies the content of the given InputStream to the specified target Path.
- **Parameters:**
  - `in` (`InputStream`) — the InputStream to be copied.
  - `target` (`Path`) — the target Path where the InputStream content will be copied to.
  - `options` (`CopyOption[]`) — optional arguments that specify how the copy should be done. Must not be `null`; pass no arguments, or an empty array, for "no options".
- **Returns:** the number of bytes read or skipped and written to the target Path.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `in`, `target` or `options` is `null`.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if reading `in` or writing `target` fails.
  - `java.io.FileNotFoundException` — if a path required by the copy is missing.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Path target = Paths.get("output.dat");
    try (InputStream in = new ByteArrayInputStream("data".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8))) {
        IOUtil.copy(in, target);                                       // copies to file (creates new)
    }
    try (InputStream in = new ByteArrayInputStream("data".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8))) {
        IOUtil.copy(in, target, StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING);  // overwrites existing file
    }
  ```
- **See also:** Files#copy(InputStream, Path, CopyOption...)
- **Signature:** `public static long copy(final Path source, final OutputStream output) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Copies the content of the file at the given source Path to the specified OutputStream.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`Path`) — the source Path of the file to be copied.
  - `output` (`OutputStream`) — the OutputStream where the file content will be copied to.
- **Returns:** the number of bytes read or skipped and written to the OutputStream.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `source` or `output` is `null`.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if reading `source` or writing `output` fails.
  - `java.io.FileNotFoundException` — if `source` does not exist.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Path source = Paths.get("input.dat");
    try (OutputStream os = new FileOutputStream("output.dat")) {
        IOUtil.copy(source, os);  // copies file content to output stream
    }
    // Edge: empty file
    Path emptyFile = Paths.get("empty.dat");
    try (OutputStream os = new FileOutputStream("output.dat")) {
        IOUtil.copy(emptyFile, os);  // copies empty file, returns 0
    }
  ```
- **See also:** Files#copy(Path, OutputStream)
##### move(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `@Deprecated public static void move(final File srcFile, final File destDir) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Moves a file from the source location to the destination directory, creating the destination directory if it doesn't exist.
- **Parameters:**
  - `srcFile` (`File`) — the source file or directory to be moved, must not be `null`.
  - `destDir` (`File`) — the destination directory where the file or directory will be moved to.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `srcFile` is `null` or is a filesystem root, or if `destDir` exists but is not a directory.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if relocating `srcFile` to `destDir` fails, such as if the destination cannot be created or written to.
  - `java.io.FileNotFoundException` — if `srcFile` does not exist (a dangling link is a source: the link itself is what moves).
  - `java.nio.file.FileAlreadyExistsException` — if `destDir` already contains an entry with the source's name.
- **Signature:** `@Deprecated @SafeVarargs public static void move(final File srcFile, final File destDir, final CopyOption... options) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Moves a file from the source file to the target directory.
- **Contract:**
  - If the destination directory does not exist, it will be created.
- **Parameters:**
  - `srcFile` (`File`) — the source file to be moved.
  - `destDir` (`File`) — the target directory where the file will be moved to.
  - `options` (`CopyOption[]`) — optional arguments that specify how the move should be done.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `srcFile`, `destDir` or `options` is `null`, if `srcFile` is a filesystem root, if `destDir` exists but is not a directory, or if `srcFile` is a directory and `destDir` is that directory or is inside it.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if relocating `srcFile` to `destDir` fails, including failure to create the destination directory.
  - `java.io.FileNotFoundException` — if `srcFile` does not exist (a dangling link is a source: the link itself is what moves).
  - `java.nio.file.FileAlreadyExistsException` — if `destDir` already contains an entry with the source's name and StandardCopyOption#REPLACE_EXISTING was not passed.
  - `java.nio.file.DirectoryNotEmptyException` — if replacement was requested and the existing destination entry is a non-empty directory.
- **Signature:** `@SafeVarargs public static Path move(final Path source, final Path target, final CopyOption... options) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Moves a file from the source path to the target path.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`Path`) — the source Path of the file to be moved.
  - `target` (`Path`) — the target Path where the file will be moved to.
  - `options` (`CopyOption[]`) — optional arguments that specify how the move should be done. Must not be `null`; pass no arguments, or an empty array, for "no options".
- **Returns:** the target path.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `source`, `target` or `options` is `null`.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if relocating `source` to `target` fails
  - `java.io.FileNotFoundException` — if `source` does not exist, or a path required by the move is missing.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Path source = Paths.get("old_name.txt");
    Path target = Paths.get("new_name.txt");
    IOUtil.move(source, target);                                        // moves/renames file
    // Alternatively, to replace an existing target (while source still exists):
    // IOUtil.move(source, target, StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING);
  ```
- **See also:** Files#move(Path, Path, CopyOption...)
##### moveToDirectory(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static void moveToDirectory(final File srcFile, final File destDir) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Moves a file or directory into the destination directory, keeping its own name, creating the destination directory if it doesn't exist.
- **Contract:**
  - An existing destination is never overwritten, matching #copyToDirectory(File, File): if `destDir` already holds a different entry with the source's name, a java.nio.file.FileAlreadyExistsException is thrown and nothing is moved.
  - When `srcFile` is a directory, `destDir` must not be that directory itself nor lie inside it; that is rejected before the destination is created.
- **Parameters:**
  - `srcFile` (`File`) — the source file or directory to be moved, must not be `null`.
  - `destDir` (`File`) — the destination directory where the file or directory will be moved to.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `srcFile` is `null` or is a filesystem root, if `destDir` exists but is not a directory, or if `srcFile` is a directory and `destDir` is that directory or is inside it.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if relocating `srcFile` to `destDir` fails, such as if the destination cannot be created or written to.
  - `java.io.FileNotFoundException` — if `srcFile` does not exist (a dangling link is a source: the link itself is what moves).
  - `java.nio.file.FileAlreadyExistsException` — if `destDir` already contains a different entry with the source's name. (A non-empty directory of that name reports this too: without StandardCopyOption#REPLACE_EXISTING the move never gets as far as trying to merge, so java.nio.file.DirectoryNotEmptyException is reachable only through #moveToDirectory(File, File, CopyOption...).)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File sourceFile = new File("/path/to/source/file.txt");
    File targetDir = new File("/path/to/destination");
    IOUtil.moveToDirectory(sourceFile, targetDir);
    // The file is now at /path/to/destination/file.txt and removed from the original location
  
    // Alternatively, to replace an existing entry (while sourceFile still exists):
    // IOUtil.moveToDirectory(sourceFile, targetDir, StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING);
  ```
- **See also:** #moveToDirectory(File, File, CopyOption...), #copyToDirectory(File, File)
- **Signature:** `@SafeVarargs public static void moveToDirectory(final File srcFile, final File destDir, final CopyOption... options) throws IllegalArgumentException, IOException`
- **Summary:** Moves a file or directory into the destination directory, keeping its own name, creating the destination directory if it doesn't exist.
- **Contract:**
  - Use #copyToDirectory(File, File) followed by #deleteRecursivelyIfExists(File) when either case is possible.
  - When `srcFile` is a directory, `destDir` must not be that directory itself nor lie inside it - a directory cannot be moved into its own subtree.
- **Parameters:**
  - `srcFile` (`File`) — the source file to be moved, must not be `null`.
  - `destDir` (`File`) — the target directory where the file will be moved to.
  - `options` (`CopyOption[]`) — optional arguments that specify how the move should be done. Without StandardCopyOption#REPLACE_EXISTING an existing destination entry is not replaced. Must not be `null`; pass no arguments, or an empty array, for "no options".
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `srcFile` is `null` or is a filesystem root, if `options` is `null`, if `destDir` exists but is not a directory, or if `srcFile` is a directory and `destDir` is that directory or is inside it.
  - `java.io.IOException` — if relocating `srcFile` to `destDir` fails, including failure to create the destination directory.
  - `java.io.FileNotFoundException` — if `srcFile` does not exist (a dangling link is a source: the link itself is what moves).
  - `java.nio.file.FileAlreadyExistsException` — if `destDir` already contains an entry with the source's name and StandardCopyOption#REPLACE_EXISTING was not given.
  - `java.nio.file.DirectoryNotEmptyException` — if the source is a directory and the destination entry is an existing non-empty directory.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Assume data.txt exists and archive is the destination directory.
    File srcFile = new File("data.txt");
    File destDir = new File("archive");
    IOUtil.moveToDirectory(srcFile, destDir, StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING);
    // srcFile no longer exists; destDir/data.txt now holds the content
  ```
- **See also:** #moveToDirectory(File, File), #copyToDirectory(File, File, boolean)
##### renameTo(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean renameTo(final File srcFile, final String newFileName) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Renames the specified source file to the new file name provided.
- **Parameters:**
  - `srcFile` (`File`) — the source file to be renamed. Can be `null`, in which case `false` is returned.
  - `newFileName` (`String`) — the new name for the file; must be a single path element (no separators or `..`). It is validated even when `srcFile` is `null`, so a bad name is always reported rather than masked by a `false` result.
- **Returns:** `true` if the renaming succeeded, `false` otherwise (including when `srcFile` is `null`).
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `newFileName` is `null`, empty, `"."`, `".."`, or contains a path separator.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File oldFile = new File("dir/old_name.txt");
    boolean success = IOUtil.renameTo(oldFile, "new_name.txt");   // the file becomes dir/new_name.txt
  ```
- **See also:** File#renameTo(File), #move(Path, Path, CopyOption...)
##### deleteQuietly(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean deleteQuietly(final File file)`
- **Summary:** Deletes the specified file or directory quietly, suppressing any exceptions that may occur.
- **Contract:**
  - If any exception occurs during the deletion process, it is caught and logged, and the method returns `false`.
  - It only deletes the file itself, not its contents if it's a directory with files.
- **Parameters:**
  - `file` (`File`) — the file or directory to delete. Can be `null`.
- **Returns:** `true` if the file was deleted successfully; `false` if the file is `null`, does not exist (a dangling symbolic link counts as present and is unlinked, as in #deleteIfExists(File)), could not be deleted, or if an exception occurred.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File file = new File("./temp-file.txt");
    boolean deleted = IOUtil.deleteQuietly(file);
    // No exception handling needed - method handles all errors internally
    System.out.println("File deleted: " + deleted);
  ```
- **See also:** File#delete(), Files#deleteIfExists(Path), #deleteIfExists(File), #deleteRecursivelyIfExists(File)
##### deleteIfExists(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean deleteIfExists(final File file)`
- **Summary:** Deletes the specified file if it exists by calling File#delete().
- **Contract:**
  - If the file is `null` or does not exist, the method returns `false` without attempting deletion.
- **Parameters:**
  - `file` (`File`) — the file or directory to delete. Can be `null`.
- **Returns:** `true` if the file was deleted successfully; `false` if the file is `null`, does not exist (and is not a dangling symbolic link), or could not be deleted.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File file = new File("./temp-file.txt");
    boolean deleted = IOUtil.deleteIfExists(file);
    if (deleted) {
        System.out.println("File deleted successfully.");
    } else {
        System.out.println("File does not exist or could not be deleted.");
    }
  ```
- **See also:** File#delete(), Files#delete(Path), Files#deleteIfExists(Path), #deleteRecursivelyIfExists(File), #deleteQuietly(File)
##### isSymbolicLinkOrJunction(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@Beta public static boolean isSymbolicLinkOrJunction(final File file) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Whether `file` is a directory entry that redirects elsewhere and must therefore never be descended into: a symbolic link on every platform, or a directory junction (mount point) on Windows.
- **Parameters:**
  - `file` (`File`) — the entry to classify; must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** `true` if the entry is a symbolic link or a Windows directory junction.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `file` is `null`.
##### deleteRecursivelyIfExists(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean deleteRecursivelyIfExists(final File file)`
- **Summary:** Deletes the specified file and all its subfiles/directories recursively if it's a directory.
- **Contract:**
  - If the specified file is a directory, it will delete all files and subdirectories within it before deleting the directory itself.
  - If the file is a regular file, it will simply delete the file.
  - If the file does not exist or is `null`, the method returns `false` without performing any operations.
  - Usage Examples: Deletion is best-effort and not transactional: every entry is attempted, one that cannot be removed does not stop the rest of the tree, and `false` is returned at the end if any of them failed - so a `false` result normally means the tree was partially removed rather than left untouched.
  - That includes a dangling link handed in directly: File#exists() answers `false` for one, but it is not "absent" here - the link itself is removed, exactly as it would be when met inside a tree.
- **Parameters:**
  - `file` (`File`) — the file or directory to delete recursively.
- **Returns:** `true` if the file/directory and all its contents were deleted successfully; `false` if the file is `null`, does not exist (and is not a dangling symbolic link), or any part of it could not be deleted (in which case part of the tree may already be gone).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File directory = new File("./temp-folder");
    boolean deleted = IOUtil.deleteRecursivelyIfExists(directory);
    if (deleted) {
        System.out.println("File/directory and all contents deleted successfully.");
    } else {
        System.out.println("File/directory does not exist or could not be deleted.");
    }
  ```
- **See also:** File#delete(), Files#delete(Path), Files#deleteIfExists(Path), #deleteIfExists(File), #deleteFilesFromDirectory(File)
##### deleteFilesFromDirectory(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean deleteFilesFromDirectory(final File dir)`
- **Summary:** Deletes all subfiles and subdirectories from the specified directory.
- **Contract:**
  - If the directory does not exist or is actually a file, the method returns `false` without performing any operations.
  - Usage Examples: Deletion is best-effort and not transactional: every entry is attempted, and `false` is returned at the end if any of them failed, so a `false` result normally means the directory was partially emptied.
- **Parameters:**
  - `dir` (`File`) — the directory from which to delete all files and subdirectories. Can be `null`.
- **Returns:** `true` if all files and directories were deleted successfully; `false` if `dir` is `null`, does not exist, is actually a file or a symbolic link, or some files could not be deleted or if the operation failed.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File directory = new File("./temp-folder");
    boolean deleted = IOUtil.deleteFilesFromDirectory(directory);
    if (deleted) {
        System.out.println("All files and subdirectories deleted successfully.");
    } else {
        System.out.println("Failed to delete some files or subdirectories.");
    }
  ```
- **See also:** File#delete(), Files#delete(Path), Files#deleteIfExists(Path), #deleteFilesFromDirectory(File, Throwables.BiPredicate), #deleteRecursivelyIfExists(File)
- **Signature:** `public static <E extends Exception> boolean deleteFilesFromDirectory(final File dir, final Throwables.BiPredicate<? super File, ? super File, E> filter) throws IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Summary:** Deletes subfiles/directories from the specified directory based on the provided filter.
- **Contract:**
  - Every subdirectory is descended into whether or not the filter accepted it, and a subdirectory is itself removed only when the filter accepted it and nothing inside it survived the filter.
  - Deletion is best-effort and not transactional: every entry is attempted, and `false` is returned at the end if any of them failed, so a `false` result normally means the tree was partially deleted.
  - `false` is also the answer when the protection above kicks in.
- **Parameters:**
  - `dir` (`File`) — the directory from which to delete files and subdirectories. Can be `null`.
  - `filter` (`Throwables.BiPredicate<? super File, ? super File, E>`) — the predicate to determine which files/directories should be deleted. Receives the parent directory and the file/directory being evaluated. It is consulted for every entry at every depth.
- **Returns:** `true` if every entry the filter accepted was deleted successfully; `false` if `dir` is `null`, does not exist, is actually a file or a symbolic link, or if any accepted entry could not be deleted.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is `null`.
  - `E` — if the filter throws an exception during evaluation.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File directory = new File("./temp-folder");
    // Delete only .txt files
    boolean deleted = IOUtil.deleteFilesFromDirectory(directory,
        (parentDir, file) -> file.getName().endsWith(".txt"));
    if (deleted) {
        System.out.println("Matching files deleted successfully.");
    } else {
        System.out.println("Failed to delete some files.");
    }
  ```
- **See also:** File#delete(), Files#delete(Path), Files#deleteIfExists(Path), #deleteFilesFromDirectory(File), #deleteRecursivelyIfExists(File)
##### createFileIfNotExists(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean createFileIfNotExists(final File file) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new empty file if one doesn't already exist at the specified path.
- **Contract:**
  - This method attempts to create a new file at the path specified by the input File object, but only if a file or directory doesn't already exist at that location.
  - If the parent directory doesn't exist, the method will attempt to create it before creating the file.
- **Parameters:**
  - `file` (`File`) — the File object representing the file to create.
- **Returns:** `true` if a new file was created successfully; `false` if an entry already exists at that path - a dangling symbolic link included, which `File.createNewFile()` counts as existing (nothing is created through it; #touch(File) does create the link's target).
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `file` is `null`.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if the filesystem cannot create `file`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File configFile = new File("/path/to/config.json");
    boolean created = IOUtil.createFileIfNotExists(configFile);
    if (created) {
        System.out.println("Created new config file");
    } else {
        System.out.println("Config file already exists");
    }
  ```
- **See also:** File#createNewFile(), #mkdirIfNotExists(File), #mkdirsIfNotExists(File)
##### mkdirIfNotExists(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean mkdirIfNotExists(final File dir) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a directory if it does not already exist.
- **Contract:**
  - If a directory with this name already exists, the method returns `false`.
  - If the directory does not exist, it is created.
  - It is returned both when the directory already existed and when creation failed, so it cannot be used as an error check.
- **Parameters:**
  - `dir` (`File`) — the directory to create, must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** `true` if the directory was created by this call; `false` if it already existed or if creation failed.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `dir` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File newDir = new File("./new-directory");
    boolean result = IOUtil.mkdirIfNotExists(newDir);
    if (result) {
        System.out.println("Directory was created successfully.");
    } else {
        System.out.println("Directory already exists or creation failed.");
    }
  ```
- **See also:** File#mkdir(), #mkdirsIfNotExists(File), #createFileIfNotExists(File), #isDirectory(File)
##### mkdirsIfNotExists(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("UnusedReturnValue") public static boolean mkdirsIfNotExists(final File dir) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates new directories if they do not exist.
- **Contract:**
  - If a directory with this name already exists, the method returns `false`.
  - If the directory does not exist, it and all necessary parent directories are created.
  - It is returned both when the directory already existed and when creation failed, so it cannot be used as an error check.
- **Parameters:**
  - `dir` (`File`) — the directory to create, including any necessary parent directories. Must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** `true` if the directories were created by this call; `false` if the directory already existed or if creation failed.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `dir` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File deepDir = new File("./parent/child/grandchild");
    boolean created = IOUtil.mkdirsIfNotExists(deepDir);
    if (created) {
        System.out.println("Directory hierarchy was created successfully.");
    } else {
        System.out.println("Directory already exists or creation failed.");
    }
  ```
- **See also:** File#mkdirs(), #mkdirIfNotExists(File), #createFileIfNotExists(File), #isDirectory(File)
