### Class IdentityHashSet (com.landawn.abacus.util.IdentityHashSet)
A Set implementation that uses reference-equality (==) instead of object-equality (equals()) when comparing elements.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- `public IdentityHashSet()` — Constructs a new, empty identity hash set with the default initial capacity of the backing IdentityHashMap.
  ```java
  IdentityHashSet<Object> set = new IdentityHashSet<>();
  ```
- `public IdentityHashSet(final int initialCapacity) throws IllegalArgumentException` — Constructs a new, empty identity hash set sized to hold approximately the specified number of elements.
  - **Throws:**
    - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the initial capacity is negative.
  ```java
  IdentityHashSet<String> set = new IdentityHashSet<>(100);
  ```
- `public IdentityHashSet(final Collection<? extends T> c)` — Constructs a new identity hash set containing the elements in the specified collection.
  ```java
  List<String> list = Arrays.asList("a", "b", "c");
    IdentityHashSet<String> set = new IdentityHashSet<>(list);
  ```

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### add(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@Override public boolean add(final T e)`
- **Summary:** Adds the specified element to this set if it is not already present using reference-equality comparison.
- **Contract:**
  - More formally, adds the specified element e to this set if the set contains no element e2 such that (e==e2).
- **Parameters:**
  - `e` (`T`) — element to be added to this set
- **Returns:** `true` if this set did not already contain the specified element
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IdentityHashSet<String> set = new IdentityHashSet<>();
    String s = "hello";
    boolean added = set.add(s);        // returns true
    boolean addedAgain = set.add(s);   // returns false
  ```
##### remove(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@Override public boolean remove(final Object o)`
- **Summary:** Removes the specified element from this set if it is present using reference-equality comparison.
- **Contract:**
  - More formally, removes an element e such that (o==e), if this set contains such an element.
- **Parameters:**
  - `o` (`Object`) — object to be removed from this set, if present
- **Returns:** `true` if the set contained the specified element
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IdentityHashSet<String> set = new IdentityHashSet<>();
    String s = "hello";
    set.add(s);
    boolean removed = set.remove(s);   // returns true
  ```
##### containsAll(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@Override public boolean containsAll(final Collection<?> c)`
- **Summary:** Returns `true` if this set contains all of the elements in the specified collection.
- **Parameters:**
  - `c` (`Collection<?>`) — collection to be checked for containment in this set; `null` is treated as empty
- **Returns:** `true` if this set contains all of the elements in the specified collection; `true` if `c` is `null` or empty
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IdentityHashSet<String> set = new IdentityHashSet<>();
    String s1 = "a", s2 = "b";
    set.add(s1);
    set.add(s2);
    boolean result = set.containsAll(Arrays.asList(s1, s2));   // returns true
  ```
##### addAll(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@Override public boolean addAll(final Collection<? extends T> c)`
- **Summary:** Adds all of the elements in the specified collection to this set using reference-equality comparison.
- **Contract:**
  - For each element e in the collection, it is added if the set contains no element e2 such that (e==e2).
- **Parameters:**
  - `c` (`Collection<? extends T>`) — collection containing elements to be added to this set; `null` is treated as empty
- **Returns:** `true` if this set changed as a result of the call
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IdentityHashSet<String> set = new IdentityHashSet<>();
    List<String> list = Arrays.asList("a", "b", "c");
    boolean changed = set.addAll(list);   // returns true
  ```
##### removeAll(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@Override public boolean removeAll(final Collection<?> c)`
- **Summary:** Removes from this set all of its elements that are contained in the specified collection using reference-equality comparison.
- **Parameters:**
  - `c` (`Collection<?>`) — collection containing elements to be removed from this set; `null` is treated as empty
- **Returns:** `true` if this set changed as a result of the call
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IdentityHashSet<String> set = new IdentityHashSet<>();
    String s1 = "a", s2 = "b";
    set.add(s1);
    set.add(s2);
    boolean changed = set.removeAll(Arrays.asList(s1));   // returns true, removes s1
  ```
##### retainAll(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@Override public boolean retainAll(final Collection<?> c)`
- **Summary:** Retains only the elements in this set that are contained in the specified collection using reference-equality comparison.
- **Parameters:**
  - `c` (`Collection<?>`) — collection containing elements to be retained in this set; `null` is treated as empty, which clears this set
- **Returns:** `true` if this set changed as a result of the call
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IdentityHashSet<String> set = new IdentityHashSet<>();
    String s1 = "a", s2 = "b", s3 = "c";
    set.add(s1);
    set.add(s2);
    set.add(s3);
    boolean changed = set.retainAll(Arrays.asList(s1, s2));   // returns true, keeps only s1 and s2
  ```
##### contains(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@Override public boolean contains(final Object valueToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns `true` if this set contains the specified element using reference-equality comparison.
- **Contract:**
  - More formally, returns `true` if and only if this set contains an element e such that (valueToFind==e).
- **Parameters:**
  - `valueToFind` (`Object`) — element whose presence in this set is to be tested
- **Returns:** `true` if this set contains the specified element based on reference equality
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IdentityHashSet<String> set = new IdentityHashSet<>();
    String s = "hello";
    set.add(s);
    boolean contains = set.contains(s);                        // returns true
    boolean containsNew = set.contains(new String("hello"));   // returns false
  ```
##### iterator(...) -> Iterator<T>
- **Signature:** `@Override public Iterator<T> iterator()`
- **Summary:** Returns an iterator over the elements in this set.
- **Contract:**
  - The iterator is fail-fast on a best-effort basis: structural modification outside the iterator after its creation will generally cause a java.util.ConcurrentModificationException, but this must not be relied on for correctness.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** an iterator over the elements in this set
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IdentityHashSet<String> set = new IdentityHashSet<>();
    set.add("a");
    set.add("b");
    Iterator<String> it = set.iterator();
    while (it.hasNext()) {
        String element = it.next();
        // process element
    }
  ```
##### toArray(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `@Override public Object[] toArray()`
- **Summary:** Returns an array containing all of the elements in this set.
- **Parameters:**

- **Returns:** an array containing all of the elements in this set
- **Examples:**
  ```java

    set.add("a");
    set.add("b");
    Object[] array = set.toArray();   // returns array with "a" and "b"
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Override public <A> A[] toArray(final A[] a) throws NullPointerException, ArrayStoreException`
- **Summary:** Returns an array containing all of the elements in this set; the runtime type of the returned array is that of the specified array.
- **Contract:**
  - If the set fits in the specified array, it is returned therein.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`A[]`) — the array into which the elements of this set are to be stored, if it is big enough; otherwise, a new array of the same runtime type is allocated
- **Returns:** an array containing all of the elements in this set
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `a` is `null`
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if the runtime type of the specified array is not a supertype of the runtime type of every element in this set
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IdentityHashSet<String> set = new IdentityHashSet<>();
    set.add("a");
    set.add("b");
    String[] array = set.toArray(new String[0]);   // returns String array with "a" and "b"
  ```
##### size(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `@Override public int size()`
- **Summary:** Returns the number of elements in this set (its cardinality).
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the number of elements in this set
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IdentityHashSet<String> set = new IdentityHashSet<>();
    set.add("a");
    set.add("b");
    int count = set.size();   // returns 2
  ```
##### isEmpty(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@Override public boolean isEmpty()`
- **Summary:** Returns `true` if this set contains no elements.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** `true` if this set contains no elements
- **Examples:**

  ```java
    set.add("a");
  ```

##### clear(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@Override public void clear()`
- **Summary:** Removes all of the elements from this set.
- **Parameters:**

##### equals(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("rawtypes") @Override public boolean equals(final Object o)`
- **Summary:** Compares the specified object with this set for equality using reference (identity) semantics.
- **Contract:**
  - Returns `true` only if the specified object is also an `IdentityHashSet` and the two sets contain the exact same object references (compared with `==`).
  - A non-`IdentityHashSet` (for example a java.util.HashSet) is never considered equal to this set, even if they appear to contain the same elements by `equals`.
- **Parameters:**

- **Returns:** `true` if `o` is an `IdentityHashSet` containing exactly the same object references as this set; `false` otherwise
- **Examples:**

#### Public Instance Methods
##### thenDoNothing(...) -> OrElse
- **Signature:** `public OrElse thenDoNothing()`
- **Summary:** Executes no action if the condition is `true`, but allows chaining to an `orElse` clause.
- **Contract:**
  - This method is useful when you only want to execute an action in the `false` case.
  - It provides a way to explicitly document the intent that no action should be taken when the condition is `true`, while still providing a fluent API for handling the `false` case.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** an OrElse instance for chaining the else clause
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Example 1: Cache check - only load if not cached
    If.is(cache.contains(key))
      .thenDoNothing()
      .orElse(() -> cache.load(key));
  
    // Example 2: Better alternative using negation
    If.not(cache.contains(key))
      .then(() -> cache.load(key));
  
    // Example 3: Explicit no-op with fallback
    If.notNull(config)
      .thenDoNothing()
      .orElse(() -> loadDefaultConfig());
  ```
##### then(...) -> OrElse
- **Signature:** `public <E extends Throwable> OrElse then(final Throwables.Runnable<E> cmd) throws IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Summary:** Executes the given runnable if the condition is `true`.
- **Contract:**
  - The provided runnable will be executed immediately if the condition evaluates to `true`, otherwise it will be skipped.
  - The method returns an OrElse instance that allows you to chain an alternative action to be executed when the condition is `false`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cmd` (`Throwables.Runnable<E>`) — the runnable to execute if the condition is `true`
- **Returns:** an OrElse instance for optional chaining of an else clause
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `cmd` is `null`.
  - `E` — if the condition is true and the supplied callback throws during execution
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Example 1: Simple conditional execution
    If.is(debugMode)
      .then(() -> logger.debug("Debug information"))
      .orElse(() -> logger.info("Normal operation"));
  
    // Example 2: Validation and processing
    If.notEmpty(items)
      .then(() -> processItems(items))
      .orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalStateException("No items to process"));
  
    // Example 3: Conditional side effects
    If.is(shouldCache)
      .then(() -> cache.put(key, value));
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Beta public <T, E extends Throwable> OrElse then(final T init, final Throwables.Consumer<? super T, E> action) throws IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Executes the given consumer with the provided input if the condition is `true`.
- **Contract:**
  - This method is useful for conditional processing of a value, allowing you to pass an initialization parameter that will be consumed if the condition evaluates to `true`.
  - This is particularly valuable when you need to perform an action with a specific context or parameter only when certain conditions are met.
- **Parameters:**
  - `init` (`T`) — the input value to pass to the consumer (can be `null`)
  - `action` (`Throwables.Consumer<? super T, E>`) — the consumer to execute if the condition is `true`
- **Returns:** an OrElse instance for optional chaining of an else clause
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `action` is `null`.
  - `E` — if the condition is true and the supplied callback throws during execution
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Example 1: Conditional processing with context
    If.notNull(user)
      .then(user, u -> saveUser(u))
      .orElse(() -> createNewUser());
  
    // Example 2: Conditional initialization with parameter
    ProcessingContext context = new ProcessingContext();
    If.notEmpty(dataList)
      .then(context, ctx -> {
          ctx.initialize();
          processDataWithContext(ctx, dataList);
      })
      .orElse(() -> handleEmptyData());
  ```
##### thenThrow(...) -> OrElse
- **Signature:** `public <E extends Throwable> OrElse thenThrow(final Supplier<? extends E> exceptionSupplier) throws IllegalArgumentException, NullPointerException, E`
- **Summary:** Throws the exception provided by the supplier if the condition is `true`.
- **Contract:**
  - This method is useful for validation scenarios where an exception should be thrown when a certain condition is met.
  - The exception supplier is only invoked if the condition is `true`, allowing for lazy creation of exception instances with dynamic messages or context.
  - Note: While this method returns an OrElse instance to maintain API consistency, it will never be reached if the condition is `true` since an exception will be thrown.
  - The `orElse()` methods can only be invoked if the condition is `false`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `exceptionSupplier` (`Supplier<? extends E>`) — the supplier that provides the exception to throw
- **Returns:** an OrElse instance for optional chaining of an else clause (unreachable if the condition is true)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `exceptionSupplier` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if the condition is true and `exceptionSupplier` returns `null`
  - `E` — if the condition is true
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Example 1: Validation with custom exception
    If.isEmpty(requiredField)
      .thenThrow(() -> new ValidationException("Required field is empty"));
  
    // Example 2: Guard clause pattern
    If.isNull(user)
      .thenThrow(() -> new IllegalArgumentException("User cannot be null"));
  
    // Example 3: Business rule validation with dynamic message
    If.is(amount < 0)
      .thenThrow(() -> new IllegalArgumentException("Amount must be positive: " + amount));
  
    // Example 4: With orElse fallback (only executes if condition is false)
    If.isEmpty(data)
      .thenThrow(() -> new DataNotFoundException("No data available"))
      .orElse(() -> processData(data));
  ```

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

- (none)

- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### orElseDoNothing(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public void orElseDoNothing()`
- **Summary:** Completes the conditional chain without performing any action when the initial condition was `false`.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)

  ```java

      .then(() -> stats.recordHit())
      .orElseDoNothing();   // explicit: a miss is not interesting here
  ```
##### orElse(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public <E extends Throwable> void orElse(final Throwables.Runnable<E> cmd) throws IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Summary:** Executes the given runnable if the initial condition was `false`.
- **Contract:**
  - This method completes the conditional chain by providing an alternative action to be executed when the initial `If` condition evaluates to `false`.
  - The provided runnable will only be executed if the initial condition was `false`.
  - If the condition was `true`, this method does nothing.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cmd` (`Throwables.Runnable<E>`) — the runnable to execute if the initial condition was `false`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `cmd` is `null`.
  - `E` — if the initial condition is false and the supplied callback throws during execution
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Example 1: Simple if-else pattern
    If.is(hasPermission)
      .then(() -> performAction())
      .orElse(() -> showAccessDeniedMessage());
  
    // Example 2: Fallback logic
    If.notEmpty(cache)
      .then(() -> loadFromCache())
      .orElse(() -> loadFromDatabase());
  
    // Example 3: Store either a preference or a default
    String userPreference = loadUserPreference();
    Holder<String> setting = Holder.of(null);
    If.notNull(userPreference)
      .then(() -> setting.setValue(userPreference))
      .orElse(() -> setting.setValue("default"));
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Beta public <T, E extends Throwable> void orElse(final T init, final Throwables.Consumer<? super T, E> action) throws IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Executes the given consumer with the provided input if the initial condition was `false`.
- **Contract:**
  - This method allows you to pass an initialization parameter that will be consumed if the initial condition evaluates to `false`.
  - This is particularly useful when you need to provide a fallback action with specific context or parameters.
- **Parameters:**
  - `init` (`T`) — the input value to pass to the consumer (can be `null`)
  - `action` (`Throwables.Consumer<? super T, E>`) — the consumer to execute if the initial condition was `false`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `action` is `null`.
  - `E` — if the initial condition is false and the supplied callback throws during execution
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Example 1: Fallback with parameter
    String key = "user:42";
    String cachedValue = findInCache(key);
    Holder<String> value = Holder.of(null);
    If.notNull(cachedValue)
      .then(() -> value.setValue(cachedValue))
      .orElse(key, k -> value.setValue(loadFromDatabase(k)));
  
    // Example 2: Context-based fallback
    ProcessingContext context = new ProcessingContext();
    If.notEmpty(dataList)
      .then(context, ctx -> processData(ctx, dataList))
      .orElse(context, ctx -> setDefaultProcessingMode(ctx));
  ```
##### orElseThrow(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public <E extends Throwable> void orElseThrow(final Supplier<? extends E> exceptionSupplier) throws IllegalArgumentException, NullPointerException, E`
- **Summary:** Throws the exception provided by the supplier if the initial condition was `false`.
- **Contract:**
  - This method is useful for validation scenarios where an exception should be thrown when a required condition is not met.
  - It provides a fluent way to express validation requirements and ensures that execution cannot continue when expected conditions fail.
  - The exception supplier is only invoked if the initial condition was `false`, allowing for lazy creation of exception instances with dynamic messages or context.
  - If the condition was `true`, this method does nothing and execution continues normally.
- **Parameters:**
  - `exceptionSupplier` (`Supplier<? extends E>`) — the supplier that provides the exception to throw
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `exceptionSupplier` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if the initial condition is false and `exceptionSupplier` returns `null`
  - `E` — if the initial condition was false
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Example 1: Validation after processing
    If.notEmpty(results)
      .then(() -> processResults(results))
      .orElseThrow(() -> new NoResultsException("No results found"));
  
    // Example 2: Required condition check
    If.notNull(user)
      .then(() -> authenticateUser(user))
      .orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalStateException("User must not be null"));
  
    // Example 3: Business rule enforcement
    If.is(balance >= amount)
      .then(() -> processWithdrawal(amount))
      .orElseThrow(() -> new InsufficientFundsException("Balance: " + balance + ", Required: " + amount));
  
    // Example 4: Data validation
    If.notBlank(email)
      .then(() -> sendEmail(email))
      .orElseThrow(() -> new ValidationException("Email address is required"));
  ```

  - `k4` (`K`) — the fourth key
  - `v4` (`V`) — the value associated with `k4`
  - `k5` (`K`) — the fifth key
  - `v5` (`V`) — the value associated with `k5`
  - `k6` (`K`) — the sixth key
  - `v6` (`V`) — the value associated with `k6`
  - `k7` (`K`) — the seventh key
  - `v7` (`V`) — the value associated with `k7`
  - `k8` (`K`) — the eighth key
  - `v8` (`V`) — the value associated with `k8`
  - `k9` (`K`) — the ninth key
  - `v9` (`V`) — the value associated with `k9`
  - `k10` (`K`) — the tenth key
  - `v10` (`V`) — the value associated with `k10`
- **Returns:** an `ImmutableBiMap` containing the provided key-value pairs
- **Throws:**

- **Examples:**
  ```java

        "one", 1, "two", 2, "three", 3, "four", 4, "five", 5,
        "six", 6, "seven", 7, "eight", 8, "nine", 9, "ten", 10
    );
  ```
##### copyOf(...) -> ImmutableBiMap<K, V>
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> ImmutableBiMap<K, V> copyOf(final BiMap<? extends K, ? extends V> map) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns an `ImmutableBiMap` containing the same mappings as the provided BiMap.
- **Contract:**
  - If the provided `BiMap` is `null` or empty, this method returns #empty().
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`BiMap<? extends K, ? extends V>`) — the `BiMap` whose mappings are to be copied; may be `null`
- **Returns:** an `ImmutableBiMap` containing the same mappings as `map`, or #empty() if `map` is `null` or empty
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `map`'s own map suppliers do not return a new, empty, distinct map on each call, because the defensive copy is made by BiMap#copy()
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  BiMap<String, Integer> mutable = new BiMap<>();
    mutable.put("one", 1);
    mutable.put("two", 2);
  
    ImmutableBiMap<String, Integer> immutable = ImmutableBiMap.copyOf(mutable);
    mutable.put("three", 3);   // does not affect 'immutable'
  ```
- **See also:** #copyOf(Map)
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("unchecked") public static <K, V> ImmutableBiMap<K, V> copyOf(final Map<? extends K, ? extends V> map) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns an `ImmutableBiMap` containing the same mappings as the provided Map.
- **Contract:**
  - If the provided map is `null` or empty, this method returns #empty().
  - The copy is skipped only when `map` is an `ImmutableBiMap` that already owns its backing storage - one produced by `of(...)`, `copyOf(...)`, #empty() or the no-arg #builder(), or the #inverse() of such a map.
  - The map's values must be unique, as required by BiMap; the entries are inserted in the source's iteration order, so which entry is reported as the offender for a duplicate value depends on that order.
  - Build the entries into a `BiMap` whose backing maps you chose and call #wrap(BiMap) (or #copyOf(BiMap)) when a particular order matters.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<? extends K, ? extends V>`) — the map whose mappings are to be copied; may be `null`
- **Returns:** the same instance if `map` is already an `ImmutableBiMap` that owns its backing storage; #empty() if `map` is `null` or empty; otherwise a new `ImmutableBiMap` containing a defensive copy of the mappings
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any key or value in `map` is `null`, or if a value is bound to more than one key, or - when `map` is a `BiMap`-backed source that has to be copied - if that source's map suppliers do not return a new, empty, distinct map on each call, because the copy is then made by BiMap#copy().
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  BiMap<String, Integer> mutable = new BiMap<>();
    mutable.put("one", 1);
  
    ImmutableBiMap<String, Integer> view = ImmutableBiMap.wrap(mutable);
    ImmutableBiMap<String, Integer> snapshot = ImmutableBiMap.copyOf(view);
  
    mutable.put("two", 2);   // visible through view, but NOT through snapshot
  ```
- **See also:** #copyOf(BiMap)
##### wrap(...) -> ImmutableBiMap<K, V>
- **Signature:** `@Beta public static <K, V> ImmutableBiMap<K, V> wrap(final BiMap<? extends K, ? extends V> map)`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Wraps the provided BiMap in an `ImmutableBiMap` without copying its entries.
- **Contract:**
  - If the provided `BiMap` is `null`, this method returns #empty().
  - Use #copyOf(BiMap) when subsequent changes to the source must not be visible.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`BiMap<? extends K, ? extends V>`) — the `BiMap` to wrap; may be `null`
- **Returns:** an `ImmutableBiMap` view backed by `map`, or #empty() if `map` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  BiMap<String, Integer> mutable = new BiMap<>();
    mutable.put("one", 1);
  
    ImmutableBiMap<String, Integer> wrapped = ImmutableBiMap.wrap(mutable);
    mutable.put("two", 2);   // this WILL be visible through 'wrapped'
  ```
##### builder(...) -> Builder<K, V>
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> Builder<K, V> builder()`
- **Summary:** Creates a new Builder for constructing an `ImmutableBiMap`.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful when the number of entries is not known at compile time or when entries are added conditionally.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a new `Builder` instance for creating an `ImmutableBiMap`
- **Examples:**
  ```java

        .put("one", 1)
        .put("two", 2)
        .put("three", 3)
        .build();
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> Builder<K, V> builder(final BiMap<K, V> backedMap) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new Builder for constructing an `ImmutableBiMap` using the provided BiMap as backing storage.
- **Contract:**
  - The builder will add entries to the provided `BiMap` and then create an immutable view of it when Builder#build() is called.
  - The given `BiMap` should not be modified outside the builder after this method is invoked.
  - Use the no-arg #builder() when an independent value is wanted.
- **Parameters:**
  - `backedMap` (`BiMap<K, V>`) — the `BiMap` to be used as backing storage for the builder
- **Returns:** a new `Builder` instance that uses `backedMap` as storage
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `backedMap` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  BiMap<String, Integer> backing = new BiMap<>();
    ImmutableBiMap<String, Integer> map = ImmutableBiMap.builder(backing)
        .put("one", 1)
        .put("two", 2)
        .build();
  ```

#### Public Instance Methods
##### getByValue(...) -> K
- **Signature:** `public K getByValue(final Object value) throws NullPointerException, ClassCastException`
- **Summary:** Returns the key to which the specified value is mapped in this `BiMap`, or `null` if this map contains no mapping for the value.
- **Parameters:**
  - `value` (`Object`) — the value whose associated key is to be returned
- **Returns:** the key to which the specified value is mapped, or `null` if this map contains no mapping for the value
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `value` is `null` and the backing `BiMap`'s value-to-key map does not permit `null` keys (optional). The `of(...)` factories and #empty() always build one that permits it; #copyOf(Map) instead derives the value map from the source, so a java.util.Hashtable or java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap source - or a `BiMap` or `ImmutableBiMap` source whose own value map rejects `null` keys - produces one that does not
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if `value` has a type that the reverse backing map cannot query or compare
- **Examples:**

  ```java
        "two", 2

  ```

- **Signature:** `public Builder<K, V> put(final K key, final V value) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Associates the specified value with the specified key in the map being built.

  - `value` (`V`) — the value to be associated with the specified key

  ```java
           .put("another", "data");
  ```

##### putAll(...) -> Builder<K, V>
- **Signature:** `public Builder<K, V> putAll(final Map<? extends K, ? extends V> m) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Copies all mappings from the specified map into the map being built.
- **Contract:**
  - If the provided map is `null` or empty, this method has no effect.

### Class ImmutableEntry (com.landawn.abacus.util.ImmutableEntry)
An immutable implementation of Map.Entry that represents a key-value pair that cannot be modified after creation.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified
**Annotations:** @Immutable

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### of(...) -> ImmutableEntry<K, V>
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> ImmutableEntry<K, V> of(final K key, final V value)`
- **Summary:** Creates an ImmutableEntry with the specified key and value.
- **Parameters:**
  - `key` (`K`) — the key for this entry, may be null
  - `value` (`V`) — the value for this entry, may be null
- **Returns:** a new ImmutableEntry containing the specified key-value pair
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableEntry<String, Integer> entry = ImmutableEntry.of("age", 25);
    System.out.println(entry.getKey());     // prints age
    System.out.println(entry.getValue());   // prints 25
  
    // Null values are allowed
    ImmutableEntry<String, String> nullEntry = ImmutableEntry.of("missing", null);
  ```
##### copyOf(...) -> ImmutableEntry<K, V>
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> ImmutableEntry<K, V> copyOf(final Map.Entry<? extends K, ? extends V> entry) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates an `ImmutableEntry` by copying the key and value from an existing Map.Entry.
- **Contract:**
  - The key and value are captured at the moment this method is called; subsequent changes to the source entry's value (if it is a mutable entry) do not affect the returned copy.
  - If the provided entry contains a `null` key or value, the returned `ImmutableEntry` will also contain `null` for those fields.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entry` (`Map.Entry<? extends K, ? extends V>`) — the entry whose key and value are to be copied; must not be `null`
- **Returns:** a new `ImmutableEntry` with the same key and value as the provided entry
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `entry` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("count", 100);
  
    Map.Entry<String, Integer> mutableEntry = map.entrySet().iterator().next();
    ImmutableEntry<String, Integer> immutableCopy = ImmutableEntry.copyOf(mutableEntry);
  
    // Modifying the source entry does not affect the snapshot copy
    mutableEntry.setValue(200);
    System.out.println(immutableCopy.getValue());   // still prints 100
  ```

### Class ImmutableList (com.landawn.abacus.util.ImmutableList)

**Thread-safety:** conditional
**Nullability:** unspecified
**Annotations:** @Immutable
**Permitted subtypes:** ImmutableList.ReverseImmutableList, ImmutableList.RandomAccessImmutableList

##### copyOf(...) -> ImmutableList<E>
- **Signature:** `public static <E> ImmutableList<E> copyOf(final E[] elements)`
- **Summary:** Returns an `ImmutableList` containing the elements of the specified array.
- **Contract:**
  - If the array is `null` or empty, an empty `ImmutableList` is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `elements` (`E[]`) — the array whose elements are to be placed into the `ImmutableList`; may be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** an `ImmutableList` containing the elements of `elements`, or an empty list if `elements` is `null` or empty
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String[] array = { "a", "b", "c" };
    ImmutableList<String> list = ImmutableList.copyOf(array);
  
    array[0] = "x";   // Does not affect list
    // list => ["a", "b", "c"]
  ```
- **See also:** #copyOf(Collection)
- **Signature:** `public static <E> ImmutableList<E> copyOf(final Collection<? extends E> c)`
- **Summary:** Returns an ImmutableList containing all elements from the provided collection.
- **Contract:**
  - If the collection is `null` or empty, an empty ImmutableList is returned.
  - The copy is skipped only when `c` is an `ImmutableList` that already owns its backing storage - that is, one produced by `of(...)`, `copyOf(...)`, #empty(), by a consumed no-argument #builder(), by `toImmutableList()` on an ObjIterator (or on any other iterator type in this package), or by #subList(int, int) or #reversed() over such a list.
  - Wrap the range in a fresh collection (`ImmutableList.copyOf(new ArrayList<>(sub))`) when a small range of a large list must stop retaining it.
- **Parameters:**
  - `c` (`Collection<? extends E>`) — the collection whose elements are to be placed into the `ImmutableList`; may be `null` or empty.
- **Returns:** the same instance if `c` is already an `ImmutableList` that owns its backing storage; an empty `ImmutableList` if `c` is `null` or empty; otherwise a new `ImmutableList` containing a defensive copy of the collection's elements.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<Integer> mutable = new ArrayList<>(Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3));
    ImmutableList<Integer> immutable = ImmutableList.copyOf(mutable);
    mutable.add(4);   // Does not affect immutable
  
    ImmutableList<Integer> view = ImmutableList.wrap(mutable);
    ImmutableList<Integer> copy = ImmutableList.copyOf(view);
    mutable.add(5);   // Visible through view, but NOT through copy
  ```
- **See also:** #copyOf(Object\[\]), #wrap(List)
##### wrap(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `@Beta public static <E> ImmutableList<E> wrap(final List<? extends E> list)`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Wraps the provided list into an ImmutableList without copying the elements.
- **Contract:**
  - If the provided list is already an ImmutableList, it is returned directly.
  - If the list is `null`, an empty ImmutableList is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `list` (`List<? extends E>`) — the list to be wrapped into an `ImmutableList`; may be `null`.
- **Returns:** the same instance if `list` is already an `ImmutableList`; an empty `ImmutableList` if `list` is `null`; otherwise an `ImmutableList` view backed by `list`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> mutable = new ArrayList<>();
    mutable.add("initial");
  
    ImmutableList<String> wrapped = ImmutableList.wrap(mutable);
    mutable.add("added later");           // This WILL be visible in wrapped!
    System.out.println(wrapped.get(1));   // prints "added later"
  ```
- **See also:** #copyOf(Collection)
- **Signature:** `@Deprecated public static <E> ImmutableCollection<E> wrap(final Collection<? extends E> c) throws UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** This method is deprecated and will always throw an UnsupportedOperationException.
- **Parameters:**
  - `c` (`Collection<? extends E>`) — the collection to wrap.
- **Returns:** never returns normally.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — always.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Collection<String> c = Arrays.asList("a", "b");
    ImmutableList.wrap(c);   // throws UnsupportedOperationException
  ```
##### builder(...) -> Builder<E>
- **Signature:** `public static <E> Builder<E> builder()`
- **Summary:** Creates a new Builder for constructing an ImmutableList.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful when the number of elements is not known at compile time.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a new Builder instance for creating an ImmutableList.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableList<String> list = ImmutableList.<String>builder()
        .add("first")
        .add("second", "third")
        .addAll(Arrays.asList("fourth", "fifth"))
        .build();
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <E> Builder<E> builder(final List<E> holder) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new Builder for constructing an ImmutableList using the provided list as storage.
- **Contract:**
  - Note that the provided list should not be modified outside the builder after this call.
  - Use the no-arg #builder() when an independent value is wanted.
- **Parameters:**
  - `holder` (`List<E>`) — the list to be used as the backing storage for the Builder; must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a new Builder instance that will use the provided list.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if holder is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<Integer> backingList = new ArrayList<>();
    ImmutableList<Integer> numbers = ImmutableList.builder(backingList)
        .add(1)
        .add(2, 3, 4)
        .build();
  ```

##### get(...) -> E
- **Signature:** `@Override public E get(final int index) throws IndexOutOfBoundsException`
- **Summary:** Returns the element at the specified position in this list.
- **Contract:**
  - The index must be valid (between 0 inclusive and size() exclusive).
- **Parameters:**
  - `index` (`int`) — the index of the element to return (0-based).
- **Returns:** the element at the specified position in this list.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if the index is out of range (index < 0 || index >= size()).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableList<String> list = ImmutableList.of("a", "b", "c");
    String second = list.get(1);   // returns "b"
  ```
- **See also:** List#get(int)
##### indexOf(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `@Override public int indexOf(final Object valueToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index of the first occurrence of the specified element in this list, or -1 if this list does not contain the element.
- **Contract:**
  - If multiple equal elements exist, the index of the first one is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `valueToFind` (`Object`) — the element to search for, may be `null`.
- **Returns:** the index of the first occurrence of the specified element in this list, or -1 if this list does not contain the element.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableList<String> list = ImmutableList.of("a", "b", "c", "b");
    int index = list.indexOf("b");      // returns 1
    int notFound = list.indexOf("d");   // returns -1
  ```
- **See also:** List#indexOf(Object)

##### listIterator(...) -> ImmutableListIterator<E>
- **Signature:** `@Override public ImmutableListIterator<E> listIterator()`
- **Summary:** Returns an immutable list iterator over the elements in this list in proper sequence.
- **Contract:**
  - The returned iterator does not support `remove()`, `set()`, or `add()` and will throw UnsupportedOperationException if any of those operations are called.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** an immutable list iterator over the elements in this list in proper sequence.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableList<String> list = ImmutableList.of("a", "b", "c");
    ImmutableListIterator<String> iter = list.listIterator();
    while (iter.hasNext()) {
        System.out.println(iter.next());
    }
  ```
- **See also:** List#listIterator()
- **Signature:** `@Override public ImmutableListIterator<E> listIterator(final int index) throws IndexOutOfBoundsException`
- **Summary:** Returns an immutable list iterator over the elements in this list in proper sequence, starting at the specified position in the list.
- **Parameters:**
  - `index` (`int`) — the index of the first element to be returned from the list iterator (by a call to next()).
- **Returns:** an immutable list iterator over the elements in this list starting at the specified position.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if the index is out of range (index < 0 || index > size()).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableList<String> list = ImmutableList.of("a", "b", "c", "d");
    ImmutableListIterator<String> iter = list.listIterator(2);
    System.out.println(iter.next());       // prints "c"
    System.out.println(iter.previous());   // prints "c" again
    System.out.println(iter.previous());   // prints "b"
  ```
- **See also:** List#listIterator(int)
##### subList(...) -> ImmutableList<E>
- **Signature:** `@Override public ImmutableList<E> subList(final int fromIndex, final int toIndex) throws IndexOutOfBoundsException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns an immutable view of the portion of this list between the specified `fromIndex` (inclusive) and `toIndex` (exclusive).
- **Contract:**
  - The semantics of the sublist are consistent with List.subList(), including the behavior when fromIndex equals toIndex (returns an empty list).
  - Take the sublist of a #copyOf(Collection) when the source may still change.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the low endpoint (inclusive) of the subList.
  - `toIndex` (`int`) — the high endpoint (exclusive) of the subList.
- **Returns:** an immutable view of the specified range within this list.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — for an out-of-range endpoint index (fromIndex < 0 || toIndex > size).
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fromIndex > toIndex`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableList<String> list = ImmutableList.of("a", "b", "c", "d", "e");
    ImmutableList<String> sub = list.subList(1, 4);
    // sub contains ["b", "c", "d"]
  ```
- **See also:** List#subList(int, int)

##### reversed(...) -> ImmutableList<E>
- **Signature:** `@Override public ImmutableList<E> reversed()`
- **Summary:** Returns a view of this immutable list in reverse order.
- **Contract:**
  - If this list owns its backing storage (it came from `of(...)`, `copyOf(...)`, #empty(), a consumed no-argument #builder(), `toImmutableList()` on an ObjIterator, or #subList(int, int) over such a list) and has one or zero elements, this same instance is returned, because such a list can never differ from its own reverse.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** an immutable view of this list with elements in reverse order; this same instance if this list owns its backing storage and has zero or one element.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> reversed = ImmutableList.of("a", "b", "c").reversed();
    // reversed contains ["c", "b", "a"]
  ```

### Class Builder (com.landawn.abacus.util.ImmutableList.Builder)
A builder for creating ImmutableList instances.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

- (none)

- (none)

##### add(...) -> Builder<E>
- **Signature:** `public Builder<E> add(final E element) throws IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Adds a single element to the list being built.
- **Parameters:**
  - `element` (`E`) — the element to add, may be `null`.
- **Returns:** this builder instance for method chaining.
- **Throws:**

- **Examples:**


- **Parameters:**

  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if #build() has already been called on this builder.


- **Signature:** `public ImmutableList<E> build()`
- **Summary:** Builds and returns an ImmutableList containing all elements added to this builder.
- **Contract:**

### Class ImmutableListIterator (com.landawn.abacus.util.ImmutableListIterator)
An immutable implementation of ListIterator that provides read-only iteration over list elements in both forward and backward directions.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### empty(...) -> ImmutableListIterator<T>
- **Signature:** `public static <T> ImmutableListIterator<T> empty()`
- **Summary:** Returns an empty ImmutableListIterator.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a shared singleton empty `ImmutableListIterator` instance
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableListIterator<String> empty = ImmutableListIterator.empty();
    System.out.println(empty.hasNext());         // prints false
    System.out.println(empty.nextIndex());       // prints 0
    System.out.println(empty.previousIndex());   // prints -1
  ```
##### of(...) -> ImmutableListIterator<T>
- **Signature:** `public static <T> ImmutableListIterator<T> of(final ListIterator<? extends T> iter)`
- **Summary:** Creates an ImmutableListIterator that wraps the provided ListIterator.
- **Contract:**
  - If the provided iterator is `null` — or is the shared instance returned by #empty() — an empty ImmutableListIterator is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `iter` (`ListIterator<? extends T>`) — the ListIterator to wrap; may be `null`
- **Returns:** an `ImmutableListIterator` wrapping the provided iterator, or #empty() if `iter` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<Integer> numbers = new ArrayList<>(Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3));
    ListIterator<Integer> mutableIter = numbers.listIterator();
    ImmutableListIterator<Integer> immutableIter = ImmutableListIterator.of(mutableIter);
  
    // Can iterate but not modify
    while (immutableIter.hasNext()) {
        System.out.println(immutableIter.next());
    }
    // immutableIter.set(4);   // Would throw UnsupportedOperationException
  ```
- **See also:** #empty()

#### Public Instance Methods
##### set(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@Deprecated @Override public void set(final T e) throws UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** This operation is not supported by `ImmutableListIterator`.
- **Contract:**
  - Use a mutable ListIterator if you need to modify elements during iteration.
- **Parameters:**
  - `e` (`T`) — the element with which to replace the last element returned by #next() or #previous()
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — always, as this is an immutable iterator
##### add(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@Deprecated @Override public void add(final T e) throws UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** This operation is not supported by `ImmutableListIterator`.
- **Contract:**
  - Use a mutable ListIterator if you need to add elements during iteration.
- **Parameters:**
  - `e` (`T`) — the element to insert
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — always, as this is an immutable iterator

##### copyOf(...) -> ImmutableMap<K, V>
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> ImmutableMap<K, V> copyOf(final Map<? extends K, ? extends V> map)`
- **Summary:** Returns an ImmutableMap containing all mappings from the provided map.
- **Contract:**
  - If the map is `null` or empty, an empty ImmutableMap is returned.
  - The copy is skipped only when `map` is a plain `ImmutableMap` that already owns its backing storage - that is, one produced by this class's own `of(...)`, `copyOf(...)`, #empty(), or a consumed no-argument #builder().
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<? extends K, ? extends V>`) — the map whose mappings are to be placed in the `ImmutableMap`.
- **Returns:** an `ImmutableMap` containing all mappings from the source map, in the source's entry iteration order; the same instance if it is already a plain `ImmutableMap` that owns its backing storage; or an empty instance if `map` is `null` or empty.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> mutable = new HashMap<>();
    mutable.put("a", 1);
    mutable.put("b", 2);
    ImmutableMap<String, Integer> immutable = ImmutableMap.copyOf(mutable);
    mutable.put("c", 3);                    // Does not affect immutable
    System.out.println(immutable.size());   // still prints 2
  ```
- **See also:** #wrap(Map)
##### wrap(...) -> ImmutableMap<K, V>
- **Signature:** `@Beta public static <K, V> ImmutableMap<K, V> wrap(final Map<? extends K, ? extends V> map)`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Wraps the provided map into an ImmutableMap without copying the entries.
- **Contract:**
  - If the provided map is already an ImmutableMap, it is returned directly.
  - If the map is `null`, an empty ImmutableMap is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<? extends K, ? extends V>`) — the map to be wrapped into an `ImmutableMap`.
- **Returns:** an `ImmutableMap` view backed by the provided map, or the same instance if it is already an `ImmutableMap`, or an empty instance if `map` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> mutable = new HashMap<>();
    mutable.put("a", 1);
    ImmutableMap<String, Integer> wrapped = ImmutableMap.wrap(mutable);
    mutable.put("b", 2);                  // This change IS visible in wrapped!
    System.out.println(wrapped.size());   // prints 2
  ```
- **See also:** #copyOf(Map)

- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> Builder<K, V> builder()`
- **Summary:** Creates a new Builder for constructing an ImmutableMap.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful when the number of entries is not known at compile time.

- **Returns:** a new Builder instance for creating an ImmutableMap.

### Class Builder (com.landawn.abacus.util.ImmutableMap.Builder)

- (none)

- (none)

##### put(...) -> Builder<K, V>
- **Signature:** `public Builder<K, V> put(final K key, final V value) throws IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Associates the specified value with the specified key in the map being built.
- **Contract:**
  - If the map previously contained a mapping for the key, the old value is replaced.
- **Parameters:**
  - `key` (`K`) — the key with which the specified value is to be associated.
  - `value` (`V`) — the value to be associated with the specified key.
- **Returns:** this builder instance for method chaining.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if #build() has already been called on this builder.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  builder.put("key", "value")
           .put("another", "data");
  ```
##### putAll(...) -> Builder<K, V>
- **Signature:** `public Builder<K, V> putAll(final Map<? extends K, ? extends V> m) throws IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Copies all of the mappings from the specified map to the map being built.
- **Contract:**
  - The behavior is undefined if the specified map is modified while this operation is in progress.
  - If the map is `null` or empty, no entries are added.
- **Parameters:**
  - `m` (`Map<? extends K, ? extends V>`) — the map whose mappings are to be added, may be `null` or empty.
- **Returns:** this builder instance for method chaining.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if #build() has already been called on this builder.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> existing = Map.of("a", 1, "b", 2);
    builder.putAll(existing)
           .put("c", 3);
  ```
##### build(...) -> ImmutableMap<K, V>
- **Signature:** `public ImmutableMap<K, V> build()`
- **Summary:** Builds and returns an ImmutableMap containing all entries added to this builder.
- **Contract:**
  - When the builder was created by ImmutableMap#builder() its storage is private and the result is an independent value; when it was created by ImmutableMap#builder(Map) the caller can still modify the map it supplied, so the result stays a live view and ImmutableMap#copyOf(Map) will copy it.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a new ImmutableMap containing all added entries.
- **Examples:**
  ```java

    // builder.put("more", 1);   // throws IllegalStateException
  ```

##### copyOf(...) -> ImmutableNavigableMap<K, V>
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> ImmutableNavigableMap<K, V> copyOf(final Map<? extends K, ? extends V> map) throws NullPointerException, ClassCastException`
- **Summary:** Returns an ImmutableNavigableMap containing the same mappings as the provided Map.
- **Contract:**
  - If the provided Map is already an instance of ImmutableNavigableMap that owns its backing storage (one produced by `of(...)`, `copyOf(...)` or #empty()), it is directly returned; a #wrap(NavigableMap)-created view is copied like any other map.
  - If the provided Map is `null`, or is empty and not a SortedMap, an empty ImmutableNavigableMap is returned.
  - If the source is a SortedMap, the returned map uses the same java.util.Comparator (or natural ordering) as the source, even when the source is empty.
  - Wrap the view in a fresh map (`copyOf(new TreeMap<>(view))`) when a small view of a large map must stop retaining it.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<? extends K, ? extends V>`) — the Map whose mappings are to be placed in the `ImmutableNavigableMap`
- **Returns:** an `ImmutableNavigableMap` containing the same mappings as the provided map, or the same instance if it is already an `ImmutableNavigableMap` that owns its backing storage. The comparator of a `SortedMap` source is retained even when the source is empty; a `null` or empty non-sorted source returns the shared empty instance.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if the map contains a `null` key and natural ordering is used
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if the keys are not mutually comparable (when the source map is not a `SortedMap`)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> mutable = new HashMap<>();
    mutable.put("b", 2);
    mutable.put("a", 1);
    ImmutableNavigableMap<String, Integer> immutable = ImmutableNavigableMap.copyOf(mutable);
    mutable.put("c", 3);             // does not affect immutable
    System.out.println(immutable);   // prints {a=1, b=2}
  ```
- **See also:** #wrap(NavigableMap)
##### wrap(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `@Beta public static <K, V> ImmutableNavigableMap<K, V> wrap(final NavigableMap<? extends K, ? extends V> navigableMap)`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Returns an ImmutableNavigableMap that is backed by the provided NavigableMap.
- **Contract:**
  - If the provided NavigableMap is already an instance of ImmutableNavigableMap, it is directly returned.
  - If the NavigableMap is `null`, an empty ImmutableNavigableMap is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `navigableMap` (`NavigableMap<? extends K, ? extends V>`) — the NavigableMap to be used as the base for the `ImmutableNavigableMap`
- **Returns:** an `ImmutableNavigableMap` backed by the provided NavigableMap, or the same instance if it is already an `ImmutableNavigableMap`, or an empty instance if `navigableMap` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  NavigableMap<Integer, String> mutable = new TreeMap<>();
    ImmutableNavigableMap<Integer, String> wrapped = ImmutableNavigableMap.wrap(mutable);
    mutable.put(1, "one");   // this change is visible in wrapped!
  ```
- **See also:** #copyOf(Map)
- **Signature:** `@Deprecated public static <K, V> ImmutableSortedMap<K, V> wrap(final SortedMap<? extends K, ? extends V> sortedMap) throws UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** This method is deprecated and will throw an UnsupportedOperationException if used.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sortedMap` (`SortedMap<? extends K, ? extends V>`) — ignored
- **Returns:** never returns normally
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — always
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  SortedMap<Integer, String> sorted = new TreeMap<>();
    ImmutableNavigableMap.wrap(sorted);   // throws UnsupportedOperationException
  ```

#### Public Instance Methods
##### lowerEntry(...) -> ImmutableEntry<K, V>
- **Signature:** `@Override public ImmutableEntry<K, V> lowerEntry(final K key) throws NullPointerException, ClassCastException`
- **Summary:** Returns a key-value mapping associated with the greatest key strictly less than the given key, or `null` if there is no such key.
- **Parameters:**
  - `key` (`K`) — the reference key whose immediate predecessor entry is requested
- **Returns:** an entry with the greatest key less than `key`, or `null` if there is no such key
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `key` is `null` and this map's comparator does not permit `null` keys
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if the specified key cannot be compared with the keys currently in the map
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableNavigableMap<Integer, String> map = ImmutableNavigableMap.of(
        1, "one", 3, "three", 5, "five"
    );
    System.out.println(map.lowerEntry(3));   // prints 1=one
    System.out.println(map.lowerEntry(4));   // prints 3=three
    System.out.println(map.lowerEntry(1));   // prints null
  ```

- **Signature:** `@Override public ImmutableEntry<K, V> ceilingEntry(final K key) throws NullPointerException, ClassCastException`
- **Summary:** Returns a key-value mapping associated with the least key greater than or equal to the given key, or `null` if there is no such key.

##### subMap(...) -> ImmutableNavigableMap<K, V>
- **Signature:** `@Override public ImmutableNavigableMap<K, V> subMap(final K fromKey, final boolean fromInclusive, final K toKey, final boolean toInclusive) throws NullPointerException, ClassCastException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns an immutable view of the portion of this map whose keys range from `fromKey` to `toKey`.
- **Contract:**
  - If `fromKey` and `toKey` are equal, the returned map is empty unless `fromInclusive` and `toInclusive` are both `true`.
  - This method throws an `IllegalArgumentException` if the starting key is greater than the ending key according to this map's ordering.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fromKey` (`K`) — low endpoint of the keys in the returned map
  - `fromInclusive` (`boolean`) — `true` if the low endpoint is to be included in the returned view
  - `toKey` (`K`) — high endpoint of the keys in the returned map
  - `toInclusive` (`boolean`) — `true` if the high endpoint is to be included in the returned view
- **Returns:** an immutable view of the portion of this map whose keys range from `fromKey` to `toKey`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if an endpoint is null and the backing map rejects null endpoints
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if the endpoints cannot be compared with each other, or an endpoint cannot be compared with a backing range bound using the configured comparator or natural ordering
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fromKey` is greater than `toKey`; or if this map itself has a restricted range, and an endpoint lies outside the bounds of the range.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableNavigableMap<Integer, String> map = ImmutableNavigableMap.of(
        1, "one", 3, "three", 5, "five", 7, "seven", 9, "nine"
    );
  
    // inclusive-inclusive sub-map: [3, 7]
    ImmutableNavigableMap<Integer, String> subMap1 = map.subMap(3, true, 7, true);
    System.out.println(subMap1);   // prints {3=three, 5=five, 7=seven}
  
    // exclusive-exclusive sub-map: (3, 7)
    ImmutableNavigableMap<Integer, String> subMap2 = map.subMap(3, false, 7, false);
    System.out.println(subMap2);   // prints {5=five}
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Override public ImmutableNavigableMap<K, V> subMap(final K fromKey, final K toKey) throws NullPointerException, ClassCastException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns an immutable view of the portion of this map whose keys range from `fromKey`, inclusive, to `toKey`, exclusive.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fromKey` (`K`) — low endpoint (inclusive) of the keys in the returned map
  - `toKey` (`K`) — high endpoint (exclusive) of the keys in the returned map
- **Returns:** an immutable navigable view of the portion of this map whose keys range from `fromKey`, inclusive, to `toKey`, exclusive
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if an endpoint is null and the backing map rejects null endpoints
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if the endpoints cannot be compared with each other, or an endpoint cannot be compared with a backing range bound using the configured comparator or natural ordering
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fromKey` is greater than `toKey`; or if this map itself has a restricted range, and an endpoint lies outside the bounds of the range.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableNavigableMap<Integer, String> map = ImmutableNavigableMap.of(
        1, "one", 2, "two", 3, "three", 4, "four"
    );
    ImmutableNavigableMap<Integer, String> sub = map.subMap(2, 4);
    System.out.println(sub);              // prints {2=two, 3=three}
    System.out.println(sub.firstKey());   // prints 2
  ```
##### headMap(...) -> ImmutableNavigableMap<K, V>
- **Signature:** `@Override public ImmutableNavigableMap<K, V> headMap(final K toKey, final boolean inclusive) throws NullPointerException, ClassCastException, IllegalArgumentException`

##### copyOf(...) -> ImmutableNavigableSet<E>
- **Signature:** `public static <E> ImmutableNavigableSet<E> copyOf(final E[] a) throws NullPointerException, ClassCastException`
- **Summary:** Returns an ImmutableNavigableSet containing the elements of the specified array in natural order.
- **Contract:**
  - If the array is `null` or empty, the cached empty set is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`E[]`) — the array whose elements are to be copied
- **Returns:** an ImmutableNavigableSet containing the array elements
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if the array contains a `null` element
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if the elements are not mutually comparable
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableNavigableSet<String> set = ImmutableNavigableSet.copyOf(new String[] { "charlie", "alpha", "beta", "alpha" });
    System.out.println(set);          // prints [alpha, beta, charlie]
    System.out.println(set.ceiling("b"));   // prints beta
  ```
- **See also:** #copyOf(Collection)
- **Signature:** `public static <E> ImmutableNavigableSet<E> copyOf(final Collection<? extends E> c) throws NullPointerException, ClassCastException`
- **Summary:** Returns an ImmutableNavigableSet containing the elements of the specified collection.
- **Contract:**
  - If the provided collection is already an instance of ImmutableNavigableSet that owns its backing storage (one produced by `of(...)`, `copyOf(...)` or #empty()), it is directly returned; a #wrap(NavigableSet)-created view is copied like any other collection.
  - If the provided collection is `null` or empty, an empty ImmutableNavigableSet is returned.
  - A SortedSet source retains its comparator, including when it is empty; its elements need not implement Comparable when that comparator supports them.
  - Other collections use natural ordering and throw ClassCastException if their elements are not mutually comparable.
  - Wrap the view in a fresh set (`copyOf(new TreeSet<>(view))`) when a small view of a large source must stop retaining it.
- **Parameters:**
  - `c` (`Collection<? extends E>`) — the collection whose elements are to be placed into this set
- **Returns:** an `ImmutableNavigableSet` containing the elements of the specified collection, or the same instance if it is already an `ImmutableNavigableSet` that owns its backing storage. The comparator of a `SortedSet` source is retained even when the source is empty; a `null` or empty non-sorted source returns the shared empty instance.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if the collection contains a `null` element and natural ordering is used
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if the elements are not mutually comparable (when the source collection is not a `SortedSet`)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> list = Arrays.asList("charlie", "alpha", "beta");
    ImmutableNavigableSet<String> set = ImmutableNavigableSet.copyOf(list);
    System.out.println(set);   // prints [alpha, beta, charlie]
  ```
- **See also:** #wrap(NavigableSet)
##### wrap(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `@Beta public static <E> ImmutableNavigableSet<E> wrap(final NavigableSet<? extends E> navigableSet)`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Wraps the provided NavigableSet into an ImmutableNavigableSet.
- **Contract:**
  - If the provided NavigableSet is already an instance of ImmutableNavigableSet, it is directly returned.
  - If the provided NavigableSet is `null`, an empty ImmutableNavigableSet is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `navigableSet` (`NavigableSet<? extends E>`) — the NavigableSet to be wrapped into an `ImmutableNavigableSet`
- **Returns:** an `ImmutableNavigableSet` backed by the provided NavigableSet, or the same instance if it is already an `ImmutableNavigableSet`, or an empty instance if `navigableSet` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  NavigableSet<String> mutableSet = new TreeSet<>();
    ImmutableNavigableSet<String> immutableView = ImmutableNavigableSet.wrap(mutableSet);
    mutableSet.add("new element");   // this change is visible in immutableView!
  ```
- **See also:** #copyOf(Collection)

##### lower(...) -> E
- **Signature:** `@Override public E lower(final E e) throws NullPointerException, ClassCastException`
- **Summary:** Returns the greatest element in this set strictly less than the given element, or `null` if there is no such element.
- **Parameters:**

- **Returns:** the greatest element less than `e`, or `null` if there is no such element
- **Throws:**

  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if the specified element cannot be compared with the elements currently in the set
- **Examples:**


##### subSet(...) -> ImmutableNavigableSet<E>
- **Signature:** `@Override public ImmutableNavigableSet<E> subSet(final E fromElement, final boolean fromInclusive, final E toElement, final boolean toInclusive) throws NullPointerException, ClassCastException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a view of the portion of this set whose elements range from `fromElement` to `toElement`.
- **Contract:**
  - If `fromInclusive` is `true`, the returned set includes `fromElement` if present.
  - If `toInclusive` is `true`, the returned set includes `toElement` if present.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fromElement` (`E`) — low endpoint of the elements in the returned set
  - `fromInclusive` (`boolean`) — `true` if the low endpoint is to be included in the returned view
  - `toElement` (`E`) — high endpoint of the elements in the returned set
  - `toInclusive` (`boolean`) — `true` if the high endpoint is to be included in the returned view
- **Returns:** a view of the portion of this set whose elements range from `fromElement` to `toElement`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if an endpoint is null and the backing set rejects null endpoints
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if the endpoints cannot be compared with each other, or an endpoint cannot be compared with a backing range bound using the configured comparator or natural ordering
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fromElement` is greater than `toElement`; or if this set itself has a restricted range, and `fromElement` or `toElement` lies outside the bounds of the range.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableNavigableSet<Integer> set = ImmutableNavigableSet.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5);
    ImmutableNavigableSet<Integer> sub = set.subSet(2, true, 4, false);
    System.out.println(sub);   // prints [2, 3]
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Override public ImmutableNavigableSet<E> subSet(final E fromElement, final E toElement) throws NullPointerException, ClassCastException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns an immutable view of the portion of this set whose elements range from `fromElement`, inclusive, to `toElement`, exclusive.
- **Parameters:**

- **Returns:** an immutable navigable view of the portion of this set whose elements range from `fromElement`, inclusive, to `toElement`, exclusive
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if an endpoint is null and the backing set rejects null endpoints
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if the endpoints cannot be compared with each other, or an endpoint cannot be compared with a backing range bound using the configured comparator or natural ordering
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fromElement` is greater than `toElement`; or if this set itself has a restricted range, and an endpoint lies outside the bounds of the range.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableNavigableSet<Integer> set = ImmutableNavigableSet.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5);

  ```

##### copyOf(...) -> ImmutableSet<E>
- **Signature:** `public static <E> ImmutableSet<E> copyOf(final E[] elements)`
- **Summary:** Returns an `ImmutableSet` containing the elements of the specified array.
- **Contract:**
  - If the array is `null` or empty, an empty `ImmutableSet` is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `elements` (`E[]`) — the array whose elements are to be placed into the `ImmutableSet`; may be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** an `ImmutableSet` containing the unique elements of `elements`, or an empty set if `elements` is `null` or empty
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String[] array = { "a", "b", "a" };
    ImmutableSet<String> set = ImmutableSet.copyOf(array);
  
    // set contains: ["a", "b"]
  
    array[0] = "x";   // Does not affect set
  ```
- **See also:** #copyOf(Collection)
- **Signature:** `public static <E> ImmutableSet<E> copyOf(final Collection<? extends E> c)`
- **Summary:** Returns an ImmutableSet containing all distinct elements from the provided collection.
- **Contract:**
  - If the collection is `null` or empty, an empty ImmutableSet is returned.
  - The copy is skipped only when `c` is a plain `ImmutableSet` that already owns its backing storage - that is, one produced by this class's own `of(...)`, `copyOf(...)` or #empty(), by a consumed no-argument #builder(), or by `toImmutableSet()` on an ObjIterator.
- **Parameters:**
  - `c` (`Collection<? extends E>`) — the collection whose distinct elements are to be placed into the `ImmutableSet`.
- **Returns:** an `ImmutableSet` containing all distinct elements from the collection, in the collection's encounter order; the same instance if it is already a plain `ImmutableSet` that owns its backing storage; or an empty instance if `c` is `null` or empty.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<Integer> numbers = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3, 2, 1);
    ImmutableSet<Integer> uniqueNumbers = ImmutableSet.copyOf(numbers);
    System.out.println(uniqueNumbers);   // order preserved from list: [1, 2, 3]
  
    Set<String> mutableSet = new HashSet<>();
    mutableSet.add("apple");
    ImmutableSet<String> immutableCopy = ImmutableSet.copyOf(mutableSet);
    mutableSet.add("banana");   // Does not affect immutableCopy
  ```
- **See also:** #wrap(Set)
##### wrap(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `@Beta public static <E> ImmutableSet<E> wrap(final Set<? extends E> set)`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Wraps the provided set into an ImmutableSet without copying the elements.
- **Contract:**
  - If the provided set is already an ImmutableSet, it is returned directly.
  - If the set is `null`, an empty ImmutableSet is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `set` (`Set<? extends E>`) — the set to be wrapped into an `ImmutableSet`.
- **Returns:** an `ImmutableSet` view backed by the provided set, or the same instance if it is already an `ImmutableSet`, or an empty instance if `set` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Set<String> mutableSet = new HashSet<>();
    mutableSet.add("initial");
  
    ImmutableSet<String> wrapped = ImmutableSet.wrap(mutableSet);
    mutableSet.add("added later");                         // This WILL be visible in wrapped!
    System.out.println(wrapped.contains("added later"));   // prints true
  ```
- **See also:** #copyOf(Collection)
- **Signature:** `@Deprecated public static <E> ImmutableCollection<E> wrap(final Collection<? extends E> c) throws UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** This method is deprecated and will always throw an UnsupportedOperationException.
- **Parameters:**
  - `c` (`Collection<? extends E>`) — the collection to wrap.
- **Returns:** never returns normally.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — always.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Collection<String> c = Arrays.asList("a", "b");
    ImmutableSet.wrap(c);   // throws UnsupportedOperationException
  ```
##### builder(...) -> Builder<E>
- **Signature:** `public static <E> Builder<E> builder()`
- **Summary:** Creates a new Builder for constructing an ImmutableSet.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful when the number of elements is not known at compile time.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a new Builder instance for creating an ImmutableSet.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableSet<String> names = ImmutableSet.<String>builder()
        .add("Alice")
        .add("Bob")
        .add("Charlie", "David")
        .addAll(Arrays.asList("Eve", "Frank"))
        .build();
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <E> Builder<E> builder(final Set<E> holder) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new Builder for constructing an ImmutableSet using the provided set as storage.
- **Contract:**
  - Note that the provided set should not be modified outside the builder after this call.
  - Use the no-arg #builder() when an independent value is wanted.
- **Parameters:**
  - `holder` (`Set<E>`) — the set to be used as the backing storage for the Builder; must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a new Builder instance that will use the provided set.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if holder is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Set<Integer> backingSet = new LinkedHashSet<>();
    ImmutableSet<Integer> numbers = ImmutableSet.builder(backingSet)
        .add(1)
        .add(2, 3, 4)
        .build();
  ```

##### add(...) -> Builder<E>
- **Signature:** `public Builder<E> add(final E element) throws IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Adds a single element to the set being built.
- **Contract:**
  - If the element is already present according to the backing set's comparison rules, it is not added again.
  - Null elements are permitted if the backing set supports them.
- **Parameters:**
  - `element` (`E`) — the element to add, may be `null`.
- **Returns:** this builder instance for method chaining.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if #build() has already been called on this builder.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableSet.Builder<String> builder = ImmutableSet.builder();
    builder.add("hello")
           .add("world")
           .add("hello");
  ```
- **Signature:** `@SafeVarargs public final Builder<E> add(final E... elements) throws IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Adds all provided elements to the set being built.
- **Contract:**
  - If the array is `null` or empty, no elements are added.
- **Parameters:**
  - `elements` (`E[]`) — the elements to add, may be `null` or empty.
- **Returns:** this builder instance for method chaining.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if #build() has already been called on this builder.
- **Examples:**


##### build(...) -> ImmutableSet<E>
- **Signature:** `public ImmutableSet<E> build()`
- **Summary:** Builds and returns an ImmutableSet containing all distinct elements added to this builder.
- **Contract:**
  - When the builder was created by ImmutableSet#builder() its storage is private and the result is an independent value; when it was created by ImmutableSet#builder(Set) the caller can still modify the holder it supplied, so the result stays a live view and ImmutableSet#copyOf(Collection) will copy it.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a new ImmutableSet containing all distinct elements added to the builder.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableSet<String> finalSet = builder.build();
    System.out.println(finalSet.size());   // prints the number of distinct elements
    // builder.add("more");   // throws IllegalStateException
  ```

##### copyOf(...) -> ImmutableSortedMap<K, V>
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> ImmutableSortedMap<K, V> copyOf(final Map<? extends K, ? extends V> map) throws NullPointerException, ClassCastException`
- **Summary:** Returns an ImmutableSortedMap containing the same mappings as the provided Map.
- **Contract:**
  - If the provided Map is `null`, or is empty and not a SortedMap, an empty ImmutableSortedMap is returned.
  - The copy is skipped only when `map` is an `ImmutableSortedMap` that already owns its backing storage - that is, one produced by `of(...)`, `copyOf(...)` or #empty().
  - Wrap the view in a fresh map (`copyOf(new TreeMap<>(view))`) when a small view of a large map must stop retaining it.
  - If the source is a SortedMap, the returned map uses the same Comparator (or natural ordering) as the source, even when the source is empty.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<? extends K, ? extends V>`) — the Map whose mappings are to be placed in the `ImmutableSortedMap`
- **Returns:** an `ImmutableSortedMap` containing the same mappings as the provided map, or the same instance if it is already an `ImmutableSortedMap` that owns its backing storage. The comparator of a `SortedMap` source is retained even when the source is empty; a `null` or empty non-sorted source returns the shared empty instance.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if the map contains a `null` key and natural ordering is used
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if the keys are not mutually comparable (when the source map is not a `SortedMap`)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> mutable = new HashMap<>();
    mutable.put("b", 2);
    mutable.put("a", 1);
    ImmutableSortedMap<String, Integer> immutable = ImmutableSortedMap.copyOf(mutable);
    mutable.put("c", 3);             // does not affect immutable
    System.out.println(immutable);   // prints {a=1, b=2}
  ```
- **See also:** #wrap(SortedMap)
