##### comparator(...) -> Comparator<? super K>
- **Signature:** `@Override public Comparator<? super K> comparator()`
- **Summary:** Returns the comparator used to order the keys in this map, or `null` if this map uses the natural ordering of its keys.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the comparator used to order the keys in this map, or `null` if this map uses the natural ordering of its keys
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableSortedMap<String, Integer> naturalOrder = ImmutableSortedMap.of("a", 1, "b", 2);
    System.out.println(naturalOrder.comparator());   // prints null
  
    Comparator<String> reverseOrder = Comparator.reverseOrder();
    SortedMap<String, Integer> customMap = new TreeMap<>(reverseOrder);
    customMap.put("a", 1);
    ImmutableSortedMap<String, Integer> customOrder = ImmutableSortedMap.wrap(customMap);
    System.out.println(customOrder.comparator() == reverseOrder);   // prints true
  ```
##### subMap(...) -> ImmutableSortedMap<K, V>
- **Signature:** `@Override public ImmutableSortedMap<K, V> subMap(final K fromKey, final K toKey) throws NullPointerException, ClassCastException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a view of the portion of this map whose keys range from `fromKey`, inclusive, to `toKey`, exclusive.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fromKey` (`K`) — low endpoint (inclusive) of the keys in the returned map
  - `toKey` (`K`) — high endpoint (exclusive) of the keys in the returned map
- **Returns:** a view of the portion of this map whose keys range from `fromKey`, inclusive, to `toKey`, exclusive
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if an endpoint is null and the backing map rejects null endpoints
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if the endpoints cannot be compared with each other, or an endpoint cannot be compared with a backing range bound using the configured comparator or natural ordering
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fromKey` is greater than `toKey`; or if this map itself has a restricted range, and `fromKey` or `toKey` lies outside the bounds of the range.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableSortedMap<Integer, String> map = ImmutableSortedMap.of(
        1, "one", 2, "two", 3, "three", 4, "four", 5, "five"
    );
    ImmutableSortedMap<Integer, String> subMap = map.subMap(2, 4);
    System.out.println(subMap);   // prints {2=two, 3=three}
  ```

##### copyOf(...) -> ImmutableSortedSet<E>
- **Signature:** `public static <E> ImmutableSortedSet<E> copyOf(final E[] a) throws NullPointerException, ClassCastException`
- **Summary:** Returns an ImmutableSortedSet containing the elements of the specified array in natural order.
- **Contract:**
  - If the array is `null` or empty, the cached empty set is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`E[]`) — the array whose elements are to be copied
- **Returns:** an ImmutableSortedSet containing the array elements
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if the array contains a `null` element
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if the elements are not mutually comparable
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableSortedSet<String> set = ImmutableSortedSet.copyOf(new String[] { "charlie", "alpha", "beta", "alpha" });
    System.out.println(set);   // prints [alpha, beta, charlie]
  ```
- **See also:** #copyOf(Collection)
- **Signature:** `public static <E> ImmutableSortedSet<E> copyOf(final Collection<? extends E> c) throws NullPointerException, ClassCastException`
- **Summary:** Returns an ImmutableSortedSet containing the elements of the specified collection.
- **Contract:**
  - If the provided collection is already an instance of ImmutableSortedSet that owns its backing storage (one produced by `of(...)`, `copyOf(...)` or #empty()), it is directly returned; a #wrap(SortedSet)-created view is copied like any other collection.
  - If the provided collection is `null` or empty, an empty ImmutableSortedSet is returned.
  - A SortedSet source retains its comparator, including when it is empty; its elements need not implement Comparable when that comparator supports them.
  - Other collections use natural ordering and throw ClassCastException if their elements are not mutually comparable.
  - Wrap the view in a fresh set (`copyOf(new TreeSet<>(view))`) when a small view of a large source must stop retaining it.
- **Parameters:**
  - `c` (`Collection<? extends E>`) — the collection whose elements are to be placed into this set
- **Returns:** an `ImmutableSortedSet` containing the elements of the specified collection, or the same instance if it is already an `ImmutableSortedSet` that owns its backing storage. The comparator of a `SortedSet` source is retained even when the source is empty; a `null` or empty non-sorted source returns the shared empty instance.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if the collection contains a `null` element and natural ordering is used
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if the elements are not mutually comparable (when the source collection is not a `SortedSet`)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> list = Arrays.asList("charlie", "alpha", "beta");
    ImmutableSortedSet<String> set = ImmutableSortedSet.copyOf(list);
    System.out.println(set);   // prints [alpha, beta, charlie]
  ```
- **See also:** #wrap(SortedSet)
##### wrap(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `@Beta public static <E> ImmutableSortedSet<E> wrap(final SortedSet<? extends E> sortedSet)`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Wraps the provided SortedSet into an ImmutableSortedSet.
- **Contract:**
  - If the provided SortedSet is already an instance of ImmutableSortedSet, it is directly returned.
  - If the provided SortedSet is `null`, an empty ImmutableSortedSet is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `sortedSet` (`SortedSet<? extends E>`) — the sorted set to wrap; may be `null`
- **Returns:** an `ImmutableSortedSet` backed by the specified `sortedSet`, the same instance if it is already an `ImmutableSortedSet`, or #empty() if `sortedSet` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  SortedSet<String> mutableSet = new TreeSet<>();
    ImmutableSortedSet<String> immutableView = ImmutableSortedSet.wrap(mutableSet);
    mutableSet.add("new element");   // this change is visible in immutableView!
  ```
- **See also:** #copyOf(Collection)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### comparator(...) -> Comparator<? super E>
- **Signature:** `@Override public Comparator<? super E> comparator()`
- **Summary:** Returns the comparator used to order the elements in this set, or `null` if this set uses the natural ordering of its elements.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the comparator used to order the elements in this set, or `null` if natural ordering is used
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableSortedSet<String> naturalOrder = ImmutableSortedSet.of("a", "b", "c");
    System.out.println(naturalOrder.comparator());   // prints null
  
    Comparator<String> reverseOrder = Comparator.reverseOrder();
    SortedSet<String> customSet = new TreeSet<>(reverseOrder);
    customSet.add("a");
    ImmutableSortedSet<String> customOrder = ImmutableSortedSet.wrap(customSet);
    System.out.println(customOrder.comparator() == reverseOrder);   // prints true
  ```
##### subSet(...) -> ImmutableSortedSet<E>
- **Signature:** `@Override public ImmutableSortedSet<E> subSet(final E fromElement, final E toElement) throws NullPointerException, ClassCastException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a view of the portion of this set whose elements range from `fromElement`, inclusive, to `toElement`, exclusive.
- **Parameters:**
  - `fromElement` (`E`) — low endpoint (inclusive) of the returned set
  - `toElement` (`E`) — high endpoint (exclusive) of the returned set
- **Returns:** a view of the portion of this set whose elements range from `fromElement`, inclusive, to `toElement`, exclusive
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if an endpoint is null and the backing set rejects null endpoints
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if the endpoints cannot be compared with each other, or an endpoint cannot be compared with a backing range bound using the configured comparator or natural ordering
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `fromElement` is greater than `toElement`; or if this set itself has a restricted range, and `fromElement` or `toElement` lies outside the bounds of the range.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableSortedSet<Integer> set = ImmutableSortedSet.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5);
    ImmutableSortedSet<Integer> subset = set.subSet(2, 4);
    System.out.println(subset);   // prints [2, 3]
  ```
##### headSet(...) -> ImmutableSortedSet<E>
- **Signature:** `@Override public ImmutableSortedSet<E> headSet(final E toElement) throws NullPointerException, ClassCastException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a view of the portion of this set whose elements are strictly less than `toElement`.

  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if the endpoint is incompatible with the ordering, or cannot be compared with a backing range bound
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if this set itself has a restricted range, and `toElement` lies outside the bounds of the range.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableSortedSet<String> set = ImmutableSortedSet.of("a", "b", "c", "d");

  ```

### Class Index (com.landawn.abacus.util.Index)
Index-finding operations for arrays, collections, iterators, and strings, returning an OptionalInt instead of a magic `-1`.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### of(...) -> OptionalInt
- **Signature:** `public static OptionalInt of(final boolean[] source, final boolean valueToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index of the first occurrence of the specified boolean value in the array.
- **Contract:**
  - If the array is `null` or empty, an empty OptionalInt is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`boolean[]`) — the boolean array to be searched, may be `null`
  - `valueToFind` (`boolean`) — the boolean value to search for
- **Returns:** an OptionalInt containing the zero-based index of the first occurrence of the value, or an empty OptionalInt if the value is not found or the array is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  boolean[] arr = {false, true, false, true, false};
    Index.of(arr, true).get();          // returns 1
    Index.of(arr, false).get();         // returns 0
    Index.of(null, true).isPresent();   // returns false
  ```
- **See also:** #of(boolean\[\], boolean, int), #of(Object\[\], Object)
- **Signature:** `public static OptionalInt of(final boolean[] source, final boolean valueToFind, final int fromIndex)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index of the first occurrence of the specified boolean value in the array, starting from the specified index.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`boolean[]`) — the boolean array to be searched, may be `null`
  - `valueToFind` (`boolean`) — the boolean value to search for
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the index to start the search from (inclusive); negative values are treated as 0
- **Returns:** an OptionalInt containing the zero-based index of the first occurrence of the value at or after `fromIndex`, or an empty OptionalInt if the value is not found, the array is `null`, or `fromIndex >= array.length`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  boolean[] arr = {false, true, false, true, false};
    Index.of(arr, true, 0).get();         // returns 1
    Index.of(arr, true, 2).get();         // returns 3
    Index.of(arr, true, 4).isPresent();   // returns false
  ```
- **See also:** #of(boolean\[\], boolean), #of(Object\[\], Object, int)

- **Signature:** `public static OptionalInt of(final float[] source, final float valueToFind, final int fromIndex, final float tolerance) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns the index of the first occurrence of the specified float value in the array, within a given tolerance and starting from the specified index.
- **Contract:**
  - Signed zero: `-0.0f` matches `0.0f` here, and it does so even when `tolerance` is `0`, because Numbers#fuzzyEquals(float, float, float) treats them as equal.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`float[]`) — the float array to be searched, may be `null`
  - `valueToFind` (`float`) — the float value to search for
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the index to start the search from (inclusive); negative values are treated as 0
  - `tolerance` (`float`) — the tolerance for matching; must be non-negative and not NaN. A value matches if it's within `valueToFind +/- tolerance`
- **Returns:** an OptionalInt containing the zero-based index of the first occurrence of a value within tolerance at or after `fromIndex`, or an empty OptionalInt if no value is found within tolerance, the array is `null`, or `fromIndex >= array.length`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `tolerance` is negative or NaN.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  float[] arr = {1.0f, 2.1f, 3.0f, 2.2f, 4.0f};
    Index.of(arr, 2.0f, 0, 0.2f).get();         // returns 1
    Index.of(arr, 2.0f, 2, 0.2f).isPresent();   // returns false (2.2f - 2.0f > 0.2f)
    Index.of(arr, 5.0f, 0, 0.1f).isPresent();   // returns false
    Index.of(arr, 2.0f, 5, 0.2f).isPresent();   // returns false
  ```
- **See also:** #of(float\[\], float, int), N#indexOf(float\[\], float, int, float)

  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if the matching value has a zero-based index greater than Integer#MAX_VALUE.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> list = Arrays.asList("a", "b", "c", "b");
    Index.of(list.iterator(), "b", 1).get();            // returns 1
    Index.of(list.iterator(), "x", 0).isPresent();      // returns false
  ```

- **Signature:** `public static OptionalInt of(final String source, final String valueToFind, final int fromIndex)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index of the first occurrence of the specified substring in the given string, starting from the specified index.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`String`) — the string to be searched, may be `null`
  - `valueToFind` (`String`) — the substring to search for, may be `null`
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the index to start the search from (inclusive); negative values are treated as 0
- **Returns:** an OptionalInt containing the zero-based index of the first occurrence of the substring at or after `fromIndex` (an empty substring returns `Math.min(Math.max(fromIndex, 0), source.length())`), or an empty OptionalInt if the substring is not found or either parameter is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Index.of("hello world hello", "hello", 1).get();   // returns 12
  ```

- **Summary:** Returns the index of the first occurrence of the specified substring in the given string, ignoring case.

- **Signature:** `public static OptionalInt last(final boolean[] source, final boolean valueToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index of the last occurrence of the specified boolean value in the given array.
- **Contract:**
  - If the array is `null` or empty, an empty OptionalInt is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`boolean[]`) — the boolean array to be searched, may be `null`
  - `valueToFind` (`boolean`) — the boolean value to search for
- **Returns:** an OptionalInt containing the zero-based index of the last occurrence of the value, or an empty OptionalInt if the value is not found or the array is `null` or empty
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  boolean[] arr = {false, true, false, true};
    Index.last(arr, true).get();                      // returns 3
    Index.last(arr, false).get();                     // returns 2
    Index.last(arr, true).orElse(-1);                 // returns 3
    Index.last((boolean[]) null, true).isPresent();   // returns false
  ```
- **See also:** #last(boolean\[\], boolean, int), #last(Object\[\], Object)
- **Signature:** `public static OptionalInt last(final boolean[] source, final boolean valueToFind, final int startIndexFromBack)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index of the last occurrence of the specified boolean value in the given array, searching backwards from the specified position.
- **Contract:**
  - If `startIndexFromBack` is greater than or equal to the array length, the entire array is searched.
  - If the array is `null` or empty, an empty OptionalInt is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`boolean[]`) — the boolean array to be searched, may be `null`
  - `valueToFind` (`boolean`) — the boolean value to search for
  - `startIndexFromBack` (`int`) — the position to start the backwards search from (inclusive); a value at or beyond the end searches the whole input, and a negative value finds nothing
- **Returns:** an OptionalInt containing the zero-based index of the last occurrence of the value at or before `startIndexFromBack`, or an empty OptionalInt if the value is not found or the array is `null` or empty
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  boolean[] arr = {false, true, false, true, false};
    Index.last(arr, true, 3).get();    // returns 3
    Index.last(arr, true, 1).get();    // returns 1
    Index.last(arr, false, 3).get();   // returns 2
    Index.last(arr, true, 10).get();   // returns 3
  ```
- **See also:** #last(boolean\[\], boolean), #last(Object\[\], Object, int)

- **Signature:** `public static OptionalInt last(final float[] source, final float valueToFind, final int startIndexFromBack)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index of the last occurrence of the specified float value in the given array, searching backwards from a specified position.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`float[]`) — the float array to be searched, may be `null`
  - `valueToFind` (`float`) — the float value to search for
  - `startIndexFromBack` (`int`) — the position to start the backwards search from (inclusive); a value at or beyond the end searches the whole input, and a negative value finds nothing
- **Returns:** an OptionalInt containing the zero-based index of the last occurrence of the value at or before `startIndexFromBack`, or an empty OptionalInt if the value is not found or the array is `null` or empty
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  float[] arr = {1.0f, 2.0f, 3.0f, 2.0f, 4.0f};
    Index.last(arr, 2.0f, 3).get();         // returns 3
    Index.last(arr, 2.0f, 1).get();         // returns 1
    Index.last(arr, 5.0f, 2).isPresent();   // returns false
    Index.last(arr, 1.0f, 0).get();         // returns 0
  ```
- **See also:** #last(boolean\[\], boolean, int), #last(float\[\], float), #last(float\[\], float, int, float), #last(Object\[\], Object, int), Float#compare(float, float)
- **Signature:** `public static OptionalInt last(final float[] source, final float valueToFind, final int startIndexFromBack, final float tolerance) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns the index of the last occurrence of the specified float value in the given array within a specified tolerance, searching backwards from the specified position.
- **Contract:**
  - Signed zero: `-0.0f` matches `0.0f` here, and it does so even when `tolerance` is `0`, because Numbers#fuzzyEquals(float, float, float) treats them as equal.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`float[]`) — the float array to be searched, may be `null`
  - `valueToFind` (`float`) — the float value to search for
  - `startIndexFromBack` (`int`) — the position to start the backwards search from (inclusive); a value at or beyond the end searches the whole input, and a negative value finds nothing
  - `tolerance` (`float`) — the tolerance for matching; must be non-negative and not NaN. A value matches if it's within `valueToFind +/- tolerance`
- **Returns:** an OptionalInt containing the zero-based index of the last occurrence of a value within tolerance at or before `startIndexFromBack`, or an empty OptionalInt if no value is found within tolerance or the array is `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `tolerance` is negative or NaN.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  float[] arr = {1.0f, 2.1f, 3.0f, 2.2f, 4.0f};
    Index.last(arr, 2.0f, 4, 0.2f).get();                    // returns 1 (2.2f at index 3 excluded: 2.2f - 2.0f > 0.2f)
    Index.last(arr, 2.0f, 2, 0.2f).get();                    // returns 1
    Index.last(arr, 5.0f, 3, 0.1f).isPresent();              // returns false
    Index.last((float[]) null, 2.0f, 4, 0.1f).isPresent();   // returns false
  ```
- **See also:** #last(float\[\], float, int), N#lastIndexOf(float\[\], float, int, float)

- **Signature:** `public static OptionalInt last(final double[] source, final double valueToFind, final int startIndexFromBack, final double tolerance) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns the index of the last occurrence of the specified double value in the given array within a specified tolerance, searching backwards from the specified position.
- **Contract:**
  - Signed zero: `-0.0` matches `0.0` here, and it does so even when `tolerance` is `0`, because Numbers#fuzzyEquals(double, double, double) treats them as equal.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`double[]`) — the double array to be searched, may be `null`
  - `valueToFind` (`double`) — the double value to search for
  - `startIndexFromBack` (`int`) — the position to start the backwards search from (inclusive); a value at or beyond the end searches the whole input, and a negative value finds nothing
  - `tolerance` (`double`) — the tolerance for matching; must be non-negative and not NaN. A value matches if it's within `valueToFind +/- tolerance`
- **Returns:** an OptionalInt containing the zero-based index of the last occurrence of a value within tolerance at or before `startIndexFromBack`, or an empty OptionalInt if no value is found within tolerance or the array is `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `tolerance` is negative or NaN.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  double[] arr = {1.0, 2.1, 3.0, 2.2, 4.0};

    Index.last(arr, 2.0, 2, 0.2).get();                     // returns 1
  ```

- **Signature:** `public static OptionalInt last(final Object[] source, final Object valueToFind, final int startIndexFromBack)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index of the last occurrence of the specified value in the given array, searching backwards from the specified index.
- **Contract:**
  - If `startIndexFromBack` is greater than or equal to the array length, the entire array is searched.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`Object[]`) — the array to be searched, may be `null`
  - `valueToFind` (`Object`) — the value to find in the array, may be `null`
  - `startIndexFromBack` (`int`) — the index to start the search from (inclusive), searching backwards; a value at or beyond the end searches the whole input, and a negative value finds nothing
- **Returns:** an OptionalInt containing the zero-based index of the last occurrence of the value at or before `startIndexFromBack`, or an empty OptionalInt if the value is not found or the array is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String[] arr = {"a", "b", "c", "b", "a"};
    Index.last(arr, "b", 4).get();         // returns 3 (searches from index 4 backward)
    Index.last(arr, "b", 2).get();         // returns 1 (searches from index 2 backward)
    Index.last(arr, "b", 0).isPresent();   // returns false (only checks index 0)
  ```
- **See also:** #last(Object\[\], Object), #of(Object\[\], Object, int)

- **Signature:** `public static OptionalInt last(final String source, final int charValueToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index of the last occurrence of the specified character in the given string.
- **Contract:**
  - If the string is `null`, an empty OptionalInt is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`String`) — the string to be searched, may be `null`
  - `charValueToFind` (`int`) — the character value (Unicode code point) to search for
- **Returns:** an OptionalInt containing the zero-based index of the last occurrence of the character, or an empty OptionalInt if the character is not found or the string is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Index.last("hello", 'l').get();               // returns 3
    Index.last("hello", 'o').get();               // returns 4
    Index.last("hello", 'x').isPresent();         // returns false
    Index.last((String) null, 'a').isPresent();   // returns false
  ```
- **See also:** #last(String, int, int), Strings#lastIndexOf(String, int), String#lastIndexOf(int)
- **Signature:** `public static OptionalInt last(final String source, final int charValueToFind, final int startIndexFromBack)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index of the last occurrence of the specified character in the given string, searching backwards from the specified position.
- **Contract:**
  - If the string is `null`, an empty OptionalInt is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`String`) — the string to be searched, may be `null`
  - `charValueToFind` (`int`) — the character value (Unicode code point) to search for
  - `startIndexFromBack` (`int`) — the position to start the backwards search from (inclusive); a value at or beyond the end searches the whole input, and a negative value finds nothing
- **Returns:** an OptionalInt containing the zero-based index of the last occurrence of the character at or before `startIndexFromBack`, or an empty OptionalInt if the character is not found, the string is `null`, or `startIndexFromBack < 0`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Index.last("hello", 'l', 3).get();         // returns 3
    Index.last("hello", 'l', 2).get();         // returns 2
    Index.last("hello", 'h', 0).get();         // returns 0
    Index.last("hello", 'x', 3).isPresent();   // returns false
  ```
- **See also:** #last(String, int), Strings#lastIndexOf(String, int, int), String#lastIndexOf(int, int)
- **Signature:** `public static OptionalInt last(final String source, final String valueToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index of the last occurrence of the specified substring in the given string.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`String`) — the string to be searched, may be `null`
  - `valueToFind` (`String`) — the substring to search for, may be `null`
- **Returns:** an OptionalInt containing the zero-based index of the last occurrence of the substring (an empty substring returns `source.length()`), or an empty OptionalInt if the substring is not found or either parameter is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Index.last("hello world hello", "hello").get();   // returns 12
    Index.last("hello world", "world").get();         // returns 6
    Index.last("hello world", "bye").isPresent();     // returns false
  ```
- **See also:** #last(String, String, int), #lastOfIgnoreCase(String, String), #of(String, String), Strings#lastIndexOf(String, String), String#lastIndexOf(String)
- **Signature:** `public static OptionalInt last(final String source, final String valueToFind, final int startIndexFromBack)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index of the last occurrence of the specified substring in the given string, searching backwards from the specified position.
- **Contract:**
  - If the string is `null`, an empty OptionalInt is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`String`) — the string to be searched, may be `null`
  - `valueToFind` (`String`) — the substring to search for, may be `null`
  - `startIndexFromBack` (`int`) — the position to start the backwards search from (inclusive); a value at or beyond the end searches the whole input, and a negative value finds nothing
- **Returns:** an OptionalInt containing the zero-based index of the last occurrence of the substring at or before `startIndexFromBack` (an empty substring returns `Math.min(startIndexFromBack, source.length())`), or an empty OptionalInt if the substring is not found, either parameter is `null`, or `startIndexFromBack < 0`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Index.last("hello world hello", "hello", 12).get();   // returns 12
    Index.last("hello world hello", "hello", 6).get();    // returns 0
    Index.last("hello", "bye", 4).isPresent();            // returns false
    Index.last("hello", "he", 1).get();                   // returns 0
  ```
- **See also:** #last(String, String), Strings#lastIndexOf(String, String, int), String#lastIndexOf(String, int)
##### lastOfIgnoreCase(...) -> OptionalInt
- **Signature:** `public static OptionalInt lastOfIgnoreCase(final String source, final String valueToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index of the last occurrence of the specified substring in the given string, ignoring case.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`String`) — the string to be searched, may be `null`
  - `valueToFind` (`String`) — the substring to search for (case-insensitive), may be `null`
- **Returns:** an OptionalInt containing the zero-based index of the last occurrence of the substring (ignoring case) (an empty substring returns `source.length()`), or an empty OptionalInt if the substring is not found or either parameter is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Index.lastOfIgnoreCase("Hello World Hello", "Hello").get();   // returns 12
    Index.lastOfIgnoreCase("Hello World", "WORLD").get();         // returns 6
    Index.lastOfIgnoreCase("Hello", "bye").isPresent();           // returns false
    Index.lastOfIgnoreCase((String) null, "a").isPresent();       // returns false
  ```

- **Signature:** `public static OptionalInt lastOfSubArray(final boolean[] source, final int startIndexFromBack, final boolean[] subArrayToFind, final int startIndexOfSubArray, final int sizeToMatch) throws IllegalArgumentException, IndexOutOfBoundsException`

- **Signature:** `public static OptionalInt lastOfSubList(final List<?> source, final int startIndexFromBack, final List<?> subListToFind, final int startIndexOfSubList, final int sizeToMatch) throws IllegalArgumentException, IndexOutOfBoundsException`
- **Summary:** Returns the index of the last occurrence of a portion of the specified sub-list in the given source list, searching backwards from the specified position.
- **Contract:**
  - Special cases (after validating the pattern slice, treating a null pattern as length zero): If `sizeToMatch` is 0, `startIndexFromBack >= 0`, and both lists are `non-null`, returns `min(startIndexFromBack, source.size())` If either list is `null`, returns empty OptionalInt If `startIndexFromBack < 0`, returns empty OptionalInt If `source.size() < sizeToMatch`, returns empty OptionalInt Usage Examples:
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`List<?>`) — the list to be searched, may be `null`
  - `startIndexFromBack` (`int`) — the highest index at which a match may start; the search includes this position. A value at or beyond the end searches the whole input, and a negative value finds nothing (an empty pattern included)
  - `subListToFind` (`List<?>`) — the sub-list to find in the source list, may be `null`
  - `startIndexOfSubList` (`int`) — the starting index within `subListToFind` of the portion to match
  - `sizeToMatch` (`int`) — the number of elements to match from `subListToFind`
- **Returns:** an OptionalInt containing the zero-based index where the last occurrence of the sub-list is found, or an empty OptionalInt if the sub-list is not found or either input is `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `sizeToMatch` is negative
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `startIndexOfSubList` and `sizeToMatch` do not denote a valid range in `subListToFind`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> source = Arrays.asList("a", "b", "c", "b", "c", "d");
    List<String> sub = Arrays.asList("b", "c", "z");
    Index.lastOfSubList(source, 5, sub, 0, 2).get();                 // returns 3
    Index.lastOfSubList(source, 2, sub, 0, 2).get();                 // returns 1
    Index.lastOfSubList(source, -1, sub, 0, 2).isPresent();          // returns false
    Index.lastOfSubList(source, 5, sub, 0, 0).get();                 // returns 5 (empty match)
    Index.lastOfSubList((List<?>) null, 5, sub, 0, 2).isPresent();   // returns false
  ```
- **See also:** #lastOfSubList(List, List), #lastOfSubList(List, int, List), #ofSubList(List, int, List, int, int)

- **Signature:** `public static BitSet allOf(final float[] source, final float valueToFind, final int fromIndex, final float tolerance) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns the indices of all occurrences of the specified value in the given array within a specified tolerance, starting from the specified index.
- **Contract:**
  - Signed zero: `-0.0f` matches `0.0f` here, and it does so even when `tolerance` is `0`, because Numbers#fuzzyEquals(float, float, float) treats them as equal.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`float[]`) — the float array to be searched, may be `null`
  - `valueToFind` (`float`) — the float value to search for
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the index to start the search from (inclusive); negative values are treated as 0
  - `tolerance` (`float`) — the tolerance within which matches will be found; must be non-negative and not NaN
- **Returns:** a BitSet containing the zero-based indices of all values within the specified tolerance at or after `fromIndex`; returns an empty BitSet if no values are found within tolerance, the array is `null` or empty, or `fromIndex >= array.length`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `tolerance` is negative or NaN.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  float[] arr = {1.0f, 2.1f, 3.0f, 2.2f, 4.0f};
    Index.allOf(arr, 2.0f, 0, 0.2f).cardinality();   // returns 1  (only 2.1f matches; 2.2f - 2.0f > 0.2f)
    Index.allOf(arr, 2.0f, 2, 0.2f).isEmpty();       // returns true (no match from index 2)
    Index.allOf(arr, 5.0f, 0, 0.1f).isEmpty();       // returns true
  ```
- **See also:** #allOf(float\[\], float, int)

- **Signature:** `public static BitSet allOf(final Object[] source, final Object valueToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns the indices of all occurrences of the specified value in the given array.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`Object[]`) — the array to be searched, may be `null`
  - `valueToFind` (`Object`) — the value to find in the array, may be `null`
- **Returns:** a BitSet containing the zero-based indices of all occurrences of the value; returns an empty BitSet if the value is not found or the array is `null` or empty
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String[] arr = {"a", "b", "a", "c", "a", "b"};
    BitSet indices = Index.allOf(arr, "a");
    // indices contains {0, 2, 4}
  
    // Convert BitSet to List
    List<Integer> list = indices.stream().boxed().collect(Collectors.toList());
    // list = [0, 2, 4]
  
    // Count occurrences
    int count = indices.cardinality();   // returns 3
  
    // Check if value exists
    boolean hasA = !indices.isEmpty();   // returns true
  
    // Handles null elements
    String[] withNulls = {"a", null, "b", null, "a"};
    // the cast is required: a bare null binds to allOf(T[], Predicate), which rejects it
    BitSet nullIndices = Index.allOf(withNulls, (Object) null);
    // nullIndices contains {1, 3}
  ```
- **See also:** #allOf(Object\[\], Object, int), #of(Object\[\], Object)

  ```java

    // Iterate over all matching indices
    indices.stream().forEach(i -> System.out.println("Found at: " + i));
  
    // Get first and last occurrence
    int first = indices.stream().findFirst().getAsInt();   // returns 0
    int last = indices.stream().max().orElse(-1);          // returns 4
  
    // Check specific index
    boolean foundAt2 = indices.get(2);                     // returns true
  ```

- **See also:** #allOf(Collection, Object)
- **Signature:** `public static <T> BitSet allOf(final T[] source, final Predicate<? super T> predicate) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns the indices of all elements in the given array that match the provided predicate.
- **Contract:**
  - If `source` is `null` or empty, returns an empty BitSet without invoking the predicate.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`T[]`) — the array to be searched, may be `null`
  - `predicate` (`Predicate<? super T>`) — the predicate to test elements
- **Returns:** a BitSet containing the zero-based indices of all elements matching the predicate; returns an empty BitSet if no elements match or the array is `null` or empty
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `predicate` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String[] arr = {"apple", "banana", "avocado", "cherry"};
    BitSet indices = Index.allOf(arr, s -> s.startsWith("a"));
    // indices contains {0, 2} (positions of "apple" and "avocado")
  ```
- **See also:** #allOf(Object\[\], Predicate, int)
- **Signature:** `public static <T> BitSet allOf(final T[] source, final Predicate<? super T> predicate, final int fromIndex) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns the indices of all elements in the given array that match the provided predicate, starting from the specified index.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`T[]`) — the array to be searched, may be `null`
  - `predicate` (`Predicate<? super T>`) — the predicate to test elements
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the index to start the search from (inclusive); negative values are treated as 0
- **Returns:** a BitSet containing the zero-based indices of all elements at or after `fromIndex` matching the predicate; returns an empty BitSet if no elements match, the array is `null`, or `fromIndex >= array.length`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `predicate` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String[] arr = {"apple", "banana", "avocado", "cherry", "apricot"};
    Index.allOf(arr, s -> s.startsWith("a"), 1).toString();   // returns "{2, 4}"
    Index.allOf(arr, s -> s.startsWith("a"), 0).toString();   // returns "{0, 2, 4}"
    Index.allOf(arr, s -> s.startsWith("z"), 0).isEmpty();    // returns true
    Index.allOf(arr, s -> s.startsWith("a"), 10).isEmpty();   // returns true (fromIndex past end)
  ```
- **See also:** #allOf(Object\[\], Predicate)
- **Signature:** `public static <T> BitSet allOf(final Collection<? extends T> source, final Predicate<? super T> predicate) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns the indices of all elements in the given collection that match the provided predicate.
- **Contract:**
  - Null Handling: If `source` is `null`, returns empty BitSet If `predicate` is `null`, throws `IllegalArgumentException` Null elements in the collection are passed to the predicate Common Mistakes:
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`Collection<? extends T>`) — the collection to be searched, may be `null`
  - `predicate` (`Predicate<? super T>`) — the predicate to test elements
- **Returns:** a BitSet containing the zero-based indices (in iteration order) of all elements matching the predicate; returns an empty BitSet if no elements match or the collection is `null` or empty
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `predicate` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // DON'T: Pass null predicate
    Index.allOf(collection, null);   // throws IllegalArgumentException!
  
    // DO: Provide valid predicate
    Index.allOf(collection, Objects::nonNull);
  
    // DON'T: Assume predicate won't receive nulls
    Index.allOf(Arrays.asList(1, null, 3), x -> x > 0);   // throws NullPointerException inside the predicate!
  
    // DO: Handle nulls in predicate
    Index.allOf(Arrays.asList(1, null, 3), x -> x != null && x > 0);
  ```
- **See also:** #allOf(Collection, Predicate, int)
- **Signature:** `public static <T> BitSet allOf(final Collection<? extends T> source, final Predicate<? super T> predicate, final int fromIndex) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns the indices of all elements in the given collection that match the provided predicate, starting from the specified index.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`Collection<? extends T>`) — the collection to be searched, may be `null`
  - `predicate` (`Predicate<? super T>`) — the predicate to test elements
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the index to start the search from (inclusive); negative values are treated as 0
- **Returns:** a BitSet containing the zero-based indices (in iteration order) of all elements at or after `fromIndex` matching the predicate; returns an empty BitSet if no elements match, the collection is `null` or empty, or `fromIndex >= collection.size()`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `predicate` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> list = Arrays.asList("apple", "banana", "avocado", "cherry", "apricot");
    Index.allOf(list, s -> s.startsWith("a"), 1).toString();   // returns "{2, 4}"
    Index.allOf(list, s -> s.startsWith("a"), 0).toString();   // returns "{0, 2, 4}"
    Index.allOf(list, s -> s.startsWith("z"), 0).isEmpty();    // returns true
    Index.allOf(list, s -> s.startsWith("a"), 10).isEmpty();   // returns true (fromIndex past end)
  ```
- **See also:** #allOf(Collection, Predicate)

### Record IndexRange (com.landawn.abacus.util.IndexRange)
Represents a half-open range of character indices, `\[start, end)`, within a string.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Record Components
- `start` (`int`) - the inclusive start index of the range, must be `>= 0`
- `end` (`int`) - the exclusive end index of the range, must be `>= start`

#### Public Constructors
- `public IndexRange(int start, int end)` — Constructs an `IndexRange` with the specified start (inclusive) and end (exclusive) indices.
  - **Throws:**
    - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `start` is negative or `end` is less than `start`

#### Public Static Methods
##### of(...) -> IndexRange

- **Summary:** Creates an `IndexRange` with the specified start (inclusive) and end (exclusive) indices.
- **Parameters:**
  - `start` (`int`) — the inclusive start index of the range, must be `>= 0`
  - `end` (`int`) — the exclusive end index of the range, must be `>= start`
- **Returns:** a new `IndexRange` `\[start, end)`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `start` is negative or `end` is less than `start`
- **Examples:**
  ```java

    range.toString();   // returns "[2, 5)"
  ```

- **Summary:** Converts this index range to a `Range<Integer>` with the same bounds.

  - (none)
- **Returns:** a half-open `Range<Integer>` `\[start, end)` covering the same indices as this range
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Range<Integer> range = new IndexRange(1, 5).toRange();
  ```

##### contains(...) -> boolean

- **Returns:** `true` if the specified index is contained in this range, `false` otherwise
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IndexRange range = new IndexRange(2, 5);
    range.contains(2);   // returns true (start is inclusive)
    range.contains(3);   // returns true
    range.contains(5);   // returns false (end is exclusive)
  ```

- **See also:** #containsRange(IndexRange)
##### containsRange(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public boolean containsRange(final IndexRange other)`
- **Summary:** Checks whether this range contains all indices of the specified range.
- **Contract:**
  - A range contains another range if every index in the other range is also contained in this range.
- **Parameters:**
  - `other` (`IndexRange`) — the range to check for containment, `null` returns `false`
- **Returns:** `true` if this range contains all indices of the specified range
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IndexRange range1 = new IndexRange(1, 10);
    IndexRange range2 = new IndexRange(3, 7);
    IndexRange range3 = new IndexRange(5, 15);
  
    range1.containsRange(range2);               // returns true
    range1.containsRange(range3);               // returns false (extends beyond upper bound)
    range1.containsRange(new IndexRange(5, 5)); // returns true (the other range is empty)
    range1.containsRange(null);                 // returns false
  ```
- **See also:** #overlaps(IndexRange)
##### isAfter(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public boolean isAfter(final int index)`
- **Summary:** Checks whether this range lies entirely after the specified index, i.e. every index in this range is greater than the specified index.
- **Parameters:**

- **Returns:** `true` if this entire range is after (greater than) the specified index
- **Examples:**
  ```java

    range.isAfter(1);   // returns true

  ```
- **See also:** #isBefore(int)
##### isAfterRange(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public boolean isAfterRange(final IndexRange other)`
- **Summary:** Checks whether this range is completely after the specified range, meaning every index in this range is greater than every index in the other range with no shared indices.
- **Parameters:**
  - `other` (`IndexRange`) — the range to compare against, `null` returns `false`
- **Returns:** `true` if this range is completely after the specified range with no shared indices
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IndexRange range1 = new IndexRange(10, 15);
    IndexRange range2 = new IndexRange(1, 5);
    IndexRange range3 = new IndexRange(1, 11);
  
    range1.isAfterRange(range2);   // returns true  (10 >= 5)
    range1.isAfterRange(range3);   // returns false (ranges share index 10)
  ```

- **See also:** #isBeforeRange(IndexRange), #overlaps(IndexRange)

- **Returns:** `true` if this entire range is before (less than) the specified index

  ```java
    range.isBefore(6);   // returns true

  ```

##### isBeforeRange(...) -> boolean

- **Parameters:**
  - `other` (`IndexRange`) — the range to compare against, `null` returns `false`
- **Returns:** `true` if this range is completely before the specified range with no shared indices
- **Examples:**
  ```java

    IndexRange range2 = new IndexRange(10, 15);
    IndexRange range3 = new IndexRange(4, 10);
  ```

##### isOverlappedBy(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@Deprecated public boolean isOverlappedBy(final IndexRange other)`
- **Summary:** Checks whether this range overlaps with the specified range.
- **Contract:**
  - Two ranges overlap if there is at least one index that is contained in both ranges.
- **Parameters:**
  - `other` (`IndexRange`) — the range to test for overlap, `null` returns `false`
- **Returns:** `true` if the specified range overlaps with this range; otherwise, `false`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IndexRange range1 = new IndexRange(1, 5);
    IndexRange range2 = new IndexRange(3, 8);
    IndexRange range3 = new IndexRange(6, 10);
    IndexRange range4 = new IndexRange(5, 10);
  
    range1.overlaps(range2);   // returns true (overlap from 3 to 5)
    range1.overlaps(range3);   // returns false (no overlap)
    range1.overlaps(range4);   // returns false (ranges touch at 5 but share no index)
  ```
- **See also:** #intersection(IndexRange), #isBeforeRange(IndexRange), #isAfterRange(IndexRange)
##### overlaps(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public boolean overlaps(final IndexRange other)`
- **Summary:** Checks whether this range overlaps with the specified range.
- **Contract:**
  - Two half-open index ranges overlap only when they share at least one index; ranges that merely touch at a boundary and empty ranges do not overlap.
- **Parameters:**
  - `other` (`IndexRange`) — the range to test for overlap, `null` returns `false`
- **Returns:** `true` if this range and `other` share at least one index; otherwise, `false`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IndexRange range = new IndexRange(1, 5);
    range.overlaps(new IndexRange(3, 8));   // returns true
    range.overlaps(new IndexRange(5, 10));  // returns false
    range.overlaps(null);                   // returns false
  ```
- **See also:** #intersection(IndexRange)
##### intersection(...) -> Optional<IndexRange>
- **Signature:** `public Optional<IndexRange> intersection(final IndexRange other)`
- **Summary:** Calculates the intersection of this range with another overlapping range.
- **Contract:**
  - If the ranges do not overlap, returns an empty `u.Optional`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `other` (`IndexRange`) — the range to intersect with this range; a `null` value is treated as non-overlapping and yields `u.Optional.empty()`
- **Returns:** an u.Optional`<IndexRange>` containing the intersection range if the ranges overlap; `u.Optional.empty()` if they do not overlap (or `other` is `null`, or either range is empty)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IndexRange range1 = new IndexRange(1, 5);
    IndexRange range2 = new IndexRange(3, 8);
    u.Optional<IndexRange> intersection = range1.intersection(range2);
    // returns u.Optional containing new IndexRange(3, 5)
  
    IndexRange range3 = new IndexRange(6, 10);
    u.Optional<IndexRange> noIntersection = range1.intersection(range3);
    // returns u.Optional.empty()
  ```
- **See also:** #overlaps(IndexRange), #span(IndexRange)
##### span(...) -> IndexRange
- **Signature:** `public IndexRange span(final IndexRange other) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns the minimal range that encloses both this range and the specified range.
- **Contract:**
  - If the input ranges are connected (overlapping or touching), the span is their union; if not, the span includes the gap between them.
- **Parameters:**
  - `other` (`IndexRange`) — the range to span with this range, must not be `null`
- **Returns:** the minimal range that contains all indices from both input ranges
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `other` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IndexRange range1 = new IndexRange(1, 3);
    IndexRange range2 = new IndexRange(5, 7);
    IndexRange span = range1.span(range2);
    // returns new IndexRange(1, 7), which also includes the indices 3..4 that are in neither input range
  
    new IndexRange(1, 3).span(new IndexRange(5, 5));   // returns [1, 3) — empty adds no indices
  ```
- **See also:** #intersection(IndexRange)
##### shift(...) -> IndexRange
- **Signature:** `public IndexRange shift(final int delta) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a new range whose start and end indices are offset by the specified delta.
- **Parameters:**

- **Returns:** a new `IndexRange` `\[start + delta, end + delta)`
- **Throws:**

- **Examples:**

  ```java
    new IndexRange(2, 5).shift(-2);   // returns new IndexRange(0, 3)
  ```

### Class Indexed (com.landawn.abacus.util.Indexed)
An immutable pairing of a value with a `long` index position - the value's place in a sequence, carried alongside the value itself.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### of(...) -> Indexed<T>
- **Signature:** `public static <T> Indexed<T> of(final T value, final int index) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new Indexed instance with the specified value and index.
- **Parameters:**
  - `value` (`T`) — the value to be associated with the index (may be `null`).
  - `index` (`int`) — the index position (must be non-negative, 0 to Integer.MAX_VALUE).
- **Returns:** a new immutable Indexed instance containing the specified value and index.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if index is negative (index < 0).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Basic usage
    Indexed<String> indexed = Indexed.of("Hello", 5);
  
    // With null value
    Indexed<String> nullValue = Indexed.of(null, 0);
  
    // Using in stream operations
    List<String> items = Arrays.asList("a", "b", "c");
    List<Indexed<String>> withIndices = IntStream.range(0, items.size())
        .mapToObj(i -> Indexed.of(items.get(i), i))
        .collect(Collectors.toList());
  
    // With complex types
    Indexed<List<Integer>> listIndexed = Indexed.of(Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3), 10);
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <T> Indexed<T> of(final T value, final long index) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new Indexed instance with the specified value and index.
- **Contract:**
  - This overload accepts a long index for cases where the index might exceed Integer.MAX_VALUE, such as when working with very large datasets, unbounded streams, or distributed systems where indices can grow beyond the int range.
- **Parameters:**
  - `value` (`T`) — the value to be associated with the index (may be `null`).
  - `index` (`long`) — the index position (must be non-negative, 0 to Long.MAX_VALUE).
- **Returns:** a new immutable Indexed instance containing the specified value and index.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if index is negative (index < 0).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Basic usage with long index
    Indexed<String> indexed = Indexed.of("Hello", 5_000_000_000L);
  
    // Working with large datasets
    Indexed<byte[]> dataChunk = Indexed.of(dataBytes, 9_999_999_999L);
  
    // Using with LongStream
    List<Indexed<Long>> squares = LongStream.range(0, 10)
        .mapToObj(i -> Indexed.of(i * i, i))
        .collect(Collectors.toList());
  
    // Passing a long literal to select this overload explicitly
    long position = 100L;
    Indexed<String> item = Indexed.of("item", position);   // resolves to of(T, long)
  
    // Representing positions in distributed systems
    long globalOffset = 10_000_000_000L;
    Indexed<Record> record = Indexed.of(recordData, globalOffset);
  ```

#### Public Instance Methods
##### value(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public T value()`
- **Summary:** Returns the value stored in this Indexed instance.
- **Contract:**
  - The returned value may be `null` if the Indexed instance was created with a `null` value.
  - However, if the value itself is a mutable object (such as a List or array), modifications to that object will be reflected in subsequent calls to this method.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the value associated with this index, may be `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Basic value retrieval
    Indexed<String> indexed = Indexed.of("Hello", 5);
    String value = indexed.value();   // returns "Hello"
    int index = indexed.index();      // returns 5
  
    // Handling null values
    Indexed<String> nullIndexed = Indexed.of(null, 0);
    String nullValue = nullIndexed.value();   // returns null
  
    // Using in stream operations
    List<Indexed<String>> indexedItems = Arrays.asList(
        Indexed.of("apple", 0),
        Indexed.of("banana", 1),
        Indexed.of("cherry", 2)
    );
    List<String> values = indexedItems.stream()
        .map(Indexed::value)
        .collect(Collectors.toList());
    // values: ["apple", "banana", "cherry"]
  
    // Filtering based on value
    List<Indexed<Integer>> numbers = Arrays.asList(
        Indexed.of(10, 0),
        Indexed.of(25, 1),
        Indexed.of(30, 2)
    );
    List<Integer> indicesOfLargeNumbers = numbers.stream()
        .filter(idx -> idx.value() > 20)
        .map(Indexed::index)
        .collect(Collectors.toList());
    // indicesOfLargeNumbers: [1, 2]
  ```
##### hashCode(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `@Override public int hashCode()`
- **Summary:** Returns the hash code of this Indexed instance.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the hash code value for this Indexed instance.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Indexed<String> idx1 = Indexed.of("Hello", 5);
    Indexed<String> idx2 = Indexed.of("Hello", 5);
    Indexed<String> idx3 = Indexed.of("World", 5);
  
    boolean sameHash = idx1.hashCode() == idx2.hashCode();        // true (same index and value)
    boolean differentHash = idx1.hashCode() != idx3.hashCode();   // true for these values
  
    // Using in HashSet
    Set<Indexed<String>> set = new HashSet<>();
    set.add(Indexed.of("A", 0));
    set.add(Indexed.of("A", 0));
    int size = set.size();         // 1
  ```
##### equals(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@Override public boolean equals(final Object obj)`
- **Summary:** Compares this Indexed instance to the specified object for equality.
- **Contract:**
  - Returns `true` if and only if the specified object is also an Indexed instance, and both instances have the same index and equal values.
  - Two Indexed instances are equal if they have the same index (primitive long comparison) and equal values.
  - This implementation follows the general contract of Object#equals(Object): Reflexive: `x.equals(x)` returns `true` Symmetric: `x.equals(y)` returns `true` if and only if `y.equals(x)` returns `true` Transitive: If `x.equals(y)` and `y.equals(z)`, then `x.equals(z)` Consistent: Multiple invocations return the same result (assuming no modification) Null comparison: `x.equals(null)` returns `false` Usage Examples:
- **Parameters:**
  - `obj` (`Object`) — the object to be compared for equality with this Indexed instance.
- **Returns:** `true` if the specified object is equal to this Indexed instance, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Basic equality
    Indexed<String> idx1 = Indexed.of("Hello", 5);
    Indexed<String> idx2 = Indexed.of("Hello", 5);
    Indexed<String> idx3 = Indexed.of("World", 5);
    Indexed<String> idx4 = Indexed.of("Hello", 6);
  
    idx1.equals(idx2);   // returns true (same index and value)
    idx1.equals(idx3);   // returns false (different values)
    idx1.equals(idx4);   // returns false (different indices)
  
    // Null value handling
    Indexed<String> nullIdx1 = Indexed.of(null, 0);
    Indexed<String> nullIdx2 = Indexed.of(null, 0);
    Indexed<String> nullIdx3 = Indexed.of(null, 1);
  
    nullIdx1.equals(nullIdx2);   // returns true (both have null values and same index)
    nullIdx1.equals(nullIdx3);   // returns false (different indices)
  
    // Different types
    Indexed<String> strIdx = Indexed.of("Hello", 5);
    String str = "Hello";
    strIdx.equals(str);   // returns false (different types)
  
    // Using in collections
    List<Indexed<String>> list = new ArrayList<>();
    Indexed<String> item = Indexed.of("test", 0);
    list.add(item);
    list.contains(Indexed.of("test", 0));   // returns true
    list.contains(Indexed.of("test", 1));   // returns false
  ```
##### toString(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `@Override public String toString()`
- **Summary:** Returns a string representation of this Indexed instance.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a string representation in the format `\[index\]=value`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Basic string representation
    Indexed<String> indexed = Indexed.of("Hello", 5);
    System.out.println(indexed);   // prints [5]=Hello
  
    // With null value
    Indexed<String> nullIndexed = Indexed.of(null, 0);
    System.out.println(nullIndexed);   // prints [0]=null
  
    // With different types
    Indexed<Integer> intIndexed = Indexed.of(42, 10);
    System.out.println(intIndexed);   // prints [10]=42
  
    Indexed<List<String>> listIndexed = Indexed.of(Arrays.asList("a", "b"), 3);
    System.out.println(listIndexed);   // prints [3]=[a, b]
  
    // Using in logging
    List<Indexed<String>> items = Arrays.asList(
        Indexed.of("apple", 0),
        Indexed.of("banana", 1),
        Indexed.of("cherry", 2)
    );
    items.forEach(System.out::println);
    // Output:
    // [0]=apple
    // [1]=banana
    // [2]=cherry
  
    // Large index values
    Indexed<String> largeIdx = Indexed.of("data", 5_000_000_000L);
    System.out.println(largeIdx);   // prints [5000000000]=data
  ```

### Class IntFunctions (com.landawn.abacus.util.IntFunctions)
Utility class providing static methods to create various types of IntFunction instances for collections, maps, arrays, and other commonly used objects.

**Thread-safety:** conditional
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### of(...) -> IntFunction<T>
- **Signature:** `public static <T> IntFunction<T> of(IntFunction<T> func) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns the provided IntFunction as-is.
- **Parameters:**
  - `func` (`IntFunction<T>`) — the `IntFunction` to return unchanged
- **Returns:** the same `IntFunction` instance passed as the argument
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `func` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Instead of explicitly typing:
    IntFunction<String[]> arrayCreator = size -> new String[size];
    // You can use:
    var arrayCreator = IntFunctions.of(size -> new String[size]);
  ```
##### ofBooleanArray(...) -> IntFunction<boolean\[\]>
- **Signature:** `public static IntFunction<boolean[]> ofBooleanArray()`
- **Summary:** Returns an `IntFunction` that creates `boolean\[\]` arrays of the specified length.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** an `IntFunction` that, given a length, creates a new `boolean\[\]` of that length
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IntFunction<boolean[]> arrayCreator = IntFunctions.ofBooleanArray();
    boolean[] array = arrayCreator.apply(10);   // returns new boolean[10]
    boolean[] empty = arrayCreator.apply(0);    // returns new boolean[0]
    arrayCreator.apply(-1);                     // throws NegativeArraySizeException
  ```

- **Signature:** `@Beta @SequentialOnly @Stateful public static <T> IntFunction<DisposableArray<T>> ofDisposableArray(final Class<T> componentType) throws IllegalArgumentException`

- **Examples:**

  ```java
    DisposableArray<String> array1 = func.apply(10);   // returns typed DisposableArray
    DisposableArray<String> array2 = func.apply(20);   // returns the same instance (length ignored)
    assert array1 == array2;                           // same instance reused
  ```

  ```java
    IntFunctions.registerForCollection(ArrayList.class, null);             // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```

### Class IntIterator (com.landawn.abacus.util.IntIterator)
A specialized iterator for primitive int values, providing better performance than Iterator<Integer> by avoiding boxing/unboxing overhead.

**Thread-safety:** not thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### empty(...) -> IntIterator
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("SameReturnValue") public static IntIterator empty()`
- **Summary:** Returns an empty `IntIterator` with no elements.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** an empty `IntIterator`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IntIterator empty = IntIterator.empty();
    empty.hasNext();   // returns false
  ```
##### of(...) -> IntIterator
- **Signature:** `public static IntIterator of(final int... a)`
- **Summary:** Creates an `IntIterator` from the specified int array.
- **Contract:**
  - If the array is `null` or empty, returns an empty iterator.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`int[]`) — the int array (may be `null`)
- **Returns:** a new `IntIterator` over the array elements, or an empty iterator if the array is `null` or empty
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IntIterator iter = IntIterator.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5);
    IntList list = iter.toList();   // returns [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static IntIterator of(final int[] a, final int fromIndex, final int toIndex) throws IndexOutOfBoundsException`
- **Summary:** Creates an `IntIterator` from a subsequence of the specified int array.
- **Contract:**
  - If `fromIndex` equals `toIndex`, an empty iterator is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`int[]`) — the int array (may be `null`)
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the starting index (inclusive)
  - `toIndex` (`int`) — the ending index (exclusive)
- **Returns:** a new `IntIterator` over the specified range, or an empty iterator if the validated range is empty
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `fromIndex < 0`, `toIndex > (a == null? 0: a.length)`, or `fromIndex > toIndex`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  int[] array = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    IntIterator iter = IntIterator.of(array, 1, 4);   // iterates over 2, 3, 4
  ```
##### defer(...) -> IntIterator
- **Signature:** `public static IntIterator defer(final Supplier<? extends IntIterator> iteratorSupplier) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a deferred IntIterator that is initialized lazily using the provided Supplier.
- **Contract:**
  - If it throws a runtime exception or error, that same failure is cached and rethrown by subsequent access attempts.
  - Its access methods throw IllegalStateException if the supplier returns `null` or recursively accesses this iterator during initialization.
  - Initialization exceptions and errors are cached and rethrown on later access, even if the supplier catches a recursive-access failure.
  - The supplier must return a valid source distinct from this deferred iterator and must not create a cycle through other delegating iterators.
- **Parameters:**
  - `iteratorSupplier` (`Supplier<? extends IntIterator>`) — a `Supplier` that provides the `IntIterator` when needed
- **Returns:** a lazily initialized `IntIterator`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `iteratorSupplier` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IntIterator iter = IntIterator.defer(() -> IntIterator.of(1, 2, 3));
    // The supplier is invoked only when iter is first used
    if (condition) {
        iter.hasNext();   // Triggers computation
    }
  ```
##### generate(...) -> IntIterator
- **Signature:** `public static IntIterator generate(final IntSupplier supplier) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates an infinite IntIterator that generates values using the provided IntSupplier.
- **Parameters:**
  - `supplier` (`IntSupplier`) — the `IntSupplier` used to generate each value
- **Returns:** an infinite `IntIterator` whose `hasNext()` always returns `true`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `supplier` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Random rand = new Random();
    IntIterator randomInts = IntIterator.generate(rand::nextInt);
    // Generates infinite random integers
  
    IntIterator constants = IntIterator.generate(() -> 42);
    // Generates infinite stream of 42
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static IntIterator generate(final BooleanSupplier hasNext, final IntSupplier supplier) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates an IntIterator that generates values while a condition is `true`.
- **Contract:**
  - Once `hasNext` has returned `false` the iterator is permanently exhausted: the condition is never re-evaluated, so the iterator does not resume even if the state it inspects changes later.
- **Parameters:**
  - `hasNext` (`BooleanSupplier`) — the `BooleanSupplier` that determines whether more elements exist
  - `supplier` (`IntSupplier`) — the `IntSupplier` used to generate each value
- **Returns:** an `IntIterator` that generates values while `hasNext` returns `true`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any of `hasNext`, `supplier` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  int[] counter = {0};
    IntIterator iter = IntIterator.generate(
        () -> counter[0] < 5,
        () -> counter[0]++
    );
    // Generates: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4
  ```

- **Summary:** Returns the next int value in the iteration.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the next int value
- **Throws:**
  - `java.util.NoSuchElementException` — if the iteration has no more elements
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IntIterator iter = IntIterator.of(1, 2, 3);
    int first = iter.nextInt();    // returns 1
    int second = iter.nextInt();   // returns 2
  ```
##### skip(...) -> IntIterator
- **Signature:** `public IntIterator skip(final long n) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a new `IntIterator` that skips the first `n` elements.
- **Contract:**
  - If `n` is greater than the number of remaining elements, all elements are skipped.
- **Parameters:**
  - `n` (`long`) — the number of elements to skip; must be non-negative
- **Returns:** this iterator unchanged if `n == 0`, otherwise a new `IntIterator` with the first `n` elements skipped
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `n` is negative.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IntIterator iter = IntIterator.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5);
    IntIterator skipped = iter.skip(2);   // Skips 1 and 2
    skipped.nextInt();                    // returns 3
  
    // Skip more than available
    IntIterator iter2 = IntIterator.of(1, 2);
    iter2.skip(10).hasNext();   // returns false
  ```
##### limit(...) -> IntIterator
- **Signature:** `public IntIterator limit(final long count) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a new `IntIterator` that will iterate over at most `count` elements.
- **Contract:**
  - If `count` is 0, an empty iterator is returned.
  - If `count` exceeds the number of remaining elements, all remaining elements are included.
- **Parameters:**
  - `count` (`long`) — the maximum number of elements to return; must be non-negative
- **Returns:** an empty iterator if `count == 0`, otherwise a new `IntIterator` limited to at most `count` elements
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `count` is negative.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Limit infinite iterator
    IntIterator iter = IntIterator.generate(() -> 1);
    IntIterator limited = iter.limit(3);
    limited.toArray();   // returns [1, 1, 1]
  
    // Limit to 0 returns empty
    IntIterator.of(1, 2, 3).limit(0).hasNext();   // returns false
  ```
##### filter(...) -> IntIterator
- **Signature:** `public IntIterator filter(final IntPredicate predicate) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a new IntIterator containing only elements that satisfy the given predicate.
- **Parameters:**
  - `predicate` (`IntPredicate`) — the predicate to test each element
- **Returns:** a new `IntIterator` containing only elements that match the predicate
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `predicate` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  IntIterator iter = IntIterator.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5);
    IntIterator evens = iter.filter(x -> x % 2 == 0);
    evens.toArray();   // returns [2, 4]
  ```

##### forEachRemaining(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@Deprecated @Override public void forEachRemaining(final java.util.function.Consumer<? super Integer> action) throws NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Performs the given action for each remaining element, boxing each `int` to an Integer.
- **Parameters:**
  - `action` (`java.util.function.Consumer<? super Integer>`) — the action to perform on each remaining element
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `action` is `null`, as specified by java.util.Iterator#forEachRemaining(java.util.function.Consumer).
- **Examples:**
  ```java

    iter.forEachRemaining(value -> System.out.println(value));   // Boxes each int — avoid this
  ```
