  ```java
    String age = Maps.getAsStringOrDefaultIfAbsent(map, "age", "Unknown");
  
    String missing = Maps.getAsStringOrDefaultIfAbsent(map, "missing", "Unknown");
    // missing = "Unknown"
  ```
##### getAs(...) -> Optional<T>
- **Signature:** `public static <K, T> Optional<T> getAs(final Map<K, ?> map, final K key, final Class<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns the mapped value wrapped in `Optional<T>`, converting it to `targetType` when necessary.
- **Contract:**
  - Returns `Optional.empty()` if the map is `null`/empty, the key is absent, the mapped value is `null`, or the conversion answers `null`.
  - N#convert(Object, Class) answers `null` when the value carries nothing convertible - notably for an empty `String` to any numeric wrapper type - so that result is reported the same way a `null` value is, rather than being wrapped.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, ?>`) — the map from which to retrieve the value.
  - `key` (`K`) — the key whose associated value is to be returned.
  - `targetType` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the target type to which the value should be converted; must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** an `Optional<T>` with the value mapped by the specified key (converted to `targetType` if necessary), or an empty `Optional<T>` if the map is `null`/empty, the key is absent, the value is `null`, or the conversion answers `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetType` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Object> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("date", "2023-12-25");
    map.put("count", "100");
  
    // date.isPresent() = true, date.get() = LocalDate.of(2023, 12, 25)
    Optional<LocalDate> date = Maps.getAs(map, "date", LocalDate.class);
  
    // count.isPresent() = true, count.get() = 100
    Optional<Integer> count = Maps.getAs(map, "count", Integer.class);
  
    Optional<BigDecimal> missing = Maps.getAs(map, "missing", BigDecimal.class);
    // missing.isPresent() = false
  ```
- **See also:** #getOrDefaultIfAbsent(Map, Object, Object), N#convert(Object, Class), N#convert(Object, Type)
- **Signature:** `public static <K, T> Optional<T> getAs(final Map<K, ?> map, final K key, final Type<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns the mapped value wrapped in `Optional<T>`, converting it to `targetType` when necessary.
- **Contract:**
  - Returns `Optional.empty()` if the map is `null`/empty, the key is absent, the mapped value is `null`, or the conversion answers `null`.
  - N#convert(Object, Class) answers `null` when the value carries nothing convertible - notably for an empty `String` to any numeric wrapper type - so that result is reported the same way a `null` value is, rather than being wrapped.
  - A stored value is returned as-is only when `targetType` carries no type arguments; anything else is routed through `N.convert`, which normalizes the elements, keys and values of a collection, map or array target.
  - The generic internals of other parameterized handlers - `Optional<T>`, `Pair<K, V>`, a generic bean - remain opaque there, so a value of the right raw class is still returned unconverted even when its type arguments differ.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, ?>`) — the map from which to retrieve the value.
  - `key` (`K`) — the key whose associated value is to be returned.
  - `targetType` (`Type<? extends T>`) — the target type to which the value should be converted; must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** an `Optional<T>` with the value mapped by the specified key (converted to `targetType` if necessary), or an empty `Optional<T>` if the map is `null`/empty, the key is absent, the value is `null`, or the conversion answers `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetType` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Object> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("items", Arrays.asList("A", "B", "C"));
  
    // items.isPresent() = true, items.get() = ["A", "B", "C"]
    Optional<List<String>> items = Maps.getAs(map, "items", new TypeReference<List<String>>() {}.type());
  
    Optional<Set<Integer>> missing = Maps.getAs(map, "missing", new TypeReference<Set<Integer>>() {}.type());
    // missing.isPresent() = false
  ```
- **See also:** #getOrDefaultIfAbsent(Map, Object, Object), N#convert(Object, Class), N#convert(Object, Type)
##### getAsOrDefaultIfAbsent(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public static <K, T> T getAsOrDefaultIfAbsent(final Map<K, ?> map, final K key, final T defaultValue, final Class<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns the mapped value converted to `targetType`, or `defaultValue` if the map is `null`/empty, the key is absent, or the mapped value is `null`.
- **Contract:**
  - `defaultValue` is returned as-is and must not be `null`; it is not used to determine the conversion target.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, ?>`) — the map from which to retrieve the value.
  - `key` (`K`) — the key whose associated value is to be returned.
  - `defaultValue` (`T`) — the default value to return if the map is `null`/empty, the key is absent, or the value is `null`; returned as-is and must not be `null`.
  - `targetType` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the class of the type to which a found, non-`null` value should be converted; must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** the value to which the specified key is mapped (converted to `targetType` if necessary), or `defaultValue` if the map is `null`/empty, the key is absent, the value is `null`, or the conversion answers `null`. Never `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `defaultValue` or `targetType` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Object> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("count", "100");
    map.put("active", "true");
  
    // count = 100 (converted from String)
    Integer count = Maps.getAsOrDefaultIfAbsent(map, "count", 0, Integer.class);
  
    // active = true (converted from String)
    Boolean active = Maps.getAsOrDefaultIfAbsent(map, "active", false, Boolean.class);
  
    Double missing = Maps.getAsOrDefaultIfAbsent(map, "missing", 0.0, Double.class);
    // missing = 0.0
  ```
- **See also:** #getOrDefaultIfAbsent(Map, Object, Object), #getByPathAsOrDefaultIfAbsent(Map, String, Object, Class), N#convert(Object, Class), N#convert(Object, Type)
##### getValuesIfPresent(...) -> List<V>
- **Signature:** `public static <V> List<V> getValuesIfPresent(final Map<?, ? extends V> map, final Collection<?> keys)`
- **Summary:** Returns the non-`null` values mapped by the specified keys.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<?, ? extends V>`) — the map to read from; may be `null` or empty
  - `keys` (`Collection<?>`) — the keys to read, in result order; may be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** a list containing one value for each key that maps to a non-`null` value; returns an empty list if `map` or `keys` is `null` or empty
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("a", 1);
    map.put("b", 2);
    map.put("c", null);
  
    List<String> keys = Arrays.asList("a", "b", "c", "d");
    List<Integer> values = Maps.getValuesIfPresent(map, keys);
    // values = [1, 2] (null value for "c" and missing "d" are not included)
  ```
##### getValuesOrDefaultIfAbsent(...) -> List<V>
- **Signature:** `public static <V> List<V> getValuesOrDefaultIfAbsent(final Map<?, ? extends V> map, final Collection<?> keys, final V defaultValue) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns one value for each requested key, preserving the order of `keys`.
- **Contract:**
  - If a key is absent or maps to `null`, `defaultValue` is used for that position.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<?, ? extends V>`) — the map to read from; may be `null` or empty
  - `keys` (`Collection<?>`) — the keys to read, in result order; may be `null` or empty
  - `defaultValue` (`V`) — the default value to use when a key is absent or mapped to `null`.
- **Returns:** a list with the same size and order as `keys`, using `defaultValue` when a key is absent or mapped to `null`; returns an empty list if `keys` is `null` or empty. If `map` is `null` or empty, the returned list contains `defaultValue` repeated `keys.size()` times.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `defaultValue` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("a", 1);
    map.put("b", 2);
    map.put("c", null);
  
    List<String> keys = Arrays.asList("a", "b", "c", "d");
    List<Integer> values = Maps.getValuesOrDefaultIfAbsent(map, keys, -1);
    // values = [1, 2, -1, -1] ("c" has null value, "d" is missing)
  ```
##### intersection(...) -> Map<K, V>
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> Map<K, V> intersection(final Map<K, V> map, final Map<? extends K, ? extends V> map2)`
- **Summary:** Returns a new map containing entries that are present in both input maps.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, V>`) — the first input map; may be `null`.
  - `map2` (`Map<? extends K, ? extends V>`) — the second input map to find common entries with; may be `null`.
- **Returns:** a new map containing entries present in both maps with equal values. If either map is `null` or empty, an empty map is returned.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map1 = new HashMap<>();
    map1.put("a", 1);
    map1.put("b", 2);
    map1.put("c", 3);
  
    Map<String, Integer> map2 = new HashMap<>();
    map2.put("b", 2);
    map2.put("c", 4);
    map2.put("d", 5);
  
    // Only "b" is included because it has the same value in both maps
    Map<String, Integer> result = Maps.intersection(map1, map2);   // result is {b=2}
  
    Map<String, String> map3 = new HashMap<>();
    map3.put("x", "foo");
    map3.put("y", "bar");
  
    Map<String, String> map4 = new HashMap<>();
    map4.put("x", "foo");
    map4.put("z", "baz");
  
    // Only "x" is included because it has the same value in both maps
    Map<String, String> result2 = Maps.intersection(map3, map4);   // result2 is {x=foo}
  ```
- **See also:** N#intersection(int\[\], int\[\]), N#intersection(Collection, Collection), N#commonSet(Collection, Collection), Iterables#intersection(Set, Set)
##### difference(...) -> Map<K, Pair<V, Nullable<V>>>
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> Map<K, Pair<V, Nullable<V>>> difference(final Map<K, V> map, final Map<? extends K, ? extends V> map2)`
- **Summary:** Calculates the difference between two maps.
- **Contract:**
  - For each included key the value is a Pair where the left element is the value from the first map and the right element is a Nullable holding the value from the second map (empty `Nullable` when the key is not present in the second map).
  - If you need to identify keys that are unique to each map, use #symmetricDifference(Map, Map) instead.
  - If the first map is `null`, an empty map is returned.
  - If the second map is `null`, all values from the first map will be paired with empty `Nullable` objects.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, V>`) — the first map to compare.
  - `map2` (`Map<? extends K, ? extends V>`) — the second map to compare.
- **Returns:** a map representing the difference between the two input maps.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map1 = N.asMap("a", 1, "b", 2, "c", 3);
    Map<String, Integer> map2 = N.asMap("a", 1, "b", 20, "d", 4);
  
    Map<String, Pair<Integer, Nullable<Integer>>> diff = Maps.difference(map1, map2);
    // diff contains:
    // "b" -> Pair.of(2, Nullable.of(20))    // different values
    // "c" -> Pair.of(3, Nullable.empty())   // key only in map1
    // "a" is NOT included because it has the same value in both maps
  ```
- **See also:** #symmetricDifference(Map, Map), Difference.MapDifference#of(Map, Map), N#difference(Collection, Collection), Iterables#difference(Set, Set), #intersection(Map, Map)
##### symmetricDifference(...) -> Map<K, Pair<Nullable<V>, Nullable<V>>>
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> Map<K, Pair<Nullable<V>, Nullable<V>>> symmetricDifference(final Map<K, V> map, final Map<? extends K, ? extends V> map2)`
- **Summary:** Returns a new map containing the symmetric difference between two maps.
- **Contract:**
  - For each key in the result map, the value is a pair where: If the key exists only in the first map, the pair contains the value from the first map and an empty Nullable If the key exists only in the second map, the pair contains an empty `Nullable` and the value from the second map If the key exists in both maps with different values, the pair contains both values Usage Examples: If either input map is `null`, it is treated as an empty map.
  - The result mirrors the first map's runtime type - and therefore its key semantics - where that type can be instantiated, falling back to the second map's type when the first is `null`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, V>`) — the first input map.
  - `map2` (`Map<? extends K, ? extends V>`) — the second input map.
- **Returns:** a new map containing the symmetric difference between the two input maps.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map1 = N.asMap("a", 1, "b", 2, "c", 3);
    Map<String, Integer> map2 = N.asMap("b", 2, "c", 4, "d", 5);
  
    Map<String, Pair<Nullable<Integer>, Nullable<Integer>>> result = Maps.symmetricDifference(map1, map2);
    // result contains:
    // "a" -> Pair.of(Nullable.of(1), Nullable.empty())   // key only in map1
    // "c" -> Pair.of(Nullable.of(3), Nullable.of(4))     // different values
    // "d" -> Pair.of(Nullable.empty(), Nullable.of(5))   // key only in map2
    // Note: "b" is not included because it has identical values in both maps
  ```
- **See also:** #difference(Map, Map), N#symmetricDifference(int\[\], int\[\]), N#symmetricDifference(Collection, Collection), Iterables#symmetricDifference(Set, Set), #intersection(Map, Map)
##### containsEntry(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean containsEntry(final Map<?, ?> map, final Map.Entry<?, ?> entry)`
- **Summary:** Checks if the specified map contains the specified entry.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<?, ?>`) — the map to check, may be `null`.
  - `entry` (`Map.Entry<?, ?>`) — the entry to check for, may be `null`.
- **Returns:** `true` if the map contains the specified entry; `false` otherwise, including when `map` or `entry` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("a", 1);
    map.put("b", 2);
  
    Map.Entry<String, Integer> entry1 = new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>("a", 1);
    Map.Entry<String, Integer> entry2 = new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>("a", 2);
  
    // contains1 = true
    boolean contains1 = Maps.containsEntry(map, entry1);
  
    boolean contains2 = Maps.containsEntry(map, entry2);
    // contains2 = false (value doesn't match)
  ```
- **See also:** #removeEntry(Map, Map.Entry)
- **Signature:** `public static boolean containsEntry(final Map<?, ?> map, final Object key, final Object value)`
- **Summary:** Checks if the specified map contains the specified key-value pair.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<?, ?>`) — the map to be checked.
  - `key` (`Object`) — the key whose presence in the map is to be tested.
  - `value` (`Object`) — the value whose presence in the map is to be tested.
- **Returns:** `true` if the map contains the specified key-value pair, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("a", 1);
    map.put("b", null);
  
    // contains1 = true
    boolean contains1 = Maps.containsEntry(map, "a", 1);
  
    // contains2 = false
    boolean contains2 = Maps.containsEntry(map, "a", 2);
  
    // contains3 = true
    boolean contains3 = Maps.containsEntry(map, "b", null);
  
    boolean contains4 = Maps.containsEntry(map, "c", null);
    // contains4 = false (key not present)
  ```
- **See also:** N#deepEquals(Object, Object)
##### putIfAbsent(...) -> V
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull public static <K, V> V putIfAbsent(final Map<K, V> map, final K key, final V value) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Puts if the specified key is not already associated with a value (or is mapped to `null`).
- **Contract:**
  - Use #getOrPutIfAbsent(Map, Object, Supplier) when the stored value must be non-`null`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, V>`) — the map to put the value in; must not be `null`.
  - `key` (`K`) — the key to associate the value with.
  - `value` (`V`) — the value to put if the key is absent; may be `null`, in which case `null` is stored - provided the supplied map permits `null` values.
- **Returns:** the existing `non-null` value associated with the specified key, or `null` if the key was absent or mapped to `null` (in which case the new value is put). (may return null)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `map` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, String> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("key1", "value1");
    map.put("key2", null);
  
    // result1 = "value1" (key1 already has a non-null value, not changed)
    // map = {key1=value1, key2=null}
    String result1 = Maps.putIfAbsent(map, "key1", "newValue");
  
    // result2 = null (key2 was null, now set to value2)
    // map = {key1=value1, key2=value2}
    String result2 = Maps.putIfAbsent(map, "key2", "value2");
  
    String result3 = Maps.putIfAbsent(map, "key3", "value3");
    // result3 = null (key3 was absent, now set to value3)
    // map = {key1=value1, key2=value2, key3=value3}
  ```
- **See also:** Map#putIfAbsent(Object, Object), #putIfAbsent(Map, Object, Supplier)
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull public static <K, V> V putIfAbsent(final Map<K, V> map, final K key, final Supplier<V> supplier) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Puts a supplied value if the specified key is not already associated with a value (or is mapped to `null`).
- **Contract:**
  - The `supplier` is invoked exactly once per call when the key is absent.
  - If you instead want the value that ends up associated with the key (the existing one, or the one just created by the supplier), use #getOrPutIfAbsent(Map, Object, Supplier).
  - Use #getOrPutIfAbsent(Map, Object, Supplier), which rejects a `null` supplier result with IllegalArgumentException, when the stored value must be non-`null`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, V>`) — the map to put the value in; must not be `null`.
  - `key` (`K`) — the key to associate the value with.
  - `supplier` (`Supplier<V>`) — the supplier to get the value from if the key is absent; must not be `null`, but may itself return `null`, in which case `null` is stored - provided the supplied map permits `null` values
- **Returns:** the existing `non-null` value associated with the specified key, or `null` if the key was absent or mapped to `null` (in which case the supplier is invoked and its value is put). (may return null)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `map` or `supplier` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, List<String>> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("key1", Arrays.asList("a", "b"));
    // Declare the supplier explicitly to avoid overload ambiguity with putIfAbsent(map, key, value)
    Supplier<List<String>> supplier = ArrayList::new;
  
    // Supplier is only called when the key is absent
    // result1 = [a, b] (key1 already has a non-null value, supplier not called)
    // map = {key1=[a, b]}
    List<String> result1 = Maps.putIfAbsent(map, "key1", supplier);
  
    List<String> result2 = Maps.putIfAbsent(map, "key2", supplier);
    // result2 = null (key2 was absent, supplier called and value set)
    // map = {key1=[a, b], key2=[]}
  ```
- **See also:** Map#putIfAbsent(Object, Object), #putIfAbsent(Map, Object, Object), #getOrPutIfAbsent(Map, Object, Supplier)
##### putAllIf(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@Beta public static <K, V> boolean putAllIf(final Map<K, V> targetMap, final Map<? extends K, ? extends V> sourceMap, final Predicate<? super K> keyFilter) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Puts all entries from the source map into the target map, but only if the key passes the specified filter predicate.
- **Contract:**
  - This method iterates through all entries in the source map and adds them to the target map if the key satisfies the filter condition.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetMap` (`Map<K, V>`) — the target map to which entries will be added; must not be `null`.
  - `sourceMap` (`Map<? extends K, ? extends V>`) — the source map from which entries will be taken. If `null` or empty, no action is taken and `false` is returned.
  - `keyFilter` (`Predicate<? super K>`) — a predicate that filters keys to be added to the target map
- **Returns:** `true` if any source entry passed the filter and was put into the target map, `false` otherwise. A `true` result does not necessarily mean that the target map's contents changed (an equal existing mapping may have been replaced).
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetMap` or `keyFilter` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> target = new HashMap<>();
    target.put("a", 1);
  
    Map<String, Integer> source = new HashMap<>();
    source.put("b", 2);
    source.put("c", 3);
    source.put("abc", 4);
  
    boolean changed = Maps.putAllIf(target, source, key -> key.length() > 1);
    // changed: true
    // target: {a=1, abc=4}
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Beta public static <K, V> boolean putAllIf(final Map<K, V> targetMap, final Map<? extends K, ? extends V> sourceMap, final BiPredicate<? super K, ? super V> entryFilter) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Puts all entries from the source map into the target map, but only if the key and value pass the specified filter predicate.
- **Contract:**
  - This method iterates through all entries in the source map and adds them to the target map if both the key and value satisfy the filter condition.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetMap` (`Map<K, V>`) — the target map to which entries will be added; must not be `null`.
  - `sourceMap` (`Map<? extends K, ? extends V>`) — the source map from which entries will be taken. If `null` or empty, no action is taken and `false` is returned.
  - `entryFilter` (`BiPredicate<? super K, ? super V>`) — a predicate that filters keys and values to be added to the target map
- **Returns:** `true` if any source entry passed the filter and was put into the target map, `false` otherwise. A `true` result does not necessarily mean that the target map's contents changed (an equal existing mapping may have been replaced).
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetMap` or `entryFilter` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> target = new HashMap<>();
    target.put("a", 1);
  
    Map<String, Integer> source = new HashMap<>();
    source.put("b", 2);
    source.put("c", 3);
    source.put("d", 10);
  
    boolean changed = Maps.putAllIf(target, source, (key, value) -> value > 2);
    // changed: true
    // target: {a=1, c=3, d=10}
  ```
##### merge(...) -> V
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull public static <K, V> V merge(final Map<K, V> map, final K key, final V value, final BiFunction<? super V, ? super V, ? extends V> mergeFunction) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Merges the given non-`null` value into the map for the specified key, mirroring Map#merge(Object, Object, BiFunction) as a static helper that behaves uniformly across map types.
- **Contract:**
  - If the key is absent (missing or mapped to `null`), it is associated with `value` and the `mergeFunction` is not invoked.
  - Otherwise the `mergeFunction` is applied to the existing value (first argument) and `value` (second argument); if it returns a non-`null` result the key is re-associated with it, and if it returns `null` the key is removed.
  - The resulting value (or `null` when the key was removed) is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, V>`) — the map in which the value is to be merged; must not be `null`.
  - `key` (`K`) — the key with which the resulting value is to be associated.
  - `value` (`V`) — the non-`null` value to merge with the existing value, or to store directly if the key is absent.
  - `mergeFunction` (`BiFunction<? super V, ? super V, ? extends V>`) — the function combining the existing value and `value` when the key is present; A `null` result removes the key.
- **Returns:** the new value associated with the key, or `null` if the key was removed (because `mergeFunction` returned `null`). (may return null)
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `map` or `value` is `null`, or if `mergeFunction` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> counts = new HashMap<>();
  
    // Absent key -> stored directly, mergeFunction not called
    Maps.merge(counts, "a", 1, Integer::sum);   // returns 1; counts = {a=1}
  
    // Present key -> existing value combined with the new value
    Maps.merge(counts, "a", 5, Integer::sum);   // returns 6; counts = {a=6}
  
    // mergeFunction returning null removes the entry
    Maps.merge(counts, "a", 6, (oldV, v) -> oldV.equals(v) ? null : oldV + v);
    // returns null; counts = {} ("a" removed)
  ```
- **See also:** Map#merge(Object, Object, BiFunction)
##### removeEntry(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean removeEntry(final Map<?, ?> map, final Map.Entry<?, ?> entry)`
- **Summary:** Removes the specified entry from the map.
- **Contract:**
  - This keeps the query/mutate idiom `if (containsEntry(m, e)) removeEntry(m, e)` safe for a `null` entry.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<?, ?>`) — the map from which the entry is to be removed.
  - `entry` (`Map.Entry<?, ?>`) — the entry to be removed from the map, may be `null`.
- **Returns:** `true` if the entry was removed, `false` otherwise, including when `map` or `entry` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("a", 1);
    map.put("b", 2);
    Map.Entry<String, Integer> entry = N.newEntry("a", 1);
    boolean removed = Maps.removeEntry(map, entry);   // returns true; map is {b=2}
  ```
- **See also:** Map#remove(Object, Object)
- **Signature:** `public static boolean removeEntry(final Map<?, ?> map, final Object key, final Object value)`
- **Summary:** Removes the specified key-value pair from the map.
- **Contract:**
  - This method removes an entry from the map only if the key is mapped to the specified value.
  - If the key is not present in the map or is mapped to a different value, the map remains unchanged.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<?, ?>`) — the map from which the entry is to be removed.
  - `key` (`Object`) — the key whose associated value is to be removed.
  - `value` (`Object`) — the value to be removed.
- **Returns:** `true` if the entry was removed, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("a", 1);
    map.put("b", 2);
  
    boolean removed1 = Maps.removeEntry(map, "a", 1);   // returns true; map is {b=2}
    boolean removed2 = Maps.removeEntry(map, "b", 3);   // returns false; value does not match
  ```
- **See also:** Map#remove(Object, Object)
##### removeEntries(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean removeEntries(final Map<?, ?> map, final Map<?, ?> entriesToRemove)`
- **Summary:** Removes the specified entries from the map.
- **Contract:**
  - An entry is removed only if both the key and value match exactly.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<?, ?>`) — the map from which the entries are to be removed.
  - `entriesToRemove` (`Map<?, ?>`) — the map containing the entries to be removed.
- **Returns:** `true` if any entries were removed, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("a", 1);
    map.put("b", 2);
    map.put("c", 3);
  
    Map<String, Integer> entriesToRemove = new HashMap<>();
    entriesToRemove.put("a", 1);
    entriesToRemove.put("b", 5);
  
    boolean changed = Maps.removeEntries(map, entriesToRemove);
    // changed: true
    // map: {b=2, c=3}  // Only "a"=1 was removed
  ```
##### removeKeys(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean removeKeys(final Map<?, ?> map, final Collection<?> keysToRemove)`
- **Summary:** Removes the specified keys from the map.
- **Contract:**
  - If any of the keys in the collection are not present in the map, they are ignored.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<?, ?>`) — the map from which the keys are to be removed.
  - `keysToRemove` (`Collection<?>`) — the collection of keys to be removed from the map.
- **Returns:** `true` if any keys were removed, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("a", 1);
    map.put("b", 2);
    map.put("c", 3);
  
    List<String> keysToRemove = Arrays.asList("a", "c", "d");
    boolean changed = Maps.removeKeys(map, keysToRemove);
    // changed: true
    // map: {b=2}
  ```
##### removeIf(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> boolean removeIf(final Map<K, V> map, final Predicate<? super Map.Entry<K, V>> filter) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Removes entries from the specified map that match the given filter predicate.
- **Contract:**
  - Three consequences follow, all of which differ from delegating to `map.entrySet().removeIf(..)`: If `filter` throws, this method removes no entries; earlier matches are retained.
  - A map that rejects removal is only rejected when there is something to remove: on an unmodifiable map a filter that matches nothing returns `false` rather than throwing UnsupportedOperationException, because `Map.remove` is never reached.
  - `map.entrySet().removeIf(..)` may throw even when no entry matches, depending on the view implementation.
  - Removal is therefore not atomic with the test; coordinate externally if that matters.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, V>`) — the map from which entries are to be removed.
  - `filter` (`Predicate<? super Map.Entry<K, V>>`) — the predicate used to determine which entries to remove.
- **Returns:** `true` if one or more entries were removed, `false` otherwise.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("a", 1);
    map.put("b", 2);
    map.put("c", 3);
  
    boolean changed = Maps.removeIf(map, entry -> entry.getValue() > 1);
    // changed: true
    // map: {a=1}
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> boolean removeIf(final Map<K, V> map, final BiPredicate<? super K, ? super V> filter) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Removes entries from the specified map that match the given filter predicate based on key and value.
- **Contract:**
  - Three consequences follow, all of which differ from delegating to `map.entrySet().removeIf(..)`: If `filter` throws, this method removes no entries; earlier matches are retained.
  - A map that rejects removal is only rejected when there is something to remove: on an unmodifiable map a filter that matches nothing returns `false` rather than throwing UnsupportedOperationException, because `Map.remove` is never reached.
  - `map.entrySet().removeIf(..)` may throw even when no entry matches, depending on the view implementation.
  - Removal is therefore not atomic with the test; coordinate externally if that matters.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, V>`) — the map from which entries are to be removed.
  - `filter` (`BiPredicate<? super K, ? super V>`) — the predicate used to determine which entries to remove.
- **Returns:** `true` if one or more entries were removed, `false` otherwise.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `filter` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("apple", 1);
    map.put("banana", 2);
    map.put("cherry", 3);
  
    boolean changed = Maps.removeIf(map, (key, value) -> key.length() > 5 && value > 1);
    // changed: true
    // map: {apple=1}  // "banana" and "cherry" were removed (both have length > 5 and value > 1)
  ```
##### removeIfKey(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static <K> boolean removeIfKey(final Map<K, ?> map, final Predicate<? super K> filter) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Removes entries from the specified map that match the given key filter predicate.
- **Contract:**
  - Three consequences follow, all of which differ from delegating to `map.keySet().removeIf(..)`: If `filter` throws, this method removes no entries; earlier matches are retained.
  - A map that rejects removal is only rejected when there is something to remove: on an unmodifiable map a filter that matches nothing returns `false` rather than throwing UnsupportedOperationException, because `Map.remove` is never reached.
  - `map.keySet().removeIf(..)` may throw even when no entry matches, depending on the view implementation.
  - Removal is therefore not atomic with the test; coordinate externally if that matters.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, ?>`) — the map from which entries are to be removed.
  - `filter` (`Predicate<? super K>`) — the predicate used to determine which keys to remove.
- **Returns:** `true` if one or more entries were removed, `false` otherwise.
- **Throws:**

##### removeIfValue(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static <V> boolean removeIfValue(final Map<?, V> map, final Predicate<? super V> filter) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Removes entries from the specified map that match the given value filter predicate.
- **Contract:**
  - Three consequences follow, all of which differ from delegating to `map.values().removeIf(..)`: If `filter` throws, this method removes no entries; earlier matches are retained.
  - A map that rejects removal is only rejected when there is something to remove: on an unmodifiable map a filter that matches nothing returns `false` rather than throwing UnsupportedOperationException, because `Map.remove` is never reached.
  - `map.values().removeIf(..)` may throw even when no entry matches, depending on the view implementation.

##### replace(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `@MayReturnNull public static <K, V> V replace(final Map<K, V> map, final K key, final V newValue)`
- **Annotations:** @MayReturnNull
- **Summary:** Replaces the entry for the specified key with the new value if the key is present in the map.
- **Contract:**
  - This method updates the value for a key only if the key exists in the map.
  - If the key is not present, the map remains unchanged.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, V>`) — the map in which the entry is to be replaced.
  - `key` (`K`) — the key with which the specified value is associated.
  - `newValue` (`V`) — the new value to be associated with the specified key.
- **Returns:** the previous value associated with the specified key, or `null` if the map is `null`/empty, there was no mapping for the key, or the key was previously mapped to `null`. (may return null)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("a", 1);
    map.put("b", 2);
  
    Integer oldValue1 = Maps.replace(map, "a", 10);   // returns 1
    Integer oldValue2 = Maps.replace(map, "c", 30);   // returns null
    // map: {a=10, b=2}
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> boolean replace(final Map<K, V> map, final K key, final V oldValue, final V newValue)`
- **Summary:** Replaces the entry for the specified key only if currently mapped to the specified value.
- **Contract:**
  - This method updates the value for a key only if the current value matches the oldValue parameter.
  - If the key is not present or the current value doesn't match oldValue, the map remains unchanged.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, V>`) — the map in which the entry is to be replaced.
  - `key` (`K`) — the key with which the specified value is associated.
  - `oldValue` (`V`) — the expected current value associated with the specified key.
  - `newValue` (`V`) — the new value to be associated with the specified key.
- **Returns:** `true` if the value was replaced, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("a", 1);
    map.put("b", 2);
  
    boolean replaced1 = Maps.replace(map, "a", 1, 10);   // returns true; map is {a=10, b=2}
    boolean replaced2 = Maps.replace(map, "b", 3, 20);   // returns false; old value does not match
  ```
- **See also:** N#deepEquals(Object, Object), Map#replace(Object, Object, Object)
##### replaceAll(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> void replaceAll(final Map<K, V> map, final BiFunction<? super K, ? super V, ? extends V> function) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException, ConcurrentModificationException`
- **Summary:** Replaces each entry's value with the result of applying the given function to that entry.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, V>`) — the map in which the entries are to be replaced.
  - `function` (`BiFunction<? super K, ? super V, ? extends V>`) — the function to apply to each entry to compute a new value.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `function` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if the supplied map does not support `put` / `setValue`.
  - `java.util.ConcurrentModificationException` — if the supplied map detects a structural modification during the replacement (most JDK maps compare their modification count and fail fast).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("a", 1);
    map.put("b", 2);
    map.put("c", 3);
  
    Maps.replaceAll(map, (key, value) -> value * 10);
    // map: {a=10, b=20, c=30}
  ```
- **See also:** Map#replaceAll(BiFunction)
##### filter(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> Map<K, V> filter(final Map<K, V> map, final Predicate<? super Map.Entry<K, V>> predicate) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Filters the entries of the specified map based on the given predicate.
- **Contract:**
  - The returned map is of the same type as the input map if possible.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, V>`) — the map to be filtered.
  - `predicate` (`Predicate<? super Map.Entry<K, V>>`) — the predicate used to filter the entries.
- **Returns:** a new map containing only the entries that match the predicate.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `predicate` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("a", 1);
    map.put("b", 2);
    map.put("c", 3);
  
    Map<String, Integer> filtered = Maps.filter(map, entry -> entry.getValue() > 1);
    // filtered: {b=2, c=3}
  ```
- **See also:** N#filter(Iterable, Predicate), Iterators#filter(Iterator, Predicate)
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> Map<K, V> filter(final Map<K, V> map, final BiPredicate<? super K, ? super V> predicate) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Filters the entries of the specified map based on the given predicate applied to key-value pairs.
- **Contract:**
  - The returned map is of the same type as the input map if possible.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, V>`) — the map to be filtered.
  - `predicate` (`BiPredicate<? super K, ? super V>`) — the predicate used to filter the entries.
- **Returns:** a new map containing only the entries that match the predicate.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `predicate` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("apple", 5);
    map.put("banana", 2);
    map.put("cherry", 8);
  
    Map<String, Integer> filtered = Maps.filter(map, (key, value) -> key.length() > 5 || value > 4);
    // filtered: {apple=5, banana=2, cherry=8}
  ```
- **See also:** N#filter(Iterable, Predicate), Iterators#filter(Iterator, Predicate)
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V, M extends Map<K, V>> M filter(final Map<K, V> map, final BiPredicate<? super K, ? super V> predicate, final IntFunction<? extends M> mapSupplier) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Filters the entries of the specified map based on the given predicate applied to key-value pairs, collecting the matching entries into a map created by the provided supplier.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, V>`) — the map to be filtered.
  - `predicate` (`BiPredicate<? super K, ? super V>`) — the predicate used to filter the entries
  - `mapSupplier` (`IntFunction<? extends M>`) — a function that creates a new Map instance given an expected size
- **Returns:** a new map (created by `mapSupplier`) containing only the entries that match the predicate; an empty map (from `mapSupplier.apply(0)`) if `map` is `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `predicate` or `mapSupplier` is `null`, or if `mapSupplier` returns `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("apple", 5);
    map.put("banana", 2);
    map.put("cherry", 8);
  
    // Collect matches into a LinkedHashMap
    LinkedHashMap<String, Integer> filtered = Maps.filter(map, (key, value) -> value > 4, LinkedHashMap::new);
    // filtered: {apple=5, cherry=8}
  ```
- **See also:** #filter(Map, BiPredicate)
##### filterByKey(...) -> Map<K, V>
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> Map<K, V> filterByKey(final Map<K, V> map, final Predicate<? super K> predicate) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Filters the entries of the specified map based on the given key predicate.
- **Contract:**
  - The returned map is of the same type as the input map if possible.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, V>`) — the map to be filtered.
  - `predicate` (`Predicate<? super K>`) — the predicate used to filter the keys.
- **Returns:** a new map containing only the entries with keys that match the predicate.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `predicate` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java

    map.put("apple", 1);
    map.put("banana", 2);
    map.put("apricot", 3);
  ```

##### filterByValue(...) -> Map<K, V>
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> Map<K, V> filterByValue(final Map<K, V> map, final Predicate<? super V> predicate) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Filters the entries of the specified map based on the given value predicate.
- **Contract:**
  - The returned map is of the same type as the input map if possible.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, V>`) — the map to be filtered.

  ```java
    // filtered: {b=20, c=30}
  ```
- **See also:** #removeIfValue(Map, Predicate), N#filter(Iterable, Predicate), Iterators#filter(Iterator, Predicate)
##### invert(...) -> Map<V, K>
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> Map<V, K> invert(final Map<K, V> map)`
- **Summary:** Inverts the given map by swapping its keys with its values.
- **Contract:**
  - If there are duplicate values, some information may be lost because each key in the resulting map must be unique.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, V>`) — the map to be inverted.
- **Returns:** a new map which is the inverted version of the input map.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("Alice", 1);
    map.put("Bob", 2);
    map.put("Charlie", 3);
  
    // inverted = {1=Alice, 2=Bob, 3=Charlie}
    Map<Integer, String> inverted = Maps.invert(map);
    // Example with duplicate values: the LAST value encountered wins. Use a LinkedHashMap when that
    // matters - "last" is only meaningful for a map with a defined iteration order.
    Map<String, String> map2 = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    map2.put("key1", "valueA");
    map2.put("key2", "valueA");
  
    Map<String, String> inverted2 = Maps.invert(map2);
    // inverted2 = {valueA=key2} (key1 was overwritten)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> Map<V, K> invert(final Map<K, V> map, final BiFunction<? super K, ? super K, ? extends K> mergeFunction) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Inverts the given map by swapping its keys with its values.
- **Contract:**
  - If there are duplicate values in the input map, the merging operation specified by mergeFunction is applied.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, V>`) — the map to be inverted.
  - `mergeFunction` (`BiFunction<? super K, ? super K, ? extends K>`) — the merging operation to be applied if there are duplicate values in the input map.
- **Returns:** a new map which is the inverted version of the input map.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mergeFunction` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // A LinkedHashMap, so that "first" and "last" below are actually defined: over a HashMap the
    // encounter order - and therefore which key the merge function sees first - is unspecified.
    Map<String, String> map = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    map.put("key1", "valueA");
    map.put("key2", "valueA");
    map.put("key3", "valueB");
    // Use the first key when there are duplicates
    // inverted1 = {valueA=key1, valueB=key3}
    Map<String, String> inverted1 = Maps.invert(map, (oldKey, newKey) -> oldKey);
    // Use the last key when there are duplicates
    // inverted2 = {valueA=key2, valueB=key3}
    Map<String, String> inverted2 = Maps.invert(map, (oldKey, newKey) -> newKey);
    // Concatenate keys when there are duplicates
    Map<String, String> inverted3 = Maps.invert(map, (oldKey, newKey) -> oldKey + "," + newKey);
    // inverted3 = {valueA=key1,key2, valueB=key3}
  ```
##### flatInvert(...) -> Map<V, List<K>>
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> Map<V, List<K>> flatInvert(final Map<K, ? extends Collection<? extends V>> map)`
- **Summary:** Inverts the given map by mapping each value in the Collection to the corresponding key.
- **Contract:**
  - A `null` element inside a collection is not skipped: it becomes a `null` key in the result, which throws NullPointerException if the result map's type rejects `null` keys.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, ? extends Collection<? extends V>>`) — the map to be inverted; may be `null`, which yields an empty map.
- **Returns:** a new map which is the inverted version of the input map.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, List<Integer>> map = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    map.put("Alice", Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3));
    map.put("Bob", Arrays.asList(2, 4));
    map.put("Charlie", Arrays.asList(3, 5));
  
    // inverted = {1=[Alice], 2=[Alice, Bob], 3=[Alice, Charlie], 4=[Bob], 5=[Charlie]}
    Map<Integer, List<String>> inverted = Maps.flatInvert(map);
    // Each value from the collections becomes a key, mapping to all original keys that contained it
  ```
##### transpose(...) -> List<Map<K, V>>
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> List<Map<K, V>> transpose(final Map<K, ? extends Collection<? extends V>> map)`
- **Summary:** Transforms a map of collections into a list of maps.
- **Contract:**
  - If the collections in the original map are of different sizes, the resulting list's size is equal to the size of the largest collection.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, ? extends Collection<? extends V>>`) — the input map, where each key is associated with a collection of values.
- **Returns:** a list of maps, where each map represents a "flat" version of the original map's entries.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, List<Integer>> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("a", Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3));
    map.put("b", Arrays.asList(4, 5, 6));
    map.put("c", Arrays.asList(7, 8));
  
    List<Map<String, Integer>> result = Maps.transpose(map);
    // result contains:
    // [{a=1, b=4, c=7}, {a=2, b=5, c=8}, {a=3, b=6}]
  ```
##### flatten(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public static Map<String, Object> flatten(final Map<String, Object> map) throws IllegalArgumentException, ClassCastException`
- **Summary:** Flattens the given map.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<String, Object>`) — the map to be flattened; may be `null`, which yields an empty result.
- **Returns:** a new map which is the flattened version of the input map.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a key (at any level) is `null`, a cyclic map structure is encountered, or two input paths produce the same flattened key.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a nested map's key is not a `String` (possible only when a raw or unchecked map has been stored as a value).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Object> map = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    map.put("name", "John");
    Map<String, Object> address = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    address.put("city", "New York");
    address.put("zip", "10001");
    map.put("address", address);
  
    Map<String, Object> flattened = Maps.flatten(map);
    // flattened contains {name=John, address.city=New York, address.zip=10001}
    // (entry order may vary - the returned map is a HashMap)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <M extends Map<String, Object>> M flatten(final Map<String, Object> map, final IntFunction<? extends M> mapSupplier) throws IllegalArgumentException, ClassCastException`
- **Summary:** Flattens the given map using a provided map supplier.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<String, Object>`) — the map to be flattened; may be `null`, which yields an empty result.
  - `mapSupplier` (`IntFunction<? extends M>`) — a function that creates a new Map instance given an expected size. It is invoked exactly once - the whole result is flat, so no nested maps are created.
- **Returns:** a new map which is the flattened version of the input map.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapSupplier` is `null`, returns `null`, or returns the input map, or if a key (at any level) is `null`, a cyclic map structure is encountered, or two input paths produce the same flattened key.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a nested map's key is not a `String` (possible only when a raw or unchecked map has been stored as a value).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Object> map = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    map.put("name", "John");
    Map<String, Object> address = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    address.put("city", "New York");
    address.put("zip", "10001");
    map.put("address", address);
    // Use a LinkedHashMap to preserve insertion order
    LinkedHashMap<String, Object> flattened = Maps.flatten(map, LinkedHashMap::new);
    // flattened = {name=John, address.city=New York, address.zip=10001}
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <M extends Map<String, Object>> M flatten(final Map<String, Object> map, final String delimiter, final IntFunction<? extends M> mapSupplier) throws IllegalArgumentException, ClassCastException`
- **Summary:** Flattens the given map using a provided map supplier and a delimiter.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<String, Object>`) — the map to be flattened; may be `null`, which yields an empty result.
  - `delimiter` (`String`) — the non-empty delimiter to be used when concatenating keys.
  - `mapSupplier` (`IntFunction<? extends M>`) — a function that creates a new Map instance given an expected size. It is invoked exactly once - the whole result is flat, so no nested maps are created.
- **Returns:** a new map which is the flattened version of the input map.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapSupplier` is `null`, returns `null`, or returns the input map, or if `delimiter` is `null` or empty, a key (at any level) is `null`, a cyclic map structure is encountered, or two input paths produce the same flattened key.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a nested map's key is not a `String` (possible only when a raw or unchecked map has been stored as a value).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Object> map = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    map.put("name", "John");
    Map<String, Object> address = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    address.put("city", "New York");
    address.put("zip", "10001");
    map.put("address", address);
    // Use underscore as delimiter instead of dot
    Map<String, Object> flattened = Maps.flatten(map, "_", LinkedHashMap::new);
    // flattened = {name=John, address_city=New York, address_zip=10001}
  ```
##### unflatten(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public static Map<String, Object> unflatten(final Map<String, Object> map) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Unflattens the given map.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<String, Object>`) — the flattened map to be unflattened; may be `null`, which yields an empty result.
- **Returns:** a new map which is the unflattened version of the input map.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a key is `null` or flat keys conflict (for example, both `"a"` and `"a.b"` are present).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Object> flattened = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    flattened.put("name", "John");
    flattened.put("address.city", "New York");
    flattened.put("address.zip", "10001");
  
    Map<String, Object> unflattened = Maps.unflatten(flattened);
    // unflattened contains {name=John, address={city=New York, zip=10001}}
    // (entry order may vary - the returned/nested maps are HashMaps)
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <M extends Map<String, Object>> M unflatten(final Map<String, Object> map, final IntFunction<? extends M> mapSupplier) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Unflattens the given map using a provided map supplier.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<String, Object>`) — the flattened map to be unflattened; may be `null`, which yields an empty result.
  - `mapSupplier` (`IntFunction<? extends M>`) — a function that creates a new Map instance given an expected size; it must return a distinct map on every invocation.
- **Returns:** a new map which is the unflattened version of the input map.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapSupplier` is `null`, returns `null`, or does not return a distinct new map on every invocation, or if a key is `null`, or flat keys conflict (for example, both `"a"` and `"a.b"` are present).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Object> flattened = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    flattened.put("name", "John");
    flattened.put("address.city", "New York");
    flattened.put("address.zip", "10001");
    // Use a LinkedHashMap to preserve insertion order
    LinkedHashMap<String, Object> unflattened = Maps.unflatten(flattened, LinkedHashMap::new);
    // unflattened = {name=John, address={city=New York, zip=10001}}
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <M extends Map<String, Object>> M unflatten(final Map<String, Object> map, final String delimiter, final IntFunction<? extends M> mapSupplier) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Unflattens the given map using a provided map supplier and a delimiter.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<String, Object>`) — the flattened map to be unflattened; may be `null`, which yields an empty result.
  - `delimiter` (`String`) — the non-empty delimiter that was used in the flattening process to concatenate keys.
  - `mapSupplier` (`IntFunction<? extends M>`) — a function that creates a new Map instance given an expected size; it must return a distinct map on every invocation.
- **Returns:** a new map which is the unflattened version of the input map. Keys without the delimiter are copied as-is; no error is raised when the delimiter is absent.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapSupplier` is `null`, returns `null`, or does not return a distinct new map on every invocation, or if `delimiter` is `null` or empty, a key is `null`, or flat keys conflict (for example, both `"a"` and `"a.b"` are present).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Object> flattened = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    flattened.put("name", "John");
    flattened.put("address_city", "New York");
    flattened.put("address_zip", "10001");
    // Use underscore as delimiter
    Map<String, Object> unflattened = Maps.unflatten(flattened, "_", LinkedHashMap::new);
    // unflattened = {name=John, address={city=New York, zip=10001}}
  ```
##### replaceKeys(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static <K> void replaceKeys(final Map<K, ?> map, final Function<? super K, ? extends K> keyConverter) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Replaces (renames) the keys in the specified map by applying the given converter to each existing key.
- **Contract:**
  - If duplicates are detected, throws IllegalStateException before modifying the map.
  - Notes: If a key converts to itself (i.e., `keyConverter.apply(key).equals(key)`), the entry is still removed and reinserted, which may affect iteration order in some map implementations.
  - If `keyConverter` returns `null`, it is treated as a valid key.
  - However, if `null` is returned for multiple keys, an IllegalStateException is thrown due to duplicate keys.
  - If the map is empty or `null`, this method returns immediately without any action.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, ?>`) — the map whose keys are to be replaced; modified in-place. If `null` or empty, no action is taken.
  - `keyConverter` (`Function<? super K, ? extends K>`) — the function applied once to each processed key to produce the new key; processing stops if conversion fails or produces a duplicate
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `keyConverter` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the converted keys contain duplicates (including multiple `null` values); the message identifies both original source keys without invoking the converter again
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `map` does not support Map#clear() or Map#putAll(Map). Failures while applying the validated copy can leave the map empty or partially populated; only failures during conversion and duplicate detection leave it untouched.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Convert keys to uppercase
    Map<String, Integer> map = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    map.put("name", 1);
    map.put("age", 2);
    map.put("city", 3);
  
    Maps.replaceKeys(map, Strings::toUpperCase);
    // map now contains: {NAME=1, AGE=2, CITY=3}
    // Add prefix to keys
    Map<String, String> data = new HashMap<>();
    data.put("id", "123");
    data.put("type", "user");
  
    Maps.replaceKeys(data, k -> "prefix_" + k);
    // data now contains: {prefix_id=123, prefix_type=user}
    // This will throw IllegalStateException (duplicate keys):
    // Maps.replaceKeys(map, k -> "constant"); // All keys convert to same value
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <K, V> void replaceKeys(final Map<K, V> map, final Function<? super K, ? extends K> keyConverter, final BiFunction<? super V, ? super V, ? extends V> mergeFunction) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Replaces (renames) keys in the specified map by applying the given converter, merging values when multiple original keys map to the same converted key.
- **Contract:**
  - If that map already contains the converted key (according to the map implementation's own key semantics), `mergeFunction` combines the existing value (first argument) and incoming value (second argument).
  - When multiple keys convert to the same new key, merges occur in that iteration order.
  - If `keyConverter` returns `null` for any key, behavior depends on the map implementation.
  - If `mergeFunction` returns `null`, the entry accumulated so far under that converted key is removed - the same rule Map#merge(Object, Object, BiFunction) and #zip(Iterable, Iterable, BiFunction, IntFunction) follow.
  - A key is therefore missing from the result only when its last collision resolved to `null`.
  - Return a sentinel value and strip it afterwards when a dropped key must stay dropped.
  - Unlike Map#merge(Object, Object, BiFunction), `mergeFunction` is invoked based on key presence: it is called even when the existing value under the new key, or the value being moved, is `null` (the corresponding argument is then `null`).
  - If the map is empty or `null`, this method returns immediately without any action.
- **Parameters:**
  - `map` (`Map<K, V>`) — the map whose keys are to be replaced; modified in-place. If `null` or empty, no action is taken.
  - `keyConverter` (`Function<? super K, ? extends K>`) — converts each existing key to its replacement key
  - `mergeFunction` (`BiFunction<? super V, ? super V, ? extends V>`) — merges values when multiple entries map to the same converted key. The function receives `(existingValue, incomingValue)` and returns the merged value. If it returns `null`, the entry is removed.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any of `keyConverter`, `mergeFunction` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `map` does not support Map#clear() or Map#putAll(Map). Failures while applying the validated copy can leave the map empty or partially populated - the copy is built first, so only failures during conversion and merging leave the map untouched.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Merge values when keys collide (sum integers)
    Map<String, Integer> map = new HashMap<>();
    map.put("a1", 10);
    map.put("a2", 20);
    map.put("b1", 30);
  
    // Explanation: "a1" (10) and "a2" (20) both map to "a", merged via sum -> 30
    Maps.replaceKeys(map, k -> k.substring(0, 1), Integer::sum);
    // map now contains: {a=30, b=30}
    // Concatenate strings on collision
    Map<String, String> data = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    data.put("user_1", "John");
    data.put("user_2", "Jane");
    data.put("admin_1", "Bob");
  
    Maps.replaceKeys(data, k -> k.split("_")[0], (v1, v2) -> v1 + ", " + v2);
    // data now contains: {user="John, Jane", admin="Bob"}
    // Use (existing, incoming) -> existing to keep the first value on a collision.
    // Use (existing, incoming) -> incoming to keep the last value on a collision.
    // Returning null removes what has accumulated under the key so far, but a still-later entry
    // converting to that key re-creates it without consulting the merger:
    Map<String, Integer> three = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    three.put("a1", 1);
    three.put("a2", 2);
    three.put("a3", 3);
    Maps.replaceKeys(three, k -> "a", (existing, incoming) -> existing == 1 ? null : existing + incoming);
    // three now contains: {a=3}   (not {})
  ```
- **See also:** #replaceKeys(Map, Function)
##### replaceKeysWithCamelCase(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static void replaceKeysWithCamelCase(final Map<String, ?> props) throws IllegalStateException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Converts the keys in the provided map from snake_case (or other delimited formats) to camelCase.
- **Contract:**
  - Conversion Examples: `"user_name"` -> `"userName"` `"first_name"` -> `"firstName"` `"USER_NAME"` -> `"userName"` `"user-name"` -> `"userName"` `"userName"` -> `"userName"` (already camelCase, unchanged) `"XMLParser"` -> `"xmlParser"` (split at the case boundary) Usage Examples: Notes: If the map is `null` or empty, this method returns immediately without any action.
  - If multiple keys convert to the same camelCase key, an IllegalStateException is thrown before any modifications are made (e.g., `"user_name"` and `"USER_NAME"` both convert to `"userName"`).
- **Parameters:**
  - `props` (`Map<String, ?>`) — the map whose keys are to be converted to camelCase; modified in-place. If `null` or empty, no action is taken.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the converted keys contain duplicates
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `props` does not support Map#clear() or Map#putAll(Map), as an immutable or unmodifiable map does
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Convert snake_case keys to camelCase
    Map<String, Object> map = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    map.put("user_name", "John");
    map.put("first_name", "Jane");
    map.put("email_address", "john@example.com");
  
    Maps.replaceKeysWithCamelCase(map);
    // map now contains: {userName=John, firstName=Jane, emailAddress=john@example.com}
    // Useful when converting database column names to Java property names
    Map<String, Object> dbRow = queryRow("SELECT user_id, created_at FROM users");
    Maps.replaceKeysWithCamelCase(dbRow); // dbRow contains {userId=..., createdAt=...}
  ```
- **See also:** #replaceKeys(Map, Function), Fn#toCamelCase(), Strings#toCamelCase(String), #replaceKeysWithSnakeCase(Map), #replaceKeysWithScreamingSnakeCase(Map)

  - If multiple keys convert to the same snake_case key, an IllegalStateException is thrown before any modifications are made (e.g., `"userName"` and `"UserName"` both convert to `"user_name"`).
- **Parameters:**
  - `props` (`Map<String, ?>`) — the map whose keys are to be converted to snake_case; modified in-place. If `null` or empty, no action is taken.

  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the converted keys contain duplicates
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `props` does not support Map#clear() or Map#putAll(Map), as an immutable or unmodifiable map does
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Convert camelCase keys to snake_case
    Map<String, Object> map = new LinkedHashMap<>();
  ```

- **Summary:** Converts the keys in the provided map from camelCase to SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (uppercase with underscores).

  - `props` (`Map<String, ?>`) — the map whose keys are to be converted to SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE; modified in-place. If `null` or empty, no action is taken.

  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the converted keys contain duplicates
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `props` does not support Map#clear() or Map#putAll(Map), as an immutable or unmodifiable map does

  ```java
    Maps.replaceKeysWithScreamingSnakeCase(map);
    // map now contains: {USER_NAME=John, FIRST_NAME=Jane, MAX_RETRY_COUNT=3}

    Map<String, Object> config = loadConfig();
    Maps.replaceKeysWithScreamingSnakeCase(config); // keys are SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE for env-variable naming
  ```

- **Signature:** `public static MediaType of(final int intValue) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns the MediaType enum constant corresponding to the specified numeric value.
- **Contract:**

- **Parameters:**
  - `intValue` (`int`) — the numeric value of the media type (must be between 0 and 5 inclusive)

### Class Median (com.landawn.abacus.util.Median)
Finds the median element (or the two middle elements) of an array, a collection, or a range of either, without modifying the input.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### of(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public static Pair<Character, OptionalChar> of(final char... source) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Finds the median value(s) from an array of characters using natural ordering.
- **Contract:**
  - The median represents the middle value(s) when the array elements are arranged in sorted order.
  - For arrays with an odd number of elements, returns the single median value in the `left` component of the pair, with the `right` component empty.
  - For arrays with an even number of elements, returns the two median values, with the smaller value in the `left` component and the larger value in the `right` component.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`char[]`) — the array of characters to find the median from. Must not be `null` or empty.
- **Returns:** a `Pair` containing the median value(s). For odd-length arrays, the `left` contains the median and `right` is empty. For even-length arrays, the `left` contains the smaller median and `right` contains the larger median.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the specified array is `null` or empty.
- **Performance:** Arrays of four or more elements are copied and the copy is sorted in O(n log n) time; shorter arrays are selected directly.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Pair<Character, OptionalChar> median = Median.of('z', 'a', 'm');
    char medianValue = median.left();  // returns 'm'
  ```
- **See also:** #of(char\[\], int, int), Pair, OptionalChar, N#lowerMedian(char\[\])
- **Signature:** `public static Pair<Character, OptionalChar> of(final char[] source, final int fromIndex, final int toIndex) throws IndexOutOfBoundsException, IllegalArgumentException`

  - The median represents the middle value(s) when the subarray elements are arranged in sorted order.

  - For subarrays with an even number of elements, returns the two median values, with the smaller value in the `left` component and the larger value in the `right` component.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`char[]`) — the array of characters to find the median from. Must not be `null` or empty.
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the starting index (inclusive) of the range within the array to consider. Must be non-negative and less than toIndex.
  - `toIndex` (`int`) — the ending index (exclusive) of the range within the array to consider. Must be greater than fromIndex and not exceed array length.
- **Returns:** a `Pair` containing the median value(s). For odd-length subarrays, the `left` contains the median and `right` is empty. For even-length subarrays, the `left` contains the smaller median and `right` contains the larger median.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `fromIndex` is negative, `toIndex` is greater than the length of the array, or `fromIndex > toIndex`. The range is validated first, so an out-of-range index always raises this rather than `IllegalArgumentException`.
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the specified array is `null` or empty, or if the (in-range) `toIndex - fromIndex` is less than 1.
- **Examples:**
  ```java

    Pair<Character, OptionalChar> median = Median.of(chars, 1, 3);
    // Considers only 'a' and 'm', returns ['a', OptionalChar.of('m')]
  ```

- **Summary:** Finds the median value(s) from an array of Comparable objects using their natural ordering.
- **Contract:**
  - The median represents the middle value(s) when the array elements are arranged in sorted order according to their natural comparison method (compareTo).
  - For arrays with an odd number of elements, returns the single median value in the `left` component of the pair, with the `right` component empty.
  - For arrays with an even number of elements, returns the two median values, with the smaller value in the `left` component and the larger value in the `right` component.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`T[]`) — the array of Comparable objects to find the median from. Must not be `null` or empty.

- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the specified array is `null` or empty.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if the selected elements cannot be compared with each other by the chosen ordering
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String[] words = {"apple", "banana", "cherry"};
    Pair<String, Nullable<String>> median = Median.of(words);
    String medianWord = median.left();  // returns "banana"
  ```

- **Signature:** `public static <T extends Comparable<? super T>> MergeResult minFirst(final T a, final T b)`
- **Summary:** Compares two comparable values and returns a MergeResult indicating which value is smaller (or equal).
- **Contract:**
  - If the first value is less than or equal to the second, #TAKE_FIRST is returned; otherwise, #TAKE_SECOND is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`T`) — the first value to compare
  - `b` (`T`) — the second value to compare
- **Returns:** #TAKE_FIRST if a is less than or equal to b, #TAKE_SECOND otherwise
- **Examples:**
  ```java

    MergeResult result2 = MergeResult.minFirst("b", "a");   // returns TAKE_SECOND
  ```

### Class MoreExecutors (com.landawn.abacus.util.MoreExecutors)
Factory and utility methods for java.util.concurrent.Executor, ExecutorService, and ThreadFactory.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### getExitingExecutorService(...) -> ExecutorService
- **Signature:** `public static ExecutorService getExitingExecutorService(final ThreadPoolExecutor executor) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Converts the given ThreadPoolExecutor into an ExecutorService that exits when the JVM exits.
- **Parameters:**
  - `executor` (`ThreadPoolExecutor`) — the executor to modify
- **Returns:** an unconfigurable ExecutorService that shuts down on JVM exit, provided all of its threads were created after this call
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `executor` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the virtual machine is already in the process of shutting down, so the shutdown hook cannot be registered.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ThreadPoolExecutor threadPool = new ThreadPoolExecutor(
        5, 10, 60L, TimeUnit.SECONDS,
        new LinkedBlockingQueue<>()
    );
    ExecutorService exitingService = MoreExecutors.getExitingExecutorService(threadPool);
  ```
- **See also:** #getExitingExecutorService(ThreadPoolExecutor, long, TimeUnit)
- **Signature:** `public static ExecutorService getExitingExecutorService(final ThreadPoolExecutor executor, final long terminationTimeout, final TimeUnit timeUnit) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Converts the given ThreadPoolExecutor into an ExecutorService that exits when the JVM exits, with a custom termination timeout.
- **Contract:**
  - If the executor doesn't terminate within the timeout, the shutdown hook will exit anyway.
  - Usage Examples: The conversion is failure-atomic: if the shutdown hook cannot be registered - Runtime#addShutdownHook throws IllegalStateException once the JVM has begun shutting down - the caller's executor is left with the thread factory it had, rather than with daemon threads and no hook to drain them.
- **Parameters:**
  - `executor` (`ThreadPoolExecutor`) — the executor to modify
  - `terminationTimeout` (`long`) — the maximum time to wait for the executor to terminate
  - `timeUnit` (`TimeUnit`) — the time unit for the termination timeout
- **Returns:** an unconfigurable ExecutorService that shuts down on JVM exit, provided all of its threads were created after this call
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `executor` or `timeUnit` is `null`, or `terminationTimeout` is negative.
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the virtual machine is already in the process of shutting down, so the shutdown hook cannot be registered.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ThreadPoolExecutor threadPool = new ThreadPoolExecutor(
        1, 1, 0L, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS,
        new java.util.concurrent.LinkedBlockingQueue<Runnable>()
    );
    ExecutorService exitingService = MoreExecutors.getExitingExecutorService(
        threadPool, 30, TimeUnit.SECONDS
    );
  ```
##### getExitingScheduledExecutorService(...) -> ScheduledExecutorService
- **Signature:** `public static ScheduledExecutorService getExitingScheduledExecutorService(final ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor executor) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Converts the given ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor into a ScheduledExecutorService that exits when the JVM exits.
- **Parameters:**
  - `executor` (`ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor`) — the scheduled executor to modify
- **Returns:** an unconfigurable ScheduledExecutorService that shuts down on JVM exit, provided all of its threads were created after this call
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `executor` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the virtual machine is already in the process of shutting down, so the shutdown hook cannot be registered.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor scheduler = new ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor(3);
    ScheduledExecutorService exitingScheduler =
        MoreExecutors.getExitingScheduledExecutorService(scheduler);
  ```
- **See also:** #getExitingScheduledExecutorService(ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor, long, TimeUnit)
- **Signature:** `public static ScheduledExecutorService getExitingScheduledExecutorService(final ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor executor, final long terminationTimeout, final TimeUnit timeUnit) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Converts the given ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor into a ScheduledExecutorService that exits when the JVM exits, with a custom termination timeout.
- **Contract:**
  - If the executor doesn't terminate within the timeout, the shutdown hook will exit anyway.
  - Usage Examples: The conversion is failure-atomic: if the shutdown hook cannot be registered - Runtime#addShutdownHook throws IllegalStateException once the JVM has begun shutting down - the caller's executor is left with the thread factory it had, rather than with daemon threads and no hook to drain them.
- **Parameters:**
  - `executor` (`ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor`) — the scheduled executor to modify
  - `terminationTimeout` (`long`) — the maximum time to wait for the executor to terminate
  - `timeUnit` (`TimeUnit`) — the time unit for the termination timeout
- **Returns:** an unconfigurable ScheduledExecutorService that shuts down on JVM exit, provided all of its threads were created after this call
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `executor` or `timeUnit` is `null`, or `terminationTimeout` is negative.
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the virtual machine is already in the process of shutting down, so the shutdown hook cannot be registered.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor scheduler = new ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor(3);
    ScheduledExecutorService exitingScheduler =
        MoreExecutors.getExitingScheduledExecutorService(scheduler, 30, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
  ```
##### addDelayedShutdownHook(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static void addDelayedShutdownHook(final ExecutorService service, final long terminationTimeout, final TimeUnit timeUnit) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Adds a shutdown hook that will attempt to shut down the given ExecutorService when the JVM exits.
- **Parameters:**
  - `service` (`ExecutorService`) — the executor service to shut down on JVM exit
  - `terminationTimeout` (`long`) — the maximum time to wait for the executor to terminate
  - `timeUnit` (`TimeUnit`) — the time unit for the termination timeout
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `service` or `timeUnit` is `null`, or `terminationTimeout` is negative.
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the virtual machine is already in the process of shutting down, so the shutdown hook cannot be registered.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ExecutorService service = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(5);
    MoreExecutors.addDelayedShutdownHook(service, 60, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
  ```

#### Public Instance Methods
- (none)

### Class Multimap (com.landawn.abacus.util.Multimap)
A collection that maps keys to multiple values, similar to Map but allowing each key to be associated with a collection of values rather than a single value.

**Thread-safety:** not thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified
**Permitted subtypes:** ListMultimap, SetMultimap

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### get(...) -> V
- **Signature:** `public V get(final Object key)`
- **Summary:** Returns the collection of values associated with the specified key.
- **Contract:**
