- **Signature:** `@Override public <R, C, T> Sheet<R, C, T> pivot(final String keyColumnName, final String pivotColumnName, final Collection<String> aggregateOnColumnNames, final Collector<? super Object[], ?, ? extends T> collector) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Performs a pivot operation on the Dataset using the specified key column, aggregate columns, pivot column, and a collector.
- **Documentation:** inherits documentation from the overridden member
- **Contract:**
  - Obtain those retained keys from Sheet#rowKeySet() and Sheet#columnKeySet(), or supply Wrapper#of(Object) keys in this Dataset when content-based lookup is required on the result.
- **Parameters:**
  - `keyColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used as the row identifier in the resulting Sheet.
  - `pivotColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used as the column identifier in the resulting Sheet.
  - `aggregateOnColumnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the names of the columns on which the aggregate operation is to be performed. Must not be `null` or empty.
  - `collector` (`Collector<? super Object[], ?, ? extends T>`) — the collector that defines the aggregate operation.
- **Returns:** a Sheet representing the result of the pivot operation.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; a column selection contains duplicate names; `aggregateOnColumnNames` is null or empty; `collector` is null; the key and pivot column names are equal, or either selected key column contains a null value.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if a collector supplier, accumulator, or finisher throws while grouping a row or producing an aggregate result.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("region", "product", "sales", "quantity"),
        new Object[][] {
             {"North", "A", 100, 10},
             {"North", "B", 200, 20},
             {"South", "A", 150, 15},
             {"South", "B", 250, 25}
        });
  
    // +--------+---------+-------+----------+
    // | region | product | sales | quantity |
    // +--------+---------+-------+----------+
    // | North  | A       | 100   | 10       |
    // | North  | B       | 200   | 20       |
    // | South  | A       | 150   | 15       |
    // | South  | B       | 250   | 25       |
    // +--------+---------+-------+----------+
  
    Sheet<String, String, Integer> pivotResult = dataset.pivot(
        "region",                                                           // "region" is the row identifier
        "product",                                                          // "product" is the column identifier
        Arrays.asList("sales", "quantity"),                                 // "sales" and "quantity" are the aggregate columns
        Collectors.summingInt(arr -> (Integer) arr[0] + (Integer) arr[1])); // sums sales + quantity
  
    // Result Sheet:
    //         +-----+-----+
    //         | A   | B   |
    // +-------+-----+-----+
    // | North | 110 | 220 |
    // | South | 165 | 275 |
    // +-------+-----+-----+
  ```
- **See also:** #pivot(String, String, String, Collector), #groupBy(Collection), #rollup(Collection), #cube(Collection), Difference between groupby and pivot_table for pandas dataframes (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/34702815)
- **Signature:** `@Override public <R, C, U, T> Sheet<R, C, T> pivot(final String keyColumnName, final String pivotColumnName, final Collection<String> aggregateOnColumnNames, final Function<? super DisposableObjArray, ? extends U> rowMapper, final Collector<? super U, ?, ? extends T> collector) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Performs a pivot operation on the Dataset using the specified key column, aggregate columns, pivot column, a row mapper, and a collector.
- **Documentation:** inherits documentation from the overridden member
- **Contract:**
  - Obtain those retained keys from Sheet#rowKeySet() and Sheet#columnKeySet(), or supply Wrapper#of(Object) keys in this Dataset when content-based lookup is required on the result.
- **Parameters:**
  - `keyColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used as the row identifier in the resulting Sheet.
  - `pivotColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used as the column identifier in the resulting Sheet.
  - `aggregateOnColumnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the names of the columns on which the aggregate operation is to be performed. Must not be `null` or empty.
  - `rowMapper` (`Function<? super DisposableObjArray, ? extends U>`) — the function to transform the row data before aggregation.
  - `collector` (`Collector<? super U, ?, ? extends T>`) — the collector that defines the aggregate operation.
- **Returns:** a Sheet representing the result of the pivot operation.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; a column selection contains duplicate names; `aggregateOnColumnNames` is null or empty; `rowMapper`, `collector` is null; the key and pivot column names are equal, or either selected key column contains a null value.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the rowMapper, a collector supplier, accumulator, or finisher throws while grouping a row or producing an aggregate result.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("region", "product", "sales", "quantity"),
        new Object[][] {
             {"North", "A", 100, 10},
             {"North", "B", 200, 20},
             {"South", "A", 150, 15},
             {"South", "B", 250, 25}
        });
  
    // +--------+---------+-------+----------+
    // | region | product | sales | quantity |
    // +--------+---------+-------+----------+
    // | North  | A       | 100   | 10       |
    // | North  | B       | 200   | 20       |
    // | South  | A       | 150   | 15       |
    // | South  | B       | 250   | 25       |
    // +--------+---------+-------+----------+
  
    Function<DisposableObjArray, Double> rowMapper = row -> (Integer) row.get(0) * 1.1;  // transforms sales with a 10% markup
  
    Sheet<String, String, Double> pivotResult = dataset.pivot(
        "region",                                                                                               // "region" is the row identifier
        "product",                                                                                              // "product" is the column identifier
        Arrays.asList("sales", "quantity"),                                                                     // "sales" and "quantity" are the aggregate columns
        rowMapper,                                                                                              // transforms each row value
        Collectors.collectingAndThen(Collectors.summingDouble(Double::doubleValue), r -> Numbers.round(r, 2))); // collects aggregated values
    //         +-------+-------+
    //         | A     | B     |
    // +-------+-------+-------+
    // | North | 110.0 | 220.0 |
    // | South | 165.0 | 275.0 |
    // +-------+-------+-------+
  ```
- **See also:** #pivot(String, String, String, Collector), #pivot(String, String, Collection, Collector), #groupBy(Collection), #rollup(Collection), #cube(Collection), Difference between groupby and pivot_table for pandas dataframes (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/34702815)
##### sortBy(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@Override public void sortBy(final String columnName) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sorts the Dataset based on the specified column name.
- **Documentation:** inherits documentation from the overridden member
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used for sorting.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if this dataset is frozen
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; the sorting algorithm detects an ordering that violates the comparator contract.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if compared non-null cell values or extracted keys are not mutually comparable under the selected ordering.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset employees = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("name", "age", "salary"), new Object[][] { { "Alice", 25, 50000.0 }, { "Bob", 30, 60000.0 } });
    employees.sortBy("age");   // sorts by age in ascending order
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Override public void sortBy(final String columnName, final Comparator<?> cmp) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sorts the Dataset based on the specified column name using the provided Comparator.
- **Documentation:** inherits documentation from the overridden member
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used for sorting.
  - `cmp` (`Comparator<?>`) — the Comparator to determine the order of the elements.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if this dataset is frozen
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; `cmp` is null; the sorting algorithm detects an ordering that violates the comparator contract.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if compared non-null cell values or extracted keys are not mutually comparable under the selected ordering.
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if a comparison is reached with a null value and the supplied comparator does not support it.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the supplied comparator throws when invoked to determine row order.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name"), new Object[][] {{2, "Bob"}, {1, "Alice"}});
    dataset.sortBy("id", Comparator.reverseOrder());  // sorts in place by id in descending order
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Override public void sortBy(final Collection<String> columnNames) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sorts the Dataset based on the specified collection of column names.
- **Documentation:** inherits documentation from the overridden member
- **Parameters:**

  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if compared non-null cell values or extracted keys are not mutually comparable under the selected ordering.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("department", "name"), new Object[][] {{"Sales", "Bob"}, {"IT", "Alice"}});
    dataset.sortBy(Arrays.asList("department", "name"));  // sorts in place by department, then by name
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Override public void sortBy(final Collection<String> columnNames, final Comparator<? super Object[]> cmp) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sorts the Dataset based on the specified collection of column names using the provided Comparator.
- **Documentation:** inherits documentation from the overridden member
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the collection of column names to be used for sorting.
  - `cmp` (`Comparator<? super Object[]>`) — the Comparator to determine the order of the elements. It compares Object arrays, each representing a row.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if this dataset is frozen
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; `columnNames` is null, contains duplicate names, or is empty while the dataset has columns; `cmp` is null; the sorting algorithm detects an ordering that violates the comparator contract.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if compared non-null cell values or extracted keys are not mutually comparable under the selected ordering.
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if a comparison is reached with a null value and the supplied comparator does not support it.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the supplied comparator throws when invoked to determine row order.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name"), new Object[][] {{2, "Bob"}, {1, "Alice"}});
    // Sort by id in descending order, comparing the first element of each row array
    dataset.sortBy(Arrays.asList("id", "name"),
        (a, b) -> Integer.compare((Integer)b[0], (Integer)a[0]));  // sorts in place with custom comparator
  ```
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("rawtypes") @Override public void sortBy(final Collection<String> columnNames, final Function<? super DisposableObjArray, ? extends Comparable> keyExtractor) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sorts the Dataset based on the specified column names and a key mapper function.
- **Documentation:** inherits documentation from the overridden member
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the names of the columns to be used for sorting. The order of the column names determines the order of the elements in the DisposableObjArray passed to the key mapper function.
  - `keyExtractor` (`Function<? super DisposableObjArray, ? extends Comparable>`) — a function that takes a DisposableObjArray representing a row of the Dataset and returns a Comparable object that is used for sorting.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if this dataset is frozen
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; `columnNames` is null, contains duplicate names, or is empty while the dataset has columns; `keyExtractor` is null; the sorting algorithm detects an ordering that violates the comparator contract.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if compared non-null cell values or extracted keys are not mutually comparable under the selected ordering.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the supplied key extractor throws when invoked to determine row order.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("firstName", "lastName"),
        new Object[][] {
            {"John", "Smith"},
            {"Jane", "Doe"},
            {"Bob", "Anderson"}
        });
    // Sort by concatenated full name (case-insensitive)
    dataset.sortBy(Arrays.asList("firstName", "lastName"),
        row -> ((String)row.get(0) + " " + (String)row.get(1)).toLowerCase());  // sorts in place by full name
  ```

##### topBy(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `@Override public Dataset topBy(final String columnName, final int n) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns the top n rows from the Dataset based on the values in the specified column.
- **Documentation:** inherits documentation from the overridden member
- **Contract:**
  - If the Dataset contains fewer than n rows, all rows are returned.
  - When more rows tie at the cut-off than there is room for, the earliest of them are kept.
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used for determining the top rows.
  - `n` (`int`) — the number of top rows to return.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset containing the top n rows.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; `n < 1`.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if compared non-null cell values or extracted keys are not mutually comparable under the selected ordering and `n < size()`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset employees = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("name", "salary", "age"), data);
    Dataset topPaid = employees.topBy("salary", 5);   // keeps top 5 highest salaries
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Override public Dataset topBy(final String columnName, final int n, final Comparator<?> cmp) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns the top n rows from the Dataset based on the values in the specified column, as ranked by the provided Comparator.
- **Documentation:** inherits documentation from the overridden member
- **Contract:**
  - If the Dataset contains fewer than n rows, all rows are returned.
  - When more rows tie at the cut-off than there is room for, the earliest of them are kept.
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used for determining the top rows.
  - `n` (`int`) — the number of top rows to return.
  - `cmp` (`Comparator<?>`) — the Comparator used to rank the column values; rows with the greatest values according to this Comparator are kept.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset containing the top n rows.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; `cmp` is null; `n < 1`.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if compared non-null cell values or extracted keys are not mutually comparable under the selected ordering and `n < size()`.
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if a comparison is reached with a null value and the supplied comparator does not support it.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the supplied comparator throws when invoked to select the top rows.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "score"), new Object[][] {{1, 85}, {2, 95}, {3, 90}});
    // With reverseOrder, the "greatest" values per the comparator are the smallest scores
    Dataset bottom = dataset.topBy("score", 2, Comparator.reverseOrder());  // keeps rows {1, 85} and {3, 90}
  ```

- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset employees = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("name", "salary"), data);
    // Rank by salary only, so the 5 lowest-paid rows are the "greatest" per this Comparator
    Dataset bottom = employees.topBy(Arrays.asList("name", "salary"), 5,
        (a, b) -> Integer.compare((Integer) b[1], (Integer) a[1]));
  ```
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("rawtypes") @Override public Dataset topBy(final Collection<String> columnNames, final int n, final Function<? super DisposableObjArray, ? extends Comparable> keyExtractor) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns the top n rows from the Dataset based on the Comparable keys derived from the specified columns by the provided keyExtractor function.
- **Documentation:** inherits documentation from the overridden member
- **Contract:**
  - If the Dataset contains fewer than n rows, all rows are returned.
  - When more rows tie at the cut-off than there is room for, the earliest of them are kept.
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the names of the columns to be used for determining the top rows.
  - `n` (`int`) — the number of top rows to return.
  - `keyExtractor` (`Function<? super DisposableObjArray, ? extends Comparable>`) — the function that maps a row to a Comparable key used for ranking. It takes a DisposableObjArray representing the specified columns of a row and returns a Comparable.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset containing the top n rows.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a specified column name is null or unknown; `columnNames` is null, contains duplicate names, or is empty while the dataset has columns; `keyExtractor` is null; `n < 1`.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if compared non-null cell values or extracted keys are not mutually comparable under the selected ordering and `n < size()`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the supplied key extractor throws when invoked to select the top rows.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset employees = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("name", "salary", "bonus"), data);
    // Keep the 5 rows with the highest salary + bonus
    Dataset top = employees.topBy(Arrays.asList("salary", "bonus"), 5,
        row -> (Integer) row.get(0) + (Integer) row.get(1));
  ```

- **Signature:** `@Override public Dataset distinctBy(final String columnName, final Function<?, ?> keyExtractor) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a new Dataset containing only the distinct rows based on the specified column from the original Dataset.

  ```java

        });
    // Get distinct rows by email, case-insensitive

    // Result: two rows (alice@example.com appears twice but is treated as one when lowercased)
  ```

##### mapColumn(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `@Override public Dataset mapColumn(final String fromColumnName, final String newColumnName, final String copyingColumnName, final Function<?, ?> mapper) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Transforms the Dataset by applying a mapping function to the specified column and creating a new column with the results.
- **Documentation:** inherits documentation from the overridden member
- **Parameters:**
  - `fromColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be used as input for the mapping function.
  - `newColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the new column that will store the results of the mapping function. Must not be `null` or empty, and must not be one of the copied columns.
  - `copyingColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the column to be copied to the new Dataset. Must not be `null`.
  - `mapper` (`Function<?, ?>`) — the mapping function to apply to each row of the specified column. It takes an instance of the column's value and returns a new value.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset with the new column added and the specified column copied.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapper` is `null`, `newColumnName` is null or empty, the new name duplicates a copied column, or a source or copied column does not exist.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if `mapper` throws an unchecked exception while mapping a row.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset employees = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("name", "salary"), new Object[][] {{"Alice", 50000.0}});
    Dataset result = employees.mapColumn("salary", "bonus", "name", salary -> (Double) salary * 0.1);
    // Result columns: name, bonus
  ```

- **Summary:** Transforms the Dataset by applying a mapping function to the specified columns and creating new rows with the results.
- **Documentation:** inherits documentation from the overridden member
- **Parameters:**
  - `fromColumnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — a collection of column names to be used as input for the mapping function.
  - `newColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the new column that will store the results of the mapping function. Must not be `null` or empty, and must not be one of the copied columns.
  - `copyingColumnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — a collection of column names to be copied to the new Dataset. May be `null` or empty, in which case the result holds only the new column.
  - `mapper` (`Function<? super DisposableObjArray, ? extends Collection<?>>`) — the mapping function to apply to each row of the specified columns. It takes an instance of DisposableObjArray, which represents the values in the Dataset's row for the specified columns, and returns a Collection of new rows. Rows for which the mapper returns `null` or an empty Collection contribute no rows to the result.

  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if `mapper` throws an unchecked exception while mapping a row.
- **Examples:**
  ```java

  ```

  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `right` is `null` or a join column is absent from its corresponding Dataset, or `onColumnNames` is null or empty, or `newColumnName` is null, empty, or already present in this Dataset, or `newColumnType` is null or is not an object-array, collection, map, or bean type, or `collSupplier` is null or returns null for a group.

  - If there is no match, the result is `null` on the left side.
- **Parameters:**
  - `right` (`Dataset`) — the other Dataset to join with.
  - `onColumnNames` (`Map<String, String>`) — a map where the key is the column name in this Dataset to join on, and the value is the column name in the other Dataset to join on. Must not be `null` or empty.
  - `newColumnName` (`String`) — the name of the new column to be added to the resulting Dataset.
  - `newColumnType` (`Class<?>`) — the type of each right-hand row stored in the new column's collection. It must be Object\[\], Collection, Map, or Bean class.
  - `collSupplier` (`IntFunction<? extends Collection>`) — a function that generates a collection to hold the joined rows for the new column for one-many or many-many mapping.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset that is the result of the right join operation, with the additional column.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `right` is `null` or a join column is absent from its corresponding Dataset, or `onColumnNames` is null or empty, or `newColumnName` is null, empty, or already present in this Dataset, or `newColumnType` is null or is not an object-array, collection, map, or bean type, or `collSupplier` is null or returns null for a group.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the collection supplier throws an unchecked exception, its result rejects a joined row, or a right-hand row cannot be constructed or populated as `newColumnType`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset left = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name"), new Object[][] {{1, "Alice"}, {1, "Alicia"}});
    Dataset right = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "score"), new Object[][] {{1, 95}, {1, 88}, {2, 85}});
    Dataset joined = left.rightJoin(right, N.asMap("id", "id"), "scores", Map.class, size -> new ArrayList<>(size));
    // Three result rows. One per matching left row, each holding a List of the matching RIGHT rows:
    //   {1, "Alice",  [{id=1, score=95}, {id=1, score=88}]}
    //   {1, "Alicia", [{id=1, score=95}, {id=1, score=88}]}
    // and, for the right key with no left match, a row whose left columns are null:
    //   {null, null,  [{id=2, score=85}]}
  ```
- **See also:** What is the difference between "INNER JOIN" and "OUTER JOIN" (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/38549)

- **Summary:** Returns multiset subtraction: each key occurs max(leftCount - rightCount, 0) times.
- **Documentation:** inherits documentation from the overridden member
- **Contract:**
  - Differing schemas are accepted when the flag is false.
- **Parameters:**
  - `other` (`Dataset`) — the non-null right operand
  - `keyColumnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — non-null key selection present in both operands; may be empty only when both have no columns
  - `requiresSameColumns` (`boolean`) — whether both operands must have identical column-name sets
- **Returns:** an independent Dataset with shallowly shared cell values
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `other` is `null`, `keyColumnNames` is null, contains an unknown or duplicate key column, or is empty unless both Datasets have no columns, or `requiresSameColumns` is true and the Datasets have different column-name sets.
##### cartesianProduct(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `@Override public Dataset cartesianProduct(final Dataset other) throws IllegalArgumentException, ArithmeticException`
- **Summary:** Performs a cartesian product operation with this Dataset and another Dataset.
- **Documentation:** inherits documentation from the overridden member
- **Contract:**
  - The resulting Dataset will have the combined columns of both Datasets, so the two Datasets must not share any column names.
  - For example, if this Dataset has 3 rows and the other Dataset has 2 rows, the resulting Dataset will have 6 rows (3 × 2).
- **Parameters:**
  - `other` (`Dataset`) — the Dataset to perform the cartesian product with.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset that is the result of the cartesian product operation.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `other` is `null`, or the Datasets share a column name.
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if the product of the row counts exceeds Integer#MAX_VALUE
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset1 = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name"),
        new Object[][] {
             {1, "Alice"},
             {2, "Bob"}
        });
    Dataset dataset2 = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("category", "score"),
        new Object[][] {
             {"A", 95},
             {"B", 90}
        });
  
    Dataset result = dataset1.cartesianProduct(dataset2);
    // Result contains columns: id, name, category, score
    // Result contains: {1, "Alice", "A", 95}, {1, "Alice", "B", 90},
    //                  {2, "Bob", "A", 95}, {2, "Bob", "B", 90}
  ```
- **See also:** #merge(Dataset), #innerJoin(Dataset, String, String), #leftJoin(Dataset, String, String), #union(Dataset)

##### slice(...) -> Dataset
- **Signature:** `@Override public Dataset slice(final Collection<String> columnNames) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns an immutable slice of this Dataset that includes only the columns specified in the columnNames collection from the original Dataset.
- **Documentation:** inherits documentation from the overridden member
- **Parameters:**
  - `columnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the collection of column names to be included in the sliced Dataset. If null or empty, the row range must also be empty.
- **Returns:** a new Dataset containing the same rows as the original Dataset, but only the columns specified in the columnNames collection.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the selection contains an unknown or duplicate column name, or `columnNames` is null or empty and the selected row range is nonempty.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name", "age"), new Object[][] {{1, "Alice", 25}, {2, "Bob", 30}});
    Dataset slice = dataset.slice(Arrays.asList("id", "name"));
  ```
- **See also:** List#subList(int, int)
- **Signature:** `@Override public Dataset slice(final int fromRowIndex, final int toRowIndex) throws IndexOutOfBoundsException`

- **Throws:**

  ```java
    dataset.println("## ");   // prints entire Dataset to console with prefix "## "
  
    // ## +----+---------+-----+---------+
    // ## | id | name    | age | salary  |
    // ## +----+---------+-----+---------+
    // ## | 1  | John    | 25  | 50000.0 |
    // ## | 2  | Jane    | 30  | 60000.0 |
    // ## | 3  | Bob     | 35  | 70000.0 |
    // ## | 4  | Alice   | 28  | 55000.0 |
    // ## | 5  | Charlie | 40  | 80000.0 |
    // ## +----+---------+-----+---------+
  ```
- **See also:** #println()
- **Signature:** `@Override public void println(final int fromRowIndex, final int toRowIndex) throws IndexOutOfBoundsException`
- **Summary:** Prints a portion of the Dataset to the standard output.
- **Documentation:** inherits documentation from the overridden member
- **Parameters:**
  - `fromRowIndex` (`int`) — the starting index of the row range (inclusive).
  - `toRowIndex` (`int`) — the ending index of the row range (exclusive).
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `fromRowIndex < 0`, `fromRowIndex > toRowIndex`, or `toRowIndex > size()`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a selected cell to text fails.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name"), data);
    dataset.println(0, 10);   // prints first 10 rows to console
  ```
- **See also:** #println(), #println(String)
- **Signature:** `@Override public void println(final int fromRowIndex, final int toRowIndex, final Collection<String> columnNames) throws IndexOutOfBoundsException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Prints a portion of the Dataset to the standard output.
- **Documentation:** inherits documentation from the overridden member
- **Parameters:**
  - `fromRowIndex` (`int`) — the starting index of the row range (inclusive).
  - `toRowIndex` (`int`) — the ending index of the row range (exclusive).
  - `columnNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the collection of column names to be printed; if `null` or empty, no columns are printed
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `fromRowIndex < 0`, `fromRowIndex > toRowIndex`, or `toRowIndex > size()`.
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a nonempty `columnNames` selection contains an unknown or duplicate column name.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a selected cell to text fails.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name", "age"), data);
    dataset.println(0, 5, Arrays.asList("id", "name"));   // prints first 5 rows, only id and name columns
  ```
- **See also:** #println(), #println(String)
- **Signature:** `@Override public void println(final Appendable output) throws IllegalArgumentException, UncheckedIOException`
- **Summary:** Prints the Dataset to the provided Appendable.
- **Documentation:** inherits documentation from the overridden member
- **Parameters:**
  - `output` (`Appendable`) — the appendable where the Dataset will be printed
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `output` is `null`.
  - `com.landawn.abacus.exception.UncheckedIOException` — if appending the formatted table to `output`, or flushing a writer, throws an java.io.IOException.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a selected cell to text fails, or the supplied output throws an unchecked exception while appending.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Dataset dataset = Dataset.rows(Arrays.asList("id", "name"), new Object[][] { { 1, "Alice" }, { 2, "Bob" } });
    StringWriter writer = new StringWriter();
    dataset.println(writer);   // prints Dataset to StringWriter
  ```
- **See also:** #println(), #println(String)

### Class Seid (com.landawn.abacus.util.Seid)
Simple Entity ID (Seid) - A flexible entity identifier implementation.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- `@Deprecated @Internal public Seid(final String entityName)` (@Internal) — Creates a new Seid with the specified entity name.
  ```java
  Seid seid = new Seid("User");
    String name = seid.entityName();   // returns "User"
    boolean empty = seid.isEmpty();    // returns true
    int size = seid.size();            // returns 0
  ```
- `public Seid(final String propName, final Object propValue) throws IllegalArgumentException` — Creates a new Seid with a single property-value pair.
  - **Throws:**
    - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `propName` is `null`.
  ```java
  Seid userId = new Seid("User.id", 123);
    // Entity name will be "User", property name will be "id"
  ```
- `public Seid(final Map<String, Object> nameValues) throws IllegalArgumentException` — Creates a new Seid from a map of property names to values.
  - **Throws:**
    - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `nameValues` is `null` or empty, or contains a `null` property name.
  ```java
  Map<String, Object> props = new HashMap<>();
    props.put("User.id", 123);
    props.put("User.version", 1);
    Seid seid = new Seid(props);
  ```

##### create(...) -> Seid
- **Signature:** `public static Seid create(final Map<String, Object> nameValues) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new Seid from a map of property names to values.
- **Parameters:**
  - `nameValues` (`Map<String, Object>`) — a map of property names to their values
- **Returns:** a new Seid instance
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `nameValues` is `null` or empty, or contains a `null` property name.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Object> props = Map.of("User.id", 123, "User.version", 1);
    Seid seid = Seid.create(props);
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static Seid create(final Object entity) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new Seid from an entity object by extracting its ID properties.
- **Contract:**
  - The entity class must declare at least one id property: a property annotated as an id (for example `@Id`, `@ReadOnlyId`, or a JPA `@Id`), or - when no property is annotated - a property named `id` whose declared type is `int`, `Integer`, `long`, `Long`, `String`, `java.sql.Timestamp` or `java.util.UUID`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entity` (`Object`) — the entity object to extract ID from; must not be `null`
- **Returns:** a new Seid containing the entity's ID properties
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `entity` is `null`, or if no ID properties are defined in the entity class.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  @Entity
    public class User {
        @Id
        private Long id;
        private String name;
  
        public User(Long id, String name) {
            this.id = id;
            this.name = name;
        }
  
        public Long getId() { return id; }
        public String getName() { return name; }
    }
  
    User user = new User(123L, "John");
    Seid userId = Seid.create(user);   // will contain id=123
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static Seid create(final Object entity, final Collection<String> idPropNames) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new Seid from an entity object using specified property names as IDs.
- **Parameters:**
  - `entity` (`Object`) — the entity object to extract values from; must not be `null`
  - `idPropNames` (`Collection<String>`) — the simple names of properties to use as ID; must not be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** a new Seid containing the specified properties and their values from the entity
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `entity` is `null`, `idPropNames` is `null` or empty, or a named property does not exist on the entity type.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  record User(Long id, String email, String name) {}
    User user = new User(123L, "john@example.com", "John");
    Seid emailId = Seid.create(user, Arrays.asList("email"));
  ```

##### get(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("unchecked") @Override public <T> T get(final String propName) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Gets the value of the specified property.
- **Parameters:**
  - `propName` (`String`) — the property name
- **Returns:** the property value, or `null` if not found
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `propName` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Seid seid = Seid.of("User.id", 123);
    Integer id = seid.get("id");         // returns 123
    Integer id2 = seid.get("User.id");   // also returns 123
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Override public <T> T get(final String propName, final Class<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Gets the value of the specified property, converting it to the target type if necessary.
- **Contract:**
  - If the property is absent or its value is `null`, the target type's default value is returned: `0` for primitive types such as `int.class`, `false` for `boolean.class`, and `null` for reference types including wrapper types such as `Integer.class`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `propName` (`String`) — the property name
  - `targetType` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the class of the target type
- **Returns:** the property value converted to the target type, or the target type's default value (which is `null` for reference types) if the property is absent or its value is `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `propName` or `targetType` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the stored value cannot be converted to `targetType`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Seid seid = Seid.of("User.active", "true");
    Boolean active = seid.get("active", Boolean.class);   // returns Boolean.TRUE
  ```
##### getInt(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `@Override public int getInt(final String propName) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Gets the value of the specified property as an int.
- **Contract:**
  - If the stored value is a Number, its `intValue()` is returned; otherwise the value is converted via type-conversion.
  - Returns `0` if the property is absent or its value is `null`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `propName` (`String`) — the property name
- **Returns:** the property value as an int, or `0` if the property is absent or `null`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `propName` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the stored value cannot be converted to the requested numeric type.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Seid seid = Seid.of("User.age", "25");
    int age = seid.getInt("age");   // returns 25 (converted from String)
  ```

- **Signature:** `@Deprecated @Internal public Seid set(final String propName, final Object propValue) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @Internal
- **Summary:** Sets a property value in this Seid.
- **Parameters:**

  - `propValue` (`Object`) — the property value

- **Signature:** `@Deprecated @Internal public void set(final Map<String, Object> nameValues) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @Internal
- **Summary:** Sets multiple property values in this Seid.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: The update is atomic with respect to validation: if any property name is invalid, this identifier is left unchanged.
- **Parameters:**
  - `nameValues` (`Map<String, Object>`) — a map of property names (simple or canonical) to their values; ignored if `null` or empty
- **Throws:**

- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Seid seid = Seid.of("User");
    Map<String, Object> props = new HashMap<>();
    props.put("User.id", 123);   // canonical name stored as "id"
    props.put("name", "John");
    seid.set(props);
    Integer id = seid.get("id");            // returns 123
    String name = seid.get("name");         // returns "John"
    int size = seid.size();                 // returns 2
    seid.set((Map<String, Object>) null);   // null map is ignored, size stays 2
  ```

  ```java
  Seid seid = Seid.of("User.id", 123, "User.name", "John");
    String str = seid.toString();   // returns "User: {id=123, name=John}"
  ```

### Class Seq (com.landawn.abacus.util.Seq)
A sequence class that represents a lazy, functional sequence of elements supporting both intermediate and terminal operations, similar to Java Streams but with support for checked exceptions.

**Thread-safety:** not thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified
**Annotations:** @Beta, @LazyEvaluation, @SequentialOnly

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### empty(...) -> Seq<T, E>
- **Signature:** `public static <T, E extends Exception> Seq<T, E> empty()`
- **Summary:** Returns an empty `Seq` with no elements.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** an empty `Seq`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Seq<String, Exception> emptySeq = Seq.empty();
    // emptySeq.count() returns 0
  ```
- **See also:** #of(Object...)
##### defer(...) -> Seq<T, E>
- **Signature:** `public static <T, E extends Exception> Seq<T, E> defer(final Supplier<? extends Seq<? extends T, ? extends E>> supplier) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a `Seq` that is lazily populated by the provided supplier.
- **Contract:**
  - The supplier is invoked when traversal first needs the supplied sequence.
  - The supplier is not invoked at all if the returned sequence is closed without ever being traversed, so a supplier that opens a resource (a file, a JDBC cursor, …) opens nothing in that case.
  - The sequence the supplier returned — and only that instance — is closed when the returned sequence is closed.
  - If the supplier throws, the exception propagates from the terminal operation and a later traversal may invoke it again.
  - If the supplier returns an already closed sequence, traversal throws IllegalStateException.
- **Parameters:**
  - `supplier` (`Supplier<? extends Seq<? extends T, ? extends E>>`) — a supplier that provides the sequence when invoked.
- **Returns:** a lazily populated `Seq`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `supplier` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Defer creation of expensive sequence until actually needed
    Seq<String, IOException> deferredSeq = Seq.defer(() ->
        Seq.ofLines(new File("data.txt"))
    );
    // File is not read until a terminal operation is called
    List<String> lines = deferredSeq.toList();
  ```
- **See also:** #just(Object)

- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Seq<String, Exception> seq = Seq.just("hello");
    // seq contains one element: "hello"
  ```

- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> map = Map.of("a", 1, "b", 2, "c", 3);
    Seq<Integer, Exception> values = Seq.ofValues(map, (k, v) -> k.equals("a") || v > 2);
    // values contains 1 and 3; encounter order follows the map's iteration order
  ```
- **See also:** #ofValues(Map, Throwables.Predicate), #ofKeys(Map, Throwables.BiPredicate)
##### ofReversed(...) -> Seq<T, E>
- **Signature:** `public static <T, E extends Exception> Seq<T, E> ofReversed(final T[] array)`
- **Summary:** Returns a `Seq` containing the elements from the specified array in reverse order.
- **Contract:**
  - If the array is `null` or empty, an empty sequence is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `array` (`T[]`) — the array whose elements will be reversed.
- **Returns:** a `Seq` containing the array elements in reverse order, or an empty sequence if the array is `null` or empty.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String[] array = {"a", "b", "c"};
    Seq<String, Exception> reversed = Seq.ofReversed(array);
    // reversed contains: "c", "b", "a"
  ```
- **See also:** #ofReversed(List), #of(Object...)
- **Signature:** `public static <T, E extends Exception> Seq<T, E> ofReversed(final List<? extends T> list)`
- **Summary:** Returns a `Seq` containing the elements from the specified list in reverse order.
- **Contract:**
  - If the list is `null` or empty, an empty sequence is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `list` (`List<? extends T>`) — the list whose elements will be reversed.
- **Returns:** a `Seq` containing the list elements in reverse order, or an empty sequence if the list is `null` or empty.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> list = Arrays.asList("a", "b", "c");
    Seq<String, Exception> reversed = Seq.ofReversed(list);
    // reversed contains: "c", "b", "a"
  ```
- **See also:** #ofReversed(Object\[\]), #of(Iterable)
##### repeat(...) -> Seq<T, E>
- **Signature:** `public static <T, E extends Exception> Seq<T, E> repeat(final T element, final long n) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a `Seq` that repeats the given element for the specified number of times.
- **Contract:**
  - If n is 0, an empty sequence is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `element` (`T`) — the element to repeat.
  - `n` (`long`) — the number of times to repeat the element. Must not be negative.
- **Returns:** a `Seq` containing the element repeated n times, or an empty sequence if n is 0.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `n` is negative.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Seq<String, Exception> seq = Seq.repeat("hello", 3);
    // seq contains: "hello", "hello", "hello"
  
    Seq<Integer, Exception> empty = Seq.repeat(42, 0);
    // empty sequence
  ```
- **See also:** #range(int, int)
##### range(...) -> Seq<Integer, E>
- **Signature:** `public static <E extends Exception> Seq<Integer, E> range(final int startInclusive, final int endExclusive)`
- **Summary:** Returns a `Seq` containing a range of integers from startInclusive (inclusive) to endExclusive (exclusive) with increment of 1.
- **Parameters:**
  - `startInclusive` (`int`) — the starting value (inclusive).
  - `endExclusive` (`int`) — the ending value (exclusive).
- **Returns:** a `Seq<Integer, E>` containing the range of integers, or an empty sequence if `endExclusive <= startInclusive`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Seq<Integer, Exception> seq = Seq.range(0, 5);
    // seq contains: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4
  
    Seq<Integer, Exception> negative = Seq.range(5, 0);
    // empty sequence (endExclusive <= startInclusive)
  ```
- **See also:** #range(int, int, int), #rangeClosed(int, int)
- **Signature:** `public static <E extends Exception> Seq<Integer, E> range(final int startInclusive, final int endExclusive, final int by) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a `Seq` containing a range of integers from startInclusive (inclusive) to endExclusive (exclusive) with the specified increment.
- **Parameters:**
  - `startInclusive` (`int`) — the starting value (inclusive).
  - `endExclusive` (`int`) — the ending value (exclusive).
  - `by` (`int`) — the increment value. Can be negative for descending ranges, but must not be zero.
- **Returns:** a `Seq<Integer, E>` containing the range of integers with the specified step.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `by` is zero.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Seq<Integer, Exception> seq = Seq.range(0, 10, 2);
    // seq contains: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8
  
    Seq<Integer, Exception> reverse = Seq.range(10, 0, -2);
    // reverse contains: 10, 8, 6, 4, 2
  ```
- **See also:** #range(int, int), #rangeClosed(int, int, int)
##### rangeClosed(...) -> Seq<Integer, E>
- **Signature:** `public static <E extends Exception> Seq<Integer, E> rangeClosed(final int startInclusive, final int endInclusive)`
- **Summary:** Returns a `Seq` containing a range of integers from startInclusive (inclusive) to endInclusive (inclusive) with increment of 1.
- **Parameters:**
  - `startInclusive` (`int`) — the starting value (inclusive).
  - `endInclusive` (`int`) — the ending value (inclusive).
- **Returns:** a `Seq<Integer, E>` containing the range of integers from start to end inclusive.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Seq<Integer, Exception> seq = Seq.rangeClosed(0, 5);
    // seq contains: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
  
    Seq<Integer, Exception> single = Seq.rangeClosed(5, 5);
    // single element: 5
  ```
- **See also:** #range(int, int), #rangeClosed(int, int, int)
- **Signature:** `public static <E extends Exception> Seq<Integer, E> rangeClosed(final int startInclusive, final int endInclusive, final int by) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a `Seq` containing a range of integers from startInclusive (inclusive) to endInclusive (inclusive) with the specified increment.
- **Parameters:**
  - `startInclusive` (`int`) — the starting value (inclusive).
  - `endInclusive` (`int`) — the ending value (inclusive).
  - `by` (`int`) — the increment value. Can be negative for descending ranges, but must not be zero.
- **Returns:** a `Seq<Integer, E>` containing the range of integers from start to end inclusive with the specified step.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `by` is zero.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Seq<Integer, Exception> seq = Seq.rangeClosed(0, 10, 2);
    // seq contains: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10
  
    Seq<Integer, Exception> reverse = Seq.rangeClosed(10, 0, -2);
    // reverse contains: 10, 8, 6, 4, 2, 0
  ```
- **See also:** #rangeClosed(int, int), #range(int, int, int)
##### split(...) -> Seq<String, E>
- **Signature:** `public static <E extends Exception> Seq<String, E> split(final CharSequence str, final char delimiter)`
- **Summary:** Splits the given character sequence into a sequence of strings based on the specified delimiter character.
- **Contract:**
  - If the string is `null`, an empty sequence is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`CharSequence`) — the character sequence to split.
  - `delimiter` (`char`) — the delimiter character to use for splitting.
- **Returns:** a `Seq<String, E>` containing the split strings (an empty sequence if the string is `null`).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Seq<String, Exception> seq = Seq.split("a,b,c", ',');
    // seq contains: "a", "b", "c"
  ```
- **See also:** #split(CharSequence, CharSequence), #split(CharSequence, Pattern), #splitToLines(String)
- **Signature:** `public static <E extends Exception> Seq<String, E> split(final CharSequence str, final CharSequence delimiter) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Splits the given character sequence into a sequence of strings based on the specified delimiter string.
- **Contract:**
  - If the string is `null`, an empty sequence is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`CharSequence`) — the character sequence to split.
  - `delimiter` (`CharSequence`) — the delimiter string to use for splitting; must not be `null` or empty.
- **Returns:** a `Seq<String, E>` containing the split strings (an empty sequence if the string is `null`).
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `delimiter` is `null` or empty.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Seq<String, Exception> seq = Seq.split("a::b::c", "::");
    // seq contains: "a", "b", "c"
  ```
- **See also:** #split(CharSequence, char), #split(CharSequence, Pattern), #splitToLines(String)
- **Signature:** `public static <E extends Exception> Seq<String, E> split(final CharSequence str, final Pattern pattern) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Splits the given character sequence into a sequence of strings based on the specified pattern.
- **Contract:**
  - If the string is `null`, an empty sequence is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`CharSequence`) — the character sequence to split.
  - `pattern` (`Pattern`) — the regex pattern to use for splitting; must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** a `Seq<String, E>` containing the split strings (an empty sequence if the string is `null`).
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `pattern` is `null`, or if it matches the empty input string (a pattern that merely has zero-length matches on non-empty input, such as `\\b`, is accepted).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Pattern pattern = Pattern.compile("\\s+");
    Seq<String, Exception> seq = Seq.split("a  b   c", pattern);
    // seq contains: "a", "b", "c"
  ```
- **See also:** #split(CharSequence, char), #split(CharSequence, CharSequence), #splitToLines(String)
##### splitToLines(...) -> Seq<String, E>
- **Signature:** `public static <E extends Exception> Seq<String, E> splitToLines(final String str)`
- **Summary:** Splits the given string into a sequence of lines.
- **Contract:**
  - If the string is `null`, an empty sequence is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to split into lines.
- **Returns:** a `Seq<String, E>` containing the lines (an empty sequence if the string is `null`).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String text = "line1\nline2\r\nline3\rline4";
    Seq<String, Exception> lines = Seq.splitToLines(text);
    // lines contains: "line1", "line2", "line3", "line4"
  ```
- **See also:** #splitToLines(String, boolean, boolean), #ofLines(File)
- **Signature:** `public static <E extends Exception> Seq<String, E> splitToLines(final String str, final boolean trim, final boolean omitEmptyLines)`
- **Summary:** Splits the given string into a sequence of lines with optional trimming and omission of empty lines.
- **Contract:**
  - If the string is `null`, an empty sequence is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to split into lines.
  - `trim` (`boolean`) — if `true`, strips leading and trailing whitespace (per Character#isWhitespace(char)) from each line.
  - `omitEmptyLines` (`boolean`) — if `true`, omits empty lines (or whitespace-only lines if trim is `true`) from the result.
- **Returns:** a `Seq<String, E>` containing the processed lines (an empty sequence if the string is `null`).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String text = " line1 \n  \nline3  ";
    Seq<String, Exception> lines = Seq.splitToLines(text, true, true);
    // lines contains: "line1", "line3" (trimmed and empty lines omitted)
  
    Seq<String, Exception> withEmpty = Seq.splitToLines(text, false, false);
    // withEmpty contains: " line1 ", "  ", "line3  "
  ```
- **See also:** #splitToLines(String), #ofLines(File)
##### splitByChunkCount(...) -> Seq<T, E>
- **Signature:** `public static <T, E extends Exception> Seq<T, E> splitByChunkCount(final int totalSize, final int maxChunkCount, final Throwables.IntBiFunction<? extends T, ? extends E> mapper) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Splits the total size into chunks based on the specified maximum chunk count.
- **Contract:**
  - The length of returned sequence may be less than the specified `maxChunkCount` if the input `totalSize` is less than `maxChunkCount`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `totalSize` (`int`) — the total size to be split. It could be the size of an array, list, etc.
  - `maxChunkCount` (`int`) — the maximum number of chunks to split into
  - `mapper` (`Throwables.IntBiFunction<? extends T, ? extends E>`) — a function to map the chunk from and to index to an element in the resulting sequence
- **Returns:** a sequence of the mapped chunk values
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `totalSize` is negative or `maxChunkCount` is not positive, or if `mapper` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  final int[] a = Array.rangeClosed(1, 7);
    Seq.splitByChunkCount(7, 5, (from, to) -> N.copyOfRange(a, from, to)).toList();   // returns [[1, 2], [3, 4], [5], [6], [7]] (larger chunks first)
    Seq.splitByChunkCount(0, 5, (from, to) -> N.copyOfRange(a, from, to)).count();    // returns 0 (empty for totalSize 0)
  ```
- **See also:** #splitByChunkCount(int, int, boolean, Throwables.IntBiFunction)
- **Signature:** `public static <T, E extends Exception> Seq<T, E> splitByChunkCount(final int totalSize, final int maxChunkCount, final boolean sizeSmallerFirst, final Throwables.IntBiFunction<? extends T, ? extends E> mapper) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Splits the total size into chunks based on the specified maximum chunk count.
- **Contract:**
  - The length of returned sequence may be less than the specified `maxChunkCount` if the input `totalSize` is less than `maxChunkCount`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `totalSize` (`int`) — the total size to be split. It could be the size of an array, list, etc.
  - `maxChunkCount` (`int`) — the maximum number of chunks to split into
  - `sizeSmallerFirst` (`boolean`) — if `true`, smaller chunks will be created first; otherwise, larger chunks will be created first
  - `mapper` (`Throwables.IntBiFunction<? extends T, ? extends E>`) — a function to map the chunk from and to index to an element in the resulting sequence
- **Returns:** a sequence of the mapped chunk values
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `totalSize` is negative or `maxChunkCount` is not positive, or if `mapper` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  final int[] a = Array.rangeClosed(1, 7);
    Seq.splitByChunkCount(7, 5, true, (fromIndex, toIndex) -> N.copyOfRange(a, fromIndex, toIndex)).toList();    // returns [[1], [2], [3], [4, 5], [6, 7]]
    Seq.splitByChunkCount(7, 5, false, (fromIndex, toIndex) -> N.copyOfRange(a, fromIndex, toIndex)).toList();   // returns [[1, 2], [3, 4], [5], [6], [7]]
  ```
- **See also:** #splitByChunkCount(int, int, Throwables.IntBiFunction), Stream#splitByChunkCount(int, int, boolean, IntBiFunction)
##### ofLines(...) -> Seq<String, IOException>
- **Signature:** `public static Seq<String, IOException> ofLines(final File file) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a `Seq` that reads lines from the specified file using the default charset.
- **Contract:**
  - The file resources are automatically closed when the sequence is closed or fully consumed.
  - Usage Examples: The file is opened by the first terminal operation, not by this method: if it does not exist or cannot be read, the IOException is thrown from that terminal operation.
- **Parameters:**
  - `file` (`File`) — the file to read lines from.
- **Returns:** a `Seq<String, IOException>` containing the lines of the file.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `file` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  try (Seq<String, IOException> lines = Seq.ofLines(new File("data.txt"))) {
        lines.filter(line -> !line.isEmpty())
             .forEach(System.out::println);
    }
  ```
- **See also:** #ofLines(File, Charset), #ofLines(Path), #splitToLines(String)
- **Signature:** `public static Seq<String, IOException> ofLines(final File file, final Charset charset) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a `Seq` that reads lines from the specified file using the given charset.
- **Contract:**
  - The file resources are automatically closed when the sequence is closed or fully consumed.
  - Usage Examples: The file is opened by the first terminal operation, not by this method: if it does not exist or cannot be read, the IOException is thrown from that terminal operation.
- **Parameters:**
  - `file` (`File`) — the file to read lines from.
  - `charset` (`Charset`) — the charset to use for decoding the file; if `null`, the default charset is used.
- **Returns:** a `Seq<String, IOException>` containing the lines of the file.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `file` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  try (Seq<String, IOException> lines = Seq.ofLines(new File("data.txt"), StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) {
        lines.map(String::toUpperCase)
             .forEach(System.out::println);
    }
  ```
- **See also:** #ofLines(File), #ofLines(Path, Charset)
- **Signature:** `public static Seq<String, IOException> ofLines(final Path path) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a `Seq` that reads lines from the specified path using the default charset.
- **Contract:**
  - The file resources are automatically closed when the sequence is closed or fully consumed.
  - Usage Examples: The file is opened by the first terminal operation, not by this method: if it does not exist or cannot be read, the IOException is thrown from that terminal operation.
- **Parameters:**
  - `path` (`Path`) — the path to read lines from.
- **Returns:** a `Seq<String, IOException>` containing the lines of the file.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `path` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  try (Seq<String, IOException> lines = Seq.ofLines(Paths.get("data.txt"))) {
        lines.filter(line -> line.startsWith("ERROR"))
             .forEach(System.out::println);
    }
  ```
- **See also:** #ofLines(Path, Charset), #ofLines(File)
- **Signature:** `public static Seq<String, IOException> ofLines(final Path path, final Charset charset) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a `Seq` that reads lines from the specified path using the given charset.
- **Contract:**
  - The file resources are automatically closed when the sequence is closed or fully consumed.
  - Usage Examples: The file is opened by the first terminal operation, not by this method: if it does not exist or cannot be read, the IOException is thrown from that terminal operation.
- **Parameters:**
  - `path` (`Path`) — the path to read lines from.
  - `charset` (`Charset`) — the charset to use for decoding the file; if `null`, the default charset is used.
- **Returns:** a `Seq<String, IOException>` containing the lines of the file.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `path` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  try (Seq<String, IOException> lines = Seq.ofLines(Paths.get("data.txt"), StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) {
        long count = lines.count();
        System.out.println("Total lines: " + count);
    }
  ```
- **See also:** #ofLines(Path), #ofLines(File, Charset)
- **Signature:** `public static Seq<String, IOException> ofLines(final Reader reader) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a `Seq` that reads lines from the given Reader.
- **Parameters:**
  - `reader` (`Reader`) — the Reader to read lines from.
- **Returns:** a `Seq<String, IOException>` containing the lines read from the Reader.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `reader` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Reader reader = new StringReader("line1\nline2\nline3");
    Seq<String, IOException> lines = Seq.ofLines(reader);
    // User must close reader after use
  ```
- **See also:** #ofLines(Reader, boolean), #ofLines(File)
- **Signature:** `public static Seq<String, IOException> ofLines(final Reader reader, final boolean closeReaderWhenStreamIsClosed) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a `Seq` that reads lines from the given Reader.
- **Parameters:**
  - `reader` (`Reader`) — the Reader to read lines from.
  - `closeReaderWhenStreamIsClosed` (`boolean`) — if `true`, the input `Reader` will be closed when the sequence is closed, whether or not the sequence was ever traversed.
- **Returns:** a `Seq<String, IOException>` containing the lines read from the Reader.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `reader` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Reader will be automatically closed
    try (Seq<String, IOException> lines = Seq.ofLines(new FileReader("data.txt"), true)) {
        lines.forEach(System.out::println);
    }
  
    // With automatic reader closing disabled, the caller still owns the Reader.
    try (Reader reader = new StringReader("alpha\nbeta");
         Seq<String, IOException> lines = Seq.ofLines(reader, false)) {
        lines.forEach(System.out::println);
    }
  ```
- **See also:** #ofLines(Reader), #ofLines(File)
##### listFiles(...) -> Seq<File, IOException>
- **Signature:** `public static Seq<File, IOException> listFiles(final File parentPath) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Lists all entries in the specified parent directory, including immediate subdirectories.
- **Contract:**
  - If the directory doesn't exist, an empty sequence is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `parentPath` (`File`) — the parent directory to list files from.
- **Returns:** a `Seq<File, IOException>` containing all entries in the directory. Returns an empty sequence if the directory doesn't exist or is not a directory.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `parentPath` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File dir = new File("/path/to/directory");
    Seq<File, IOException> files = Seq.listFiles(dir);
    files.forEach(file -> System.out.println(file.getName()));
  ```
- **See also:** #listFiles(File, boolean), File#listFiles()
- **Signature:** `public static Seq<File, IOException> listFiles(final File parentPath, final boolean recursively) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Lists all files in the specified parent directory with optional recursive traversal.
- **Contract:**
  - If recursively is `false`, only immediate children files are listed.
  - If recursively is `true`, all descendant files are listed.
  - Directories are included in the results in both modes; when `recursively` is `true`, subdirectories are also traversed.
  - The method uses a breadth-first traversal when recursive listing is enabled.
- **Parameters:**
  - `parentPath` (`File`) — the parent directory to list files from.
  - `recursively` (`boolean`) — if `true`, lists files recursively in all subdirectories; if `false`, lists only immediate children files
- **Returns:** a sequence containing File objects representing the files in the parent directory. Returns an empty sequence if the parent directory doesn't exist or is not a directory. When recursive, the sequence includes both files and directories.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `parentPath` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  File dir = new File("/path/to/directory");
  
    // List only immediate children
    Seq<File, IOException> files = Seq.listFiles(dir, false);
  
    // List all files recursively
    Seq<File, IOException> allFiles = Seq.listFiles(dir, true);
    allFiles.filter(File::isFile)
            .forEach(file -> System.out.println(file.getAbsolutePath()));
  ```
- **See also:** #listFiles(File), File#listFiles()
##### concat(...) -> Seq<T, E>
- **Signature:** `@SafeVarargs public static <T, E extends Exception> Seq<T, E> concat(final T[]... a)`
- **Summary:** Concatenates multiple arrays into a single sequence.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`T[][]`) — the arrays to be concatenated. Can be empty, contain `null` arrays, or be `null` itself
- **Returns:** a sequence containing all elements from all provided arrays in order. Returns an empty sequence if no arrays are provided or all arrays are `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Integer[] a1 = {1, 2, 3};
    Integer[] a2 = {4, 5, 6};
    Seq<Integer, Exception> result = Seq.concat(a1, a2);
    // result contains: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
  
    Seq<Integer, Exception> empty = Seq.empty();
    // empty.count() returns 0
  
    Integer[] a3 = null;
    Seq<Integer, Exception> withNull = Seq.concat(a1, a3, a2);
    // withNull contains: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6] (null array skipped)
  ```
- **See also:** #concat(Iterable...), #concat(Iterator...), #concat(Seq...)
- **Signature:** `@SafeVarargs public static <T, E extends Exception> Seq<T, E> concat(final Iterable<? extends T>... a)`
- **Summary:** Concatenates multiple Iterables into a single sequence.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`Iterable<? extends T>[]`) — the Iterables to be concatenated. Can be empty, contain `null` Iterables, or be `null` itself
- **Returns:** a sequence containing all elements from all provided Iterables in order. Returns an empty sequence if no Iterables are provided or all Iterables are `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> list1 = List.of("a", "b");
    Set<String> set2 = new LinkedHashSet<>(Arrays.asList("c", "d"));
    Seq<String, Exception> result = Seq.concat(list1, set2);
    // result contains: ["a", "b", "c", "d"]
  
    Seq<String, Exception> empty = Seq.concat(Collections.emptyList());
    // empty.count() returns 0
  
    Seq<String, Exception> withNull = Seq.concat(list1, null, set2);
    // withNull contains: ["a", "b", "c", "d"] (null Iterable skipped)
  ```
- **See also:** #concat(Object\[\]\[\]), #concat(Iterator...), #concat(Seq...)
- **Signature:** `@SafeVarargs public static <T, E extends Exception> Seq<T, E> concat(final Iterator<? extends T>... a)`
- **Summary:** Concatenates multiple Iterators into a single sequence.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`Iterator<? extends T>[]`) — the Iterators to be concatenated. Can be empty, contain `null` Iterators, or be `null` itself
- **Returns:** a sequence containing all elements from all provided Iterators in order. Returns an empty sequence if no Iterators are provided or all Iterators are `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Iterator<String> iter1 = List.of("a", "b").iterator();
    Iterator<String> iter2 = List.of("c", "d").iterator();
    Seq<String, Exception> result = Seq.concat(iter1, iter2);
    // result contains: ["a", "b", "c", "d"]
  
    Seq<String, Exception> empty = Seq.empty();
    // empty.count() returns 0
  
    Seq<String, Exception> withNull = Seq.concat(iter1, null, iter2);
    // withNull contains: ["a", "b", "c", "d"] (null Iterator skipped)
  ```
- **See also:** #concat(Object\[\]\[\]), #concat(Iterable...), #concat(Seq...)
- **Signature:** `@SafeVarargs public static <T, E extends Exception> Seq<T, E> concat(final Seq<? extends T, E>... a)`
- **Summary:** Concatenates multiple sequences into a single sequence.
- **Contract:**
  - All input sequences will be automatically closed when the returned sequence is closed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`Seq<? extends T, E>[]`) — the sequences to be concatenated. Can be empty, contain `null` sequences, or be `null` itself
- **Returns:** a sequence containing all elements from all provided sequences in order. Returns an empty sequence if no sequences are provided or all sequences are `null`. The returned sequence will close all input sequences when it is closed.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Seq<String, Exception> seq1 = Seq.of("a", "b");
    Seq<String, Exception> seq2 = Seq.of("c", "d");
    Seq<String, Exception> result = Seq.concat(seq1, seq2);
    // result contains: ["a", "b", "c", "d"]
  
    Seq<String, Exception> empty = Seq.empty();
    // empty.count() returns 0
  
    Seq<String, Exception> withNull = Seq.concat(seq1, null, seq2);
    // withNull contains: ["a", "b", "c", "d"] (null Seq skipped)
  ```
- **See also:** #concat(Collection)
- **Signature:** `public static <T, E extends Exception> Seq<T, E> concat(final Collection<? extends Seq<? extends T, E>> c)`
- **Summary:** Concatenates a collection of sequences into a single sequence.
- **Contract:**
  - All input sequences will be automatically closed when the returned sequence is closed.
  - The collection's membership and encounter order are snapshotted when this method is called, so later structural changes to the caller's collection neither change traversal nor prevent the original sequences from being closed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `c` (`Collection<? extends Seq<? extends T, E>>`) — the collection of sequences to be concatenated. Can be empty, contain `null` sequences, or be `null` itself
- **Returns:** a sequence containing all elements from all provided sequences in order. Returns an empty sequence if the collection is empty or `null`. The returned sequence will close all input sequences when it is closed.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<Seq<String, Exception>> seqs = List.of(Seq.of("a"), Seq.of("b", "c"));
    Seq<String, Exception> result = Seq.concat(seqs);
    // result contains: ["a", "b", "c"]
  
    Seq<String, Exception> empty = Seq.concat(Collections.emptyList());
    // empty.count() returns 0
  
    Seq<String, Exception> withNulls = Seq.concat(Arrays.asList(Seq.of("a"), null, Seq.of("b")));
    // withNulls contains: ["a", "b"] (null Seq skipped)
  ```
- **See also:** #concat(Seq...)

  - `b` (`B[]`) — the second array to zip. Can be `null` or empty

- **Examples:**

- **Signature:** `public static <A, B, T, E extends Exception> Seq<T, E> zip(final Seq<? extends A, E> a, final Seq<? extends B, E> b, final A valueForNoneA, final B valueForNoneB, final Throwables.BiFunction<? super A, ? super B, ? extends T, ? extends E> zipFunction) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Zips two sequences into a single sequence by combining corresponding elements using the provided zip function.
- **Contract:**
  - If one sequence is shorter than the other, the provided default values are used for the missing elements.
  - All input sequences will be automatically closed when the returned sequence is closed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`Seq<? extends A, E>`) — the first sequence to zip. Can be `null` or empty
  - `b` (`Seq<? extends B, E>`) — the second sequence to zip. Can be `null` or empty
  - `valueForNoneA` (`A`) — the default value to use when the first sequence runs out of elements. Can be `null`
  - `valueForNoneB` (`B`) — the default value to use when the second sequence runs out of elements. Can be `null`
  - `zipFunction` (`Throwables.BiFunction<? super A, ? super B, ? extends T, ? extends E>`) — a function that combines elements from the two sequences. Takes an element (or default value) from each sequence and returns the combined result
- **Returns:** a sequence of combined elements. The length equals the longer sequence's length. The returned sequence will close both input sequences when it is closed.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `zipFunction` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Seq<Integer, Exception> a = Seq.of(1, 2);
    Seq<String, Exception> b = Seq.of("a", "b", "c");
    Seq.zip(a, b, 0, "X", (i, s) -> i + s).toList();   // returns ["1a", "2b", "0c"] (0 used for the missing element of the first sequence)
  ```
- **See also:** #zip(Seq, Seq, Throwables.BiFunction), N#zip(Iterable, Iterable, Object, Object, java.util.function.BiFunction)
- **Signature:** `public static <A, B, C, T, E extends Exception> Seq<T, E> zip(final Seq<? extends A, E> a, final Seq<? extends B, E> b, final Seq<? extends C, E> c, final A valueForNoneA, final B valueForNoneB, final C valueForNoneC, final Throwables.TriFunction<? super A, ? super B, ? super C, ? extends T, ? extends E> zipFunction) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Zips three sequences into a single sequence by combining corresponding elements using the provided zip function.
- **Contract:**
  - If one sequence is shorter than the others, the provided default values are used for the missing elements.
  - All input sequences will be automatically closed when the returned sequence is closed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`Seq<? extends A, E>`) — the first sequence to zip. Can be `null` or empty
  - `b` (`Seq<? extends B, E>`) — the second sequence to zip. Can be `null` or empty
  - `c` (`Seq<? extends C, E>`) — the third sequence to zip. Can be `null` or empty
  - `valueForNoneA` (`A`) — the default value to use when the first sequence runs out of elements. Can be `null`
  - `valueForNoneB` (`B`) — the default value to use when the second sequence runs out of elements. Can be `null`
  - `valueForNoneC` (`C`) — the default value to use when the third sequence runs out of elements. Can be `null`
  - `zipFunction` (`Throwables.TriFunction<? super A, ? super B, ? super C, ? extends T, ? extends E>`) — a function that combines elements from the three sequences. Takes an element (or default value) from each sequence and returns the combined result
- **Returns:** a sequence of combined elements. The length equals the longest sequence's length. The returned sequence will close all input sequences when it is closed.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `zipFunction` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java

    Seq<String, Exception> b = Seq.of("a", "b", "c");
    Seq<Boolean, Exception> c = Seq.of(true);
    Seq.zip(a, b, c, 0, "X", false, (i, s, x) -> i + s + x).toList();   // returns ["1atrue", "2bfalse", "0cfalse"] (defaults fill missing elements)
  ```
