  - This is the most efficient option when splitting by a single character.
- **Parameters:**
  - `delimiter` (`char`) — the character to use as a delimiter for splitting.
- **Returns:** a new Splitter instance configured with the specified character delimiter.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> parts = Splitter.with(',').split("apple,banana,cherry");
    // Returns ["apple", "banana", "cherry"]
  ```
- **See also:** #with(CharSequence), #with(Pattern)
- **Signature:** `public static Splitter with(final CharSequence delimiter) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a new Splitter instance that uses the specified character sequence as a delimiter.
- **Contract:**
  - Its contents are captured when this method is called, so subsequent mutations to a mutable CharSequence do not change the configured delimiter.
  - If the delimiter is a single character, this method delegates to the more efficient single-character version.
- **Parameters:**
  - `delimiter` (`CharSequence`) — the character sequence to use as a delimiter for splitting, not `null` or empty.
- **Returns:** a new Splitter instance configured with the specified delimiter.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the specified delimiter is `null` or empty.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> parts = Splitter.with("::").split("a::b::c");
    // Returns ["a", "b", "c"]
  
    List<String> words = Splitter.with(" AND ").split("red AND green AND blue");
    // Returns ["red", "green", "blue"]
  ```
- **See also:** #with(char), #with(Pattern), #pattern(CharSequence)
- **Signature:** `public static Splitter with(final Pattern delimiter) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Returns a new Splitter instance that uses the specified regular expression pattern as a delimiter.
- **Contract:**
  - The pattern must not match the empty input string.
- **Parameters:**
  - `delimiter` (`Pattern`) — the Pattern to use as a delimiter for splitting, not `null`.
- **Returns:** a new Splitter instance configured with the specified pattern delimiter.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the specified delimiter is `null`, or if the pattern matches the empty input string (a pattern that merely has zero-length matches on non-empty input, such as `\\b`, is accepted — see above).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Splitter.with(Pattern.compile("\\b")).split("ab cd");   // returns ["", "ab", " ", "cd", ""]
    Arrays.asList("ab cd".split("\\b", -1));                // returns ["ab", " ", "cd", ""]
  ```
  ```java
  Pattern comma = Pattern.compile(",");
    List<String> parts = Splitter.with(comma).split("a,b,c");
    // Returns ["a", "b", "c"]
  
    Pattern whitespace = Pattern.compile("\\s+");
    List<String> words = Splitter.with(whitespace).split("one  two   three");
    // Returns ["one", "two", "three"]
  ```
- **See also:** #pattern(CharSequence), #with(CharSequence)
##### pattern(...) -> Splitter
- **Signature:** `public static Splitter pattern(final CharSequence delimiterRegex) throws IllegalArgumentException, PatternSyntaxException`
- **Summary:** Returns a new Splitter instance that uses the specified regular expression as a delimiter.
- **Parameters:**
  - `delimiterRegex` (`CharSequence`) — the regular expression to use as a delimiter for splitting, not `null` or empty.
- **Returns:** a new Splitter instance configured with the compiled pattern delimiter.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the specified delimiter regex is `null` or empty, or if the resulting pattern matches the empty input string (see #with(Pattern) for how zero-length matches on non-empty input are treated).
  - `java.util.regex.PatternSyntaxException` — if `delimiterRegex` is not a valid regular expression
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> words = Splitter.pattern("\\s+").split("one  two   three");
    // Returns ["one", "two", "three"]
  
    List<String> parts = Splitter.pattern("[,;]").split("a,b;c");
    // Returns ["a", "b", "c"]
  ```
- **See also:** #with(Pattern), #with(CharSequence)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### omitEmptyStrings(...) -> Splitter
- **Signature:** `public Splitter omitEmptyStrings(final boolean omitEmptyStrings)`
- **Summary:** Configures this Splitter to omit empty strings from the results when the specified parameter is `true`.
- **Contract:**
  - Empty strings can occur when there are consecutive delimiters or when delimiters appear at the beginning or end of the input.
- **Parameters:**
  - `omitEmptyStrings` (`boolean`) — `true` to omit empty strings from results, `false` to include them.
- **Returns:** this Splitter instance for method chaining.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Splitter.with(",").omitEmptyStrings(true).split("a,,b,");    // returns ["a", "b"]
    Splitter.with(",").omitEmptyStrings(false).split("a,,b,");   // returns ["a", "", "b", ""]
  ```
- **See also:** #omitEmptyStrings()
- **Signature:** `public Splitter omitEmptyStrings()`
- **Summary:** Configures this Splitter to omit empty strings from the results.
- **Contract:**
  - Empty strings can occur when there are consecutive delimiters or when delimiters appear at the beginning or end of the input.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** this Splitter instance for method chaining.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> result = Splitter.with(",")
        .omitEmptyStrings()
        .split("a,,b,");
    // Returns ["a", "b"] instead of ["a", "", "b", ""]
  ```
- **See also:** #trimResults(), #stripResults()
##### trim(...) -> Splitter
- **Signature:** `public Splitter trim(final boolean trim)`
- **Summary:** Configures this Splitter to trim leading and trailing spaces from each resulting substring when the specified parameter is `true`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `trim` (`boolean`) — `true` to trim spaces from results, `false` to leave them as-is. Passing `true` also turns strip mode off.
- **Returns:** this Splitter instance for method chaining.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Splitter.with(",").trim(true).split("a , b , c");    // returns ["a", "b", "c"]
    Splitter.with(",").trim(false).split("a , b , c");   // returns ["a ", " b ", " c"]
  ```
  ```java
  Splitter.with(',').trimResults().split("a	, b");    // returns ["a	", "b"] -- the tab survives
    Splitter.with(',').stripResults().split("a	, b");   // returns ["a", "b"]
  ```
- **See also:** #trimResults(), #stripResults()
##### trimResults(...) -> Splitter
- **Signature:** `public Splitter trimResults()`
- **Summary:** Configures this Splitter to trim leading and trailing spaces from each resulting substring.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** this Splitter instance for method chaining.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> result = Splitter.with(",")
        .trimResults()
        .split("a , b , c");
    // Returns ["a", "b", "c"] instead of ["a ", " b ", " c"]
  ```
  ```java
  Splitter.with(',').trimResults().split("a	, b");    // returns ["a	", "b"] -- the tab survives
    Splitter.with(',').stripResults().split("a	, b");   // returns ["a", "b"]
  ```
- **See also:** #stripResults(), #omitEmptyStrings(), Joiner#trimBeforeAppend()
##### strip(...) -> Splitter
- **Signature:** `public Splitter strip(final boolean strip)`
- **Summary:** Configures this Splitter to remove leading and trailing whitespace characters from each resulting substring when the specified parameter is `true`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `strip` (`boolean`) — `true` to strip whitespace from results, `false` to leave them as-is. Passing `true` also turns trim mode off.
- **Returns:** this Splitter instance for method chaining.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Splitter.with(",").strip(true).split("a\t,\nb ,\tc");   // returns ["a", "b", "c"]
    Splitter.with(",").strip(false).split("a\t, b ,c");     // returns ["a\t", " b ", "c"]
  ```
- **See also:** Character#isWhitespace(char), #stripResults(), #trimResults()
##### stripResults(...) -> Splitter
- **Signature:** `public Splitter stripResults()`
- **Summary:** Configures this Splitter to remove leading and trailing whitespace characters from each resulting substring.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** this Splitter instance for method chaining.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> result = Splitter.with(",")
        .stripResults()
        .split("a\t,\nb\t,\tc");
    // Returns ["a", "b", "c"] with surrounding whitespace removed
  ```
- **See also:** #trimResults(), #omitEmptyStrings(), Character#isWhitespace(char), Joiner#stripBeforeAppend()
##### limit(...) -> Splitter
- **Signature:** `public Splitter limit(final int limit) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Configures this Splitter to limit the maximum number of substrings to return when splitting.
- **Contract:**
  - If the limit is reached, the remainder of the input string will be included in the last substring, without further splitting.
  - Before the final substring starts, each token is trimmed or stripped, then dropped if it is empty, and only retained tokens count toward the limit.
  - The final substring starts at the next retained token and includes the remaining input without further splitting; internal delimiters and empty fields remain, while its outer whitespace is still trimmed or stripped if configured.
- **Parameters:**
  - `limit` (`int`) — the maximum number of substrings to return; must be positive.
- **Returns:** this Splitter instance for method chaining.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the provided limit is not a positive integer.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> result = Splitter.with(",")
        .limit(2)
        .split("a,b,c,d");
    // Returns ["a", "b,c,d"]
  ```
  ```java
  Splitter.with(",").omitEmptyStrings().limit(2).split(",,a,b,c");   // returns ["a", "b,c"]
    Splitter.with(",").omitEmptyStrings().limit(2).split("a,,,b,c");   // returns ["a", "b,c"]
    Splitter.with(",").omitEmptyStrings().limit(2).split("a,b,,c");   // returns ["a", "b,,c"]
    Splitter.with(",").omitEmptyStrings().limit(1).split(",");         // returns []
    ",,a,b,c".split(",", 2);                                           // returns ["", ",a,b,c"]
  ```
  ```java
  Splitter.with(",").limit(2).split(",,a,b,c");                      // returns ["", ",a,b,c"]
  ```
- **See also:** #split(CharSequence), #omitEmptyStrings()
##### split(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public List<String> split(final CharSequence source)`
- **Summary:** Splits the specified CharSequence using this Splitter's configuration and returns the results as a List of strings.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to split; may be `null`.
- **Returns:** a new ArrayList containing the split results; returns an empty list if source is `null`, and a single-element list holding the empty string if source is empty (unless #omitEmptyStrings() is configured).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> parts = Splitter.with(",").split("a,b,c");
    // Returns ["a", "b", "c"]
  
    Splitter.with(",").split((CharSequence) null);         // returns [] (size 0)
    Splitter.with(",").split("");                          // returns [""] (size 1)
    Splitter.with(",").omitEmptyStrings().split("");       // returns [] (size 0)
  ```
- **See also:** #splitToCollection(CharSequence, Supplier), #split(CharSequence, Function), #split(CharSequence, Class), #splitToArray(CharSequence), #splitInto(CharSequence, Collection), #splitToStream(CharSequence)
- **Signature:** `public <T> List<T> split(final CharSequence source, final Class<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Splits the specified CharSequence using this Splitter's configuration and converts each resulting substring to the specified target type using the type system's valueOf method.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to split; may be `null`.
  - `targetType` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the Class representing the type to convert each substring to, not `null`.
- **Returns:** a new List containing the converted results.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if targetType is `null`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if resolving the requested conversion type or converting a split token fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<Integer> numbers = Splitter.with(",").split("10,20,30", Integer.class);
    // Returns [10, 20, 30]
  
    List<BigDecimal> amounts = Splitter.with(";").split("1.5;2.75;3.25", BigDecimal.class);
    // Returns [1.5, 2.75, 3.25]
  ```
  ```java
  Splitter.with(",").split("1,,3", Integer.class);                      // returns [1, null, 3]
    Splitter.with(",").split("", Integer.class);                          // returns [null]  (size 1)
    Splitter.with(",").omitEmptyStrings().split("1,,3", Integer.class);   // returns [1, 3]
  ```
- **See also:** #split(CharSequence, Type), #splitToCollection(CharSequence, Class, Supplier), #splitToArray(CharSequence, Class)
- **Signature:** `public <T> List<T> split(final CharSequence source, final Type<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Splits the specified CharSequence using this Splitter's configuration and converts each resulting substring to the specified target type using the provided Type instance for conversion.
- **Contract:**
  - This method is useful when working with the type system directly or when Class objects are insufficient (e.g., for generic types).
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to split; may be `null`.
  - `targetType` (`Type<? extends T>`) — the Type instance used for converting strings to the target type.
- **Returns:** a new List containing the converted results.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if targetType is `null`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a split token fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Split and convert to List<Integer> using Type
    Type<Integer> intType = N.typeOf(Integer.class);
    List<Integer> numbers = Splitter.with(",").split("1,2,3", intType);
    // Returns [1, 2, 3]
  ```
  ```java
  Splitter.with(",").split("1,,3", Integer.class);                      // returns [1, null, 3]
    Splitter.with(",").split("", Integer.class);                          // returns [null]  (size 1)
    Splitter.with(",").omitEmptyStrings().split("1,,3", Integer.class);   // returns [1, 3]
  ```
- **See also:** #split(CharSequence, Class), #splitToCollection(CharSequence, Type, Supplier)
- **Signature:** `public <T> List<T> split(final CharSequence source, final Function<? super String, ? extends T> mapper) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Splits the specified CharSequence using this Splitter's configuration and applies the provided mapping function to each resulting substring.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to split; may be `null`.
  - `mapper` (`Function<? super String, ? extends T>`) — a function to apply to each split string.
- **Returns:** a new List containing the mapped results.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapper` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<Integer> numbers = Splitter.with(",").split("1,2,3", Integer::parseInt);
    // Returns [1, 2, 3]
  ```
- **See also:** #split(CharSequence), #split(CharSequence, Class), #splitThenApply(CharSequence, Function)
##### splitToCollection(...) -> C
- **Signature:** `public <C extends Collection<String>> C splitToCollection(final CharSequence source, final Supplier<? extends C> supplier) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Splits the specified CharSequence using this Splitter's configuration and returns the results in a Collection created by the provided supplier.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to split; may be `null`.
  - `supplier` (`Supplier<? extends C>`) — a Supplier that creates a new Collection instance to hold the results.
- **Returns:** the Collection created by the supplier, populated with the split results.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `supplier` is `null` or returns `null`.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if the supplied Collection rejects insertion and at least one element is produced.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  LinkedHashSet<String> uniqueParts = Splitter.with(",").splitToCollection("a,b,a,c", LinkedHashSet::new);
    // Returns a LinkedHashSet containing ["a", "b", "c"]
  ```
- **See also:** #split(CharSequence), #splitToCollection(CharSequence, Class, Supplier)
- **Signature:** `public <T, C extends Collection<T>> C splitToCollection(final CharSequence source, final Class<? extends T> targetType, final Supplier<? extends C> supplier) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, NullPointerException, ClassCastException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Splits the specified CharSequence using this Splitter's configuration, converts each resulting substring to the specified target type, and returns the results in a Collection created by the provided supplier.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to split; may be `null`.
  - `targetType` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the Class representing the type to convert each substring to.
  - `supplier` (`Supplier<? extends C>`) — a Supplier that creates a new Collection instance to hold the results.
- **Returns:** the Collection created by the supplier, populated with the converted results.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if targetType is `null`, or if `supplier` is `null` or returns `null`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if resolving the requested conversion type or converting a split token fails
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if a converted element is `null` and the destination rejects it
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a converted element has a type that the destination cannot accept or compare
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if the supplied Collection rejects insertion and at least one element is produced.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Set<Integer> uniqueNumbers = Splitter.with(",").splitToCollection("1,2,1,3", Integer.class, HashSet::new);
    // Returns a HashSet containing {1, 2, 3}
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <T, C extends Collection<T>> C splitToCollection(final CharSequence source, final Type<? extends T> targetType, final Supplier<? extends C> supplier) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, NullPointerException, ClassCastException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Splits the specified CharSequence using this Splitter's configuration, converts each resulting substring to the specified target type using the provided Type instance, and returns the results in a Collection created by the provided supplier.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to split; may be `null`.
  - `targetType` (`Type<? extends T>`) — the Type instance used for converting strings to the target type.
  - `supplier` (`Supplier<? extends C>`) — a Supplier that creates a new Collection instance to hold the results.
- **Returns:** the Collection created by the supplier, populated with the converted results.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if targetType is `null`, or if `supplier` is `null` or returns `null`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a split token fails
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if a converted element is `null` and the destination rejects it
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a converted element has a type that the destination cannot accept or compare
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if the supplied Collection rejects insertion and at least one element is produced.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Split into a TreeSet of Integers using Type
    Type<Integer> intType = N.typeOf(Integer.class);
    TreeSet<Integer> uniqueNumbers = Splitter.with(",").splitToCollection("3,1,2,1,3", intType, TreeSet::new);
    // Returns sorted unique values: [1, 2, 3]
  ```
##### splitInto(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public void splitInto(final CharSequence source, final Collection<String> output) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Splits the specified CharSequence using this Splitter's configuration and adds the resulting substrings to the provided output collection.
- **Contract:**
  - This method is useful when you want to append split results to an existing collection rather than creating a new one.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to split; may be `null`.
  - `output` (`Collection<String>`) — the Collection to add the split results to, not `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if output is `null`.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `output` rejects insertion (for example an immutable or fixed-size collection) and at least one element is produced.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> allParts = new ArrayList<>();
    Splitter.with(",").splitInto("a,b", allParts);
    Splitter.with(";").splitInto("c;d", allParts);
    // allParts now contains ["a", "b", "c", "d"]
  ```
- **See also:** #split(CharSequence), #splitToCollection(CharSequence, Supplier)
- **Signature:** `public <T> void splitInto(final CharSequence source, final Class<? extends T> targetType, final Collection<T> output) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, NullPointerException, ClassCastException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Splits the specified CharSequence using this Splitter's configuration, converts each resulting substring to the specified target type, and adds the converted values to the provided output collection.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to split; may be `null`.
  - `targetType` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the Class representing the type to convert each substring to.
  - `output` (`Collection<T>`) — the Collection to add the converted results to.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if targetType or output is `null`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if resolving the requested conversion type or converting a split token fails
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if a converted element is `null` and the destination rejects it
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a converted element has a type that the destination cannot accept or compare
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `output` rejects insertion and at least one element is produced.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<Integer> numbers = new ArrayList<>();
    Splitter.with(",").splitInto("1,2,3", Integer.class, numbers);
    Splitter.with(";").splitInto("4;5;6", Integer.class, numbers);
    // numbers now contains [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <T> void splitInto(final CharSequence source, final Type<? extends T> targetType, final Collection<T> output) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, NullPointerException, ClassCastException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Splits the specified CharSequence using this Splitter's configuration, converts each resulting substring to the specified target type using the provided Type instance, and adds the converted values to the provided output collection.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to split; may be `null`.
  - `targetType` (`Type<? extends T>`) — the Type instance used for converting strings to the target type.
  - `output` (`Collection<T>`) — the Collection to add the converted results to.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if targetType or output is `null`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a split token fails
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if a converted element is `null` and the destination rejects it
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a converted element has a type that the destination cannot accept or compare
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `output` rejects insertion and at least one element is produced.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<Double> results = new ArrayList<>();
    Type<Double> doubleType = N.typeOf(Double.class);
    Splitter.with(",").splitInto("1.5,2.7,3.9", doubleType, results);
    // results now contains [1.5, 2.7, 3.9]
  ```
- **Signature:** `public void splitInto(final CharSequence source, final String[] output) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Splits the specified CharSequence using this Splitter's configuration and populates the provided String array with the results.
- **Contract:**
  - If the array is larger than the number of split results, remaining elements are left unchanged.
  - If the array is smaller than the number of split results, only the first array.length results are stored.
  - This method is useful when you want to reuse an existing array or have pre-allocated storage.
  - Clear the array first, or use #splitToArray(CharSequence) when the number of results is not known in advance.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to split; may be `null`.
  - `output` (`String[]`) — the String array to populate with split results, not `null`; an empty array is a no-op.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if output is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String[] parts = new String[3];
    Splitter.with(",").splitInto("a,b,c,d", parts);
    // parts now contains ["a", "b", "c"] (4th element "d" is not stored)
  
    Splitter.with(",").splitInto("a,b", new String[0]);   // no-op
  ```
- **See also:** #splitToArray(CharSequence), #splitInto(CharSequence, Collection)

- **Summary:** Splits the specified CharSequence using this Splitter's configuration, converts the results to the specified array type, and returns the array.
- **Contract:**
  - The array type must be an array class (e.g., String\[\].class, Integer\[\].class).

  - `source` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to split; may be `null`.

  ```java
    // Returns [10, 20, 30]
  ```

##### limit(...) -> MapSplitter
- **Signature:** `public MapSplitter limit(final int limit) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Sets the maximum number of map entries to produce when splitting.
- **Contract:**
  - Limit Semantics - "Up To N": `limit(N)` means: produce AT MOST N map entries If input has fewer than N pairs: returns all pairs If input has exactly N pairs: returns all N pairs - but the N-th entry always extends to the end of the input, so anything left after it (a trailing entry delimiter, or trailing empty entries) is absorbed into that entry's value rather than discarded.
  - After `omitEmptyStrings(false)` that internal empty entry is kept and counted, and the same input yields the key `",b"` instead If input has more than N pairs: the remaining input is absorbed into the N-th entry (it is not discarded), and that whole entry is then split on its own first key-value delimiter.
  - So the residue lands in the value when the N-th entry's delimiter precedes it - `limit(2).split("a=1,b=2,c=3")` gives key `b` the value `"2,c=3"` - but in the key when it does not: `limit(2).split("a=1,b,c=2")` gives the key `"b,c"` the value `"2"` The limit caps the number of entries parsed, not the size of the returned map: two parsed entries whose keys are equal collapse into one, so the map can be smaller than N - see Duplicate keys in the class javadoc Common Confusion: `limit(2)` does NOT mean "return 1 entry" `limit(2)` means "return up to 2 entries" This is consistent with `String.split()` limit behavior Usage Examples: Common Mistakes:
- **Parameters:**
  - `limit` (`int`) — the maximum number of entries to return; must be > 0.
- **Returns:** this MapSplitter for method chaining.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `limit` <= 0.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MapSplitter splitter = MapSplitter.with(",", "=");
  
    // Input has more entries than limit
    Map<String, String> firstTwo = splitter.limit(2).split("a=1,b=2,c=3,d=4");
    // Returns: {a=1, b=2,c=3,d=4} - 2 entries; the last value absorbs the remaining input
  
    // Input has exactly limit entries
    Map<String, String> exactlyTwo = splitter.limit(2).split("a=1,b=2");
    // Returns: {a=1, b=2} - all 2 entries
  
    // Input has fewer entries than limit
    Map<String, String> fewerThanFive = splitter.limit(5).split("a=1,b=2");
    // Returns: {a=1, b=2} - all available entries (only 2)
  
    // Input is empty
    Map<String, String> empty = splitter.limit(2).split("");
    // Returns: {} - empty map
  
    // Combined with other options
    Map<String, String> combined = splitter.limit(2).trimResults().omitEmptyStrings()
        .split(" a = 1 , , b = 2 , c = 3 ");
    // Returns: {a=1, b="2 , c = 3"}. Empty entries are dropped before the limit is counted, so the
    // final entry starts at the first non-empty entry and absorbs the remaining input from there.
  ```
  ```java
  MapSplitter splitter = MapSplitter.with(",", "=");
    Map<String, String> result = splitter.limit(2).split("a=1,b=2,c=3");
    assert result.size() == 2;   // limit(2) means up to two map entries
  
    String[] parts = "a,b,c".split(",", 2);
    assert Arrays.equals(new String[] { "a", "b,c" }, parts);
    // Both APIs limit the number of produced results; MapSplitter produces map entries.
  ```
- **See also:** Splitter#limit(int)

##### splitInto(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public void splitInto(final CharSequence source, final Map<String, String> output) throws IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Splits the specified CharSequence into string key-value pairs and adds them to the provided output map.
- **Contract:**
  - Each entry must contain at least one key-value delimiter; an entry with no key-value delimiter causes an IllegalArgumentException.
  - Because the key-value splitting is limited to two parts, if an entry contains more than one key-value delimiter, the first occurrence separates the key from the value and the value retains the remaining text (including any further delimiters).
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to split into a map; may be `null`
  - `output` (`Map<String, String>`) — the Map to add the parsed key-value pairs to
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if output is `null`, or if any entry string cannot be properly parsed into a key-value pair.
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if `output` rejects insertion (for example an immutable map) and at least one entry is produced.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, String> config = new HashMap<>();
    MapSplitter.with(",", "=").splitInto("a=1,b=2", config);
    MapSplitter.with(";", ":").splitInto("c:3;d:4", config);
    // config now contains {a=1, b=2, c=3, d=4}
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <K, V> void splitInto(final CharSequence source, final Class<K> keyType, final Class<V> valueType, final Map<K, V> output) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, NullPointerException, ClassCastException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Splits the specified CharSequence into key-value pairs, converts them to the specified types, and adds them to the provided output map.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to split into a map; may be `null`
  - `keyType` (`Class<K>`) — the Class representing the type to convert keys to
  - `valueType` (`Class<V>`) — the Class representing the type to convert values to
  - `output` (`Map<K, V>`) — the Map to add the converted key-value pairs to
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if keyType, valueType, or output is `null`, or if any entry string cannot be properly parsed into a key-value pair.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if resolving a requested conversion type or converting a key or value fails
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if a converted key or value is `null` and the destination rejects it
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a converted key or value has a type that the destination cannot accept or compare
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if the destination map rejects insertion and an entry is produced
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<Integer, String> data = new HashMap<>();
    MapSplitter.with(",", ":").splitInto("1:apple,2:banana", Integer.class, String.class, data);
    // data now contains {1=apple, 2=banana}
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <K, V> void splitInto(final CharSequence source, final Type<K> keyType, final Type<V> valueType, final Map<K, V> output) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException, NullPointerException, ClassCastException, UnsupportedOperationException`
- **Summary:** Splits the specified CharSequence into key-value pairs, converts them using the provided Type instances, and adds them to the provided output map.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to split into a map; may be `null`
  - `keyType` (`Type<K>`) — the Type instance used for converting strings to keys
  - `valueType` (`Type<V>`) — the Type instance used for converting strings to values
  - `output` (`Map<K, V>`) — the Map to add the converted key-value pairs to
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if keyType, valueType, or output is `null`, or if any entry string cannot be properly parsed into a key-value pair.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if converting a key or value fails
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if a converted key or value is `null` and the destination rejects it
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a converted key or value has a type that the destination cannot accept or compare
  - `java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException` — if the destination map rejects insertion and an entry is produced
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Integer> config = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    Type<String> strType = N.typeOf(String.class);
    Type<Integer> intType = N.typeOf(Integer.class);
  
    MapSplitter.with(",", "=").splitInto("port=8080,timeout=30", strType, intType, config);
    MapSplitter.with(";", ":").splitInto("retry:3;delay:500", strType, intType, config);
    // config now contains {port=8080, timeout=30, retry=3, delay=500}
  ```
##### splitToImmutableMap(...) -> varies by overload

- **Summary:** Splits the specified CharSequence into a map of string key-value pairs and returns the results as an ImmutableMap.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to split into a map; may be `null`
- **Returns:** an ImmutableMap containing the parsed key-value pairs

  ```java
        .splitToImmutableMap("host=localhost,port=8080");
    // Returns an immutable map {host=localhost, port=8080}
  ```
- **See also:** #split(CharSequence), #splitToImmutableMap(CharSequence, Class, Class)
- **Signature:** `public <K, V> ImmutableMap<K, V> splitToImmutableMap(final CharSequence source, final Class<K> keyType, final Class<V> valueType) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Splits the specified CharSequence into a map with keys and values converted to the specified types, and returns the results as an ImmutableMap.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to split into a map; may be `null`
  - `keyType` (`Class<K>`) — the Class representing the type to convert keys to, not `null`
  - `valueType` (`Class<V>`) — the Class representing the type to convert values to, not `null`
- **Returns:** an ImmutableMap containing the parsed and converted key-value pairs
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if keyType or valueType is `null`, or if any entry string cannot be properly parsed into a key-value pair.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if resolving a requested conversion type or converting a key or value fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ImmutableMap<Integer, String> data = MapSplitter.with(",", ":")
        .splitToImmutableMap("1:apple,2:banana", Integer.class, String.class);
    // Returns an immutable map {1=apple, 2=banana}
  ```
- **See also:** #splitToImmutableMap(CharSequence), #split(CharSequence, Class, Class)
##### splitToStream(...) -> Stream<Map.Entry<String, String>>
- **Signature:** `public Stream<Map.Entry<String, String>> splitToStream(final CharSequence source)`
- **Summary:** Splits the specified CharSequence into a Stream of Map.Entry objects.
- **Contract:**
  - The entry-level configuration is captured when the stream is created, while the key/value-level configuration is read as each entry is consumed, so a change made in between would apply to only half the pipeline.
  - Usage Examples: During traversal, the returned stream throws IllegalArgumentException if an entry does not yield both a key and a value under the configured key-value splitter.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to split into entries; may be `null`
- **Returns:** a Stream of Map.Entry objects containing the parsed key-value pairs; returns an empty stream if source is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  long count = MapSplitter.with(",", "=")
        .splitToStream("a=1,b=2,c=3")
        .filter(e -> e.getValue().equals("2"))
        .count();
    // Returns 1
  ```
- **See also:** #split(CharSequence), #splitToEntryStream(CharSequence)
##### splitToEntryStream(...) -> EntryStream<String, String>
- **Signature:** `public EntryStream<String, String> splitToEntryStream(final CharSequence source)`
- **Summary:** Splits the specified CharSequence into an EntryStream of string key-value pairs.
- **Contract:**
  - Usage Examples: During traversal, the returned stream throws IllegalArgumentException if an entry does not yield both a key and a value under the configured key-value splitter.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to split into entries; may be `null`
- **Returns:** an EntryStream containing the parsed key-value pairs; returns an empty EntryStream if source is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, String> filtered = MapSplitter.with(",", "=")
        .splitToEntryStream("a=1,b=2,c=3")
        .filter(e -> !e.getKey().equals("b"))
        .toMap();
    // Returns {a=1, c=3}
  ```
- **See also:** #splitToStream(CharSequence)
##### splitThenApply(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public <T> T splitThenApply(final CharSequence source, final Function<? super Map<String, String>, T> converter) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Splits the specified CharSequence into a map and applies the provided function to transform the resulting map.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to split into a map; may be `null`
  - `converter` (`Function<? super Map<String, String>, T>`) — a function that transforms the parsed map into a result.
- **Returns:** the result of applying the converter function to the parsed map
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the callback is `null`, or an entry does not yield both a key and a value
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  int valueSum = MapSplitter.with(",", "=")
        .splitThenApply("a=1,b=2,c=3", map ->
            map.values().stream()
                .mapToInt(Integer::parseInt)
                .sum());
    // Returns 6
  ```
- **See also:** #split(CharSequence), #splitThenAccept(CharSequence, Consumer)
##### splitThenAccept(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public void splitThenAccept(final CharSequence source, final Consumer<? super Map<String, String>> consumer) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Splits the specified CharSequence into a map and passes it to the provided consumer.
- **Parameters:**
  - `source` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to split into a map; may be `null`
  - `consumer` (`Consumer<? super Map<String, String>>`) — a consumer that processes the parsed map.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the callback is `null`, or an entry does not yield both a key and a value
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MapSplitter.with(",", "=").splitThenAccept("a=1,b=2", map -> {
        System.out.println("Parsed " + map.size() + " entries");
        map.forEach((k, v) -> System.out.println(k + " -> " + v));
    });
  ```
- **See also:** #split(CharSequence), #splitThenApply(CharSequence, Function)

### Class Stopwatch (com.landawn.abacus.util.Stopwatch)
Note: It's copied from Google Guava under Apache License 2.0 and may be modified.

**Thread-safety:** not thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### createUnstarted(...) -> Stopwatch
- **Signature:** `public static Stopwatch createUnstarted()`
- **Summary:** Creates (but does not start) a new stopwatch using System#nanoTime as its time source.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a new stopwatch instance that is not running
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stopwatch sw = Stopwatch.createUnstarted();   // returns Stopwatch, not running
    sw.isRunning();                               // returns false
    sw.elapsed(TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS);             // returns 0
    sw.elapsed();                                 // returns java.time.Duration.ZERO
  
    sw.start();
    doSomething();
    sw.stop();
    sw.elapsed(TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);   // returns elapsed time
  
    sw.start();                          // resumes accumulation after stop
  
    sw.reset();
    sw.elapsed(TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);                   // returns 0 after reset
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static Stopwatch createUnstarted(final Ticker ticker) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates (but does not start) a new stopwatch, using the specified time source.
- **Contract:**
  - This is useful for testing or when you need to use an alternative time source.
- **Parameters:**
  - `ticker` (`Ticker`) — the time source to use for measuring elapsed time
- **Returns:** a new stopwatch instance that is not running
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `ticker` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Ticker ticker = Ticker.systemTicker();
    Stopwatch sw = Stopwatch.createUnstarted(ticker);   // returns Stopwatch using given ticker
    sw.isRunning();                                     // returns false
  
    sw.start();
    doSomething();
    sw.stop();
    sw.elapsed(TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);                   // returns elapsed based on ticker
  
    Ticker mockTicker = new Ticker() {
        private long time = 0;
        public long read() { return time += 1000000; }
    };
    Stopwatch sw2 = Stopwatch.createUnstarted(mockTicker);
    sw2.start();
    sw2.stop();
    sw2.elapsed(TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);         // returns elapsed based on mock ticker
  
    Stopwatch.createUnstarted((Ticker) null);   // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
##### createStarted(...) -> Stopwatch
- **Signature:** `public static Stopwatch createStarted()`
- **Summary:** Creates (and starts) a new stopwatch using System#nanoTime as its time source.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a new stopwatch instance that is already running
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stopwatch sw = Stopwatch.createStarted();   // starts immediately
    sw.isRunning();                             // returns true
    doSomething();
    sw.elapsed(TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);                   // returns elapsed time
  
    sw.stop();
    sw.elapsed();                        // returns a java.time.Duration of the elapsed time
  
    sw.start();                          // resumes accumulation after stop (no reset needed)
  
    Stopwatch.createStarted().start();   // throws IllegalStateException (already running)
  
    sw.reset();
    sw.elapsed(TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS);   // returns 0 after reset
    sw.start();                         // OK, can restart after reset
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static Stopwatch createStarted(final Ticker ticker) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates (and starts) a new stopwatch, using the specified time source.
- **Parameters:**
  - `ticker` (`Ticker`) — the time source to use for measuring elapsed time
- **Returns:** a new stopwatch instance that is already running
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `ticker` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Ticker ticker = Ticker.systemTicker();
    Stopwatch sw = Stopwatch.createStarted(ticker);   // starts immediately with given ticker
    sw.isRunning();                                   // returns true
    doSomething();
    sw.stop();
    sw.elapsed(TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);                   // returns elapsed based on ticker
  
    Ticker mockTicker = new Ticker() {
        private long time = 0;
        public long read() { return time += 1000000; }
    };
    Stopwatch sw2 = Stopwatch.createStarted(mockTicker);   // starts with mock ticker
    sw2.elapsed(TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);                    // returns elapsed based on mock
  
    Stopwatch.createStarted((Ticker) null);                // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```

#### Public Instance Methods
##### isRunning(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public boolean isRunning()`
- **Summary:** Returns `true` if #start() has been called on this stopwatch, and neither #stop() nor #reset() has been called since the last call to `start()`.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** `true` if the stopwatch is currently running, `false` otherwise
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stopwatch sw = Stopwatch.createUnstarted();
    sw.isRunning();                                      // returns false
  
    sw.start();
    sw.isRunning();                                      // returns true
  
    sw.stop();
    sw.isRunning();                                      // returns false
  
    sw.reset();
    sw.isRunning();                                      // returns false after reset
  
    if (sw.isRunning()) { sw.stop(); }
  ```
##### start(...) -> Stopwatch
- **Signature:** `public Stopwatch start() throws IllegalStateException`
- **Summary:** Starts the stopwatch.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** this `Stopwatch` instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stopwatch is already running
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stopwatch sw = Stopwatch.createUnstarted();
    Stopwatch same = sw.start();   // returns this for method chaining
    sw.isRunning();                // returns true
  
    sw.stop();
    sw.elapsed(TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);   // returns elapsed for first period
  
    sw.start();                          // resumes accumulation after stop (no reset needed)
    sw.stop();
    sw.elapsed(TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);   // returns total accumulated time
  
    Stopwatch.createStarted().start();   // throws IllegalStateException (already running)
  
    sw.start().stop().reset().start();   // chain: start → stop → reset → start fresh
  ```
- **See also:** #stop(), #isRunning()
##### stop(...) -> Stopwatch
- **Signature:** `public Stopwatch stop() throws IllegalStateException, ArithmeticException`
- **Summary:** Stops the stopwatch.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** this `Stopwatch` instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stopwatch is already stopped
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if adding this interval would overflow the signed `long` nanosecond representation; in that case the stopwatch remains running
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stopwatch sw = Stopwatch.createStarted();
    doSomething();
    Stopwatch same = sw.stop();                        // returns this for method chaining
    sw.isRunning();                                    // returns false
    long millis = sw.elapsed(TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);   // returns elapsed at stop time
  
    Thread.sleep(10);
    long millis2 = sw.elapsed(TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);   // returns same as millis (stopped, no advance)
  
    sw.stop();                                          // throws IllegalStateException (already stopped)
  
    Stopwatch.createUnstarted().stop();                 // throws IllegalStateException (never started)
  ```
- **See also:** #start(), #isRunning()
##### reset(...) -> Stopwatch
- **Signature:** `public Stopwatch reset()`
- **Summary:** Sets the elapsed time for this stopwatch to zero, and places it in a stopped state.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** this `Stopwatch` instance for method chaining
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stopwatch sw = Stopwatch.createStarted();
    doSomeWork();
    Stopwatch same = sw.reset();        // returns this for method chaining
    sw.isRunning();                     // returns false
    sw.elapsed(TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS);   // returns 0
  
    sw.start();                         // start fresh after reset
    doMoreWork();
    sw.stop();
    sw.elapsed(TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);          // returns elapsed for second period only
  
    Stopwatch.createStarted().stop().reset();   // reset while stopped, no exception
  
    sw.start().stop().reset().start();          // method chaining: start → stop → reset → start
  ```
- **See also:** #start()
##### elapsed(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public long elapsed(final TimeUnit desiredUnit) throws IllegalArgumentException, ArithmeticException`
- **Summary:** Returns the current elapsed time shown on this stopwatch, expressed in the desired time unit, with any fraction rounded down.
- **Parameters:**
  - `desiredUnit` (`TimeUnit`) — the unit of time to express the elapsed time in; must not be `null`
- **Returns:** the elapsed time in the specified unit, rounded down
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `desiredUnit` is `null`
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if the accumulated running time cannot be represented as a signed `long` number of nanoseconds
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stopwatch sw = Stopwatch.createStarted();
    doSomething();
    sw.elapsed(TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);                            // returns elapsed in milliseconds
    sw.elapsed(TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS);                             // returns elapsed in nanoseconds
    sw.elapsed(TimeUnit.SECONDS);                                 // returns elapsed in seconds (rounded down)
  
    Stopwatch.createUnstarted().elapsed(TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);   // returns 0 (never started)
  
    sw.elapsed((TimeUnit) null);                                  // throws IllegalArgumentException
  ```
- **See also:** #elapsed()
- **Signature:** `public java.time.Duration elapsed() throws ArithmeticException`
- **Summary:** Returns the current elapsed time shown on this stopwatch as a java.time.Duration.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a `java.time.Duration` representing the elapsed time
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if the accumulated running time cannot be represented as a signed `long` number of nanoseconds
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stopwatch sw = Stopwatch.createStarted();
    doSomething();
    java.time.Duration d = sw.elapsed();     // nanosecond precision
    d.toNanos();                             // returns total nanoseconds
    d.toMillis();                            // returns total milliseconds
  
    java.time.Duration d2 = sw.elapsed();    // returns an updated value if still running
  
    Stopwatch.createUnstarted().elapsed();   // returns java.time.Duration.ZERO
  
    if (d.compareTo(java.time.Duration.ofSeconds(5)) > 0) {
        System.out.println("Took more than 5 seconds");
    }
  ```
##### toString(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `@Override public String toString() throws ArithmeticException`
- **Summary:** Returns a string representation of the current elapsed time.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a string representation of the elapsed time with appropriate unit
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.ArithmeticException` — if the accumulated running time cannot be represented as a signed `long` number of nanoseconds
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stopwatch sw = Stopwatch.createStarted();
    doSomething();
    sw.toString();                                       // returns e.g. "12.34 ms"
  
    sw.stop();
    sw.toString();                            // returns same formatted string while stopped
  
    Stopwatch.createUnstarted().toString();   // returns e.g. "0.000 ns" (not null)
  
    String s = sw.toString();                 // the returned string is never null
  ```

### Class StringWriter (com.landawn.abacus.util.StringWriter)
An unsynchronized string writer implementation backed by a StringBuilder.

**Thread-safety:** not thread-safe
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- `public StringWriter()` — Creates a new StringWriter with a default initial capacity.
  ```java
  StringWriter writer = new StringWriter();
    writer.write("Hello, World!");
  ```
- `public StringWriter(final int initialSize) throws NegativeArraySizeException` — Creates a new StringWriter with the specified initial capacity.
  - **Throws:**
    - `java.lang.NegativeArraySizeException` — if `initialSize` is negative
  ```java
  // If expecting approximately 1000 characters
    StringWriter writer = new StringWriter(1000);
  ```
- `public StringWriter(final StringBuilder sb) throws IllegalArgumentException` — Creates a new StringWriter that wraps the provided StringBuilder.
  - **Throws:**
    - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `sb` is `null`.
  ```java
  StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder("Existing content. ");
    StringWriter writer = new StringWriter(sb);
    writer.write("New content.");
    // sb now contains "Existing content. New content."
  ```

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### stringBuilder(...) -> StringBuilder
- **Signature:** `public StringBuilder stringBuilder()`
- **Summary:** Returns the underlying StringBuilder used by this writer.
- **Contract:**
  - This allows direct manipulation of the buffer when needed.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the internal StringBuilder buffer
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  StringWriter writer = new StringWriter();
    writer.write("Hello");
    StringBuilder sb = writer.stringBuilder();
    sb.reverse();   // Writer now contains "olleH"
  ```

- **Signature:** `@Override public StringWriter append(final CharSequence csq, final int start, final int end) throws IndexOutOfBoundsException`
- **Summary:** Appends a subsequence of the specified character sequence to this writer.
- **Contract:**
  - If `csq` is `null`, characters are appended as if `csq` contained the four characters `"null"`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `csq` (`CharSequence`) — the character sequence from which a subsequence is appended, may be `null`
  - `start` (`int`) — the index of the first character in the subsequence (inclusive)
  - `end` (`int`) — the index of the character following the last character in the subsequence (exclusive)
- **Returns:** this StringWriter instance for method chaining
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `start` or `end` are negative, `start` is greater than `end`, or `end` is greater than the effective sequence length (four when `csq` is `null`)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  writer.append("Hello World", 0, 5);   // Appends "Hello"
  ```

  - `len` (`int`) — the number of characters to write
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `off` is negative, `len` is negative, or `off + len` is greater than the effective sequence length (four when `str` is `null`)
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  writer.write("Hello, World!", 7, 5);   // Writes "World"
  ```

##### isValidJavaIdentifier(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean isValidJavaIdentifier(final CharSequence cs)`
- **Summary:** Checks if the given CharSequence is a valid Java identifier.
- **Contract:**
  - A valid Java identifier starts with a code point accepted by Character#isJavaIdentifierStart(int); every subsequent code point must be accepted by Character#isJavaIdentifierPart(int).
  - Context can impose further restrictions: for example, a method named `yield` requires a qualifier when invoked.
  - Keyword checks use `SourceVersion` from the compiler API (`javax.lang.model`), which must be present at runtime.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cs` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to be checked, may be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** `true` if the CharSequence is a valid Java identifier, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Valid Java identifiers
    Strings.isValidJavaIdentifier("myVariable");      // returns true
    Strings.isValidJavaIdentifier("_privateField");   // returns true
    Strings.isValidJavaIdentifier("$money");          // returns true
    Strings.isValidJavaIdentifier("MAX_VALUE");       // returns true
    Strings.isValidJavaIdentifier("userId123");       // returns true
    Strings.isValidJavaIdentifier("when");            // returns true (contextual keyword)
    Strings.isValidJavaIdentifier("module");          // returns true (contextual keyword)
    Strings.isValidJavaIdentifier("var");             // returns true (restricted for TYPE names only)
    Strings.isValidJavaIdentifier("record");          // returns true (restricted for TYPE names only)
  
    // Invalid Java identifiers
    Strings.isValidJavaIdentifier(null);               // returns false
    Strings.isValidJavaIdentifier("");                 // returns false
    Strings.isValidJavaIdentifier("   ");              // returns false
    Strings.isValidJavaIdentifier("123abc");           // returns false (starts with digit)
    Strings.isValidJavaIdentifier("class");            // returns false (keyword)
    Strings.isValidJavaIdentifier("null");             // returns false (literal)
  ```
- **See also:** #isValidJavaTypeIdentifier(CharSequence), #isJavaKeyword(CharSequence), Character#isJavaIdentifierStart(int), Character#isJavaIdentifierPart(int), SourceVersion#isKeyword(CharSequence), SourceVersion#latest(), Java Language Specification - Identifiers (https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se17/html/jls-3.html#jls-3.8)
##### isValidJavaTypeIdentifier(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean isValidJavaTypeIdentifier(final CharSequence cs)`
- **Summary:** Checks if the given CharSequence is a valid Java type identifier, that is, a name that can declare a class, interface, enum, record, annotation type or type parameter.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cs` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to be checked, may be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** `true` if the CharSequence can be used as a Java type name, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Valid Java type identifiers
    Strings.isValidJavaTypeIdentifier("Order");       // returns true
    Strings.isValidJavaTypeIdentifier("Record");      // returns true (case sensitive)
    Strings.isValidJavaTypeIdentifier("record1");     // returns true (exact match only)
    Strings.isValidJavaTypeIdentifier("module");      // returns true (contextual keyword, still a legal type name)
  
    // Invalid Java type identifiers
    Strings.isValidJavaTypeIdentifier("record");      // returns false (restricted identifier)
    Strings.isValidJavaTypeIdentifier("var");         // returns false (restricted identifier)
    Strings.isValidJavaTypeIdentifier("class");       // returns false (keyword)
    Strings.isValidJavaTypeIdentifier(null);          // returns false
  ```
- **See also:** #isValidJavaIdentifier(CharSequence), #isJavaKeyword(CharSequence), Java Language Specification - Identifiers (https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se17/html/jls-3.html#jls-3.8)
##### isJavaKeyword(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean isJavaKeyword(final CharSequence cs)`
- **Summary:** Checks if the given CharSequence is a Java keyword.
- **Contract:**
  - The restricted identifiers `permits`, `record`, `sealed`, `var`, and `yield` are contextual keywords and return `false`; use #isValidJavaIdentifier(CharSequence) to check whether a name is usable for a declaration, or #isValidJavaTypeIdentifier(CharSequence) when the name has to declare a type.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cs` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to be checked, may be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** `true` if the CharSequence is a Java keyword (or `true`/`false`/`null` literal) for this JVM's latest source version, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Java keywords
    Strings.isJavaKeyword("class");        // returns true
    Strings.isJavaKeyword("public");       // returns true
    Strings.isJavaKeyword("if");           // returns true
    Strings.isJavaKeyword("return");       // returns true
    Strings.isJavaKeyword("true");         // returns true (literal, treated as a keyword)
    Strings.isJavaKeyword("var");          // returns false (contextual keyword)
    Strings.isJavaKeyword("when");         // returns false (contextual keyword)
  
    // Not Java keywords
    Strings.isJavaKeyword("Class");        // returns false (case sensitive)
    Strings.isJavaKeyword("myVariable");   // returns false
    Strings.isJavaKeyword(null);           // returns false
    Strings.isJavaKeyword("");             // returns false
  ```
- **See also:** javax.lang.model.SourceVersion#isKeyword(CharSequence), SourceVersion#latest()

  ```java
    Strings.isValidEmailAddress(null);                       // returns false
    Strings.isValidEmailAddress("");                         // returns false
  ```

##### isValidUrl(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean isValidUrl(final CharSequence cs)`
- **Summary:** Checks if the given CharSequence is a syntactically valid URL.
- **Contract:**
  - The scheme must be `http`, `https`, `ftp`, or `file` (case-insensitive).
  - For `http`, `https`, and `ftp` the authority must parse as a server authority (URI#parseServerAuthority()) with a non-`null` host, which rejects malformed hosts such as `foo_bar.com` or `999.999.999.999`.
  - A non-empty `file` authority must parse as a host without user-info, a port, or an empty port delimiter (RFC 8089 does not allow those components in file URLs).
  - Callers guarding redirects or fetches must additionally apply an explicit scheme/host allowlist.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cs` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to be checked, may be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** `true` if the CharSequence is a syntactically valid URL with an allowed scheme, `false` otherwise
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Valid URLs
    Strings.isValidUrl("http://www.example.com");            // returns true
    Strings.isValidUrl("https://example.com:8080/path");     // returns true
    Strings.isValidUrl("ftp://files.example.com/doc.pdf");   // returns true
    Strings.isValidUrl("file:///C:/Users/doc.txt");          // returns true
  
    // Invalid URLs
    Strings.isValidUrl("not a url");                          // returns false
    Strings.isValidUrl("www.example.com");                    // returns false (no protocol)
    Strings.isValidUrl("http://a<script>");                   // returns false (illegal character)
    Strings.isValidUrl("http://foo_bar.com");                 // returns false (invalid host)
    Strings.isValidUrl("http://example.com:65536/");          // returns false (port out of range)
    Strings.isValidUrl("javascript:alert(1)");                // returns false (scheme not allowed)
    Strings.isValidUrl("file://user@host/path");              // returns false (user-info not allowed in file URLs)
    Strings.isValidUrl("file://C:/Users/doc.txt");            // returns false ('C:' is an authority, not a drive path)
    Strings.isValidUrl(null);                                 // returns false
    Strings.isValidUrl("");                                   // returns false
  ```
- **See also:** #isValidHttpUrl(CharSequence), java.net.URI
##### isValidHttpUrl(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean isValidHttpUrl(final CharSequence cs)`
- **Summary:** Checks if the given CharSequence is a syntactically valid HTTP(S) URL.
- **Contract:**
  - Callers guarding redirects or fetches must additionally apply an explicit host allowlist.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cs` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to be checked, may be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** `true` if the CharSequence is a syntactically valid HTTP(S) URL, `false` otherwise
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Valid HTTP(S) URLs
    Strings.isValidHttpUrl("http://www.example.com");         // returns true
    Strings.isValidHttpUrl("https://example.com/path");       // returns true
    Strings.isValidHttpUrl("https://example.com/foo-bar");    // returns true
    Strings.isValidHttpUrl("https://api.example.com:8443");   // returns true
  
    // Invalid HTTP(S) URLs
    Strings.isValidHttpUrl("ftp://files.example.com");         // returns false (not HTTP)
    Strings.isValidHttpUrl("www.example.com");                 // returns false (no protocol)
    Strings.isValidHttpUrl("file:///C:/doc.txt");              // returns false (not HTTP)
    Strings.isValidHttpUrl("http://a<script>");                // returns false (illegal character)
    Strings.isValidHttpUrl("http://example.com:65536/");       // returns false (port out of range)
    Strings.isValidHttpUrl(null);                              // returns false
    Strings.isValidHttpUrl("");                                // returns false
  ```
- **See also:** #isValidUrl(CharSequence), java.net.URI
##### isEmpty(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean isEmpty(final CharSequence cs)`
- **Summary:** Checks if the specified `CharSequence` is `null` or empty.

##### isBlank(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean isBlank(final CharSequence cs)`
- **Summary:** Checks if the given CharSequence is `null` or contains only whitespace characters.
- **Contract:**
  - A CharSequence is considered blank if it is `null`, empty, or contains only whitespace.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cs` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to be checked, may be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** `true` if the CharSequence is `null` or contains only whitespace characters, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java

    Strings.isBlank("\t\n\r");    // returns true
    Strings.isBlank(Character.toString(0xA0));   // returns false (U+00A0 NBSP is not Character.isWhitespace)
    Strings.isBlank("  abc  ");   // returns false
    Strings.isBlank("abc");       // returns false
    Strings.isBlank(null);        // returns true
    Strings.isBlank("");          // returns true
  ```

  ```java
    Strings.isNotEmpty(null);                        // returns false
  ```

##### isAllEmpty(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean isAllEmpty(final CharSequence a, final CharSequence b)`
- **Summary:** Checks if both of the provided CharSequences are empty or `null`.
- **Contract:**
  - This method returns `true` only when both CharSequences are either `null` or empty.
  - If at least one CharSequence is not empty, the method returns `false`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`CharSequence`) — the first CharSequence to be checked, may be `null`
  - `b` (`CharSequence`) — the second CharSequence to be checked, may be `null`
- **Returns:** `true` if both CharSequences are `null` or empty, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.isAllEmpty("abc", "xyz");   // returns false
    Strings.isAllEmpty(null, null);     // returns true
    Strings.isAllEmpty("", "");         // returns true
    Strings.isAllEmpty(null, "");       // returns true
    Strings.isAllEmpty("", null);       // returns true
    Strings.isAllEmpty("abc", "");      // returns false
    Strings.isAllEmpty("", "xyz");      // returns false
  ```
- **See also:** #isEmpty(CharSequence), #isAllEmpty(CharSequence, CharSequence, CharSequence), #isAllEmpty(CharSequence...), #isAnyEmpty(CharSequence, CharSequence)
- **Signature:** `public static boolean isAllEmpty(final CharSequence a, final CharSequence b, final CharSequence c)`
- **Summary:** Checks if all the provided CharSequences are empty or `null`.
- **Contract:**
  - This method returns `true` only when all three CharSequences are either `null` or empty.
  - If at least one CharSequence is not empty, the method returns `false`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`CharSequence`) — the first CharSequence to be checked, may be `null`
  - `b` (`CharSequence`) — the second CharSequence to be checked, may be `null`
  - `c` (`CharSequence`) — the third CharSequence to be checked, may be `null`
- **Returns:** `true` if all CharSequences are `null` or empty, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.isAllEmpty(null, null, null);   // returns true
    Strings.isAllEmpty("", "", "");         // returns true
    Strings.isAllEmpty(null, "", null);     // returns true
    Strings.isAllEmpty("abc", "", "");      // returns false
    Strings.isAllEmpty("", "xyz", "");      // returns false
    Strings.isAllEmpty("", "", "123");      // returns false
  ```
- **See also:** #isEmpty(CharSequence), #isAllEmpty(CharSequence, CharSequence), #isAllEmpty(CharSequence...), #isAnyEmpty(CharSequence, CharSequence, CharSequence)
- **Signature:** `@SafeVarargs public static boolean isAllEmpty(final CharSequence... css)`
- **Summary:** Checks if all the CharSequences are empty or `null`.
- **Contract:**
  - This method returns `true` only when all provided CharSequences are either `null` or empty.
  - If the input array itself is `null` or empty, the method returns `true`.
  - If at least one CharSequence is not empty, the method returns `false`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `css` (`CharSequence[]`) — the CharSequences to check, may be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** `true` if all the CharSequences are empty or `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.isAllEmpty(" ", "bar");        // returns false
    Strings.isAllEmpty("foo", "bar");      // returns false
    Strings.isAllEmpty((String[]) null);   // returns true (cast needed to disambiguate from the Iterable overload)
    Strings.isAllEmpty(null, "");          // returns true
    Strings.isAllEmpty(new String[] {});   // returns true
    Strings.isAllEmpty(null, "foo");       // returns false
    Strings.isAllEmpty("", "bar");         // returns false
    Strings.isAllEmpty("bob", "");         // returns false
    Strings.isAllEmpty("  bob  ", null);   // returns false
  ```
- **See also:** #isEmpty(CharSequence), #isAllEmpty(CharSequence, CharSequence), #isAllEmpty(Iterable), #isAnyEmpty(CharSequence...)
- **Signature:** `public static boolean isAllEmpty(final Iterable<? extends CharSequence> css)`

  - If the Iterable itself is `null` or empty, the method returns `true`.
  - If at least one CharSequence is not empty, the method returns `false`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `css` (`Iterable<? extends CharSequence>`) — the Iterable of CharSequences to be checked, may be `null`
- **Returns:** `true` if all CharSequences in the Iterable are `null` or empty, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  List<String> list1 = Arrays.asList(null, "", null);
    Strings.isAllEmpty(list1);   // returns true
  
    List<String> list2 = Arrays.asList("", "abc", "");
    Strings.isAllEmpty(list2);                 // returns false
  
    Strings.isAllEmpty((List<String>) null);   // returns true
    Strings.isAllEmpty(new ArrayList<>());     // returns true
  ```
- **See also:** #isEmpty(CharSequence), #isAllEmpty(CharSequence...), #isAnyEmpty(Iterable)

##### isAnyEmpty(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean isAnyEmpty(final CharSequence a, final CharSequence b)`
- **Summary:** Checks if any of the provided CharSequences are empty or `null`.
- **Contract:**
  - This method returns `true` if at least one of the two CharSequences is either `null` or empty.
  - It returns `false` only when both CharSequences are not empty.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`CharSequence`) — the first CharSequence to be checked, may be `null`
  - `b` (`CharSequence`) — the second CharSequence to be checked, may be `null`
- **Returns:** `true` if any of the CharSequences are `null` or empty, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.isAnyEmpty("abc", "xyz");   // returns false
    Strings.isAnyEmpty("   ", "xyz");   // returns false (spaces are not empty)
    Strings.isAnyEmpty(null, null);     // returns true
    Strings.isAnyEmpty("", "");         // returns true
    Strings.isAnyEmpty("abc", "");      // returns true
    Strings.isAnyEmpty("", "xyz");      // returns true
    Strings.isAnyEmpty(null, "xyz");    // returns true
  ```
- **See also:** #isEmpty(CharSequence), #isAnyEmpty(CharSequence, CharSequence, CharSequence), #isAnyEmpty(CharSequence...), #isAllEmpty(CharSequence, CharSequence)
- **Signature:** `public static boolean isAnyEmpty(final CharSequence a, final CharSequence b, final CharSequence c)`
- **Summary:** Checks if any of the provided CharSequences are empty or `null`.
- **Contract:**
  - This method returns `true` if at least one of the three CharSequences is either `null` or empty.
  - It returns `false` only when all CharSequences are not empty.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`CharSequence`) — the first CharSequence to be checked, may be `null`
  - `b` (`CharSequence`) — the second CharSequence to be checked, may be `null`
  - `c` (`CharSequence`) — the third CharSequence to be checked, may be `null`
- **Returns:** `true` if any of the CharSequences are `null` or empty, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.isAnyEmpty("abc", "def", "xyz");   // returns false
    Strings.isAnyEmpty("   ", "def", "xyz");   // returns false (spaces are not empty)
    Strings.isAnyEmpty(null, null, null);      // returns true
    Strings.isAnyEmpty("abc", "", "xyz");      // returns true
    Strings.isAnyEmpty("", "def", "xyz");      // returns true
    Strings.isAnyEmpty("abc", "def", null);    // returns true
  ```
- **See also:** #isEmpty(CharSequence), #isAnyEmpty(CharSequence, CharSequence), #isAnyEmpty(CharSequence...), #isAllEmpty(CharSequence, CharSequence, CharSequence)
- **Signature:** `@SafeVarargs public static boolean isAnyEmpty(final CharSequence... css)`
- **Summary:** Checks if any of the CharSequences are empty or `null`.
- **Contract:**
  - This method returns `true` if at least one of the provided CharSequences is either `null` or empty.
  - If the input array itself is `null` or has zero length, the method returns `false`.
  - It returns `false` only when all CharSequences in the array are not empty.
- **Parameters:**
  - `css` (`CharSequence[]`) — the CharSequences to check, may be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** `true` if any of the CharSequences are empty or `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.isAnyEmpty(" ", "bar");          // returns false
    Strings.isAnyEmpty("foo", "bar");        // returns false
    Strings.isAnyEmpty((String) null);       // returns true
    Strings.isAnyEmpty((String[]) null);     // returns false
    Strings.isAnyEmpty(null, "foo");         // returns true
    Strings.isAnyEmpty("", "bar");           // returns true
    Strings.isAnyEmpty("bob", "");           // returns true
    Strings.isAnyEmpty("  bob  ", null);     // returns true
    Strings.isAnyEmpty(new String[] {});     // returns false
    Strings.isAnyEmpty(new String[] {""});   // returns true
  ```
- **See also:** #isEmpty(CharSequence), #isAnyEmpty(CharSequence, CharSequence), #isAnyEmpty(Iterable), #isAllEmpty(CharSequence...)

##### isAnyBlank(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean isAnyBlank(final CharSequence a, final CharSequence b)`
- **Summary:** Checks if any of the provided CharSequences are blank or `null`.
- **Contract:**
  - This method returns `true` if at least one of the two CharSequences is either `null`, empty, or contains only whitespace.
  - It returns `false` only when both CharSequences contain non-whitespace characters.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`CharSequence`) — the first CharSequence to be checked, may be `null`
  - `b` (`CharSequence`) — the second CharSequence to be checked, may be `null`
- **Returns:** `true` if any of the CharSequences are `null` or blank, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.isAnyBlank("   ", "xyz");    // returns true
    Strings.isAnyBlank("abc", "\t\n");   // returns true
    Strings.isAnyBlank("abc", "xyz");    // returns false
    Strings.isAnyBlank(null, null);      // returns true
    Strings.isAnyBlank("", "");          // returns true
    Strings.isAnyBlank(null, "xyz");     // returns true
  ```
- **See also:** #isBlank(CharSequence), #isAnyBlank(CharSequence, CharSequence, CharSequence), #isAnyBlank(CharSequence...), #isAllBlank(CharSequence, CharSequence)
