- **Signature:** `public static boolean isNumericSpace(final CharSequence cs)`
- **Summary:** Checks if the CharSequence contains only Unicode digits or space (' ').
- **Parameters:**
  - `cs` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to check, may be `null`
- **Returns:** `true` if only contains digits or spaces and is non-null/non-empty, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Unicode numeric strings with spaces
    Strings.isNumericSpace("123 456");               // returns true
    Strings.isNumericSpace("१२३ ४५६");               // returns true (Devanagari digits with space)
    Strings.isNumericSpace("");                      // returns false (empty)
    Strings.isNumericSpace("  ");                    // returns true (only spaces)
    Strings.isNumericSpace("१२३");               // returns true
    Strings.isNumericSpace("१२ ३");              // returns true
  
    // Invalid strings
    Strings.isNumericSpace(null);                    // returns false
    Strings.isNumericSpace("ab2c");                  // returns false (contains letters)
    Strings.isNumericSpace("12-3");                  // returns false (contains hyphen)
    Strings.isNumericSpace("12.3");                  // returns false (contains decimal point)
    Strings.isNumericSpace("12\t3");                 // returns false (contains tab)
  ```
- **See also:** #isNumeric(CharSequence), Character#isDigit(int)
##### isWhitespace(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean isWhitespace(final CharSequence cs)`
- **Summary:** Checks if the CharSequence contains only whitespace.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cs` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to check, may be `null`
- **Returns:** `true` if only contains whitespace and is non-null/non-empty, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Whitespace strings
    Strings.isWhitespace("");         // returns false (empty)
    Strings.isWhitespace("  ");       // returns true (spaces)
    Strings.isWhitespace("\t\n\r");   // returns true (tab, newline, carriage return)
    Strings.isWhitespace("  \t  ");   // returns true (mixed whitespace)
  
    // Non-whitespace strings
    Strings.isWhitespace(null);       // returns false
    Strings.isWhitespace("abc");      // returns false (contains letters)
    Strings.isWhitespace("ab2c");     // returns false (contains letters and digit)
    Strings.isWhitespace("ab-c");     // returns false (contains letters and hyphen)
    Strings.isWhitespace(" a ");      // returns false (contains letter)
  ```
- **See also:** Character#isWhitespace(int)
##### isInteger(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@Deprecated public static boolean isInteger(final String str)`
- **Summary:** Checks if the given string represents a valid integer value (signed or unsigned).
- **Contract:**
  - The entire string must match this pattern — no surrounding whitespace or extra characters are allowed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to check, may be `null`
- **Returns:** `true` if the string is a valid integer representation, `false` otherwise
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.isInteger("123");    // returns true
    Strings.isInteger("-456");   // returns true
    Strings.isInteger("+7");     // returns true
    Strings.isInteger("0");      // returns true
    Strings.isInteger("12.3");   // returns false (decimal point not allowed)
    Strings.isInteger("abc");    // returns false
    Strings.isInteger("");       // returns false
    Strings.isInteger(null);     // returns false
  ```
- **See also:** RegExUtil#INTEGER_MATCHER, RegExUtil#POSITIVE_INTEGER_MATCHER, RegExUtil#NEGATIVE_INTEGER_MATCHER, RegExUtil#NUMBER_MATCHER, Numbers#isParsable(String), Numbers#isCreatable(String), #isAsciiInteger(CharSequence)
##### isAsciiInteger(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public static boolean isAsciiInteger(final CharSequence cs)`
- **Summary:** Checks if the given CharSequence contains only valid ASCII integer characters.
- **Contract:**
  - This method checks if the CharSequence is a valid integer representation using only ASCII characters.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cs` (`CharSequence`) — the CharSequence to check, may be `null`
- **Returns:** `true` if the CharSequence represents a valid ASCII digit integer, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Valid ASCII digit integers
    Strings.isAsciiInteger("0");       // returns true
    Strings.isAsciiInteger("123");     // returns true
    Strings.isAsciiInteger("-123");    // returns true
    Strings.isAsciiInteger("+123");    // returns true
    Strings.isAsciiInteger("+0");      // returns true
    Strings.isAsciiInteger("-0");      // returns true
  
    // Invalid strings
    Strings.isAsciiInteger(null);      // returns false
    Strings.isAsciiInteger("");        // returns false
    Strings.isAsciiInteger(" 0.1 ");   // returns false (contains spaces and decimal)
    Strings.isAsciiInteger("12.34");   // returns false (contains decimal point)
    Strings.isAsciiInteger("abc");     // returns false (contains letters)
    Strings.isAsciiInteger("1 a");     // returns false (contains space and letter)
    Strings.isAsciiInteger("2e10");    // returns false (contains exponential notation)
    Strings.isAsciiInteger("+");       // returns false (only sign, no digits)
  ```
- **See also:** #isAsciiNumeric(CharSequence), Numbers#isParsable(String)
##### indexOf(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `public static int indexOf(final String str, final int charValueToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index within the input string of the first occurrence of the specified character.
- **Contract:**
  - If a character with value `charValueToFind` occurs in the character sequence represented by the input `String` object, then the index of the first such occurrence is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `charValueToFind` (`int`) — the character value or Unicode code point to find, matching String#indexOf(int)
- **Returns:** the index of the first occurrence of the character in the input string, or -1 if the character does not occur.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Character found
    Strings.indexOf("hello", 'h');         // returns 0
    Strings.indexOf("hello", 'e');         // returns 1
    Strings.indexOf("hello", 'o');         // returns 4
    Strings.indexOf("hello world", ' ');   // returns 5
  
    // Character not found
    Strings.indexOf("hello", 'x');         // returns -1
    Strings.indexOf(null, 'a');            // returns -1
    Strings.indexOf("", 'a');              // returns -1
  ```
- **See also:** String#indexOf(int), #countMatches(String, int)
- **Signature:** `public static int indexOf(final String str, final int charValueToFind, int fromIndex)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index within the input string of the first occurrence of the specified character, starting the search at the specified index.
- **Contract:**
  - If a character with value `charValueToFind` occurs in the character sequence represented by the input `String` object at an index no smaller than `fromIndex`, then the index of the first such occurrence is returned.
  - If `fromIndex` is negative, it is treated as zero.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `charValueToFind` (`int`) — the character value or Unicode code point to find, matching String#indexOf(int, int)
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the index to start the search from.
- **Returns:** the index of the first occurrence of the character in the input string, or -1 if the character does not occur.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Character found
    Strings.indexOf("hello", 'l', 0);   // returns 2
    Strings.indexOf("hello", 'l', 3);   // returns 3
    Strings.indexOf("hello", 'o', 0);   // returns 4
  
    // Character not found
    Strings.indexOf("hello", 'h', 1);   // returns -1
    Strings.indexOf("hello", 'x', 0);   // returns -1
    Strings.indexOf(null, 'a', 0);      // returns -1
    Strings.indexOf("", 'a', 0);        // returns -1
  ```
- **See also:** String#indexOf(int, int)
- **Signature:** `public static int indexOf(final String str, final String valueToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index within the input string of the first occurrence of the specified substring.
- **Contract:**
  - If a substring with value `valueToFind` occurs in the character sequence represented by the input `String` object, then the index of the first character of the first such substring is returned.
  - The method returns `-1` if the substring is not found, or if either parameter is `null`, or if the substring is longer than the string.
  - Apache Commons Lang's ordinal methods return the same boundary for every positive ordinal when the needle is empty.
  - Usage Examples: Returns `-1` when the substring is not found.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `valueToFind` (`String`) — the substring to be found.
- **Returns:** the index of the first occurrence of the substring in the input string, or -1 if the substring does not occur.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Substring found
    Strings.indexOf("hello world", "world");   // returns 6
    Strings.indexOf("hello world", "hello");   // returns 0
    Strings.indexOf("hello world", "o");       // returns 4
    Strings.indexOf("hello world", "");        // returns 0 (empty string always found at index 0)
  
    // Substring not found
    Strings.indexOf("hello", "world");         // returns -1
    Strings.indexOf(null, "test");             // returns -1
    Strings.indexOf("test", null);             // returns -1
    Strings.indexOf("", "test");               // returns -1 (substring longer than string)
  ```
- **See also:** String#indexOf(String), StrUtil#indexOfToken(String, String, String), Index#of(String, String)
- **Signature:** `public static int indexOf(final String str, final String valueToFind, int fromIndex)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index within the input string of the first occurrence of the specified substring, starting the search at the specified index.
- **Contract:**
  - If a substring with value `valueToFind` occurs in the character sequence represented by the input `String` object at an index no smaller than `fromIndex`, then the index of the first character of the first such substring is returned.
  - If `fromIndex` is negative, it is treated as zero.
  - The method returns `-1` if the substring is not found, or if either parameter is `null`, or if the substring cannot fit in the remaining portion of the string from `fromIndex`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `valueToFind` (`String`) — the substring to be found.
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the index to start the search from.
- **Returns:** the index of the first occurrence of the substring in the input string, or -1 if the substring does not occur.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Substring found
    Strings.indexOf("hello world", "o", 0);       // returns 4
    Strings.indexOf("hello world", "o", 5);       // returns 7
    Strings.indexOf("hello world", "world", 0);   // returns 6
    Strings.indexOf("hello", "", 3);              // returns 3
    Strings.indexOf("hello", "", 99);             // returns 5 (terminal boundary)
  
    // Substring not found
    Strings.indexOf("hello", "o", 5);             // returns -1 (fromIndex beyond string)
    Strings.indexOf("hello", "world", 0);         // returns -1
    Strings.indexOf(null, "test", 0);             // returns -1
    Strings.indexOf("test", null, 0);             // returns -1
  ```
- **See also:** String#indexOf(String, int), StrUtil#indexOfToken(String, String, String, int)
##### indexOfAny(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `public static int indexOfAny(final String str, final char... valuesToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index of the first specified character (in argument order) that occurs in the input string.
- **Contract:**
  - The two are not identical once surrogate code units are involved: Commons Lang's `char` overload pairs a matched high surrogate with the next candidate and suppresses the hit when they do not form the same surrogate pair, whereas this family matches by bare UTF-16 code unit.
  - All of these return `-1` when nothing matches.
  - How to choose: Which method to use Need Use First candidate in argument order that occurs `indexOfAny` / lastIndexOfAny Leftmost match, order-independent minIndexOfAll Rightmost match, order-independent maxLastIndexOfAll Leftmost among each candidate's last hit minLastIndexOfAll Rightmost among each candidate's first hit maxIndexOfAll Use `indexOfAny` when argument order is priority (prefer this token if it exists, else that one).
  - Use minIndexOfAll when you want the earliest delimiter in the string — the Commons Lang meaning of `StringUtils.indexOfAny`, subject to the surrogate caveat above.
  - The method returns `-1` if none of the characters are found, or if the input string is `null` or empty, or if the character array is `null` or empty.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `valuesToFind` (`char[]`) — the array of characters to be found.
- **Returns:** the index of the first candidate character, in argument order, that occurs in the input string, or -1 if none of the candidate characters occur.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Characters found
    Strings.indexOfAny("hello", 'e', 'o');        // returns 1 (first match found)
    Strings.indexOfAny("hello", 'o', 'l');        // returns 4 ('o' is tried first and found at 4; not 2, the leftmost 'l')
    Strings.indexOfAny("hello", 'x', 'y', 'h');   // returns 0 (first match found)
  
    // Characters not found
    Strings.indexOfAny("hello", 'x', 'y', 'z');     // returns -1
    Strings.indexOfAny("hello", new char[] {'h'});  // returns 0 (see the single-character note above)
    Strings.indexOfAny(null, new char[] {'a'});     // returns -1
    Strings.indexOfAny("", new char[] {'a'});       // returns -1
    Strings.indexOfAny("hello", new char[0]);       // returns -1 (empty array)
  
    // Surrogate code units are treated as ordinary UTF-16 code units (no validation).
    Strings.indexOfAny("abc", (char) 0xDC00, 'a');  // returns 0 ('a' is found; the lone low surrogate U+DC00 does not match)
    Strings.indexOfAny("abc", (char) 0xD800, 'a');  // returns 0 ('a' is found; the lone high surrogate U+D800 does not match)
  ```
- **See also:** #indexOfAny(String, int, char...), #indexOf(String, int), #lastIndexOfAny(String, char\[\]), #lastIndexOfAny(String, int, char\[\]), #minIndexOfAll(String, char\[\]), #minIndexOfAll(String, int, char\[\]), #maxIndexOfAll(String, char\[\]), #maxIndexOfAll(String, int, char\[\]), #minLastIndexOfAll(String, char\[\]), #minLastIndexOfAll(String, int, char\[\]), #maxLastIndexOfAll(String, char\[\]), #maxLastIndexOfAll(String, int, char\[\])
- **Signature:** `public static int indexOfAny(final String str, int fromIndex, final char... valuesToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index of the first specified character (in argument order) that occurs at or after the specified index.
- **Contract:**
  - The method returns `-1` if none of the characters are found, or if the input string is `null` or empty, or if the character array is `null` or empty, or if `fromIndex` is at or beyond the string length.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the index to start the search from.
  - `valuesToFind` (`char[]`) — the array of characters to be found.
- **Returns:** the index of the first candidate character, in argument order, that occurs at or after `fromIndex`, or -1 if none of the candidate characters occur.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Characters found
    Strings.indexOfAny("hello", 0, 'e', 'o');      // returns 1 (first 'e')
    Strings.indexOfAny("hello", 2, 'e', 'o');      // returns 4 (first 'o' after index 2)
    Strings.indexOfAny("hello", 0, 'l');           // returns 2 (first 'l')
  
    // Characters not found
    Strings.indexOfAny("hello", 5, 'h', 'e');      // returns -1 (no match after index 5)
    Strings.indexOfAny("hello", 0, 'x', 'y');      // returns -1
    Strings.indexOfAny(null, 0, 'a');              // returns -1
  
    // Surrogate code units are treated as ordinary UTF-16 code units (no validation).
    Strings.indexOfAny("abc", 0, (char) 0xDC00, 'a');  // returns 0 ('a' is found; the lone low surrogate U+DC00 does not match)
    Strings.indexOfAny("abc", 0, (char) 0xD800, 'a');  // returns 0 ('a' is found; the lone high surrogate U+D800 does not match)
  ```
- **See also:** #indexOfAny(String, char...), #indexOf(String, int, int), #lastIndexOfAny(String, int, char\[\]), #minIndexOfAll(String, int, char\[\]), #maxIndexOfAll(String, int, char\[\]), #minLastIndexOfAll(String, int, char\[\]), #maxLastIndexOfAll(String, int, char\[\])
- **Signature:** `public static int indexOfAny(final String str, final String... valuesToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index of the first specified substring (in argument order) that occurs in the input string.
- **Contract:**
  - All of these return `-1` when nothing matches.
  - How to choose: Which method to use Need Use First candidate in argument order that occurs `indexOfAny` / lastIndexOfAny Leftmost match, order-independent minIndexOfAll Rightmost match, order-independent maxLastIndexOfAll Leftmost among each candidate's last hit minLastIndexOfAll Rightmost among each candidate's first hit maxIndexOfAll Use `indexOfAny` when argument order is priority (prefer this token if it exists, else that one).
  - Use minIndexOfAll when you want the earliest delimiter in the string — the Commons Lang meaning of `StringUtils.indexOfAny`.
  - The method returns `-1` if none of the substrings are found, or if the input string is `null`, or if the substring array is `null` or empty.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `valuesToFind` (`String[]`) — the array of substrings to be found.
- **Returns:** the index of the first candidate substring, in argument order, that occurs in the input string, or -1 if none of the candidate substrings occur.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Substrings found
    Strings.indexOfAny("hello world", "world", "hello");   // returns 6 ("world" is the first array element that matches)
    Strings.indexOfAny("hello world", "xyz", "world");     // returns 6 ("world" found)
    Strings.indexOfAny("hello world", "o", "e");           // returns 4 ("o" is the first array element that matches)
  
    // Substrings not found
    Strings.indexOfAny("hello", "xyz", "abc");             // returns -1
    Strings.indexOfAny(null, "test");                      // returns -1
    Strings.indexOfAny("test", (String[]) null);           // returns -1
    Strings.indexOfAny("test", new String[0]);             // returns -1 (empty array)
  ```
- **See also:** #indexOfAny(String, int, String...), #indexOf(String, String), #lastIndexOfAny(String, String\[\]), #lastIndexOfAny(String, int, String\[\]), #minIndexOfAll(String, String\[\]), #minIndexOfAll(String, int, String\[\]), #maxIndexOfAll(String, String\[\]), #maxIndexOfAll(String, int, String\[\]), #minLastIndexOfAll(String, String\[\]), #minLastIndexOfAll(String, int, String\[\]), #maxLastIndexOfAll(String, String\[\]), #maxLastIndexOfAll(String, int, String\[\])
- **Signature:** `public static int indexOfAny(final String str, int fromIndex, final String... valuesToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index of the first specified substring (in argument order) that occurs at or after the specified index.
- **Contract:**
  - The method returns `-1` if none of the substrings are found, or if the input string is `null`, or if the substring array is `null` or empty, or if `fromIndex` is greater than the string length (even for an empty (`""`) element).
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the index to start the search from.
  - `valuesToFind` (`String[]`) — the array of substrings to be found.
- **Returns:** the index of the first candidate substring, in argument order, that occurs at or after `fromIndex`, or -1 if none of the candidate substrings occur.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Argument order vs leftmost remaining match
    Strings.indexOfAny("abca", 1, "a", "b");       // returns 3 ("a" is tried first; next "a" is at 3)
    Strings.minIndexOfAll("abca", 1, "a", "b");    // returns 1 (leftmost remaining: "b" at 1)
  
    // Substrings found
    Strings.indexOfAny("hello world", 0, "world", "hello");   // returns 6 ("world" is the first array element that matches)
    Strings.indexOfAny("hello world", 6, "world", "hello");   // returns 6 ("world" at index 6)
    Strings.indexOfAny("hello world", 7, "world", "o");       // returns 7 ("o" at index 7)
  
    // Substrings not found
    Strings.indexOfAny("hello", 0, "xyz", "abc");             // returns -1
    Strings.indexOfAny("hello", 10, "h", "e");                // returns -1 (fromIndex beyond string)
    Strings.indexOfAny(null, 0, "test");                      // returns -1
  ```
- **See also:** #indexOfAny(String, String...), #indexOf(String, String, int), #lastIndexOfAny(String, int, String\[\]), #minIndexOfAll(String, int, String\[\]), #maxIndexOfAll(String, int, String\[\]), #minLastIndexOfAll(String, int, String\[\]), #maxLastIndexOfAll(String, int, String\[\])
##### indexOfAnyBut(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `public static int indexOfAnyBut(final String str, final char... valuesToExclude)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index within the input string of the first occurrence of any character that is not in the specified array of characters to exclude.
- **Contract:**
  - If a character not within the array `valuesToExclude` occurs in the character sequence represented by the input `String` object, then the index of the first such occurrence is returned.
  - The method returns `-1` if all characters in the string are in the exclusion array, or if the string is `null` or empty.
  - If the exclusion array is `null` or empty, returns 0 (the first character is not excluded).
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `valuesToExclude` (`char[]`) — the array of characters to exclude from the search.
- **Returns:** the index of the first occurrence of any character not in the array of characters to exclude, or -1 if all characters are in the array or the string is `null` or empty.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Characters not in exclusion array found
    Strings.indexOfAnyBut("hello", 'h', 'e');   // returns 2 (first 'l')
    Strings.indexOfAnyBut("hello", 'x', 'y');   // returns 0 (first 'h')
    Strings.indexOfAnyBut("aaabbb", 'a');       // returns 3 (first 'b')
  
    // All characters excluded or special cases
    Strings.indexOfAnyBut("aaa", 'a');          // returns -1 (all excluded)
    Strings.indexOfAnyBut(null, 'a');           // returns -1
    Strings.indexOfAnyBut("", 'a');             // returns -1
    Strings.indexOfAnyBut("hello");             // returns 0 (empty exclusion array)
  ```
- **See also:** #indexOfAnyBut(String, int, char...)
- **Signature:** `public static int indexOfAnyBut(final String str, int fromIndex, final char... valuesToExclude)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index within the input string of the first occurrence of any character that is not in the specified array of characters to exclude, starting the search at the specified index.
- **Contract:**
  - If a character not within the array `valuesToExclude` occurs in the character sequence represented by the input `String` object at an index no smaller than `fromIndex`, then the index of the first such occurrence is returned.
  - If `fromIndex` is negative, it is treated as zero.
  - The method returns `-1` if all characters from `fromIndex` onwards are in the exclusion array, or if the string is `null` or empty.
  - If the exclusion array is `null` or empty, returns `fromIndex` (if valid).
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the index to start the search from.
  - `valuesToExclude` (`char[]`) — the array of characters to exclude from the search.
- **Returns:** the index of the first occurrence of any character not in the array of characters to exclude, or -1 if all characters are in the array or the string is `null` or empty.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Characters not in exclusion array found
    Strings.indexOfAnyBut("hello", 0, 'h', 'e');      // returns 2 (first 'l')
    Strings.indexOfAnyBut("hello", 3, 'h', 'e');      // returns 3 (first 'l' from index 3)
    Strings.indexOfAnyBut("aaabbb", 0, 'a');          // returns 3 (first 'b')
    Strings.indexOfAnyBut("aaabbb", 3, 'a');          // returns 3 (first 'b' from index 3)
  
    // All characters excluded or special cases
    Strings.indexOfAnyBut("aaa", 0, 'a');             // returns -1 (all excluded)
    Strings.indexOfAnyBut("hello", 10, 'x');          // returns -1 (fromIndex beyond string)
    Strings.indexOfAnyBut(null, 0, 'a');              // returns -1
  
    // Surrogate code units are treated as ordinary UTF-16 code units (no validation).
    Strings.indexOfAnyBut("abc", 0, (char) 0xDC00, 'a');  // returns 1 ('a' is excluded, 'b' is the first non-excluded char; low surrogate U+DC00 does not match)
    Strings.indexOfAnyBut("abc", 0, (char) 0xD800, 'a');  // returns 1 ('a' is excluded, 'b' is the first non-excluded char; high surrogate U+D800 does not match)
  ```
- **See also:** #indexOfAnyBut(String, char...)
##### indexOfIgnoreCase(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `public static int indexOfIgnoreCase(final String str, final String valueToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index within the input string of the first occurrence of the specified substring, ignoring case considerations.
- **Contract:**
  - If a substring with value `valueToFind` occurs in the character sequence represented by the input `String` object, then the index of the first such occurrence is returned.
  - The method returns -1 if the substring is not found, or if either the input string or the substring to find is `null`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `valueToFind` (`String`) — the substring to be found, may be `null`.
- **Returns:** the index of the first occurrence of the substring in the input string, or -1 if the substring does not occur or if either parameter is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.indexOfIgnoreCase("Hello World", "WORLD");   // returns 6
    Strings.indexOfIgnoreCase("Hello World", "world");   // returns 6
    Strings.indexOfIgnoreCase("Hello World", "xyz");     // returns -1
    Strings.indexOfIgnoreCase("straße", "SS");      // returns -1 ("ß" is not a same-length match for "SS")
    Strings.indexOfIgnoreCase(null, "test");             // returns -1
    Strings.indexOfIgnoreCase("test", null);             // returns -1
  ```
- **See also:** #indexOfIgnoreCase(String, String, int), StrUtil#indexOfTokenIgnoreCase(String, String, String)
- **Signature:** `public static int indexOfIgnoreCase(final String str, final String valueToFind, int fromIndex)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index within the input string of the first occurrence of the specified substring, ignoring case considerations, starting the search at the specified index.
- **Contract:**
  - If a substring with value `valueToFind` occurs in the character sequence represented by the input `String` object at or after the specified `fromIndex`, then the index of the first such occurrence is returned.
  - The method returns -1 if the substring is not found, or if either the input string or the substring to find is `null`.
  - If `fromIndex` is negative, it is treated as 0.
  - If `fromIndex` is greater than the string length, -1 is returned for a non-empty needle; an empty needle still matches at `str.length()`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `valueToFind` (`String`) — the substring to be found, may be `null`.
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the index to start the search from. Negative values are treated as 0.
- **Returns:** the index of the first occurrence of the substring in the input string, or -1 if the substring does not occur or if either string parameter is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.indexOfIgnoreCase("Hello World Hello", "hello", 0);   // returns 0
    Strings.indexOfIgnoreCase("Hello World Hello", "hello", 7);   // returns 12
    Strings.indexOfIgnoreCase("Hello World", "WORLD", 10);        // returns -1
    Strings.indexOfIgnoreCase("test", "TEST", -5);                // returns 0
    Strings.indexOfIgnoreCase("abc", "", 10);                     // returns 3 (empty needle)
  ```
- **See also:** StrUtil#indexOfTokenIgnoreCase(String, String, String, int)
##### lastIndexOf(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `public static int lastIndexOf(final String str, final int charValueToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index within the input string of the last occurrence of the specified character.
- **Contract:**
  - If a character with value `charValueToFind` occurs in the character sequence represented by the input `String` object, then the index of the last such occurrence is returned.
  - The method returns -1 if the character is not found, or if the input string is `null` or empty.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `charValueToFind` (`int`) — the character value or Unicode code point to find, matching String#lastIndexOf(int)
- **Returns:** the index of the last occurrence of the character in the input string, or -1 if the character does not occur or if the string is `null` or empty.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.lastIndexOf("Hello World", 'o');   // returns 7
    Strings.lastIndexOf("Hello World", 'x');   // returns -1
    Strings.lastIndexOf("", 'a');              // returns -1
    Strings.lastIndexOf(null, 'a');            // returns -1
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static int lastIndexOf(final String str, final int charValueToFind, int startIndexFromBack)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index within the input string of the last occurrence of the specified character, searching backward starting at the specified index.
- **Contract:**
  - If no such character occurs in the input string at or before position `startIndexFromBack`, then -1 is returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `charValueToFind` (`int`) — a character (Unicode code point).
  - `startIndexFromBack` (`int`) — the index to start the search from. There is no restriction on the value of `startIndexFromBack`. If it is greater than or equal to the input length, it has the same effect as if it were equal to one less than the input length: the entire input may be searched. If it is negative, -1 is returned.
- **Returns:** the index of the last occurrence of the character in the input string that is less than or equal to `startIndexFromBack`, or `-1` if the character does not occur before that point.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.lastIndexOf("Hello World", 'o', 10);   // returns 7
    Strings.lastIndexOf("Hello World", 'o', 5);    // returns 4
    Strings.lastIndexOf("Hello World", 'o', 3);    // returns -1
    Strings.lastIndexOf("Hello", 'l', -1);         // returns -1
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static int lastIndexOf(final String str, final String valueToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index within the input string of the last occurrence of the specified substring.
- **Contract:**
  - If the substring does not occur, -1 is returned.
  - The method returns -1 if either the input string or the substring to find is `null`, or if the substring is longer than the input string.
  - Usage Examples: Returns `-1` when the substring is not found.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `valueToFind` (`String`) — the substring to be found, may be `null`.
- **Returns:** the index of the last occurrence of the substring in the input string, or -1 if the substring does not occur or if either parameter is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.lastIndexOf("Hello World Hello", "Hello");   // returns 12
    Strings.lastIndexOf("Hello World", "World");         // returns 6
    Strings.lastIndexOf("Hello World", "xyz");           // returns -1
    Strings.lastIndexOf("abc", "");                      // returns 3 (empty needle matches at str.length())
    Strings.lastIndexOf(null, "test");                   // returns -1
    Strings.lastIndexOf("test", null);                   // returns -1
  ```
- **See also:** Index#last(String, String)
- **Signature:** `public static int lastIndexOf(final String str, final String valueToFind, int startIndexFromBack)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index within `str` of the last occurrence of the specified `valueToFind`, searching backward starting at the specified index.
- **Contract:**
  - If no such value of k exists, then `-1` is returned.
  - The method returns -1 if either the input string or the substring to find is `null`, if `startIndexFromBack` is negative, or if the substring is longer than the input string.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `valueToFind` (`String`) — the substring to be found, may be `null`.
  - `startIndexFromBack` (`int`) — the index to start the search from, searching backward. If greater than or equal to the string length, the entire string is searched.
- **Returns:** the index of the last occurrence of the substring at or before the specified index, or -1 if the substring does not occur or if any parameter is invalid.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.lastIndexOf("Hello World Hello", "Hello", 15);   // returns 12
    Strings.lastIndexOf("Hello World Hello", "Hello", 10);   // returns 0
    Strings.lastIndexOf("Hello World", "World", 5);          // returns -1
    Strings.lastIndexOf("abc", "", 2);                       // returns 2 (empty needle matches at min(startIndexFromBack, str.length()))
    Strings.lastIndexOf("test", "test", -1);                 // returns -1
  ```
- **See also:** StrUtil#lastIndexOfToken(String, String, String, int)
##### lastIndexOfIgnoreCase(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `public static int lastIndexOfIgnoreCase(final String str, final String valueToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index within the input string of the last occurrence of the specified substring, ignoring case considerations.
- **Contract:**
  - If a substring with value `valueToFind` occurs in the character sequence represented by the input `String` object, then the index of the last such occurrence is returned.
  - The method returns -1 if the substring is not found, or if either the input string or the substring to find is `null`, or if the substring is longer than the input string.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `valueToFind` (`String`) — the substring to be found, may be `null`.
- **Returns:** the index of the last occurrence of the substring in the input string, or -1 if the substring does not occur or if either parameter is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.lastIndexOfIgnoreCase("Hello World HELLO", "hello");   // returns 12
    Strings.lastIndexOfIgnoreCase("Hello World", "WORLD");         // returns 6
    Strings.lastIndexOfIgnoreCase("Hello World", "xyz");           // returns -1
    Strings.lastIndexOfIgnoreCase(null, "test");                   // returns -1
    Strings.lastIndexOfIgnoreCase("test", null);                   // returns -1
  ```
- **See also:** #indexOfIgnoreCase(String, String, int)
- **Signature:** `public static int lastIndexOfIgnoreCase(final String str, final String valueToFind, int startIndexFromBack)`
- **Summary:** Returns the index within the input string of the last occurrence of the specified substring, ignoring case considerations, searching backward starting at the specified index.
- **Contract:**
  - If a substring with value `valueToFind` occurs in the character sequence represented by the input `String` object at or before the specified `startIndexFromBack`, then the index of the last such occurrence is returned.
  - The method returns -1 if the substring is not found at or before the specified index, or if either the input string or the substring to find is `null`, if `startIndexFromBack` is negative, or if the substring is longer than the input string.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `valueToFind` (`String`) — the substring to be found, may be `null`.
  - `startIndexFromBack` (`int`) — the index to start the search from, searching backward. If greater than or equal to the string length, the entire string is searched.
- **Returns:** the index of the last occurrence of the substring at or before the specified index, or -1 if the substring does not occur or if any parameter is invalid.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.lastIndexOfIgnoreCase("Hello World HELLO", "hello", 15);   // returns 12
    Strings.lastIndexOfIgnoreCase("Hello World HELLO", "hello", 10);   // returns 0
    Strings.lastIndexOfIgnoreCase("Hello World", "WORLD", 5);          // returns -1
    Strings.lastIndexOfIgnoreCase("test", "TEST", -1);                 // returns -1
  ```
- **See also:** #indexOfIgnoreCase(String, String, int), StrUtil#lastIndexOfTokenIgnoreCase(String, String, String, int)
##### lastIndexOfAny(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `public static int lastIndexOfAny(final String str, final char... valuesToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns the last index of the first specified character (in argument order) that occurs in the input string.
- **Contract:**
  - The method returns -1 if none of the characters are found, or if the input string is `null` or empty, or if the character array is `null` or empty.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `valuesToFind` (`char[]`) — the array of characters to be found, may be `null` or empty.
- **Returns:** the last index of the first candidate character, in argument order, that occurs in the input string, or -1 if none occurs or if the string or character array is `null` or empty.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.lastIndexOfAny("Hello World", 'o', 'l');        // returns 7 ('o' is tried first; its last index is 7 — not 9, the last 'l')
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny("Hello World", 'x', 'y', 'z');   // returns -1
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny("", 'a', 'b');                   // returns -1
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny(null, new char[] {'a'});         // returns -1
  
    // Surrogate code units are treated as ordinary UTF-16 code units (no validation).
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny("abc", (char) 0xDC00, 'a');      // returns 0 ('a' is found; the lone low surrogate U+DC00 does not match)
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny("abc", (char) 0xD800, 'a');      // returns 0 ('a' is found; the lone high surrogate U+D800 does not match)
  ```
- **See also:** #minLastIndexOfAll(String, char\[\]), #minLastIndexOfAll(String, int, char\[\]), #maxLastIndexOfAll(String, char\[\]), #maxLastIndexOfAll(String, int, char\[\])
- **Signature:** `public static int lastIndexOfAny(final String str, int startIndexFromBack, final char... valuesToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns the last index, at or before the specified index, of the first specified character (in argument order) that occurs in the input string.
- **Contract:**
  - The method returns -1 if `startIndexFromBack` is negative, if none of the characters are found at or before it, or if the input string or character array is `null` or empty.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `startIndexFromBack` (`int`) — the index to start the search from, searching backward. A negative value returns `-1`; a value at or beyond the string length searches the entire string.
  - `valuesToFind` (`char[]`) — the array of characters to be found, may be `null` or empty.
- **Returns:** the last index, at or before `startIndexFromBack`, of the first candidate character in argument order, or -1 if none occurs or if the string or character array is `null` or empty.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.lastIndexOfAny("Hello World", 8, 'o', 'l');         // returns 7 ('o' is tried first; its last index at or before 8 is 7)
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny("Hello World", 5, 'o', 'l');         // returns 4 ('o' is tried first; its last index at or before 5 is 4)
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny("Hello World", 10, 'x', 'y', 'z');   // returns -1
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny("Hello World", -1, 'o', 'l');        // returns -1
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny("", 0, 'a', 'b');                    // returns -1
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny(null, 0, 'a');                       // returns -1
  
    // Surrogate code units are treated as ordinary UTF-16 code units (no validation).
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny("abc", 0, (char) 0xDC00, 'a');       // returns 0 ('a' is found; the lone low surrogate U+DC00 does not match)
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny("abc", 0, (char) 0xD800, 'a');       // returns 0 ('a' is found; the lone high surrogate U+D800 does not match)
  ```
- **See also:** #lastIndexOfAny(String, char\[\]), #minLastIndexOfAll(String, int, char\[\]), #maxLastIndexOfAll(String, int, char\[\])
- **Signature:** `public static int lastIndexOfAny(final String str, final String... valuesToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns the last index of the first specified substring (in argument order) that occurs in the input string.
- **Contract:**
  - The method returns -1 if none of the substrings are found, or if the input string is `null`, or if the substring array is `null` or empty.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `valuesToFind` (`String[]`) — the array of substrings to be found, may be `null` or empty.
- **Returns:** the last index of the first candidate substring, in argument order, that occurs in the input string, or -1 if none occurs, if `str` is `null`, or if the substring array is `null` or empty.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.lastIndexOfAny("Hello World", "World", "Hello");   // returns 6 ("World" is tried first and found at 6)
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny("Hello World", "xyz", "abc");       // returns -1
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny("abc", "");                         // returns 3
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny("", "");                            // returns 0
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny("test", null, "test");              // returns 0
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny(null, "test");                      // returns -1
  ```
- **See also:** #minLastIndexOfAll(String, String\[\]), #minLastIndexOfAll(String, int, String\[\]), #maxLastIndexOfAll(String, String\[\]), #maxLastIndexOfAll(String, int, String\[\])
- **Signature:** `public static int lastIndexOfAny(final String str, int startIndexFromBack, final String... valuesToFind)`
- **Summary:** Returns the last index, at or before the specified index, of the first specified substring (in argument order) that occurs in the input string.
- **Contract:**
  - The method returns -1 if `startIndexFromBack` is negative, if none of the substrings are found at or before it, or if the input string is `null`, or if the substring array is `null` or empty.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `startIndexFromBack` (`int`) — the index to start the search from, searching backward. A negative value returns `-1`; a value at or beyond the string length searches the entire string.
  - `valuesToFind` (`String[]`) — the array of substrings to be found, may be `null` or empty.
- **Returns:** the last index, at or before `startIndexFromBack`, of the first candidate substring in argument order, or -1 if none occurs, if `str` is `null`, or if the substring array is `null` or empty.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.lastIndexOfAny("Hello World", 10, "World", "Hello");   // returns 6 ("World" is tried first and found at 6)
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny("Hello World", 5, "World", "Hello");    // returns 0
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny("Hello World", 10, "xyz", "abc");       // returns -1
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny("abc", 100, "");                        // returns 3 (empty needle at length)
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny("abc", -1, "a");                        // returns -1
    Strings.lastIndexOfAny(null, 10, "test");                      // returns -1
  ```
- **See also:** #lastIndexOfAny(String, String...), #minLastIndexOfAll(String, int, String\[\]), #maxLastIndexOfAll(String, int, String\[\])
##### minIndexOfAll(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `public static int minIndexOfAll(final String str, final String... valuesToFind)`
- **Summary:** Finds the smallest index of all specified substrings within the input string.
- **Contract:**
  - The method returns -1 if none of the substrings are found, or if the input string is `null`, or if the substring array is `null` or empty.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `valuesToFind` (`String[]`) — the array of substrings to be found, may be `null` or empty.
- **Returns:** the smallest index of all substrings within the input string or -1 if none of the substrings occur.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.minIndexOfAll("Hello World", "World", "o");       // returns 4
    Strings.minIndexOfAll("Hello World", "xyz", "abc");       // returns -1
    Strings.minIndexOfAll("test string", "string", "test");   // returns 0
    Strings.minIndexOfAll(null, "test");                      // returns -1
  ```
- **See also:** #indexOfAny(String, String\[\]), #indexOfAny(String, int, String\[\])
- **Signature:** `public static int minIndexOfAll(final String str, int fromIndex, final String... valuesToFind)`
- **Summary:** Finds the smallest index of all substrings in `valuesToFind` within the input string from `fromIndex`.
- **Contract:**
  - The method returns -1 if none of the substrings are found from the specified index, or if the input string is `null`, if `fromIndex` is greater than the string length, or if the substring array is `null` or empty.
  - If `fromIndex` is negative, it is treated as 0.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the index to start the search from. Negative values are treated as 0.
  - `valuesToFind` (`String[]`) — the array of substrings to be found, may be `null` or empty.
- **Returns:** the smallest index of all substrings within the input string from `fromIndex` or -1 if none of the substrings occur.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.minIndexOfAll("Hello World", 0, "World", "o");   // returns 4
    Strings.minIndexOfAll("Hello World", 5, "World", "o");   // returns 6
    Strings.minIndexOfAll("Hello World", 8, "World", "o");   // returns -1
    Strings.minIndexOfAll("test", -5, "test");               // returns 0
  ```
- **See also:** #indexOfAny(String, String\[\]), #indexOfAny(String, int, String\[\])
- **Signature:** `public static int minIndexOfAll(final String str, final char... valuesToFind)`
- **Summary:** Finds the smallest (leftmost) index of any of the specified characters.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to search, may be `null` or empty
  - `valuesToFind` (`char[]`) — the characters to find, may be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** the smallest index among the specified characters, or `-1` if none occurs
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.minIndexOfAll("hello world", 'w', 'h');   // returns 0
    Strings.minIndexOfAll("hello", 'o', 'l');         // returns 2
    Strings.minIndexOfAll("hello", 'x', 'y');         // returns -1
    Strings.minIndexOfAll("hello", new char[] {'l'}); // returns 2 (single character needs an explicit array)
    Strings.minIndexOfAll("", 'a', 'b');              // returns -1
    Strings.minIndexOfAll(null, 'a', 'b');            // returns -1
  ```
- **See also:** #indexOfAny(String, char\[\]), #minIndexOfAll(String, String...)
- **Signature:** `public static int minIndexOfAll(final String str, int fromIndex, final char... valuesToFind)`
- **Summary:** Finds the smallest (leftmost) index of any of the specified characters at or after `fromIndex`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to search, may be `null` or empty
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the index to start the search from
  - `valuesToFind` (`char[]`) — the characters to find, may be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** the smallest index among the specified characters at or after `fromIndex`, or `-1` if none occurs
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.minIndexOfAll("hello world", 0, 'o', 'h');   // returns 0 (min of first hits 'o'@4 and 'h'@0)
    Strings.minIndexOfAll("hello world", 3, 'o', 'h');   // returns 4 (only 'o' still occurs at or after 3)
    Strings.minIndexOfAll("hello", 0, 'x', 'y');         // returns -1
    Strings.minIndexOfAll("hello", -5, 'l');             // returns 2 (a negative fromIndex clamps to 0)
    Strings.minIndexOfAll(null, 0, 'a');                 // returns -1
  ```
- **See also:** #indexOfAny(String, int, char\[\]), #minIndexOfAll(String, int, String...)
##### maxIndexOfAll(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `public static int maxIndexOfAll(final String str, final String... valuesToFind)`
- **Summary:** Finds the largest of the first-occurrence indices for the specified substrings.
- **Contract:**
  - The method returns -1 if none of the substrings are found, or if the input string is `null`, or if the substring array is `null` or empty.
  - Empty (`""`) elements are NOT ignored (like #indexOfAny(String, String\[\])): an empty string element matches at index `0`, so it can make the result `0` (rather than `-1`) even when no other element occurs.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `valuesToFind` (`String[]`) — the array of substrings to be found, may be `null` or empty.
- **Returns:** the largest first-occurrence index among the specified substrings, or -1 if none occurs.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.maxIndexOfAll("Hello World", "o", "World");   // returns 6
    Strings.maxIndexOfAll("Hello World", "H", "d");       // returns 10
    Strings.maxIndexOfAll("abca", "a", "b");              // returns 1 (max of first-occurrence indices 0 and 1)
    Strings.maxIndexOfAll("Hello World", "xyz", "abc");   // returns -1
    Strings.maxIndexOfAll(null, "test");                  // returns -1
  ```
- **See also:** #indexOfAny(String, String\[\]), #indexOfAny(String, int, String\[\]), #maxLastIndexOfAll(String, String\[\])
- **Signature:** `public static int maxIndexOfAll(final String str, final int fromIndex, final String... valuesToFind)`
- **Summary:** Finds the largest of the first-occurrence indices for the specified substrings from `fromIndex`.
- **Contract:**
  - The method returns -1 if none of the substrings are found from the specified index, or if the input string is `null`, if `fromIndex` is greater than the string length, or if the substring array is `null` or empty.
  - If `fromIndex` is negative, it is treated as 0.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to be checked, may be `null` or empty.
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the index to start the search from. Negative values are treated as 0.
  - `valuesToFind` (`String[]`) — the array of substrings to be found, may be `null` or empty.
- **Returns:** the largest first-occurrence index among the specified substrings at or after `fromIndex`, or -1 if none occurs.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.maxIndexOfAll("Hello World", 0, "o", "World");   // returns 6
    Strings.maxIndexOfAll("Hello World", 5, "o", "H");       // returns 7
    Strings.maxIndexOfAll("abca", 0, "a", "b");              // returns 1 (first eligible matches are at 0 and 1)
    Strings.maxIndexOfAll("Hello World", 8, "o", "World");   // returns -1
    Strings.maxIndexOfAll("test", -5, "test", "t");          // returns 0
  ```
- **See also:** #indexOfAny(String, String\[\]), #indexOfAny(String, int, String\[\]), #maxLastIndexOfAll(String, String\[\])
- **Signature:** `public static int maxIndexOfAll(final String str, final char... valuesToFind)`
- **Summary:** Finds the largest of the first-occurrence indices for the specified characters.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to search, may be `null` or empty
  - `valuesToFind` (`char[]`) — the characters to find, may be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** the largest first-occurrence index among the specified characters, or `-1` if none occurs
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.maxIndexOfAll("hello", 'o', 'l');         // returns 4
    Strings.maxIndexOfAll("hello world", 'h', 'w');   // returns 6
    Strings.maxIndexOfAll("hello", 'x', 'y');         // returns -1
    Strings.maxIndexOfAll("hello", new char[] {'l'}); // returns 2 (single character needs an explicit array)
    Strings.maxIndexOfAll("", 'a', 'b');              // returns -1
    Strings.maxIndexOfAll(null, 'a', 'b');            // returns -1
  ```
- **See also:** #indexOfAny(String, char\[\]), #maxIndexOfAll(String, String...)
- **Signature:** `public static int maxIndexOfAll(final String str, int fromIndex, final char... valuesToFind)`
- **Summary:** Finds the largest of the first-occurrence indices for the specified characters at or after `fromIndex`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to search, may be `null` or empty
  - `fromIndex` (`int`) — the index to start the search from
  - `valuesToFind` (`char[]`) — the characters to find, may be `null` or empty
- **Returns:** the largest first-occurrence index among the specified characters at or after `fromIndex`, or `-1` if none occurs
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.maxIndexOfAll("hello world", 0, 'o', 'l');   // returns 4 (max of first hits 'o'@4 and 'l'@2)
    Strings.maxIndexOfAll("hello world", 3, 'o', 'l');   // returns 4 (first hits at or after 3: 'o'@4, 'l'@3)
    Strings.maxIndexOfAll("hello", 0, 'x', 'y');         // returns -1
    Strings.maxIndexOfAll(null, 0, 'a');                 // returns -1
  ```
- **See also:** #indexOfAny(String, int, char\[\]), #maxIndexOfAll(String, int, String...)
##### minLastIndexOfAll(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `public static int minLastIndexOfAll(final String str, final String... valuesToFind)`
- **Summary:** Finds the smallest last index of all substrings in `valuesToFind` within the input string.
- **Contract:**
  - The method returns -1 if none of the substrings are found, or if the input string is `null`, or if the substring array is `null` or empty.
  - Empty (`""`) elements are NOT ignored (like #lastIndexOfAny(String, String\[\])): an empty string element matches at `str.length()` (the position past the last character), so it can make the result non-negative even when no other element occurs.
- **Parameters:**
  - `str` (`String`) — the string to search within, may be `null`.
  - `valuesToFind` (`String[]`) — the substrings to find within the string, may be empty or `null`.
- **Returns:** the smallest last index of all substrings within the input string or -1 if none of the substrings occur.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.minLastIndexOfAll("Hello World", "o", "World");   // returns 6
    Strings.minLastIndexOfAll("Hello Hello", "Hello", "o");   // returns 6
    Strings.minLastIndexOfAll("test", "xyz", "abc");          // returns -1
    Strings.minLastIndexOfAll(null, "test");                  // returns -1
  ```
- **See also:** #lastIndexOfAny(String, String\[\]), #lastIndexOfAny(String, int, String\[\])
- **Signature:** `public static int minLastIndexOfAll(final String str, int startIndexFromBack, final String... valuesToFind)`

  - `valuesToFind` (`String[]`) — the substrings to find within the string, may be empty or `null`.
- **Returns:** the smallest last index of all substrings within the input string at or before `startIndexFromBack` or -1 if none of the substrings occur.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Strings.minLastIndexOfAll("Hello World", 10, "o", "World");   // returns 6
    Strings.minLastIndexOfAll("Hello World", 5, "o", "World");    // returns 4
    Strings.minLastIndexOfAll("Hello World", 3, "o", "World");    // returns -1
    Strings.minLastIndexOfAll("test", -1, "test");                // returns -1
  ```
