##### unzipToLists(...) -> Triple<List<A>, List<B>, List<C>>
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings({ "rawtypes", "unchecked" }) public Triple<List<A>, List<B>, List<C>> unzipToLists(final Supplier<? extends List> supplier) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Unzips all remaining triples in this `TriIterator` into three `List`s.
- **Contract:**
  - If a source callback or Collection#add(Object) throws, the source and the lists may be partially consumed/populated.
  - Output collections must be distinct instances; aliasing is rejected with IllegalArgumentException before consumption.
  - Callers must also avoid distinct wrappers that share mutable backing storage.
- **Parameters:**
  - `supplier` (`Supplier<? extends List>`) — a supplier invoked three times to create the left, middle, and right lists; each call must return a `non-null` `List`
- **Returns:** a `Triple` whose left, middle, and right lists contain all first, second, and third components, respectively
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `supplier` is `null`, if any of the three calls to it returns `null`, or if any two of the three returned lists are the same instance.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String[] names = {"Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"};
    Integer[] ages = {25, 30, 35};
    Boolean[] active = {true, false, true};
    Triple<List<String>, List<Integer>, List<Boolean>> result =
        TriIterator.zip(names, ages, active).unzipToLists(ArrayList::new);
    List<String> nameList = result.left();       // returns [Alice, Bob, Charlie]
    List<Integer> ageList = result.middle();     // returns [25, 30, 35]
    List<Boolean> activeList = result.right();   // returns [true, false, true]
  ```
- **See also:** #unzipToCollections(Supplier, Supplier, Supplier)
##### unzipToCollections(...) -> Triple<LC, MC, RC>
- **Signature:** `public <LC extends Collection<A>, MC extends Collection<B>, RC extends Collection<C>> Triple<LC, MC, RC> unzipToCollections( final Supplier<? extends LC> leftSupplier, final Supplier<? extends MC> middleSupplier, final Supplier<? extends RC> rightSupplier) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Unzips all remaining triples in this `TriIterator` into three independently supplied collections.
- **Contract:**
  - Use this overload when the three components should be collected into different collection implementations or when each component needs a separate sizing policy.
  - If source processing or a collection's `add` operation throws, the source and output collections may be partially updated.
  - Usage Examples: Output collections must be distinct instances; aliasing is rejected with IllegalArgumentException before consumption.
  - Callers must also avoid distinct wrappers that share mutable backing storage.
- **Parameters:**
  - `leftSupplier` (`Supplier<? extends LC>`) — a supplier that provides the collection for first components; must return a `non-null` collection
  - `middleSupplier` (`Supplier<? extends MC>`) — a supplier that provides the collection for second components; must return a `non-null` collection
  - `rightSupplier` (`Supplier<? extends RC>`) — a supplier that provides the collection for third components; must return a `non-null` collection
- **Returns:** a `Triple` whose left, middle, and right collections contain all first, second, and third components, respectively
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any of `leftSupplier`, `middleSupplier`, `rightSupplier` is `null`, if any of them returns `null`, or if any two of the three returned collections are the same instance.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  TriIterator<String, Integer, Boolean> iter = TriIterator.zip(
        new String[] { "a", "b" }, new Integer[] { 1, 2 }, new Boolean[] { true, false });
    Triple<Set<String>, List<Integer>, List<Boolean>> result = iter.unzipToCollections(LinkedHashSet::new, ArrayList::new, ArrayList::new);
  ```
- **See also:** #unzipToLists(Supplier), #unzipToSets(Supplier)
##### unzipToSets(...) -> Triple<Set<A>, Set<B>, Set<C>>
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings({ "rawtypes", "unchecked" }) public Triple<Set<A>, Set<B>, Set<C>> unzipToSets(final Supplier<? extends Set> supplier) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Unzips all remaining triples in this `TriIterator` into three `Set`s.
- **Contract:**
  - If source processing or `Set.add` throws, the source and output sets may be partially updated.
  - Prefer #unzipToCollections(Supplier, Supplier, Supplier) when the supplier is anything other than a plain constructor reference such as `LinkedHashSet::new`.
  - Output collections must be distinct instances; aliasing is rejected with IllegalArgumentException before consumption.
  - Callers must also avoid distinct wrappers that share mutable backing storage.
- **Parameters:**
  - `supplier` (`Supplier<? extends Set>`) — a supplier invoked three times to create the left, middle, and right sets; each call must return a `non-null` `Set`
- **Returns:** a `Triple` whose left, middle, and right sets contain the distinct first, second, and third components, respectively
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `supplier` is `null`, if any of the three calls to it returns `null`, or if any two of the three returned sets are the same instance.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String[] names = {"Alice", "Bob", "Alice"};
    Integer[] ages = {25, 30, 25};
    Boolean[] active = {true, false, true};
    Triple<Set<String>, Set<Integer>, Set<Boolean>> result =
        TriIterator.zip(names, ages, active).unzipToSets(LinkedHashSet::new);
    Set<String> nameSet = result.left();       // returns [Alice, Bob] (duplicates removed, insertion order)
    Set<Integer> ageSet = result.middle();     // returns [25, 30]
    Set<Boolean> activeSet = result.right();   // returns [true, false]
  ```
- **See also:** #unzipToCollections(Supplier, Supplier, Supplier)
##### toArray(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings({ "deprecation", "unchecked" }) public Triple<A, B, C>[] toArray()`
- **Summary:** Converts all remaining triples in this TriIterator to an array of Triple objects.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** an array containing all remaining triples from this TriIterator
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String[] names = {"Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"};
    Integer[] ages = {25, 30, 35};
    String[] cities = {"NYC", "LA", "Chicago"};
    Triple<String, Integer, String>[] array = TriIterator.zip(names, ages, cities).toArray();
    for (Triple<String, Integer, String> triple : array) {
        System.out.println(triple.left() + " - " + triple.middle() + " - " + triple.right());
    }
  ```
- **Signature:** `@Deprecated public <T> T[] toArray(final T[] a) throws NullPointerException, ArrayStoreException`
- **Summary:** Converts all remaining triples in this TriIterator to an array of the specified type.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`T[]`) — the array into which the elements of this TriIterator are to be stored, if it is big enough; otherwise, a new array of the same runtime type is allocated for this purpose
- **Returns:** an array containing all remaining triples from this TriIterator
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `a` is `null`; rejected before consuming any elements
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if a remaining triple cannot be stored in the runtime component type of `a`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  String[] names = {"Alice", "Bob"};
    Integer[] ages = {25, 30};
    String[] cities = {"NYC", "LA"};
    @SuppressWarnings("deprecation")
    Object[] arr = TriIterator.zip(names, ages, cities).toArray(new Object[0]); // length is 2
    // arr[0] -> (Alice, 25, NYC), arr[1] -> (Bob, 30, LA)
  ```

- **Summary:** Converts all remaining triples in this TriIterator to a List of Triple objects.

  ```java
    list.forEach(triple ->
        System.out.println(triple.left() + " is " + triple.middle() + " from " + triple.right()));
  ```

### Class Triple (com.landawn.abacus.util.Triple)
A container class that holds three values of potentially different types.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors

  ```java
  Triple<String, Integer, Boolean> triple = new Triple<>();

    triple.setMiddle(42);
    triple.setRight(true);
  ```

  ```java
  Triple<String, Integer, Boolean> triple = Triple.of("text", 42, true);
    Integer newValue = triple.setAndGetMiddle(100);
    // newValue is 100, triple.middle() is also 100
  ```
##### getAndSetRight(...) -> R
- **Signature:** `public R getAndSetRight(final R newRight)`
- **Summary:** Returns the current value of the right element and then updates it with the specified new value.
- **Contract:**
  - This method is useful when you need to retrieve the old value while setting a new one in a single method call.
- **Parameters:**
  - `newRight` (`R`) — the new value to set for the right element, may be `null`.
- **Returns:** the previous value of the right element, may be `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Triple<String, Integer, Boolean> triple = Triple.of("text", 42, true);
    Boolean oldValue = triple.getAndSetRight(false);
    // oldValue is true, triple.right() is now false
  ```
##### setAndGetRight(...) -> R
- **Signature:** `public R setAndGetRight(final R newRight)`
- **Summary:** Sets the right element to the specified new value and then returns the new value.
- **Contract:**
  - This method is useful when you want to set a value and immediately use it in a fluent style or chain of operations.
- **Parameters:**
  - `newRight` (`R`) — the new value to set for the right element, may be `null`.
- **Returns:** the new value of the right element (same as the parameter), may be `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Triple<String, Integer, Boolean> triple = Triple.of("text", 42, true);
    Boolean newValue = triple.setAndGetRight(false);
    // newValue is false, triple.right() is also false
  ```
##### setLeftIf(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public <E extends Exception> boolean setLeftIf(final Throwables.TriPredicate<? super L, ? super M, ? super R, E> predicate, final L newLeft) throws IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Summary:** Conditionally sets the left element to the specified new value.
- **Contract:**
  - If the predicate returns `true`, the left element is updated to `newLeft`; otherwise this triple remains unchanged.
  - If it throws an exception, the left element is not modified and the exception is propagated to the caller.
- **Parameters:**
  - `predicate` (`Throwables.TriPredicate<? super L, ? super M, ? super R, E>`) — a tri-predicate evaluated against the current left, middle and right values; if it returns `true`, the left element is updated
  - `newLeft` (`L`) — the new value to assign to the left element if the predicate passes; may be `null`
- **Returns:** `true` if the left element was updated, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `predicate` is `null`.
  - `E` — if the predicate throws an exception
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Triple<String, Integer, Boolean> triple = Triple.of("old", 42, true);
  
    boolean wasSet = triple.setLeftIf((l, m, r) -> m > 40 && r,
            "new");
    // wasSet == true, triple.left() == "new" because 42 > 40 and true
  
    wasSet = triple.setLeftIf((l, m, r) -> m < 0,
            "another");
    // wasSet == false, triple.left() is still "new" because 42 is not < 0
  ```
##### setMiddleIf(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public <E extends Exception> boolean setMiddleIf(final Throwables.TriPredicate<? super L, ? super M, ? super R, E> predicate, final M newMiddle) throws IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Summary:** Conditionally sets the middle element to the specified new value.
- **Contract:**
  - If the predicate returns `true`, the middle element is updated to `newMiddle`; otherwise this triple remains unchanged.
  - If it throws an exception, the middle element is not modified and the exception is propagated to the caller.
- **Parameters:**
  - `predicate` (`Throwables.TriPredicate<? super L, ? super M, ? super R, E>`) — a tri-predicate evaluated against the current left, middle and right values; if it returns `true`, the middle element is updated
  - `newMiddle` (`M`) — the new value to assign to the middle element if the predicate passes; may be `null`
- **Returns:** `true` if the middle element was updated, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `predicate` is `null`.
  - `E` — if the predicate throws an exception
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Triple<String, Integer, Boolean> triple = Triple.of("text", 42, true);
  
    boolean wasSet = triple.setMiddleIf((l, m, r) -> r && m < 50,
            100);
    // wasSet == true, triple.middle() == 100 because true && 42 < 50
  
    wasSet = triple.setMiddleIf((l, m, r) -> m > 1000,
            200);
    // wasSet == false, triple.middle() is still 100 because 100 is not > 1000
  ```
##### setRightIf(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public <E extends Exception> boolean setRightIf(final Throwables.TriPredicate<? super L, ? super M, ? super R, E> predicate, final R newRight) throws IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Summary:** Conditionally sets the right element to the specified new value.
- **Contract:**
  - If the predicate returns `true`, the right element is updated to `newRight`; otherwise this triple remains unchanged.
  - If it throws an exception, the right element is not modified and the exception is propagated to the caller.
- **Parameters:**
  - `predicate` (`Throwables.TriPredicate<? super L, ? super M, ? super R, E>`) — a tri-predicate evaluated against the current left, middle and right values; if it returns `true`, the right element is updated
  - `newRight` (`R`) — the new value to assign to the right element if the predicate passes; may be `null`
- **Returns:** `true` if the right element was updated, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `predicate` is `null`.
  - `E` — if the predicate throws an exception
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Triple<String, Integer, Boolean> triple = Triple.of("text", 42, true);
  
    boolean wasSet = triple.setRightIf((l, m, r) -> r && m > 40,
            false);
    // wasSet == true, triple.right() == false because true && 42 > 40
  
    wasSet = triple.setRightIf((l, m, r) -> m < 0,
            true);
    // wasSet == false, triple.right() is still false because 42 is not < 0
  ```
##### setIf(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public <E extends Exception> boolean setIf(final Throwables.TriPredicate<? super L, ? super M, ? super R, E> predicate, final L newLeft, final M newMiddle, final R newRight) throws IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Summary:** Conditionally sets all three elements to the specified new values.
- **Contract:**
  - If the predicate returns `true`, all three elements are updated to `newLeft`, `newMiddle` and `newRight` respectively.
  - If the predicate returns `false`, this triple remains unchanged.
  - The update of all three fields is performed sequentially within a single method call; either all three values are changed (when the predicate returns `true`), or none are (when it returns `false`).
  - The predicate is evaluated at most once; if it throws an exception, no element is modified and the exception is propagated to the caller.
- **Parameters:**
  - `predicate` (`Throwables.TriPredicate<? super L, ? super M, ? super R, E>`) — a tri-predicate evaluated against the current left, middle and right values; if it returns `true`, all three elements are updated
  - `newLeft` (`L`) — the new value to assign to the left element if the predicate passes; may be `null`
  - `newMiddle` (`M`) — the new value to assign to the middle element if the predicate passes; may be `null`
  - `newRight` (`R`) — the new value to assign to the right element if the predicate passes; may be `null`
- **Returns:** `true` if all three elements were updated, `false` otherwise
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `predicate` is `null`.
  - `E` — if the predicate throws an exception
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Triple<String, Integer, Boolean> triple = Triple.of("old", 42, true);
  
    boolean wasSet = triple.setIf((l, m, r) -> m < 50 && r,
            "new", 100, false);
    // wasSet == true, triple is now ("new", 100, false)
  
    wasSet = triple.setIf((l, m, r) -> m > 1000,
            "another", 1, true);
    // wasSet == false, triple remains ("new", 100, false)
  ```
##### copy(...) -> Triple<L, M, R>
- **Signature:** `public Triple<L, M, R> copy()`
- **Summary:** Creates and returns a shallow copy of this Triple.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a new Triple instance containing the same elements as this Triple.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Triple<String, Integer, Boolean> original = Triple.of("text", 42, true);
    Triple<String, Integer, Boolean> copy = original.copy();
    // copy contains the same values as original
    // Modifying copy does not affect original
    copy.setLeft("modified");
    // original.left() still returns "text"
  ```
##### toArray(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public Object[] toArray()`
- **Summary:** Converts this Triple into an array containing the three elements in order: left, middle, right.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a new Object array of length 3 containing the left, middle, and right elements.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Triple<String, Integer, Boolean> triple = Triple.of("text", 42, true);
    Object[] array = triple.toArray();
    // array[0] is "text", array[1] is 42, array[2] is true
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <A> A[] toArray(A[] a) throws NullPointerException, ArrayStoreException`
- **Summary:** Converts this Triple into an array of the specified type, storing the three elements in order: left, middle, right.
- **Contract:**
  - If the provided array has a length of at least 3, the elements are stored in it; otherwise, a new array of the same type with length 3 is created and returned.
  - Note: Unlike java.util.Collection#toArray(Object\[\]), this method does not null-terminate the returned array when the supplied array has length > 3; any elements at indices >= 3 are left untouched.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`A[]`) — the array into which the elements are to be stored, if it has length >= 3; otherwise, a new array of the same runtime type is allocated
- **Returns:** an array containing the three elements of this Triple.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if `a` is `null`
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if an element is incompatible with the runtime component type of `a`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Triple<String, String, String> triple = Triple.of("one", "two", "three");
    String[] array = triple.toArray(new String[3]);
    // array[0] is "one", array[1] is "two", array[2] is "three"
  ```
##### forEach(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public <E extends Exception> void forEach(final Throwables.Consumer<? super Object, E> consumer) throws IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Summary:** Applies the given consumer function to each element of this Triple in order: left, middle, then right.
- **Contract:**
  - Because the three elements may have unrelated types, the consumer must accept `Object`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `consumer` (`Throwables.Consumer<? super Object, E>`) — the consumer function to apply to each element; must accept `Object`, since the three elements may have unrelated types; must not be `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `consumer` is `null`.
  - `E` — if the consumer throws an exception.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Triple<String, String, String> triple = Triple.of("one", "two", "three");
    triple.forEach(System.out::println);
    // Prints:
    // one
    // two
    // three
  
    // Element-typed processing goes through accept(TriConsumer):
    Triple<String, Integer, Boolean> mixed = Triple.of("a", 1, true);
    mixed.accept((l, m, r) -> System.out.println(l + m + r));
  ```
- **See also:** #accept(Throwables.TriConsumer)
##### accept(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public <E extends Exception> void accept(final Throwables.TriConsumer<? super L, ? super M, ? super R, E> action) throws IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Summary:** Applies the given tri-consumer action to the three elements of this Triple.
- **Parameters:**
  - `action` (`Throwables.TriConsumer<? super L, ? super M, ? super R, E>`) — the tri-consumer action to apply to the three elements.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `action` is `null`.
  - `E` — if the action throws an exception.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Triple<String, Integer, Boolean> triple = Triple.of("text", 42, true);
    triple.accept((l, m, r) -> {
        System.out.println("Left: " + l);
        System.out.println("Middle: " + m);
        System.out.println("Right: " + r);
    });
  ```
- **Signature:** `public <E extends Exception> void accept(final Throwables.Consumer<? super Triple<L, M, R>, E> action) throws IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Summary:** Applies the given consumer action to this Triple instance as a whole.
- **Parameters:**
  - `action` (`Throwables.Consumer<? super Triple<L, M, R>, E>`) — the consumer action to apply to this Triple.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `action` is `null`.
  - `E` — if the action throws an exception.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Triple<String, Integer, Boolean> triple = Triple.of("text", 42, true);
    triple.accept(t -> {
  ```

- **Signature:** `public <U, E extends Exception> U map(final Throwables.Function<? super Triple<L, M, R>, ? extends U, E> mapper) throws IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Summary:** Applies the given function to this Triple instance as a whole and returns the result.

  - `mapper` (`Throwables.Function<? super Triple<L, M, R>, ? extends U, E>`) — the function to apply to this Triple.

### Class Try (com.landawn.abacus.util.Try)
A utility class that provides enhanced try-with-resources functionality and exception handling mechanisms.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### with(...) -> Try<T>
- **Signature:** `public static <T extends AutoCloseable> Try<T> with(final T targetResource) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new Try instance with the specified AutoCloseable resource.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetResource` (`T`) — the resource to be managed by the Try instance.
- **Returns:** a new Try instance managing the specified target resource.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the targetResource is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Try.with(new ByteArrayInputStream("data".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)))
       .run(stream -> {
           // Process the stream
           byte[] data = stream.readAllBytes();
           System.out.println(new String(data, StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
       });
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <T extends AutoCloseable> Try<T> with(final T targetResource, final Runnable finalAction) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new Try instance with the specified resource and a final action to execute after resource cleanup.
- **Contract:**
  - If resource acquisition itself fails, the final action still runs.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetResource` (`T`) — the resource to be managed by the Try instance.
  - `finalAction` (`Runnable`) — the action to be executed after the resource is closed.
- **Returns:** a new Try instance managing the specified target resource and final action.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if the targetResource is `null`, or if `finalAction` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AtomicBoolean finished = new AtomicBoolean();
    Try.with(new BufferedReader(new StringReader("database row")), () -> finished.set(true))
       .run(reader -> System.out.println(reader.readLine()));
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <T extends AutoCloseable> Try<T> with(final Throwables.Supplier<T, ? extends Exception> targetResourceSupplier) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new Try instance with a supplier that provides the AutoCloseable resource.
- **Contract:**
  - The resource is created lazily when the operation is executed.
  - This is useful when resource creation itself might throw an exception or when you want to delay resource creation until it's actually needed.
  - Usage Examples: When a later operation acquires the resource, a `null` supplier result causes IllegalArgumentException; overloads with a fallback route that acquisition failure to the fallback.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetResourceSupplier` (`Throwables.Supplier<T, ? extends Exception>`) — the supplier that provides the closeable resource; must not be `null`, and must not return `null` when it is invoked
- **Returns:** a new Try instance managing the specified target resource supplier.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetResourceSupplier` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Throwables.Supplier<java.io.StringWriter, Exception> writerSupplier = java.io.StringWriter::new;
    Try.with(writerSupplier)
       .run(writer -> {
           writer.write("Hello, World!");
           writer.flush();
       });
  ```
- **Signature:** `public static <T extends AutoCloseable> Try<T> with(final Throwables.Supplier<T, ? extends Exception> targetResourceSupplier, final Runnable finalAction) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Creates a new Try instance with a resource supplier and a final action.
- **Contract:**
  - The resource is created when needed, and the final action is executed after the resource is closed.
  - If creation fails, the final action still runs.
  - Usage Examples: When a later operation acquires the resource, a `null` supplier result causes IllegalArgumentException; overloads with a fallback route that acquisition failure to the fallback.
- **Parameters:**
  - `targetResourceSupplier` (`Throwables.Supplier<T, ? extends Exception>`) — the supplier that provides the closeable resource; must not be `null`, and must not return `null` when it is invoked
  - `finalAction` (`Runnable`) — the action to be executed after the resource is closed.
- **Returns:** a new Try instance managing the specified target resource supplier and final action.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetResourceSupplier` or `finalAction` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  AtomicBoolean finished = new AtomicBoolean();
    Throwables.Supplier<ByteArrayInputStream, Exception> inputSupplier =
        () -> new ByteArrayInputStream("OK".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
    String response = Try.with(
        inputSupplier,
        () -> finished.set(true)
    ).call(stream -> new String(stream.readAllBytes(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
  ```
##### run(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public static void run(final Throwables.Runnable<? extends Exception> cmd) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes the provided runnable, converting any checked exception to a RuntimeException.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cmd` (`Throwables.Runnable<? extends Exception>`) — the runnable task that might throw an exception.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `cmd` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the operation throws; checked exceptions are converted to unchecked exceptions
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Instead of handling InterruptedException
    Try.run(() -> Thread.sleep(1000));
  
    // Working with I/O operations
    Path path = Path.of("output.txt");
    byte[] data = "content".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    Try.run(() -> Files.write(path, data));
  ```
- **See also:** Throwables#run(Throwables.Runnable)
- **Signature:** `public static void run(final Throwables.Runnable<? extends Exception> cmd, final Consumer<? super Exception> actionOnError) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes the provided runnable and handles any exception with the specified error handler.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cmd` (`Throwables.Runnable<? extends Exception>`) — the runnable task that might throw an exception.
  - `actionOnError` (`Consumer<? super Exception>`) — the consumer to handle any exceptions thrown by the `cmd`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any of `cmd`, `actionOnError` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if `actionOnError` throws a runtime exception while handling an exception from `cmd`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Try.run(
        () -> { throw new IOException("mail server unavailable"); },
        ex -> System.err.println("Failed to send email: " + ex.getMessage())
    );
  
    // With recovery logic
    AtomicBoolean fallbackUsed = new AtomicBoolean();
    Try.run(
        () -> { throw new IOException("primary service unavailable"); },
        ex -> fallbackUsed.set(true)
    );
  ```
- **See also:** Throwables#run(Throwables.Runnable, Consumer)
##### call(...) -> R
- **Signature:** `public static <R> R call(final java.util.concurrent.Callable<? extends R> cmd) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes the provided callable and returns its result, converting any checked exception to a RuntimeException.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cmd` (`java.util.concurrent.Callable<? extends R>`) — the callable task that might throw an exception and returns a result.
- **Returns:** the result of the `cmd`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `cmd` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the operation throws; checked exceptions are converted to unchecked exceptions
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Read file content without explicit exception handling
    String content = Try.call(() -> Files.readString(Path.of("config.txt")));
  
    // Parse a value without a checked-exception declaration at the call site
  ```

- **Signature:** `public static <R> R call(final java.util.concurrent.Callable<? extends R> cmd, final Function<? super Exception, ? extends R> actionOnError) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes the provided callable and returns its result, or applies the error function if an exception occurs.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cmd` (`java.util.concurrent.Callable<? extends R>`) — the callable task that might throw an exception and returns a result.
  - `actionOnError` (`Function<? super Exception, ? extends R>`) — the function to apply to the exception if one is thrown by the `cmd`.
- **Returns:** the result of the `cmd` or the result of applying the `actionOnError` function to the exception if one is thrown.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any of `cmd`, `actionOnError` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if `actionOnError` throws a runtime exception while handling an exception from `cmd`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Return null on error
    String user = Try.call(
        () -> { throw new IOException("user service unavailable"); },
        ex -> null
    );
  
    // Transform exception to error response
    String response = Try.call(
        () -> { throw new IOException("request failed"); },
        ex -> "error: " + ex.getMessage()
    );
  ```
- **See also:** Throwables#call(Throwables.Callable, Function)
- **Signature:** `public static <R> R call(final java.util.concurrent.Callable<? extends R> cmd, final Supplier<R> supplier) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes the provided callable and returns its result, or returns the value from the supplier if an exception occurs.
- **Contract:**
  - This method allows for lazy evaluation of the fallback value, which is only computed if an exception actually occurs.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cmd` (`java.util.concurrent.Callable<? extends R>`) — the callable task that might throw an exception and returns a result.
  - `supplier` (`Supplier<R>`) — the supplier to provide a return value when an exception occurs.
- **Returns:** the result of the `cmd` or the result of the `supplier` if an exception occurs.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any of `cmd`, `supplier` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the fallback supplier throws after a failure
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Lazy default value computation
    java.util.Properties config = Try.call(
        () -> { java.util.Properties p = new java.util.Properties(); p.load(new StringReader("mode=safe")); return p; },
        (java.util.function.Supplier<java.util.Properties>) java.util.Properties::new   // cast required: a
            // no-arg constructor reference fits both the Supplier and the Function overload
    );
  
    // With expensive fallback
    byte[] cachedData = Try.call(
        () -> Files.readAllBytes(Path.of("cache.bin")),
        () -> new byte[0]
    );
  ```
- **See also:** Throwables#call(Throwables.Callable, Supplier)
- **Signature:** `public static <R> R call(final java.util.concurrent.Callable<? extends R> cmd, final R defaultValue) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Executes the provided callable and returns its result, or returns the default value if an exception occurs.
- **Contract:**
  - This is the simplest form of exception handling with a fallback value, useful when you have a known default that should be used when the callable throws an exception.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cmd` (`java.util.concurrent.Callable<? extends R>`) — the callable task that might throw an exception and returns a result.
  - `defaultValue` (`R`) — the default value to return if an exception occurs during the execution of the `cmd`, may be `null`.
- **Returns:** the result of the `cmd` or the default value if an exception occurs.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `cmd` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Parse with default
    String userInput = "not a number";
    int value = Try.call(() -> Integer.parseInt(userInput), 0);
  
    // A missing property returns null normally, so the exception fallback is not used.
    java.util.Properties properties = new java.util.Properties();
    String setting = Try.call(
        () -> properties.getProperty("advanced.setting"),
        "default-value"
    );
  ```
- **See also:** #call(java.util.concurrent.Callable, Supplier)
- **Signature:** `public static <R> R call(final java.util.concurrent.Callable<? extends R> cmd, final Predicate<? super Exception> predicate, final Supplier<R> supplier) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes the callable with conditional exception handling based on a predicate.
- **Contract:**
  - If an exception occurs and the predicate returns `true`, the supplier provides the return value.
  - If the predicate returns `false`, the exception is rethrown as a RuntimeException.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cmd` (`java.util.concurrent.Callable<? extends R>`) — the callable task that might throw an exception.
  - `predicate` (`Predicate<? super Exception>`) — the predicate to test the exception.
  - `supplier` (`Supplier<R>`) — the supplier to provide a return value when an exception occurs and the `predicate` returns `true`.
- **Returns:** the result of the `cmd` or the result of the `supplier` if an exception occurs and the `predicate` returns `true`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any of `cmd`, `predicate`, `supplier` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the fallback supplier throws after a failure, or if the predicate throws or rejects the caught exception
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Only handle specific exceptions
    String result = Try.call(
        () -> { throw new IOException("read failed"); },
        ex -> ex instanceof IOException,
        () -> "default for IO errors"
    );
  
    // Supply a fallback on timeout
    String data = Try.call(
        () -> { throw new TimeoutException("timed out"); },
        ex -> ex instanceof TimeoutException,
        () -> "timeout fallback"
    );
  ```
- **See also:** Throwables#call(Throwables.Callable, Predicate, Supplier)
- **Signature:** `public static <R> R call(final java.util.concurrent.Callable<? extends R> cmd, final Predicate<? super Exception> predicate, final R defaultValue) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes the callable with conditional exception handling and a default value.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cmd` (`java.util.concurrent.Callable<? extends R>`) — the callable task that might throw an exception and returns a result.
  - `predicate` (`Predicate<? super Exception>`) — the predicate to test the exception. If it returns `true`, the default value is returned. If it returns `false`, the exception is rethrown.
  - `defaultValue` (`R`) — the default value to return if an exception occurs during the execution of the `cmd` and the `predicate` returns `true`.
- **Returns:** the result of the `cmd` or the default value if an exception occurs and the `predicate` returns `true`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any of `cmd`, `predicate` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the predicate throws or rejects the caught exception
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Return -1 only for NumberFormatException
    String input = "not a number";
    int value = Try.call(
        () -> Integer.parseInt(input),
        ex -> ex instanceof NumberFormatException,
        -1
    );
  
    // Return null only for specific database errors
    String user = Try.call(
        () -> { throw new SQLException("Connection timeout"); },
        ex -> ex.getMessage().contains("Connection timeout"),
        (String) null
    );
  ```
- **See also:** #call(java.util.concurrent.Callable, Predicate, Supplier)

##### run(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public void run(final Throwables.Consumer<? super T, ? extends Exception> cmd) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes the provided consumer with the managed resource.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cmd` (`Throwables.Consumer<? super T, ? extends Exception>`) — the consumer that operates on the managed resource; must not be `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `cmd` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if resource acquisition, the operation, or resource closing throws; checked exceptions are converted to unchecked exceptions, or if the configured final action throws after otherwise successful or recovered execution
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Try.with(new BufferedReader(new StringReader("first line\nsecond line")))
       .run(reader -> {
           String line;
           while ((line = reader.readLine()) != null) {
               System.out.println(line);
           }
       });
  ```
- **Signature:** `public void run(final Throwables.Consumer<? super T, ? extends Exception> cmd, final Consumer<? super Exception> actionOnError) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Executes the provided consumer with the managed resource and custom exception handling.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cmd` (`Throwables.Consumer<? super T, ? extends Exception>`) — the consumer that operates on the managed resource; must not be `null`.
  - `actionOnError` (`Consumer<? super Exception>`) — the error handler invoked with any exception thrown while creating the resource, executing the `cmd`, or closing the resource; must not be `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any of `cmd`, `actionOnError` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the error handler throws while handling an acquisition, operation, or close failure, or if the configured final action throws after otherwise successful or recovered execution
- **Examples:**
  ```java

    Try.with(new java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream())
       .run(

           ex -> System.err.println("Failed to write data: " + ex.getMessage())
       );
  ```

- **Throws:**

- **Examples:**

### Class Tuple (com.landawn.abacus.util.Tuple)
A comprehensive utility class for creating and managing structurally immutable, fixed-size tuples that can contain between 0 and 9 elements of potentially different types.

**Thread-safety:** conditional
**Nullability:** unspecified
**Annotations:** @Immutable
**Permitted subtypes:** Tuple0, Tuple1, Tuple2, Tuple3, Tuple4, Tuple5, Tuple6, Tuple7, Tuple8, Tuple9

  - `_7` (`T7`) — the seventh element to be contained in the tuple.
  - `_8` (`T8`) — the eighth element to be contained in the tuple.
  - `_9` (`T9`) — the ninth element to be contained in the tuple.

  ```java

    @SuppressWarnings("deprecation")

        Tuple.of("John", "Doe", 35, "john@example.com", "555-1234",
                 "123 Main St", "Apt 4B", "Boston", "MA");
  
    // Better approach - use a record or class:
    record ContactInfo(

        String email, String phone, String street,
        String apartment, String city, String state

  ```

##### fromArray(...) -> Tuple<?>


#### Public Instance Methods
##### arity(...) -> int
- **Signature:** `public abstract int arity()`
- **Summary:** Returns the number of elements in this tuple.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the arity (size) of this tuple, which is the count of elements it contains.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Tuple3<String, Integer, Boolean> t = Tuple.of("a", 1, true);
    int size = t.arity();   // returns 3
  ```
##### anyNull(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public abstract boolean anyNull()`
- **Summary:** Checks if any element in this tuple is `null`.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** `true` if at least one element in this tuple is `null`, `false` if all elements are `non-null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Tuple3<String, Integer, Boolean> t1 = Tuple.of("a", null, true);
    boolean hasNull = t1.anyNull();   // returns true
  
    Tuple3<String, Integer, Boolean> t2 = Tuple.of("a", 1, true);
    boolean hasNull2 = t2.anyNull();   // returns false
  ```
##### allNull(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public abstract boolean allNull()`
- **Summary:** Checks if all elements in this tuple are `null`.
- **Contract:**
  - This method performs a logical AND operation across all elements, returning `true` only if every element is `null`.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** `true` if every element in this tuple is `null`, `false` if at least one element is `non-null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Tuple3<String, Integer, Boolean> t1 = Tuple.of(null, null, null);
    boolean allNull = t1.allNull();   // returns true
  
    Tuple3<String, Integer, Boolean> t2 = Tuple.of("a", null, null);
    boolean allNull2 = t2.allNull();   // returns false
  ```
##### contains(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `public abstract boolean contains(final Object valueToFind)`
- **Summary:** Checks if this tuple contains the specified value.
- **Parameters:**
  - `valueToFind` (`Object`) — the value to search for in this tuple, may be `null`.
- **Returns:** `true` if this tuple contains an element equal to the specified value, `false` otherwise.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Tuple3<String, Integer, Boolean> t = Tuple.of("hello", 42, true);
    boolean found1 = t.contains(42);        // returns true
    boolean found2 = t.contains("world");   // returns false
    boolean found3 = t.contains(null);      // returns false
  ```
##### toArray(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public abstract Object[] toArray()`
- **Summary:** Returns an array containing all elements of this tuple in their positional order.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** an Object array containing all tuple elements in order; non-empty tuples return a new array, while the arity-0 tuple returns a shared empty array
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Tuple3<String, Integer, Boolean> t = Tuple.of("a", 1, true);
    Object[] array = t.toArray();   // returns ["a", 1, true]
  ```
- **Signature:** `public abstract <A> A[] toArray(A[] a) throws NullPointerException, ArrayStoreException`
- **Summary:** Returns an array containing all elements of this tuple, using the specified array type.
- **Contract:**
  - If the provided array is large enough to hold all elements, it is used directly to store the tuple elements at positions `0..arity()-1`; any positions beyond the tuple's elements are left unchanged.
- **Parameters:**
  - `a` (`A[]`) — the array into which the elements of this tuple are to be stored, if it is big enough; otherwise, a new array of the same runtime type is allocated for this purpose.
- **Returns:** an array containing all elements of this tuple.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if the specified array is `null`.
  - `java.lang.ArrayStoreException` — if the runtime type of the specified array is not a supertype of the runtime type of every element in this tuple.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Tuple2<String, String> t = Tuple.of("hello", "world");
    String[] array = t.toArray(new String[0]);   // returns a new String[2]: ["hello", "world"]
  
    // Using pre-sized array
    String[] existing = new String[5];
    String[] result = t.toArray(existing);   // Uses existing array, fills indexes 0..1
  ```
- **See also:** #toArray()
##### forEach(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `public abstract <E extends Exception> void forEach(Throwables.Consumer<? super Object, E> consumer) throws IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Summary:** Performs the given action for each element of this tuple in order.
- **Contract:**
  - Because tuple positions may have unrelated types, the consumer must accept `Object`.
- **Parameters:**
  - `consumer` (`Throwables.Consumer<? super Object, E>`) — the action to be performed for each element; must accept `Object`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `consumer` is `null`.
  - `E` — if the consumer throws an exception.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Tuple3<String, Integer, Boolean> t = Tuple.of("hello", 42, true);
    t.forEach(System.out::println);   // Prints each element on a new line
  
    // Collecting elements
    List<Object> list = new ArrayList<>();
    t.forEach(list::add);
  ```
##### accept(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("unchecked") public <E extends Exception> void accept(final Throwables.Consumer<? super TP, E> action) throws IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Summary:** Performs the given action on this tuple as a whole.
- **Parameters:**
  - `action` (`Throwables.Consumer<? super TP, E>`) — the action to be performed on this tuple.
- **Throws:**

  - `E` — if the action throws an exception.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Tuple2<String, Integer> t = Tuple.of("age", 25);
    t.accept(tuple -> System.out.println(tuple._1 + ": " + tuple._2));
    // Prints: "age: 25"
  ```

- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("unchecked") public <R, E extends Exception> R map(final Throwables.Function<? super TP, ? extends R, E> mapper) throws IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Summary:** Applies the given mapping function to this tuple and returns the result.
- **Parameters:**
  - `mapper` (`Throwables.Function<? super TP, ? extends R, E>`) — the mapping function to apply to this tuple.
- **Returns:** the result of applying the mapping function to this tuple.
- **Throws:**

  - `E` — if the mapper throws an exception.
- **Examples:**
  ```java

  ```

- **Annotations:** @Beta
- **Summary:** Returns an Optional containing this tuple if it matches the given predicate, otherwise returns an empty Optional.
- **Parameters:**
  - `predicate` (`Throwables.Predicate<? super TP, E>`) — the predicate to test this tuple against.
- **Returns:** an Optional containing this tuple if the predicate returns `true`, otherwise an empty Optional.

  - `E` — if the predicate throws an exception.
- **Examples:**

  ```java
    // Returns Optional containing the tuple

    // Returns empty Optional
  ```

  ```java
        Tuple.of("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "H", "I");
  
    // Using a smaller array - new array created
    String[] small = new String[5];
    String[] result1 = t.toArray(small);   // new String[9] array created
  
    // Using exact size array
    String[] exact = new String[9];
    String[] result2 = t.toArray(exact);   // same array returned
  ```

### Class TypeAttrParser (com.landawn.abacus.util.TypeAttrParser)
A parser for type attribute strings that extracts class names, generic type parameters, and constructor parameters from complex type declarations.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
##### parse(...) -> TypeAttrParser
- **Signature:** `public static TypeAttrParser parse(final String attr) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Parses a type attribute string into its component parts: class name, generic type parameters, and constructor parameters.
- **Parameters:**
  - `attr` (`String`) — the type attribute string to parse
- **Returns:** a `TypeAttrParser` instance containing the parsed components; the returned instance never has `null` type-parameter or constructor-parameter arrays
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `attr` is `null`, or if the class name (ignoring any trailing array brackets) or a generic parameter at any nesting level is empty, if generic angle brackets, constructor parentheses, or quoted constructor arguments are missing, unbalanced, out of order, or otherwise malformed, or if the declaration needs more than 64 levels of recursive parsing. That limit counts parsing levels rather than textual nesting levels: a generic nesting level costs one level and so does an array suffix, while a parameterized qualified-member segment costs two (its owner arguments are validated, then the normalized name is re-parsed). A declaration that repeats one of the two-level shapes, `A<...>\[\]` or `Owner<...>.Member`, is therefore rejected beyond 32 textual levels. Array dimensions on their own, such as `int\[\]\[\]\[\]` or `int\[\] \[\] \[\]`, do not recurse per dimension and are not limited by this nesting limit.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Simple class
    TypeAttrParser p1 = TypeAttrParser.parse("String");
  
    // Generic type
    TypeAttrParser p2 = TypeAttrParser.parse("List<String>");
  
    // Nested generics
    TypeAttrParser p3 = TypeAttrParser.parse("Map<String, List<Integer>>");
  
    // With constructor parameters
    TypeAttrParser p4 = TypeAttrParser.parse("HashMap<K, V>(16, 0.75f)");
  ```
- **See also:** #getClassName(), #getTypeParameters(), #getParameters()
##### newInstance(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `@SuppressWarnings("unchecked") public static <T> T newInstance(Class<T> cls, final String attr, final Object... args) throws IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Summary:** Reflectively creates a new instance described by the type attribute plus explicit constructor arguments.
- **Contract:**
  - If no exact match exists and `attr` contains any constructor parameters, a fallback tries replacing those parameters with a single `String\[\]` parameter.
- **Parameters:**
  - `cls` (`Class<T>`) — the target class to instantiate, or `null` to derive it from the class name in `attr`
  - `attr` (`String`) — the type attribute string with optional generics and constructor params
  - `args` (`Object[]`) — alternating `(Class, value)` pairs prepended to the parsed parameters; must have an even length, with every even-indexed element being a `Class`
- **Returns:** a new instance of the specified class
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `args` or `attr` is `null`, `attr` has malformed type syntax, `args` has an odd length or an even-indexed element that is not a `Class`, or no matching constructor is found
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if the class cannot be resolved or instantiation fails
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Select StringBuilder(CharSequence) with one explicit (Class, value) pair.
    StringBuilder builder = TypeAttrParser.newInstance(
        StringBuilder.class, "StringBuilder", CharSequence.class, "initial text");
  ```
- **See also:** #parse(String)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### getClassName(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `public String getClassName()`
- **Summary:** Returns the parsed class name without generic type parameters or constructor arguments.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the class name portion of the parsed type attribute
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  TypeAttrParser parser = TypeAttrParser.parse("ArrayList<String>(10)");
    String name = parser.getClassName();   // returns "ArrayList"
  ```
##### getTypeParameters(...) -> String\[\]
- **Signature:** `public String[] getTypeParameters()`
- **Summary:** Returns a copy of the parsed generic type parameters as an array of strings.
- **Contract:**
  - Returns an empty array if no type parameters were present.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** an array of generic type parameter strings, never null
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  TypeAttrParser parser = TypeAttrParser.parse("Map<String, List<Integer>>");
    String[] types = parser.getTypeParameters();   // returns ["String", "List<Integer>"]
  ```
##### getParameters(...) -> String\[\]
- **Signature:** `public String[] getParameters()`
- **Summary:** Returns a copy of the parsed constructor parameters as an array of strings.
- **Contract:**
  - Returns an empty array if no constructor parameters were present.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** an array of constructor parameter strings, never null
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  TypeAttrParser parser = TypeAttrParser.parse("StringBuilder(100)");
    String[] params = parser.getParameters();   // returns ["100"]
  
    parser = TypeAttrParser.parse("HashMap(16, 0.75f)");
    params = parser.getParameters();   // returns ["16", "0.75f"]
  ```
##### toString(...) -> String
- **Signature:** `@Override public String toString()`
- **Summary:** Returns a string representation of this parser instance showing all parsed components.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** a string representation of the parsed components
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  TypeAttrParser parser = TypeAttrParser.parse("HashMap<K, V>(16, 0.75f)");
    System.out.println(parser);
    // Output: {className=HashMap, typeParameters=[K, V], parameters=[16, 0.75f]}
  ```

### Class TypeReference (com.landawn.abacus.util.TypeReference)
A utility class for capturing and representing generic type information at runtime.

**Thread-safety:** unspecified
**Nullability:** unspecified

#### Public Constructors
- (none)

#### Public Static Methods
- (none)

#### Public Instance Methods
##### javaType(...) -> java.lang.reflect.Type
- **Signature:** `public java.lang.reflect.Type javaType()`
- **Summary:** Returns the raw java.lang.reflect.Type instance representing the captured generic type.
- **Contract:**
  - This raw Type representation is particularly useful when working with reflection-based frameworks, serialization libraries, or any code that needs to introspect generic types at runtime.
  - `TypeReference` is primarily a bridge to Java's reflection type system, and callers typically use this accessor when they need the original java.lang.reflect.Type captured from the anonymous subclass.
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the raw java.lang.reflect.Type instance representing the generic type T; never `null` (validated during construction).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Capture complex nested generic type
    TypeReference<List<Map<String, Integer>>> complexType =
        new TypeReference<List<Map<String, Integer>>>() {};
  
    java.lang.reflect.Type type = complexType.javaType();
  
    // Inspect the type structure
    if (type instanceof ParameterizedType) {
        ParameterizedType pt = (ParameterizedType) type;
        System.out.println("Raw type: " + pt.getRawType());
        System.out.println("Type arguments: " + Arrays.toString(pt.getActualTypeArguments()));
    }
  ```
- **See also:** #type(), ParameterizedType
##### reflectType(...) -> java.lang.reflect.Type
- **Signature:** `public java.lang.reflect.Type reflectType()`
- **Summary:** Returns the captured java.lang.reflect.Type - an exact alias of #javaType().
- **Parameters:**
  - (none)
- **Returns:** the raw java.lang.reflect.Type instance representing the generic type T; never `null` (validated during construction).
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  TypeReference<List<String>> ref = new TypeReference<List<String>>() {};
  
    ref.reflectType();         // java.util.List<java.lang.String>   (a ParameterizedType)
    ref.type().javaType();     // interface java.util.List           (the raw Class - a different meaning!)
    ref.type().reflectType();  // interface java.util.List           (also raw - NOT the captured type)
  ```

##### encode(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public static String encode(final Object parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, ClassCastException`
- **Summary:** Encodes the provided parameters into a URL-encoded query string using UTF-8.
- **Contract:**
  - This method accepts various parameter formats: `Map<String,?>`: non-null String keys and their values are encoded as name=value pairs JavaBean: Bean properties are encoded with their original names (NamingPolicy#NO_CHANGE) `Object\[\]`: pairs of non-null String names and arbitrary values (must have even length) `CharSequence`: if it contains `'='` it is taken to be an ALREADY-ENCODED query string and is appended verbatim (nothing is escaped, and duplicate names are preserved); otherwise it is encoded as a single form field.
- **Parameters:**
  - `parameters` (`Object`) — the parameters to encode (Map, bean, Object array pairs, String, or any other value); may be `null`. A `CharSequence` containing `'='` is treated as an already URL-encoded query string and appended verbatim; one without `'='` is encoded as a single form field. Any other value - including a primitive array and a `Collection` - is converted with N#stringOf(Object) and encoded as a single valueless form field; it is NOT split into name/value pairs.
- **Returns:** a URL-encoded query string (e.g., "name=John+Doe&age=30"); returns empty string if `parameters` is `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a Map key or `Object\[\]` name element is `null`, an `Object\[\]` has odd length, an effective name is empty and its value is null, or text to encode contains malformed UTF-16
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a non-null Map key or `Object\[\]` name element is not a String
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Object> params = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    params.put("name", "John Doe");
    params.put("age", 30);
    String query = URLEncodedUtil.encode(params);
    // query: "name=John+Doe&age=30"
  ```
- **See also:** #encode(Object, Charset), #encode(Object, Charset, NamingPolicy), URLEncoder#encode(String, Charset)
- **Signature:** `public static String encode(final Object parameters, final Charset charset) throws IllegalArgumentException, ClassCastException`

- **Parameters:**
  - `parameters` (`Object`) — the parameters to encode (Map, bean, Object array pairs, String, or any other value); may be `null`. A `CharSequence` containing `'='` is treated as an already URL-encoded query string and appended verbatim; one without `'='` is encoded as a single form field. Any other value - including a primitive array and a `Collection` - is converted with N#stringOf(Object) and encoded as a single valueless form field; it is NOT split into name/value pairs.
  - `charset` (`Charset`) — the charset to use for percent-encoding; if `null`, defaults to UTF-8.

- **Signature:** `public static String encode(final Object parameters, final Charset charset, final NamingPolicy namingPolicy) throws IllegalArgumentException, ClassCastException`

- **Contract:**
  - This method accepts various parameter formats: `Map<String,?>`: non-null String keys and arbitrary values are encoded as name=value pairs (keys transformed by naming policy) JavaBean: Bean properties are encoded with names transformed according to the naming policy `Object\[\]`: pairs of non-null String names and arbitrary values (must have even length; names transformed by naming policy) `CharSequence`: if it contains `'='` it is taken to be an ALREADY-ENCODED query string and is appended verbatim (nothing is escaped, and duplicate names are preserved); otherwise it is encoded as a single form field.
- **Parameters:**
  - `parameters` (`Object`) — the parameters to encode (Map, bean, Object array pairs, String, or any other value); may be `null`. A `CharSequence` containing `'='` is treated as an already URL-encoded query string and appended verbatim; one without `'='` is encoded as a single form field. Any other value - including a primitive array and a `Collection` - is converted with N#stringOf(Object) and encoded as a single valueless form field; it is NOT split into name/value pairs.
  - `charset` (`Charset`) — the charset to use for percent-encoding; if `null`, defaults to UTF-8.
  - `namingPolicy` (`NamingPolicy`) — the naming policy to transform property/key names (e.g., CAMEL_CASE, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE); if `null` or NO_CHANGE, names are not transformed.
- **Returns:** a URL-encoded query string; returns empty string if `parameters` is `null`.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a Map key or `Object\[\]` name element is `null`, an `Object\[\]` has odd length, an effective name is empty and its value is null, or text to encode contains malformed UTF-16 or a character that `charset` cannot represent
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a non-null Map key or `Object\[\]` name element is not a String
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Object> user = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    user.put("firstName", "John");
    user.put("userAge", 30);
    String query = URLEncodedUtil.encode(user, StandardCharsets.UTF_8, NamingPolicy.SNAKE_CASE);
    // query: "first_name=John&user_age=30"
  ```
- **See also:** #encode(Object, Charset)
- **Signature:** `public static String encode(final String url, final Object parameters) throws IllegalArgumentException, ClassCastException`
- **Summary:** Encodes parameters and appends them to a URL as a query string using UTF-8.
- **Contract:**
  - If the URL already contains a '?' the encoded parameters are joined with &.
  - If `parameters` is a `CharSequence` containing `'='`, it is treated as an already URL-encoded query string and appended verbatim (duplicate parameter names are preserved).
  - If `parameters` is `null`, an empty Map, an empty CharSequence, an empty Object array, or an object whose encodable fields are all omitted (for example, an all-null bean), the original URL is returned unchanged.
- **Parameters:**
  - `url` (`String`) — the base URL to which the query string will be appended (e.g., "http://example.com/path").
  - `parameters` (`Object`) — the parameters to encode and append (Map, bean, Object array pairs, String, or any other value); may be `null`. Any other value - including a primitive array and a `Collection` - is converted with N#stringOf(Object) and encoded as a single valueless form field; it is NOT split into name/value pairs. An empty `Collection` or empty primitive array is therefore not one of the empty cases below - it encodes as the text `\[\]`.
- **Returns:** the URL with the encoded query string appended (e.g., "http://example.com/path?name=value"); returns the original URL if `parameters` is `null`, an empty `Map`, an empty `CharSequence`, an empty `Object\[\]`, or otherwise produces no encoded fields.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `url`, a Map key, or an `Object\[\]` name element is `null`; if an `Object\[\]` has odd length; if an effective name is empty and its value is `null`; or if text to encode contains malformed UTF-16.
  - `java.lang.ClassCastException` — if a non-null Map key or `Object\[\]` name element is not a String
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, Object> params = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    params.put("q", "java url encoding");
    params.put("page", 1);
    String fullUrl = URLEncodedUtil.encode("http://search.example.com", params);
    // fullUrl: "http://search.example.com?q=java+url+encoding&page=1"
  ```
- **See also:** #encode(String, Object, Charset), #encode(Object)

  - `charset` (`Charset`) — the charset to use for percent-encoding; if `null`, defaults to UTF-8.
  - `namingPolicy` (`NamingPolicy`) — the naming policy to transform property/key names (e.g., CAMEL_CASE, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE); if `null` or NO_CHANGE, names are not transformed.


##### decode(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `public static Map<String, String> decode(final String urlQuery) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Decodes a URL-encoded query string into a `Map<String, String>` using UTF-8.
- **Contract:**
  - If a parameter appears multiple times, only the last occurrence is retained (use #decodeToMultimap(String) to preserve all values).
  - Decoding is strict: a percent escape must contain two ASCII hexadecimal digits, and each contiguous run of encoded bytes must be valid UTF-8.
- **Parameters:**
  - `urlQuery` (`String`) — the URL query string to decode (e.g., "key1=value1&key2=value2"), may be `null` or empty.
- **Returns:** a `LinkedHashMap` containing parameter names as keys and decoded parameter values as values; returns an empty map if `urlQuery` is `null` or empty. A token without `'='` is stored with a `null` value.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a percent escape or its UTF-8 byte sequence is malformed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, String> params = URLEncodedUtil.decode("name=John+Doe&age=30");
    // params: {name=John Doe, age=30}
  ```
- **See also:** #decode(String, Charset), #decodeToMultimap(String), URLDecoder#decode(String, String)
- **Signature:** `public static Map<String, String> decode(final String urlQuery, final Charset charset) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Decodes a URL-encoded query string into a `Map<String, String>` using the specified charset.
- **Contract:**
  - If a parameter appears multiple times, only the last occurrence is retained.
  - Decoding is strict: percent escapes accept ASCII hexadecimal digits only, and encoded bytes must be valid in the selected charset.
- **Parameters:**
  - `urlQuery` (`String`) — the URL query string to decode, may be `null` or empty.
  - `charset` (`Charset`) — the charset to use for decoding percent-encoded characters; if `null`, defaults to UTF-8.
- **Returns:** a `LinkedHashMap` containing parameter names as keys and decoded parameter values as values; returns an empty map if `urlQuery` is `null` or empty. A token without `'='` is stored with a `null` value.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a percent escape or its encoded byte sequence is malformed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, String> params = URLEncodedUtil.decode("name=%E4%B8%AD%E6%96%87", StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    // params: {name=中文}
  ```
- **See also:** #decode(String), #decode(String, Charset, Supplier), URLDecoder#decode(String, Charset)
- **Signature:** `public static <M extends Map<String, String>> M decode(final String urlQuery, final Charset charset, final Supplier<M> mapSupplier) throws IllegalArgumentException, NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Decodes a URL-encoded query string into a custom `Map` implementation using the specified charset and map supplier.
- **Contract:**
  - If a parameter appears multiple times, only the last occurrence is retained.
- **Parameters:**
  - `urlQuery` (`String`) — the URL query string to decode, may be `null` or empty.
  - `charset` (`Charset`) — the charset to use for decoding percent-encoded characters; if `null`, defaults to UTF-8.
  - `mapSupplier` (`Supplier<M>`) — a supplier that provides an instance of the desired Map implementation; must not be `null` and must not return `null`.
- **Returns:** a Map of type M containing parameter names as keys and decoded parameter values as values; returns an empty map (from supplier) if `urlQuery` is `null` or empty. A token without `'='` is stored with a `null` value, so the supplied `Map` must tolerate `null` values.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapSupplier` is `null` or returns `null`, or if a percent escape or its encoded byte sequence is malformed
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if the `Map` returned by `mapSupplier` does not permit `null` values (for example `Hashtable` or `ConcurrentHashMap`) and `urlQuery` contains a token without `'='`; use a `null`-tolerant `Map` or #decodeToMultimap(String) instead
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  TreeMap<String, String> params = URLEncodedUtil.decode("b=2&a=1", StandardCharsets.UTF_8, TreeMap::new);
    // params: {a=1, b=2} (sorted by key)
  ```
- **See also:** #decode(String, Charset)
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T decode(final String urlQuery, final Class<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException, NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Decodes a URL-encoded query string into a bean or Map of the specified type using UTF-8.
- **Parameters:**
  - `urlQuery` (`String`) — the URL query string to decode, may be `null` or empty.
  - `targetType` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the class of the bean or Map to create and populate; must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** an instance of type T populated with the decoded parameter values; returns an empty instance if `urlQuery` is `null` or empty.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetType` is `null`, neither a `Map` type nor a supported bean class, a `Map` type for which no assignable mutable instance can be created (for example ImmutableMap, ImmutableSortedMap, ImmutableNavigableMap or java.util.EnumMap), a percent escape or its UTF-8 byte sequence is malformed, or conversion fails
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if the `Map` created for `targetType` does not permit `null` values (for example `Hashtable`, `ConcurrentHashMap` or `ConcurrentSkipListMap`, which `ConcurrentMap.class` and `ConcurrentNavigableMap.class` also resolve to) and `urlQuery` contains a token without `'='`; use a `null`-tolerant `Map` or #decodeToMultimap(String) instead
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Given a public User JavaBean with a no-arg constructor and name/age accessors:
    User user = URLEncodedUtil.decode("name=John&age=30", User.class);
    // user.getName() returns "John" and user.getAge() returns 30
  ```
- **See also:** #decode(String, Charset, Class)
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T decode(final String urlQuery, final Charset charset, final Class<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException, NullPointerException`
- **Summary:** Decodes a URL-encoded query string into a bean or Map of the specified type using the specified charset.
- **Contract:**
  - If `targetType` is a Map class, this method delegates to #decode(String, Charset, Supplier).
- **Parameters:**
  - `urlQuery` (`String`) — the URL query string to decode, may be `null` or empty.
  - `charset` (`Charset`) — the charset to use for decoding percent-encoded characters; if `null`, defaults to UTF-8.
  - `targetType` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the class of the bean or Map to create and populate; must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** an instance of type T populated with the decoded parameter values; returns an empty instance if `urlQuery` is `null` or empty.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetType` is `null`, neither a `Map` type nor a supported bean class, a `Map` type for which no assignable mutable instance can be created (for example ImmutableMap, ImmutableSortedMap, ImmutableNavigableMap or java.util.EnumMap), a percent escape or its encoded byte sequence is malformed, or conversion fails
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if the `Map` created for `targetType` does not permit `null` values (for example `Hashtable`, `ConcurrentHashMap` or `ConcurrentSkipListMap`, which `ConcurrentMap.class` and `ConcurrentNavigableMap.class` also resolve to) and `urlQuery` contains a token without `'='`; use a `null`-tolerant `Map` or #decodeToMultimap(String) instead
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  // Given a public Product JavaBean with a no-arg constructor and name/price accessors:
    Product p = URLEncodedUtil.decode("name=Laptop&price=999.99", StandardCharsets.UTF_8, Product.class);
    // p.getName() returns "Laptop" and p.getPrice() returns 999.99
  ```
- **See also:** #decode(String, Class)

##### decodeToMultimap(...) -> ListMultimap<String, String>
- **Signature:** `public static ListMultimap<String, String> decodeToMultimap(final String urlQuery) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Decodes a URL-encoded query string into a `ListMultimap<String, String>` using UTF-8.
- **Contract:**
  - Unlike #decode(String), this method preserves all values when a parameter appears multiple times in the query string.
- **Parameters:**
  - `urlQuery` (`String`) — the URL query string to decode (e.g., "color=red&color=blue&size=L"), may be `null` or empty.
- **Returns:** a `ListMultimap` containing parameter names as keys and lists of decoded parameter values; returns an empty multimap if `urlQuery` is `null` or empty. A token without `'='` is stored with a `null` value.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a percent escape or its UTF-8 byte sequence is malformed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ListMultimap<String, String> params = URLEncodedUtil.decodeToMultimap("color=red&color=blue&size=L");
    // params: {color=[red, blue], size=[L]}
  ```
- **See also:** #decodeToMultimap(String, Charset), #decode(String)
- **Signature:** `public static ListMultimap<String, String> decodeToMultimap(final String urlQuery, final Charset charset) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Decodes a URL-encoded query string into a `ListMultimap<String, String>` using the specified charset.
- **Contract:**
  - Unlike #decode(String, Charset), this method preserves all values when a parameter appears multiple times in the query string.
- **Parameters:**
  - `urlQuery` (`String`) — the URL query string to decode, may be `null` or empty.
  - `charset` (`Charset`) — the charset to use for decoding percent-encoded characters; if `null`, defaults to UTF-8.
- **Returns:** a `ListMultimap` containing parameter names as keys and lists of decoded parameter values; returns an empty multimap if `urlQuery` is `null` or empty. A token without `'='` is stored with a `null` value.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if a percent escape or its encoded byte sequence is malformed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  ListMultimap<String, String> params = URLEncodedUtil.decodeToMultimap("tag=java&tag=url", StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    // params: {tag=[java, url]}
  ```
- **See also:** #decodeToMultimap(String), #decode(String, Charset)
##### decodeToMultimapLenient(...) -> ListMultimap<String, String>

- **Summary:** Leniently decodes a URL-encoded query string into a `ListMultimap<String, String>` using UTF-8, preserving repeated parameters in encounter order.

- **Parameters:**

- **See also:** #decodeToMultimap(String, Charset)
##### convertToBean(...) -> T
- **Signature:** `public static <T> T convertToBean(final Map<String, String[]> parameters, final Class<? extends T> targetType) throws IllegalArgumentException`
- **Summary:** Converts a parameter map (with String array values) into a bean of the specified type.
- **Contract:**
  - The keys in the map should correspond to bean property names (exact match first, falling back to case-insensitive matching).
  - If a property has multiple values and the target property type is `String\[\]`, all values are set.
  - If a parameter value is `null`, empty, or contains only a single empty or `null` string, the property is set to its default value (as determined by the property type).
- **Parameters:**
  - `parameters` (`Map<String, String[]>`) — the map of parameters to convert, where keys are property names and values are String arrays; may be `null` or empty.
  - `targetType` (`Class<? extends T>`) — the class of the bean to create and populate; must not be `null`.
- **Returns:** an instance of type T with properties populated from the parameter map; returns an empty instance if `parameters` is `null` or empty.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `targetType` is `null` or not a supported bean type.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Map<String, String[]> params = new HashMap<>();
    params.put("name", new String[] {"Alice"});
    params.put("tags", new String[] {"java", "coding"});
    User user = URLEncodedUtil.convertToBean(params, User.class);
    // user: {name="Alice", tags="java, coding"}
  ```
