##### mapLastOrElse(...) -> Stream<R>
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @IntermediateOp public abstract <R> Stream<R> mapLastOrElse(Function<? super T, ? extends R> mapperForLast, Function<? super T, ? extends R> mapperForElse) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Returns a stream consisting of the elements of this stream with the last element transformed by the specified `mapperForLast` and all other elements transformed by `mapperForElse`.
- **Contract:**
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
  - For example, if this stream contains elements \[a, b, c, d\], the resulting stream will contain \[g(a), g(b), g(c), f(d)\], where f is the mapperForLast function and g is the mapperForElse function.
- **Parameters:**
  - `mapperForLast` (`Function<? super T, ? extends R>`) — a non-interfering, stateless function to apply to the last element of this stream.
  - `mapperForElse` (`Function<? super T, ? extends R>`) — a non-interfering, stateless function to apply to all other elements of this stream.
- **Returns:** a new stream consisting of the results of applying the appropriate mapper function to each element
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any of `mapperForLast`, `mapperForElse` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of("apple", "banana", "cherry")
          .mapLastOrElse(String::toUpperCase, s -> s.substring(0, 1))
          .toList();   // returns ["a", "b", "CHERRY"]
  
    Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4)
          .mapLastOrElse(x -> x * 10, x -> x * 2)
          .toList();   // returns [2, 4, 6, 40]
  ```

##### flatMap(...) -> Stream<R>
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @IntermediateOp public abstract <R> Stream<R> flatMap(Function<? super T, ? extends Stream<? extends R>> mapper) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Transforms the elements in the stream by applying a function to each element.
- **Contract:**
  - The function should return a Stream of elements.
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
  - The mapper function should be non-interfering and stateless for correct behavior in parallel streams.
- **Parameters:**
  - `mapper` (`Function<? super T, ? extends Stream<? extends R>>`) — a non-interfering, stateless function that transforms each element
- **Returns:** a new Stream consisting of the elements obtained by replacing each element of this stream with the contents of a mapped stream produced by applying the provided mapping function to each element.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapper` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java

          .flatMap(s -> Stream.of(s.split(",")))
          .toList();   // returns ["apple", "banana", "cherry", "date", "elderberry"]
  
    Stream.of(Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3), Arrays.asList(4, 5, 6))
          .flatMap(list -> Stream.of(list.toArray(new Integer[0])))
          .toList();   // returns [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
  ```

##### flatmapToEntry(...) -> EntryStream<K, V>
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @IntermediateOp public abstract <K, V> EntryStream<K, V> flatmapToEntry(Function<? super T, ? extends Map<? extends K, ? extends V>> mapper) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Transforms the elements in the stream by applying a function to each element.
- **Contract:**
  - The function should return a Map of key-value pairs.
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
  - The mapper function should be non-interfering and stateless for correct behavior in parallel streams.
- **Parameters:**
  - `mapper` (`Function<? super T, ? extends Map<? extends K, ? extends V>>`) — a non-interfering, stateless function that transforms each element into a Map
- **Returns:** a new EntryStream consisting of Map.Entry instances obtained by transforming each element of this stream into a Map and then flattening these Maps into a stream of their entries.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapper` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of("user1", "user2")
          .flatmapToEntry(user -> {
              Map<String, String> props = new HashMap<>();
              props.put(user + "_name", user.toUpperCase());
              props.put(user + "_status", "active");
              return props;
          })
          .toMap();   // returns {user1_name=USER1, user1_status=active, user2_name=USER2, user2_status=active}
  ```
- **See also:** #flatMapToEntry(Function), #flattMapToEntry(Function), #mapToEntry(Function, Function)
##### flattMapToEntry(...) -> EntryStream<K, V>
- **Signature:** `@Beta @ParallelSupported @IntermediateOp public abstract <K, V> EntryStream<K, V> flattMapToEntry(Function<? super T, ? extends EntryStream<? extends K, ? extends V>> mapper) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta, @ParallelSupported, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Transforms the elements in the stream by applying a function to each element.
- **Contract:**
  - The function should return an EntryStream of key-value pairs.
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
  - The mapper function should be non-interfering and stateless for correct behavior in parallel streams.
  - Each non-`null` EntryStream returned by the mapper is closed after its entries are consumed, or when the returned EntryStream is closed while consuming it.
- **Parameters:**
  - `mapper` (`Function<? super T, ? extends EntryStream<? extends K, ? extends V>>`) — a non-interfering, stateless function that transforms each element into an EntryStream
- **Returns:** a new EntryStream consisting of key-value pairs obtained by transforming each element of this stream into an EntryStream and then flattening these EntryStreams into a single EntryStream.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapper` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of("user1", "user2")
          .flattMapToEntry(user -> EntryStream.of(user + "_name", user.toUpperCase(), user + "_status", "active"))
          .toMap();   // returns {user1_name=USER1, user1_status=active, user2_name=USER2, user2_status=active}
  ```
- **See also:** #flatMapToEntry(Function), #flatmapToEntry(Function)

- **Annotations:** @Beta, @ParallelSupported, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Applies a mapping operation on the stream with multiple output elements for each input element.

  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.

- **Parameters:**
  - `mapper` (`BiConsumer<? super T, ? super Consumer<R>>`) — a BiConsumer that takes an input element and a Consumer for output elements, and produces multiple output elements for each input element.

  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapper` is `null`
- **Examples:**

##### mapPartial(...) -> Stream<R>
- **Signature:** `@Beta @ParallelSupported @IntermediateOp public abstract <R> Stream<R> mapPartial(Function<? super T, Optional<R>> mapper) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta, @ParallelSupported, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Applies a partial mapping operation on the stream.
- **Contract:**
  - If the Optional is empty, the element is not included in the resulting stream.
  - If the Optional contains a value, that value is included in the resulting stream.
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
  - The mapper function should be non-interfering and stateless for correct behavior in parallel streams.
- **Parameters:**
  - `mapper` (`Function<? super T, Optional<R>>`) — a Function that takes an element and produces an Optional of a new element of type R.
- **Returns:** a new Stream consisting of the results of applying the Function to each element
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapper` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of("1", "abc", "2", "def", "3")
          .mapPartial(s -> {
              try {
                  return Optional.of(Integer.parseInt(s));
              } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
                  return Optional.empty();
              }
          })
          .toList();   // returns [1, 2, 3]
  ```
- **See also:** #mapPartialJdk(Function), #filter(Predicate), #map(Function)

##### groupBy(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @IntermediateOp @TerminalOpTriggered public abstract <K> Stream<Map.Entry<K, List<T>>> groupBy(final Function<? super T, ? extends K> keyMapper) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @IntermediateOp, @TerminalOpTriggered
- **Summary:** Groups the elements of the stream by the classification function provided.
- **Contract:**
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
  - The keyMapper function should be non-interfering and stateless for correct behavior in parallel streams.
- **Parameters:**
  - `keyMapper` (`Function<? super T, ? extends K>`) — the function to be applied to each element in the stream to determine the group it belongs to.
- **Returns:** a new Stream consisting of Map.Entry instances where the key is the group identifier and the value is a list of elements belonging to that group.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `keyMapper` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of("apple", "apricot", "banana", "blueberry", "cherry")
          .groupBy(s -> s.charAt(0))
          .forEach(e -> System.out.println(e.getKey() + "=" + e.getValue()));   // prints these entries (key order unspecified): a=[apple, apricot], b=[banana, blueberry], c=[cherry]
  ```
- **See also:** #groupBy(Function, Supplier), #groupBy(Function, Function), #groupBy(Function, Collector)

- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @IntermediateOp, @TerminalOpTriggered
- **Summary:** Groups the elements of the stream by applying a key mapping function and a value mapping function to each element.
- **Contract:**
  - In parallel streams, the merge function must be associative and stateless.
- **Parameters:**
  - `keyMapper` (`Function<? super T, ? extends K>`) — the function to be applied to each element in the stream to determine the group it belongs to.
  - `valueMapper` (`Function<? super T, ? extends V>`) — the function to be applied to each element in the stream to determine its value in the group.
  - `mergeFunction` (`BinaryOperator<V>`) — the function to be used for merging values in case of key collision.
  - `mapFactory` (`Supplier<? extends Map<K, V>>`) — the supplier providing a new empty Map into which the results will be inserted.
- **Returns:** a new Stream consisting of Map.Entry instances where the key is the group identifier and the value is the result of applying the value mapping function to the elements of the group and merging them using the merge function
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any of `keyMapper`, `valueMapper`, `mergeFunction`, `mapFactory` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java

          .groupBy(s -> s.charAt(0),
                   s -> s.length(),
                   Integer::sum,
                   Suppliers.ofMap())
          .forEach(System.out::println);
    // Prints entries like: a=12, b=6, c=6
  ```

##### partitionBy(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @IntermediateOp @TerminalOpTriggered public abstract Stream<Map.Entry<Boolean, List<T>>> partitionBy(final Predicate<? super T> predicate) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @IntermediateOp, @TerminalOpTriggered
- **Summary:** Partitions the elements of the stream according to a Predicate.
- **Contract:**
  - If the Predicate returns `true` for an element, it is included in the List corresponding to the key `true` in the Map.Entry.
  - If the Predicate returns `false` for an element, it is included in the List corresponding to the key `false` in the Map.Entry.
  - The returned `Stream` always contains mappings for both `false` and `true` keys, even if this stream is empty.
- **Parameters:**
  - `predicate` (`Predicate<? super T>`) — a non-interfering, stateless predicate to be used for partitioning the stream elements
- **Returns:** a new Stream consisting of Map.Entry where the key is a Boolean and the value is a List of elements
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `predicate` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)
          .partitionBy(n -> n % 2 == 0)
          .forEach(System.out::println);
    // Prints: false=[1, 3, 5], true=[2, 4, 6]
  ```
- **See also:** #partitionByToEntry(Predicate), #partitionTo(Throwables.Predicate), Collectors#partitioningBy(Predicate)

- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @IntermediateOp, @TerminalOpTriggered
- **Summary:** Partitions the elements of the stream according to a Predicate and a Collector.
- **Contract:**
  - If the Predicate returns `true` for an element, it is included in the group corresponding to the key `true` in the Map.Entry.
  - If the Predicate returns `false` for an element, it is included in the group corresponding to the key `false` in the Map.Entry.
  - The returned `Stream` always contains mappings for both `false` and `true` keys, even if this stream is empty.
- **Parameters:**
  - `predicate` (`Predicate<? super T>`) — a non-interfering, stateless predicate to be used for partitioning the stream elements
  - `downstream` (`Collector<? super T, ?, D>`) — the Collector to be applied to the elements of each group.
- **Returns:** a new Stream consisting of Map.Entry where the key is a Boolean and the value is the result of applying the Collector to the elements of the group
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `predicate` or `downstream` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java

          .partitionBy(s -> s.length() > 5,

  ```

  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `keyMapper` is `null`.
- **Examples:**

  ```java
          .countBy(s -> s.charAt(0))
          .forEach(System.out::println);
  ```

##### collapse(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `@SequentialOnly @IntermediateOp public abstract Stream<List<T>> collapse(final BiPredicate<? super T, ? super T> collapsible) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @SequentialOnly, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Collapses consecutive elements in the stream into groups based on a predicate.
- **Contract:**
  - Elements for which the predicate returns `true` when applied to adjacent elements are grouped together into lists.
  - A failed later read does not replay elements already incorporated into the unfinished group; a successfully read candidate remains cached if the grouping predicate throws.
- **Parameters:**
  - `collapsible` (`BiPredicate<? super T, ? super T>`) — a predicate that determines if two consecutive elements should be collapsed into the same group. The first parameter is the last (not the first) element of the current group, and the second parameter is the next element to check.
- **Returns:** a stream of lists, each containing a sequence of consecutive elements that are collapsible with each other
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `collapsible` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of(1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 10)
          .collapse((a, b) -> b - a <= 2)
          .forEach(System.out::println);
    // Prints: [1, 2], [5, 6, 7], [10]
  ```
- **See also:** #collapse(BiPredicate, Supplier), #collapse(BiPredicate, BinaryOperator)
- **Signature:** `@SequentialOnly @IntermediateOp public abstract <C extends Collection<T>> Stream<C> collapse(final BiPredicate<? super T, ? super T> collapsible, Supplier<? extends C> supplier) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @SequentialOnly, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Collapses consecutive elements in the stream into custom collections based on a predicate.
- **Contract:**
  - Elements for which the predicate returns `true` when applied to adjacent elements are grouped together into collections created by the supplied collection factory.
  - A failed later read does not replay elements already incorporated into the unfinished group; a successfully read candidate remains cached if the grouping predicate throws.
- **Parameters:**
  - `collapsible` (`BiPredicate<? super T, ? super T>`) — a predicate that determines if two consecutive elements should be collapsed into the same group. The first parameter is the last (not the first) element of the current group, and the second parameter is the next element to check.
  - `supplier` (`Supplier<? extends C>`) — a factory to create new collection instances for each group.
- **Returns:** a stream of collections, each containing a sequence of consecutive elements that are collapsible with each other
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any of `collapsible`, `supplier` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of(1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 10)
          .collapse((a, b) -> b - a <= 2, () -> new LinkedHashSet<Integer>())
          .forEach(System.out::println);
    // Prints sets: [1, 2], [5, 6, 7], [10]
  ```
- **See also:** #collapse(BiPredicate), #collapse(BiPredicate, Collector)
- **Signature:** `@SequentialOnly @IntermediateOp public abstract Stream<T> collapse(final BiPredicate<? super T, ? super T> collapsible, final BinaryOperator<T> mergeFunction) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @SequentialOnly, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Collapses consecutive elements in the stream by applying a merge function when elements are collapsible.
- **Contract:**
  - When adjacent elements satisfy the collapsible predicate, they are merged using the provided merge function.
  - A failed later read does not replay elements already incorporated into the unfinished group; a successfully read candidate remains cached if the grouping predicate throws.
- **Parameters:**
  - `collapsible` (`BiPredicate<? super T, ? super T>`) — a predicate that determines if two consecutive elements should be collapsed into the same group. The first parameter is the last (not the first) element of the current group, and the second parameter is the next element to check.
  - `mergeFunction` (`BinaryOperator<T>`) — a function to merge two collapsible elements into one.
- **Returns:** a stream of merged elements
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any of `collapsible`, `mergeFunction` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of(1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 10)
          .collapse((a, b) -> b - a <= 2, Integer::sum)
          .forEach(System.out::println);
    // Prints: 3, 18, 10
  ```
- **See also:** #collapse(BiPredicate), #collapse(BiPredicate, Object, BiFunction)
- **Signature:** `@SequentialOnly @IntermediateOp public abstract <U> Stream<U> collapse(final BiPredicate<? super T, ? super T> collapsible, final U init, final BiFunction<? super U, ? super T, U> mergeFunction) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @SequentialOnly, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Collapses consecutive elements in the stream into an accumulator of type U.
- **Contract:**
  - When adjacent elements satisfy the collapsible predicate, the accumulator value and the current element are combined using the provided merge function.
  - A failed later read does not replay elements already incorporated into the unfinished group; a successfully read candidate remains cached if the grouping predicate throws.
- **Parameters:**
  - `collapsible` (`BiPredicate<? super T, ? super T>`) — a predicate that determines if two consecutive elements should be collapsed into the same group. The first parameter is the last (not the first) element of the current group, and the second parameter is the next element to check.
  - `init` (`U`) — the initial value for each accumulation.
  - `mergeFunction` (`BiFunction<? super U, ? super T, U>`) — a function to incorporate an element into an accumulated result.
- **Returns:** a stream of accumulated values
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `collapsible` or `mergeFunction` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of(1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 10)
          .collapse((a, b) -> b - a <= 2,

          .forEach(System.out::println);

  ```

  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any of `collapsible`, `mergeFunction` is `null`


  - A failed later read does not replay elements already incorporated into the unfinished group; a successfully read candidate remains cached if the grouping predicate throws.

  - `collapsible` (`TriPredicate<? super T, ? super T, ? super T>`) — a predicate that determines if the next element from this stream should be collapsed with the first and last elements of current group The collapsible predicate takes three elements: the first and last elements of current group, and the next element to check.

  - `mergeFunction` (`BiFunction<? super U, ? super T, U>`) — a function to incorporate an element into an accumulated result.

- **Examples:**

- **Annotations:** @SequentialOnly, @IntermediateOp

  - Collection happens lazily when those elements are pulled, not when this method returns.

  - `collector` (`Collector<? super T, ?, R>`) — the collector to be used for collecting elements of each part of the stream
- **Returns:** a new Stream consisting of two elements: the collected first part followed by the collected second part
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `position` is negative or `collector` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.range(0, 7)
          .splitAt(3, Collectors.toSet())
          .toList();   // returns [{0, 1, 2}, {3, 4, 5, 6}]
  ```

- **Contract:**
  - If increment equals windowSize, windows don't overlap.
  - If increment is less than windowSize, windows overlap.
  - If increment is greater than windowSize, some elements may be skipped.
  - When `increment > windowSize`, a new window also requires an element after the skipped gap; exhausting the source in that gap produces no additional window.

- **Parameters:**
  - `windowSize` (`int`) — the size of the window to be used for sliding over the Stream elements. Must be positive.
  - `increment` (`int`) — the number of elements to move the window by each time. Must be positive.
- **Returns:** a new Stream where each element is a List of elements from the original Stream, representing a window
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if windowSize or increment is not positive.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
          .sliding(3, 2)
          .toList();   // returns [[1, 2, 3], [3, 4, 5]]
  ```
- **See also:** #sliding(int), #sliding(int, int, IntFunction)

  ```java
          .sliding(3, 2, ArrayList::new)
          .toList();   // returns [ArrayList[1,2,3], ArrayList[3,4,5], ArrayList[5,6]]
  ```
- **See also:** #sliding(int, int), #sliding(int, int, Collector)
- **Signature:** `@SequentialOnly @IntermediateOp public abstract <R> Stream<R> sliding(int windowSize, int increment, Collector<? super T, ?, R> collector) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @SequentialOnly, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Creates a sliding window over the elements of the Stream, where each window is collected using the provided Collector.
- **Contract:**
  - During manual iteration of a sequential stream, if `hasNext()` or `next()` encounters a source failure while skipping the gap between windows, the next such call resumes the unfinished gap.
- **Parameters:**
  - `windowSize` (`int`) — the size of the window to be used for sliding over the Stream elements. Must be positive.
  - `increment` (`int`) — the number of elements to move the window by each time. Must be positive.
  - `collector` (`Collector<? super T, ?, R>`) — the collector to be used for reduction of the elements in each window
- **Returns:** a new Stream where each element is a result container of the collected elements from the original Stream, representing a window
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if windowSize or increment is not positive, or collector is null.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of("a", "b", "c", "d", "e")
          .sliding(3, 2, Collectors.joining())
          .toList();   // returns ["abc", "cde"]
  ```
- **See also:** #sliding(int, Collector), #sliding(int, int)

##### top(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `@SequentialOnly @IntermediateOp public abstract Stream<T> top(int n) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @SequentialOnly, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Returns a Stream consisting of the top n elements of this stream, according to the natural order of the elements.
- **Contract:**
  - If this stream contains fewer elements than `n`, all elements are returned.
  - Elements must be Comparable.
  - If there are fewer than n elements, all elements are returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `n` (`int`) — the number of top elements to select from the stream. Must be non-negative.
- **Returns:** a new stream that contains the top (largest) n elements of the original stream, according to the natural order of the elements. There is no guarantee on the order of the returned elements.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if n is less than zero.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of(5, 3, 8, 1, 9, 2)
          .top(3)
          .toList();   // returns the 3 largest elements: 5, 8, 9 (in unspecified order)
  ```
- **See also:** #top(int, Comparator), #kthLargest(int, Comparator)
- **Signature:** `@SequentialOnly @IntermediateOp public abstract Stream<T> top(int n, Comparator<? super T> comparator) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @SequentialOnly, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Returns a Stream consisting of the top n elements of this stream compared by the provided Comparator.
- **Contract:**
  - If this stream contains fewer elements than `n`, all elements are returned.
  - If there are fewer than n elements, all elements are returned.
- **Parameters:**
  - `n` (`int`) — the number of top elements to select from the stream. Must be non-negative.
  - `comparator` (`Comparator<? super T>`) — a Comparator to be used to compare stream elements; the `n` elements considered "greatest" by this comparator are returned
- **Returns:** a new Stream consisting of the top n elements of this stream compared by the provided Comparator. There is no guarantee on the order of the returned elements.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `n` is negative or `comparator` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of("apple", "banana", "cherry", "date")
          .top(2, Comparator.comparing(String::length))
          .toList();   // returns the 2 longest strings: "banana", "cherry" (in unspecified order)
  ```
- **See also:** #top(int), #kthLargest(int, Comparator)
##### skipRange(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `@SequentialOnly @IntermediateOp public abstract Stream<T> skipRange(int startInclusive, int endExclusive) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @SequentialOnly, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Skips a range of elements in the stream.
- **Contract:**
  - If startInclusive equals endExclusive, no elements are skipped.
  - If iteration is retried after a source failure, any unfinished portion of the skipped range is still skipped.
- **Parameters:**
  - `startInclusive` (`int`) — the first position in the range to skip, inclusive. Must be non-negative.
  - `endExclusive` (`int`) — the last position in the range to skip, exclusive. Must be >= startInclusive.
- **Returns:** a new stream that skips the specified range of the original stream
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if startInclusive is negative or endExclusive < startInclusive.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)
          .skipRange(2, 5)
          .toList();   // returns [0, 1, 5, 6]
  ```
- **See also:** #skip(long), #limit(long)

  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if n is negative.
- **Examples:**
  ```java

          .skipLast(2)
          .toList();   // returns [1, 2, 3]
  ```

- **Summary:** Performs the provided action on the first element of the stream as it is consumed.

  - If the stream is empty, the action is not performed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `action` (`Consumer<? super T>`) — a non-interfering action to perform on the first element of the stream
- **Returns:** a new stream that includes the action on the first element
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `action` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
          .onFirst(e -> System.out.println("First: " + e))
          .toList();   // prints "First: 1" and returns [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
  ```
- **See also:** #onLast(Consumer), #peekFirst(Consumer)

##### peek(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `@Beta @ParallelSupported @IntermediateOp @Override public Stream<T> peek(Consumer<? super T> action) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta, @ParallelSupported, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Performs the given action as elements are pulled during traversal, including manual iteration.
- **Contract:**
  - The action should be non-interfering and stateless for correct behavior in parallel streams.
- **Parameters:**
  - `action` (`Consumer<? super T>`) — the action to perform as elements are pulled during traversal, including manual iteration.
- **Returns:** a new Stream consisting of the elements of this stream with the provided action applied to each element.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `action` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of("apple", "banana", "cherry")
          .peek(System.out::println)  // prints each element
          .map(String::toUpperCase)
          .toList();
  ```
- **See also:** #onEach(Consumer)
##### peekFirst(...) -> Stream<T>

- **Parameters:**

- **See also:** #onFirst(Consumer), #onEach(Consumer)

##### peekIf(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `@Beta @ParallelSupported @IntermediateOp public Stream<T> peekIf(final Predicate<? super T> predicate, final Consumer<? super T> action) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta, @ParallelSupported, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Performs the provided action only on the elements pulled by downstream/terminal operation which satisfy the given predicate as they are consumed.
- **Contract:**
  - This operation is stateless and can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
- **Parameters:**
  - `predicate` (`Predicate<? super T>`) — a non-interfering predicate to test on the elements of the stream
  - `action` (`Consumer<? super T>`) — a non-interfering action to perform on the elements that satisfy the predicate
- **Returns:** a new stream that includes the action on the elements that satisfy the predicate
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `predicate` or `action` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
          .peekIf(x -> x % 2 == 0, x -> System.out.println("Even: " + x))
          .toList();   // prints "Even: 2" and "Even: 4", returns [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
  ```
- **See also:** #onEach(Consumer), #peekIf(BiPredicate, Consumer)
- **Signature:** `@Beta @ParallelSupported @IntermediateOp public Stream<T> peekIf(final BiPredicate<? super T, ? super Long> predicate, final Consumer<? super T> action) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta, @ParallelSupported, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Performs the provided action only on the elements pulled by downstream/terminal operation which satisfy the given predicate as they are consumed.
- **Parameters:**
  - `predicate` (`BiPredicate<? super T, ? super Long>`) — a non-interfering predicate to test on the elements of the stream and their iteration count
  - `action` (`Consumer<? super T>`) — a non-interfering action to perform on the elements that satisfy the predicate
- **Returns:** a new stream that includes the action on the elements that satisfy the predicate
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `predicate` or `action` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of("a", "b", "c", "d", "e")
          .peekIf((e, count) -> count % 2 == 0, e -> System.out.println("Even position: " + e))
          .toList();   // prints "Even position: b" and "Even position: d", returns ["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"]
  ```
- **See also:** #onEach(Consumer), #peekIf(Predicate, Consumer)
##### foreach(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@Beta @ParallelSupported @TerminalOp public void foreach(final Consumer<? super T> action) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`

- **Summary:** Performs the provided action for each element of the Stream.

  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.

- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `action` is `null`.

  ```java
  Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
          .foreach(System.out::println);   // prints each number on a new line
  ```
- **See also:** #forEach(Throwables.Consumer)
##### forEach(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @TerminalOp public abstract <E extends Exception> void forEach(Throwables.Consumer<? super T, E> action) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @TerminalOp
- **Summary:** Performs the provided action for each element of the Stream.
- **Contract:**
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
  - In parallel execution, the action must be thread-safe as it may be called concurrently.
- **Parameters:**
  - `action` (`Throwables.Consumer<? super T, E>`) — the action to be performed for each element
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `action` is `null`
  - `E` — Exception thrown by the Consumer
- **Examples:**
  ```java

          .forEach(s -> System.out.println(s.toUpperCase()));   // prints APPLE, BANANA, CHERRY
  ```
- **See also:** java.util.function.Consumer, com.landawn.abacus.util.Throwables.Consumer
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @TerminalOp public abstract <E extends Exception, E2 extends Exception> void forEach(Throwables.Consumer<? super T, E> action, Throwables.Runnable<E2> onComplete) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, E, E2`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @TerminalOp
- **Summary:** Performs the provided action for each element of the Stream.
- **Contract:**
  - The completion callback runs only after successful traversal; it is not invoked if traversal or the action fails.
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
- **Parameters:**
  - `action` (`Throwables.Consumer<? super T, E>`) — the action to be performed for each element
  - `onComplete` (`Throwables.Runnable<E2>`) — the Runnable to execute after all elements have been processed successfully
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any of `action`, `onComplete` is `null`
  - `E` — Exception thrown by the Consumer
  - `E2` — Exception thrown by the Runnable
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of(1, 2, 3)
          .forEach(
              x -> System.out.println("Processing: " + x),
              () -> System.out.println("All done!")
          );
    // Prints: Processing: 1, Processing: 2, Processing: 3, All done!
  ```
- **See also:** N#forEach(Iterable, Throwables.Consumer)
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @TerminalOp public abstract <U, E extends Exception, E2 extends Exception> void forEach(Throwables.Function<? super T, ? extends Iterable<? extends U>, E> flatMapper, Throwables.BiConsumer<? super T, ? super U, E2> action) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, E, E2`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @TerminalOp
- **Summary:** Transforms the elements in the stream by applying the flatMapper function to each element and then performs the provided action for each element of the Stream.
- **Contract:**
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
  - The flatMapper should produce finite iterables for each element.
- **Parameters:**
  - `flatMapper` (`Throwables.Function<? super T, ? extends Iterable<? extends U>, E>`) — the function to transform elements of the Stream into Iterables
  - `action` (`Throwables.BiConsumer<? super T, ? super U, E2>`) — the action to be performed for each element of the Stream and each element of the Iterable produced by the flatMapper function
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any of `flatMapper`, `action` is `null`
  - `E` — Exception thrown by the flatMapper function
  - `E2` — Exception thrown by the BiConsumer action
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of("hello", "world")
          .forEach(
              s -> Arrays.asList(s.split("")),
              (word, letter) -> System.out.println(word + " -> " + letter)
          );
    // Prints: hello -> h, hello -> e, hello -> l, hello -> l, hello -> o, world -> w, etc.
  ```
- **See also:** N#forEach(Iterable, Throwables.Function, Throwables.BiConsumer)
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @TerminalOp public abstract <T2, T3, E extends Exception, E2 extends Exception, E3 extends Exception> void forEach( Throwables.Function<? super T, ? extends Iterable<T2>, E> flatMapper, Throwables.Function<? super T2, ? extends Iterable<T3>, E2> flatMapper2, Throwables.TriConsumer<? super T, ? super T2, ? super T3, E3> action) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, E, E2, E3`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @TerminalOp
- **Summary:** Transforms the elements in the stream by applying the flatMapper/flatMapper2 function to each element and then performs the provided action for each element of the Stream.
- **Contract:**
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
  - Both flatMappers should produce finite iterables for each element.
- **Parameters:**
  - `flatMapper` (`Throwables.Function<? super T, ? extends Iterable<T2>, E>`) — the first function to transform elements of the Stream into Iterables
  - `flatMapper2` (`Throwables.Function<? super T2, ? extends Iterable<T3>, E2>`) — the second function to transform elements of the first Iterable into further Iterables
  - `action` (`Throwables.TriConsumer<? super T, ? super T2, ? super T3, E3>`) — the action to be performed for each element of the Stream and each element of the Iterables produced by the flatMapper functions
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any of `flatMapper`, `flatMapper2`, `action` is `null`
  - `E` — Exception thrown by the first flatMapper function
  - `E2` — Exception thrown by the second flatMapper function
  - `E3` — Exception thrown by the TriConsumer action
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of("AB", "CD")
          .forEach(
              s -> Arrays.asList(s.split("")),
              c -> Arrays.asList(c.toLowerCase(), c.toUpperCase()),
              (original, letter, variant) -> System.out.println(original + ": " + letter + " -> " + variant)
          );
    // Prints: AB: A -> a, AB: A -> A, AB: B -> b, AB: B -> B, etc.
  ```
- **See also:** N#forEach(Iterable, Throwables.Function, Throwables.Function, Throwables.TriConsumer)
##### forEachIndexed(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@Beta @ParallelSupported @TerminalOp public abstract <E extends Exception> void forEachIndexed(Throwables.IntObjConsumer<? super T, E> action) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Annotations:** @Beta, @ParallelSupported, @TerminalOp
- **Summary:** Performs the provided action for each element of the Stream, where the action is an instance of Throwables.IntObjConsumer.

  - `action` (`Throwables.IntObjConsumer<? super T, E>`) — the action to be performed for each element
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed

  - `E` — if the action throws an exception
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of("a", "b", "c")
  ```

##### forEachUntil(...) -> void
- **Signature:** `@Beta @ParallelSupported @TerminalOp public abstract <E extends Exception> void forEachUntil(Throwables.BiConsumer<? super T, MutableBoolean, E> action) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Annotations:** @Beta, @ParallelSupported, @TerminalOp
- **Summary:** Performs the provided action for each element of the Stream until the action sets the MutableBoolean to `true`.
- **Contract:**
  - Iteration on this stream will also be stopped when this flag is set to `true`.
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
- **Parameters:**
  - `action` (`Throwables.BiConsumer<? super T, MutableBoolean, E>`) — the action to be performed for each element, which accepts an element and a MutableBoolean
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `action` is `null`
  - `E` — if the action throws an exception
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
          .forEachUntil((value, stopFlag) -> {
              System.out.println(value);
              if (value >= 3) stopFlag.setTrue();
          });   // prints 1, 2, 3
  ```
- **See also:** #forEachUntil(MutableBoolean, Throwables.Consumer)
- **Signature:** `@Beta @ParallelSupported @TerminalOp public abstract <E extends Exception> void forEachUntil(MutableBoolean flagToBreak, Throwables.Consumer<? super T, E> action) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Annotations:** @Beta, @ParallelSupported, @TerminalOp
- **Summary:** Performs the provided action for each element of the Stream until the flagToBreak is set to `true`.
- **Contract:**
  - Iteration on this stream will also be stopped when the flagToBreak is set to `true`.
  - If the flagToBreak is set to `true` at the beginning, no elements will be iterated from the stream before it is stopped and closed.
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
- **Parameters:**
  - `flagToBreak` (`MutableBoolean`) — a flag to break the for-each loop. Set it to `true` to break the loop if you don't want to continue the action. Iteration on this stream will also be stopped when this flag is set to `true`.
  - `action` (`Throwables.Consumer<? super T, E>`) — the action to be performed for each element
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `flagToBreak` or `action` is `null`.
  - `E` — if the action throws an exception
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  MutableBoolean stopFlag = MutableBoolean.of(false);
    Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
          .forEachUntil(stopFlag, value -> {
              System.out.println(value);
              if (value >= 3) stopFlag.setTrue();
          });   // prints 1, 2, 3
  ```
- **See also:** #forEachUntil(Throwables.BiConsumer)

##### anyMatch(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @TerminalOp public abstract <E extends Exception> boolean anyMatch(Throwables.Predicate<? super T, E> predicate) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @TerminalOp
- **Summary:** Checks if any elements of this Stream match the provided predicate.
- **Contract:**
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
  - It can stop when a match is found; parallel workers may already be processing other elements.
- **Parameters:**
  - `predicate` (`Throwables.Predicate<? super T, E>`) — the predicate to apply to elements of this stream
- **Returns:** `true` if any elements match the predicate, otherwise `false`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `predicate` is `null`
  - `E` — if the predicate throws an exception
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  boolean hasEven = Stream.of(1, 3, 5, 6, 7)
                            .anyMatch(x -> x % 2 == 0);   // returns true
  ```
- **See also:** #allMatch(Throwables.Predicate), #noneMatch(Throwables.Predicate)
##### allMatch(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @TerminalOp public abstract <E extends Exception> boolean allMatch(Throwables.Predicate<? super T, E> predicate) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @TerminalOp
- **Summary:** Checks if all elements of this Stream match the provided predicate.
- **Contract:**
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
  - It can return `false` when a non-match is found; parallel workers may already be processing other elements.
  - Returns `true` if the stream is empty.
- **Parameters:**
  - `predicate` (`Throwables.Predicate<? super T, E>`) — the predicate to apply to elements of this stream
- **Returns:** `true` if all elements match the predicate or this Stream is empty, otherwise `false`
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `predicate` is `null`
  - `E` — if the predicate throws an exception
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  boolean allPositive = Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
                                .allMatch(x -> x > 0);   // returns true
  ```
- **See also:** #anyMatch(Throwables.Predicate), #noneMatch(Throwables.Predicate)
##### noneMatch(...) -> boolean
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @TerminalOp public abstract <E extends Exception> boolean noneMatch(Throwables.Predicate<? super T, E> predicate) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, E`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @TerminalOp
- **Summary:** Checks if no elements of this Stream match the provided predicate.
- **Contract:**
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
  - It can return `false` when a match is found; parallel workers may already be processing other elements.

- **Throws:**

  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `predicate` is `null`
  - `E` — if the predicate throws an exception
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if the selected element is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java

    Optional<Integer> none = Stream.of(1, 3, 5).findFirst(x -> x % 2 == 0);   // returns Optional.empty()
  ```

- **Summary:** Collects the elements of this stream into an immutable map.

  - `keyMapper` (`Throwables.Function<? super T, ? extends K, E>`) — a function to produce the keys for the map
  - `valueMapper` (`Throwables.Function<? super T, ? extends V, E2>`) — a function to produce the values for the map
  - `mergeFunction` (`BinaryOperator<V>`) — the function to merge values associated with the same key; a `null` result removes the key, as Map#merge(Object, Object, BiFunction) does
- **Returns:** an immutable map containing the elements of this stream
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any of `keyMapper`, `valueMapper`, or `mergeFunction` is `null`.
  - `E` — if the keyMapper function throws an exception
  - `E2` — if the valueMapper function throws an exception

##### foldLeft(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `@SequentialOnly @TerminalOp public abstract Optional<T> foldLeft(BinaryOperator<T> accumulator) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @SequentialOnly, @TerminalOp
- **Summary:** Performs a reduction on the elements of this stream, using the provided BinaryOperator, and returns an Optional.
- **Parameters:**
  - `accumulator` (`BinaryOperator<T>`) — the function for combining two values.
- **Returns:** an Optional describing the result of the fold, or an empty Optional if the stream is empty
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `accumulator` is `null`
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if the result of the reduction is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of("a", "b", "c")
          .foldLeft((a, b) -> a + b)
          .get();   // returns "abc"
  
    Stream.<String>empty()
          .foldLeft((a, b) -> a + b);   // returns Optional.empty()
  ```
- **See also:** #reduce(BinaryOperator)
- **Signature:** `@SequentialOnly @TerminalOp public abstract <U> U foldLeft(U identity, BiFunction<? super U, ? super T, U> accumulator) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @SequentialOnly, @TerminalOp
- **Summary:** Performs a reduction on the elements of this stream, using the provided accumulator function, and returns the reduced value.
- **Parameters:**
  - `identity` (`U`) — the initial value.
  - `accumulator` (`BiFunction<? super U, ? super T, U>`) — the function for combining the current reduced value and the current stream element.
- **Returns:** the result of the reduction
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `accumulator` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of("a", "b", "c")
          .foldLeft("", (acc, s) -> acc + s);   // returns "abc"
  ```
- **See also:** #reduce(Object, BiFunction, BinaryOperator)

##### reduce(...) -> varies by overload
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @TerminalOp public abstract Optional<T> reduce(BinaryOperator<T> accumulator) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @TerminalOp
- **Summary:** Performs a reduction on the elements of this stream, using the provided accumulator function, and returns the reduced value.
- **Contract:**
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
  - The accumulator should be associative for correct behavior in parallel streams.
- **Parameters:**
  - `accumulator` (`BinaryOperator<T>`) — the function for combining the current reduced value and the current stream element. Must be associative.
- **Returns:** an Optional describing the result of the reduction. If the stream is empty, an empty `Optional` is returned.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `accumulator` is `null`
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if the result of the reduction is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4)
          .reduce((a, b) -> a + b)
          .get();   // returns 10
  
    Stream.<Integer>empty()
          .reduce((a, b) -> a + b);   // returns Optional.empty()
  ```
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @TerminalOp public T reduce(final T identity, final BinaryOperator<T> accumulator) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @TerminalOp
- **Summary:** Performs a reduction on the elements of this stream, using the provided accumulator function, and returns the reduced value.
- **Contract:**
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
  - The accumulator should be associative for correct behavior in parallel streams.
  - `identity` must be a true identity for `accumulator`, i.e.
  - `accumulator.apply(identity, t)` must equal `t` for every `t`.
  - For the same reason `identity` must not be a shared mutable object — every worker would accumulate into the same instance.
- **Parameters:**
  - `identity` (`T`) — the identity value for the accumulating function, i.e. `accumulator.apply(identity, t) == t`.
  - `accumulator` (`BinaryOperator<T>`) — the function for combining the current reduced value and the current stream element. Must be associative.
- **Returns:** the result of the reduction
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `accumulator` is `null`.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4)
          .reduce(0, (a, b) -> a + b);   // returns 10
  ```
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @TerminalOp public abstract <U> U reduce(U identity, BiFunction<? super U, ? super T, U> accumulator, BinaryOperator<U> combiner) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @TerminalOp
- **Summary:** Performs a reduction on the elements of this stream, using the provided accumulator function and combiner function, and returns the reduced value.
- **Contract:**
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
  - The combiner must be associative and compatible with the accumulator: combining a partial result with the result of accumulating one element from the identity must equal accumulating that element directly into the partial result.
  - `identity` must be a true identity for `combiner`, i.e.
  - `combiner.apply(identity, u)` must equal `u` for every `u`.
  - For the same reason `identity` must not be a shared mutable object — every worker would accumulate into the same instance.
- **Parameters:**
  - `identity` (`U`) — the initial value of the reduction operation.
  - `accumulator` (`BiFunction<? super U, ? super T, U>`) — the function for combining the current reduced value and the current stream element.
  - `combiner` (`BinaryOperator<U>`) — the function for combining the results of the accumulator function. Must be associative.
- **Returns:** the result of the reduction
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any of `accumulator`, `combiner` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of("a", "b", "c")
          .reduce("",
                  (acc, s) -> acc + s,
                  (acc1, acc2) -> acc1 + acc2);   // returns "abc"
  
    // For a mutable container use collect(...), not reduce(...):
    Stream.of("a", "b", "c")
          .collect(StringBuilder::new, StringBuilder::append, StringBuilder::append)
          .toString();   // returns "abc"
  ```
##### collect(...) -> R
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @TerminalOp public abstract <R> R collect(Supplier<R> supplier, BiConsumer<? super R, ? super T> accumulator, BiConsumer<R, R> combiner) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @TerminalOp
- **Summary:** Performs a mutable reduction operation on the elements of this stream.
- **Contract:**
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
  - The combiner should be associative for correct behavior in parallel streams.
- **Parameters:**
  - `supplier` (`Supplier<R>`) — a function that creates a new result container. For a parallel execution, this function may be called multiple times and must return a fresh value each time.
  - `accumulator` (`BiConsumer<? super R, ? super T>`) — an associative, non-interfering, stateless function for incorporating an additional element into a result.
  - `combiner` (`BiConsumer<R, R>`) — an associative, non-interfering, stateless function for combining two values, which must be compatible with the accumulator function. For supported container types, use the two-argument #collect(Supplier, BiConsumer) overload to supply a default combiner.
- **Returns:** the result of the reduction
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any of `supplier`, `accumulator`, `combiner` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of(1, 2, 3, 4)
          .collect(ArrayList::new,
                   (list, x) -> list.add(x),
                   (list1, list2) -> list1.addAll(list2));
    // Returns [1, 2, 3, 4]
  
    Stream.of(1, 2, 3)
          .collect(ArrayList::new,
                   (list, x) -> list.add(x));
    // Returns [1, 2, 3] (auto-merged for Collection type)
  ```
- **See also:** #collect(Supplier, BiConsumer), #collect(Collector), BiConsumers#ofAddAll(), BiConsumers#ofPutAll()
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @TerminalOp public abstract <R> R collect(Supplier<R> supplier, BiConsumer<? super R, ? super T> accumulator) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, RuntimeException`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @TerminalOp
- **Summary:** Performs a mutable reduction operation on the elements of this stream.
- **Contract:**
  - Only call this method when the returned type `R` is one of these types: `Collection/Map/StringBuilder/Multiset/Multimap/BooleanList/IntList/.../DoubleList`.
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
- **Parameters:**
  - `supplier` (`Supplier<R>`) — a function that creates a new result container. For a parallel execution, this function may be called multiple times and must return a fresh value each time.
  - `accumulator` (`BiConsumer<? super R, ? super T>`) — an associative, non-interfering, stateless function for incorporating an additional element into a result.
- **Returns:** the result of the reduction
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if any of `supplier`, `accumulator` is `null`
  - `java.lang.RuntimeException` — if this stream is parallel and the result type `R` is not one of: `Collection/Map/StringBuilder/Multiset/Multimap/BooleanList/IntList/.../DoubleList` (the default combiner cannot merge the per-thread containers); sequential streams perform no such check.
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of("a", "b", "c")
          .collect(StringBuilder::new,
                   (sb, s) -> sb.append(s));
    // Returns StringBuilder with "abc"
  ```
- **See also:** #collect(Supplier, BiConsumer, BiConsumer), #collect(Collector)
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @TerminalOp public abstract <R> R collect(Collector<? super T, ?, R> collector) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @TerminalOp
- **Summary:** Performs a mutable reduction operation on the elements of this stream using a Collector.
- **Contract:**
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
- **Parameters:**
  - `collector` (`Collector<? super T, ?, R>`) — the Collector encapsulating the reduction operation. It provides functions for creating a new result container, incorporating an element into a result, and combining two result containers.
- **Returns:** the result of the reduction
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `collector` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of("apple", "banana", "cherry")
          .collect(Collectors.toList());
    // Returns [apple, banana, cherry]
  ```

##### minBy(...) -> Optional<T>
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @TerminalOp @SuppressWarnings("rawtypes") public Optional<T> minBy(final Function<? super T, ? extends Comparable> keyMapper) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @TerminalOp
- **Summary:** Returns an Optional describing the minimum element of this stream according to the natural order of the keys produced by the provided keyMapper function.
- **Contract:**
  - Elements with `null` keys are considered larger than elements with `non-null` keys and are selected as the minimum only when all extracted keys are `null`.
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
  - Usage Examples: `keyMapper` is applied to every element, `null` ones included, so it must tolerate `null` whenever the stream may contain one.
  - `minBy(Person::getAge)` over a stream holding a `null` element throws a NullPointerException from the extractor itself, even when that `null` element is not the minimum.
- **Parameters:**
  - `keyMapper` (`Function<? super T, ? extends Comparable>`) — a function to apply to each element to determine its key for comparison.
- **Returns:** an Optional describing the minimum element of this stream, or an empty Optional if the stream is empty.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `keyMapper` is `null`.
  - `java.lang.NullPointerException` — if the selected element is `null`, or if `keyMapper` rejects a `null` element
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of("apple", "banana", "cherry")
          .minBy(String::length)
          .get();   // returns "apple"
  ```

- **Examples:**


- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @TerminalOp public abstract long sumInt(ToIntFunction<? super T> mapper) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`

  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.

  - `mapper` (`ToIntFunction<? super T>`) — the function to extract integer values from the elements.

  ```java
          .sumInt(String::length);   // returns 17

          .sumInt(String::length);   // returns 0
  ```

  ```java
          .kthLargest(3, Integer::compare)

  ```

- **Signature:** `@SequentialOnly @IntermediateOp public abstract Stream<List<T>> combinations() throws IllegalStateException`
- **Annotations:** @SequentialOnly, @IntermediateOp

- **Parameters:**

  ```java
  Stream.of(1, 2, 3).combinations().forEach(Fn.println());
    // output
    // []

    // [2]
    // [3]

    // [1, 3]

    // [1, 2, 3]
  ```
- **See also:** #combinations(int), #combinations(int, boolean)
- **Signature:** `@SequentialOnly @IntermediateOp public abstract Stream<List<T>> combinations(int len) throws IllegalStateException, IndexOutOfBoundsException`
- **Annotations:** @SequentialOnly, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Generates all possible combinations of the elements in this stream of the specified length.
- **Parameters:**
  - `len` (`int`) — the length of each combination. Must be non-negative and not bigger than the number of elements in this stream.
- **Returns:** a new stream where each element is a list representing a combination of elements from the original stream.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `len` is negative or bigger than the number of elements in this stream
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of(1, 2, 3).combinations(2).forEach(Fn.println());
    // output
    // [1, 2]
    // [1, 3]
    // [2, 3]
  ```
- **See also:** #combinations(int, boolean), #permutations()
- **Signature:** `@SequentialOnly @IntermediateOp public abstract Stream<List<T>> combinations(int len, boolean repeat) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException, IndexOutOfBoundsException`
- **Annotations:** @SequentialOnly, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Generates combinations without repetition, or the ordered Cartesian power when repetition is enabled.
- **Parameters:**
  - `len` (`int`) — the length of each combination. Must be non-negative, and must not be bigger than the number of elements in this stream if `repeat` is `false`.
  - `repeat` (`boolean`) — if `true`, elements can be repeated in the combinations; otherwise, elements are not repeated.
- **Returns:** a new stream where each element is a list representing a combination of elements from the original stream.
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `len` is negative, or if repetition produces more than `Integer.MAX_VALUE` results.
  - `java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException` — if `repeat` is `false` and `len` exceeds the number of stream elements
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of(1, 2, 3).combinations(2, false).forEach(Fn.println());
    // output
    // [1, 2]
    // [1, 3]
    // [2, 3]
    // ===================================================
    Stream.of(1, 2, 3).combinations(2, true).forEach(Fn.println());
    // output
    // [1, 1]
    // [1, 2]
    // [1, 3]
    // [2, 1]
    // [2, 2]
    // [2, 3]
    // [3, 1]
    // [3, 2]
    // [3, 3]
  ```

  ```java
    // [2, 1, 3]
  ```

  ```java
    // [1, 4, 7]
    // [1, 5, 6]
    // [1, 5, 7]
    // [2, 4, 6]
    // [2, 4, 7]
    // [2, 5, 6]
    // [2, 5, 7]
    // [3, 4, 6]
    // [3, 4, 7]
    // [3, 5, 6]
    // [3, 5, 7]
  ```

##### intersection(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @IntermediateOp public abstract <U> Stream<T> intersection(Function<? super T, ? extends U> mapper, Collection<U> c) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Returns a stream consisting of the elements of this stream that are also present in the specified collection based on a mapping function.
- **Contract:**
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
  - When several elements have the same key, parallel workers may select different occurrences between runs.
  - A downstream operation must still be able to terminate; exhausting the requested keys does not itself stop traversal of an infinite source.
- **Parameters:**
  - `mapper` (`Function<? super T, ? extends U>`) — a function that transforms stream elements into a form that can be compared with collection elements.
  - `c` (`Collection<U>`) — the collection to find common elements with.
- **Returns:** a new Stream containing elements whose mapped values are present in the collection
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapper` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream<String> stream = Stream.of("apple", "apple", "apple", "banana", "banana", "cherry");
    Collection<Integer> lengths = Arrays.asList(5, 6, 5);
  
    Stream<String> result = stream.intersection(String::length, lengths);
    // result contains: "apple", "apple", "banana"
    // (two "apple"s because 5 appears twice in the collection, and "banana" because its length 6 is in the collection)
  ```
- **See also:** N#intersection(int\[\], int\[\]), N#intersection(Collection, Collection), N#commonSet(Collection, Collection), Collection#retainAll(Collection)
##### difference(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @IntermediateOp public abstract <U> Stream<T> difference(Function<? super T, ? extends U> mapper, Collection<U> c) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Returns a stream consisting of elements from this stream that are not present in the specified collection, after applying the provided mapping function.
- **Contract:**
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
  - When several elements have the same key, parallel workers may select different occurrences between runs.
- **Parameters:**
  - `mapper` (`Function<? super T, ? extends U>`) — a function that transforms stream elements into values for comparison.
  - `c` (`Collection<U>`) — the collection of values to exclude from the stream.
- **Returns:** a new stream containing elements whose mapped values have more occurrences in this stream than in the collection
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `mapper` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream<String> stream = Stream.of("apple", "apple", "apple", "banana", "banana", "cherry");
    Collection<Integer> lengths = Arrays.asList(5, 6, 5);
    Stream<String> result = stream.difference(String::length, lengths);
    // Result: ["apple", "banana", "cherry"]
  
    // Explanation (occurrences subtracted per mapped key):
    // - "apple" (length 5): 3 in stream, 2 of length-5 in collection, 3-2=1 "apple" remains
    // - "banana" (length 6): 2 in stream, 1 of length-6 in collection, 2-1=1 "banana" remains
    // - "cherry" (length 6): 1 in stream, 0 of length-6 remaining in collection, 1-0=1 "cherry" remains
  ```
- **See also:** #intersection(Function, Collection), N#difference(Collection, Collection), N#symmetricDifference(Collection, Collection), Difference#of(Collection, Collection), Iterables#symmetricDifference(Set, Set)

##### mergeWith(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `@SequentialOnly @IntermediateOp public abstract Stream<T> mergeWith(final Collection<? extends T> b, final BiFunction<? super T, ? super T, MergeResult> nextSelector) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @SequentialOnly, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Merges the current Stream with a given Collection.
- **Contract:**
  - If the BiFunction returns MergeResult.TAKE_FIRST, the element from the current Stream is selected.
  - If it returns MergeResult.TAKE_SECOND, the element from the given Collection is selected.
- **Parameters:**
  - `b` (`Collection<? extends T>`) — the Collection to be merged. It should be ordered consistently with the current Stream.
  - `nextSelector` (`BiFunction<? super T, ? super T, MergeResult>`) — a BiFunction that determines the order of elements in the merged Stream.
- **Returns:** a new Stream that is the result of merging the current Stream with the given Collection
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `nextSelector` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of(1, 3, 5)
          .mergeWith(Arrays.asList(2, 4, 6),
                     (a, b) -> a < b ? MergeResult.TAKE_FIRST : MergeResult.TAKE_SECOND)
          .toList();   // returns [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
  ```
- **Signature:** `@SequentialOnly @IntermediateOp public abstract Stream<T> mergeWith(final Stream<? extends T> b, final BiFunction<? super T, ? super T, MergeResult> nextSelector) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @SequentialOnly, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Merges the current Stream with a given Stream.
- **Contract:**
  - If the BiFunction returns MergeResult.TAKE_FIRST, the element from the current Stream is selected.
  - If it returns MergeResult.TAKE_SECOND, the element from the given Stream is selected.
- **Parameters:**
  - `b` (`Stream<? extends T>`) — the Stream to be merged. It should be ordered consistently with the current Stream.
  - `nextSelector` (`BiFunction<? super T, ? super T, MergeResult>`) — a BiFunction that determines the order of elements in the merged Stream.
- **Returns:** a new Stream that is the result of merging the current Stream with the given Stream
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `nextSelector` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of("a", "c", "e")
          .mergeWith(Stream.of("b", "d", "f"),
                     (a, b) -> a.compareTo(b) < 0 ? MergeResult.TAKE_FIRST : MergeResult.TAKE_SECOND)
          .toList();   // returns ["a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"]
  ```
##### zipWith(...) -> Stream<R>
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @IntermediateOp public abstract <T2, R> Stream<R> zipWith(final Collection<T2> b, final BiFunction<? super T, ? super T2, ? extends R> zipFunction) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Zips this stream with the given collection using the provided zip function.
- **Contract:**
  - This operation can be parallelized if the stream supports parallel processing.
- **Parameters:**
  - `b` (`Collection<T2>`) — the Collection to be combined with the current Stream.
  - `zipFunction` (`BiFunction<? super T, ? super T2, ? extends R>`) — a BiFunction that determines the combination of elements in the combined Stream.

- **Throws:**

  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `zipFunction` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java

          .zipWith(Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3, 4),

  ```

  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `zipFunction` is `null`
- **Examples:**

- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @IntermediateOp public abstract <T2, T3, R> Stream<R> zipWith(final Stream<T2> b, final Stream<T3> c, final TriFunction<? super T, ? super T2, ? super T3, ? extends R> zipFunction) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Zips this stream with two other streams using the provided zip function.
- **Contract:**
  - If any stream is longer, its remaining elements are ignored.
- **Parameters:**
  - `b` (`Stream<T2>`) — the second Stream to be combined with the current Stream. Will be closed along with this Stream.
  - `c` (`Stream<T3>`) — the third Stream to be combined with the current Stream. Will be closed along with this Stream.
  - `zipFunction` (`TriFunction<? super T, ? super T2, ? super T3, ? extends R>`) — a TriFunction that determines the combination of elements in the combined Stream.
- **Returns:** a new Stream that is the result of combining the current Stream with the given Streams
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `b`, `c`, or `zipFunction` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of(1, 2, 3)
          .zipWith(Stream.of("a", "b"), Stream.of(true, false),
                   (i, s, b) -> i + s + b)
          .toList();   // returns ["1atrue", "2bfalse"]
  ```
- **See also:** #zipWith(Stream, Stream, Object, Object, Object, TriFunction), N#zip(Iterable, Iterable, Iterable, TriFunction)
- **Signature:** `@ParallelSupported @IntermediateOp public abstract <T2, T3, R> Stream<R> zipWith(final Stream<T2> b, final Stream<T3> c, final T valueForNoneA, final T2 valueForNoneB, final T3 valueForNoneC, final TriFunction<? super T, ? super T2, ? super T3, ? extends R> zipFunction) throws IllegalStateException, IllegalArgumentException`
- **Annotations:** @ParallelSupported, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Zips this stream with two other streams using the provided zip function, with default values for missing elements.
- **Contract:**
  - Default values are used when any stream runs out of elements before the others.
- **Parameters:**
  - `b` (`Stream<T2>`) — the second Stream to be combined with the current Stream. Will be closed along with this Stream.
  - `c` (`Stream<T3>`) — the third Stream to be combined with the current Stream. Will be closed along with this Stream.
  - `valueForNoneA` (`T`) — the default value to use for the current Stream when it runs out of elements
  - `valueForNoneB` (`T2`) — the default value to use for the second Stream when it runs out of elements
  - `valueForNoneC` (`T3`) — the default value to use for the third Stream when it runs out of elements
  - `zipFunction` (`TriFunction<? super T, ? super T2, ? super T3, ? extends R>`) — a TriFunction that determines the combination of elements in the combined Stream.
- **Returns:** a new Stream that is the result of combining the current Stream with the given Streams
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
  - `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` — if `b`, `c`, or `zipFunction` is `null`
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of(1, 2, 3)
          .zipWith(Stream.of("a"), Stream.of(true),
                   0, "z", false,
                   (i, s, b) -> i + s + b)
          .toList();   // returns ["1atrue", "2zfalse", "3zfalse"]
  ```
- **See also:** N#zip(Iterable, Iterable, Iterable, Object, Object, Object, TriFunction)
##### onEachSave(...) -> Stream<T>
- **Signature:** `@Beta @SequentialOnly @IntermediateOp public abstract Stream<T> onEachSave(File output) throws IllegalStateException`
- **Annotations:** @Beta, @SequentialOnly, @IntermediateOp
- **Summary:** Writes each element of this stream as a separate line to the specified file.
- **Contract:**
  - Prefer #persist(File) when the stream should be fully consumed and closed as the write sink.
  - The output file is opened when the first element is pulled.
- **Parameters:**
  - `output` (`File`) — the file to save each element to.
- **Returns:** a new stream with the same elements as this stream; writing occurs as a side effect when elements are pulled
- **Throws:**
  - `java.lang.IllegalStateException` — if the stream is already closed
- **Examples:**
  ```java
  Stream.of("Hello", "World")
          .onEachSave(new File("output.txt"))
          .map(String::toUpperCase)
          .toList();   // file contains "Hello\nWorld\n", returns ["HELLO", "WORLD"]
  ```
- **See also:** #persist(File), N#stringOf(Object), #onEach(Consumer)

  ```java
          .onEachSave(x -> "Number: " + x, new File("output.txt"))

  ```
